Meanwhile `studio.py` and the live brief each call a DIFFERENT view 'THE DELIVERY FRAME'.

Use this one if you only use one.")`. Live brief §2: `python3 visibility_budget.py 3840 out/r75_hero34f.png` under "RANK BY PIXELS OF THE DELIVERY FRAME".
findings.why_it_matters: The delivery chain's default view and the package's headline asset are a view nothing renders. Two different views are documented as 'the delivery frame' in live files, so 'render the hero' is ambiguous at the moment someone acts on it.

findings.claim: Transparent-background output is BUILT and GUARDED but has not been exercised for thirteen revisions. Every frame in `out/` today is RGB with no alpha, and `deliver.py` correctly refuses them.
findings.evidence: PNG IHDR read on all five frames in out/: `out/r75_hero34f.png 1600x1100 depth=16 colortype=2` (2 = truecolour, no alpha). studio.py `setup_render`: `if _alpha_delivery(): sc.render.image_settings.color_mode = 'RGBA' else: ... 'RGB'`. Ran `python3 deliver.py --prefix r75 --outdir <scratch>`: "CONTROLS: 4 checked, 1 FAILED -- C1", "[FAIL] C1 ... FAILING ON: hero34f, hero34r, side, front", "PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY". findings.why_it_matters: The single capability the owner's ruling turns on — "It is going on different backgrounds for promotional material" — is one env var away but is thirteen revisions un-run. Nothing in the repo today can be dropped onto a background.

findings.claim: `deliver.py` writes the entire 21-file package plus its README even when it refuses. Only the zip is withheld.
findings.evidence: After the run above printed "PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY", `find` on the output directory lists 22 files: 4 full_frame, 8 layers, 4 trimmed, 4 web PNGs, contact_sheet.png and READ_ME_FIRST.txt. `ls *.zip` → "No such file or directory". Source order in `main()`: the `ctl(...)` calls and `save(...)` per view run before `bad = [k for k, v in CTL.items() if not v]`.
findings.why_it_matters: F49's exact shape on a second script — "a guard whose exit code nobody reads is not a guard". A folder that looks like a finished promo pack, with a README that says "Every image here has a TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND", exists on disk after a refusal.

findings.claim: Only ONE of `deliver.py`'s four controls fires on the failure mode actually present in this repository. C2, C3 and C4 all pass on unusable frames.
findings.evidence: Same run: "[PASS] C2 the vehicle/shadow split holds on every frame", "[PASS] C3 the two layers RECOMBINE", "[PASS] C4 KILL: fed an opaque black frame". The per-view table reads `footprnt 1760000` on a 1600x1100 frame — i.e. the footprint is the ENTIRE frame (1600 × 1100 = 1,760,000) — with `shadow% 0.1`, `veh opaq 1.000`.
findings.why_it_matters: Three of the four controls give a green reading on a frame whose alpha carries no silhouette. C4's kill is an 8×8 synthetic, not the real case. The package's trustworthiness rests on C1 alone.

findings.claim: `post.py` DISCARDS the alpha channel. The optics chain and the transparency chain are mutually exclusive, and this is measured, not inferred.
findings.evidence: Built a 64×96 RGBA PNG with a partial-alpha band (colortype 6), ran `python3 post.py in_rgba.png out_post.png --backdrop white`; output header reads `colortype=2 depth=8`. Source: `rgba = np.asarray(Image.open(src).convert("RGBA"))` then `im = rgba[..., :3].astype(np.float64) / 255.0`, and the save is `Image.fromarray(np.clip(out * 255 + 0.5, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).save(dst)` on the 3-channel array.
findings.why_it_matters: A designer can have optics (bloom/CA/vignette/grain) or a cut-out, never both from this repo. deliver.py's header states the omission as a deliberate choice; post.py nowhere states that it destroys alpha, so anyone routing an alpha master through the documented delivery chain silently loses the silhouette.

findings.claim: The entire large-format delivery chain is 8-bit. The render is authored at 16-bit and both `stitch.py` and `post.py` throw the low byte away at the first step.
findings.evidence: studio.py `setup_render`: `sc.render.image_settings.color_depth = '16'  # audit optics-16`. Measured on a real frame: `Image.open('out/r75_side.png')` → mode RGB, `np.array(im.convert('RGBA'))` → `dtype=uint8 max=255`, on a file whose IHDR reads `depth=16`. stitch.py: `a = np.array(Image.open(p).convert("RGBA"))`; ran it on two synthetic strips and the output header read `colortype=6 depth=8`. post.py reads through the same PIL path.
findings.why_it_matters: F192 records the owner ruling "Bigger — large-format print". The chain that would serve that ruling delivers 8 bits per channel, so the 16-bit render setting buys nothing downstream. deliver.py documents its own 8-bit choice as deliberate; stitch.py and post.py document nothing, so the loss is undeclared exactly where print grading would need the depth.

findings.claim: `hq_render.py` — the current documented delivery chain — does not disable per-strip optics, while `hero.py`, the chain it replaced, explicitly does.
findings.evidence: `grep -c T1_FX hq_render.py` → 0. hero.py line 112: `"T1_SUB": a.sub, "T1_PREVIEW": a.view, "T1_FX": "0",` with its docstring: "Optics (bloom/CA/vignette/grain) are forced OFF during the strip renders with T1_FX=0 and applied once by post.py to the stitched frame. Per-strip optics band at the seams". studio.py `composite_on_white`: `on = optics and _envi("T1_FX", 1)` — default 1. hq_render.py calls `ST.render_set([VIEW], ...)` in-process with no env change. Live proof the chain is on by default: /tmp/r75.log prints `optics: contact shadow ... bloom thr=3.20 ... CA disp=0.0045; vignette 5.5% at corner; grain 0.016`.
findings.why_it_matters: Unless the operator exports T1_FX=0 by hand, the delivery render applies the compositor optics per strip — the banding mechanism post.py's own docstring exists to avoid — and then post.py applies a SECOND numpy optics pass on the stitch. No document names this step.

findings.claim: There is NO export path to any 3D interchange format. The only way to get the model out of this repo as geometry is an undocumented `.blend` save.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn "export_scene|wm.obj_export|export_mesh|gltf|usd_export|fbx" --include=*.py .` returns nothing. The only persistence is build.py: `if os.environ.get("T1_SAVE"): bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=os.environ["T1_SAVE"])`. `.blend` is in .gitignore. `grep -c T1_SAVE` returns **0** in each of PASTE_INTO_CLAUDE_CODE.txt, HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md, START_HERE.md and OPEN_FINDINGS.md.
findings.why_it_matters: The owner's stated goal is "a 3d render from which to build promotional material from." What exists is a 2D PNG generator. A designer cannot take the vehicle into C4D, Blender, Cinema, Substance or a web viewer; they cannot relight it, re-angle it, or hand it to anyone else. The one lever that would help is in no handoff document.

findings.claim: The live 32 KB action brief names NONE of the seven delivery-chain tools. They survive only in HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md at one or two mentions each, and T1_MATTE survives in neither.

findings.claim: Resolutions actually rendered: the highest ever is 4320×2880 (rev 15), the current chain is proven only at 3840×2640 (rev 57), and nothing since rev 70 has exceeded 1600×1100.
findings.evidence: HANDOFF_rev15.md §9: "`out/rev15_hero34f.png` — **4320×2880** ... SUB=2, 56 samples, **18 strips**, worst seam **z = 2.75** against a threshold of 4." LEDGER_rev57.md §6.7: "Delivery frame as shipped: `out/hq_hero.png` (3840×2640, 256 spp, SUB=2, ten margin'd strips)", run 3 "seam-free, worst z = 1.62. SHIPPED", 6408 s = 106.8 min. F192's clause that the seam check "has never been exercised above 3840" is contradicted by HANDOFF_rev15 — it WAS exercised at 4320 and passed at z=2.75 — but through hero.py's PAD chain, not hq_render.py's MARGIN chain.

findings.claim: `post.py`'s module docstring contradicts its own live default.
findings.evidence: Docstring: "DEFAULTS ARE THE SHIPPED LOOK. `--backdrop white` is the SPEC sec.6 lock ... `--backdrop headroom` is the opt-in other arm of the A/B and changes nothing unless it is asked for." findings.why_it_matters: The default is what an operator gets, and headroom without `--matte` falls back to a border-connected heuristic that the file's own docstring says misclassifies speculars. On my synthetic it selected zero pixels and exited non-zero. Anyone trusting the docstring will not pass `--matte`.

findings.claim: STATE.md's headline dimension row reads +525.0 mm OUT in the same file whose guard block reads VERIFY: 0 fail, 0 warn. The cause is the propped tail board, and it is reconcilable inside the file.

HANDOFF_CARRIERS §0.05 gives tail_board's bbox as x −2.420…−1.846; 2.160 − (−2.420) = 4.580 exactly.

The number is real and correct for the posed subject — the tail board is propped and does project 515 mm aft — but the row's name says 'ex counter', not 'with the tail board down'.

findings.claim: What the mesh actually contains today is substantial and clean, and it is the strongest thing this project has.
findings.evidence: STATE.md (live, commit 8bbe354, rev 75): 229 mesh objects, 376,383 vertices, 366,490 faces; body faces 229,489 quad / 1,040 tri / 5,186 ngon; `non-manifold edges (body) | 0`; `cutters rolled back | none`; 45 material datablocks, 43 bound to ≥1 mesh, 5 still constant roughness (amber, glass, lens, reflector, ruby); W=1.7497 (−0.3 mm), wheelbase +0.0 mm, tracks +0.0 mm, tyre diameter −0.1 mm. Inventory includes a full cab and galley: dash, dash_grille, speedo_face/bezel/glass, seats, pedals, gear_lever, mirror_int, plus ~30 `gal_*` objects, counter, plancha, menucards, bulb_string. findings.why_it_matters: The asset itself is real and presentable — this is not a blocked project, it is a project with no way to hand its asset over. Zero non-manifold body edges and a bound material set mean the geometry would survive an export if one existed.

findings.claim: A designer's actual best output TODAY, without Blender and without new modelling, is the optics-finished `_post` set from the four existing frames — and that path runs in seconds.
findings.evidence: `judge_set.sh` loops `for v in front side hero34f hero34r` over `out/${PFX}_${v}.png` and calls `post.py ... --bloom 1.0 --ca 1.0 --vig 1.0 --grain 1.0 --backdrop headroom`, writing `out/${PFX}_${v}_post.png`. All four r75 frames are present in out/. post.py is pure numpy/PIL — my synthetic run completed instantly. Its measured effect (judge_set.sh header, on out/r61f_hero.png): "frame exactly (255,255,255) 47.89 % -> 1.54 %; corner value 255.0 -> 246.4 (a real vignette); high-frequency sigma 0.000 -> 1.317 (real grain)".
findings.why_it_matters: This is the honest answer to 'what can a designer get today': four 1600×1100 8-bit RGB frames on white — front, side, front-3/4, rear-3/4 — optionally with lens/film character applied. Enough for a web deck or a small print. Not enough for a banner, not compositable, and not the six views deliver.py is written around.

ceilings: I was instructed not to run Blender, so NOTHING about what a NEW render would produce is measured here. Every claim about T1_ALPHA's live behaviour, hq_render.py's per-strip optics, and any resolution above 1600x1100 is read off source plus the register — not observed. In particular: T1_ALPHA has not been run since rev 62 (no LEDGER contains the string), so 'transparent output works' is a rev-62 result carried forward, not a current measurement. I verified only that the switch is present, read literally, and guarded by three verify_clone rows.

Whether hq_render.py's missing `T1_FX=0` actually produces visible seam banding is NOT established. The mechanism is documented in two places (hero.py's docstring and post.py's), and the switch is genuinely absent from hq_render.py — but the rev-57 3840 frame that would settle it is gone (`out/` is untracked and starts empty), and stitch.py's z=1.62 only tests row-to-row continuity at the seam rows, which a smooth radial vignette need not disturb. It may also be that the rev-57 operator exported T1_FX=0 by hand and no document records it.

The 4320x2880 record is prose in HANDOFF_rev15.md, not a machine-written file, and the frame is not in the repo. I could not re-verify it. It contradicts F192's clause that stitch.py's seam check "has never been exercised above 3840" — I can show the contradiction but cannot say which is right, only that rev 15 used hero.py's PAD chain, not hq_render.py's MARGIN chain, so the two claims may be about different chains.

Render timings for a full delivery set are ARITHMETIC on the brief's own quoted figure ("~5.5 min a frame" at 1600x1100/96 spp) and rev 57's measured 106.8 min for one 3840x2640/256 spp view. I measured neither. Do not treat 6 views x 106.8 min as a budget without re-timing on this machine.
I did not test whether deliver.py's C2/C3 would catch a PARTIALLY broken alpha — only that they pass on a completely absent one. C1 is the only control I watched fire.
I did not verify the READ_ME_FIRST claim that 'Senor' is drawn "roughly 0.83 x 0.86" of the photograph's size, in either direction. Three of its four defect claims I checked; that one I did not.

STATE.md is at commit 8bbe354 while HEAD is a55dd42, so it is one commit behind. I read the live file rather than the copy imported into my context (which was the rev-74 version and differs in provenance). The mesh figures were identical between the two, but a geometry change in a55dd42 would not be reflected.

The contact sheet and emblem crops I looked at were generated from out/r75_*.png, which I did not render and whose provenance I take from the file names and the brief's §0 command. `probe_rev73_tailboard.py`-class ambiguity applies: I did not confirm which tree those frames were built from.

I did not audit `playa_env.py` or the four Playa views beyond noting they have zero rendered-file mentions. The owner's ruling on that deliverable is "DEPRIORITISED, NOT CANCELLED" (HANDOFF_CARRIERS §4), so their absence is expected, not a defect.

Whether the model would survive an export to OBJ/glTF/USD if one were written is unknown — 0 non-manifold body edges is encouraging but says nothing about UVs, material translation, or the 5,186 ngons.

findings.claim: BODY LIVERY — BUILT. Two-tone: cream upper body + roof, orange-red lower body, split on the belt line which sweeps down the nose into the T1 V-swage (light wedge down the nose centre, red in the two outboard lower zones containing both headlamps).

findings.claim: FLANK FOLK ART — BUILT, but as TEXTURE ONLY (no geometry). `tex/swirl.png` (show side, +Y), `tex/swirl_b.png` (off side), `tex/nose.png` (nose front face), all bound in the paint shader and box-projected.
findings.evidence: t1_mats.py: `swirl = _img(nt, "swirl.png", -1180, -420, projection='BOX',`, `swirl_b = _img(nt, "swirl_b.png", -1180, -640, projection='BOX',`, `_nose = _img(nt, "nose.png", -1140, -1380, projection='FLAT', ext='CLIP')`. findings.why_it_matters: The art is a flat decal in the render — no relief, no paint edge, no brush thickness. For print or animation the artwork is recoverable as a 4096² RGBA asset, which is the useful form, but it will never catch a highlight.

findings.claim: THE FOLK ART'S VISUAL LANGUAGE — THREE INKS, read off ref_playa_34.png at 5× and ref_side.jpg at 4×. (1) FLAT CHROME-YELLOW/GOLD scrollwork: one dominant C-curve acanthus trunk with secondary fronds, every stroke thick-to-hairline tapered and terminating in a tight rolled volute or a hook. (2) ROSETTES: small ~8-lobed flowers, pale cream petals, an inner maroon/red scalloped ring, a gold or white centre pip; scattered as a free field, NOT attached to the scroll. (3) DARK MAROON/near-black COMMA TENDRILS: thin S-curves with a bulbous head and a whip tail, each carrying a row of 2–4 dots along the concave side, used as fillers at the edges of the gold mass and in the bare red.
findings.evidence: My crops: ref_playa_34.png (120,190)-(320,340) [cab door] and ref_side.jpg (620,440)-(1000,620) [rear quarter]. SPEC.md §3 agrees on palette: "| Folk art | **gold + yellow + white + dark-red** Mexican folk-art florals over the **red only**. **Density graded** — dense bouquet on the nose flanks and rear quarter, trailing vine along the belt, sparse under the script |".
findings.why_it_matters: This is the palette a designer actually draws from: a three-ink Mexican signwriter's vocabulary. The rosette is the single most re-usable mark (it tiles, scales and reads at any size); the comma-with-dots is the connective tissue; the acanthus scroll is the hero form.

findings.claim: FOLK ART PLACEMENT — the art lives ON THE RED ONLY, never on the cream, and it stops at the rear corner radius: it wraps the corner but does not reach the flat tail face. Two dominant masses per side (cab door, rear quarter) with the script between them.
findings.evidence: t1_mats.py's tail gate, measured: "rear quarter, cols 830-940   43.687 % gold   n = 19 800 px  <- control / flat tail face, cols 965-1150 0.006 % gold   n = 33 300 px" on ref_rear34.jpg rows 545-725, and "the aft-most gold is at image column 952, which is the cream/red branch intersection, i.e. the station where the corner turns." Confirmed by looking at ref_side.jpg (620,440)-(1000,620).
findings.why_it_matters: Four orders of magnitude with a positive control in the same rows — this is the one composition rule of the livery that is actually measured, and it tells a designer where the art may and may not go on any new surface.

findings.claim: THE BUILT FLANK ART DOES NOT HAVE THE PHOTOGRAPH'S LINE QUALITY OR SCALE. Composited over the body red and looked at, `tex/swirl.png`'s authored band is several SMALL, thin, scribbly gold clusters with tiny rosettes; the photograph's cab door carries ONE bold large-scale acanthus with broad tapering strokes.
findings.evidence: I composited tex/swirl.png over sRGB(150,25,18) and looked at it. Against folk_gen.py's own measured table: "gold connected components, whole flank  66 (ref_side) / 95 (rev 10) / 30 (rev 11)" and "gold in the LARGEST component  47.8 % / 32.4 % / 44.9 %".
findings.why_it_matters: The generator's coverage statistics nearly match while the DRAWING does not — folk_gen.py's own opening says so: "Coverage is a MARGINAL; a generator can match it exactly and still be wrong, because the same 10 % gold over the same flank can be one bouquet or five hundred commas." A designer taking the asset gets the density but not the hand.

findings.claim: MURAL LID (the flower board) — BUILT. One hinged roof lid carrying `tex/lidmural.png`: a dark-brown ground, ~11 stylised 10-lobed flowers with concentric rings and a peace-glyph centre on orange stems, over dense red/orange scrollwork, framed by olive-yellow strips lettered in dark red ("★ FRESH JUICES, GOURMET TACOS & TORTAS ★", side strips "GOURMET / TACOS & TORTAS / FRESH / JUICES / CEVICHE TOSTADAS / SHRIMP & FISH / TACOS") with small painted food illustrations.
findings.evidence: build.py: `A(lid_boards[0], "lidmural")           # flower mural + yellow menu strips`. STATE.md object inventory: `lid_board | 1`, `lid_main | 1`, `lid_rail | 2`, `lid_strut | 2`. Asset viewed at tex/lidmural.png, 4096×2476 RGB. Photograph: ref_side.jpg full frame, the propped board.
findings.why_it_matters: This board is the loudest graphic on the vehicle and the only place the brand's typography appears in a display weight. It is the natural source for a poster.

findings.claim: MURAL LID DEFECT — the shipped `tex/lidmural.png` is CROPPED AT THE BOTTOM: no bottom yellow strip, the bottom row of flowers is sliced mid-bloom and the side columns truncate, where ref_side.jpg shows a board framed on all four sides.
findings.evidence: OPEN_FINDINGS.md F74(a): "`tex/lidmural.png` is **cropped at the bottom** — the bottom row of flowers is sliced mid-bloom and the yellow side columns are truncated, where `ref_side.jpg` shows a board framed on all four sides. The render is faithful to the asset, so the defect is in `lid_gen.py`'s output." Confirmed by looking at the asset. Grade MEASURED-rev58, still OPEN.
findings.why_it_matters: An asset a designer would crop into is itself mis-cropped; and `lid_gen.py` is NOT called by `build.py`, so regenerating it is a hand step or the render silently keeps the old file.

findings.claim: THE "LA SANTA" BOARD (cream, red brush script, red star) — ASSET EXISTS, NOT IN THE DEFAULT BUILD. `tex/lidsign.png` is bound only to `sign_boards[0]`, and `signboard()` returns empty unless `T1_SIGNBOARD=1`.
findings.evidence: t1_shell.py signboard(): "So it is not a roof lid, and it is not on the vehicle at all.  It is a detached sign that happens to fall behind the combi in ref_rear34.jpg." and "`T1_SIGNBOARD=1` restores it.  It is deliberately NOT the default, and no hero should be rendered with it on." Guarded by `if not int(os.environ.get("T1_SIGNBOARD", "0")): return [], [], []`. STATE.md's object inventory contains no `sign_face` or `sign_panel`.
findings.why_it_matters: A designer must not treat the "La Santa" script as vehicle livery — the owner ruled it restaurant furniture (F164, RULED-rev62: "The forward one is separate from the Bus."). It is in the palette of the PLACE, not of the BUS.

findings.claim: WHICH FACE OF THE ROOF LID CARRIES THE FLOWERS IS CONTRADICTED INSIDE THE TREE, AND NOTHING RESOLVES IT. `lid_gen.py` says outward/upper; `SPEC.md` §4 says underside.
findings.evidence: lid_gen.py: "tex/lidmural.png   FRONT lid, OUTWARD (upper) face -- flower mural + strips" / "tex/lidsign.png    FRONT lid, INWARD  (lower) face -- cream + red script". SPEC.md §4: "underside of the raised roof lid painted with flowers and menu strips (only visible if the lid is ever modelled open)." And lid_gen's premise that lidsign is the same board's other face is superseded by the rev-62 ruling above.
findings.why_it_matters: If the mural is on the underside, the board reads as flowers ONLY when open and as plain cream when shut — which changes every closed-lid render and every animation of the lid opening.

findings.claim: THE MURAL LID'S OTHER FACE IS UNKNOWN. `lid_skins` get plain cream `paint`; only `lid_boards[0]` is textured, so in the default build one face of the board is blank cream. No frame we hold shows it.
findings.evidence: build.py: `A(lid_skins, "paint")` then `A(lid_boards[0], "lidmural")`. In ref_side.jpg and ref_rear34.jpg only the flowered face is presented to camera; ref_workshop.jpg shows a DIFFERENT (green) vehicle whose raised lid underside is plain cream.
findings.why_it_matters: It cannot be recovered from what we hold. A designer planning a lid-opening animation has no reference for the reverse face.

findings.claim: BULB STRING — BUILT, one merged object, running the drip rail. Photographs also put a second, separate string along the tail board's edge and a third along the mural/chalkboard lid's frame.
findings.evidence: STATE.md: `bulb_string | 1`, `tb_bulbs | 1`, `tb_bulbflex | 1`. t1_detail.py: `ob = join([ob, flex], "bulb_string")` and the measured note "the aperture surround is a matte white bobble fringe, not lamps, and the only lit string is on the drip rail OUTSIDE the skin, ~55 mm above the aperture heads". Photographs: ref_nolita_front34b.jpg (continuous warm string the full length of the gutter), ref_side.jpg crop (830,180)-(1024,340) (bulbs along the tail board), ref_workshop.jpg (bulbs along the raised lid's free edge).
findings.why_it_matters: The lit string is the vehicle's only self-luminous element and the whole night-time mood. Two of its three photographed runs (lid frame, tail board) exist — tb_bulbs is built — but the lid-frame run is not.

findings.claim: TAIL BOARD — BUILT, in the right colours: cream face, red edge stripe, dark edge, chrome stay, bulb row. Its ANGLE and CHORD are measured; its WIDTH is an admitted pose choice.
findings.evidence: STATE.md: `tail_board | 1`, `tail_board_stay | 1`, `tb_edge_red | 1`, `tb_edge_dark | 1`, `tb_bulbs | 1`, and `tail board pose (F163/F165/F245): principal-axis chord 0.7110 m, angle 38.0 deg, tip z 2.2087`. t1_shell.py: `TB_WIDTH    = 0.5500      # POSE CHOICE, NOT MEASURED.  Inside the 0.59 bound.` HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §0.05 on ref_side.jpg rows 180-320 cols 855-1010: "a **CREAM face, a RED edge stripe, a dark navy/black stripe on the lower edge, and a lit bulb string along it.**" Confirmed by my crop.
findings.why_it_matters: The board's silhouette angle is a strong compositional diagonal in any rear-three-quarter frame, and 38° is a real measurement (±2.3) while 0.55 m of width is not — a designer must not treat the built proportion as fact.

findings.claim: THE TAIL BOARD'S DARK ANGLED RECESS — PHOTOGRAPHED IN ONE FRAME, NOT BUILT, AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT.
findings.evidence: LEDGER_rev75.md: "The feature exists in **one frame**, `IMG_3840.jpeg` (480×320), at **u 401..430, v 108..119 — 30 × 12 px, 58 pixels below lum 90** in a 45 × 25 px window." and "That frame is **byte-identical to `ref_nolita_doorshut.jpg`**, so it is **n = 1**" (F325). I confirmed the identity: both md5 f1b6f98c6a12b6e9ea0ec3edc68e945a.
findings.why_it_matters: An honest n=1 at 30×12 px. It is a real result that it cannot be grounded, not a to-do.

findings.claim: SERVING COUNTER — BUILT: shelf, brass/gold nosing strip, top, with a radiused tail overhanging the body.
findings.evidence: STATE.md object inventory: `counter | 1`, `counter_nosing | 1`, `counter_top | 1`; and `length excludes opened lids: 4.317 with them, 4.065 without (what projects: counter, counter_nosing, counter_top, ...)`. SPEC.md §4: "brass edge strip on the counter lip · radiused counter tail overhanging the body". Visible in ref_side.jpg and ref_rear34.jpg.
findings.why_it_matters: The counter is the vehicle's strongest horizontal and it breaks the silhouette 250 mm past the body — it is what makes the shape read as a taqueria rather than a bus.

findings.claim: GALLEY — BUILT, and heavily: ~30 distinct `gal_*` meshes (worktop, backdrop, racks, shelves, warmer + tap, appliance, caddies, cans, bottles, tubes, tools, hooks, pale, wrap), plus `plancha`, `galley_top`, `galley_backdrop`.
findings.evidence: STATE.md object inventory rows: `gal_hook | 6`, `gal_bot | 4`, `gal_botcap | 4`, `gal_band | 3`, `gal_can_u | 3`, `gal_caddy | 2`, `gal_can_l | 2`, `gal_rack_up | 2`, `gal_stack | 2`, `gal_tool | 2`, plus singletons `gal_appliance`, `gal_warmer`, `gal_warmer_tap`, `gal_worktop`, `gal_sqbottle`, `plancha`, `galley_top`, `galley_backdrop`. build.py: `A(D.galley(), "steel")`.
findings.why_it_matters: Everything a designer sees THROUGH the serving apertures exists. F10–F14 are the open galley cluster and F14 (gal_end_f's sight lines) is the oldest INHERITED row in the register — the galley is present but its framing has never been re-measured.

findings.claim: VW NOSE EMBLEM — BUILT as pressed relief geometry painted body-red on the cream nose (vw_ring + vw_disc + vwbar strokes), which is what the target bus shows. The workshop/green vehicle shows the same pressing in CHROME.
findings.evidence: STATE.md: `vw_disc | 1`, `vw_ring | 1`, `vwbar | 2`. SPEC.md §3: "| VW nose roundel | painted **RED on the cream nose**, **V above W**, pressed relief not chrome. ... **LIVE:** `build.ROUNDEL_D = 0.2800`, `build.ROUNDEL_Z_AG = 1.0170`." Confirmed: red-painted in ref_playa_34.png (20,180)-(200,290) and ref_nolita_front34.jpg; chrome in IMG_2073.jpeg (240,480)-(420,720) and ref_workshop.jpg.
findings.why_it_matters: The red-on-cream roundel is the single most recognisable mark on the vehicle and the most likely logo lockup for merch. It is a PAINTED PRESSING, so it carries a relief shadow that flat vector art will lose.

findings.claim: THE EMBLEM IS STILL WRONG, AND IT IS THE OWNER'S NINTH REPORT. The defect is the strokes' DIRECTIONS: the built strokes radiate where the real mark's are near-parallel.
findings.evidence: PASTE_INTO_CLAUDE_CODE.txt: "**THE EMBLEM IS STILL HIS NINTH REPORT AND IT IS STILL WRONG. F191 AND F234 BOTH STAND.**" and "P2 crossed its 0.85 bar at **0.8528** against P1b's own ceiling of **0.9465**, so it is still ~0.09 short, and **the objective still has no legibility term** (rule 56)." HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §0.07: "**THE INK IS THE RIGHT AMOUNT AND THE WRONG ARRANGEMENT** ... **the built spread is 60.9°**". Confirmed by eye on IMG_2073.jpeg: the V's arms and the W's outer strokes are near-parallel bars.
findings.why_it_matters: Any design using a render of the nose inherits a mark the owner has rejected nine times. Use the photograph (or the factory pressing) for the emblem, not the model.

findings.claim: "SEÑOR TACOMBI" SCRIPT — BUILT as a decal panel on both flanks (`script_L`, `script_R`) carrying `tex/senor.png`: silver, two-line lockup, small "Señor" raised over a large "Tacombi", ornate swash capital T, spiral counters in a/c/o/m/b.
findings.evidence: build.py: `SCR = dict(x0=0.784, x1=-0.494, z0=0.4453, z1=0.9896)    # 2.357:1 = tex AR` then `A(D.conform_panel_true(body, ... name="script_L"), "script")`. STATE.md: `script_L | 1`, `script_R | 1`. script_gen.py measured the ink: "ink is neutral silver, not white and not gold: median RGB (127,122,125), saturation 0.080, over a ground of (129,21,14)."
findings.why_it_matters: This is the wordmark. It is hand-drawn from measured control points, not a font — script_gen.py exists precisely because the owner rejected a system face by name.

findings.claim: THE SCRIPT'S DARK KEYLINE AND DROP SHADOW ARE MISSING FROM THE SHIPPED ASSET — MEASURED. `tex/senor.png` contains no dark ink at all.
findings.evidence: I measured tex/senor.png (4096×1738 RGBA): of pixels with alpha>200, the 1st-percentile luma is 168.3 and the fraction below luma 80 is 0.0000. `grep -n -i "keyline\|shadow" script_gen.py` returns nothing, and `grep -n -i "keyline\|outline\|drop shadow" t1_mats.py` finds nothing in the `silver_script()` path. SPEC.md §3 requires: "| Side script | **\"Señor Tacombi\"**, **SILVER** with a dark keyline and drop shadow". Both ref_playa_34.png and ref_side.jpg show a distinct dark outline and cast shadow round the silver.
findings.why_it_matters: Silver on red without a keyline loses almost all contrast — this is why the wordmark reads flat in the render and crisp in the photograph. It is a one-asset fix and it is the cheapest visible improvement in the inventory.

findings.claim: "100% CALIDAD" DECAL — BUILT (`calidad_L`, `tex/calidad.png`): a spiky hand-painted sunburst graded red→orange→yellow, white bold italic type on two lines set at −19.7°, on the solid cream rear-corner panel aft of bay 3, plus a small pink star.
findings.evidence: build.py: `CAL = dict(x0=-1.155, x1=-1.668, z0=1.4200, z1=1.8000)   # 1.350:1 = tex AR` and `A(T.conform_panel(... name="calidad_L"), "calidad")`. STATE.md: `calidad_L | 1`. cal_gen.py: "the burst is a SPIKY sunburst -- many narrow sharp points of uneven length, not a regular 24-point star", `ANG = math.radians(-19.7)        # measured type / bunting angle`, `PINK = (232, 96, 122)`. Confirmed by my crops of ref_side.jpg (700,290)-(880,400) and ref_playa_34.png (395,100)-(500,180).
findings.why_it_matters: The only decal on the CREAM. It is the vehicle's one piece of mid-century supermarket graphic language and contrasts deliberately with the folk art.

findings.claim: THE PINK STAR IS BUILT ON THE WRONG SIDE OF THE BURST. Both red frames put it ABOVE-LEFT; the model builds it BELOW.
findings.evidence: OPEN_FINDINGS.md F16 (OPEN, INHERITED-rev49): "A13 / A16 — the isolated star is built BELOW the burst where both red frames put it above; every flank rosette is drawn at the diameter of its **gold core**". Confirmed by looking: in ref_side.jpg (700,290)-(880,400) and ref_playa_34.png (395,100)-(500,180) the pink star sits clearly above and left of the burst.
findings.why_it_matters: A designer laying out the decal from the render will place the star wrong. The same row also says every flank rosette is drawn at the diameter of its gold core — i.e. the rosettes are systematically too small.

findings.claim: THE BARS ABOVE THE BURST ARE UNRESOLVED, AND THE MODEL SHIPS NEITHER READING. The source retracted them as bodywork louvres; ref_side.jpg at 8× shows two thin RED bars with triangular pennants hanging below.
findings.evidence: cal_gen.py: "THERE IS NO BUNTING.  THE LINES ARE VENT SLATS, AND THEY ARE BODYWORK." and "In IMG_2073 the slats are BODY COLOUR -- green, the same paint as the panel -- and read dark only because each pressed slot SELF-SHADOWS." Against OPEN_FINDINGS.md F74(c) (MEASURED-rev58, OPEN): "the `100% Calidad` decal is missing **two thin detached red arcs with radiating tick-strokes above the main burst** that the photograph shows clearly separated from it". My own crops: ref_side.jpg (700,290)-(880,400) shows red bars with triangular teeth; ref_playa_34.png (395,100)-(500,180) shows dark-grey straight bars with a red streak.
findings.why_it_matters: Two live records of the same 2–3 px feature disagree and the model draws neither. Whether the vehicle carries bunting is a real graphic-language question (festive vs. mechanical) and it cannot be settled at these scales from what we hold.

findings.claim: HUBCAPS AND WHEELS — BUILT: blackwall tyres (now with transverse tread), cream-painted steel rims, red domed hubcaps carrying a light VW roundel badge.
findings.evidence: STATE.md: `tyre | 4`, `rim1 | 4`, `rim-1 | 4`, `cap | 4`, `capring | 4`, `capvw | 8`; `measured TRACK_F=1.3713  TRACK_R=1.3613  TYRE_D=0.6649`; `hubcap badge: 4 rings R 0.043429 (= CAP_EMBLEM_D/2), glyph extreme 0.043429, spread 0.00e+00 m`. build.py: `A(t, "tyre")          # blackwall`, `A([br, dc], "wheelcream")`, `A(hc, "capred")`, `A(emb, "capwhite")`. Confirmed by my crop of ref_side.jpg (660,520)-(800,640).
findings.why_it_matters: Red cap + cream rim + black tyre is a three-colour roundel that repeats the nose emblem's colour logic at wheel scale — a strong, reusable graphic unit.

findings.claim: THE HUBCAP BADGE IS SELF-CONSISTENCY ONLY — its width fraction has never been compared to any frame.
findings.evidence: STATE.md: "hubcap badge is SELF-CONSISTENCY ONLY -- CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC has never been compared to a frame; see PHOTOS_WANTED item 7". HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §4: "`PHOTOS_WANTED_rev52.md` is the carrier for item 7 (ONE HUBCAP, SQUARE ON AND CLOSE)."
findings.why_it_matters: The small VW on the cap is a candidate logo mark and its proportions are unverified.

findings.claim: GLASS AND SEALS — BUILT throughout: two-piece windscreen, cab vent + door glass, three bay glasses, rear glass, and a rubber seal for every one of them.
findings.evidence: STATE.md: `glass_ws | 2`, `glass_dv | 2`, `glass_dm | 2`, `glass_bay0_R | 1`, `glass_bay1_R | 1`, `glass_bay2_R | 1`, `glass_rear | 1`, `seal_ws | 2`, `seal_dv | 2`, `seal_dm | 2`, `seal_bay | 6`, `seal_rear | 1`. build.py: `A(S.rear_seal(), "rubber")          # rev 72: the ONE glazed aperture that had none`.
findings.why_it_matters: Complete glazing means a designer can pose interior-visible frames. The register still carries F71 (flat glazing) as a look problem, so glass is present but not necessarily convincing.

findings.claim: PAINTED LETTERING ON THE SERVING GLASS ("POLLO", "TACO &…", "…& FISH" in gold) — PHOTOGRAPHED ONLY, NOT BUILT. It belongs to the Nolita/chalkboard livery state.
findings.evidence: Looked at in ref_nolita_flank.jpg and ref_nolita_front34b.jpg. No source path binds a texture to any `glass_bay*` object — build.py assigns `A(S.side_glass(), "glass")` only.
findings.why_it_matters: Rule 11: this is a different livery state of the same vehicle, so its artwork does not transfer to the target. It is nonetheless part of the brand's real graphic vocabulary and a designer may legitimately want it.

findings.claim: REAR HATCH — BUILT, AND OPEN, BUT ITS OPENING ANGLE IS AN UNMEASURED POSE.
findings.evidence: STATE.md: "rear hatch: glass_rear swung +64.00 deg SIGNED about its hinge (declared 64.0, NOT MEASURED -- a POSE); seal_rear tracks it to 0.045 deg and sits 0.0 mm off it". t1_shell.py carries `REAR_OPEN_DEG = 64.0`. HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §0.05: "**THAT 64° IS THE LIVE DEFECT: an unmeasured POSE (F242) with no ablation switch and no guard, on the item the owner named.**" (Ablation `T1_REAR_OPEN` now exists.)
findings.why_it_matters: 64° is a choice, not a fact — every rear-three-quarter composition inherits it, and about a third of the dark rectangle it opens is bare aperture with no pane in front of it (F254).

findings.claim: ROOF — BUILT: cream, rake 17.75 mm/m, drip rail full length, roof vent, and a roof aperture that is genuinely open with solid fore/aft/both-sides.
findings.evidence: STATE.md: `roof aperture: open, and solid fore / aft / both sides`, `rake 17.75 mm/m (locked 17.75); drop at x=0 47.9 mm`, `roof at tail = 1.988`, `roof line slope (measured off the mesh) | -18.1 mm/m`; objects `gutter | 2`, `roof_vent | 1`, `lid_main | 1`, `lid_trunk | 1`.
findings.why_it_matters: The roof's absolute height is OPEN and UNMEASURED (H_ROOF 1.960 retired at rev 22) — a designer should not quote a height off this model.

findings.claim: ROOF LOUDSPEAKERS — PHOTOGRAPHED IN ONE SCENE, DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT: retired as a POSE, not vehicle geometry.
findings.evidence: PASTE_INTO_CLAUDE_CODE.txt §2.2: "**F143's roof loudspeakers are now RETIRED as a geometry item (F309): they are a POSE.** ... **three frames of the same vehicle show the roof BARE** ... the evidence is TWO independent scenes, not three, at n = 1 on the present side." I confirmed the dark box on the roof in ref_rear34.jpg and the bare roof in ref_playa_34.png, ref_nolita_front34.jpg, ref_nolita_front34b.jpg.
findings.why_it_matters: Event gear, not livery. Building it would plant removable kit permanently into every delivery frame.

findings.claim: WHITE BOBBLE / BALL-FRINGE TRIM — BUILT round the three serving apertures only. The photographs also show it round the WINDSCREEN, which is NOT built.
findings.evidence: t1_detail.py: "white bobble / ball-fringe trim round each serving aperture.  CONFIRMED present in ref_side.jpg -- a scalloped row of white balls runs round the inside edge of all three apertures.  Ball diameter and pitch are INFERRED (each ball is ~2 px)." and `for i, (xr, xf) in enumerate(S.BAYS):` — three bays only. STATE.md: `fringe | 3`. My crop of ref_playa_34.png (55,105)-(230,200) shows an unmistakable row of white balls running the full inner edge of the windscreen aperture.
findings.why_it_matters: A found element nothing in the tree records. The bobble fringe is one of the vehicle's most distinctive textures and it is under-built by one large aperture.

findings.claim: INTERIOR RED SCALLOPED VALANCE WITH GOLD LOOPED FRINGE, above the windscreen — PHOTOGRAPHED, NOT BUILT, AND IN NO CARRIER I CAN FIND.
findings.evidence: My crop of ref_playa_34.png (55,105)-(230,200): three red scalloped lobes with gold loop-fringe hanging below, inside the top of the windscreen. `grep -ril "curtain\|valance\|pelmet" --include=t1_*.py --include=build.py .` finds only `valance` used for the body's rear valance PANEL ("lower edge fouling the rear valance", "the bumper, the valance and the whole lower nose") — a different object entirely.
findings.why_it_matters: It is a fourth ink in the vehicle's palette (red + gold passementerie) that no document in the repo names, and it is visible straight through the windscreen in any front or front-three-quarter frame.

findings.claim: PILLAR MENU CARDS — BUILT, three of them, on the cream pillars between apertures.
findings.evidence: STATE.md: `menucard | 3`. t1_detail.py: `name=f"menucard{i}"` and material `rough_field("gal_menucard", scale=260.0,  # 96 x 311 mm card -> 3.8 mm`. build.py's SPEC-§4 list: "aperture bobble fringe, drip-rail bulb string, pillar menu cards". Confirmed by my crop of ref_side.jpg (285,300)-(560,410): a tall white card with a red header block and red/black list text on each pillar.
findings.why_it_matters: The cards carry the menu typography at small scale — the third distinct type voice on the vehicle after the display lettering and the script.

findings.claim: NUMBER PLATE "1963" — BUILT (plate + digits), and REAR-QUARTER LOUVRES — BUILT.
findings.evidence: STATE.md: `plate | 1`, `plate_digits | 1`, `louvres | 2`, `louvbay | 2`. t1_detail.py: `d = join(digits, "plate_digits")`. SPEC.md §4: "chrome number-plate surround on the engine lid reading **\"1963\"**, empty". Photograph: ref_rear34.jpg shows the "1963" plate on the tail; ref_side.jpg (620,440)-(1000,620) shows the louvre slots above the rear arch.
findings.why_it_matters: "1963" is a date-stamp graphic the brand can use directly. The louvres are the only repeating linear texture on the body and read as a deliberate rhythm at poster scale.

ceilings: I DID NOT RENDER. `out/` is untracked and starts empty, and I was instructed not to run Blender. Every statement about a BUILT element is from STATE.md, the source, and the texture assets on disk — NOT from a rendered frame. Anything about how the model LOOKS is therefore unverified, and this project's own first rule is that every shipped defect passed VERIFY and was found by looking at a crop.

I inspected the ARTWORK ASSETS (tex/*.png), not their appearance on the body. The paint shader box-projects `swirl.png`/`swirl_b.png`, FLAT-projects `nose.png`, multiplies alpha by `W_ART` (=1.00 shipped) and gates the flat tail face, so tile coverage is not on-body coverage. ceilings: I MEASURED NOTHING. Every figure above is quoted from a file — OPEN_FINDINGS.md, HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §4, the rev-43 brief, LEDGER_rev61.md, SPEC.md, deliver.py, studio.py. I ran no probe, no render and no build (instructed read-only, no Blender), so no number here has been re-derived and several carry old grades: F92 RULED-rev57b, F156/F157/F159/F160/F155 rev-62, F191 rev-64, F192/F193 rev-64/65, F230 rev-68, F259 rev-71.

THERE IS NO OWNER RULING ON ANIMATION OR MOTION ANYWHERE IN THIS RECORD. `grep -rli "animat"` across all .md/.txt returns exactly ONE file, PANEL_rev61.md, and its single hit is a panel persona description — "focus in 3d modeling, high resolution photography, hyper-realistic animation, etc" — not a ruling, not a request, not a deliverable. If the new program is an animation program, it has NO grounding in the owner's stated rulings and must be put to him.

THE STICKER'S DEFERRAL TRIGGER IS AMBIGUOUS AND I CANNOT RESOLVE IT FROM WHAT WE HOLD. F18's trigger is "build it after the model is done"; F191/F193 hold the delivery render on the same condition; but nothing in the record states whether the sticker and the render share one gate or two. Do not assume.

I COULD NOT VERIFY THE PROMOTIONAL PACKAGE END-TO-END. `delivery/` does not exist on disk (`ls delivery` -> No such file or directory) and `out/` starts empty, so deliver.py's four controls (C1..C4) and its "PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY" refusal path have not been exercised by me. F160's figures — 37.8/62.2 % partition, 97.1 % opaque, 99.99 % one component — are rev-62 readings on a proof frame I have not seen.

THE 'EMOTIONAL BAR' AND THE PLAYA QUOTE COME THROUGH TWO LAYERS. The owner's words are quoted in NEXT_CONTEXT_PROMPT_rev43.md §7 item 4 and re-quoted in F92 and HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §4; I have no primary transcript. The record itself flags that this carrier was DELETED once at rev 44 and only recovered at rev 57b.

WHETHER THE NEW CREATIVE PROGRAM IS THE SAME OBJECT AS ANY RULING ABOVE IS NOT SOMETHING I CAN DECIDE — and rule 34 exists because this project has already applied a ruling about the studio RIG to a different deliverable and published the misattribution for twelve revisions (F92/F188). Every 'ENABLES/CONSTRAINS/FORBIDS' verdict above is scoped to the object the ruling names, and each ruling's object is quoted so the caller can check it.

findings.claim: FATAL AT EVERY SIZE: the body red images salmon, not brand red. On out/r75_side.png the photograph's three annuli read median RGB (158,16,6)/(153,15,6)/(144,14,5), the render (196,81,67)/(195,82,68)/(191,81,69); G/R 0.114/0.106/0.107 vs 0.422/0.434/0.445. Converting those display values to CIELAB (my arithmetic, not the repo's) gives dE76 = 22.6/22.9/23.3, roughly 10x a just-noticeable difference. Hex #9E1006 -> #C45143; HSV saturation 0.962 -> 0.658, value 0.620 -> 0.769.
findings.evidence: flank_compare.py out/r75_side.png, live: 'reference 20- 40 mm n=4193 median (158.0, 16.0, 6.0) G/R 0.114' and 'render 20- 40 mm n=7084 median (196.0, 81.0, 67.0) G/R 0.422'. Register F240: 'it images salmon where the bus is vivid red, and it is the largest colour error in the delivery frame'. F21 is CEILED-rev55 on the same gap.
findings.why_it_matters: A large-area colour is judged at ANY reproduction size - 3-inch sticker, t-shirt, 40-inch poster, 200-px web thumbnail. There is no viewing distance at which dE 23 on the vehicle's dominant surface stops being visible, so this is the one defect that shrinking the deliverable cannot hide. It is a brand-colour failure, not a modelling nit. Cause is already ruled: F261/F266 say the physics is correct and the render is a white studio while the reference is outdoor shade, so the remedy is a grade or an environment change - both owner calls under W6 - not a shader fix.

findings.claim: THE PAINT READS MATTE, over the two largest surfaces in the frame. gloss_compare on out/r75_hero34f.png: render SPREAD 0.495 against the photograph's 1.202, i.e. 0.412 of it against a 0.60 bar; HEADROOM 0.120 against 1.008, i.e. its brightest 1 percent sits 0.119 as far above its own median as the photograph's does. The gate FAILS. visibility_budget ranks this defect at 2.08e6 px^2 (cream upper body) + 8.08e5 px^2 (red flank) of a 3840 px frame - items 2 and 3 of 16.
findings.evidence: gloss_compare.py out/r75_hero34f.png, live: 'render 28014 0.600 106.1 1.095 0.495 0.120 / photo 20127 0.592 54.0 1.794 1.202 1.008' then 'the render's paint spreads 0.412 of the photograph's (bar 0.60) ... FAIL gloss vs ref_nolita_front34.jpg'. Its CONTROL 1 shows the statistic is exposure-free (spread 0.4952 at 0.70x, 1.00x and 1.40x).
findings.why_it_matters: Specular structure is what makes automotive paint read as paint. Absent it, the body reads as flat vinyl or toy plastic. This is a low-spatial-frequency property, so like the colour it survives downscaling: it is as visible on a 76 mm sticker as on a 1 m poster. It is the direct enemy of the owner's own standard, 'I want this 3d model to look like new. Enhanced from the photo.' The gate's own words limit the blame: 'this gate does NOT say the shader is wrong. Part of the gap is the white cyclorama having nothing to reflect, which the owner has ruled stays.'

findings.claim: THE EMBLEM IS A CLOSE-CROP KILLER AND IT IS RESOLVABLE EVEN ON A 3-INCH STICKER IF THE NOSE IS IN VIEW. ROUNDEL_D = 0.2800 m on a 4.065 m vehicle. If the bus fills the print width, the nose roundel measures 5.25 mm on a 76 mm sticker, 19.3 mm on a 279 mm chest print, 42.0 mm on a 610 mm poster. At 1 arcmin acuity and 300 mm reading distance (0.087 mm) the sticker roundel spans about 60 resolvable elements - ample to read V-over-W versus X. The four hubcap badges are D 0.0869 m -> 1.63 mm on the same sticker, about 19 elements, below what is needed to judge the glyph's arrangement.
findings.evidence: t1_core.py: 'The locked diameter has been ROUNDEL_D = 0.2800'. STATE.md: 'hubcap badge: 4 rings R 0.043429 (= CAP_EMBLEM_D/2)' and 'overall length (ex counter) 4.5800 / 4.0550' with the live dims line 'dims L=4.065'. Print sizes and the acuity conversion are my arithmetic from those measured lengths; nothing in the repo measures perceptibility.
findings.why_it_matters: It settles the size question the design program actually asked. A side-elevation die-cut sticker at 3 inches hides the emblem defect (hubcaps only, ~19 elements). A front or three-quarter sticker at the same 3 inches does NOT - the roundel is a 60-element mark and its arrangement is judgeable. On a 24-inch poster the roundel is 42 mm and about 240 elements at arm's length: every stroke is individually inspectable. This is the owner's ninth report of the same object.

findings.claim: WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG WITH THE EMBLEM, MEASURED THREE WAYS, AND IT IS ARRANGEMENT NOT AMOUNT. Pose-free shape IoU is 0.8528 against a same-search control ceiling of 0.9465 - about 0.094 short. The miss is inside the ring (interior IoU 0.8402) not on the band (0.8900), and photo-only/model-only inside the ring is 73/178, near balanced. The built cream cells read elongation 2.84 against the photograph's 3.39, i.e. 1.19x too round. C4 - the live free-spine construction against the photographed landmarks - reads 0.0745 against a 0.045 bar and is RED.
findings.evidence: probe_rev69_fitpose.py live: 'P2 ... best IoU over the frames is 0.8528'; 'P1b ... IoU 0.9465, against 0.9886 uncropped'; 'P3 ... band IoU 0.8900 against interior IoU 0.8402 ... photo-only/model-only inside the ring is 73/178 -- NEAR BALANCED, so the ink AMOUNT is right and the ARRANGEMENT is wrong'. probe_rev46_vw.py live: '12 checked, 2 FAILED -- C4,C10' and C8 'photo 3.39, built 2.84 -- the built cells are 1.19x TOO ROUND. Four fat wedges meeting at the centre IS the X the owner has reported five times; the photograph's cream is seven thin slivers.'
findings.why_it_matters: It tells a designer exactly what a customer will see rather than a score: the mark reads as a fat X where it should read as a V over a W. That is a legibility failure of a trademark, and legibility failures are the class that gets noticed instantly and remembered. It also warns against the obvious fix - the objective has no legibility term (rule 56), and F262 records that the construction that scores BEST on this IoU renders as disconnected shards.

findings.claim: THE RENDER'S EMBLEM LOSES A CELL AT PREVIEW RESOLUTION, BUT THAT IS SUBSTANTIALLY A RESOLUTION ARTEFACT, NOT NEW GEOMETRY. On out/r75_front.png (roundel 120x124 px) the render cuts 5/5/2 interior cream cells at thresholds 20/30/40 against the photograph's 6/6/6. E2 FAILS. But C6, reading the mesh's own raster, passes 6 = 6, and F233 recorded 6/5/2 at 3200x2200 (roundel 241 px) - the count recovering at the lowest threshold when the roundel doubles in pixels.
findings.evidence: probe_rev69_emblem.py out/r75_front.png live: 'RENDER roundel 120 x 124 px | ink 60.8 % of the disc | CREAM CELLS (raw/interior) at thr 20/30/40: 5/5 6/5 3/2' and '[FAIL] E2 ... render 5/5/2 against the photograph's 6/6/6'. probe_rev46_vw C6 live: 'photo 6, built 6'. Register F233: 'at the lowest threshold the render MATCHES the photograph's six'.
findings.why_it_matters: Two consequences for delivery. First, do not budget a revision fixing a floating stroke that is largely the preview's fault - the shape defect (C8/P2 above) is the real one. Second, F233's own mechanism is that the render's mark is far lighter against its own cream than the photograph's - 'ink as a fraction of the cream it sits on: photograph 0.409, render 0.587' - which is the SAME red-desaturation defect as finding 1. At poster scale the emblem's contrast against the nose cream will be visibly weaker than the reference even after the count recovers.

findings.claim: THE LARGEST PIECE OF ARTWORK ON THE VEHICLE IS MIS-PLACED BY ~76-83 mm, AND TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES AGREE. The Senor Tacombi lockup measures 1275.9 x 541.1 mm on the flank - 31 percent of the vehicle's length. flank_compare's registration search finds the render's lockup has to move +76.2 mm forward and -47.6 mm down to sit where the calibrated map puts the photograph's; an independent cross-check sharing no step with it reads +83 / +80 mm aft and the ink top +61.1 mm high.
findings.evidence: flank_compare.py out/r75_side.png, live: 'registration as-placed IoU 0.2695; best integer shift (-16, -10) cells = (+76.2 mm in x, -47.6 mm in z), search +-160 mm' / 'that shift IS a measurement: the render's lockup has to move +76.2 mm forward and -47.6 mm down' / 'SCR's own x extents are +83 / +80 mm aft of flank_X(LOCKUP), and the cream/red differential puts the ink top +61.1 mm high.' Also 'render 1275.9 x 541.1 mm aspect 2.3581'.
findings.why_it_matters: Placement, unlike letterform, is judged against the rest of the vehicle rather than against fine detail, so it survives every downscale. 76 mm on a 610 mm poster is 11.4 mm of lateral shift and 7.1 mm of vertical - a designer laying the render beside a reference photograph will see the script sitting wrong on the panel. It is also the one defect on this list that is cheap: it is a placement number, not a shape problem, and both routes already agree on it. F39 grades it 'a placement/artwork job, not a render one'.

findings.claim: THE SCRIPT'S LETTERFORMS FAIL ONLY ON A CLOSE CROP. Of nine regions, two are below the 0.75-of-own-ceiling bar: 'i' at 0.686 (IoU 0.582, ceiling 0.848) and 'b' at 0.747. Whole-lockup IoU PASSES at 0.7563 = 0.880 of the measured 0.8591 ceiling, and ink area passes at 1.0358. The 'Senor' row at 0.750 is F156's DELIBERATE DEPARTURE - the owner ruled the word to bright silver, so that row now scores away from its own reference and must not be 'fixed'.
findings.evidence: flank_compare.py out/r75_side.png, live region table: 'i 0.582 0.848 0.686 657 662 0.647' and 'b 0.645 0.863 0.747 994 1057 0.709'; 'FAIL worst region 0.686 (i)'; 'PASS IoU vs ceiling 0.7563 target >= 0.7302'. F156: 'those rows got BETTER by moving AWAY from the photograph ... a revision fixing the overshoot would be undoing an owner ruling.'
findings.why_it_matters: Sizing: at 1275.9 mm the whole lockup is 23.9 mm on a 3-inch sticker - an individual letter is roughly 3 mm, about 34 acuity elements at reading distance, legible but not scrutinisable, so the 'i' defect is invisible there. On a 610 mm poster the lockup is 191 mm and a letter roughly 24 mm - a 0.686-of-ceiling shape error in a 24 mm letter is plainly visible to anyone who knows the wordmark. This is the clearest 'fatal on a poster, fine on a sticker' item on the list. Note the 'i' region's ink areas match (657 ref vs 662 render, +0.8 percent), so it is a shape/position defect, not a weight one.

findings.claim: THE TYRES RENDER 1.31x TOO LIGHT AGAINST THEIR OWN RIMS, AND THIS IS A TONE DEFECT THAT SURVIVES EVERY DOWNSCALE. probe_rev70_tyre on out/r75_side.png: tyre/rim ratio 0.2556 against the photograph's 0.1953. The finder's control recovers a known synthetic 0.2000 exactly, so the instrument is sound. The gate's own ceiling is about +/- 20 percent because both tyres sit under an arch and neither rim does.
findings.evidence: probe_rev70_tyre.py out/r75_side.png, live: 'RENDER r75_side.png tyre 46.7 rim 182.5 TYRE/RIM 0.2556' vs 'PHOTOGRAPH ref_side.jpg tyre 29.4 rim 150.7 TYRE/RIM 0.1953'; '[FAIL] T2 ... 1.31x. The lever is dust_film's road film on M["tyre"] ... CEILING: both tyres sit under an arch and neither rim does, so shadowing is not cancelled; good to about +-20 %'. The brief warns this moved 0.2457 -> 0.2558 when the tread shipped (F318) and says 'DO NOT FIX IT BY LOWERING T1_TYRE_FILM'.
findings.why_it_matters: Four tyres are 664.9 mm each - 12.5 mm apiece even on a 76 mm sticker, and 100 mm on a 610 mm poster. Tyres reading mid-grey rather than near-black is a large-area tone error that reads as 'CG' at every size, and it directly contradicts the owner's 'look like new' standard: the model's tyres are dusted, and a new bus's are not. 1.31x is only 1.06x outside the gate's own +/- 20 percent ceiling, so state it as real-but-near-the-instrument's-limit, not as a settled magnitude.

findings.claim: THE TREAD BECOMES COUNTABLE ON A POSTER AND ITS COUNT IS A DECLARATION, NOT A MEASUREMENT. TREAD_LUGS = 64 gives a lug pitch of pi*0.6649/64 = 32.6 mm - 0.61 mm on a 76 mm sticker but 4.89 mm on a 610 mm poster. The probe REFUSES to publish a count: six estimates from two methods at three radii read 55/64/61/74/48/84, a 48..84 bracket. The groove depth 0.0060 m is declared too.
findings.evidence: t1_detail.py: 'TREAD_LUGS = 64 # DECLARED, inside the MEASURED bracket 48..84 (F308)' and 'TREAD_CUT = 0.0060 # DECLARED groove depth, m. NOT measured'. probe_rev74_tread.py out/r75_side.png, live: 'six estimates (2 methods x 3 radii): peak@0.86 55, fft@0.86 64, peak@0.91 61, fft@0.91 74, peak@0.96 48, fft@0.96 84' and '[PASS] T2 REFUSES to publish a lug count: the bracket is 48..84 per revolution, a 1.73x span'.
findings.why_it_matters: At 4.89 mm pitch on a 24-inch poster the lugs are individually countable by a customer. The model asserts 64 where the evidence admits anything from 48 to 84 - a 1.73x span - so a poster crop publishes a specific, checkable claim the project cannot defend. The named remedy is cheap and unowed: PHOTOS_WANTED has never carried a tyre item, and one close square-on tyre frame would close it. Until then a close tyre crop should be avoided in any deliverable.

findings.claim: THE DELIVERY CHAIN ITSELF IS A CEILING, INDEPENDENT OF ANY MODEL DEFECT. The delivery render is under a standing owner HOLD, restated three times; the large-format chain has never been proven; and 3840 px is explicitly not the target. At 3840 px the frame carries 734 px/m, i.e. 1.36 mm per pixel on the vehicle - which is 160 dpi across a 610 mm poster and 96 dpi across a 1016 mm one, both below the 300 dpi print convention.
findings.evidence: visibility_budget.py 3840 out/r75_hero34f.png, live: 'scale: 734 px/m (1.36 mm per pixel) [measured off out/r75_hero34f.png (1600 px wide)]'. HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md section 4: F191 'Keep holding - fix the emblem first' (no delivery render until he says so); F193 the render when it comes is 'MULTIPLE SIZES, MAX RESOLUTION, MAX FIDELITY, ALL IN ONE FOLDER'; F192 'Bigger - large-format print ... 3840 is not the target'. Section 6: 'THE DELIVERY FRAME - DO NOT RUN IT.' The dpi arithmetic is mine.
findings.why_it_matters: Even if every gate above were green, a design program cannot ship from this today: the frames in out/ are 1600x1100 previews, the only large-format path (hq_render.py + stitch.py + post.py) has never been validated end to end, and the owner has held the delivery render pending the emblem. The practical consequence is that poster-scale deliverables need both a resolution decision from the owner and a proving run of the stitch chain - stitch.py's exit code 2 on a seam (F49) being the specific failure to watch for.

findings.claim: THE STICKER - THE PROJECT'S ORIGINAL DELIVERABLE - IS NOT THIS RENDER AT ALL, AND EVERY VIEWING-SIZE ANSWER ABOVE ASSUMES OTHERWISE. F18 locks the sticker's style to 'cartoon with rendered depth' and its scene to 'nothing but the bus, die-cut tight, plus the sun and the papel picado'. The photoreal render does not satisfy that, and the build trigger is 'build it after the model is done'. Only the mechanical half exists: deliver.py's trimmed/ output is the die-cut silhouette.
findings.evidence: OPEN_FINDINGS.md F18: 'STYLE LOCKED - "cartoon with rendered depth"; SCENE LOCKED - "nothing but the bus, die-cut tight, plus the sun and the papel picado" ... DO NOT RE-PUT IT UNTIL THEN'. F161: 'NOT CLOSED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT. Two of F18's own conditions are unmet ... the STYLE IS LOCKED to "cartoon with rendered depth" and this render is photoreal.'
findings.why_it_matters: It changes which defects matter for which product. A cartoon-stylised sticker is largely immune to the gloss deficit (finding 2) and to the tread's declared count (finding 9), because both are photoreal properties a cartoon pass discards - but it is NOT immune to the red (finding 1) or the emblem's arrangement (findings 3 and 4), because a stylisation pass inherits hue and glyph shape. So the sticker's real exposure is colour and trademark legibility; the poster's is everything.

ceilings: NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY MEASURES PERCEPTIBILITY. Every viewing-size figure I give is MY arithmetic, built from measured on-vehicle lengths (STATE.md's L=4.065 m, ROUNDEL_D 0.2800 m, CAP_EMBLEM_D/2 0.043429 m, TYRE_D 0.6649 m, flank_compare's live 1275.9 x 541.1 mm lockup) plus a textbook 1-arcmin acuity assumption. No print has ever been made from this model, no observer has ever been asked, and no probe in the tree scores legibility. Treat the size thresholds as orders of magnitude, not as measurements.

visibility_budget.py states its own limit and it applies to my ranking too: 'pixels are not visibility. A hard-edged error reads louder per pixel than a soft one, Senor being the clearest case here -- it is small and it is loud. Use this to catch ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE, not to rank neighbours.'

MY dE76 OF 23 IS NOT A COLORIMETRIC CLAIM ABOUT THE PAINT. It is computed by me from flank_compare's 8-bit display-space medians, treating them as sRGB. The frames are 16-bit and flank_compare reads through PIL, which truncates silently (F263/rule 58); the values are also post-AgX tone-mapped, and inverse-sRGB does not undo AgX (rule 57a). The DIRECTION and the ORDER of magnitude are solid; the third significant figure is not.

THE RED GAP'S CAUSE CANNOT BE SPLIT FROM WHAT WE HOLD. flank_compare says so in its own verdict: 'Whether the red's G/R gap is the paint or the light CANNOT BE RECOVERED FROM WHAT WE HOLD, and W6 makes it the owner's call either way.' F261/F266 attribute it to the studio being a different scene from the reference; that attribution is what makes it a grading decision, but it is not a licence to call the render correct.

THE TYRE'S 1.31x IS BARELY OUTSIDE ITS OWN INSTRUMENT. probe_rev70_tyre's T2 carries 'good to about +-20 %' because both tyres sit under an arch and neither rim does. 1.31/1.25 is inside that band's width, so the magnitude is soft even though the direction has held across four revisions.

I DID NOT RUN BLENDER, build.py, bootstrap.sh --guards, or any render, per instruction. So I have NOT verified: the T3 rotation kill (probe_rev73_tailboard), verify.py's VERIFY block, the mottle render arm (mottle_measure.py needs Blender), or any ablation. Everything above is read off the four r75 frames already in out/ plus pure-python probes.

I CANNOT SAY WHICH SIDE FRAME IS WHICH. out/ holds both r75_side.png and r75b_side.png; LEDGER_rev75.md records that a second render was deleted and re-made, so 'r75b' is render 3. I named my frame on every reading (r75_side for flank_compare, tyre and tread; r75_hero34f for gloss and visibility_budget; r75_front for the emblem), but I did not check that these are the frames the ledger's own figures came from.

THE EMBLEM'S RENDER-SIDE CELL COUNT IS RESOLUTION-CONFOUNDED AND I COULD NOT SEPARATE IT. E2 reads 5/5/2 at a 120 px roundel; F233 recorded 6/5/2 at a 241 px roundel; C6 on the mesh raster reads 6=6. Only two resolutions have ever been measured and only the thr-20 column moved between them, so 'the count recovers with pixels' is a two-point claim.

THE HUBCAP EMBLEM HAS NEVER BEEN COMPARED TO A PHOTOGRAPH AT ALL. STATE.md: 'hubcap badge is SELF-CONSISTENCY ONLY -- CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC has never been compared to a frame; see PHOTOS_WANTED item 7.' So the four hubcap instances in visibility_budget's item 11 (1.28e4 px^2) have no fidelity reading whatsoever - I ruled them out on SIZE only, not on correctness.

FOUR OF SEVEN NAMED ARTWORK PARTS HAVE NO INSTRUMENT AT ALL. F94 records the owner's 'ABSOLUTE REPLICATION OF ALL ARTWORK' as a hard bar and notes that the menu strips and cards, the rear-lid lettering, the plate surround and the mural board have no register row. I could not assess their fidelity because nothing measures them - and the mural board is a large, high-contrast, customer-facing surface.

F45 (roof-aperture interior, 2.91e5 px^2, item 6 of 16 and dead centre of the hero frame) and F15 (A7 unlit roofed body, 6.92e5 px^2, item 4) are both UNGATED. Neither has ever been measured against a photograph, so they are absent from my failing-gate analysis for want of an instrument, not for want of a defect.

MY PRINT-SIZE TABLE ASSUMES THE BUS FILLS THE PRINT WIDTH AND THAT PROJECTED LENGTH EQUALS 4.065 m. On the three-quarter hero frames the vehicle is foreshortened, so the real on-print feature sizes are SMALLER than I quote - my numbers are an upper bound on visibility, which is the conservative direction for 'is it safe at this size' but the wrong direction for 'is it fatal at this size'.

findings.claim: The palette is a FIVE-part system, not the two-part 'red + cream' the source constants suggest: (1) a warm vermillion red, (2) an off-white cream, (3) a golden-yellow folk-art gold, (4) a burnt-orange/brick mural ground, and (5) BRASS/GOLD as the connective trim metal. Gold is not decoration — it is the line that ties every element together.
