The tree already authors the first three: t1_mats.py `RED = (0.5520, 0.0294, 0.0176)   # = sRGB(196,49,36), hue 5.0, sat 0.816`, `CREAM = (0.6172, 0.6308, 0.5776) # = sRGB(206,208,200)`, `GOLD = (0.8600, 0.5400, 0.0600)`. Gold's spread is visible in crops of ref_side.jpg (820,270)-(1000,420) — a continuous brass band around the whole counter perimeter — and (120,270)-(420,330), a brass/chrome drip rail carrying the bulbs.
findings.why_it_matters: A design system built from this bus needs five tokens, not two, and the fifth (gold) is the one that makes the other four read as one object. Any key art, title card or lower-third that uses only red/cream will look like a generic VW; the gold keyline is the brand's actual signature.

findings.claim: The cream is not one colour — it is a colour that CHANGES ROLE with the light, and the three environments each give it a different cast. The authored CREAM is a cool, slightly green-shifted white (G > R), which matches the skylit frame and NOT the sunlit one.
findings.evidence: Painted windows: ref_playa_34.png roof (105,95)-(175,112) #E1E5E3 (R225 G229 B227 — neutral-to-cool, G>R); ref_side.jpg belt band (470,430)-(560,450) #D4BDA7 (R212 G189 B167 — warm ivory, R>G>B); ref_workshop.jpg (330,340)-(430,380) #989883 (R152 G152 B131 — grey-green under fluorescent). t1_mats.py's comment on the constant says it: `# measured (206,208,200) sRGB -> sun-bleached near-neutral off-white` and `rev-3 had R > G; the measurement has G > R`.
findings.why_it_matters: For an animation or a multi-environment campaign, the cream is the mood dial. Same albedo, three completely different emotional readings — beach ivory, market grey, workshop institutional. Grade the light, never repaint the body.

findings.claim: THE VEHICLE'S HERO SURFACE IS NOT THE BODY — IT IS THE LID, AND IT IS TWO-SIDED. The raised roof lid's inner face carries the flower mural + yellow menu strips facing the customer; its OUTER/rear face is a separate plain cream signboard carrying red hand-lettered script and a red star.
findings.evidence: ref_rear34.jpg cropped (560,0)-(1200,270): the large plain cream panel at left carries red script reading 'La Sant…' with a five-point red star, its rear edge bound in tan; the flower mural with its yellow menu-strip border is the SAME lid seen foreshortened at right. t1_shell.py already models the inner face: `the flower mural with the yellow menu strips -- faces the counter. That is the one arrangement which reproduces all three photographs` and `the mural is on the lid's UNDERSIDE`. The outer face's signwriting is not named in that comment.
findings.why_it_matters: The single most photogenic move this object makes is opening — one gesture turns a van into a stage with a painted ceiling and a signboard back. That is the animation beat: the lid rising. It is also two distinct artwork surfaces to art-direct, and only one of them is currently accounted for.

findings.claim: The lid face is a CANVAS that changes per vehicle and per era, not a fixed graphic. The green sister ship carries a button-tufted cream-and-green upholstered ceiling with rosette medallions in a diamond lattice, inside a green scalloped fretwork valance with gold scallop edging and a gold-backed bulb rim — where the red bus carries a painted flower mural.
findings.evidence: IMG_2073.jpeg cropped (440,0)-(1000,340): tufted cream vinyl with green rosettes on a diamond grid, green scalloped border, gold scallop trim, warm bulbs on a gold rail around the outer edge, two white tension cables. ref_workshop.jpg shows the same architecture bare: a cream ribbed shell lid hoisted open with an orange bulb string on its edge.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the design family's grammar: same architecture, bespoke ceiling. It is a licence to design NEW lid treatments for promotional material without inventing anything. CEILING: this is ARTWORK on the GREEN vehicle, so under the project's rule 11 it does NOT transfer to the red bus's paint — it transfers as a design idea only.

findings.claim: The bulb string reads as a CONTINUOUS GLOWING AMBER LINE that traces the vehicle's silhouette — a drawn line of light, not a row of discrete pearls. It runs the drip rail, wraps the rear roof dome, edges the raised lid, and outlines each serving aperture.
findings.evidence: ref_side.jpg cropped (120,270)-(420,330) at 4x: an unbroken warm orange-gold bead running the full drip rail on a brass/chrome strip. ref_rear34.jpg cropped (950,60)-(1200,420): the same bead curving over the rear roof corner on a gold rail, and again along the raised lid's edge. The register agrees the render is short of this: OPEN_FINDINGS.md F144 — `THE FESTOON BULBS READ AS PEARLS, NOT LIGHTS`.
findings.why_it_matters: For key art and for motion, this line IS the logo. It is the one element that describes the vehicle's whole outline in a single stroke, works at any scale down to a favicon, and animates for free (chase, flicker, ignite). Treat it as a graphic asset with a drawn path, not as N individual emissive spheres.

findings.claim: The nose emblem on the target bus is a RAISED PRESSING PAINTED BODY-RED on a cream nose panel, standing proud with a hard cast shadow to its lower right — and its V and W strokes read as NEAR-PARALLEL diagonals whose outer terminals land ON the ring. It is not chrome on the red bus.
findings.evidence: ref_nolita_front34.jpg cropped (120,170)-(260,290) at 5x: red ring and red strokes on off-white, with a visible drop shadow and a fine cream pinstripe keyline where the red flank meets the cream. ref_playa_34.png cropped (25,195)-(75,250) at 9x shows the same red-on-cream roundel in the folk-art state. Contrast IMG_2073.jpeg, where the GREEN bus's emblem is chrome/silver. This matches the register's own diagnosis, OPEN_FINDINGS.md F104 as cited in HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md: `THE INK IS THE RIGHT AMOUNT AND THE WRONG ARRANGEMENT` and `The built strokes RADIATE where the real mark's are near-PARALLEL`.
findings.why_it_matters: Fifteen revisions of emblem work have optimised a silhouette. What an art director sees first is not the outline — it is that the mark is PAINTED and PROUD, so it has a shadow, a paint edge and a body-colour identity. In a design program the emblem is a red-on-cream badge, and its readability comes from the shadow and the parallel strokes, not from the IoU.

findings.claim: The wheel is a four-layer graphic bullseye and it is the second-strongest motif on the vehicle after the bulb line: outer chrome trim ring / cream painted rim dish / deep-red domed hubcap / cream VW roundel on the dome. The tyre is a plain blackwall that photographs as a warm brown-black, not neutral black.
findings.evidence: ref_side.jpg cropped (680,540)-(820,680) at 4x — cream dish, red dome, cream VW. ref_nolita_front34.jpg cropped (370,290)-(470,390) at 5x — chrome ring clearly visible outside the cream dish, bright red dome, white VW. Painted windows: hubcap dome ref_side.jpg (742,588)-(764,604) #AD4A3B; tyre ref_side.jpg (686,652)-(716,670) #352A27 (R53 G42 B39 — warm, not neutral). Same treatment on the folk-art (ref_playa_34.png, ref_rear34.jpg) and plain (ref_nolita_flank.jpg) states.
findings.why_it_matters: Four concentric bands of the exact brand palette, repeated four times around the vehicle. It is a ready-made badge, spinner, loading state and pattern tile. CLAUDE.md records the render has failed here before — `hubcaps that render as five-petal flowers` — so it is worth verifying visually every time.

findings.claim: The tail lamp is a SMALL AMBER-BROWN OVAL in a thin bright surround — there is no red disc — and the rear carries a chrome licence-plate frame with '1963' embossed on its top rail and no plate in it.
findings.evidence: ref_rear34.jpg cropped (880,560)-(1200,824) at 3x: a small oval amber/brown lens set in a chrome bezel on the red quarter, folk-art flowers immediately beside it; an empty chrome plate frame with '1963' on the upper rail and a small chrome push-button engine-lid handle below.
findings.why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md lists `a disc of body red at the centre of every tail lamp` among defects that passed VERIFY and were found only by looking. The '1963' frame is a free, true, human detail — the owner literally dated the object on its own back — and it is exactly the kind of thing that sells a hero render as a photograph of a real bus.

findings.claim: The vehicle's CHARACTER is a parked, open, working stage — it is never shown driving, and its silhouette in every in-service frame is asymmetric: lid up on one side, counter shelf cantilevered out on the other. The stance is low and planted, with tight arch-to-tyre gaps and a slight nose-down rake.
findings.evidence: All five in-service frames (ref_side.jpg, ref_rear34.jpg, ref_nolita_front34.jpg, ref_nolita_front34b.jpg, ref_nolita_doorshut.jpg, ref_nolita_flank.jpg) show it stationary with the lid raised and staff working it; only ref_playa_34.png shows it closed and static. STATE.md's machine figures agree with the read: `rear arch lip above hub 0.3722 m (ARCH_R 0.3735) -> tyre gap 39.7 mm`, `front arch → tyre gap 40.7 mm`, `rake 17.75 mm/m (locked 17.75)`.
findings.why_it_matters: The delivery frame should not be a three-quarter beauty shot of a closed van. The object's identity is the OPEN configuration — that is the shape people recognise. For animation, the whole story is the transformation: arrive, drop the counter, raise the lid, light the bulbs.

findings.claim: THE THREE ENVIRONMENTS ARE THREE DIFFERENT EMOTIONAL PRODUCTS, and each has its own light. Playa/Mexico = hot open shade, warm bounce, palm shadows, papel-picado garlands: FIESTA. Nolita indoor market = cool grey-blue fill from high fluorescents on concrete, headlamps ON as practicals, crowds close: URBAN CULT. Workshop = flat overhead fluorescent on bare block and concrete, no dressing: ORIGIN STORY.
findings.evidence: ref_side.jpg / ref_rear34.jpg: palm fronds, a palapa roof, a hanging floral garland strung across the frame (ref_rear34.jpg upper edge), warm bounce off cream walls; painted paving window (60,700)-(140,750) #838285 warm-neutral. ref_nolita_front34.jpg: painted floor window (560,400)-(660,450) #5D6C70 — cool blue-grey concrete — with the bus's headlamps visibly lit and white-coated staff either side. ref_workshop.jpg: overhead strip fluorescents, breeze-block walls, pallets, a bench vice, the lid hoisted on ceiling wires.
findings.why_it_matters: Three campaigns, one asset. The playa frame is the poster, the Nolita frame is the social/editorial, the workshop frame is the founder's-story cutaway. Each needs its own lighting rig and its own cream cast; none of them is the featureless white void the current studio uses.

findings.claim: THE LIVERY STATES ARE A DELIBERATE ASSET, AND THERE ARE AT LEAST THREE DRESS STATES PLUS A SISTER-SHIP COLOURWAY. (A) Mexico folk-art: full yellow/gold paisley and flowers, silver-leaf 'Señor Tacombi', flower-mural lid. (B) Nolita plain: no folk art, no script, plain red/cream, a white-and-red awning lid. (C) Nolita chalkboard: same plain body, but the lid is a black slate menu in a cream-and-gold frame lettered in Mexican-flag tricolour. (D) The GREEN sister ship: same architecture, white/silver folk art with daisies, BLACK outlined script.
findings.evidence: (A) ref_side.jpg, ref_rear34.jpg, ref_playa_34.png. (B) ref_nolita_front34.jpg — flank is unbroken plain red, no script anywhere. (C) ref_nolita_doorshut.jpg ≡ IMG_3840.jpeg (md5 f1b6f98c6a12b6e9ea0ec3edc68e945a), cropped (140,0)-(360,130): 'TACOMBI' in green/white/red shadowed caps, 'NUEVA YORK' / 'PLAYA DEL CARMEN' on the rails, 'BIENVENIDOS' vertically down both jambs in red with gold stars, 'VENGA A NOLITA ★' along the base, black slate chalked in white. (D) IMG_2073.jpeg and ref_workshop.jpg. Painted green window ref_workshop.jpg (560,560)-(660,600) #5E7A50.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a skinnable object with an established, owner-sanctioned variant history. For a promotional program it means seasonal/city liveries are IN CHARACTER rather than invention — and the chalkboard state is a built-in place to put live copy (menu, date, city) in any campaign or animation, without touching the model.

findings.claim: There are THREE distinct lettering voices on this vehicle and they are used consistently by role: (1) fat psychedelic display for the name, hand-laid in SILVER LEAF with visible tarnish; (2) shadowed slab/serif caps in tricolour for place and category; (3) a small upright condensed caps + red cursive pairing for the civic/address line.
findings.evidence: (1) ref_side.jpg cropped (300,460)-(620,580): 'Tacombi' in a fat 1960s-70s swash display face, silver with warm iridescent tarnish, 'Señor' above it smaller and noticeably more tarnished/brown. The tree already ships this ruling — PASTE_INTO_CLAUDE_CODE.txt / HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §4 quote the owner: `"Bright silver, same as Tacombi."` (2) ref_nolita_doorshut.jpg (140,0)-(360,130): 'TACOMBI' shadowed slab caps in green/white/red. (3) ref_nolita_doorshut.jpg (280,140)-(470,230) at 5x: '267 / ELIZABETH STREET / NUEVA YORK' in small black condensed caps above 'Gracias por su Preferencia' in red script, hand-lettered on the cream counter fascia.
findings.why_it_matters: A ready-made type hierarchy for any deliverable: display face for the wordmark, tricolour slab for headline/place, condensed-plus-script for the fine print. It also names the finish — silver LEAF with tarnish, not flat grey ink — which is a material, not a colour.

findings.claim: THE ROOF GEAR CORRELATES WITH THE SERVING POSE, NOT WITH THE VEHICLE — which gives the register's retirement of the roof loudspeakers a mechanism it did not have. In both frames where the lid is UP and the bus is trading in Mexico there is an object on the roof; in every frame where the lid is DOWN or the bus is in Nolita, the roof is bare and shows a single clean chrome gutter line.
findings.evidence: ref_rear34.jpg cropped (540,180)-(900,300): a silver/chrome-faced box speaker with a black driver sitting on the roof lip. ref_side.jpg cropped (270,255)-(420,300): an ochre/tan object with a dark rectangular face and a metal bracket at the lid's forward end. Against that, ref_playa_34.png cropped (180,80)-(420,115): a completely bare cream roof with one bright polished gutter rail. The register's retirement reads (PASTE_INTO_CLAUDE_CODE.txt §2): `F143's roof loudspeakers are now RETIRED as a geometry item (F309): they are a POSE.`
findings.why_it_matters: Confirms visually that roof gear is EVENT DRESSING, so it belongs in a dressing layer that can be switched on for a fiesta frame and off for the clean hero — exactly the way a design program wants variant assets. CEILING: at 1024x768 the ref_side object cannot be identified; I can say something is there, not what it is.

findings.claim: PAPEL PICADO AND HANGING GARLANDS ARE PART OF THE VEHICLE'S NATIVE SETTING, which matters because the project's oldest open deliverable specifies exactly that motif and has been treated as an unrelated task.
findings.evidence: ref_rear34.jpg cropped (560,0)-(1200,270): a floral/cut-paper garland strung across the palapa directly above the bus, plus the palm canopy. OPEN_FINDINGS.md F18 records the owner's locked scene for the die-cut sticker: `"nothing but the bus, die-cut tight, plus the sun and the papel picado"`, with the style locked to `"cartoon with rendered depth"` and the intent `"should spark joy and be something families keep"`.
findings.why_it_matters: The sticker's scene brief is not an abstract instruction — it is a description of ref_rear34.jpg. The reference for the project's original deliverable is already in the repository, which removes one stated blocker on it.

findings.claim: The counter is a designed piece of furniture in its own right and reads as the bus's 'shopfront': a cream cantilevered slab wrapping the rear corner on a big soft radius, edged with a continuous brass band, on a wood-toned nosing, dressed with chrome-and-black condiment tins and a chrome plancha.
findings.evidence: ref_side.jpg cropped (600,330)-(960,430) and (820,270)-(1000,420) at 3-4x: a brass/gold band running the entire counter perimeter including around the radiused rear corner, cream top, honey-toned nosing beneath, five chrome-topped dispensers, a chrome griddle/toaster. The tree already carries the intent — t1_mats.py: `brass nosing on the OUTER EDGE, body cream below`, `COUNTERTAN = (0.5870, 0.4930, 0.3060)     # = sRGB (201,186,150), h 42, s 0.25`.
findings.why_it_matters: The counter's radiused corner plus brass edge is the shape that says 'mid-century cantina' rather than 'food truck'. It is the natural anchor for any layout — the horizontal it draws across the frame is where copy wants to sit.

findings.claim: THE RED IS UNRECOVERABLE FROM THE NOLITA FRAMES AND IS WILDLY DIFFERENT ACROSS FRAMES — so any single 'the photograph's red' figure is a fiction. Its measured 8-bit G/R spans 0.109 to 0.221 across three frames of the folk-art state alone, and the Nolita frame is 23 % clipped in R.
findings.evidence: Painted windows, 8-bit sRGB medians with clipping fraction reported: ref_side.jpg (620,470)-(690,510) #810E06, G/R 0.109, clip 0 %; ref_playa_34.png (370,255)-(420,275) #912015, G/R 0.221, clip 0 %; ref_nolita_front34.jpg (350,175)-(430,205) #FF3511, G/R 0.208, clip>=254 22.6 %. The project's own instrument says the same thing in linear: HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md quotes probe_rev71_red.py — `the photograph's red G/R is 0.0149 .. 0.0344, a 2.3x span. DO NOT QUOTE A SINGLE FIGURE FOR IT.`
findings.why_it_matters: For a design program, pick the brand red from the ARTWORK-CLEAN, unclipped frame and declare it, rather than trying to average the photographs. And do not chase the render's red toward a clipped photograph — the target moves 2x between frames of the same bus on the same day.

ceilings: EVERY COLOUR FIGURE I QUOTE IS AN 8-BIT DISPLAY-sRGB MEDIAN of a hand-painted window in a JPEG/PNG under uncontrolled illumination. It is NOT linear, NOT white-balanced, and NOT comparable with the project's linear albedo constants or with probe_rev71_red.py's linear G/R figures. I did not import photometry.py; I read through PIL, which the register (F263/rule 58) records as an 8-bit path. Treat every hex value as a MOOD reference, never as an albedo.

I PAINTED EVERY WINDOW AND LOOKED AT IT, AND FOUR OF MY FIRST WINDOWS WERE WRONG — a 'playa cream nose' box landed on the windscreen, a 'side red flank low' box landed in the shadow under the bus (#0E0C0A), a 'nolita cream' box landed on a hubcap, and a 'rear red clean' box landed on a hubcap. Those readings are discarded and are not quoted above. The windows I do quote are the ones whose crops I viewed as swatch tiles.

I CANNOT ESTABLISH THAT THE MEXICO FRAMES AND THE NOLITA FRAMES ARE THE SAME PHYSICAL VEHICLE. The record asserts it (HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §0.1 lists all seven under 'the RED target bus'). What I can show is that the DRESSING differs completely — folk art present vs absent, silver script present vs absent, mural lid vs awning vs chalkboard — while the wheel treatment, the body split line and the emblem's red-on-cream painted finish are consistent. Identity is inherited from the record, not measured by me.

THE RED SCRIPT ON THE MURAL LID'S OUTER FACE IS ONLY PARTLY LEGIBLE. In ref_rear34.jpg at 2x I can read 'La Sant' plus a red five-point star; the remainder runs off behind the raised lid. I am NOT naming the full word.

THE OBJECT ON THE ROOF IN ref_side.jpg CANNOT BE IDENTIFIED at 1024x768 — it is an ochre/tan mass with a dark rectangular face and a metal bracket. I can say the roof is NOT bare in that frame; I cannot say it is a loudspeaker. Only ref_rear34.jpg shows an unambiguous box speaker.

THE 'GOLD KEYLINE' AROUND THE PLAYA EMBLEM MAY BE CHROMA FRINGING. ref_playa_34.png is 500x400 and the roundel spans roughly 45 px; the warm fringe on the lower-left of the strokes is consistent with either a painted gold keyline or JPEG/resample chroma error. It cannot be separated at this resolution. The red-on-cream reading itself is safe — ref_nolita_front34.jpg at 700x467 shows it unambiguously.

THE TUFTED CEILING AND SCALLOPED VALANCE ARE ARTWORK ON THE GREEN VEHICLE (IMG_2073.jpeg, ref_workshop.jpg). Under the project's rule 11 artwork does NOT transfer between vehicles. They are design-language evidence for what a Tacombi lid interior can be; they are NOT evidence about the red bus's lid, whose inner face the photographs show carrying the painted flower mural.

I DID NOT RENDER ANYTHING AND I DID NOT COMPARE THE MODEL TO THE PHOTOGRAPHS. out/ is untracked and starts empty, and I was instructed not to run Blender. Every statement above about what the MODEL does is read from source strings or STATE.md, never from a frame.

THE MURAL'S BORDER COPY IS PARTLY OCCLUDED BY PALM FRONDS in ref_side.jpg. I can read 'FRESH JUICES', '& TORTAS', 'GOURMET TACOS', 'SHRIMP & FISH' on the strips; the centre of the top rail is behind foliage in the only frame that shows it broadside.
I DID NOT MEASURE STANCE. STATE.md's rake, arch gaps and track are quoted from the machine; my 'low and planted' reading is a visual impression from the frames and has no ruler under it.

findings.claim: Tacombi's own origin account — which SPEC.md already quotes and grades as source-class (S) — describes a vehicle that was DISMANTLED, not driven. Engine scrapped, transmission sold, seats out, roof cut back. It is a building, not a van.
findings.evidence: SPEC.md §0.1: **S** — Tacombi's own account: *"We purchased a 1963 'combi' bus in Mexico City, wheeled it slowly (very slowly) through the Yucatan peninsula and parked it comfortably in … Playa del Carmen. The engine was scrapped, transmission sold, seats swapped for cooking equipment, and the roof was reeled back to produce a taco serving stand."* Corroborated independently by WebSearch summaries of tacombi.com/our-story and CNBC 2023-01-09.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the single hardest constraint on any animation in the program. A driving loop, a rolling wheel, a road-trip beat, exhaust, motion blur on the tyres — every one of these contradicts the brand's own telling. The correct motion vocabulary is the SERVING vocabulary: the roof lid opening, the tail board propping, the bulb string lighting, the counter shutters going up. Rev 74 shipped a transverse tyre tread (F308); that tread will never be seen turning.

findings.claim: 'Combi' is a Mexican word for a working-class public-transport microbus (pesero), not a countercultural hippie bus. The name is a portmanteau of taco + combi.
findings.evidence: WebSearch (Wikipedia 'Pesero', mexicanspanish.com, Medium 'The Combi: Transportation and Community in Small-Town Mexico'): "A combi is a converted Volkswagen microbus that picks up and lets off passengers along its route"; "By the 1980s, pesero owners started using Volkswagen Microbus vehicles for increased capacity"; "Working class Mexicans in small communities used this mode of transportation to get to and from work." CNBC/Fast Company: "Wolos named his restaurant after the van, making a portmanteau from the words 'taco' and 'combi,' a word that describes a microbus in Mexico."
findings.why_it_matters: This is the anti-derivative axis for the whole program. The US/European reading of this body shape is Woodstock — Smithsonian: "How the Volkswagen Bus Became a Symbol of Counterculture." The Mexican reading is a workhorse that hauls people and sells food. Every trope in §2 below belongs to the FIRST reading. Tacombi's own name commits it to the SECOND. Any design move that reaches for peace signs, tie-dye, surfboards or a sunset is not merely generic — it is the wrong country's meaning of the same object.

findings.claim: The three serving hatches — the vehicle's most recognisable feature — exist because the $3,000 donor bus was already missing its glass. The signature is an accident of cheapness, and the record says so.
findings.evidence: SPEC.md §0.1: "**S** — Founder Dario Wolos: the bus was **green** when bought, cost **$3,000**, was **\"missing three of its windows\"** and **\"only had the front bench\"**; he *\"figured out how to **cut open** the Tacombi\"*. Opened 6 February 2006." and "**E** — 'Missing three of its windows' is almost certainly *why* the show side became three serving hatches: the donor bus already had no glass there." (Note SPEC grades this E = inference, not measured.)
findings.why_it_matters: It is a story only this vehicle can tell, and it is the opposite of the restored-collector fantasy every VW-bus print sells. It also gives the render program a narrative frame that does not require the VW badge to carry the meaning: three holes where the windows should be IS the logo.

findings.claim: On this vehicle the VW roundel is PAINTED RED on the cream nose — pressed relief, not chrome — and the hubcaps are red domes with a light VW. The brand mark is subordinated by the vehicle itself.
findings.evidence: SPEC.md: "| VW nose roundel | painted **RED on the cream nose**, **V above W**, pressed relief not chrome." and "| Wheels | **BLACKWALL** tyres; **cream/off-white painted steel rims**; **red domed hubcaps** with a **light VW** in the centre | **M** |". Retired-readings list: "⚠ **VW nose roundel painted cream** — it is painted **red on the cream nose** (**M**, §8.3)"; "chrome hubcaps — they are **red domes with a light VW**".
findings.why_it_matters: Two consequences. (1) Every stock VW-bus asset hero-shots a CHROME badge; this bus paints over it. That is free differentiation the geometry already has. (2) It partially de-risks the trademark exposure below — the mark is present as relief under paint, not as a reproduced chrome logo — though it does not remove it. It also reframes the emblem work (F191/F234, the owner's ninth report): the emblem matters because it is a painted-over pressing catching light, not because it is a logo to be reproduced legibly.

findings.claim: Volkswagen actively enforces its marks against merchandise, and the bus SHAPE itself is claimed as a trademark. This program's stated purpose is promotional material.
findings.evidence: WebSearch (mandourlaw.com, avvo.com, justanswer): "when it comes to their attention that a business is using a Volkswagen trademark without permission, that business can expect to receive a letter from Volkswagen"; "You cannot refer to the brand name Volkswagen, or VW on products without a license. The images of classic Beetle and Bus vehicles are themselves protected as trademarks"; "Volkswagen AG has notified Etsy about listings they believe infringe." Contrast the eBay listing title in results: "Volkswagen Bus VW Sunset Camping **Officially Licensed** T-Shirt." Against owner ruling in HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §4: *"The ultimate goal is a 3d render from which to build promotional material from."*
findings.why_it_matters: The program's deliverable is commercial merchandise imagery of a trademarked vehicle carrying a trademarked roundel. This is a live commercial constraint that no document in this repo currently carries, and it is a question for the owner (who may already have an arrangement, being the brand), not a design decision to be made by a render. It is also an argument for the compositional moves that emphasise the CONVERSION over the donor vehicle: the counter, the hatches, the open lid, the folk art — none of which is VW's.

findings.claim: Tacombi's existing typographic identity is the same 1960s fat-display family as the hand-painted script on the bus's flank. The vehicle's lettering is the brand's typographic DNA, not decoration on top of it.
findings.evidence: WebSearch summary of fontsinuse.com: Tacombi's identity (credited to designers at Brandibble) uses "Cooper Black … designed in 1922 by Oswald Bruce Cooper", "ITC Bauhaus Pro Bold", "Davida by Louis Minott (1965)" "utilized a lot throughout the menu", and "ITC Bookman"; Vista Hermosa packaging "uses PAG Revolucion for their logotype, and Davida and Roberta throughout their line … Davida is used with Balloon Drop Shadow". Against NEXT_CONTEXT_PROMPT_rev8.md on the flank script: "It is fat, rounded, late-1960s psychedelic display lettering in **silver** — not white, not gold. 'Señor' small and raised upper-left; 'Tacombi' large. The capital **T** carries a long ribbon swash sweeping back over 'Señor'. The **o, a, c and b have rolled spiral counters**".
findings.why_it_matters: The owner's repeated complaint — "señor Tacombi still isn't clearer" (HANDOFF_rev45.md) — is a BRAND-IDENTITY defect, not only a fidelity defect. The script is the one element on the vehicle that is also the brand's voice in every other channel. It ranks above its pixel area. It also means any typography the program authors around the render has an existing house family to sit in (Cooper Black / Davida / Bookman), rather than needing invention — and that a generic 'Mexican restaurant' font would read as counterfeit.

findings.claim: Tacombi's existing merch voice is deadpan leisure-outfitter catalogue copy, not folk-art maximalism.
findings.evidence: WebSearch of shop.tacombi.com: store described as providing "casual, convenient leisure products since 2006". Product names: "Tacombi Icon Tote" ("The famous delivery bag makes its debut in tote fabric form"), "The Seaside Expo Tote" ("a convenient coastal super sac"), "Horizon Beanie" ("a purpose-built, all-weather knit beanie"), "Monument T" ("an original leisure-filled T for relaxed coastal living"), "'Your Flavor Has Arrived' Hat". Earlier line (Dan's Papers, 2013): "Tropi-Tees … a statement of international beach adventure", incl. a "Toma Lupita" design.
findings.why_it_matters: A photoreal hero render has to sit beside this voice. The copy is understated, faintly institutional, and product-catalogue in register — 'purpose-built', 'expo', 'monument', 'horizon'. That argues for the SPEC-sheet / catalogue-plate register for the render's presentation, and against a warm nostalgic poster. It also suggests the render's most on-brand framing is the deadpan one: the object, presented straight, named like equipment.

findings.claim: The VW-bus merchandise market is saturated by a small, nameable set of visual moves. All of them are available to name and forbid.
findings.evidence: WebSearch across Redbubble, Etsy, Amazon, eBay, AllPosters, Fine Art America, Dreamstime: (a) SUNSET SILHOUETTE — "a retro VW Bus parked in front of a stunning sunset backdrop, flanked by breezy palm trees and surfboards"; (b) SURF — "beach, ocean, sunset, surfing, tropical landscape, surfboard, palm tree silhouette"; (c) HIPPIE/FLOWER-POWER — "Peace signs, floral motifs like daisies and sunflowers, and celestial designs", "Sunflower or daisy murals … the mascots of the hippie movement"; (d) 70s/80s RETRO WASH — "vintage 80s aesthetics", "Venice Beach, California in the 70's and 80's"; (e) MINIMAL LINE ART — "Minimalist illustrator styles featuring trace monotone and black lines", "a vintage minimalist line drawing style"; (f) BLUEPRINT/TECHNICAL — Dreamstime carries a standing category "Vw Van Blueprint Stock Illustrations"; (g) BOHO / WATERCOLOUR / POP-ART colourways — "abstract vw bus art, vintage vw bus art, boho vw bus art, and minimalist vw bus art", "pop art compositions".
findings.why_it_matters: Two of these are traps this program is ALREADY standing next to. The BLUEPRINT/exploded-diagram move is the obvious way to dramatise a photoreal 3D model and is a stock category — Dreamstime sells it by the sheet. And the FLOWER move is worse than generic here: this bus genuinely carries hand-painted florals (SPEC: "**gold + yellow + white + dark-red** Mexican folk-art florals over the **red only**"), so a design that leans on them will be READ as hippie flower-power even though the source is Mexican folk art. The florals need context — the counter, the hatches, the Spanish signage — to read correctly.

findings.claim: The one thing the market does not have is what this repo has been building for 75 revisions: THIS vehicle, measured, with its conversion. Every distinctive feature is a thing a stock VW-bus asset does not possess.
findings.evidence: SPEC.md §1 table and §4: "THREE stock side windows with the glass removed — open serving hatches"; "**cantilevered cream-painted slab counter** under the three hatches, chamfered front end, running past the tail"; roof "**cut into rigid hinged steel lids**, modelled **OPEN** … underside carrying the flower mural + yellow menu strips"; "**'100% Calidad'** — white slanted type on a **red-to-orange spiky sunburst** … with a small pink star to its left"; and the Tacombi-specific list: "white bobble / ball-fringe trim round each serving aperture · printed menu cards on the pillars between apertures · string of small bulbs along the drip rail · brass edge strip on the counter lip · radiused counter tail overhanging the body · chrome number-plate surround on the engine lid reading **\"1963\"**, empty". Plus "bumpers … **painted cream**", "cream/off-white painted steel rims", and the tail board (STATE.md: `tail_board`, `tb_bulbs`, `tb_edge_red`, `tb_bulbflex`).
findings.why_it_matters: This is the anti-derivative asset list. Rank future geometry and future art direction by which of these it shows. A frame that shows the counter, an open hatch and the propped tail board with its bulbs cannot be mistaken for stock; a three-quarter front that shows mostly the nose and the roundel can. Note this directly re-ranks the delivery-frame choice: `hero34f` shows the nose (generic + trademarked); the SHOW SIDE and the rear three-quarter show the things nobody else has.

findings.claim: The brand has FOUR canonical looks of one vehicle, and the green→red arc is itself a narrative asset the merch program could use — but the project's own rule forbids mixing them.
findings.evidence: LEDGER_rev51.md verified table: "**RED, CURRENT** … scrollwork, Señor Tacombi script, Calidad burst"; "**RED, EARLIER** | the four *nolita* frames | plain red flank, `TACOMBI.COM`, no scrollwork, no script, no burst"; "**GREEN, IN SERVICE** | `IMG_2073.jpeg` | script in **BLACK**, plus white/blue scrollwork with yellow daisies, plus a **100 % Calidad starburst**, plus orange TACOS / BREAKFAST SPECIAL"; "**GREEN, CONVERSION** | `ref_workshop.jpg` | script **ONLY**, silver outline. No scrollwork, no daisies, no burst. Headlamps **not fitted** … both road wheels are bare painted rims with NO HUB CAP." SPEC.md §7.1: owner ruled it is the SAME VEHICLE in different livery states; "livery is still state-dependent, so folk art, script, aperture glazing and roof-board treatment may never be carried across states."
findings.why_it_matters: A merch program has a legitimate four-state story (bought green and bare → green in service → red plain with TACOMBI.COM → red folk-art) that no competitor can tell, and the model can render all four from one mesh because geometry transfers and paint does not. But it is also a trap: any single frame that blends states is a fake, and the owner has ruled on this. If the program ever wants a 'timeline' piece, it must render four separate paint states, never one composite.

findings.claim: The vehicle's body is a 1963 split-screen T1, while the Mexican 'combi' that carries the working-class meaning is the later Puebla-built bay-window T2. The bus straddles the two readings and the program has to choose deliberately.
findings.evidence: SPEC.md §0.1: "a **1963 Volkswagen Type 2 (T1)**"; rev-14 owner settlement: "**The windscreen is a SPLIT screen — two panes, centre divider.**" Against WebSearch (VW media, Wikipedia, heritagepartscentre): "Production of the Combi … began in October 1970 at the Volkswagen plant in Puebla" / "VW de Mexico produced the first Type 2s for their home market on October 1st 1971, in Puebla"; the first Mexican VW plant was "Xalostoc, State of Mexico in 1962, under the name PROMEXA".
findings.why_it_matters: The split-screen T1 is exactly the silhouette the hippie merch market has worn out; the T2 bay-window is the shape a Mexican would picture on hearing 'combi'. So the vehicle cannot escape the surf-bus silhouette by shape alone — it escapes it only through the CONVERSION and the signage. That is a design conclusion, not a preference: the anti-derivative content is everything above the sill and behind the cab door, not the profile.

findings.claim: There is an organised audience for this object in Mexico, independent of the US nostalgia market.
findings.evidence: WebSearch result title, Yucatán Magazine: "National Combi Day brings together fans of the classic VW Bus". Also from search summaries: "Out of production for more than four years, the boxy minivan has cult status in Mexico. Owners like to trick them out and paint them in bright colors"; "The Vocho … and the Combi … are two of the most iconic symbols of Mexico's car culture." Brazilian production of the Type 2 ended 2013-12-31 after "more than 3,500,000".
findings.why_it_matters: The bright-colours, tricked-out Mexican combi culture is the register Tacombi's actual bus belongs to — hand-painted, over-decorated, working. That is the reference pool to mine for art direction, and it is largely unmined by the English-language merch market.

findings.claim: Public sources contradict each other on the founding facts, and the repo's SPEC is the better authority.
findings.evidence: The fontsinuse-derived search summary states Tacombi was "founded in a VW Kombi bus in Mexico City in 2005"; CNBC/NBC/tacombi.com say the bus was BOUGHT in Mexico City and the taqueria opened in Playa del Carmen; SPEC.md §0.1 records "Opened 6 February 2006" and "bought in Mexico City in 2006, driven through the Yucatán". Note SPEC's own internal tension: it says bought in 2006 and opened 6 Feb 2006.
findings.why_it_matters: Do not let a merch caption or a program document inherit a web-summary date. If any deliverable states a year, it must state the one SPEC grades S, and SPEC's own buy-date/open-date proximity should be checked against Tacombi's page before anything is printed.

ceilings: EVERY FIRST-PARTY TACOMBI PAGE IS EGRESS_BLOCKED IN THIS CONTAINER. WebFetch returned `EGRESS_BLOCKED` for www.tacombi.com, shop.tacombi.com and fontsinuse.com. Everything I report from those three sites is a WebSearch SUMMARY of them, not verbatim first-party text. The single exception is the 'our story' passage, which is already quoted inside SPEC.md §0.1 and graded S there — I corroborated it against search summaries but did not re-read the page.

I NEVER SAW ANY TACOMBI MERCHANDISE ARTWORK. I have product NAMES and COPY fragments from search summaries only. I cannot say whether the bus appears on any current Tacombi product, what the 'Tacombi Icon' actually depicts, what the colourways are, or how the wordmark is locked up on a garment. That is the single biggest gap in this brief and it is one browser session away from being closed by the owner.

TACOMBI'S OFFICIAL BRAND COLOURS, LOGO LOCKUP AND ANY BRAND GUIDELINES ARE UNESTABLISHED. I found 'yellow and green' attributed to Vista Hermosa packaging in one search summary and nothing else. No hex values, no primary/secondary structure, no clear-space rules. Do not let any program document state a Tacombi brand colour.

THE TYPEFACE LIST IS SECOND-HAND AND THE AGENCY ATTRIBUTION IS UNVERIFIED. 'Cooper Black / ITC Bauhaus Pro Bold / Davida (Louis Minott, 1965) / ITC Bookman', 'PAG Revolucion / Roberta / Balloon Drop Shadow / Brush Script', and the credit to 'Brandibble' all come from a search summary of a fontsinuse page I could not open. Plausible and mutually consistent, but I did not see the page or the specimens.

I DID NOT LOOK AT THE REFERENCE PHOTOGRAPHS MYSELF. Every livery and fitting detail I list is read out of SPEC.md, LEDGER_rev51.md and STATE.md — the project's own records, which carry their own grades (M measured / S source / R reported / E inferred). I quoted the grade where SPEC prints one. This is transcription of the record, which CLAUDE.md warns against; treat the inventory as a pointer to those files, not as an independent measurement.

VW TRADEMARK EXPOSURE IS NAMED, NOT RESOLVED. I established that VW enforces and that 'officially licensed' VW bus tees exist. I could NOT establish whether Tacombi holds any licence, has an arrangement, or has ever been challenged — nor whether depicting a specific, real, modified vehicle owned by the depicting company changes the analysis. This is a question for the owner and, if it goes anywhere, a lawyer. It is not legal advice.

WHETHER PHOTOREAL CGI IS ITSELF A SATURATED MERCH CATEGORY IS UNRESOLVED. Search confirmed 'car render' is a live tag on Redbubble and that automotive CGI is a mature commercial practice, but returned nothing on whether photoreal classic-car prints read as fresh or as stock. So I cannot tell you whether the program's core deliverable is differentiated BY BEING a render. My finding is that it is differentiated by its SUBJECT, not by its technique.

THE PROVENANCE OF A 1963 T1 IN MEXICO IS NOT RECOVERABLE FROM WHAT I COULD REACH. Puebla Type 2 production starts 1970/71 (T2); the 1962 Xalostoc plant results I found concern the Beetle. Whether this bus was imported, or assembled somewhere else, or is simply a used import — unestablished.

NO ACCESS TO TACOMBI'S INSTAGRAM, ITS BRAND FILM, OR ANY VIDEO. NEXT_CONTEXT_PROMPT_rev15.md records the same blocks at rev 15 ('Instagram retrospective post (robots-disallowed)' and 'the brand film on YouTube (rate-limited over six attempts)') — so this is a standing, not a transient, ceiling. The owner can open either in a browser in seconds.

I DID NOT SURVEY COMPETITOR TAQUERIA / FOOD-TRUCK BRAND MERCH AT ALL. The trope list is VW-bus merch only. Whether the food-brand-merch category has its own clichés (which it certainly does) is unexamined.

THE TROPE LIST IS QUALITATIVE. I can name the recurring moves and quote listing copy for each, but I have no counts, no share-of-market, and no ranking of which trope is most saturated. 'Recurring' is what I can defend; 'most common' is not.

AUDIT_rev43.md's STICKER dimension survives only as 8 table rows and one ceiling paragraph, all HARD-TRUNCATED at fixed character widths. Every `fix location` cell is EXACTLY 120 characters; every per-dimension ceiling paragraph is EXACTLY 900 characters; the finding cells cap at 150.
findings.evidence: Measured by parsing AUDIT_rev43.md: the 8 rows beginning `| \`sticker\`` have finding-cell lengths 142/149/114/149/121/118/131/150 and fix-cell lengths 120/120/120/120/120/120/120/120. Three findings end mid-sentence: `...and "nothing but the bus"`, `...the fifth casualty is the silver s`. All eight §5 ceiling paragraphs (COUNTER, WHEELS, ROOF, TAIL, OPTICS, TYPOGRAPHY, BRANDING, STICKER) are 900 chars exactly; STICKER's ends `...and the orderings are the s`. findings.why_it_matters: OPEN_FINDINGS.md F18 says "The full art-direction specification already exists and is NOT owed: AUDIT_rev43.md §5" and LEDGER_rev44.md says "the spec is not owed... What is missing is the ASSET, not the specification." Both are OVER-STATED. What survives is eight headline SENTENCES and their figures. The REASONING (why 18°, why 0.159 m, what scale the millimetres are quoted at, which symbols to draw from) is gone. A creative team is inheriting eight assertions, not a spec — so they are far freer than the register implies, and they should not treat the truncated rows as a completed brief.

findings.claim: The eight surviving STICKER findings, verbatim, with their severities. These are the whole of the surviving art direction.
findings.evidence: AUDIT_rev43.md §2. SEVERITY 5 — (1) "VIEWPOINT — 18° front three-quarter from the serving side, eye height 1.55 m. The face and the flank are provably exclusive; choose the flank." (2) "OWNER QUESTION, MULTIPLE CHOICE — the cab door. Open at 49° opens a 0.306 m void that only a PERSON fills in the reference, and "nothing but the bus"[TRUNCATED]" (3) "THE FLANK IS A TRIPTYCH AND THE WORDMARK SITS IN A 1.51 m GAP WITH 63 mm OF CLEARANCE. Do not "enrich" the middle." SEVERITY 4 — (4) "THE SACRIFICE RULE IS ALREADY MEASURED: 48 of the flank's 66 gold components carry 2.29% of the ink and every one lands under 0.40 mm. Delete all 48." (5) "DIE-CUT OUTLINE — bridge the underbody with the cast shadow, and let no feature narrower than 0.159 m touch the cut line." (6) "LINE WEIGHT AND THE DEPTH BUDGET — three strokes, a 0.15 mm floor, four contact lines, and DO NOT outline the paisley." (7) "THE SUN — it must NOT be a rayed disc. The vehicle already carries ELEVEN radial bursts, and it is the drawing's only light source." SEVERITY 3 — (8) "COLOUR SEPARATION — the whole vehicle is ONE 70° hue wedge plus four neutrals. Seven inks printed; five if cut, and the fifth casualty is the silver s[TRUNCATED]". The additional figures appear only in the §5 ceiling: "the 48-of-66 gold-component rule, the 0.159 m minimum cut feature, the 0.30 mm louvre pitch, the 0.58 mm menu lettering... the triptych 29.08 / 0.29 / 27.86, the eleven radial bursts, the single 70° hue wedge".
findings.why_it_matters: Item 7 is the one that most constrains any sun-bearing artwork and it is a GOOD constraint, independently checkable: the vehicle is already full of radiating motifs (cal_gen.starburst, the mural rosettes, the hubcap rings, the headlamps, the wheel spokes), so a rayed-disc sun competes with the subject. Item 6's "DO NOT outline the paisley" and item 3's "do not enrich the middle" are compositional restraint rules that transfer to ANY artefact — poster, apparel, packaging — not only to F18.

findings.claim: TWO of the sticker's figures are INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCIBLE from live source, so the 48-of-66 sacrifice rule is real and not an assertion.
findings.evidence: folk_gen.py: `#     66 components carry 0.2826 m2 of gold.` and `COMP_HIST = [ ("<100", 24, 0.42), ("100-300", 21, 1.32), ("300-1k", 3, 0.55), ("1k-3k", 10, 5.96), ("3k-10k", 5, 7.32), ("10k-30k", 0, 0.00), (">30k", 3, 84.43)]`. The first three bins sum to 24+21+3 = 48 components carrying 0.42+1.32+0.55 = 2.29 % of all gold — exactly the audit's "48 of the flank's 66 gold components carry 2.29% of the ink". The triptych is also live: `DOOR_GOLD = 29.08`, `OPEN_GOLD = 0.29  # X +0.872 .. -0.62`, `REAR_GOLD = 27.86  # X -1.45 .. -2.007`, and `COMP_TOP = {1: 47.8, 2: 73.7, 3: 84.4, 5: 87.8, 10: 93.5}` — the largest THREE components carry 84.4 % of the gold.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the strongest transferable fact in the whole sticker record and it is a general graphic-design principle already measured on THIS vehicle: three blobs carry 84 % of the ornament and forty-eight carry 2.3 %. Any stylisation at any scale — sticker, screen-print, embroidery, animation cel, 20-frame logo reveal — can delete the 48 and lose almost nothing. It is a measured licence to simplify, not a restriction.

This recovered clause is the single most actionable sentence in the sticker record and it has been missing from the brief for 32 revisions.

findings.claim: HALF OF THE F18 ASSET ALREADY EXISTS AND IS BUILT, TESTED AND REFUSING-ON-FAILURE: deliver.py produces the die-cut silhouette, a shadow-separated layer set, and a web set. It is a working promotional-asset pipeline, not a stub.
findings.evidence: deliver.py header: "deliver.py -- BUILD THE PROMOTIONAL ASSET PACKAGE FROM AN RGBA RENDER SET." It writes four subdirectories `("full_frame", "trimmed", "layers", "web")`; `trimmed/` is "The same images cropped tight to the artwork", `layers/` writes `combi_%s_no_shadow.png` and `combi_%s_shadow_only.png`. Its own view catalogue names the use case: `"front": ("front_elevation", "Flat front elevation. Symmetrical -- good for centred layouts, stickers and icons.")` and `"side": (... "Best for banners, letterheads and anything where the vehicle sits in a strip.")`. OPEN_FINDINGS.md F161 records the same: "THE MECHANICAL HALF OF F18 — THE DIE-CUT SILHOUETTE — NOW EXISTS... `deliver.py`'s `trimmed/` output is exactly that geometry". findings.why_it_matters: For any 2D artefact — sticker, poster, apparel, packaging, motion — the hard part (silhouette on transparency, shadow as a separable layer with correct partial alpha, six catalogued camera angles) is DONE and verified. A cartoon/vector track can take `layers/*_no_shadow.png` as the flat-fill reference and `layers/*_shadow_only.png` as the occlusion pass, which is literally the rev-39 technique clause. Nobody needs to re-solve alpha, shadow separation or cropping.

opportunities.idea: THE CREAM IS THE #1 LOOK DEFECT AND NOBODY HAS IT ON A LIST. Render the weathering ladder on hero34f and put it to the owner as a picture. I cropped out/r75_side.png and out/r75_hero34f.png and looked (rule 1): the upper body — the single largest surface in every frame, 2.08e6 px² and item 2 of 16 in visibility_budget — reads as blotchy galvanised zinc or concrete primer, not cream paint. It is not a colour error, it is AMPLITUDE: t1_mats carries `MOTTLE_AMP = float(os.environ.get("T1_MOT_AMP", 0.55))` plus FADEV plus the WEATHER group's dust chain, all landing on the same panel. The record tracks the red (F240) and the gloss (F239) and has no row at all on the cream's blotch. RECIPE, 5 frames, all hero34f, ~28 min sequential: L0 shipped (rendered TWICE — rule 49, the floor); L1 `T1_MOT_AMP=0.18 T1_W_DLO=0.15`; L2 `T1_WEATHER=0.35`; L3 `T1_WEATHER=0`. Read gloss_compare's HEADROOM and flank_compare's cream bands on each, then crop the flank at 3x and look. This is F230(b)'s owner question — 'look like new' (rev 61) vs SPEC §3's WEATHERED lock — arriving with a picture instead of a paragraph, which is the only form it can be asked in.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Every switch already exists and ships with an ablation; T1_WEATHER was built at rev 69 precisely so this question could be asked and it has never been used to ask it. And F230 says this collision gates the delivery render and cannot be answered by code — so it needs a rendered A/B and the question tool, not another revision of measurement.

opportunities.idea: REBUILD THE GLOSS TARGET ON THE RIGHT STATISTIC. gloss_compare prints two numbers and the project has been steering on the wrong one. Live on out/r75_hero34f.png: render spread 0.495 vs photo 1.202 (0.412 of it, bar 0.60) AND render HEADROOM 0.120 vs photo 1.008 — an 8.4x miss. Headroom is 'how far the brightest 1 % sits above the median', i.e. IS THERE A HIGHLIGHT. Spread is the whole distribution's width, which any bright environment COMPRESSES by lifting the paint's floor. F239's own table shows it: env 21.0 + coat 0.55 buys headroom 0.118 → 0.181 (+44 %) while spread falls 0.412 → 0.399, and rule 44 correctly killed it against the spread bar. That was the right call under that guard and the wrong guard for the question — rule 56 running in the opposite direction. RECIPE: 3 hero34f frames, ~17 min. G1 `T1_REFLENV=21.0 T1_BODY_COAT=0.55 T1_BODY_COATRGH=0.045`; G2 as G1 plus `T1_BODY_RGH=0.120`; G3 as G1 on top of whichever weather rung wins above (they interact — a chalky base cannot glint whatever the world does). Publish headroom AND spread on every row, state in advance that spread will fall, and say plainly that headroom is now the objective and why.

It DUCKS the two defects that gate everything else: an elevation wants flat even light, so the gloss deficit stops being a defect and becomes a convention; and the side elevation does not contain the nose roundel at all, so the owner's ninth report is out of frame. It also lands exactly on Tacombi's existing merch voice — 'purpose-built', 'expo', 'monument' — where a warm nostalgic hero would not.
opportunities.why_this_asset: The ortho cameras are the most-exercised code in views() (side appears 27 times across LEDGER_rev66..75) and are the only views whose framing cannot drift. STATE.md is machine-written, so the callouts regenerate rather than rot — the one artefact in this whole program whose figures cannot go stale.
opportunities.effort: One `rear` render (~6 min) plus layout. No model work, no lighting work, no gate cleared.

opportunities.idea: A PASS KIT — `passes.py`, ~80 lines, modelled line-for-line on matte_tap(). The tree has ZERO pass infrastructure: `grep -n "pass_index\|use_pass" *.py` returns nothing outside studio.py's denoiser config. Add on the view layer: use_pass_z, use_pass_normal, use_pass_position, use_pass_diffuse_color, use_pass_diffuse_direct/indirect, use_pass_object_index, use_pass_material_index, and use_pass_cryptomatte_object/material. Drive pass_index from build.py's own ASSIGN list — the `A(obj, key)` calls give 17 stable material keys (paint, chrome, chrome_d, glass, tyre, rubber, dark, steel, bumpercream, countercream, capred, capwhite, lidmural, lidsign, roundelred, amber, bulb) so the ID islands map to design intent for free. Write each through a File Output node copying matte_tap's colour contract EXACTLY — `color_management='OVERRIDE'`, `view_transform='Raw'`, look 'None', gamma 1.0 — because a File Output slot otherwise inherits AgX/Punchy and every pass comes back S-curved. Z and crypto go to OPEN_EXR_MULTILAYER (Z is metres and unbounded; a normalised PNG depth must state its near/far in the filename or it is a number with no ruler). WATCHED KILL: render the rig with the vehicle deleted and confirm object index is identically zero — matte_tap already did exactly this negative control and got cover 0.0000 % against 0.267 mean alpha, a factor of 3900.
opportunities.why_this_asset: matte_tap is a proven tap with a written contract and a measured null (tap-ON sits inside the render-to-render noise: off_A/off_B max 40 mean 0.2465, off_A/ON max 41 mean 0.2458). Every mistake this kit could make has already been made and documented once. And passes are the substrate for every NPR idea below — no passes, no toon, no line, no relight.
opportunities.effort: ~1 revision to write and guard. Budget for Blender 4.5 socket-name drift — matte_tap's own docstring records that class of breakage on the CA node ('socket names moved between versions; address by index').

opportunities.idea: CEL SHADING IN THE COMPOSITOR, NOT IN THE SHADER — and this is the recipe that keeps the artwork. Cycles has no ShaderToRGB (that is EEVEE), so the standard toon trick is unavailable. Instead: render diffuse_direct + diffuse_indirect + diffuse_color as separate passes, reconstruct lighting L = dir + ind, QUANTISE L to N bands through a stated ColorRamp (start N=3: terminator at 0.28, mid at 0.55, key at 1.0), then multiply the banded L back by diffuse_color. You get a true cel look driven by the real rig, and every piece of artwork — the folk art, the mural, the Señor script, the Calidad burst — survives untouched inside diffuse_color, which is the whole subject. Entirely 2D once the passes exist, so it iterates in numpy in seconds instead of 5.5 min a look. Add the line pass on top (below) and you have flat colour + drawn line, which is precisely the owner's own rev-39 technique clause.
opportunities.why_this_asset: The vehicle's identity is 90 % ARTWORK on a simple body. Any toon route that overrides materials (clay_all(), a material_override) throws away the identity and leaves you with a grey van. Splitting lighting from albedo is the only route that keeps both. And 45 material datablocks with 43 bound means diffuse_color is dense and correct everywhere.
opportunities.effort: ~2 days on top of the pass kit. Pure numpy; no Blender in the loop after the one pass render.

opportunities.idea: LINE EXTRACTION, THREE ROUTES, NOT EQUIVALENT — and the second one is the one that matters. (a) FREESTYLE: works with Cycles, real stylised strokes, silhouette/crease/border edge types, renders to its own pass. Best line quality, slowest; on 229 objects and 366,490 faces budget minutes. Crease angle 30–40°, NOT lower — T1_body is shade_smooth and a low angle will find the subdivision. (b) GREASE PENCIL LINE ART MODIFIER: fast, and it produces EDITABLE VECTOR STROKES that export to SVG. That is what a designer actually needs for vinyl, screen-print, embroidery or a die-cut. Nothing in this tree has ever tried it and it is the single highest-value NPR route here. (c) COMPOSITOR EDGE on the normal and Z passes: Sobel on normals catches creases, Sobel on Z catches silhouette and occlusion contours; pure 2D, cheapest to iterate, but line weight is uniform and it cannot taper. Prototype with (c) tomorrow; ship (b). BONUS, and it is sitting in the tree unused: t1_mats' WEATHER group already contains `Bevel -> DotProduct -> EDGE(1-dot)` — a shader-space curvature detector. probe_rev55_truenorm.py establishes it collapses on the smooth-shaded shell against `Normal` and that `True Normal` is the fix. Tap that with `True Normal` through an Emission AOV and you get a curvature/edge pass with no new machinery — probe_rev54_aov.py is a working precedent for driving Emission off an arbitrary internal socket by graph walk.
opportunities.why_this_asset: The mesh is clean enough to trust a line renderer: 0 non-manifold body edges, 229,489 quads against 1,040 tris and 5,186 ngons, cutters rolled back none. Line extraction fails on dirty meshes; this one is not dirty.
opportunities.effort: (c) one day. (b) 2-3 days including an SVG export path. (a) an afternoon to configure, then wait.

opportunities.idea: THE FIVE-PLATE SCREEN-PRINT SEPARATION, WITH THE SACRIFICE ALREADY MEASURED. AUDIT_rev43's colour finding: 'the whole vehicle is ONE 70° hue wedge plus four neutrals. Seven inks printed; five if cut.' And folk_gen.py's own component census gives the simplification rule with a number under it: `COMP_HIST` sums to 48 of 66 gold components carrying 0.42+1.32+0.55 = 2.29 % of all gold, every one under 0.40 mm at the sticker's scale, while `COMP_TOP = {1: 47.8, 2: 73.7, 3: 84.4, ...}` says the largest THREE carry 84.4 %. So: red / cream / gold / dark / silver, five plates, delete 48 gold components and lose 2.3 % of the ink. That is a measured licence to simplify that applies to ANY flat artefact — poster, tee, tote, tile, animation cel — not only to F18's die-cut.
opportunities.why_this_asset: It is the rarest thing in a design program: a stylisation decision with a measurement under it, computed on THIS vehicle's own artwork rather than asserted. And it is independently reproducible from live source — folk_gen.py's COMP_HIST reproduces the audit's figure exactly, which is more than most numbers in this repository can say.
opportunities.effort: Half a day to script the separation off the ID + artwork passes.

opportunities.idea: LIGHT THE BULBS AND MAKE THE FRAME AT DUSK. F144 stands: 'THE FESTOON BULBS READ AS PEARLS, NOT LIGHTS.' In ref_side.jpg the drip-rail string reads as a CONTINUOUS glowing amber line tracing the vehicle's whole silhouette — nose to tail on the rail, wrapping the rear roof dome, edging the raised lid, and along the tail board. STATE.md has `bulb_string | 1`, `tb_bulbs | 1`, `tb_bulbflex | 1`, and t1_mats has an `emissive(name, colour, strength=8.0, ...)` builder. Push the emission above post.py's BLOOM_THR = 0.94 so it actually flares, drop the key (T1_KEY), and you have the vehicle's only self-luminous element carrying an entire mood the project has never rendered. That drawn line of light is the most reusable graphic the object owns: it describes the whole outline in one stroke, works down to a favicon, and animates for free.
opportunities.why_this_asset: The emitters exist, the bloom threshold exists in both the compositor chain and post.py, and T1_BULB_STR / T1_BULB_BASEV are already ablation switches. Nothing needs modelling.
opportunities.effort: ~1 day of lookdev plus 2-3 test frames. State clearly it is a MOOD arm, not the delivery frame — F191 and F193 both still hold.

opportunities.idea: FIX THE GROUND SO THE VEHICLE STOPS FLOATING — the owner explicitly licensed this. F259, rev 71: 'Relight the studio and fix the ground if necessary.' Two levers, both built. (1) T1_SHADOW ships at 9.0 and lands G1 on 0.8729, deliberately chosen as the WEAKEST of four photographed readings (0.3049 / 0.7300 / 0.6950 / 0.8713) because moving to a mean whose sd is a third of its value is laundering. That reasoning is right for a FIDELITY target and wrong for a picture: for a wall print, ladder T1_SHADOW toward the strongest reading and watch C3 (the backdrop-level control that fires at T1_SHADOW=20). (2) post.py's `--backdrop headroom` (the live default, contra its own stale docstring) gives the sweep tone instead of paper — measured corners 246.043 against pure white. Together they stop the bus being a cut-out.
opportunities.why_this_asset: An owner ruling that names the ground specifically, plus two shipped switches with watched controls on both. The one constraint travelling with F259: DO NOT change RED — that is the option he declined.
opportunities.effort: ~20 min render for a 3-rung shadow ladder. No source edit.

opportunities.idea: MATERIAL WORK, RANKED BY VISIBLE RETURN PER HOUR, ALL NAMED. (1) THE SCRIPT HAS NO DARK KEYLINE — measured on tex/senor.png: of alpha>200 pixels the 1st-percentile luma is 168.3 and the fraction below luma 80 is 0.0000, while SPEC §3 requires "SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow". Silver on red without a keyline is why the wordmark reads flat and washed in r75_side.png. It is a script_gen.py edit + hand regeneration (script_gen is NOT called by build.py), it is a REPLICATION requirement under SPEC §10.10's hard bar rather than a taste call, and it is the cheapest visible improvement in the whole inventory. (2) tex/lidmural.png is CROPPED AT THE BOTTOM (F74a) — flowers sliced mid-bloom, side columns truncated, where ref_side.jpg shows a board framed on all four sides. That board is the loudest, most saturated graphic in every single frame I looked at; it carries the composition, and it is clipped. lid_gen.py, hand regen. (3) The 5 constant-roughness materials are amber/glass/lens/reflector/ruby — and in my nose crop the headlamps read as chrome BUTTONS, not glass. Give `lens` a roughness field and a real IOR. (4) In ref_playa_34.png the headlamp bezels read BRASS/GOLD; the render is cold white chrome. Ground that first with photometry.py on a painted window before touching the `chrome` material.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Three of the four are texture-generator edits with no geometry risk and no gate exposure, on the three highest-contrast artwork surfaces in the frame. The keyline in particular is a defect the render is faithfully reproducing from the asset — the shader is innocent.
opportunities.effort: (1) half a day. (2) half a day. (3) one day. (4) grounding first, then half a day.

opportunities.idea: AN EXPORT PATH — `T1_SAVE` EXISTS AND IS IN NO HANDOFF DOCUMENT. build.py carries `if os.environ.get("T1_SAVE"): bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(...)` and `grep -c T1_SAVE` returns 0 in the brief, HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md, START_HERE.md and OPEN_FINDINGS.md alike. There is no glTF/USD/OBJ export anywhere in the tree. Add `export.py` writing glTF (web viewers, AR, Spline/Three.js) and USD (any DCC), driven off the same build. The owner's stated goal is 'a 3d render from which to build promotional material from' and what exists is a 2D PNG generator — a designer today cannot relight it, re-angle it, or hand it to anyone.
opportunities.why_this_asset: 0 non-manifold body edges and 43 of 45 materials bound means the mesh would survive an export. The risk is UVs and the 5,186 ngons, which is a real unknown — triangulate on export and check the artwork's UV islands survive, because the folk art is BOX-projected in the shader and box projection does NOT export.
opportunities.effort: ~2 days, and the box-projection problem is the whole job: the flank artwork must be baked to a UV set before any exchange format can carry it.

opportunities.idea: HDRI / ENVIRONMENT LOOKDEV AS A SEPARATE ARM, kept strictly out of the delivery path. W6 ('keep studio', given twice) and F92 ('Playa DEPRIORITISED, NOT CANCELLED') both stand, and F57 records that T1_SCENE=playa renders NO VEHICLE — a dark cylinder on a grey plane, cause unknown. So the environment route through build.py is broken and the environment route through playa_env.py is parked. The route that IS open and works: T1_ALPHA=1 gives an RGBA frame whose contact shadow lives in PARTIAL ALPHA (F159, measured on the proof frame: 184 distinct alpha values, 57.9 % transparent / 25.5 % opaque / 16.6 % partial, partial pixels carrying RGB (0.9,0.8,0.7)) and composites correctly over any colour, photograph or texture. That is a compositing route, not a relight, and it should be described as one — the paint will not pick up the background's colour.
opportunities.why_this_asset: T1_ALPHA is built and guarded by three verify_clone rows, but no LEDGER contains the string, so it is a rev-62 result carried forward thirteen revisions unexercised. Re-run it before anyone promises it.
opportunities.effort: One render to re-validate T1_ALPHA (~6 min). The honest ceiling on composited work is that it is a cut-out on a background, not a lit object in a scene.

opportunities.idea: MOTION, WITH THE ONE CONSTRAINT THAT DECIDES ITS ENTIRE VOCABULARY: THIS BUS DOES NOT DRIVE. Tacombi's own account, graded S in SPEC §0.1: 'The engine was scrapped, transmission sold, seats swapped for cooking equipment, and the roof was reeled back to produce a taco serving stand.' A driving loop, a rolling wheel, motion blur on the tyres — every one contradicts the brand's own telling, and the transverse tread rev 74 shipped will never be seen turning. The correct vocabulary is the SERVING vocabulary and the geometry already supports it: the roof lid rises (lid_main, lid_board, lid_rail ×2, lid_strut ×2), the tail board props (tail_board, tail_board_stay), the rear hatch swings (glass_rear at a declared +64.00° about its hinge, with seal_rear tracking to 0.045°), the bulbs ignite. Arrive → drop the counter → raise the lid → light the string. Four beats, all built, all posable from constants that already exist.
opportunities.why_this_asset: The hinge poses are parameterised, not baked — REAR_OPEN_DEG, TB_TILT_DEG, the strut geometry — so an animation is a keyframe on a constant, not new modelling. CEILING: there is NO owner ruling on animation anywhere in the record; `grep -rli animat` across every .md/.txt returns one file and one hit, a panel persona description. An animation program is ungrounded and must be put to him.
opportunities.effort: A test beat (lid rise, 48 frames) is ~4.5 hours of CPU at preview settings — and never fan out Blender, it is CPU-bound on 4 cores.

opportunities.idea: A LENS DECISION, because f/8 at 15 m is not a photographic choice. hero34f is 78 mm at ~15.2 m, f/8; dof_limits puts the hyperfocal around 25 m, so essentially everything is sharp and the DoF is decorative. Two directions worth one frame each: LONG — 135-180 mm from further back on the same axis, which compresses the counter against the flank and makes the object read heavy and near; or SHORT-AND-CLOSE — the `counter` view's 90 mm at f/6.3 from 4 m, where the near counter lip goes soft and the mural board sits behind it. `aim()` already reads T1_FSTOP from the environment, logs measured near/far/hyperfocal on every frame, and sets 9 aperture blades with an 11° rotation so out-of-focus speculars are 9-sided rather than perfect discs — the machinery for real bokeh is there and unused.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Lens character is the cheapest thing that separates a photograph from a product plate, and this rig already reports its own DoF numerically so the choice is measured rather than felt.
opportunities.effort: 2 frames, ~11 min. `T1_FSTOP` is an env var; the lens needs one dict entry in views().

blockers: F191 AND F193 BOTH STAND: no delivery render until the owner says so — 'Keep holding — fix the emblem first' (rev 64), reaffirmed rev 65 as 'I don't think the bus is ready yet.' Everything above must be framed and labelled as LOOK-DEVELOPMENT, not as the delivery frame. That is not a workaround, it is the honest description: 'get the bus ready' is exactly what look-dev is for.

THE LARGE-FORMAT CHAIN IS 8-BIT END TO END AND NOTHING DOCUMENTS IT. studio.setup_render sets `color_depth = '16'`, and both stitch.py and post.py read through `Image.open(...).convert("RGBA")`, which has no 16-bit RGB path and truncates silently (rule 58 / F263). deliver.py at least declares its 8-bit choice; stitch.py and post.py declare nothing, so the loss is undeclared exactly where print grading needs the depth. For a gallery print this is the real blocker and it is not the model's fault. FIX: route both through photometry.read_png and write 16-bit. Until then cap the honest claim at 8-bit.

post.py DESTROYS ALPHA — measured: RGBA in (colortype 6), colortype 2 out. `rgba[..., :3]` at the top, 3-channel array at the save. So optics and cut-out are mutually exclusive today: you can have bloom/CA/vignette/grain OR a silhouette, never both from this repo. It is ~5 lines to carry the alpha through and re-attach at save, and post.py's docstring nowhere warns that it is happening.

hq_render.py DOES NOT SET T1_FX=0 (`grep -c T1_FX hq_render.py` → 0) while hero.py, the chain it replaced, forces it off with the docstring 'Per-strip optics band at the seams'. studio.composite_on_white defaults `on = optics and _envi("T1_FX", 1)`. So unless the operator exports T1_FX=0 by hand, a strip render applies compositor optics PER STRIP and then post.py applies a second numpy pass on the stitch. No document names this step. Export it by hand until hq_render is fixed.

NOTHING ABOVE 1600x1100 EXISTS ON DISK AND `out/` IS UNTRACKED. The highest resolution ever rendered is 4320x2880 (rev 15, via hero.py's PAD chain, worst seam z=2.75); the current MARGIN chain is proven only at 3840x2640 (rev 57, 106.8 min for one view). Both frames are gone and the model has changed for 18-60 revisions since. F192 says 3840 is NOT the target and the exact dimension is still open — do not re-ask it cold, ask once a medium is named.

deliver.py WRITES THE FULL 21-FILE PACKAGE PLUS ITS README EVEN WHEN IT REFUSES — only the zip is withheld. And that README misstates the model in four ways: it says the emblem 'READS AS AN X ... reported six times' (it is his NINTH report, and I cropped out/r75_front.png and out/r75_hero34f.png and looked — it renders as a V over a W in a ring, not an X), and it claims the tyres have no tread (shipped rev 74, F308) and that two roof loudspeakers are missing (retired as a geometry item, F309). It is the ONLY document in the repo written for a non-technical reader and it is the one the owner would read. Do not send a package until that string is fixed.

T1_ALPHA HAS NOT BEEN RUN SINCE REV 62 — no LEDGER_rev*.md contains the string. Every frame in out/ today is RGB with no alpha (IHDR colortype=2) and deliver.py correctly refuses them: 'CONTROLS: 4 checked, 1 FAILED -- C1' / 'PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY'. The one capability the owner's compositing ruling turns on is one env var away and thirteen revisions unexercised. Re-validate before promising it.

CYCLES ON 4 CPU CORES: ~5.5 min a frame at 1600x1100/96 spp. DO NOT FAN OUT BLENDER — two instances make both slower. Render sequentially from one backgrounded script (setsid, not a bare nohup &) and analyse in the foreground. And DO NOT EDIT SOURCE WHILE A QUEUE RUNS.

lid_gen.py AND script_gen.py ARE NOT CALLED BY build.py. Two of the four cheapest material fixes I name (the script's missing keyline, the mural's bottom crop) live in those generators, so the texture must be regenerated BY HAND or the render silently uses the old file.

THE PLAYA / ENVIRONMENT ROUTE IS BLOCKED TWO WAYS: F92 says do not re-propose playa_env.py (DEPRIORITISED, NOT CANCELLED — do not act on it either), and F57 records that T1_SCENE=playa renders NO VEHICLE, 'a dark cylinder on a grey plane', reported and not diagnosed. The composite route (T1_ALPHA + deliver.py) is the one that works.

THE EMBLEM'S WEIGHT IS CLOSED TO RE-ASKING — F314, rev 74: 'I can't tell them apart — stop tuning the weight.' Recorded UNRESOLVED, not settled. And F156 is a live trap for anyone tuning the wordmark: flank_compare's `Senor` row now scores a DELIBERATE DEPARTURE (F157, 'Bright silver, same as Tacombi'), so 'improving' it toward the photograph would silently reverse an owner ruling and no gate would say so.

NO OWNER RULING ON ANIMATION EXISTS ANYWHERE. `grep -rli animat` across every .md and .txt returns one file, PANEL_rev61.md, and its single hit is a persona description. Any motion program is ungrounded and has to be put to him rather than inferred.
first_moves: Launch ONE background render queue, sequential, before reading anything else — the machine is idle while you think. `nohup setsid env T1_SUB=1 T1_PREVIEW=hero,low34,counter,rear T1_PFX=g0 T1_RX=1600 T1_RY=1100 T1_SAMP=96 /tmp/blender/blender -b -P build.py > /tmp/g0.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &`. Four cameras this project has never rendered, ~22 min. `grep -c Saved: /tmp/g0.log` must be 4.

While it runs, read the two numbers that already exist and nobody is steering on: `python3 gloss_compare.py out/r75_hero34f.png` prints render headroom 0.120 against the photograph's 1.008 on the same line as the spread it is graded on. Write down that HEADROOM is the highlight statistic and SPREAD is the distribution width that any bright environment compresses. That reframing is the whole gloss argument and it costs one command.

Crop out/r75_side.png at 3x on the cream between the belt and the gutter, and look. Do not measure first. The upper body reads as blotchy zinc, not paint; that is MOTTLE_AMP=0.55 plus FADEV plus the WEATHER dust chain landing on the largest surface in every frame, and it has no register row.

When the queue drains, run the weathering ladder as ONE queue: L0 shipped twice (the two-render floor — rule 49), then `T1_MOT_AMP=0.18 T1_W_DLO=0.15`, then `T1_WEATHER=0.35`, then `T1_WEATHER=0`, all hero34f, ~28 min. Name the frame on every reading you publish.

Then the gloss ladder on top of whichever weather rung wins — they interact, a chalky base cannot glint whatever the world does. `T1_REFLENV=21.0 T1_BODY_COAT=0.55 T1_BODY_COATRGH=0.045`, then the same plus `T1_BODY_RGH=0.120`. Publish HEADROOM and SPREAD on every row and say in advance that spread will fall, so it is not read as a regression.

Put ONE question to the owner with the question tool, as multiple choice, with the crops attached: the weathering ladder as four labelled crops of the same panel, asking which cream is his bus. That is F230(b) — 'look like new' against SPEC §3's WEATHERED lock — arriving as a picture. It gates the delivery render, it cannot be answered by code, and it has been open since rev 61.

Write `passes.py`. Copy matte_tap()'s colour contract verbatim — color_management='OVERRIDE', view_transform='Raw', look 'None', gamma 1.0 — or every pass comes back through AgX/Punchy. Drive pass_index off build.py's ASSIGN list so the ID islands carry the 17 material keys. Z and cryptomatte to OPEN_EXR_MULTILAYER. Watch the kill: render the rig with the vehicle deleted and confirm object index is identically zero.

Prototype the cel look purely in numpy off diffuse_direct + diffuse_indirect + diffuse_color: band the reconstructed lighting to three levels, multiply back by diffuse_color. No Blender in the loop, seconds per iteration, and the folk art / mural / script / Calidad all survive inside diffuse_color. Then add a Sobel line off the normal and Z passes on top.

Try the Grease Pencil Line Art modifier on the `side` ortho and export SVG. Nothing in this tree has ever done it, the mesh is clean enough to trust (0 non-manifold body edges, 229,489 quads), and editable vector strokes are what every downstream 2D artefact actually needs.

Fix tex/senor.png's missing dark keyline in script_gen.py and REGENERATE BY HAND — script_gen.py is not called by build.py. Measured: of alpha>200 pixels the 1st-percentile luma is 168.3 and the fraction below luma 80 is 0.0000, against SPEC §3's 'SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow'. Cheapest visible improvement in the inventory and it sits inside SPEC §10.10's replication bar, not outside it.
Before ANY package leaves the building, fix deliver.py's READ_ME_FIRST manifest string — four wrong claims about the model, in the one document written for the owner to read.
what_would_embarrass_us: Shipping a frame and calling it the delivery render while F191 and F193 hold. He has held it four times (rev 58, 64, 65, 65) and volunteered the third one. Label every frame LOOK-DEV.

Sending the owner a promo package whose README tells him his emblem 'READS AS AN X ... reported six times' when it is his ninth report and it renders as a V over a W — I cropped the frame and looked — and which lists as open two things rev 74 shipped and retired. Running the delivery chain without exporting T1_FX=0 by hand and getting vignette + grain banding at every strip seam, then a SECOND optics pass laid over it by post.py. hero.py's docstring warns about exactly this and hq_render.py has no such switch.

'Fixing' the wordmark to score better against the photograph and silently reversing F157's 'Bright silver, same as Tacombi.' flank_compare's `Senor` row scores a deliberate departure (F156) and reads improvement as convergence — no gate in the tree will catch it.

Steering the gloss work on gloss_compare's SPREAD, watching it fall, and reporting a regression on a change that added the highlight. Or the reverse: quoting a headroom gain without publishing the spread beside it. Publish both, every row, named frame.

Quoting a single figure for 'the photograph's red'. probe_rev71_red.py prints the prohibition directly above the number: 'the photograph's red G/R is 0.0149 .. 0.0344, a 2.3x span. DO NOT QUOTE A SINGLE FIGURE FOR IT.' And ref_nolita_front34.jpg is 22.6 % clipped in R, so it cannot be a target at all.

Rendering an A/B and calling a change visible with no two-render floor under it. The render is not deterministic: ~2.04 % of pixels move >8 levels on hero34f, and the floor is LOCAL — 4.37 % inside the front-wheel box, 7.90 % on the body. Rev 74 called a localised change visible and its own box-local floor refuted it.

Producing an animation of this bus DRIVING. Tacombi's own account, graded S: 'The engine was scrapped, transmission sold.' The tread rev 74 shipped will never be seen turning, and a rolling wheel contradicts the brand's own origin story.

Toon-shading by overriding materials and handing back a grey van. clay_all() clears every material slot; the artwork IS the vehicle's identity. Split lighting from albedo instead — the cel look must ride on top of diffuse_color, not replace it.

Publishing a depth pass as a PNG with no stated near/far. Z is metres and unbounded; a normalised depth with an unstated range is a number with no ruler. And any File Output slot that does not force view_transform='Raw' inherits AgX/Punchy and writes an S-curved 'linear' pass — matte_tap's docstring records exactly that trap.

Promising a designer they can take the model into another DCC. There is no export path (`grep` for export_scene/gltf/usd_export returns nothing), and the flank folk art is BOX-PROJECTED in the shader — box projection does not export. It must be baked to a UV set first, and whether the 5,186 ngons and the UV islands survive that is unknown.

Quoting verify_clone.sh's total as fidelity. Its own verdict block says otherwise: not one of its rows compares the model to a photograph. Four things do — flank_compare, gloss_compare, probe_rev70_tyre, probe_rev69_fitpose — and all four fail.
