expert_plans.discipline: Animation direction — short-form brand motion, loops and title design

opportunities.idea: THE OPENING — the five-hinge sequence, and it is the flagship. The vehicle shut and unlit; then, in order, the roof lid rises on its two struts, the tail board props out, the rear hatch swings up, and last the bulb string ignites nose-to-tail along the drip rail. Final held frame IS the delivery hero. Cut it stepped, 8–12 fps, with holds — not a 24 fps tween. Three of the four hinges are already free parameters (T1_LIDDEG, T1_REAR_OPEN, T1_TB_TILT) and the lid's two prop struts already re-solve their feet from the angle (t1_shell.py: 'DERIVED FROM THE POSE, not typed, so the foot follows the angle'), so the struts stay attached at every rung without any rig work.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Tacombi's own origin account, graded S in SPEC.md §0.1, says 'The engine was scrapped, transmission sold, seats swapped for cooking equipment, and the roof was reeled back.' This vehicle cannot drive. Its entire motion vocabulary is OPENING — it is a building that unfolds, not a van that arrives. The bbox goes from roof-at-tail 1.988 m to 3.046 m tall with the lids up (studio.py's own note on the hero fit) — a 53% silhouette change, which is an enormous graphic gesture. No competitor asset can make this move because no stock VW bus has these hinges.
opportunities.effort: MEDIUM. Blocked on one line: LID_W is coupled to the lid angle as 1/sin (see blockers) — fix that and the sequence is a bash for-loop over env vars. 12 stepped poses ≈ 12 renders ≈ 1.2 h at 1600×1100/96spp (my arithmetic on the brief's ~5.5 min/frame plus the carriers' ~20 s build). Per-bulb ignition needs the bulb objects kept separate before t1_detail's join([ob, flex], 'bulb_string').

opportunities.idea: THE SIGNWRITER — the bus paints itself. Open on the plain red Nolita-state body: no folk art, no script. The gold folk art then paints on in the signwriter's real working order — the three big masses first, then the tendrils, then the rosettes — and the silver Señor Tacombi lockup lands last. Hold. Loop or cut to black.
opportunities.why_this_asset: This is the best idea in the brief and the repo already holds the ordering as a MEASUREMENT rather than an invention. folk_gen.py carries the connected-component census off ref_side.jpg: COMP_TOP = {1: 47.8, 2: 73.7, 3: 84.4, 5: 87.8, 10: 93.5} — three components carry 84.4% of the gold — and COMP_HIST shows 48 of 66 components carry 2.29% between them. So 'largest first' is a measured painting order, not a guess. It is also the brand's literal origin: a $3,000 green bus, missing three windows, cut open and hand-painted. And it dramatises the one thing the owner calls a hard bar — 'ABSOLUTE REPLICATION OF ALL ARTWORK' — by showing the artwork being made.
opportunities.effort: MEDIUM-HIGH. A crude version ships today: T1_W_ART is a live global opacity on the folk-art alpha (t1_mats.py: '_math(nt, MULTIPLY, amask.outputs[0], W_ART, ...)'), so 0→1 gives a whole-flank fade-on for ~10 renders. The GOOD version needs folk_gen.py to emit a per-component paint-order channel into swirl.png's alpha (it already computes the components), then a threshold sweep. ~1–2 h render for 12–16 steps. The script lands last as a separate texture and needs no new work.

opportunities.idea: THE HINGE LOOP — the scroll-stopper. 2-second seamless loop. Orthographic side elevation, flat ground, no environment. The roof lid goes up and comes down. Nothing else in frame moves. Ease out on the rise, a 2–3 frame overshoot and settle at the top (that reads as the strut clacking home), a slower fall.
opportunities.why_this_asset: The market research names BLUEPRINT/technical-diagram as a standing stock category (Dreamstime sells 'Vw Van Blueprint' by the sheet) — this is that trope beaten at its own game, because it is a real orthographic elevation that MOVES and the shape change is huge. The 'side' view is already defined and is the cheapest to render: studio.py has it as ortho 5.90 with lens=None, so no DOF and no perspective solve. It is also the view flank_compare and every side-frame probe already reads, so it is the best-instrumented camera in the tree.
opportunities.effort: LOW once LID_W is unblocked. 16 frames ping-ponged = 8 unique renders ≈ 45 min. This is the cheapest genuinely good thing on the list and should be the first sequence attempted.

opportunities.idea: THE FILAMENT — the bulb string as the brand's animated logo. The vehicle's outline drawn purely as its own light: the festoon running the drip rail, wrapping the rear roof dome, edging the raised lid and the tail board. Loop: the line ignites as a CHASE nose-to-tail, holds lit, flickers once on the inverter, repeats. Works down to favicon size because it is a single continuous stroke describing the whole silhouette.
opportunities.why_this_asset: The art-direction survey reads it in the photographs as 'an unbroken warm orange-gold bead' — a drawn line, not a row of pearls — and the register already carries the render-side defect: F144, 'THE FESTOON BULBS READ AS PEARLS, NOT LIGHTS'. It is the vehicle's only self-luminous element, so it is the only thing that can carry a whole frame at night or at 32 px. Three of its photographed runs exist (drip rail, tail board via tb_bulbs) and the material is already emissive at strength 9.0 with a live ablation, T1_BULB_STR.
opportunities.effort: MEDIUM. The chase requires the bulbs NOT be joined into one object with one material — currently t1_detail does join([ob, flex], 'bulb_string') and t1_mats binds a single M['bulb']. Keeping ~115 bulbs as instances with a per-bulb driver is a contained build change. Fixing F144 (lights, not pearls) is a shading job that this animation makes worth doing.

opportunities.idea: THE SHUT / OPEN HARD CUT — no tween at all. Two frames. Same camera, same light, same everything: closed and dark, then open and lit and dressed. One frame of each, cut on a beat, ping-ponged. Post it as a 1-second loop.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Transformation reads hardest when you show only the endpoints — the viewer's eye does the animating. It also costs two renders instead of a hundred, which on a 4-core CPU-bound Cycles machine with no fan-out allowed is the difference between shipping this week and not. And the closed state has NEVER BEEN BUILT OR LOOKED AT in 76 revisions, so this concept doubles as the reveal of a genuinely new picture of the vehicle.
opportunities.effort: VERY LOW — 2 renders, ~12 min — once LID_W is unblocked. Do this the same afternoon as the LID_W fix, as its proof.

opportunities.idea: THE FOUR LIVERIES — a history reel on a locked camera and a locked pose. Green-and-bare (conversion, no headlamps, bare rims), green-in-service, red-plain Nolita, red folk-art Playa. Cut, don't dissolve; four held frames on a beat.
opportunities.why_this_asset: LEDGER_rev51.md verifies all four states as the SAME architecture in different paint, and CLAUDE.md rule 11 makes the split exact: geometry transfers between reference frames, paint and artwork do not. So one mesh renders all four legitimately, and only paint changes. Nobody else can tell this story — it requires being the brand that owns the bus. It is also the safest possible use of rule 11 because the camera and geometry are provably identical across cuts.
opportunities.effort: HIGH on artwork, LOW on render. Only the red folk-art state is textured today. The green states need paint authored (ref_workshop.jpg gives a green reading; the artdirection pass measured #5E7A50) and the Nolita chalkboard lid is a whole 4K asset. Budget this as an artwork revision, not a render one. WARNING: any single frame that blends two states is a fake, and the owner has ruled on this.

opportunities.idea: THREE-BAY RHYTHM — the triptych cut. The three serving apertures are the vehicle's signature and they are equal (STATE.md: 'bay widths 0.516 0.515 0.516'). Cut a three-up: one bay per beat, something landing in each in turn — a menu card, a bulb, the galley behind. Or a single locked side frame with a light travelling bay to bay.
opportunities.why_this_asset: The three holes ARE the logo. SPEC.md §0.1 records why they exist: the $3,000 donor bus was 'missing three of its windows', graded S, with the inference that this is why the show side became three hatches. Three equal openings on a strict 0.5155 m pitch is a ready-made rhythmic grid — it is the only regular repeat on the vehicle apart from the louvres, and rhythm is what a loop needs. Everything behind them is built: ~30 gal_* objects, plancha, counter, menucards×3.
opportunities.effort: LOW-MEDIUM. Needs no new geometry. Needs the interior lit — F45 (roof-aperture interior) and F15 (unlit roofed body) are both ungated and unmeasured, so the inside may render dead. Render one side frame first and look through the bays before committing.

opportunities.idea: THE PLANCHA — steam as the only organic motion in an otherwise rigid, hand-built world. Everything on this vehicle moves in hard straight lines about hinges. One soft, drifting element off the griddle is the entire emotional payload, and by contrast it will read enormous.
opportunities.why_this_asset: The plancha is BUILT (STATE.md object inventory: plancha | 1) and sits inside the galley behind the apertures, so a wisp reads THROUGH the three bays — tying the steam to the signature feature rather than floating beside it. It is also the only cue in the whole vocabulary that says food rather than vehicle, on a brand whose product is tacos.
opportunities.effort: HIGH and it is genuinely new work. There is no volumetric anywhere in the tree — grep for smoke/volume across the .py files returns only unrelated hits. This is a new Blender volume domain plus a per-frame simulation, which breaks the 'one build per frame' model entirely (a sim needs continuity between frames). Do this only after a .blend-based pipeline exists. Flagged as the most expensive idea here, and worth it later.

opportunities.idea: THE SPEC PLATE — a stepped orthographic rotation that is NOT a turntable. Cut, don't spin: front elevation, side elevation, rear elevation, and back, each held for a beat, each labelled in the brand's own catalogue voice. All four ortho cameras already exist in studio.views() ('front', 'side', 'rear' at ortho 3.55/5.90/3.55).
opportunities.why_this_asset: Tacombi's actual merch voice is deadpan leisure-outfitter catalogue copy — 'purpose-built, all-weather knit beanie', 'The Seaside Expo Tote', 'Monument T'. A spec plate is that voice in motion. Cutting between true orthographic elevations is also a distinctly designerly move that a turntable is not: a turntable says 'someone had a 3D file', a cut ortho sequence says 'someone measured this'. Which, after 76 revisions, is true.
opportunities.effort: LOW. 3–4 existing views, one render each ≈ 20 min. But note only 4 of the 14 defined views have been exercised in ten revisions — 'rear' has ZERO rendered-file mentions across LEDGER_rev66..rev75, so render it and LOOK before designing to it.

opportunities.idea: EXPLODED CONVERSION — not an exploded vehicle. Float out ONLY the parts that are not VW: the counter and its brass nosing, the tail board with its bulbs and stay, the mural lid, the bobble fringe, the menu cards, the folk art as a floating decal layer. The bus stays whole underneath. Reassemble on the beat.
opportunities.why_this_asset: The generic exploded-diagram move is a stock category and should be avoided; this is its anti-derivative form. It shows exactly the delta between a 1963 Type 2 and a taqueria, which is the only content on this object that is proprietary. It also sidesteps the VW trademark exposure the market research raises (VW enforces against merchandise and claims the bus shape itself), because every floating part is Tacombi's, not Volkswagen's.
opportunities.effort: MEDIUM. Requires per-object transform animation, which means a .blend-based pipeline (T1_SAVE) rather than a rebuild-per-frame loop — the parts are separate objects already (counter, counter_nosing, counter_top, tail_board, tail_board_stay, tb_bulbs, lid_board, fringe×3, menucard×3), so once there is a .blend this is straightforward keyframing.

opportunities.idea: THE 1963 STING — a 1–2 second title/end card built on the empty chrome plate frame. Push in on the tail, the plate reads 1963, cut. Or use it as the number in a countdown/anniversary piece.
opportunities.why_this_asset: SPEC.md §4 records it verbatim: 'chrome number-plate surround on the engine lid reading "1963", empty'. It is built (STATE.md: plate | 1, plate_digits | 1). The owner literally date-stamped the object on its own back — it is a free, true, human detail that requires no invention and no new asset, and it gives any piece an ending.
opportunities.effort: VERY LOW. One or two renders through a new tight camera on the tail. There is no such camera defined; 'detail_f' is the nose. Adding a 'detail_r' to studio.views() is a few lines.

opportunities.idea: THE COUNTER AS THE TYPE RAIL — a title system, not a shot. The counter is the strongest horizontal in every frame and overhangs the body (STATE.md: 'length excludes opened lids: 4.317 with them, 4.065 without', the counter among what projects). Its brass nosing is a hard bright line. Wipe titles on and off along it; hang lower thirds from it; let the bulb string be the underline above and the nosing the baseline below.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Motion design needs a grid that comes from the subject rather than from a template, and this object supplies three: the counter's horizontal, the bulb line's traced silhouette, and the three-bay vertical rhythm. The brand also has an existing type family to sit in — Cooper Black / Davida / ITC Bookman per the fontsinuse research — so nothing needs inventing. CEILING: that type attribution is a search summary of a page that was blocked, and Tacombi's brand colours and lockup are unestablished. Confirm before setting anything.
opportunities.effort: LOW — this is 2D layout over existing frames, not render work. It can be prototyped today against the four r75 frames in out/.

opportunities.idea: SOUND-IMPLIED MOTION — a craft rule for every item above. This vehicle has a specific sound design and none of it is an engine: the metallic clack of a strut seating, the creak of the tail board's stay taking load, the tick of a festoon inverter, the plancha hiss, a crowd. Animate to those events even in a silent loop: the lid should overshoot 2–3° and settle (that IS the clack), the stay should take load with one frame of hitch, the bulbs should catch raggedly rather than fade up together.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Because the engine is gone, the usual automotive audio bed is unavailable and a silent, mechanical, hand-built vocabulary is what is left — which is far more distinctive. Every one of these events maps to a part that is BUILT and solved: lid_strut×2 whose feet already re-solve from the pose, tail_board_stay whose landing is measured at z 1.5780, and the bulb string. The overshoot is free — it is one extra rung on the angle sweep.
opportunities.effort: FREE. It is a choice about spacing, not new geometry. Costs 2–3 extra frames per hinge event.

opportunities.idea: THE ANTI-LIST — moves to refuse by name, so nobody spends a revision on them. (1) The turntable: generic, and at ~5.5 min/frame the single worst value on the list. (2) Any driving/rolling/wheel-spin shot: contradicts the brand's own origin account. Rev 74 shipped a transverse tyre tread; that tread will never be seen turning, and that is correct. (3) Sunset silhouette with palms and surfboards — the market's single most saturated VW-bus trope. (4) A rotating rayed-sun background. (5) Motion blur on the wheels.
opportunities.why_this_asset: AUDIT_rev43's sticker spec already forbids the sun as a rayed disc for a reason that is stronger in motion than in stills: 'The vehicle already carries ELEVEN radial bursts, and it is the drawing's only light source.' A spinning ray field would compete with the Calidad starburst, the hubcap rings, the headlamps and the mural rosettes simultaneously. And the hippie/flower-power reading is a live hazard specifically here, because this bus genuinely carries hand-painted florals — they need the counter, the hatches and the Spanish signage in frame to read as Mexican folk art rather than as Woodstock.
opportunities.effort: FREE, and it saves render-days.

blockers: THE ROOF LID CANNOT BE ANIMATED AS BUILT — THIS IS THE HEADLINE BLOCKER AND IT IS ONE LINE. t1_shell.py: `LID_W = (LID_X0 - LID_X1) / LID_ASPECT / math.sin(math.radians(LID_OPEN_DEG))`. The lid's WIDTH is coupled to its opening angle as 1/sin, because the width was solved from the photographed projected width. I computed the sweep from the live constants (LID_X0 0.9640, LID_X1 -1.0700, LID_ASPECT 1.7130): 76 deg -> 1.2237 m (shipped), 60 -> 1.3711, 45 -> 1.6792, 30 -> 2.3748, 20 -> 3.4717, 10 -> 6.8379, 5 -> 13.6238, and 0 deg is a ZeroDivisionError. So a naive T1_LIDDEG sweep does not close the lid — it INFLATES it to longer than the bus and then crashes. FIX: freeze LID_W at its shipped 76-degree value as a constant, with an ablation (say T1_LID_WCOUPLE=1) restoring the coupling, plus a guard row that the built panel's width does not move when the angle does. Watch the guard FAIL on the coupled build before believing it. This is the single change that unlocks the flagship sequence, the hinge loop and the shut/open cut.

THE LID'S 'LEANS OVER THE COUNTER' ASSERT WILL FIRE NEAR THE CLOSED END. t1_shell.py: `assert _top.co.y > LID_Y_HINGE + 0.010` with `_top = max(main.data.vertices, key=lambda v: v.co.z)`. Near 0 degrees the panel is flat and the topmost-vertex pick is degenerate, so which vertex wins is float ordering. The guard is correct for a POSED still and wrong for a SWEPT sequence. It needs a closed branch that says so in the row's own label, not a relaxation — and per this project's rules a re-base needs the cause named plus a companion row.

THE RENDER FLICKER FLOOR IS ALREADY MEASURED AND NOBODY HAS EVER READ IT AS FLICKER. The record's own figure: the render is not run-to-run deterministic, floor ~2.044 % of pixels differing by >8 levels on hero34f at 1600x1100/96 spp, and 'take the floor IN THE BOX YOU ARE READING: it is 4.37 % inside the front-wheel box and 7.90 % on the body' (F308). For a still that is noise. For a SEQUENCE that is the per-frame flicker amplitude, and 7.90 % on the large flat body panels is a visible boil. OpenImageDenoise IS on (studio.py: `use_denoising = True`, `denoiser = 'OPENIMAGEDENOISE'`, RGB_ALBEDO_NORMAL) but it is spatial-only with no temporal pass, so the low-frequency blotch shifts every frame. Mitigations: raise samples (expensive), fix the Cycles seed, or LEAN IN — an 8-12 fps hand-drawn cadence genuinely wants a boiling line, and that is the elegant escape. Decide deliberately; do not discover it in dailies.

post.py's GRAIN SEED IS FIXED AT 7 — `def grain(srgb, amount=1.0, sigma=0.0042, seed=7, ...)` then `rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)`. Identical grain on every frame is not film grain, it is a dirty gate: it will sit static over moving imagery and instantly betray a still-image pipeline. FIX: seed from the frame number. judge_set.sh calls post.py per view with no concept of a frame, so the frame index has to be threaded in. One-line change, but nothing in the tree has a frame index today.

THERE IS NO ANIMATION INFRASTRUCTURE AT ALL. Zero hits for frame_start / keyframe_insert / render(animation=True) across the .py files (the one frame_set is in an unrelated probe). Every hinge BAKES its rotation into vertices (`_hinge`, `_hinge_y` rewrite v.co in place), so today one pose == one full rebuild. Budget, my arithmetic on the brief's ~5.5 min/frame and the carriers' ~20 s SUB=1 build: ~5.8 min per animated frame. 24 fps x 3 s = 72 frames ~= 7.0 h; 12 fps x 3 s = 36 frames ~= 3.5 h; a 12-pose stepped sequence ~= 1.2 h. And CLAUDE.md forbids fanning out Blender ('It is CPU-bound; two instances make both slower'), so none of this parallelises on this 4-core machine.

THE REAL UNLOCK IS T1_SAVE AND IT IS IN NO HANDOFF DOCUMENT. build.py's only persistence is `if os.environ.get("T1_SAVE"): bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(...)`, and the pipeline researcher found `grep -c T1_SAVE` returns 0 in the brief, HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md, START_HERE.md and OPEN_FINDINGS.md alike. Save one .blend, parent each lid to an empty on its already-computed hinge axis instead of baking the rotation, and you get real keyframes, one build instead of N, per-object animation (the exploded conversion), and a file another artist can open. It also converts the flicker problem, because a single scene can render an actual frame range. This is the highest-leverage engineering item in the whole brief and no document names it.

NO ALPHA IN THE OUTPUT, AND THE OPTICS CHAIN DESTROYS IT. Every frame in out/ is colortype 2 (no alpha); T1_ALPHA exists and is guarded but has not been run since rev 62 (no LEDGER contains the string). Worse for motion: post.py reads `rgba[..., :3]` and saves 3 channels, so a sequence can have optics OR a cut-out, never both. Any motion piece meant to composite over colour, footage or type needs that resolved first.

NO CAB DOOR, NO OPENABLE COUNTER, NO PEOPLE, NO VOLUMETRICS. The door shut lines are GAPS CUT IN THE SHELL, not separable panels — opening one means separating the panel along the existing gap and building an inner return and shut face that do not exist, plus AUDIT_rev43's 0.306 m void 'that only a PERSON fills in the reference'. The counter is a fixed cantilever with no folded state in the record; a deploy animation would be an INVENTION (permissible for a derived artefact, per the papel-picado precedent, but never for the model). No human figures and no smoke/volume anywhere in the tree.

THE OWNER'S HOLD IS LIVE AND APPLIES TO THE DELIVERY RENDER. F191 'Keep holding — fix the emblem first' and F193 'We need the bus to be ready before investing seriously in the render' both stand at rev 76, and the emblem is his ninth report. There is ALSO no owner ruling on animation anywhere in the record — grep across all .md/.txt finds one hit for 'animat', a persona description in PANEL_rev61.md. So motion is unmandated territory: propose it as a distinct artefact, say plainly that it is not the held delivery render, and put it to him.

THE EMBLEM IS IN EVERY FRONT-FACING FRAME AND IT IS WRONG. P2 reads 0.8528 against P1b's ceiling 0.9465; the defect is the strokes' arrangement (photo-only/model-only inside the ring 73/178, 'near balanced, so the ink AMOUNT is right and the ARRANGEMENT is wrong'). Any loop that pushes in on the nose publishes a mark the owner has rejected nine times. Compose around it: the side elevation, the counter, the tail and the three bays are all clean; the nose is not.
first_moves: FIX THE LID_W COUPLING FIRST — nothing else moves until it does. Freeze LID_W at its shipped 76-degree value (1.2237 m, computed from the live constants), add T1_LID_WCOUPLE=1 to restore the old behaviour, and add a verify row that the built panel's width is unchanged across at least three angles. WATCH THE ROW FAIL on the coupled build before trusting it pass. In the same edit, give the near-closed case a branch in the 'leans over the counter' assert with the cause named in the row's own label.

THEN RENDER THE VEHICLE SHUT AND LOOK AT IT: `T1_SUB=1 T1_LIDDEG=2 T1_REAR_OPEN=0 T1_PREVIEW=side,hero34f T1_PFX=shut ... build.py`. This picture has never existed in 76 revisions and every transformation concept in this brief depends on the closed silhouette being good. Two frames, ~12 min. Crop it and look — do not read a gate and call it done.

SHOOT THE HINGE LOOP AS THE FIRST SEQUENCE: 8 unique side-elevation renders at T1_LIDDEG = 2, 12, 28, 44, 58, 68, 74, 76, ping-ponged to 16 frames. ~45 min of render. It is the cheapest genuinely good thing available and it proves the whole stepped-pose method. Assemble at 10 fps and look at the boil before deciding the cadence.

ADD T1_TRUNK_OPEN. TRUNK_OPEN_DEG = 0.0 is a hardcoded constant on a lid whose lateral hinge is already solved and printed ('trunk lid: separated %dv, hinge (x %.4f, z %.4f) lateral'). Two lines gives a fourth hinge and a fourth beat in the opening sequence, and it costs nothing to build.
SEED post.py's GRAIN FROM THE FRAME NUMBER. One line plus threading an index through judge_set.sh. Do it before any sequence is graded, or every frame carries an identical dirt plate.

MEASURE THE FLICKER AS FLICKER: render the SAME pose twice and diff, then render two ADJACENT poses and diff, both in the same painted window on the body panel — where the recorded floor is 7.90 %. That tells you how much of the frame-to-frame change is the animation and how much is the denoiser boiling. Publish both figures side by side; a difference with no floor under it is not a measurement.

RUN T1_ALPHA=1 ONCE AND LOOK AT THE RESULT. It has not been exercised in thirteen revisions and every compositing concept depends on it. Confirm the frames come back colortype 6 and that deliver.py's C1 goes green. Note in the same breath that post.py discards alpha, so decide which chain a motion piece uses.

PROTOTYPE T1_SAVE. `T1_SAVE=/tmp/combi.blend T1_SUB=1 ... build.py`, then open it and try parenting lid_main + its two lid_struts + lid_board to an empty on the hinge axis (y = LID_Y_HINGE = -0.5450, z from roof_z at the lid midpoint). If that holds, the whole rebuild-per-frame economy collapses and real keyframing becomes available. This is the highest-leverage experiment on the list.

SPLIT THE BULB STRING BEFORE JOINING IT. In t1_detail, keep the per-bulb objects addressable rather than collapsing them with join([ob, flex], 'bulb_string'), so the chase and the flicker become drivable. Keep the joined path behind an ablation so nothing regresses.

TEACH folk_gen.py TO EMIT A PAINT-ORDER CHANNEL. It already computes the 66 connected components and their sizes (COMP_TOP, COMP_HIST). Write the component rank into an unused channel of swirl.png/swirl_b.png so a threshold sweep paints the art on largest-first. Regenerate by hand — folk_gen and lid_gen are not called by build.py, so a stale texture ships silently.

PUT IT TO THE OWNER AS MULTIPLE CHOICE, WITH FRAMES ATTACHED, USING THE QUESTION TOOL: show the shut frame beside the open frame and ask which of three motion pieces he wants first — the opening sequence, the signwriter, or the hinge loop. There is no ruling on animation anywhere in the record, so this is unmandated work and he has never been asked. Do NOT re-ask the emblem weight (F314), the nose (F214/F215), or the papel picado (F18).

BEFORE ANY OF IT SHIPS: correct deliver.py's READ_ME_FIRST. It is the only document in the tree written for a non-technical reader, it is what the owner would read, and it currently states the emblem 'READS AS AN X ... you have reported six times' (it is his ninth, and it renders as a V over a W), that 'the tyres have no tread' (shipped at rev 74, F308), and that 'two loudspeakers on the roof are missing' (retired as a pose, F309). Any motion package built on deliver.py inherits that document.
what_would_embarrass_us: SHIPPING A LOOP WHERE THE LID GROWS AS IT CLOSES. LID_W = 1/sin(angle) means a naive T1_LIDDEG sweep inflates the mural board from 1.22 m to 3.47 m at 20 degrees and 6.84 m at 10 — longer than the vehicle. It would render clean, pass VERIFY's other rows, and look like a cartoon accordion. This is exactly the class CLAUDE.md's first rule exists for: render it, crop it, and look at it, before and after.

SHIPPING A DRIVING SHOT. The engine was scrapped and the transmission sold, in Tacombi's own words, graded S in the project's own SPEC. A rolling wheel or a drive-by is not merely a cliche — it is a factual lie about the object, told by the brand about itself, and anyone at Tacombi who knows the origin story will see it immediately.

THE BOIL. Rendering 72 frames without ever checking temporal stability, then discovering the body panels shimmer because OpenImageDenoise is spatial-only and the record's own measured 7.90 % on-body per-frame difference was sitting there the whole time, read as a stills floor and never as flicker. Seven hours of render, unusable.
STATIC GRAIN. post.py's seed=7 applied identically to every frame reads as dirt on the lens. It is the most amateur possible tell and it is one line.

A NOSE-FORWARD HERO LOOP THAT PUSHES IN ON THE EMBLEM. It is the owner's NINTH report, P2 is ~0.09 short of its own control ceiling, and the objective still has no legibility term. Putting a slow push-in on the one mark he has rejected nine times is the single worst compositional choice available.

A SUNSET, PALMS, A SURFBOARD, OR A ROTATING RAY-BURST BACKGROUND. Every one is a named, documented saturation point in the VW-bus merch market, and the flowers on this bus make the hippie misread actively likely rather than merely possible. The sun-as-rayed-disc is additionally forbidden by the project's own sticker spec for a reason that is stronger in motion: eleven radial bursts already compete for it.

BLENDING TWO LIVERY STATES IN ONE FRAME. Folk art from Playa on a Nolita-plain body, or the chalkboard lid over the flower mural. Rule 11 is explicit, the owner has ruled on it, and it has already killed F99, F100 and F140. In a cut sequence it would be one careless keyframe.

CLAIMING A SEQUENCE IS THE DELIVERY RENDER. F191 and F193 both stand and the owner has held it four times. Offer motion as a distinct artefact, say so in the same sentence, and do not let a nice loop become an implicit argument that the bus is ready.

PROMISING 'THE WHEELS AS DRAWN IN THE EARLIER CARTOON VERSION'. That artefact does not exist in this repository — 793 commits, no matching path, no matching blob, and the only pointer is START_HERE.md's `/areas/tacombi-combi-sticker.md`, a directory that does not exist here. Promising to match a drawing nobody in the session can see is promising against a memory. Say so plainly and show him options instead.

SHIPPING A PACKAGE WHOSE README UNDER-REPORTS HIS OWN COMPLAINTS. deliver.py writes its full 21-file package and its READ_ME_FIRST to disk EVEN WHEN IT PRINTS 'PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY' — only the zip is withheld. A folder that looks finished, claiming transparent backgrounds it does not have, describing an emblem defect that changed twelve revisions ago, handed to the owner, is the worst single outcome available from this pipeline.

QUOTING ANY FRAME FROM out/ WITHOUT NAMING IT. out/ is untracked and starts empty; both r75_side.png and r75b_side.png exist and the ledger records a re-render. This project has already attributed a reading to a frame a probe could not have read (F320c, F322). In a sequence with dozens of frames that failure mode multiplies.

expert_plans.discipline: Apparel graphics — screen-print, DTG and embroidery production

opportunities.idea: THE THREE-HATCH MARK — the brand's most ownable graphic is not the bus, it is the hole in the bus. Three equal rounded apertures, drawn straight from live constants and needing no render at all: t1_shell.py `BAY_W = 0.5155  # equal, measured`, `Z_SILL, Z_HEAD, BAY_R = 1.3720, 1.7750, 0.0550` and `BAY_CX = (0.6720, 0.0470, -0.5980)`. That gives three 515.5 x 403.0 mm apertures (1.279:1), 55.0 mm corner radius, on centre pitches of 625.0 and 645.0 mm — so the pillars between them are 109.5 mm and 129.5 mm, NOT equal. Draw it at that asymmetry. Prints as ONE ink at any size from a 12 mm woven label to a 500 mm back print; embroiders as three satin-outlined rectangles at 45 mm left chest with a 1.4 mm column, comfortably above the 1.2 mm satin floor.
opportunities.why_this_asset: SPEC.md §0.1 grades it S that the donor bus was 'missing three of its windows' and Wolos 'figured out how to cut open the Tacombi' — the signature feature is the conversion, not the vehicle. It carries no VW trademark, no emblem (so it is not gated by F191), no folk art (so nothing collapses under reduction), and the slightly unequal pillars are the detail that makes it read as observed rather than styled. It is the single strongest answer to 'what would a person wear who does not want to be a walking advert': a mark only a customer decodes.
opportunities.effort: Half a day in Illustrator. Zero pipeline, zero model work, zero render.

opportunities.idea: THE HUBCAP BULLSEYE for caps, beanies and left chest. Four concentric bands in the exact brand logic: black tyre / cream painted rim dish / red domed cap / cream VW. Live sizes: t1_detail.py `CAP_EMBLEM_D = 0.3170 * CAP_D` with `CAP_D = 2 * (CAP_R + 0.0025)`, and STATE.md publishes the badge at `4 rings R 0.043429 (= CAP_EMBLEM_D/2)` — so CAP_D = 274 mm and the badge 86.9 mm, i.e. the badge is 31.7 % of the cap. Embroider the whole bullseye at 55 mm on a cap front: rings at 55 / 37 / 17 mm, four needles, roughly 6-8k stitches. Replace the inner VW with a plain disc, a '63', or nothing.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Four concentric bands of the four brand colours, repeated four times around the vehicle — a ready-made roundel that is not a logo. It is also the one motif whose proportions are locked in source as a RATIO rather than a literal, so it scales without a decision. CEILING, and it must be carried: STATE.md says in terms 'hubcap badge is SELF-CONSISTENCY ONLY -- CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC has never been compared to a frame; see PHOTOS_WANTED item 7.' Draw the ring proportions from the model, and draw the inner glyph from a photograph or drop it.
opportunities.effort: One day to draw, one digitising session (~£80) for the DST. No render.

opportunities.idea: GARMENT-AS-BODY-COLOUR: let the shirt be the red. Print only cream + gold + dark maroon onto a red garment, or only red + gold + dark onto a natural/ecru garment. Measured off the shipped masters, this is a genuine 3-screen job: tex/swirl.png's ink resolves to 4 quantised bins covering 95 %, and those are two inks — gold #D0B010 at 68.9 % (+8.6 % darker gold, +5.9 % pale gold = ~83 %) and dark maroon #501010 at 14.6 %. tex/nose.png is the same two at 81.6 / 18.3. My own count of a whole flat-art vehicle lands on seven spot inks (red, cream, gold, dark maroon, silver, black, white) — which independently reproduces AUDIT_rev43.md's truncated row 'Seven inks printed; five if cut'. Removing the body field removes both the largest screen and the ink-slab edge that makes a shirt look like a sticker.
opportunities.why_this_asset: The vehicle is a two-tone object split on the belt line, so the garment can carry one whole tone for free. It cuts a 7-colour job to 3-4, halves the setup cost, deletes the heaviest ink deposit, and produces a soft hand with no white under-base. It also sidesteps the project's worst measured defect entirely: you never have to choose a printed red that matches a render whose red images salmon (flank_compare live on out/r75_side.png: render median (196,81,67) against the photograph's (158,16,6)).
opportunities.effort: One day of separation work per design. No model work.

opportunities.idea: ONE ROSETTE, embroidered. folk_gen.py's measured inventory gives their real sizes: `FLANK_ROSETTES` areas 3632 / 3564 / 1838 / 1816 / 1524 / 1435 / 1076 / 740 mm² — the largest is a ~68 mm equivalent circle on the vehicle. Embroider it AT ROUGHLY LIFE SIZE, 45-60 mm, left chest or cap back: two colours (gold satin petals, dark maroon centre ring), ~9k stitches. At life size every stroke is 8-15 mm on the vehicle and therefore 8-15 mm on the garment — nothing is reduced, nothing collapses.
opportunities.why_this_asset: This is the only way the folk art survives on a garment, and it is measured why. On the shipped 4096² tile (box-projected at `mp.inputs["Scale"] = (0.2600, ...)`, i.e. a 3.846 m period = 0.939 mm per tile pixel) the gold's stroke width runs p10 2.66 mm / p50 13.15 mm / p90 45.07 mm on the vehicle. Reduce the whole flank to a 280 mm chest print (1:14.5) and the median stroke becomes 0.91 mm and the p10 becomes 0.18 mm — below any reliable positive line. Print one motif at 1:1 and the problem does not exist.
opportunities.effort: One day to isolate and redraw, one digitising session.

opportunities.idea: THE BULB LINE as a drawn path. The lit festoon is the one element that describes the entire silhouette in a single stroke — it runs the drip rail, wraps the rear roof dome, edges the propped tail board and outlines each aperture. Extract it as ONE continuous vector path and use it four ways: a single-ink print at any size; a chain-stitch or bean-stitch embroidery (a running stitch, so no 1.2 mm satin floor applies); a printed side-seam or hem stripe; and the animation asset that ignites, chases and flickers for free.
opportunities.why_this_asset: OPEN_FINDINGS F144 records the render fails at exactly this — 'THE FESTOON BULBS READ AS PEARLS, NOT LIGHTS' — so the render is the wrong source and a drawn line is the right one. A one-colour continuous path is the most scale-robust graphic form there is: it works at 12 mm on a label and 900 mm on a back print with no reduction penalty, and it is the vehicle's only self-luminous element, which is the whole night-time mood of the brand.
opportunities.effort: One to two days to trace from ref_side.jpg + ref_rear34.jpg. No render, no model work.

opportunities.idea: A LARGE FLANK FRAGMENT at 1:2 or 1:3, back print or oversized front. folk_gen.py measures the two dominant masses: `MASS-R1  rear-most quarter` X -2.007..-1.557, 73213 mm², elongation 1.35, and `MASS-R2 over the rear arch`, 30285 mm². Take MASS-R1 alone at 450 mm wide (1:1) or 300 mm (1:1.5). At 1:1.5 the median stroke is still 8.8 mm and the p10 is 1.8 mm — everything prints. Two inks.
opportunities.why_this_asset: It is the ONLY placement where the folk art's real line quality survives on a garment, and the measured evidence says so twice: my component census of the shipped tile finds 196 gold components with the largest 3 carrying 66.4 % and 161 of them carrying just 5 %; folk_gen's photograph census is 66 components with the top 3 carrying 84.4 % (`COMP_TOP = {1: 47.8, 2: 73.7, 3: 84.4, ...}`). Both agree: three blobs are the drawing. Print one blob big rather than all of it small.
opportunities.effort: Two days. Draw from ref_side.jpg at magnification per SPEC §10.10's own method, not from the tile — the shipped tile is measurably more fragmented than the photograph (196 vs 66 components, top-3 66.4 % vs 84.4 %).

opportunities.idea: THE TECHNICAL PLATE — the side elevation as a deadpan documentation drawing, two inks, dimensioned with the machine's own numbers. STATE.md publishes them: wheelbase 2.4000 (+0.0 mm), track front 1.3690, track rear 1.3590, width 1.7497 (-0.3 mm), tyre 0.6649, `rake 17.75 mm/m`, `rear arch lip above hub 0.3722 m ... -> tyre gap 39.7 mm`, `tail board pose: principal-axis chord 0.7110 m, angle 38.0 deg`, and the conversion's own numbers — bay 515.5 mm, counter overhang (4.317 - 4.065 = 252 mm of lid, and the counter parts project past the body).
opportunities.why_this_asset: It matches Tacombi's actual merch voice, which is equipment-catalogue deadpan: 'casual, convenient leisure products since 2006', 'Monument T', 'Horizon Beanie', 'purpose-built, all-weather knit'. It reads premium precisely because it is documentation rather than celebration. CAUTION AND THE DIFFERENTIATOR: 'VW van blueprint' is a stock category (Dreamstime sells it by the sheet), so dimension the CONVERSION — the apertures, the counter, the tail board's 38.0° — and never the VW body, or you have drawn what everyone else draws.
opportunities.effort: Three days. No render needed for the dimensions; a side elevation line pass would help but is not required.

opportunities.idea: CUT-AND-SEW, ZERO INK. The belt line is the vehicle's whole identity and it is a SEAM, not a print: cream yoke over a red body, the split sweeping down the front into the V-swage. STATE.md locks the geometry — `belt line @ x=0.962 (live) 1.2070`, `V-swage apex @ x=0.962 0.3400`, `V_APEX + V_RISE == Z_BELT | 1.2070 == 1.2070 — held` — and SPEC §3 describes the break as 'sweeping down across the nose into the T1 V-swage'. Translate that to a colour-blocked tee, a two-tone crew, a bowling shirt, a coach jacket.
opportunities.why_this_asset: A garment with no graphic on it cannot be a walking advert, and it is the most premium form the brand can take. It also transfers the ONE bit of the vehicle that is unmistakably this bus at 20 metres — the two-tone break — without printing anything at all. And it dodges every defect on the list: no red to match, no emblem, no folk art to reduce, no trademark.
opportunities.effort: Two weeks with a garment maker. No pipeline dependency whatsoever.

opportunities.idea: THE CALIDAD BURST as a SINGLE-SCREEN SPLIT FOUNTAIN. tex/calidad.png quantises to 5 bins covering 95 %: #D03010 50.8 %, white 23.3 %, then #D05010 / #F05010 / #F07010. That is a red-to-yellow gradient plus white type — one blended screen and one white screen, not four. cal_gen.py has the authored stops: `RED = (214, 46, 30)`, `ORANGE = (238, 122, 22)`, `YELLOW = (247, 189, 46)`, with `ANG = math.radians(-19.7)` for the type and bunting angle.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Split-fountain is a signature of good screen printing and cannot be faked by DTG — it is instantly readable as a printed object rather than a digital one, which is the premium tell. FIX FIRST: OPEN_FINDINGS F16 (OPEN) says 'the isolated star is built BELOW the burst where both red frames put it above'. Draw the star from ref_side.jpg (700,290)-(880,400), not from the model, or you reproduce a known error a thousand times.
opportunities.effort: One day of art, plus a press setup that can hold a blend. Requires F16 to be checked visually first.

opportunities.idea: THE SCRIPT ALONE, silver on red, at 200-260 mm across the chest. Measured on the shipped master: tex/senor.png maps to build.py's `SCR = dict(x0=0.784, x1=-0.494, ...)` = 1278 mm on the vehicle, giving 0.312 mm/px. Stroke widths on the vehicle are p10 3.95 mm / p50 19.54 mm / p90 48.28 mm. At 240 mm print width (1:5.3) that is p10 0.74 mm / p50 3.67 mm — every stroke prints, including the swash hairlines. It is a 3-component drawing that carries 100 % of its own ink.
opportunities.why_this_asset: It is the brand's actual voice — script_gen.py: 'there is no font here. Every glyph is built from primitives whose control points were read off ref_side.jpg at 6-14x magnification' — and the owner has already ruled its finish: 'Bright silver, same as Tacombi' (F157). BLOCKED ON ONE ASSET FIX: I measured tex/senor.png and it contains NO dark ink at all — of pixels with alpha > 200 the 1st-percentile luma is 165.7 and the fraction below luma 80 is 0.0000 — while SPEC §3 requires 'SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow'. Silver ink with no keyline on a cream or natural garment is an invisible wordmark. See first_moves.
opportunities.effort: Half a day of art once the keyline exists. The keyline is the blocker, not the layout.

opportunities.idea: THE APERTURE BAND AS A REPEAT — three rounded rects on a 625/645 mm pitch, run as an all-over, a side-seam tape, a cuff band, a tote gusset, a hem repeat, or a jacquard. One ink, one tile, and the uneven pitch keeps it from reading as machine-generated wallpaper.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Repeats are where apparel programmes make money without shouting, and this repeat is measured rather than invented (BAY_CX pitch 625.0 / 645.0 mm against BAY_W 515.5). It also solves the 'no walking advert' problem structurally: an all-over reads as pattern first and reference second, so only someone who knows the bus sees the bus.
opportunities.effort: One day for the tile, then it is free across the range.

opportunities.idea: EMBROIDERED BUS SILHOUETTE IN FOUR TONAL BLOCKS at 75-85 mm, left chest — no folk art, no script, no emblem. Blocks: body red, cream upper, black glazing/tyres, gold counter line. Four needles, ~11k stitches, satin outline at 1.6 mm.
opportunities.why_this_asset: It is the ONLY way the whole vehicle survives at left-chest scale, and the arithmetic says why: at 90 mm the side elevation is 1:45.2, at which the folk-art median stroke is 0.29 mm and the roundel is 6.2 mm — the folk art is gone and the emblem would be an illegible blob. Deleting them is therefore not a stylistic choice, it is the measurement. Deleting the emblem also removes the object the owner has rejected nine times (F191/F234 both stand) AND the most trademark-exposed element, so this design can ship while the emblem is still open.
opportunities.effort: Two days to draw the tonal reduction, one digitising session. Needs a clean side-elevation silhouette — see first_moves.

opportunities.idea: INSIDE-NECK BRANDING, SILENT OUTSIDE FACE. Put the wordmark where the wearer sees it and the room does not: inside-neck print, hem tab, sleeve-seam label, under-placket, care label. Use the vehicle's own civic register for the inside line — the Nolita counter fascia carries '267 / ELIZABETH STREET / NUEVA YORK' in small condensed caps above 'Gracias por su Preferencia.' in red cursive.
opportunities.why_this_asset: This is the whole answer to the brief's last question, and it costs nothing. A garment whose outside face carries one 45 mm decoded mark and whose inside neck carries the brand is a garment people buy for themselves. CEILING TO CARRY: that fascia lettering is Nolita/state-B artwork. Rule 11 forbids carrying it into a state-A render of the bus — but as TYPE on a label it is the brand's own hand-lettering, not the vehicle's paint. Say which you are doing, in writing, so nobody later mistakes a label for evidence about the bus.
opportunities.effort: One day. Woven-label MOQs are typically 500-1000.

opportunities.idea: TONE-ON-TONE. Cream ink on a cream garment one shade off; gold on natural; black on black; a matt ink on a garment-dyed ground. Take one motif — the rosette, the three hatches, the bulb line — at 200-300 mm and print it at near-zero contrast.
opportunities.why_this_asset: AUDIT_rev43.md's surviving colour-separation row says the whole vehicle is 'ONE 70° hue wedge plus four neutrals', which is a measured licence to work in a single narrow hue family. Tone-on-tone is the fastest, cheapest and most reliable way to make a graphic read premium rather than souvenir, because it removes the two things that signal souvenir: high contrast and a hard ink edge. One screen, soft hand, garment-dyed heavyweight (200-240 gsm) doing the rest of the work.
opportunities.effort: Half a day per design. It is the cheapest premium move in this whole list.

opportunities.idea: THE '1963' PLATE as a micro-mark. SPEC §4: 'chrome number-plate surround on the engine lid reading "1963", empty', and STATE.md builds it (`plate | 1`, `plate_digits | 1`). Use it at 25-40 mm: a woven hem tag, an embroidered sleeve mark, a heat-transfer inside the neck, a debossed leather patch on a cap.
opportunities.why_this_asset: The owner literally dated the object on its own back. A four-digit year in a chrome frame is a complete graphic at 25 mm with one colour, needs no emblem, no VW mark and no folk art, and it reads as provenance rather than promotion. It is also the fastest thing on this list to ship.
opportunities.effort: Half a day.

opportunities.idea: THE MURAL BOARD AS A POSTER / TOTE PANEL — but printed, not screened. My count of tex/lidmural.png (4096x2476): 68 distinct 32-step colour bins with 13 needed to cover 95 % of the field, top bins #B09010 19.2 %, #903010 17.8 %, #503010 11.9 %, #501010 9.7 %. That is a painting, not signwriting.
opportunities.why_this_asset: It is the loudest, most photogenic surface on the vehicle and the only place the brand's display typography appears at scale ('GOURMET TACOS & TORTAS ★ FRESH JUICES ★ SHRIMP & FISH'). But 13 separations is not a screen-print job — it is DTG on a light garment, or a litho poster, or a sublimated tote panel. FIX FIRST: OPEN_FINDINGS F74(a) is OPEN — 'tex/lidmural.png is cropped at the bottom — the bottom row of flowers is sliced mid-bloom and the yellow side columns are truncated'. And lid_gen.py is NOT called by build.py, so a regeneration is a hand step.
opportunities.effort: One revision to repair the crop in lid_gen.py and regenerate by hand. Then half a day of layout per product.

opportunities.idea: A DIE-CUT APPLIQUÉ PATCH from deliver.py's own trimmed silhouette — merrowed or laser-cut edge, satin-stitched to a jacket back or a cap. deliver.py already produces exactly this geometry: it writes `full_frame`, `trimmed`, `layers`, `web`, with `trimmed/` being 'The same images cropped tight to the artwork' and `layers/` writing `combi_%s_no_shadow.png` and `combi_%s_shadow_only.png`.
opportunities.why_this_asset: OPEN_FINDINGS F161 says the mechanical half of the original sticker deliverable already exists: 'deliver.py's trimmed/ output is exactly that geometry'. A patch is a garment artefact, not F18's sticker, so it is not gated by F18's 'build it after the model is done' trigger — but it reuses the same solved silhouette. NOTE: this is offered as a DIFFERENT artefact from F18, not as F18.
opportunities.effort: Blocked on one alpha render (see first_moves), then one day of art and a patch supplier.

blockers: NO ALPHA FRAME EXISTS ON DISK AND THE OPTICS CHAIN DESTROYS ALPHA. Every PNG in out/ is colortype 2 (truecolour, no alpha) and deliver.py's C1 fails on all four. The pipeline researcher measured that post.py reads `rgba = np.asarray(Image.open(src).convert("RGBA"))` then `im = rgba[..., :3]` and saves 3-channel — so you can have optics or a cut-out, never both. Apparel needs the cut-out. T1_ALPHA has not been run since rev 62 (no LEDGER_rev*.md contains the string).

NO VECTOR OF THE VEHICLE EXISTS ANYWHERE. The only .svg in the tree is vw_canonical_2019.svg, which F168 records as a DIFFERENT OBJECT from the 1955-67 pressing. Screen-print separations want vector or 1-bit bitmaps at 300-600 dpi at final size; embroidery digitising wants clean vector. There is also no 3D export path at all — the only persistence is build.py's `if os.environ.get("T1_SAVE"): bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(...)`, and T1_SAVE appears in zero handoff documents.

RESOLUTION. Live: `visibility_budget.py 3840 out/r75_hero34f.png` prints 'scale: 734 px/m (1.36 mm per pixel)', so at a 3840 nominal frame the 4.065 m vehicle spans 2984 px. A 280 mm chest print at 300 dpi needs 3307 px (nominal ~4256); an A2 poster at 300 dpi needs 4961 px (nominal ~6385). Nothing above 3840 has ever been stitched (F192/F49), hq_render.py has no T1_FX=0 where hero.py explicitly does, and out/ is untracked so every large frame ever made is gone.

THE RED IS NOT AVAILABLE AS AN INK FROM ANY CURRENT SOURCE. flank_compare live on out/r75_side.png reads the render at median (196,81,67) against the photograph's (158,16,6), G/R 0.422 vs 0.114 — it images salmon. And the photographs cannot supply one either: probe_rev71_red.py prints its own prohibition, 'the photograph's red G/R is 0.0149 .. 0.0344, a 2.3x span. DO NOT QUOTE A SINGLE FIGURE FOR IT.' Three authored reds also disagree: t1_mats `RED = sRGB(196,49,36)`, lid_gen `RED = (159, 45, 22)`, cal_gen `RED = (214, 46, 30)`.

THE WORDMARK HAS NO KEYLINE IN THE SHIPPED ASSET. I measured tex/senor.png: of pixels with alpha > 200, 1st-percentile luma is 165.7 and the fraction below luma 80 is 0.0000 — zero dark ink. SPEC §3 requires 'SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow'. lid_gen.py already authors the convention (`DARKLINE = (72, 26, 16)`); script_gen.py does not. Until this is fixed, silver script on a light garment is invisible and silver on red has no edge.

THE EMBLEM IS THE OWNER'S NINTH REPORT AND IT IS STILL WRONG (F191 and F234 both stand). probe_rev69_fitpose P2 reads 0.8528 against P1b's 0.9465 ceiling; probe_rev46_vw C8 reads 'photo 3.39, built 2.84 -- the built cells are 1.19x TOO ROUND'. At a 280 mm full-width chest print the roundel is 19.3 mm (ROUNDEL_D = 0.2800 on a 4.065 m vehicle) — large enough that its arrangement is judgeable. So no front or three-quarter bus on apparel from the model until it lands, or crop the nose out, or draw the emblem from the photograph.

VW TRADEMARK EXPOSURE IS NAMED AND UNRESOLVED, and apparel is the most enforced category. This is an owner-plus-counsel question, not a design decision. Partial mitigation is inherent: on this bus the roundel is painted red relief, not chrome, and the marks that carry the brand — the hatches, the counter, the folk art, the script — are not VW's.

THE DELIVERY RENDER IS UNDER A STANDING HOLD, THREE TIMES GIVEN. F191 'Keep holding — fix the emblem first'; F193 'I don't think the bus is ready yet.' Apparel art derived from a preview render is not the delivery render — but say which you are offering, in the proposal, or the hold reads as a blocker on work it does not cover.

THE ONE CUSTOMER-FACING DOCUMENT IN THE REPO IS STALE. deliver.py's generated READ_ME_FIRST says 'THE VW EMBLEM ON THE NOSE READS AS AN X. This is the defect you have reported six times' (it is his ninth, and it renders as V-over-W) and 'The tyres have no tread ... Two loudspeakers on the roof are missing' (the tread SHIPPED at rev 74, F308; the loudspeakers were RETIRED at rev 74, F309). Do not hand any package to the owner until that text is corrected.

REDUCTION IS A DECLARED DECISION, NOT A SILENT ONE. SPEC §10.10 is 'a hard bar, not a preference': 'Every painted element on this vehicle must be REPRODUCED from photographs of the actual combi. Not approximated. Not invented.' Its object is the MODEL's decals, not derived garment art — but any simplification for print must be published with its measured basis (folk_gen's 48-of-66 components carrying 2.29 %; my census of the shipped tile, 161 of 196 components carrying 5 %), or it looks like the bar being quietly dropped.
first_moves: RENDER ONE ALPHA SET AND DO NOT POST-PROCESS IT. `T1_ALPHA=1 T1_SUB=2 T1_PREVIEW=side,front,hero34f,hero34r T1_PFX=a01 ...` and then keep the files as they land — do NOT run post.py or judge_set.sh on them, because post.py drops the alpha channel. Run deliver.py against that set and watch C1 go from FAIL to PASS. This is the single unblocking action for every silhouette-, patch- and composite-based idea above, and the switch has not been exercised since rev 62.

PRINT A PHYSICAL SCALE PROOF BEFORE ANY ART IS APPROVED. Output tex/swirl.png's flank band at 1:14.5 (280 mm chest), 1:45 (90 mm left chest) and 1:74 (55 mm cap), on the actual garment, with a stepped line-width wedge (2.0 / 1.0 / 0.7 / 0.5 / 0.35 / 0.25 mm) alongside. This is 'render it, crop it and look at it' for apparel, and the arithmetic predicts it will fail: at 1:14.5 the folk art's median stroke is 0.91 mm but its p10 is 0.18 mm and 95 of 196 gold components have their thickest point under 0.52 mm. Confirm that on cloth before anyone commits a screen.

DRAW THE TWO NO-RENDER MARKS TOMORROW. (a) The three-hatch mark from t1_shell.py: three 515.5 x 403.0 mm apertures, corner radius 55.0 mm, centres at 0.6720 / 0.0470 / -0.5980 giving pillars of 109.5 and 129.5 mm. (b) The hubcap bullseye from t1_detail.py: CAP_D 274 mm with the badge at 31.7 % of it (86.9 mm), drawn as a ratio so it scales. Neither needs Blender, a render, or the model to be finished.

FIX THE SCRIPT'S KEYLINE, AND SAY WHAT IT IS NOT. Add a dark outline to script_gen.py using lid_gen.py's own authored `DARKLINE = (72, 26, 16)`; regenerate tex/senor.png BY HAND (script_gen.py is not called by build.py, so the render silently keeps the old texture); re-measure and watch the 1st-percentile luma fall from 165.7. State explicitly in the commit that F157 ('Bright silver, same as Tacombi') governs the WORD's brightness and not its outline, and that the b flag, i dot and swash keep their measured tarnish — F157 ruled on `Senor`, not on `TARNISH_ZONES`.

BUILD THE FLAT-ART PASS — three renders from one camera: a Freestyle line pass, a flat material/ID pass, and an AO pass. This is literally the owner's own lost clause, recovered by the prior-art researcher from NEXT_CONTEXT_PROMPT_rev39.md: 'cartoon with rendered depth — vector line and flat colour, shading and occlusion sampled from the 3D asset', which was dropped between rev 39 and rev 43 and has been missing from every carrier for 32 revisions. It needs no new geometry and it serves apparel, patches, posters and animation at once. It is also the only route from this repo to anything vector.

CHOOSE AND DECLARE THE BRAND RED AS AN INK, once, in SPEC. Take it from t1_mats.py `RED = (0.5520, 0.0294, 0.0176)  # = sRGB(196,49,36)` or from an unclipped photograph window — ref_playa_34.png is the only frame with a neutral white-balance reference (paving 116,119,120) — and never from a render. Record a Pantone and a garment-dye reference beside it. Every design above depends on this and nothing in the tree currently supplies it.

PROVE THE LARGE-FORMAT CHAIN AT ~4300 NOMINAL, ONCE, and export T1_FX=0 by hand while doing it (hq_render.py has no T1_FX, where hero.py's docstring says the optics 'are forced OFF during the strip renders with T1_FX=0 ... Per-strip optics band at the seams'). Check stitch.py's exit code — F49 records 'THE GUARD FIRED AND THE RUNNER IGNORED IT'. Until this runs, no chest print above about 240 dpi is available.

PUT ONE MULTIPLE-CHOICE QUESTION TO THE OWNER, with a garment mock attached: which garment strategy — (a) red garment, cream + gold + dark print; (b) natural/ecru garment, red + gold + dark; (c) black garment, gold + cream; (d) tone-on-tone, one shade off. Naming a garment and a print size is also the precondition F192 states for asking the delivery dimension ('Do NOT re-ask it cold; ask it once he names the medium'), so this closes two things at once. DO NOT re-ask the papel picado (F18) or the emblem's stroke weight (F314).

CHECK F16 BEFORE ANY CALIDAD-DERIVED GRAPHIC SHIPS. OPEN_FINDINGS F16 is OPEN: 'the isolated star is built BELOW the burst where both red frames put it above; every flank rosette is drawn at the diameter of its gold core'. Look at ref_side.jpg (700,290)-(880,400) and ref_playa_34.png (395,100)-(500,180) and draw the star from the photograph. The same row means every rosette in the shipped tile is undersized — which matters for the life-size embroidery idea.

RAISE THE TRADEMARK QUESTION IN WRITING TO THE OWNER BEFORE ANY UNIT IS ORDERED. One paragraph, no legal opinion: apparel is the enforced category; does Tacombi have an arrangement, and does he want the emblem on merchandise at all? Note that every design in this list except the technical plate can ship with no VW mark visible.
what_would_embarrass_us: A 280 mm chest print of the whole flank in which the folk art fills in and reads as mud. It is predicted, not hypothetical: at 1:14.5 the shipped tile's p10 gold stroke is 0.18 mm and its thinnest whole component is 0.13 mm, against a realistic positive-line minimum of ~0.5 mm on jersey. That is the exact element the owner named in his 'ABSOLUTE REPLICATION OF ALL ARTWORK' hard bar.

Five hundred units carrying a front-facing bus with the emblem he has rejected NINE times. At 280 mm the roundel is 19.3 mm — big enough that a customer can see it is a fat X rather than a V over a W, which is precisely what probe_rev46_vw's C8 measures ('the built cells are 1.19x TOO ROUND').

Salmon ink on the garment because someone eyedropped a render. flank_compare reads the render's red at (196,81,67) against the photograph's (158,16,6). A brand red is judged at every size and every distance; there is no viewing condition in which that is close.

Moiré across the louvre block and the tyre tread. LOUV_PITCH is 21.111 mm and the tread pitch is pi x 0.6649 / 64 = 32.6 mm; at a 280 mm chest print those become 1.45 mm and 2.25 mm, which is three to five cells of a 55 lpi halftone (0.462 mm) — the exact band where a regular repeat beats against the screen. On a left-chest print they are 0.47 and 0.72 mm and it is worse.

A silver wordmark that vanishes. tex/senor.png contains zero pixels below luma 80; printed as one metallic ink on a cream or natural garment with no keyline, the whole lockup disappears at two metres.

Publishing 'sixty-four treads' or any countable detail on a poster crop. probe_rev74_tread's T2 refuses to publish a count and prints six estimates spanning 48..84; t1_detail.py says so in the source — `TREAD_LUGS = 64  # DECLARED, inside the MEASURED bracket 48..84`. At a 610 mm poster the lug pitch is 4.9 mm and a customer can count them.

Handing the owner a package whose README tells him the emblem 'reads as an X ... reported six times', that the tyres have no tread, and that two roof loudspeakers are missing — when the tread shipped at rev 74, the loudspeakers were retired at rev 74, and it is his ninth report. deliver.py writes all 22 files and that README even in the run that prints 'PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY'.
Reproducing the pink star on the wrong side of the burst a thousand times, when OPEN_FINDINGS F16 has said it is on the wrong side since rev 49.

Putting the 'La Santa' board on a garment as bus livery. F164 is an owner ruling: 'The forward one is separate from the Bus' — it is restaurant furniture, and t1_shell.py's own signboard() says 'it is not on the vehicle at all'.

Mixing livery states in one graphic — folk art from Playa with the Nolita chalkboard or the painted glass lettering. Rule 11 has already killed F99, F100 and F140 on exactly this, and a customer who knows the Nolita bus will see the composite immediately.
A cease-and-desist from Volkswagen on a garment run, on a question nobody wrote down.

Selling a photoreal render on a t-shirt. gloss_compare reads the render's paint spread at 0.412 of the photograph's against a 0.60 bar — the body images as flat vinyl. A simulated-process print of a matte, salmon-red, gloss-free render is the definition of the souvenir-shop object this brief exists to avoid.

expert_plans.discipline: Die-cut sticker and vinyl production design — cut-path engineering, kiss-cut sheet systems, substrate/finish selection (gloss/matte/clear/holographic underbase), weeding and registration tolerance, and the reduction ladder that decides which marks survive at which physical size.

opportunities.idea: BUILD A REDUCTION LADDER BEFORE ANY DRAWING. I computed one from live constants and watched it print. At a sticker whose BODY measures 51 / 76 / 102 / 152 mm (overall length is 1.127x that if you cut the propped silhouette: 57.5 / 85.6 / 114.9 / 171.3 mm), the final millimetres are: tyre 8.34 / 12.43 / 16.68 / 24.86; serving aperture 6.47x5.06 / 9.65x7.53 / 12.95x10.11 / 19.29x15.07; nose roundel 3.51 / 5.23 / 7.03 / 10.47; hubcap 3.44 / 5.12 / 6.88 / 10.25; hubcap VW badge 1.09 / 1.62 / 2.18 / 3.25; 'Senor Tacombi' lockup 16.03x6.83 / 23.89x10.17 / 32.07x13.65 / 47.79x20.34; Calidad decal 6.44x4.77 / 9.59x7.10 / 12.87x9.54 / 19.18x14.21; rosette gold cores 0.39-0.85 / 0.57-1.27 / 0.77-1.71 / 1.15-2.54; louvre pitch 0.26 / 0.39 / 0.53 / 0.79; lid_rail 0.27 / 0.40 / 0.53 / 0.80; arch-to-tyre gap 0.50 / 0.74 / 1.00 / 1.48; menu card width 1.20 / 1.79 / 2.41 / 3.59. Against a printed-detail read floor of ~0.35 mm and a comfortable floor of ~0.6 mm, this partitions the vehicle cleanly: at 51 mm you get silhouette + two-tone + three apertures + a wheel bullseye + a silver GESTURE (the lockup is 6.8 mm tall, so 'Tacombi' cap height is ~2 mm — a swash T survives, the spiral counters in a/c/o/m/b do not). At 76 mm the nose roundel is 5.2 mm and its V-over-W is legible and JUDGEABLE. At 102 mm the biggest rosettes (1.71 mm) grow petals. At 152 mm the ten louvres (0.79 mm pitch) become ten strokes rather than a grey band, and the hubcap VW (3.25 mm) reads.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Every one of these came from a constant in this tree — ROUNDEL_D = 0.2800 (build.py), CAP_EMBLEM_D = 0.3170 * CAP_D with STATE.md's 'hubcap badge: 4 rings R 0.043429 (= CAP_EMBLEM_D/2)' giving CAP_D = 0.2740, STATE.md's 'measured ... TYRE_D=0.6649' and 'bay widths 0.516 0.515 0.516' and 'band 1.372-1.775 un-dropped (1.307-1.710 AG)', t1_detail.py's 'LOUV_PITCH = (LOUV_Z_TOP - LOUV_Z_BOT) / (LOUV_N - 1)          # 0.021111' with LOUV_N = 10, STATE.md's 'lid_rail width = RAIL_PROUD 0.0213 m', 'rear arch lip above hub 0.3722 m (ARCH_R 0.3735) -> tyre gap 39.7 mm', build.py's 'SCR = dict(x0=0.784, x1=-0.494, z0=0.4453, z1=0.9896)' (1.278 x 0.544 m) and 'CAL = dict(x0=-1.155, x1=-1.668, z0=1.4200, z1=1.8000)' (0.513 x 0.380 m), folk_gen.py's FLANK_ROSETTES areas 740-3632 mm^2 (equivalent diameters 30.7-68.0 mm), and STATE.md's 'dims L=4.065' / 'x range [-2.157, 2.160]' with the tail board reaching x -2.420 (HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §0.05) giving the full propped silhouette 4.580 x 3.132 m = 1.462:1. No other VW-bus sticker programme in the world can compute this table, because nobody else has the vehicle as measured geometry.
opportunities.effort: Half a day. Write it as a script that IMPORTS the constants (t1_detail.LOUV_PITCH, CAP_D, build.SCR/CAL/ROUNDEL_D, t1_shell.BAYS) and prints final millimetres for a list of sticker lengths — do not transcribe my numbers, re-derive them, because a transcribed table goes stale silently and this project has a rule about that.

opportunities.idea: THE CUT PATH IS NOT THE SILHOUETTE, AND THE SHADOW IS THE PLINTH. Do not contour-cut the true outline. At a 76 mm body the arch-to-tyre gap is 0.74 mm and the propped tail board is a 22 mm-thick blade (t1_shell.py TB_T on a 0.7110 m chord) reading 0.31 mm thick and 13 mm long — both are below every weeding, blade-tracking and lifting threshold I would accept (internal radius >= 1.5 mm, no notch narrower than ~3 mm of vinyl, external corner >= 0.8 mm). The fix is also the best drawing decision available: run the cut along a ground line / cast shadow so the bus sits on a solid base, absorb the mirrors and the lid struts inside a closed hull, and let the propped lid and tail board project ONLY where they can carry >= 3 mm of vinyl. Implement it as a morphological CLOSING of the alpha mask at a radius chosen in FINAL MILLIMETRES (r = 1.5 mm / k), then trace it. The tracer already exists and is selftested: trace_outline.py's trace_with_holes(), whose header says 'selftest() checks the tracer on shapes whose area and perimeter are known BY CONSTRUCTION'. Add a guard that MEASURES minimum notch width and minimum internal radius along the produced path, and watch it go red on the raw silhouette before you believe it green on the closed one.
opportunities.why_this_asset: AUDIT_rev43.md's surviving sticker row already says 'DIE-CUT OUTLINE — bridge the underbody with the cast shadow, and let no feature narrower than 0.159 m touch the cut line' — 0.159 m is 2.26 mm at that audit's implied ~1:70, i.e. exactly the practical vinyl minimum, arrived at independently. And the plinth is semantically right for THIS vehicle: SPEC.md §0.1 quotes Tacombi's own account — 'The engine was scrapped, transmission sold, seats swapped for cooking equipment, and the roof was reeled back'. It is a building, not a van. A sticker that sits on a shadow rather than floating on four tyres tells the truth about it.
opportunities.effort: 1-2 days once an alpha frame exists. trace_outline.py is written and selftested; the closing, the simplification and the min-feature guard are ~150 lines of numpy and need no Blender.

opportunities.idea: THE SET IS A LIVERY SERIES: ONE CUT PATH, FOUR PRINT FILES. Build the side-elevation die-cut ONCE and print it in four documented states — green-and-bare (workshop conversion, no scrollwork, no daisies, no burst, bare painted rims with no hubcaps), green-in-service (black script, white/blue scrollwork with yellow daisies, Calidad starburst), red-plain/Nolita (TACOMBI.COM, no folk art, no script, chalkboard lid), and red-folk-art/Playa (gold scrollwork, silver Senor Tacombi, flower mural lid, Calidad burst). One die, four SKUs, a genuine collectible ladder, and a founding story no competitor can tell. Critically, this makes the project's hardest rule into the product's feature: geometry is shared, paint is not.
opportunities.why_this_asset: LEDGER_rev51.md carries the four states as a VERIFIED table, and SPEC.md §7.1 records the owner's ruling that they are the same vehicle in different livery states, with the standing constraint that 'folk art, script, aperture glazing and roof-board treatment may never be carried across states.' CLAUDE.md rule 11 says the same. So the series is not invention — it is the record's own taxonomy sold as a set. It also converts a modelling liability (four unreconciled reds across t1_mats.py RED = sRGB(196,49,36), lid_gen.py RED = (159,45,22), cal_gen.py RED = (214,46,30)) into a deliberate per-state ink choice.
opportunities.effort: Cheap on the print side (four flat-colour files off one master drawing). Expensive if you want it RENDERED per state: build.py binds the folk art, script and Calidad unconditionally, so a T1_LIVERY switch is required model work — maybe 1 revision. For a drawn/vector series it costs nothing but illustration time.

opportunities.idea: CLEAR VINYL WITH SELECTIVE WHITE UNDERBASE — THE APERTURE STICKER. Print white ink everywhere EXCEPT the three serving hatches, the windscreen and the cab door glass, on clear PVC. Stuck on a window the taqueria's own light comes through the holes. This is the one material move that is native to this specific vehicle and unavailable to every stock VW-bus sticker, because a stock bus has glass and this one does not. STATE.md: 'open serving apertures on +Y: 3'. At 76 mm each aperture is 9.65 x 7.53 mm — comfortably above every cut, weed and registration threshold, so it works even at the giveaway size.
opportunities.why_this_asset: SPEC.md §0.1 records why the hatches exist at all: Dario Wolos bought the bus for $3,000, 'missing three of its windows', and 'figured out how to cut open the Tacombi'. The signature feature is an absence. A substrate that renders it as an actual absence is the strongest single idea in this brief and it costs one extra ink channel. Requires a vendor with a white-ink channel (Roland VersaUV / UV flatbed / DTF); confirm before designing, because a shop without white ink will silently print it on white vinyl and you lose the whole point.
opportunities.effort: Design: 1 day on top of an existing master. Production: ask three vendors for a white-ink test tile this week; the answer is yes/no in 48 hours.

opportunities.idea: SPOT HOLOGRAPHIC, RESTRICTED TO TWO ELEMENTS — THE SILVER SCRIPT AND THE BULB STRING. Not a holographic whole sticker (cliché, and rainbow holo destroys the vermillion). Print on brushed-silver or linear holographic stock with a white underbase EVERYWHERE except the 'Senor Tacombi' lockup and the festoon bulbs. The wordmark then IS metal leaf rather than grey ink, and the bulbs glint as the sticker tilts. This is the only sticker gimmick on the shelf that is semantically CORRECT here rather than decorative.
opportunities.why_this_asset: script_gen.py measured the real ink: 'ink is neutral silver, not white and not gold: median RGB (127,122,125), saturation 0.080, over a ground of (129,21,14)' — a neutral metal, which flat grey ink cannot reproduce and a metallic substrate can. And the owner has already ruled on this element specifically: 'Bright silver, same as Tacombi' (F157), which overrides SPEC §3's WEATHERED lock for that word only. The bulb string is the vehicle's one self-luminous element and OPEN_FINDINGS.md F144 records that even the 3D render fails it — 'THE FESTOON BULBS READ AS PEARLS, NOT LIGHTS'. A substrate solves in one ink channel what the renderer has not solved in seventy-five revisions.
opportunities.effort: Design: 1 day (two spot masks off the existing artwork). Note the lockup is 23.9 mm long at a 76 mm sticker and 47.8 mm at 152 mm — the spot mask is easily large enough for reliable registration at both.

opportunities.idea: MAKE THE PRIMARY UNIT A KISS-CUT A6 SHEET, NOT A SINGLE DIE-CUT. For children at a restaurant counter a sheet beats a single on every axis: one SKU, one price, one weeding pull, a play pattern (peel and place), and a printed backing card that is free real estate. Layout that fits: A6 105 x 148 mm, 5 mm margins, live 95 x 138 mm. Hero bus at 90 mm overall (that is a 79 mm body, so the ladder's 76 mm column applies) at the propped silhouette's 1.462:1 = 61.6 mm tall. That leaves 95 x 72 mm for satellites at 4 mm gutters: a 3 x 2 grid of ~28 mm marks plus a 90 x 12 mm strip. Satellites, each harvested at ITS OWN scale rather than shrunk from the bus: the wheel bullseye (chrome ring / cream dish / red dome / cream VW), the nose roundel, one rosette, the Calidad burst with its pink star, the '1963' plate, a menu card, and the festoon bulb strip. Reserve one slot and DO NOT fill it — that is where the papel picado goes if and when the owner rules on it.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Every satellite is a mark this vehicle actually carries, and each dies at bus-scale but lives at its own scale: the hubcap VW is 1.62 mm on a 76 mm bus (a dot) but 20 mm as its own sticker (a legible badge); a rosette gold core is 0.57-1.27 mm on the bus and 25 mm alone. The kiss-cut constraint set is simple and checkable: no sticker's cut path may carry a concave notch narrower than ~3 mm, and no two cut paths may come within ~4 mm, so the negative web lifts in one pull. F18's own audience clause — 'For children at the restaurant; should spark joy and be something families keep' — is better served by twelve things to place than by one thing to stick.
opportunities.effort: 2-3 days of illustration once the palette and the master drawing exist. The papel picado slot costs nothing and honours the owner's standing 'Leave it open, I'll decide when the sticker is actually being built. DO NOT RE-PUT IT UNTIL THEN.'

opportunities.idea: THREE-TIER ARTWORK WITH A REDUCTION SWITCH, AND THE 84/2 RULE MAKES IT ALMOST FREE. Author every drawing in three separable layers — T1 silhouette and flat colour blocks; T2 identity marks (roundel, wordmark, wheel bullseye, apertures, tail board, counter); T3 texture (folk art, louvres, bulbs, menu cards, chipping). Each SKU ships T1, T1+T2, or T1+T2+T3 according to the ladder. The T3-to-T2 reduction is nearly costless because folk_gen.py's own census says so: 'COMP_TOP = {1: 47.8, 2: 73.7, 3: 84.4, 5: 87.8, 10: 93.5}' and 'COMP_HIST' whose first three bins are (24, 0.42%), (21, 1.32%), (3, 0.55%) — so 48 of the 66 gold components carry 2.29% of the ink and the largest THREE carry 84.4%. Keep MASS-R1 (73213 mm^2), MASS-R2 (30285 mm^2) and the door mass; delete the 48. AND: line weights must be specified in FINAL MILLIMETRES per SKU, never scaled. Scaling a 0.6 mm stroke from 152 mm to 51 mm gives 0.2 mm and the louvres, the rosette petals and the script counters all die at once, silently, in the same step.
opportunities.why_this_asset: This is a measured licence to simplify on THIS artwork rather than a general design platitude, and it transfers beyond stickers to embroidery, screen-print, favicons and a 20-frame logo reveal. AUDIT_rev43.md states it as a sticker rule — 'THE SACRIFICE RULE IS ALREADY MEASURED: 48 of the flank's 66 gold components carry 2.29% of the ink and every one lands under 0.40 mm. Delete all 48.' — and I reproduced the arithmetic independently from folk_gen.py's live constants, which is the only reason I trust it.
opportunities.effort: It is a file-organisation decision made on day one and it costs nothing then; retrofitting it after the master is drawn costs the master.

opportunities.idea: A DELIBERATE F18 TRACK, BUILT TO THE RECOVERED CLAUSE RATHER THAN THE SHORT ONE. The rev-43 style lock everyone quotes — 'cartoon with rendered depth' — is a truncation. NEXT_CONTEXT_PROMPT_rev39.md §7 item 3 carries the owner's full sentence: 'Style LOCKED by me: cartoon with rendered depth — vector line and flat colour, shading and occlusion sampled from the 3D asset.' That is not a mood word, it is a buildable pipeline: flat vector fills plus an AO/shadow pass lifted off the Blender model. deliver.py already emits half of it — 'layers/ ... *_no_shadow.png the vehicle alone, nothing under it / *_shadow_only.png the shadow alone' — and probe_rev54_aov.py demonstrates the AOV plumbing for the other half. Build the F18 sticker to the FULL clause, honour its scene lock (bus + sun + [papel picado deferred]), and obey its sun rule: 'THE SUN — it must NOT be a rayed disc. The vehicle already carries ELEVEN radial bursts, and it is the drawing's only light source.'
opportunities.why_this_asset: That clause has been missing from every carrier since rev 43 and it is the single most actionable sentence in the whole sticker record. Recovering it turns F18 from an unbuilt mood brief into a defined render-plus-vector pipeline whose inputs already exist. State plainly in the proposal that this ONE track is the F18 deliverable and is gated by F18's own trigger ('build it after the model is done', restated at rev 62 as 'once i determine the model is done'), and that every other tier above is a DIFFERENT artefact and is not gated by it.
opportunities.effort: 3-5 days for a first proof, of which the AO pass is the only unknown. Do not promise the wheel treatment: see blockers.

opportunities.idea: A MATTE 'PLATE' TIER THAT MATCHES THE BRAND'S EXISTING COPY VOICE. Orthographic side elevation, no sun, no shadow, no ornament beyond T2, on matte white PVC with matte lamination, captioned in a hairline: 1963 / Type 2 / Playa del Carmen. This is the laptop/adult tier and it sits beside shop.tacombi.com's actual register — 'casual, convenient leisure products since 2006', 'purpose-built, all-weather knit beanie', 'Monument T'. Matte kills laptop glare, and the studio.py 'side' camera is ALREADY the right one: 'side: dict(loc=(0.0, 26.0, 1.52), tgt=(0.0, 0.0, 1.52), lens=None, ortho=5.90)' — orthographic, at 1.52 m eye height, which is within 30 mm of the reference photograph's own camera height that REF_MEASUREMENTS.md derives ('a pinhole model with camera height ~ 1.55 m, horizon y ~ 340'). Pre-compensate the red for matte: matte lamination will read roughly 8-10% darker and duller, so ink it hotter than the gloss SKU.
opportunities.why_this_asset: The side elevation also SEQUENCES the programme correctly. On a side view the nose roundel is absent and only the four hubcap badges remain, at 1.62 mm on a 76 mm sticker — below any threshold at which the emblem's defect is judgeable. The emblem is the owner's ninth report and gates the delivery render (F191/F234 both stand). So the side-elevation SKUs are shippable while the emblem is still wrong, and the front-facing SKUs are not. Ship in that order deliberately and say why.
opportunities.effort: 1-2 days. It is the cheapest SKU in the system and the least gated.

opportunities.idea: TWO LONG-THIN KISS-CUT SINGLES: THE BULB STRIP AND THE WORDMARK. The festoon string is the vehicle's best pure-graphic asset — a continuous drawn line of light that describes the whole outline in one stroke, works at any scale down to a favicon, and animates for free. Cut it as a 200 x 12 mm strip for a laptop edge or a shelf lip, on holographic stock. The 'Senor Tacombi' lockup as its own long single on brushed silver is the second. Both are geometry-free, so neither is blocked by any open model finding.
