opportunities.why_this_asset: Nothing in the model or the register gates these — they come off tex/senor.png (4096 x 1738, verified by reading the PNG header) and a drawn bead path, not off a render. They are the two SKUs you could produce this month with the render pipeline entirely broken.
opportunities.effort: 1 day each. The lockup needs its dark keyline and drop shadow ADDED, which the shipped texture lacks — see blockers — but for a flat sticker you draw it, you do not fix the shader.

blockers: NO ALPHA FRAME EXISTS TODAY, AND THE CUT PATH HAS NOTHING TO TRACE. Every PNG in out/ is truncolour with no alpha (colortype 2), studio.py's setup_render only sets RGBA 'if _alpha_delivery()', and T1_ALPHA has not been run since rev 62 — no LEDGER contains the string. deliver.py run against out/r75_* prints 'CONTROLS: 4 checked, 1 FAILED -- C1', '[FAIL] C1 ... FAILING ON: hero34f, hero34r, side, front' and 'PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY'. This is a one-env-var fix, but until it is run the entire die-cut half of the programme has no source silhouette.

DELIVER.PY WRITES THE WHOLE PACKAGE AND ITS README EVEN WHEN IT REFUSES — only the zip is withheld. So a folder exists on disk whose READ_ME_FIRST says 'Every image here has a TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND. Drop them straight onto any colour, photograph or texture' produced by the same run that printed 'PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY'. That README also under-reports the owner's own complaint count ('THE VW EMBLEM ON THE NOSE READS AS AN X. This is the defect you have reported six times' against the brief's ninth) and names as open two things rev 74 closed — 'The tyres have no tread' (the tread SHIPPED, F308) and 'Two loudspeakers on the roof are missing' (RETIRED as a pose, F309). Do not hand that folder to anyone, including internally.

post.py DESTROYS ALPHA, so the optics chain and the cut-out chain are mutually exclusive. Measured: an RGBA input comes back colortype 2. For print this is fine — you want neither film grain nor chromatic aberration on a sticker — but it means judge_set.sh's '_post' set, which is the best-looking output the repo can make today, is unusable as sticker source.

THE AUDIT'S SPECIFIED STICKER VIEWPOINT DOES NOT EXIST AS A CAMERA. AUDIT_rev43.md locks 'VIEWPOINT — 18 degree front three-quarter from the serving side, eye height 1.55 m.' studio.py's hero34f is loc=(12.20, 8.55, 3.55) tgt=(-0.15, 0.00, 1.34): azimuth atan(8.55/12.35) = 34.7 degrees and camera height 3.55 m — right side (+Y is the serving side per STATE.md 'open serving apertures on +Y: 3'), wrong angle and wrong eye height. front34 is on -Y, the wrong side entirely. A new view dict entry is required and is trivial; nobody has noticed it is missing.

RESOLUTION. Nothing above 1600x1100 exists on disk and out/ is untracked. At the 300 dpi print convention a 1600 px master covers a 135 mm sticker; at 600 dpi it covers 68 mm. So a 3-4 inch photoreal sticker is servable from a preview frame and a 6 inch one is not. The large-format chain has never been proven above 3840x2640 (rev 57, one view, 106.8 min), is 8-bit end to end (stitch.py and post.py both read through PIL), and hq_render.py does not set T1_FX=0 where the chain it replaced explicitly did — so per-strip optics band at the seams unless the operator exports it by hand.

THE DELIVERY RENDER IS UNDER A STANDING OWNER HOLD, HELD FOUR TIMES. F191 'Keep holding — fix the emblem first', F193 'I don't think the bus is ready yet. We need the bus to be ready before investing seriously in the render.' Anything offered AS the F18 deliverable inherits F18's own trigger, 'build it after the model is done'. Nothing above except the F18 track is gated by that, but the proposal must say which artefact is which or the hold reads as blocking everything.

THE EMBLEM IS WRONG AND IT IS RESOLVABLE ON A STICKER. Pose-free shape IoU 0.8528 against a control ceiling of 0.9465; probe_rev46_vw's C8 reads 'photo 3.39, built 2.84 -- the built cells are 1.19x TOO ROUND'; probe_rev69_fitpose's P3 reads 'photo-only/model-only inside the ring is 73/178 -- NEAR BALANCED, so the ink AMOUNT is right and the ARRANGEMENT is wrong'. At a 76 mm sticker the roundel is 5.23 mm — roughly 60 resolvable elements at reading distance, i.e. plainly judgeable. Front-facing SKUs are therefore gated on the emblem; side-elevation SKUs, where only 1.62 mm hubcap badges remain, are not.

THE RENDER'S RED IMAGES SALMON AND MUST NOT BE SAMPLED. flank_compare on out/r75_side.png: photograph median (158,16,6) G/R 0.114 against the render's (196,81,67) G/R 0.422. And the photograph side is not a single number either — probe_rev71_red.py prints 'the photograph's red G/R is 0.0149 .. 0.0344, a 2.3x span. DO NOT QUOTE A SINGLE FIGURE FOR IT.' The palette must be DECLARED from the artwork masters and the one neutral-white-balance frame (ref_playa_34.png, neutral on the paving at 116,119,120), not eyedroppered off any render.

NO 3D EXPORT PATH. grep for export_scene/gltf/usd_export/fbx across the tree returns nothing; the only persistence is build.py's 'if os.environ.get("T1_SAVE"): bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(...)', .blend is gitignored, and T1_SAVE appears in none of the brief, the carriers, CLAUDE.md, README.md, START_HERE.md or OPEN_FINDINGS.md. THE 'EARLIER CARTOON VERSION' HE PRAISED IS NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY. 793 commits, no artefact, no deleted file, no path matching cartoon/toon/sticker; the only vector ever committed is vw_canonical_2019.svg; the repo's first commit records 'no git history was present in tarball'; and START_HERE.md still points at '/areas/tacombi-combi-sticker.md', which does not exist in this container. ARTWORK-MASTER DEFECTS THAT PROPAGATE INTO ANY HARVESTED SATELLITE: tex/lidmural.png is cropped at the bottom (F74a, still OPEN — flowers sliced mid-bloom, yellow side columns truncated) and lid_gen.py is not called by build.py, so regenerating it is a hand step; the pink star is built BELOW the Calidad burst where both red frames put it above-left (F16, OPEN), so draw that satellite from the photograph not the model; tex/senor.png contains no dark ink at all (measured: of pixels with alpha>200 the 1st-percentile luma is 168.3 and the fraction below luma 80 is 0.0000) while SPEC §3 requires the wordmark 'SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow' — so the shipped master is missing exactly the contrast that makes silver-on-red read; and tex/emblem.png (1024x1024) is an orphan no material binds, which texgen.py says the tree cannot regenerate — do not use it as a mark.

VW TRADEMARK EXPOSURE IS NAMED AND UNRESOLVED. The programme's output is commercial merchandise imagery of a trademarked vehicle carrying a trademarked roundel, and merchandise is where VW enforces. That this bus PAINTS OVER its roundel in body red (SPEC §3: 'painted RED on the cream nose, V above W, pressed relief not chrome') is a partial mitigation, and the conversion elements — counter, three hatches, lid, folk art, script — are not VW's at all. This is an owner-and-counsel question, not a design decision, and it should be asked before a print run rather than after.

PAPEL PICADO IS MEASURED ABSENT AND IS CLOSED TO RE-ASKING. SPEC.md: 'And there is no papel picado. The band across the top of the reference is a continuous flowering mass — 55.1 % foliage, 13.4 % crimson heads, 5.5 % cream florets, jagged interpenetrating lower edge, no flag silhouettes. Bunting in that render would be an invention.' The owner ruled 'Leave it open, I'll decide when the sticker is actually being built. DO NOT RE-PUT IT UNTIL THEN.' Design the slot; leave it empty; do not raise it.
first_moves: Render ONE alpha set and nothing else: T1_SUB=1 T1_ALPHA=1 T1_FX=0 T1_PREVIEW=front,side,hero34f,hero34r T1_PFX=a01 T1_RX=1600 T1_RY=1100 T1_SAMP=96, launched with setsid per F173. Then run python3 deliver.py --prefix a01 and READ C1's line, not the exit code. Do NOT route any of it through post.py — post.py returns colortype 2 and throws the silhouette away. This is the single dependency the whole die-cut half of the programme sits on and it has been one env var away for thirteen revisions.

Add a sticker18 camera to studio.views(): azimuth 18 degrees off the nose toward +Y (the serving side), eye height 1.55 m, tgt at roughly the same height, long lens or orthographic. Verify my arithmetic on hero34f first — loc=(12.20, 8.55, 3.55), tgt=(-0.15, 0.00, 1.34) gives azimuth 34.7 degrees and elevation 8.4 degrees at 3.55 m camera height, which is not the audit's specified viewpoint and is not close to it. Record that hero34f is on the correct side and front34 is not.

Run trace_outline.selftest() and watch it pass, then trace the alpha of a01_side and a01_sticker18 with trace_with_holes(). Measure and PRINT the silhouette's minimum notch width and minimum internal radius in final millimetres at sticker body lengths 51 / 76 / 102 / 152 mm. Expect the arch-to-tyre gap (0.50 / 0.74 / 1.00 / 1.48 mm) and the tail-board blade (~0.31 mm thick at 76 mm) to fail every threshold. That failure IS the cut-path brief — do not fix it by lowering the threshold.

Write ladder.py: import the constants (build.ROUNDEL_D, build.SCR, build.CAL, t1_detail.CAP_D, t1_detail.CAP_EMBLEM_D, t1_detail.LOUV_PITCH, t1_shell.BAYS, folk_gen.FLANK_ROSETTES, plus STATE.md's TYRE_D) and print final millimetres at a list of sticker lengths. Re-derive; do not transcribe the table in this report. Then PRINT the four sizes on the actual substrate, laminate them, and look at them at 400 mm — the ladder predicts which elements die, and only a print can confirm it.

Declare the palette in one file with provenance per swatch: one red, one cream, one gold, one dark, one silver. Source them from the artwork masters (tex/swirl.png 4096x4096, tex/senor.png 4096x1738, tex/lidmural.png 4096x2476, tex/calidad.png 3072x2267 — all verified by reading the PNG headers) and from ref_playa_34.png, the one frame HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §0.1 records as neutral on the paving. Do NOT eyedropper a render. Record in the same file that the tree currently holds four unreconciled reds and that this choice supersedes none of them for the 3D model.

Ship the matte side-elevation 'plate' SKU first, at 102 mm body (114.9 mm overall on the propped silhouette, 1.462:1). It is the least gated thing in the system: the side camera already exists and is orthographic at 1.52 m, the emblem is not resolvable on it, and a 1600 px master covers 102 mm at over 390 dpi. Use it as the pilot that proves the cut path, the vendor, the registration tolerance and the matte red compensation before any money goes near a sheet run.

Put ONE question to the owner, multiple choice, with printed proofs physically attached, using the question tool: the substrate and finish tier — (A) gloss white PVC, (B) matte white PVC, (C) clear PVC with the three serving hatches and the windscreen left unprinted, (D) brushed-silver holographic with spot underbase so the wordmark and the bulbs are metal. Do not ask him the papel picado (F18 forbids it until the sticker is being built) and do not ask him the size cold — but note that F192's own condition is met the moment a medium is named, so the sticker ladder is the legitimate occasion to close 'Bigger — large-format print', asked WITH the printed ladder in hand.

Before any of the above ships, get a written vendor answer to three questions: does the press have a white-ink channel (kills or confirms the clear-vinyl tier); what is the guaranteed contour-cut registration tolerance (I am designing to +/-0.5 mm, with 1.5 mm of printed bleed outside every cut line and a >=1.5 mm border on any bordered SKU); and what is the minimum kiss-cut web between adjacent stickers on a sheet (I am designing to 4 mm, and to no concave notch narrower than 3 mm, so the negative lifts in one pull).
what_would_embarrass_us: Handing anyone the deliver.py output folder. Its READ_ME_FIRST promises 'Every image here has a TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND' in the same run that prints 'PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY', tells the owner he has reported the emblem 'six times' when the brief says ninth, and lists the tyre tread and the roof loudspeakers as open defects when rev 74 shipped one and retired the other. It is the only document in the repo written for a non-technical reader and it is the one he would read.

Contour-cutting the true silhouette. At a 76 mm body the arch-to-tyre gap is 0.74 mm and the propped tail board reads 0.31 mm thick — the vinyl tears on weeding, the blade will not track the internal radius, and whatever survives lifts at the corner in a child's pocket within a week. A returned sticker is a worse outcome than a duller drawing.

Drawing a rayed-disc sun. AUDIT_rev43.md's rule is right and independently checkable: the vehicle already carries eleven radial bursts (the Calidad starburst, the mural rosettes, the hubcap rings, the headlamps, the wheel spokes), so a rayed sun competes with its own subject and the drawing loses its only light source to visual noise.

Sampling the brand red off a render. flank_compare reads the render at G/R 0.422 against the photograph's 0.114 on out/r75_side.png; the register calls it 'the largest colour error in the delivery frame' and says it 'images salmon where the bus is vivid red'. A printed sticker in that hue, beside the actual bus at the actual restaurant, is the most public possible version of that error.

Mixing livery states in one drawing — folk art plus a chalkboard lid, or the Nolita glass lettering on the Playa flank. The project has killed three findings on exactly this (F99, F100, F140) and the owner ruled it: geometry transfers between states, paint and artwork do not.

Promising 'the wheels as in the earlier cartoon version'. It is not in this repository, in any of 793 commits, and the path START_HERE.md points at does not exist here. Promising to match an artefact nobody in the room can look at is how the next revision discovers it matched nothing.

Scaling one master to four sizes. A 0.6 mm stroke scaled from 152 mm to 51 mm becomes 0.2 mm; the ten louvres (0.79 mm pitch at 152, 0.26 mm at 51), the rosette petals and the script's spiral counters all vanish in the same step, and nothing warns you — the file still opens, the PDF still previews, and the print comes back grey mush.

Putting a large, legible VW roundel at the centre of a merchandise sticker without the trademark question having been asked. Merchandise is precisely where Volkswagen enforces, and 'officially licensed' VW bus tees exist on the shelf for a reason.

Quoting any figure off out/ without naming the frame. out/ is untracked and starts empty, it currently holds both r75_side.png and r75b_side.png, and the last two revisions each recorded a reading attributed to a frame the probe could not have read. Every number in this brief that came from a frame names it.

Deciding the papel picado. It is measured ABSENT from the reference — the band in the photograph is a continuous flowering mass at 55.1 / 13.4 / 5.5 percent — and the owner explicitly parked it until the sticker is actually being built. Filling that slot on our own initiative would be inventing scene content into an artefact whose scene he personally locked.

expert_plans.discipline: Poster and large-format print art direction — composition, crop, scale, stock/ink, typography, series structure and edition mechanics, judged against what this specific render chain can actually deliver to a printer.

opportunities.idea: THE PLATE — a true 1:20 orthographic side elevation with measured dimension lines and no perspective. Landscape ISO sheet, image in the upper two-thirds, a caption band beneath carrying only dimension rules and figures. This is the single strongest anti-advert move available, because an advert can never show you this: a photograph of a vehicle is always a projection, and `studio.views()['side']` is `lens=None, ortho=5.90` — a genuine parallel projection. Every number on the sheet is machine-measured and defensible from STATE.md: L 4.065 m, W 1.7497 m, wheelbase 2.4000, TRACK_F 1.3690 / TRACK_R 1.3590, TYRE_D 0.6649, roof at rear axle 1.9833, rake 17.75 mm/m. A car advert sells you a feeling about a machine; a plate hands you the machine as a fact and lets you live with it. Existing aspect is already nearly right — 1600x1100 = 1.4545:1 against ISO landscape 1.414:1, so the reframe is a 3% trim, not a new camera.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Nothing else in the world can produce this. The reference set is three usable folk-art-livery photographs, all perspective, all warm-balanced, one with the cab door open occluding the nose. The orthographic elevation exists only because someone spent 75 revisions measuring the object. It is also the crop where the model is strongest: I measured out/r75_side.png at 77.8% x 77.5% frame fill with clean margin on all four sides and no clipping, unlike front (clipped both ends) and hero34r (clipped at the right edge).
opportunities.effort: LOW–MEDIUM. The frame exists today. Needs: a poster-aspect re-render at scale, a decision on ortho_scale margin, and the typography. No model work.

opportunities.idea: CROP THE ADVERT OUT — the aft-55% crop of the side elevation. Cut through the vehicle at roughly the B-pillar and keep only: the counter cantilever and its brass nosing, serving bay 3, the 100% Calidad sunburst on the cream, the louvre block, the rear wheel bullseye, and the tail board's thin blade running out of frame top-right. Advertising has one inviolable law — never cut the product. Cutting it is therefore the fastest way to signal this is a picture, not a sale. It also reads as a shopfront rather than a vehicle, which is what the object actually is.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Three defects are cropped out by construction and none of them need fixing first: the VW roundel (the owner's ninth report, F191/F234 both standing), the nose (F197, open), and the front bumper bow (F231, unrecoverable). The crop is also the LOWEST red-per-unit-area frame available, which minimises exposure to the render's largest measured colour error — flank_compare on out/r75_side.png reads render G/R 0.422 against the photograph's 0.114. Less red on the sheet, less salmon to explain.
opportunities.effort: LOW. It is a crop of a frame that already exists. Ship a proof this week.

opportunities.idea: THE THREE HOLES — a horizontal triptych of the three serving apertures, cropped tight above and below so the bays alone fill the sheet, galley visible through them. Tacombi's own founder account says the $3,000 donor bus was 'missing three of its windows'; the signature feature is an accident of cheapness. That is a story only this object owns, and the composition states it without a word: three rectangles where windows should be, with a kitchen inside.
opportunities.why_this_asset: STATE.md reads 'open serving apertures on +Y: 3' and 'bay widths 0.516 0.515 0.516' — the bays are EQUAL, so the crop is a genuine rhythm, not an approximate one. Everything visible through them is built: roughly thirty gal_* meshes, plancha, galley_top, galley_backdrop. This is also the frame that carries the white bobble fringe, which is the vehicle's most distinctive texture and reads as a scalloped line at poster scale.
opportunities.effort: MEDIUM. Wants a bay-level camera at the right height rather than a crop of the 5.90 ortho; and F45 (roof-aperture interior) and F15 (unlit roofed body, 6.92e5 px²) are both ungated illumination items that sit directly behind this crop.

opportunities.idea: THE BOARD — the flower mural as its own poster, flat, at full bleed, with no vehicle at all. tex/lidmural.png is a 4096x2476 master: eleven stylised flowers with concentric rings on orange stems over dense red scrollwork on a dark brown ground, framed in olive-yellow menu strips lettered in dark red. It is the loudest and most beautiful piece of graphic design on the vehicle and it needs no render, no camera, no lighting rig and no delivery chain to print.
opportunities.why_this_asset: It routes entirely around every technical risk on this list — no stitch, no 8-bit optics pass, no seam, no gloss deficit, no salmon red, no emblem. It is flat art at 4K. It is also the one poster you could physically print next week. CAUTION: F74(a) is open and correct — the shipped asset is CROPPED AT THE BOTTOM, the bottom flower row sliced mid-bloom and the yellow side columns truncated, where ref_side.jpg shows a board framed on all four sides. Print it as-is and you print the defect at a metre wide.
opportunities.effort: MEDIUM — but the effort is one asset regeneration in lid_gen.py, which build.py does not call, so it is hand-run and does not touch the model.

opportunities.idea: FOUR ELEVATIONS, ONE SHEET, ONE SCALE — front / side / rear / plan on a grid, all orthographic, all at identical px/m, with a single scale bar serving all four. The set reads as a technical document, which is the register furthest from an advert and the register people actually frame. Print it big; the pleasure is in walking up to it.
opportunities.why_this_asset: All four cameras already exist in studio.views() — front, side, rear, topdown — and three of the four have never been rendered by any preview list in ten revisions. The 'one scale' claim is only honest because the cameras are orthographic and the mesh is measured; on any perspective view it would be a lie.
opportunities.effort: MEDIUM. BLOCKED BY A DEFECT I MEASURED TODAY — see 'name required model work'. The front and rear orthos CLIP the vehicle at both ends at the standing aspect. Fix that first or the plate ships with the wheels and the raised board cut off.

opportunities.idea: THE PARTS — six small prints at one common scale, sold as a set: the hubcap bullseye (chrome ring / cream dish / red dome / cream VW), the amber tail-lamp oval in its bright bezel, the empty chrome plate frame reading '1963', the bobble fringe, the bulb string on its brass drip rail, and the counter's radiused corner with its brass nosing. A poster earns a wall by rewarding proximity; a set of six earns a whole wall and turns one image into a purchase decision with a natural upsell.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Every one of these is built and named in STATE.md (cap/capring/capvw, tail, plate + plate_digits, fringe, bulb_string, counter_nosing) and every one is a thing a stock VW-bus print does not possess — they are the CONVERSION, not the donor vehicle. The set deliberately excludes the emblem, so it is unblocked by F191. '1963' in particular is free, true and human: the owner dated the object on its own back.
opportunities.effort: MEDIUM. Six camera set-ups in the detail_f class (lens=100, f/6.3), plus a real look at each crop — CLAUDE.md's own list of shipped defects found only by looking includes 'a disc of body red at the centre of every tail lamp' and 'hubcaps that render as five-petal flowers', both of which are in this set.

opportunities.idea: LEAVE CMYK ALTOGETHER — a four-or-five-ink spot screen print on uncoated stock: a spot warm vermillion, a warm off-white/cream, a folk-art ochre-gold, a warm near-black, plus silver for the wordmark. AUDIT_rev43's colour-separation row already establishes the vehicle as 'ONE 70° hue wedge plus four neutrals', and folk_gen.py's own component census says the largest three gold components carry 84.4% of all the gold with 48 of 66 components carrying 2.29% — a measured licence to delete forty-eight marks and lose almost nothing.
opportunities.why_this_asset: This inverts the project's biggest weakness into a non-issue. The render's red is measured ~dE 23 from the photograph and the paint reads matte (gloss_compare: spread 0.412 of the photograph, FAIL against a 0.60 bar). Both are photoreal failures. A spot-colour separation does not carry gloss and does not carry a process red — you choose the ink, you hit full chroma on uncoated stock that CMYK cannot reach, and the flatness stops being a deficit and becomes the idiom. It also honours the object: the real bus is hand-painted flat colour, not automotive clearcoat.
opportunities.effort: MEDIUM–HIGH. Needs a separation pass off the render's own layers and a printer conversation. But it removes the two hardest fidelity blockers from the critical path entirely.

opportunities.idea: THE STEP — a one-or-two-colour silhouette poster of the open vehicle. Lid up on one side, counter cantilevered on the other: this object is ASYMMETRIC and STEPPED when it is working, and no car has that. Print the outline solid, at full bleed, cut by the sheet edge, with the shadow as the second ink.
opportunities.why_this_asset: deliver.py's trimmed/ + layers/ output IS this geometry and it is already measured and guarded: the vehicle side is '97.1% fully opaque and 99.99% ONE connected component', and the shadow separates cleanly ('near-black, max channel < 12/255' against a vehicle mean of 143). The contact shadow is also the single largest item in visibility_budget at 3.83e6 px² — 'what makes it read planted rather than floating'. Making it a designable second ink rather than a rendering artefact is the whole move.
opportunities.effort: LOW once T1_ALPHA is proven — and proving it is a prerequisite for the entire programme anyway (see blockers).

opportunities.idea: SPOT FOIL OR SPOT UV ON THE BULB STRING ONLY. The lit festoon is the vehicle's sole self-luminous element and reads in every reference frame as a continuous glowing amber line tracing the silhouette — the drip rail, the rear roof dome, the raised lid, the tail board. A metallic or gloss-varnish treatment on that one path catches the actual light in the actual room the poster hangs in. A printed highlight cannot do that; a car advert would never think to.
opportunities.why_this_asset: F144 in the register says the render's bulbs 'READ AS PEARLS, NOT LIGHTS' — the model cannot currently make this element glow. Moving it into the finish rather than the render turns an open model defect into the poster's most memorable physical property, with zero model work.
opportunities.effort: LOW design effort, MEDIUM print effort (one extra pass, one extra plate). Adds cost per sheet — put it on the limited edition only.

opportunities.idea: A 1:1 WHEEL. TYRE_D is 0.6649 m; on a 700 mm sheet the wheel is life size and the poster carries a scale claim nobody else can make. Four concentric bands of the exact brand palette — black tyre, cream rim dish, red dome, cream roundel — filling a square sheet.
opportunities.why_this_asset: It is a ready-made badge, and 1:1 is a thing only a measured model can honestly assert. CAUTION, stated up front: STATE.md says 'hubcap badge is SELF-CONSISTENCY ONLY — CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC has never been compared to a frame; see PHOTOS_WANTED item 7.' A 1:1 hubcap publishes an unverified proportion at maximum size, which is exactly the wrong direction. Either close item 7 (one close square-on hubcap photograph) or crop the badge out and print the rim geometry, which IS measured.
opportunities.effort: MEDIUM, plus one owner photograph to make it honest.

opportunities.idea: THE EDITION AS A DESIGNED OBJECT — two tiers, not one. OPEN edition: matte-coated litho, unnumbered, shop price. LIMITED edition: spot-colour screen print on heavy uncoated, hand-numbered in pencil lower-left, no signature, authenticated by a BLIND EMBOSS chop rather than a certificate card. Foot of every sheet carries a 6 pt colophon naming the render's own real figures — revision, resolution, sample count, date.
opportunities.why_this_asset: There is no artist's hand to sign a render, and a forged signature on a CGI print is embarrassing; a chop is the correct authentication for an authorless work and gives the buyer a tactile reason to hold the paper. The colophon is where this project's method becomes a selling point: 'rev 76 · 3840 × 2640 · 256 spp · 2026' is unfakeable provenance and completely anti-advert. Edition band: 100–250 for a brand this size. Anything over 500 is a print run, not an edition — price and describe it as one.
opportunities.effort: LOW. Design and print-spec work only.

opportunities.idea: THE DAY — one view, three lights: workshop fluorescent, Nolita cool grey-blue market fill, Playa warm open shade. The same object, three emotional products. This is the most beautiful idea on the list and I am naming it with its blockers attached rather than pretending it is cheap.
opportunities.why_this_asset: F259 is an owner ruling that OPENS the rig: 'Relight the studio and fix the ground if necessary' — the studio stays, the lighting is now open, and 'DO NOT change RED' is the one constraint. The cream is already measured to change role with the light across the three reference scenes (skylit near-neutral, warm ivory, grey-green under fluorescent), so this is a grade, not a repaint.
opportunities.effort: HIGH and PARTLY BLOCKED. F57 records T1_SCENE=playa renders no vehicle at all ('a dark cylinder on a grey plane'); F92 parks the Playa hero as 'DEPRIORITISED, NOT CANCELLED' and explicitly licenses nothing to do now. Route it through T1_ALPHA + composite instead of through the in-tree environment path, and put the Playa question to the owner rather than acting on it.

blockers: THE LARGE-FORMAT CHAIN HAS NEVER BEEN PROVEN AT SCALE AND THE HONEST CEILING IS SMALLER THAN THE AMBITION. Highest ever rendered: 4320x2880 at rev 15, but through hero.py's PAD chain, on a model 60 revisions old, and the frame is gone (out/ is untracked and starts empty). The CURRENT chain (hq_render.py's MARGIN chain) has been proven ONCE, at 3840x2640, at rev 57, 106.8 min, worst seam z=1.62 — and that frame is also gone. Nothing since rev 70 has exceeded 1600x1100. THE ARITHMETIC A PRINTER NEEDS: 3840 px is 325 mm at 300 dpi, 488 mm at 200 dpi, 650 mm at 150 dpi. So the proven chain already supports an A2 poster at ~232 dpi, which is genuinely fine. A1 (594 mm) at 200 dpi wants 4677 px — 22% above proven. B1 (707 mm) at 200 dpi wants 5567 px — 45% above. That is the real ladder: A2 today, A1 after one proving run, B1 only after the seam detector has been exercised there.

EVERYTHING DOWNSTREAM OF THE RENDER IS 8-BIT, AND THIS IS THE BIGGEST PRINT-SPECIFIC RISK NOBODY HAS NAMED. studio.setup_render sets color_depth = '16' and every PNG in out/ carries IHDR depth=16 — then stitch.py does `np.array(Image.open(p).convert("RGBA"))` and post.py reads through the same PIL path, both truncating to uint8 silently. On a 1 m print, an 8-bit soft vignette across a large flat cream body is textbook banding territory, and post.py's own default applies a 5.5% corner vignette. This will be discovered at the printer if it is not fixed before. Mitigation is either a 16-bit read path or a deliberate dither on export; do not just hope.

post.py DESTROYS ALPHA — measured: feed it a colortype-6 RGBA file and the output header reads colortype=2. So you can have optics (bloom/CA/vignette/grain) OR a cut-out silhouette, never both, and post.py's docstring nowhere says so. For a poster you generally want a controlled ground AND the optics, which means compositing onto your ground BEFORE post — but post's backdrop logic assumes white. Plan the order deliberately.

post.py's DEFAULT BACKDROP IS NOT WHITE. Live constant is BACKDROP = 'headroom' with BACKDROP_PEAK = 252.0, while the module docstring still claims '--backdrop white is the SPEC sec.6 lock'. A render field at 252 sitting inside a #FFFFFF poster margin is a visible rectangle on the sheet. Either render RGBA and composite onto your own ground, or pass --backdrop white explicitly. Never eyeball it.

hq_render.py DOES NOT DISABLE PER-STRIP OPTICS. grep -c T1_FX hq_render.py is 0, while hero.py — the chain it replaced — sets T1_FX=0 explicitly and its docstring says why: 'Per-strip optics band at the seams.' studio.composite_on_white defaults T1_FX to 1. Unless the operator exports T1_FX=0 by hand, the delivery render applies bloom/CA/vignette/grain per strip and then post.py applies a SECOND pass on the stitch. No document names this step.

expert_plans.discipline:
BRAND STRATEGY — positioning and creative territory.

THE POSITIONING LINE: **"The bus that stopped."**

Longer form, for internal use: *Every other VW bus in the merchandise category is going somewhere. Ours arrived, got cut open, and started feeding people.* Tacombi owns ARRIVAL — the category's entire emotional stock is escape.

This is not a copywriting flourish; it is the brand's own published fact and SPEC.md grades it **S** (sourced, Tacombi's own account), §0.1: *"We purchased a 1963 'combi' bus in Mexico City, wheeled it slowly (very slowly) through the Yucatan peninsula and parked it comfortably in … Playa del Carmen. The engine was scrapped, transmission sold, seats swapped for cooking equipment, and the roof was reeled back to produce a taco serving stand."* The object is a BUILDING THAT WAS ONCE A VEHICLE. It cannot drive. It has no engine and no gearbox. Founder Dario Wolos, same section, grade **S**: the bus was green, cost **$3,000**, was *"missing three of its windows"* and *"only had the front bench"*; he *"figured out how to cut open the Tacombi."*

Two strategic consequences fall straight out of that, and both are load-bearing for everything below.

1. **THE ANTI-TROPE IS FREE.** The VW-bus merch market is sunset, surf, palms, peace signs, daisies, 70s wash, minimal line art, blueprint. Every one of those sells MOTION and ESCAPE, and every one of them is the American counterculture reading of this body shape. Tacombi's own name refuses it: "combi" in Mexico is a pesero — a working-class microbus that hauls people to work. So the brand's name commits it to the workhorse reading while its silhouette invites the Woodstock one. We do not fight that with taste; we fight it with the handbrake. The bus never moves in any asset we make. Ever.

2. **"COMBI" IS ALSO THE WRONG BODY.** Honesty ceiling: the Mexican combi that carries the pesero meaning is the later Puebla-built bay-window T2; ours is a 1963 split-screen T1 (SPEC §0.1), which IS the silhouette the hippie market wore out. So we cannot escape the trope by profile. We escape it by everything above the sill and behind the cab door — the counter, the three hatches, the propped lid, the bulbs, the signwriting. **The anti-derivative content is the CONVERSION, not the vehicle.** That single sentence should govern every crop, every camera, and every die-cut in the program.

WHAT THE PROGRAM SHOULD SAY: *We drove it once. Then we stopped, cut three holes in the side, and started cooking.* Understatement, Spanish first, English second, and never a superlative. The existing shop voice is already deadpan leisure-outfitter — "purpose-built," "expo," "monument," "horizon" — and that register is right: it treats the bus as EQUIPMENT, which is what it now is. (Ceiling: those product names come from a WebSearch summary of shop.tacombi.com, which was EGRESS_BLOCKED in this container. Nobody in this session has seen a single piece of current Tacombi merchandise. That is the biggest gap in this brief and it is one browser session away from closing.)

ADVERT vs. THING-A-PERSON-WANTS — three tests, in order of power:

**Test 1 — THE LOGO-REMOVAL TEST.** An advert dies without the wordmark. A keeper gets BETTER without it and is still recognisable. Tacombi passes this test better than almost any restaurant brand alive, because the object has a silhouette: three holes in a flank, a slab counter cantilevered past the tail, a lid propped like an awning, a line of bulbs tracing the roof. **That outline is the logo.** Design so that removing the word "Tacombi" costs nothing. This is also the legal hedge — VW enforces its marks against merchandise and claims the bus shape itself, and our most-photographed face carries a VW roundel that the owner has now rejected nine times (F191 and F234 both stand). Everything that makes this brand ownable is a thing VW never built.

**Test 2 — THE INDEPENDENT-USE TEST.** Does the object do a job in the wearer's life that has nothing to do with us? A tote carries groceries. A beanie is warm. A sticker covers a scratch on a scooter. Merch that only signals is an advert with a price tag.

**Test 3 — THE INSIDER TEST.** Does it carry one small true thing that rewards the person who knows and does not punish the person who doesn't? We have an unusual number of these already measured and on the vehicle: **"1963"** embossed on an empty chrome plate frame (SPEC §4) — the object dated itself. **"Gracias por su Preferencia"** hand-lettered on the counter fascia. **"100% Calidad"** on a spiky sunburst. **"$3,000."** **"Missing three of its windows."** A person who ate there gets it; a stranger just sees a good graphic. That asymmetry is exactly what makes something get kept.

THE THING THE PROGRAM MUST NOT SAY: nostalgia. This bus is not a memory, it is open for lunch. The record's own live tension — SPEC §3 locks the finish **WEATHERED** while the owner ruled at rev 61 *"I want this 3d model to look like new. Enhanced from the photo."* — resolves cleanly on the brand side even though the model side is unresolved: **the bus is WORN but the brand is NEW.** Patina is a fact about the object, not a mood for the campaign. Surface that to him; do not silently pick a side (the record explicitly forbids that).

opportunities.idea: TERRITORY 1 — ARRIVED. The handbrake, not the highway. The emotional payload is the RELIEF OF STOPPING: you have got where you were going, sit down, eat. Design rules: the vehicle is never in motion, never on a road, never at a jaunty angle; it is always planted and always DEPLOYED — counter down, lid up, bulbs lit, something happening at the hatch. Motion vocabulary for any animation is DEPLOYMENT, not driving: the lid rising, the counter dropping, the bulb string igniting left-to-right, the tail board propping. Wheels never turn. Copy register: coordinates and dates, no verbs of travel. 'Playa del Carmen, 2006. Handbrake.' / 'Arrived once. Never left.' The hero format is enormous white space, one horizon line, one vehicle, small type — the opposite of the category's full-bleed sunset.
opportunities.why_this_asset: It is the brand's own S-graded published story (SPEC §0.1: 'The engine was scrapped, transmission sold'), so it is unfalsifiable and uncopyable — no other VW-bus seller can claim a bus that cannot drive. It also converts a production liability into a rule: TREAD_LUGS = 64 is commented in t1_detail.py as 'DECLARED, inside the MEASURED bracket 48..84 (F308)' and probe_rev74_tread's T2 refuses to publish a count at all, so a spinning wheel would publish a claim the project cannot defend. A stationary bus never has to. Uses the `side` view, which is the only camera with a real render history (27 mentions across LEDGER_rev66..75 versus 1 for hero34r).
opportunities.effort: Cheap. Needs no new geometry and no new render — the four r75 frames plus judge_set.sh's optics pass already support a poster series. 1 designer-week for the layout system.

opportunities.idea: TERRITORY 2 — THE CUT. Hospitality as a hole in the wall. The three serving hatches — the single most recognisable thing about this vehicle — exist because the $3,000 donor bus was already missing three windows. Emotion: generosity made out of damage; the opening as the invitation. Design into a GRAPHIC DEVICE, not a picture: three rounded-rectangle apertures in a row, in the measured proportion (STATE.md: 'open serving apertures on +Y: 3' / 'bay widths 0.516 0.515 0.516' — they are EQUAL, and SPEC's old 0.507/0.516/0.526 taper is retired), optionally carrying the white bobble fringe. Use it as a masking/window system across every medium: menu panels, photo crops, packaging die-cuts, animation lower-thirds, a three-panel grid on a tote. Copy: 'It was missing three windows. We left them that way.'
opportunities.why_this_asset: This is the most ownable single fact in the entire record and it is currently doing NO work: SPEC §0.1 grades it E (inference) — "'Missing three of its windows' is almost certainly *why* the show side became three serving hatches: the donor bus already had no glass there." A three-aperture mark is a logo that is not the VW roundel, which matters twice over: VW enforces its marks against merchandise and claims the bus shape itself, and our roundel is the owner's ninth reported defect (probe_rev46_vw C8 live: 'photo 3.39, built 2.84 — the built cells are 1.19x TOO ROUND'). It gives the brand a mark it fully owns, drawn from the exact feature the model measures best.
opportunities.effort: Cheap to design (it is a proportion, already measured). Medium to systematise across media. Zero model work required.

opportunities.idea: TERRITORY 3 — THE PAINTED CEILING. The lid is the brand's canvas, and it is a PROGRAM, not a graphic. When the roof lid goes up, a van becomes a room with a painted ceiling — flower mural, olive-yellow menu strips lettered in dark red, bulbs along the frame. That gesture is the most photogenic thing this object does and its whole payload is SURPRISE: industrial shell outside, fiesta overhead. Design into a rotating commissioned-lid series — seasonal, city-specific, painted by named Mexican rotulistas and folk painters — rendered on the model and merchandised as the flat square artwork ALONE: bandana, scarf, tote panel, tile, album-format print, phone wallpaper, animated title card. The lid is where live copy legitimately lives (menu, city, date) because the vehicle itself already has a chalkboard-lid state that does exactly that.
opportunities.why_this_asset: The design family already treats the lid as a variable canvas and the repo holds the evidence: the red bus carries the flower mural, and IMG_2073.jpeg / ref_workshop.jpg show the GREEN sister ship with a completely different lid treatment. That makes seasonal liveries IN CHARACTER rather than invention. The master is high-resolution and on disk (tex/lidmural.png, 4096x2476), and the lid is already hinged geometry (STATE.md: lid_board, lid_main, lid_rail x2, lid_strut x2). It also converts an artist-collaboration budget into brand equity instead of ad spend, which is precisely Test 2 and Test 3 above.
opportunities.effort: Medium, and it names REQUIRED MODEL WORK: F74(a) is open — 'tex/lidmural.png is cropped at the bottom … the yellow side columns are truncated, where ref_side.jpg shows a board framed on all four sides. The render is faithful to the asset, so the defect is in lid_gen.py's output.' And lid_gen.py is NOT called by build.py, so regeneration is a hand step or the render silently uses the old texture. Fix the crop before any lid artwork ships. Also unresolved and worth one owner question: lid_gen.py says the mural is on the OUTWARD face, SPEC §4 says the underside — that decides whether a closed-lid render shows flowers or plain cream.

opportunities.idea: TERRITORY 4 — THE HAND. Rotulismo: something a person painted, with a brush, on a Tuesday. This is the anti-CGI territory and the one that keeps a photoreal program from feeling like stock. The vehicle's lettering is not typography, it is signwriting — silver leaf with real tarnish, an ornate swash T, rolled spiral counters in a/c/o/m/b, hand-painted menu cards, 'Gracias por su Preferencia' in red cursive under condensed black caps. Design into a LETTERING SYSTEM rather than a typeface: headline art hand-drawn and kept irregular, silver rendered as an actual FINISH (foil stamp on print, metallic thread or puff on apparel, real specular in motion), Spanish set first and larger, English small and beneath. Never set the wordmark in a system face — the owner rejected exactly that by name at rev 8: 'That script i see on the p9 hero is NOT it.'
opportunities.why_this_asset: script_gen.py exists precisely because a font was refused, and it records the ink as measured, not chosen: 'ink is neutral silver, not white and not gold: median RGB (127,122,125), saturation 0.080, over a ground of (129,21,14).' The owner also ruled the finish (F157, rev 62): 'Bright silver, same as Tacombi' — which overrides SPEC §3's WEATHERED lock FOR THAT WORD ONLY. The wordmark is simultaneously the most merch-facing element on the vehicle and the brand's voice in every other channel, so its fidelity ranks far above its pixel area.
opportunities.effort: 1 revision of model work, and it is the CHEAPEST VISIBLE IMPROVEMENT IN THE INVENTORY. SPEC §3 requires 'SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow' and the shipped asset has NO dark ink at all — measured on tex/senor.png (4096x1738 RGBA): among pixels with alpha>200 the 1st-percentile luma is 168.3 and the fraction below luma 80 is 0.0000, while grep for keyline/shadow in script_gen.py and t1_mats.silver_script finds nothing. Silver on red without a keyline loses nearly all its contrast, which is exactly why the wordmark reads flat in the render and crisp in the photograph — and why it will die on a t-shirt. Note script_gen.py is NOT called by build.py; regenerate tex/senor.png by hand. Separately, flank_compare on out/r75_side.png says the lockup is MIS-PLACED: 'the render's lockup has to move +76.2 mm forward and -47.6 mm down', with an independent route agreeing at +83/+80 mm aft. Placement survives every downscale; fix it in the same edit.

opportunities.idea: TERRITORY 5 — THE KEEPSAKE. For children; the thing families keep. This is the owner's own oldest brief and it is the only territory with art direction already locked, so ONE track should honour it deliberately: 'cartoon with rendered depth', 'nothing but the bus, die-cut tight, plus the sun and the papel picado', for children at the restaurant, 'should spark joy and be something families keep'. The strategic unlock nobody has stated in these words: THE STICKER WAS NEVER A FIDELITY ARTEFACT. SPEC measures the reference and says flatly 'And there is no papel picado. The band across the top of the reference is a continuous flowering mass — 55.1 % foliage, 13.4 % crimson heads, 5.5 % cream florets … Bunting in that render would be an invention.' He locked the bunting into the sticker anyway. That is sanctioned decorative invention — a licence to CHARM rather than replicate — and it should govern the whole keepsake tier: kid-scale objects (sticker sheets, a paper model, a colouring placemat, a lunchbox, a window cling) drawn with warmth and no obligation to the measurements.
opportunities.why_this_asset: Half the asset already exists and is verified: deliver.py's trimmed/ output is the die-cut silhouette (F161, MEASURED-rev62, and the shadow/vehicle split is measured — 'the vehicle side is 97.1 % fully opaque and 99.99 % ONE connected component'). And the RENDERING TECHNIQUE was written down and then lost: NEXT_CONTEXT_PROMPT_rev39.md §7 item 3 said 'Style LOCKED by me: cartoon with rendered depth — vector line and flat colour, shading and occlusion sampled from the 3D asset', and the clause after the em-dash was dropped by rev 43 and is missing from every carrier since. That is a buildable pipeline, and deliver.py's layers/ already emits exactly its two inputs: combi_*_no_shadow.png for the flat fills and combi_*_shadow_only.png for the occlusion pass. Restore that clause to a carrier (rule 16).
opportunities.effort: Medium, and GATED — do not offer this AS the F18 deliverable. F18's trigger is 'build it after the model is done', restated at rev 62 as 'once i determine the model is done', and F191/F193 show he has held that gate four times. Offer the keepsake tier as a DIFFERENT artefact and say so in the proposal, and the hold stops being a blocker. Also: do NOT re-put the papel-picado question — he ruled 'Leave it open, I'll decide when the sticker is actually being built.'

opportunities.idea: THE VOICE THAT RUNS ACROSS ALL FIVE — DEADPAN EQUIPMENT. Present the bus the way a catalogue presents a tool: straight on, named, numbered, unglamorised. 'Unit 01. 1963. Playa del Carmen. Engine: none.' This is the ONE register where a photoreal render is genuinely the right medium rather than an expensive way to make an illustration, and it turns 75 revisions of measurement into content — dimensions as design.
opportunities.why_this_asset: It matches the existing shop voice ('purpose-built', 'expo', 'monument') and it uses the project's real distinctive asset: nobody else has measured this vehicle. THE TRAP, NAMED: the blueprint/exploded-diagram move is a saturated stock category (Dreamstime carries a standing 'Vw Van Blueprint Stock Illustrations' shelf) and it is the obvious way to dramatise a 3D model. The difference that makes it ours: a stock blueprint annotates a generic VW. Ours annotates the CONVERSION — the counter overhang, the equal 0.516 m bays, the tail board at 38°, the propped lid, 'engine: none'. A spec sheet of the parts VW never made. If it could be drawn from a factory manual, do not draw it.
opportunities.effort: Cheap once the alpha path works. Needs no new geometry.

opportunities.idea: MAKE THE BULB LINE THE MOTION SIGNATURE. The lit festoon traces the whole vehicle's outline in a single continuous stroke — drip rail, over the rear roof dome, along the propped tail board. Three shapes reproduce the read — which is exactly what screen-print, embroidery and vinyl need.

blockers: THERE IS NO WAY TO RENDER THIS VEHICLE WITHOUT THE VW ROUNDEL, AND I CHECKED THE SOURCE. `build.py` runs `vr, vd = D.roundel(R=ROUNDEL_D / 2)` and `for b in D.vw_logo_fit(ROUNDEL_D / 2, x=GLYPH_X):` with no env guard on either, assigning material `"roundelred"` to both. `T1_VW_NOARC`, `T1_VW_TRACED`, `T1_VW_FREE` and `T1_VW_CAPMIN` all change the mark's construction; none removes it. The hubcap glyphs (`capvw`, 8 objects in STATE.md) have no switch either. Every risk-reduction strategy that depends on omitting or repainting the mark is blocked until `T1_VW_MARK` exists.

NO CUT-OUT ASSET EXISTS TODAY, AND HAS NOT FOR THIRTEEN REVISIONS. Every frame in `out/` is `colortype=2` (RGB, no alpha); `deliver.py` correctly refuses with `CONTROLS: 4 checked, 1 FAILED -- C1` and `PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY`; `delivery/` does not exist on disk. `T1_ALPHA` appears in ZERO ledgers, so the capability the owner's own ruling turns on — "it is going on different backgrounds" — is a rev-62 result carried forward on paper, never re-run. Die-cut, compositing, apparel and motion all sit behind one env var and one render that nobody has done.

`post.py` DESTROYS ALPHA — measured, colortype 6 in, colortype 2 out. Optics (bloom/CA/vignette/grain) and a cut-out are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE from this repo, and no document says so. A designer routing an alpha master through the documented delivery chain silently loses the silhouette.

THE ONE CUSTOMER-FACING DOCUMENT IN THE REPO IS FACTUALLY WRONG IN FOUR WAYS, and it ships even when the script refuses. `deliver.py`'s READ_ME_FIRST says the emblem "READS AS AN X" and was "reported six times" (it is a V over a W and it is his NINTH report), that "the tyres have no tread" (shipped at rev 74, F308) and that "Two loudspeakers on the roof are missing" (retired as a POSE at rev 74, F309) — while asserting "Every image here has a TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND" in the same run that printed PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY. In an IP-sensitive program the document that leaves the building is the last thing that may be wrong.

NO 3D EXPORT PATH. `grep` for `export_scene|gltf|usd_export|fbx` across the tree returns nothing; the only persistence is `if os.environ.get("T1_SAVE"): bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(...)`, `.blend` is gitignored, and `T1_SAVE` appears in NO handoff document. The owner's stated goal is "a 3d render from which to build promotional material" and what exists is a 2D PNG generator. A designer cannot relight, re-angle, or hand the asset to anyone.

NO LARGE-FORMAT CAPABILITY IS PROVEN. Nothing above 1600x1100 exists on disk (`out/` is untracked and starts empty); `grep -c T1_FX hq_render.py` returns 0 where the chain it replaced forced optics off per strip; `stitch.py` and `post.py` are both 8-bit. F192 says "3840 is NOT the target" and the exact dimension is OPEN. Poster and banner deliverables need a resolution decision from the owner AND a proving run before anything is promised.

THE DELIVERY RENDER IS UNDER A STANDING OWNER HOLD (F191 "Keep holding — fix the emblem first", F193 "the bus be ready before investing seriously in the render"), and F18's sticker trigger — "build it after the model is done" — has not fired. Exploratory work, variant switches and asset plumbing are NOT held; the finished delivery render is. Say which one you are proposing, in the proposal, and the hold stops being a blocker.

THE LEGAL POSTURE IS UNKNOWN AND NOT RESOLVABLE HERE. Nothing in this repository records whether Tacombi holds any VW licence, has any arrangement, or has ever been contacted. Depicting a real, heavily modified vehicle the company itself owns, in that company's own promotional material, is a materially different posture from selling generic 'VW Bus' merch — but WHICH way it cuts is a lawyer's call on the actual products and the actual markets, not a design judgement and not something I can settle from the record.

TACOMBI'S OWN BRAND ASSETS ARE UNVERIFIED. `shop.tacombi.com`, `tacombi.com` and `fontsinuse.com` all returned EGRESS_BLOCKED; the typeface list (Cooper Black / Davida / ITC Bookman / Bauhaus) and the agency credit are second-hand search summaries of a page nobody opened. This is one browser session away from being closed by the owner.

THE 'EARLIER CARTOON VERSION' THE OWNER PRAISED IS NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY. 793 commits, no matching path, no matching deleted file, no matching blob; `START_HERE.md` points at `/areas/tacombi-combi-sticker.md` and `/areas` does not exist in this container. Any promise to 'match the wheels from the earlier cartoon' is a promise against an artefact nobody in this session can see. Treat the wheel treatment as an OPEN design decision to show him — which is also a free hand.

THE STICKER SPEC IS TRUNCATED AND ITS SCALE IS LOST. AUDIT_rev43.md §5's STICKER rows are hard-cut at fixed field widths (every `fix location` cell exactly 120 chars, the ceiling paragraph exactly 900) and no longer version exists in git history. Every millimetre rule in it — 0.159 m minimum cut feature, 0.15 mm line floor, 0.40 mm sacrifice threshold — is a projection through a stated scale that DID NOT SURVIVE THE CUT. Treat those figures as orderings, not dimensions. F18's claim that 'the ASSET is missing, not the spec' is over-stated.

MODEL WORK THE MERCH PROGRAM ACTUALLY NEEDS, NAMED: (a) `T1_VW_MARK`; (b) `T1_ALPHA` exercised and `deliver.py`'s C1 watched going green; (c) `post.py` given an alpha-preserving path or a documented refusal; (d) `deliver.py`'s READ_ME_FIRST corrected against OPEN_FINDINGS with an arithmetic guard row, not a grep; (e) sub-crop presets; (f) an export path; (g) `tex/lidmural.png` regenerated to fix F74(a)'s bottom crop — and note `lid_gen.py` is NOT called by `build.py`, so that is a hand step or the render silently keeps the old file.
first_moves: ASK THE OWNER ONE MULTIPLE-CHOICE QUESTION, WITH THE QUESTION TOOL, AND ATTACH TWO CROPS: the nose roundel from `out/r75_front.png` beside a counter-and-tail-board crop from a `hero34r` frame. The question is a PREMISE CHECK, not a legal one: does Tacombi hold any VW licence or arrangement, or has it ever been contacted about this vehicle's use in marketing? The answer changes the entire posture of the program, and the record contains nothing on it. Fold the medium into the same asking — naming a medium is exactly the precondition F192 says unlocks the size question ('Do NOT re-ask it cold; ask it once he names the medium'), so this one asking can close a ruling that has been open since rev 64.

RENDER `hero34r` AND `side` WITH `T1_ALPHA=1`, THEN RUN `python3 deliver.py`. Watch control C1 go green for the first time in thirteen revisions and read the summary line, not the exit code. This is one env var and two renders, and it is the single capability the whole merch program turns on. Until it is done, 'die-cut', 'on any background', apparel and motion are all unavailable. Name the frame in every figure you publish off it.

ADD `T1_VW_MARK` WITH THREE STATES (1 ship / 0 mark-neutral repaint / -1 not built), hanging state 0 off the existing `_EMBLEM_PLATE` list and the `capvw` prefix and their two materials `roundelred` and `capwhite`. Then do the thing this project insists on: RENDER `front` AT EACH STATE, CROP IT AND LOOK. Add the guard in the same edit, and make it a row that READS THE MESH (rule 10) — a grep for a switch name is not a test that the switch works (rule 50).

CORRECT `deliver.py`'s READ_ME_FIRST BEFORE ANY PACKAGE LEAVES THE BUILDING. Four claims are refuted by the live register: the emblem's reading, his complaint count, the tyre tread (F308, shipped), the roof loudspeakers (F309, retired). Add a verify_clone row that ties the README's defect claims to OPEN_FINDINGS rows arithmetically. Separately, move the `bad = [k for k, v in CTL.items() if not v]` check ABOVE the `save(...)` calls so a refusing run does not leave 22 files and a confident README on disk.

RE-WEIGHT THE PREVIEW LIST so `hero34r` stops being the least-rendered live view. It is the frame the source itself says 'shows the counter wrap and the louvre block', it is the least-VW-forward angle available, and it has one rendered-file mention across ten revisions. Render it at delivery size, crop it, and look at it — the counter, the tail board's 38-degree diagonal, the louvres and the bulb run are the assets the merch program is built on and nobody has inspected them at scale.

ADD SUB-CROP PRESETS TO `deliver.py` — counter-and-hatch strip, tail-board-and-bulbs vignette, hatch triptych, wheel-arch-and-folk-art panel — each named, each recording which frame it came from. Cheap, and it makes the distinctive framing the default framing instead of something a designer has to remember to do.

RESTORE THE REV-39 STYLE CLAUSE INTO F18'S CARRIER: 'cartoon with rendered depth — VECTOR LINE AND FLAT COLOUR, SHADING AND OCCLUSION SAMPLED FROM THE 3D ASSET.' It is the owner's own words, it is a buildable pipeline rather than a mood word, it has been missing from every carrier for 32 revisions, and `deliver.py`'s `layers/` output already emits exactly the two passes it describes. Rule 16 applies: this is a carrier that was silently trimmed.

ADD AN EXPORT PATH AND NAME IT IN A CARRIER. At minimum document `T1_SAVE` (it appears in zero handoff documents); better, add a glTF/USD export behind one switch. Zero non-manifold body edges and 43 bound materials say the mesh would probably survive it — but UVs, material translation and the 5,186 ngons are untested, so state that as a ceiling rather than a promise. Without this the design program has a PNG generator, not a 3D asset, and the owner's stated goal is the latter.

HAVE A TRADEMARK LAWYER REVIEW THE SHORTLIST BEFORE ANYTHING IS PRINTED, WORN OR SOLD — per product, per market, and with the actual artwork in front of them, not a description of it. Everything above is a design posture chosen to reduce exposure while making the work more distinctive; none of it is clearance, and the design side does not get to decide what is safe.
what_would_embarrass_us: SHIPPING MERCH WHOSE HERO FRAME IS `hero34f` OR `front` — the two most VW-forward views, the two most instrumented, and the two that look most like every stock VW-bus asset on Redbubble — while `hero34r` and `side` carry the counter, the hatches, the tail board, the folk art and the script that nobody else on earth has. The generic framing and the high-exposure framing are the same framing, and we would have chosen it by inertia.

PUTTING A VW LOGO THE OWNER HAS REJECTED NINE TIMES ONTO A PRODUCT, AT POSTER SCALE. The mark currently reads 0.8528 against its own control ceiling of 0.9465, C4 is RED at 0.0745 against a 0.045 bar, and the built cells are 1.19x too round — four fat wedges meeting at the centre, which the instrument itself calls 'the X the owner has reported five times'. My arithmetic off `ROUNDEL_D = 0.2800` on a 4.065 m vehicle: the roundel is ~5.3 mm on a 76 mm sticker and ~42 mm on a 610 mm poster, so on anything poster-sized every stroke is individually inspectable. A WRONG VW logo is worse on both counts at once — off-brand for VW and the owner's own standing complaint.

A 'BLUEPRINT' OR EXPLODED-DIAGRAM TREATMENT. It is the obvious way to dramatise a photoreal 3D model, it is maximally SHAPE-forward — i.e. the worst possible posture on the trade-dress claim — and it is already a standing stock category (Dreamstime sells 'Vw Van Blueprint' by the sheet). Derivative and exposed simultaneously.

LETTING THE FOLK ART READ AS HIPPIE FLOWER-POWER. This bus genuinely carries hand-painted florals (SPEC: 'gold + yellow + white + dark-red Mexican folk-art florals over the red only'), so florals cut loose from the counter, the hatches and the Spanish signage will be read as Woodstock — which is both the most saturated trope in the category and the WRONG COUNTRY'S MEANING of the object. 'Combi' is a Mexican pesero, a working microbus; the name is taco + combi. The florals need their context to read correctly.

MIXING LIVERY STATES IN ONE IMAGE. The owner ruled these are the same vehicle in different states and SPEC §7.1 says folk art, script, aperture glazing and roof-board treatment 'may never be carried across states'. A frame with the Playa folk art AND the Nolita chalkboard is a fake, and it is the exact defect that killed F99, F100 and F140.

PUBLISHING A TACOMBI BRAND COLOUR, TYPEFACE OR LOGO LOCKUP AS FACT. Every first-party Tacombi page was EGRESS_BLOCKED; the type list is a search summary of a page nobody opened; no one in this program has seen a single piece of current Tacombi merchandise artwork. Handing the owner a 'brand system' built on second-hand summaries of his own brand would be indefensible.

PROMISING TO MATCH 'THE WHEELS FROM THE EARLIER CARTOON VERSION'. That artefact is in no commit, no deleted file and no blob across 793 commits, and the directory START_HERE.md points at does not exist here. Quietly guessing at it and presenting the guess as compliance with his ruling would be the project's oldest failure mode — a claim in prose standing in for a thing nobody has.

SHIPPING A CLOSE TYRE CROP. `TREAD_LUGS = 64` is carried in the source as `# DECLARED, inside the MEASURED bracket 48..84` and the probe REFUSES to publish a count (six estimates: 55/64/61/74/48/84). At a 32.6 mm lug pitch the lugs are ~4.9 mm apart on a 610 mm poster — countable by a customer. We would be publishing a specific checkable claim the project explicitly cannot defend. And PHOTOS_WANTED has never had a tyre item; one close square-on frame would close it.

QUOTING `verify_clone.sh`'s TOTAL AS EVIDENCE THE MERCH IS ACCURATE. The script says so itself: not one of its rows compares the model to a photograph. Zero fidelity, N self-consistency. Any deck slide that reads '429 checks passing' next to a product shot is a misrepresentation of what was measured.

SAYING ANY CROP OR TREATMENT 'IS SAFE', OR OFFERING ANY OF THIS AS A CLEARANCE OPINION. Design-side risk reduction is not legal advice, a lower-exposure framing is not a cleared framing, and the lawyer makes the final call on every product in every market.

all_concepts.note: The empty tail sections are the best idea here: a punchline the viewer finds unaided, proprietary to this one vehicle (STATE.md's inventory contains no engine object, matching the S-graded 'engine was scrapped'), unfakeable by any competitor with a stock shell, and it converts the project's least-used asset — a clean manifold 229-object mesh — into the content itself. Sections-as-contact-sheet is a boat-lofting/CT idiom nobody has pointed at a food truck. Real risk is engineering, not taste: the capping problem is the whole picture (an uncapped 2.8 mm skin renders as two hairlines), the off-side void behind GAL_Y_BACK = -0.4800 is worst exactly at the three money sections, and this tree has a documented history of booleans collapsing the shell at SUB=2 — but it proposes the right test (three trial sections, crop, look) before committing, and 27 small tiles sidestep the unproven large-format stitch entirely.

concept.title: TWENTY-FOUR SECTIONS
concept.one_line: The bus sliced transversely every 150 mm and every slice drawn as a filled cross-section on one sheet — a CT scan of a taco stand, in which the three sections through the serving bays are dense with machinery and the sections through the engine bay are empty.
concept.the_image:
THE RISKY ONE. A cautious team rejects it because at thumbnail size it does not look like a bus.

The vehicle is cut transversely at a regular station interval and every slice is drawn as a filled closed shape, arranged in a grid and read left-to-right, nose to tail, like a contact sheet. Across the 4.065 m body (STATE.md: `dims L=4.065`), 150 mm gives 27 sections, 200 mm gives 21. Every section is printed at the same scale, on the same ground line, so the object's anatomy evolves as your eye travels the grid.

Each section is FILLED COLOUR, not line: the outer body a solid warm red band, the cream upper a solid band, glass a thin dark line, and everything the plane passes through drawn solid in the galley's own seven colours.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY REVEALS — this is the entire idea and it is three distinct acts:

ACT ONE, the cab. Sections forward of about x = +1.04 pass through a fully built interior: `seat_back`, `seat_base`, `seat_welt` and their passenger pairs, `wheel_rim` / `wheel_hub` / `wheel_horn` / two `wheel_spoke`, `dash`, `dash_grille`, `dash_glovebox`, three pedals, `gear_lever`, `mirror_int`. Dense, small, mechanical.

ACT TWO, the galley — and the body wall OPENS. The three sections at the measured bay centres (`BAY_CX = (0.6720, 0.0470, -0.5980)`) cut straight through the serving apertures. Each of those three shows: a break in the flank 515.5 mm wide; the counter slab in section, 107 mm thick (`CNT_ZT, CNT_ZB = 1.2540, 1.1470`) projecting 321 mm in plan (`CNT_Y_IN, CNT_Y_OUT = 0.8450, 1.1660`); the plancha or the worktop; a rack; the strip light near the roof line at z 1.788–1.802; and the back wall at y = −0.480. Three sections in the run are full of the machinery of feeding people. That is the cutaway, and it arrives as a rhythm rather than as a single reveal.

ACT THREE, the tail, and it is the punchline. The sections aft of about x = −1.30 pass through the engine bay of a 1963 Type 2 — and there is NOTHING IN THEM. An empty ring of sheet metal where on any other split-screen bus on earth there would be a dense air-cooled flat-four. That is Tacombi's own founding sentence rendered as a drawing rather than written as copy: "The engine was scrapped, transmission sold" (SPEC.md §0.1, graded S).

COMPOSITION: a 4 × 6 or 3 × 7 grid on warm paper. Each cell holds one section, labelled only with its station in millimetres from the front axle. Consistent ground line across every cell. No leader lines, no callouts, no perspective anywhere. Gold hairlines for the station labels and the cell rules only. One line of type at the foot in the brand's deadpan register — something at the exact temperature of "1963 Type 2 · transverse sections at 150 mm · station −1900: empty."

MOTION VERSION, and it is nearly free once the sections exist: the slices play in sequence nose to tail as a 3-second loop — the shape breathing open at the three bays and hollowing out at the tail. That is a title card, a social loop and a menu-screen ident from one asset. And it obeys the only motion law this vehicle has: it never drives. The SECTION PLANE moves; the bus does not.
concept.emotional_claim:
Awe first, then a small joke, and the gap between them is where the artefact lives.

The awe is the sheer measured-ness. You cannot fake this image. Twenty-seven consistent cross-sections of a specific vehicle is visibly the output of someone who knows the object to the millimetre, and it lands as evidence of care before it lands as information. That is the emotional payload of every good technical illustration and it is unusually strong here.

Then, six or seven seconds later, you notice the tail sections are empty — and if you know what a Type 2's tail contains, or you read the one line of type, the whole poster reorganises itself around an absence. It is the brand's origin story delivered as a punchline you find yourself, which is the strongest form.

And it is warm despite being a scan, because the palette is warm and the sections are hand-weighted: the reds and creams and ambers of a kitchen, arranged with the patience of a boat-lofting drawing.
formats: B1 707 × 1000 mm, edition print, hand-numbered in pencil, authenticated with a blind emboss chop rather than a signature (there is no artist's hand on a render and a forged signature on CGI is embarrassing). Colophon at the foot in 6 pt naming revision, resolution, sample count and date — unfakeable provenance and completely anti-advert

ALL-OVER APPAREL REPEAT. The sections tile beautifully: pattern at three metres, anatomy at thirty centimetres. This is the format that solves the walking-advert problem structurally — it reads as texture first and as a bus second, so only someone who knows sees the bus
Wrapping paper, cup sleeves, and a menu's endpapers, from the same repeat
3-SECOND LOOP, 1:1 and 9:16, for social and for the in-store menu screen — sections playing nose to tail
SINGLE-SECTION MICRO-GOODS: station +0.047, the middle bay, the one with the griddle in it, as a 40 mm enamel pin, a woven label, or a 25 mm sticker. This is the entry point that teaches the poster
Postcard set: three cards, one per bay section, at 148 × 105
concept.why_not_derivative:
Nothing in the VW-bus merchandise market is remotely like this, and the two nearest tropes are both refused on purpose.

It is NOT A BLUEPRINT. Dreamstime sells "Vw Van Blueprint Stock Illustrations" by the sheet, and the blueprint move is the obvious way to dramatise a 3D model — white lines on cyan, orthographic elevation, dimension arrows. This is filled colour shapes on warm paper with no elevation and no dimension arrows anywhere. And critically, a stock blueprint annotates a generic VW; every section here is of the CONVERSION.

It is NOT AN EXPLODED DIAGRAM. Nothing floats, nothing hovers, nothing is pulled apart on an axis. The vehicle is intact; the plane moves.

Its actual relatives are medical imaging and boat lofting, neither of which has ever been pointed at a food truck. And it can only exist because someone measured this exact object for seventy-five revisions — it converts the program's most exotic and least-used asset (a clean, manifold, 229-object mesh with `non-manifold edges (body) | 0`) directly into content, which nothing else in the program does.

And the punchline is proprietary. "The engine bay is empty" is a fact about ONE bus in the world. No competitor can print it, because every other bus in the category still drives — which is precisely the thing the category is selling.
concept.production_notes:
WHY A CAUTIOUS TEAM REJECTS IT, said plainly so it is not discovered late: at thumbnail it reads as abstract pattern, and someone will say customers will not understand it. Ship it anyway. The pattern-at-distance / anatomy-up-close split is the feature, not the bug, and the single-section pin is the cheap entry point that teaches the poster. Do not sand this into a friendlier cutaway; the friendlier cutaway is Concept 1 and it already exists.

FILLED SHAPES, NOT LINE. The temptation will be to outline every section for legibility. Resist it — filled colour is what separates this from the blueprint category, and the sections have enough internal contrast (red band, cream band, steel, amber, green) to read without a keyline.

STATION LABELS FROM THE DATUM, GENERATED. Label from the front axle, and generate every figure from the constants at layout time.

THE ENGINE-BAY CAPTION MUST BE HONEST AND IT IS A TWO-PART FACT. The MODEL has no engine object — STATE.md's inventory contains none. The REAL VEHICLE has no engine, by the brand's own S-graded account. Those are two different facts that happen to agree, and the caption must not claim the model measured an absence it simply never modelled. Say it the true way: "no engine is modelled, because there is none in the vehicle." That sentence is better copy than the dishonest version anyway.

SPOT INKS AGAIN — five, per AUDIT_rev43's "seven inks printed; five if cut." The sections are large flat areas of a small number of colours, which is the ideal screen-print case and terrible CMYK material (large flat process fields band and mottle).

RENDER EACH SECTION AS ITS OWN TILE at high resolution. This entirely sidesteps the large-format stitch problem: no single frame needs to be 4677 px, because the sheet is assembled from 27 small ones. That is a real production advantage over both other concepts and it is worth saying out loud.

MOTION: 27 frames at ~5.5 min each is roughly 2.5 hours of render for the whole loop, and it never needs re-rendering because the sequence is the same asset as the poster. Do not fan out Blender — it is CPU-bound on four cores and two instances make both slower.

SEED THE GRAIN PER FRAME IF POST IS EVER APPLIED. post.py's grain is `seed=7`, fixed — identical grain on every frame reads as dirt on the lens and instantly betrays a still-image pipeline. For this concept the right answer is simply no grain at all.
model_work_required: A SECTION CUTTER — and there is nothing like it in the tree. build.py step 3 issues windscreen, side, rear and gap cutters and nothing else; there is no clip plane, no slice, no section path anywhere. Needs a `T1_SECTION_X` boolean intersect against a thin slab, run N times. ⚠ AND THIS IS EXACTLY THE OPERATION THIS TREE HAS BEEN BURNED BY: STATE.md's own warning reads "The cab-door gap booleans passed at SUB=1 and collapsed the shell at SUB=2 for six revisions. Run both." Watch the slice fail before believing it.

CAPPING, AND IT IS THE REAL ENGINEERING. A boolean slice leaves open boundary edges. The body shell is a thin skin — 2.8 mm per the source's own description of the galley as "a sealed 2.8 mm steel box" — so an UNCAPPED section renders as two hairlines rather than a solid band, and the entire visual idea collapses. Every cut surface must be capped and given the section's own fill material. Prototype this on ONE station before committing to twenty-seven.

THE OFF-SIDE PROBLEM IS AT ITS ABSOLUTE WORST HERE, AND IT IS THE LARGEST PIECE OF NEW GEOMETRY ANY OF THESE THREE CONCEPTS NEEDS. Every transverse section crosses the backdrop plane at `GAL_Y_BACK = -0.4800` and continues to the off-side flank — and beyond that 24 mm slab there is NOTHING. The source is explicit that `gal_end_f` and `gal_end_a` exist "to stop a camera seeing past the backdrop into unlit body cavity." Sections aft of the galley will be honest; the three money sections THROUGH the galley will show a 24 mm slab floating in a void unless a real off-side liner and floor are built. Build them. They are worth having regardless, and both other concepts benefit.

VERIFY THE SECTIONS AGAINST THE MESH, NOT AGAINST THE PICTURE. Each cut's cross-sectional area and its component count should be printed and checked, so a section that silently loses a capped face is caught by a number rather than by someone squinting at cell 14 of 27.

NO ALPHA STRICTLY REQUIRED (each section renders on its own tile), NO EMBLEM WORK, NO NOSE WORK, and no dependency on the stitch chain at delivery size. The cab and galley objects benefit from Concept 2's form work but do not require it — at section scale a box reads as a box legitimately, because in section it IS a rectangle.

ONE HONEST CHECK BEFORE ANY OF IT: render three trial sections — one cab, one bay centre at x = +0.047, one tail at x ≈ −1.90 — crop them and LOOK. If the tail section is not legibly, satisfyingly empty, the punchline does not land and the concept should be reconsidered rather than rescued.

all_concepts.note: The standout. 'A loteria deck with no archetypes in it' is a category error nobody has committed in any market, and three cards — La Cortina (a fringe alone), La Sombra (only the shadow), La Combi Cerrada (a picture this project has never rendered in 76 revisions) — are each better ideas than most whole concepts here. Culturally exactly right for taco+combi without costume-Mexican. The engraving argument is load-bearing and true: hatching that follows the normal needs normals, so this is the one treatment only available to someone who built the geometry. Honest about 24 illustrations before one unit ships.

concept.title: EL COMBI — La Lotería
concept.one_line: A 24-card lotería deck in which every card is an engraving of one part of this one vehicle — the game of archetypes played with a taco truck's components.
concept.the_image:
Pure black line on warm cream uncoated stock. No tone, no colour, no shading — a 19th-century trade-catalogue engraving crossed with a Mexican broadside. Card face 60 × 100 mm: a single object, centred, floating in cream, inside a 2 mm black rule with a 1 mm inner hairline; a number top-left in a slab face; the Spanish name in caps along the foot in hand-drawn condensed grotesque, English small beneath.

THE LINE SYSTEM, which is the whole idea: silhouette 0.5 mm, creases 0.3 mm, hatching 0.12–0.18 mm. No flat black mass wider than ~3 mm anywhere. Value comes ONLY from hatch density — four densities at roughly 8 / 4 / 2 / 1 lines per mm. And the hatch direction FOLLOWS THE SURFACE: it runs longitudinally along the flank, wraps circumferentially round the tyre, radiates from the pole of the hubcap dome, and cross-hatches only in true occlusion — under the counter, inside the wheel arches, behind the apertures. That is the difference between an engraving and a Photoshop filter, and it requires a normal pass, which is to say it requires the model.

THE DECK, 24 cards: 1 El Combi (the whole vehicle, lid propped, counter out — the full asymmetric 4.580 × 3.132 m propped silhouette, 1.462:1). 2 La Ventana (one serving aperture, 515.5 × 403.0 mm with its 55 mm corner radius, bobble fringe running the whole inner edge). 3 El Mostrador (the counter's radiused tail and brass nosing). 4 La Rueda (the hubcap bullseye: 274.0 mm cap, 86.9 mm badge). 5 El Farol (one festoon bulb on its flex). 6 La Plancha. 7 El Tablero (the mural lid, propped). 8 La Flor (one mural rosette, ten lobes, peace-glyph centre — carry it, don't sanitise it). 9 La Calidad (the sunburst, type at −19.7°). 10 El Sol. 11 El Espejo. 12 La Bocina. 13 El Sesenta y Tres (the empty chrome plate frame). 14 La Rejilla (the louvre block, ten slots at 21.111 mm pitch). 15 La Cinta (the bulb string alone, a single continuous line running edge to edge off both sides of the card). 16 El Toldo (the tail board on its stay, 0.7110 m chord at 38.0°). 17 La Carta (a menu card). 18 La Cortina (the bobble fringe alone, a scalloped run, nothing else). 19 El Faro. 20 El Pico (the nose blade and its two irons — CROPPED BELOW THE ROUNDEL). 21 El Vaso. 22 La Llave. 23 La Sombra (the cast shadow alone: a card that is only the shape the bus makes on the ground). 24 La Combi Cerrada — the same vehicle SHUT, which is a picture this project has never rendered in 76 revisions.
concept.emotional_claim: The absurd dignity of giving a taco truck's parts the treatment normally reserved for the moon, the mermaid and death. A child gets a game and asks what La Cortina is. An adult gets the joke — this is a deck of archetypes with no archetypes in it — and then, a beat later, gets the affection underneath it: somebody decided every one of these things. Somebody chose the fringe.
