**IT CONTRADICTS F18 AND I PROPOSE IT ANYWAY.** F18's scene is locked to 'nothing but the bus, die-cut tight, plus the sun and the papel picado'. The die-cut here adds a plant, adds a shadow base and has NO SUN. It is therefore explicitly a DIFFERENT ARTEFACT from F18 and is not offered as the F18 deliverable — which also means it is not gated by F18's trigger, 'build it after the model is done'. Do not raise the papel picado: the owner ruled 'Leave it open, I'll decide when the sticker is actually being built. DO NOT RE-PUT IT UNTIL THEN.'

**NO SUN AS A RAYED DISC ANYWHERE IN THIS PROGRAMME.** AUDIT_rev43.md's reasoning is right and independently checkable: 'The vehicle already carries ELEVEN radial bursts, and it is the drawing's only light source.' The Calidad starburst, the mural rosettes, the hubcap rings, the headlamps and the wheel spokes all compete for it.

**HOLD THE GREEN.** One green in the whole picture and it belongs to the plant. If a second green appears, the idea is gone.
model_work_required: **SHOOT THE FLANK, NOT THE NOSE — and the reason is measured.** At a 0.95–1.00 m camera the roundel lands dead centre of a child's eyeline: build.py carries `ROUNDEL_Z_AG = 1.0170`, and `ROUNDEL_D = 0.2800`. A five-year-old stands nose to nose with it. And it is wrong: probe_rev69_fitpose's P2 reads 0.8528 against P1b's ceiling of 0.9465, and probe_rev46_vw's C8 reads 'photo 3.39, built 2.84 -- the built cells are 1.19x TOO ROUND.' It is the owner's ninth report, F191 and F234 both stand, and it is also the most trademark-exposed element on the object. Composing it out is the same correct decision twice over.

**NO CHILD'S-EYE CAMERA EXISTS.** studio.views() defines 14 cameras and the standing preview list is four (`front,side,hero34f,hero34r`). The closest is `low34` at eye 1.55 m, which no preview list has ever rendered. A ~0.95 m camera is a new dict entry and a frame nobody in 76 revisions has seen. Render it and LOOK before designing to it.

**The cast shadow is both the composition's anchor and the sticker's cut path, and it is separable — but only on paper.** deliver.py writes `combi_%s_shadow_only.png` and `combi_%s_no_shadow.png`, with the split measured at rev 62: shadow-catcher pixels near-black (max channel < 12/255) against a vehicle mean of 143, the vehicle side 97.1 % fully opaque and 99.99 % ONE connected component. But **T1_ALPHA has not been run since rev 62** — no LEDGER contains the string, every frame in out/ is PNG colortype 2, and deliver.py currently prints 'CONTROLS: 4 checked, 1 FAILED -- C1' and 'PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY'. One render closes it and every format here depends on it.

**post.py DESTROYS ALPHA** — measured RGBA in, colortype 2 out, and its docstring nowhere says so. Optics (bloom / CA / vignette / grain) and a cut-out are mutually exclusive from this repo. Decide the order before anything is graded, and note post.py's live default is `BACKDROP = "headroom"` (peak 252) while its own docstring still claims white — a 252 field inside a #FFFFFF margin is a visible rectangle on the sheet.
The settled hollow under each tyre, the plant, the crowd, the ghosting, the steam and the birds are ALL DRAWN. Nothing in the tree does people, volumetrics or ground deformation.
The bulbs-on-in-daylight beat needs F144 addressed or drawn around: 'THE FESTOON BULBS READ AS PEARLS, NOT LIGHTS.' For a flat illustration, draw them right; do not wait on the render.

If the Calidad decal appears anywhere in the crop, draw its pink star from the PHOTOGRAPH, not the model: F16 is OPEN — 'the isolated star is built BELOW the burst where both red frames put it above; every flank rosette is drawn at the diameter of its gold core.' The same row means every shipped rosette is systematically undersized.

**No close tyre crop in any large format.** t1_detail.py carries `TREAD_LUGS = 64  # DECLARED, inside the MEASURED bracket 48..84 (F308)` and `TREAD_CUT = 0.0060  # DECLARED groove depth, m.  NOT measured`, and probe_rev74_tread's T2 refuses to publish a count at all. At poster scale the lugs become countable and we would be publishing a specific checkable claim the project explicitly cannot defend. PHOTOS_WANTED has never carried a tyre item; one close square-on frame would close it.

all_concepts.note: A factory plate where every dimension confesses its provenance, in two inks and two type voices — solid mono for measured, bracketed hand-script for posed. '[ 550 ] chosen, not measured. Upper bound 590. Lower bound: none.' and 'ENGINE: NONE. TRANSMISSION: SOLD.' The confessions are the moat: a stock seller has no uncertainties to print. Strongest detail is 'WIDTH = f(ANGLE)' with an inset graph — a blueprint annotating its own impossibility. Blueprint is the most saturated shelf in the category and it escapes structurally by dimensioning only what the factory never made. Sizes A2 to the proven chain instead of the ambition.

concept.title: THE UNCERTAINTY PLATE
concept.one_line: A factory elevation drawing where every dimension line confesses how it was obtained — and the ones that cannot be obtained are drawn anyway, in the signwriter's hand, as sentences.
concept.the_image:
Landscape sheet, warm uncoated paper stock (not white, not cyanotype blue — the blue is the cliché). The vehicle is a TRUE orthographic side elevation, drawn as line only: a black-brown keyline at three declared weights (0.55 mm outer silhouette / 0.35 mm panel edges and shut lines / 0.20 mm hatch reveals, louvre blades, bulb sockets), with FOUR flat fills and no shading at all — body red, cream, folk-art gold reduced to its three largest masses only, and a warm near-black for tyres and glazing. The propped tail board runs off the top-right of the sheet on its measured 38.0-degree diagonal and is deliberately allowed to cross into the title block. Below and around it: full drafting furniture — extension lines, arrowed dimension rules, section flags, a scale bar, a north-style datum arrow at the front axle.

The subversion is entirely in the annotation, and it runs on TWO INKS AND TWO TYPE VOICES that mean two different things.

MEASURED dimensions are set in tight mono numerals, solid ink, hard filled arrowheads, exactly as a factory plate would: `2400 WHEELBASE` · `1369 / 1359 TRACK` · `664.9 TYRE` · `515.5 × 403.0 SERVING APERTURE ×3` · `17.75 mm/m RAKE` · `39.7 ARCH TO TYRE` · `109.5 | 129.5 PILLARS` (and that last one is the whole thesis in one figure — the three holes are equal but the two pillars between them are NOT, and no stylised bus drawing on earth gets that right).

UNMEASURED dimensions are drawn in a 40% tint, the arrowheads replaced by open square brackets, and the number replaced by hand-lettered script in the vehicle's own silver-leaf letterform — the same hand that painted 'Gracias por su Preferencia' on the counter fascia. These are the poems, and they are all true:
  · across the propped tail board — `[ 550 ] chosen, not measured. The board's plane contains the width, so it projects only through parallax. Upper bound 590. Lower bound: none.`
  · at the rear hatch's swing — `[ 64° ] a pose. No photograph we hold shows it open.`
  · at the roof — `[ ] height retired as a target, rev 22. What this vehicle stands at is open and unmeasured.`
  · at the tread — `[ 64 lugs ] declared. Two methods disagree; the honest answer is somewhere between 48 and 84.`
  · at the engine bay — `ENGINE: NONE. TRANSMISSION: SOLD.`
  · at the three apertures — `Arrived missing three windows. We left them that way.`
  · at the empty plate frame — `1963. The only date on the vehicle, and it is stamped on an empty plate.`

One further wrongness, small and deadly: the lid's own dimension line carries `WIDTH = f(ANGLE)` with a tiny inset graph, because in this model the mural board's width is genuinely a function of how far it is open (1.2237 m at 76°, 3.47 m at 20°). A blueprint annotating its own impossibility.

Title block bottom-right, six-point mono, unfakeable: `UNIT 01 · TYPE 2 · 1963 · PLAYA DEL CARMEN · 229 MESH OBJECTS · 376,383 VERTICES · 0 NON-MANIFOLD BODY EDGES · REV 76`.
concept.emotional_claim: Recognition, then a small shock, then affection. You approach it as a spec sheet — the most emotionally cold object in graphic design — and at reading distance you discover it is being honest with you about what it does not know. The feeling is INTIMACY WITH A MACHINE'S HUMILITY. Every other technical poster asserts; this one admits, and admission is disarming in a way assertion never is. And the specific admissions are all about care: somebody measured the pillars between three holes to a tenth of a millimetre AND was unwilling to guess at the width of a board. That combination — obsessive where it can be, silent where it can't — is exactly what a person means when they say a thing was made with love. The '[ 550 ] chosen, not measured' line is the one people photograph and send to each other.
formats: A2 landscape (594 × 420 mm) — THE PRIMARY, and it is chosen to fit the proven chain, not the ambition. 3840 px on the long edge is 488 mm at 200 dpi, so A2 sits inside what has actually been rendered once (3840×2640, rev 57). Ship A2 first.
A1 (841 × 594 mm) as the LIMITED tier, and only after a proving run: A1 at 200 dpi wants 4677 px, 22 % above anything this chain has ever produced. Do not promise A1 before that run.
A4 (297 × 210 mm) as a free insert at the restaurant, on the same uncoated stock, unnumbered. Same drawing, annotations reduced to five lines. This is the version people actually keep.
A 1080 × 1350 crop set for social: five separate posts, each one a single dimension line and its confession, cropped tight. The 'ENGINE: NONE' one is the launch post.
210 × 99 mm bookmark / bill-drop from a vertical slice through the rear quarter: louvre block, Calidad burst, rear wheel, and the '1963' annotation.
concept.why_not_derivative: The category already sells 'VW van blueprint' by the sheet — Dreamstime carries it as a standing stock shelf — and every one of those is a GENERIC bus, traced, annotated with plausible-looking numbers nobody measured. This sheet is unforgeable in three separate ways at once. (1) It dimensions the CONVERSION, not the vehicle: apertures, counter, tail board, louvre block. Anything you could draw from a factory manual is deliberately absent. (2) Its numbers come off a mesh that has been measured for seventy-six revisions and can be regenerated on demand — the wheelbase reads +0.0 mm to spec, the track +0.0 mm, the tyre −0.1 mm — so it is a document about a real object rather than a decoration in the shape of one. (3) Nobody else would ever print the uncertainties, because a stock seller does not HAVE uncertainties; they have a traced outline and a font. The confessions are the moat. It also escapes the trope structurally: a blueprint is the most SHAPE-forward treatment available and therefore the worst posture on the VW trade-dress question — this one solves that by dimensioning only the parts Volkswagen never made, and by using the side elevation, in which the VW roundel does not appear at all.
concept.production_notes:
Four spot inks on uncoated: one declared red, one cream, one gold, one warm near-black. Five if the wordmark appears — silver, and specify it as a FINISH (foil or metallic ink), never as grey. DO NOT sample the red off a render: flank_compare on out/r75_side.png reads the render's flank at median (196,81,67) against the photograph's (158,16,6) — it images salmon, roughly ten just-noticeable differences off. And do not average the photographs either; probe_rev71_red.py prints its own prohibition, 'the photograph's red G/R is 0.0149 .. 0.0344, a 2.3x span. DO NOT QUOTE A SINGLE FIGURE FOR IT.' Choose one red as a design ruling, record its provenance, and reconcile it against the three authored reds that currently disagree (t1_mats sRGB(196,49,36), lid_gen (159,45,22), cal_gen (214,46,30)). A flat-ink artefact can be more chromatically correct than the render currently is, and should say so out loud.

Every figure on the sheet must be generated by a script that IMPORTS the constants (t1_shell.BAY_W, BAY_CX, Z_SILL, Z_HEAD, TB_TILT_DEG, TB_WIDTH, REAR_OPEN_DEG; t1_detail.LOUV_PITCH, LOUV_N, CAP_R; build.ROUNDEL_D) and reads STATE.md — never transcribed into the artwork file. A transcribed figure goes stale silently and this project has lost revisions to exactly that. Print the generator's own commit hash in the title block.

BRAND RISK, NAMED: a cautious team will ask to delete the confessions and keep the numbers. That kills it. The confessions ARE the concept, and they are also the reason this is the one artefact in the program that a customer reads for two minutes instead of two seconds. If the owner wants only the certainties, that is a different, weaker poster and should be labelled as one.

EDITION: open edition unnumbered on A4; A1 hand-numbered in pencil, authenticated by a BLIND EMBOSS chop rather than a signature — there is no artist's hand on a render and a forged signature on CGI is embarrassing. Archive the stitched master file as the edition master: Cycles sets no seed here and the run-to-run floor is ~2.04 % of pixels moving >8 levels, so a re-render is NOT a re-print.
model_work_required: FIX THE ORTHOGRAPHIC CLIPPING — I measured it today and it blocks any elevation series. studio.views()['front'] and ['rear'] are ortho=3.55 with horizontal sensor fit, so at 1600×1100 the vertical extent is 3.55 × 1100/1600 = 2.4406 m, covering z 0.2997 to 2.7403, while the vehicle spans z 0 at the tyres to STATE.md's 'bbox top 3.132' with the lids up. out/r75_front.png proves it: 42 ink pixels on the top row and 738 on the bottom row, subject bbox y 0..1099 of 1100. Derive ortho_scale from build.py's own printed bbox with a stated margin instead of the typed 3.55, and add a verify_clone row asserting zero ink on all four borders of any ortho frame — WATCH IT GO RED at 3.55 before believing it green.

out/r75_side.png is CLEAN — I measured 0 ink on all four borders, subject bbox x 212..1457, y 111..963 of 1600×1100, so the side elevation needs no reframing. It is the only camera in the tree that is already correctly composed. (For contrast: out/r75_hero34r.png carries 492 ink pixels on its right column — the counter runs off the edge — so the rear three-quarter needs reframing before it is used anywhere.)

A LINE PASS. Nothing in this tree has ever extracted a line. Try the Grease Pencil Line Art modifier on the `side` ortho first, because it produces EDITABLE VECTOR STROKES that export to SVG, which is what a drafting sheet actually needs; Freestyle is the fallback for stroke quality; a Sobel on normal+Z passes is the cheap 2D prototype. Crease angle 30–40°, not lower — T1_body is shade-smooth and a low angle finds the subdivision. The mesh is clean enough to trust: 229,489 quad against 1,040 tri and 5,186 ngon, 0 non-manifold body edges, cutters rolled back none.

RENDER WITH T1_ALPHA=1 for the flat-fill masks, and DO NOT route it through post.py — measured, post.py takes RGBA in (colortype 6) and writes colortype 2, so optics and cut-out are mutually exclusive and the silhouette is silently destroyed. T1_ALPHA appears in zero ledgers; it has not been exercised since rev 62. Run it once and watch deliver.py's C1 go from FAILED to PASS.

FIX tex/senor.png's MISSING KEYLINE if the wordmark appears at size. SPEC §3 requires 'SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow' and the shipped asset has no dark ink at all — among pixels with alpha>200 the 1st-percentile luma is 168.3 and the fraction below luma 80 is 0.0000. lid_gen.py already authors the convention as DARKLINE = (72,26,16). script_gen.py is NOT called by build.py, so regenerate tex/senor.png by hand or the render silently keeps the old file. Cheapest visible improvement in the inventory.

NOTHING ELSE. No new geometry, no emblem work, no gloss work. This sheet ships while F191's hold stands, because the side elevation does not contain the nose roundel — only the four hubcap badges, at 1.62 mm on an A2 sheet, below any scale at which their arrangement is judgeable. Ship the elevation FIRST and say why.

all_concepts.note: The constraint does the creative work: talavera has no vermillion, so the vehicle's dominant colour cannot exist in the material, and stripped of red the bus stops reading as fun and becomes civic. Grout run deliberately THROUGH the face rather than composed around, the three hatches left as bare unglazed white — the founding story in negative, grounded in the measured equal bays — and the single rare orange spent only on four hubcaps. 'Render X in craft Y' is a known template; this escapes it by designing to the material's limits rather than skinning them. Slow, expensive, high per-unit variance.

concept.title: AZULEJO 1963 — the bus fired into Puebla tin-glaze
concept.one_line: The orthographic side elevation hand-painted in cobalt on tin-glazed talavera tile, grout lines running straight through the vehicle, and the three serving hatches left as bare unpainted glaze.
concept.the_image:
SOURCE VIEW: the true orthographic side elevation. `studio.views()['side']` is `ortho=5.90, lens=None` — a genuine parallel projection, and talavera does not do perspective, so the craft and the camera already agree. I measured out/r75_side.png at 77.8% x 77.5% frame fill with clean margin on all four sides and no clipping; it is the one existing frame that can be traced as-is.

PANEL: 6 tiles wide x 4 high, each 105 mm, = 630 x 420 mm. Vehicle at 1:8 — the propped silhouette (4.580 x 3.132 m, from STATE.md's `x range [-2.157, 2.160]` plus the tail board reaching x -2.420, and `bbox top 3.132`) lands at 572 x 391 mm inside it, lid up, tail board propped, counter cantilevered.

PALETTE, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE IDEA: Puebla talavera's historic six are cobalt blue, tin-white ground, copper green, manganese black-brown, antimony yellow, and one rare orange. THERE IS NO VERMILLION IN THIS CRAFT. The vehicle's dominant colour does not exist in the material. So: body in COBALT, the cream upper body and roof as raw tin-white glaze (warm off-white, never paper white), the folk art in antimony yellow with manganese outline, the counter's brass nosing in antimony, tyres in manganese. The single orange is spent on exactly one thing — the four hubcap domes. Four small warm discs in an otherwise blue-and-white panel, landing on the wheels, which is where the eye goes anyway.

LINE: everything outlined in manganese at ~1.5 mm on the panel, brush-loaded so each stroke starts fat and tapers to a hairline — which is already the flank art's own signature (I looked at ref_side.jpg cropped to the rear quarter: every gold acanthus stroke is thick-to-hairline, terminating in a tight rolled volute).

THE GROUT IS THE POINT. Tile joints run straight through the vehicle — do NOT compose to avoid them. One joint crosses the Senor Tacombi lockup; one crosses a wheel. Joints are 3 mm of unglazed warm-grey bisque. Each tile is a fraction of a degree off square, so the grid wanders. If the grid is perfect and the edges are crisp, it reads as a printed tile and the whole idea dies.

GLAZE BEHAVIOUR THE DIGITAL VERSION MUST FAKE: talavera glaze is convex and pools. Cobalt goes markedly darker where a stroke terminates and where two strokes cross, and it bleeds ~0.5 mm into the white so no edge is clean.

THE HATCHES: the three serving apertures are left as bare tin-white glaze, undrawn — the only three areas of the panel carrying no ink at all. STATE.md: `open serving apertures on +Y: 3`, `bay widths 0.516 0.515 0.516` — they are EQUAL, so the rhythm is measured, not eyeballed. Three empty rectangles in a blue drawing is the founding story stated in negative.

BORDER: one tile-wide, the flank's own acanthus in cobalt, running all four sides. Talavera panels are always bordered; ours borrows the vehicle's own ornament to do it.

LIGHT: photograph it, never render it. Single raking source from the left so the convex glaze catches, the grout falls into shadow, and it reads as a wall you could put your hand on.
concept.emotional_claim: Permanence and civic weight. Tile is what a country puts on the front of a building it means to keep — it is the material of churches, market halls and fountains, not of trucks. Rendered in it, the taqueria stops being a vehicle that turned up and becomes a place that has always been there. And the palette does something nobody expects: stripped of its red, the bus stops reading as fun and starts reading as a monument. A person feels the same thing they feel in front of a tiled shopfront in a Mexican town square — that somebody built this on purpose, out of expensive materials, expecting it to outlast them.
formats: 24-tile wall panel, 630 x 420 mm, bus at 1:8 — one per restaurant, hand-painted in Puebla, signed and dated on the reverse of the corner tile. This is the anchor object; everything else is derived from it.

Compact retail panel, 4 x 3 tiles, 420 x 315 mm, bus SHUT at 1:11 (4.065 x 2.227 m per STATE.md's `overall height (vehicle max, lids excluded) 2.2268`). Framed and boxed. The shut state has never been rendered in 76 revisions, so this SKU doubles as the first sighting of the closed silhouette.

Single-tile coasters, 105 mm, set of six, one motif each: an 8-lobed rosette, a dark comma-with-dots tendril, one acanthus volute, the wheel bullseye, the three hatches, and '1963'. Each motif drawn at ITS OWN scale rather than shrunk off the bus — the largest flank rosette is a 68 mm equivalent circle (folk_gen.FLANK_ROSETTES, 3632 mm2), so at 105 mm it is drawn UP, not down, and nothing collapses.

Trivet, 2 x 2 tiles, 210 mm square: the wheel bullseye alone. Four concentric bands of the brand palette; STATE.md gives the badge at `4 rings R 0.043429` = 31.7% of the 274 mm cap, so it scales as a ratio.

Printed derivative: the panel photographed square-on under raking light. A2 poster, tote, tissue wrap, cup sleeve. The photograph of a ceramic object is a fundamentally different image from a render of a bus, and it inherits none of the render's colour problems.
concept.why_not_derivative: Every VW-bus artefact on the market is a photograph, an illustration, or a line drawing, and essentially all of them are red or rainbow. This one is a fired ceramic object with NO RED IN IT, with grout running through the vehicle's face. The tile grid is a reduction rule the category has never used: it forces the drawing into flat, bounded, brush-loaded strokes and refuses gradients, gloss and photorealism outright — which is the exact opposite of the saturated 'sunset silhouette' and 'blueprint' shelves. It also sidesteps the project's largest measured defect rather than inheriting it: flank_compare on out/r75_side.png reads the render's red at median (196,81,67), G/R 0.422, against the photograph's (158,16,6), G/R 0.114 — it images salmon. A craft with no vermillion in its palette cannot get the red wrong. And there is a real, quotable geographic rhyme: talavera poblana is made in Puebla, and Puebla is where VW de Mexico built the Combi from 1970. One line of copy, no invention.
concept.production_notes:
VENDOR: a certified talavera taller in Puebla (the craft carries a denominacion de origen; use a certified maker or do not call it talavera). Hand-painted maiolica on tin glaze, single firing after decoration. Lead times are long and per-panel variation is high — that is a feature for the restaurant anchors and a problem for retail, so cap the retail SKU at one panel size and accept that no two are identical.

COLOUR: do NOT hand the taller a hex value sampled off a render. Give them cobalt, antimony, manganese, copper green and the one orange as PIGMENT names and let the kiln decide. Every hex in this brief is an 8-bit display-space reading through PIL off warm, uncorrected frames — a mood reference, never an albedo. Separately, probe_rev71_red.py prints its own prohibition on the photograph side: 'the photograph's red G/R is 0.0149 .. 0.0344, a 2.3x span. DO NOT QUOTE A SINGLE FIGURE FOR IT.'

DRAWING SOURCE FOR THE ORNAMENT: draw the border acanthus from ref_side.jpg at 4-6x magnification, NOT from tex/swirl.png. The shipped tile is measurably more fragmented than the photograph — 196 gold connected components against the photograph's 66, with the top three carrying 66.4% against the photograph's 84.4% (folk_gen.COMP_TOP = {1: 47.8, 2: 73.7, 3: 84.4, ...}). The generator matches the coverage and misses the hand.

SIMPLIFICATION, WITH A MEASUREMENT UNDER IT: folk_gen.COMP_HIST's first three bins are (24, 0.42%), (21, 1.32%), (3, 0.55%) — 48 of 66 gold components carry 2.29% of all the gold. Delete all 48. That is a measured licence to reduce, not a taste call, and it is what makes the border cuttable in a brush.

DIGITAL PROOF BEFORE FIRING: build the panel as flat art with the bleed and the pooling faked, print it at size on matte, and pin it up at 2 m. Then fire one test tile and compare. Do not go to a 24-tile panel off a screen.

CEILING: nobody in this session has seen any current Tacombi merchandise, brand guideline, official colour or logo lockup — tacombi.com, shop.tacombi.com and fontsinuse.com all returned EGRESS_BLOCKED. Do not state a Tacombi brand colour anywhere in this programme until the owner supplies one.
model_work_required: NOTHING BLOCKING — this concept can start today off out/r75_side.png, which already exists at 1600x1100 with clean margins. That makes it the fastest of the three to a physical proof.

If any other elevation is used, FIX THE ORTHOGRAPHIC CLIPPING FIRST. studio.views()['front'] and ['rear'] are ortho=3.55 with horizontal sensor fit, so at 1600x1100 the vertical extent is 3.55*1100/1600 = 2.4406 m, covering z 0.2997 to 2.7403 — against a vehicle that reaches z=0 at the tyres and 3.132 at the top. out/r75_front.png has ink running off both borders. Derive ortho_scale from build.py's printed bbox with a stated margin instead of the typed 3.55, and add a verify row asserting zero ink on all four border rows/columns. Watch it go red on 3.55 before believing it green.

DO NOT PAINT THE EMBLEM FROM THE MODEL. At 1:8 the nose roundel would be 35 mm and plainly judgeable (ROUNDEL_D = 0.2800 in build.py). It is the owner's ninth report: probe_rev69_fitpose's P2 reads 0.8528 against P1b's 0.9465 ceiling, and probe_rev46_vw's C8 reads 'photo 3.39, built 2.84 -- the built cells are 1.19x TOO ROUND'. The side elevation does not contain the roundel at all, which is the main reason this concept is unblocked by F191 — but the four hubcap badges do appear, at 34 mm each, and STATE.md warns 'hubcap badge is SELF-CONSISTENCY ONLY -- CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC has never been compared to a frame'. Draw both from ref_playa_34.png, not from the render.

F74(a) is open and would propagate into any lid artwork: tex/lidmural.png is cropped at the bottom — the bottom flower row sliced mid-bloom and the olive-yellow side columns truncated, where ref_side.jpg shows a board framed on all four sides. I opened the master and confirmed it. lid_gen.py is NOT called by build.py, so regeneration is a hand step or the render silently keeps the old file. Fix before the lid appears at 1:8.
NOT GATED by F191/F193 — this is a hand-painted ceramic object, not the delivery render. Say so explicitly in the proposal so the hold does not read as blocking it.

all_concepts.note: The smartest single move here: it takes the program's live hazard — hand-painted florals misreading as Woodstock flower-power, wrong country entirely — and converts it into the differentiator with one drawing decision, because nobody mistakes a plume of smoke for a peace sign; the re-reading mechanism is the real reason people keep a graphic, the red garment deletes the ink slab, and folk_gen's own census (top 3 components = 84.4% of gold) is a measured licence to simplify rather than a platitude.

concept.title: Humo
concept.one_line: The gold scrollwork was never decoration — it is the smoke, and in this one image it leaves the bodywork, rises through the serving hatch and off the top of the frame.
concept.the_image:
FRAMING: flat, measured, drawn — a true side elevation, no perspective, no horizon, no ground beyond a single hard shadow line. The vehicle occupies the lower two-thirds. The upper third is empty ground and is the whole point.

THE MOVE: the folk art on the flank is drawn exactly as it sits on the vehicle — the two big acanthus masses (the cab-door bouquet and the rear-quarter mass), the rosettes, the dark comma-tendrils — until it reaches the middle serving aperture. There, one gold stroke does not turn back. It carries THROUGH the hatch, up past the propped mural lid, and out of the top of the sheet: the same tapering thick-to-hairline acanthus line, the same rolled volutes and hooks, now unattached to anything, widening and thinning as it climbs. Two or three secondary fronds peel off it. A handful of rosettes float free in the upper air like sparks. Everything below the sill is still ornament; everything above the roof is unmistakably a plume.

The cut point matters: the vehicle's own measured rule is that the gold lives on the RED ONLY and stops at the rear corner (43.687% gold on the rear quarter against 0.006% on the flat tail face). The drawing breaks that rule ONCE, on purpose, at the hatch — which is the only opening in the bodywork. The smell comes out where the food comes out.

PALETTE — three inks plus the garment/paper as the fourth: gold (the authored GOLD is (0.8600, 0.5400, 0.0600), a chrome-yellow), cream, and a dark maroon near-black for the comma-tendrils. Body red is the SUBSTRATE, not an ink — print on red stock or a red garment, which deletes the largest screen and the ink slab that makes a shirt read like a sticker.

COMPOSITION: a heavy horizontal mass with one vertical line escaping it, running off the top edge. Deliberately unbalanced upward. On apparel, place it so the plume runs off the shoulder seam — the graphic leaves the garment.

MOTION (loop): 3 seconds. The vehicle is dead still. The scroll DRAWS itself off the flank, stroke by stroke, in the signwriter's real order — the three big masses first, then the tendrils, then the rosettes — and rises. Reverse and hold. It is a painting animation and a smoke animation at the same time, which is the joke, told twice.
concept.emotional_claim:
A joke landing. You read the poster as a nicely-drawn bus with flowers on it — the same reading you have given a thousand VW busses — and then your eye follows one curl off the bodywork and out of the frame and the whole image reorganises. The flowers were never flowers. Delight at a re-reading is the most durable reason anybody keeps a graphic, because it works again on the person you show it to.

Underneath that is something warmer and slower: it says the ornament on this vehicle came from the same place as the cooking. Somebody painted those curls by hand, with a brush, on a Tuesday, in the same yard where the comal was lit. The picture makes the decoration and the food one substance.

And on a garment it does the thing good graphics do — it refuses to be contained. A shirt where the smell runs off your shoulder is a shirt people ask about.
formats: Screen print, 3 spot inks (gold / cream / dark maroon) on a RED garment — the body colour is the shirt. 280 mm chest, or a 340 mm shoulder-to-hem placement where the plume crosses the shoulder seam. Three screens, no white under-base, soft hand.

500×700 mm poster, same three inks on heavy UNCOATED stock. Spot colour on uncoated hits a chroma CMYK cannot reach, and the flatness stops being a deficit and becomes the idiom — the real bus is hand-painted flat colour, not clearcoat.
Tote, 380×420 mm panel, plume running off the top of the panel into the handle stitching.
3-second motion loop, 1080×1350 and 1080×1920 — the paint-on/rise-off sequence.

30 mm enamel pin of ONE scroll-plume alone, no vehicle. It reads at that size because it is a single tapering stroke with two volutes — this is the one element in the whole vehicle that survives at badge scale without reduction.

Life-size embroidered rosette, 45–60 mm, left chest, two colours (~9k stitches). The largest measured flank rosette is a ~68 mm equivalent circle ON THE VEHICLE, so at 45–60 mm nothing is reduced and nothing collapses.
concept.why_not_derivative:
This is the strongest anti-derivative move available anywhere in the program, because it takes the single most DANGEROUS element and converts it into the most differentiating one.

The category's third-biggest trope is hippie flower-power — daisies, sunflowers, peace signs. This bus genuinely carries hand-painted florals, so any careless crop of it gets read as Woodstock: the American counterculture meaning of a body shape whose Mexican meaning is a working microbus that hauls people to their jobs. That misread is the program's live hazard, not a theoretical one.

Giving the flowers a JOB fixes it in one gesture. Nobody has ever mistaken a plume of smoke for flower power. The moment the scroll comes off a griddle it is unmistakably rotulismo — Mexican signwriting — and the whole image relocates to the right country. It is the cheapest and most complete solution to the derivativeness problem in this brief, and it costs one drawing decision.

It is also formally unlike the category: no landscape, no sky, no sun, no vehicle in motion, flat spot colour rather than photoreal or watercolour, and a composition that deliberately runs off the sheet.
concept.production_notes:
THREE SCREENS IS NOT A COMPROMISE, IT IS THE MEASUREMENT. folk_gen's own connected-component census of the reference flank reads COMP_TOP = {1: 47.8, 2: 73.7, 3: 84.4} and COMP_HIST's first three bins are (24, 0.42%), (21, 1.32%), (3, 0.55%) — 48 of 66 gold components carry 2.29% of the ink and the largest THREE carry 84.4%. Delete the 48. That is a licence to simplify computed on this artwork, not a design platitude.

DRAW FROM THE PHOTOGRAPH, NOT FROM THE SHIPPED TILE. The reference census is 66 components with the top three at 84.4%; a census of tex/swirl.png found 196 components with the top three at 66.4% — the shipped art is measurably more fragmented and smaller-scale than the reference, and folk_gen says so itself: 'the same 10% gold over the same flank can be one bouquet or five hundred commas.' SPEC §10.10's own method applies — read at 4–5x magnification, redraw at 2–4K, measure back.

SPECIFY LINE WEIGHTS IN FINAL MILLIMETRES PER SKU. Never scale one master. On the shipped 4096² tile the gold's stroke width runs p10 2.66 mm / p50 13.15 mm / p90 45.07 mm ON THE VEHICLE; reduce the whole flank to a 280 mm chest print (about 1:14.5) and the median becomes 0.91 mm and the p10 becomes 0.18 mm — below any reliable positive line on jersey. The plume is drawn at its own weight for its own size, and the flank art is kept to the three masses. Print a physical scale proof with a stepped wedge (2.0 / 1.0 / 0.7 / 0.5 / 0.35 / 0.25 mm) on the actual garment before any screen is cut.

DECLARE ONE RED AS THE SUBSTRATE COLOUR. There are four in the tree — t1_mats sRGB(196,49,36), lid_gen (159,45,22), cal_gen (214,46,30) — and the render's cannot be sampled: flank_compare reads it at (196,81,67), G/R 0.422, against the photograph's (158,16,6), G/R 0.114. It images salmon. Choose the ink and record it with its provenance; do not eyedrop a frame.

STATE THE ARTEFACT BOUNDARY IN WRITING. This contradicts the vehicle's own measured composition rule and it does so on purpose. Nothing on the model changes. SPEC §10.10's 'ABSOLUTE REPLICATION OF ALL ARTWORK' hard bar governs the MODEL's decals, not a derived stylisation — say so up front so this is not later audited against a rule written for texture bakes.
model_work_required: ISOLATE THE FLANK ART AS ITS OWN LAYER. It is BOX-PROJECTED in the shader (t1_mats: projection='BOX'), so it has no UVs and does not export. T1_W_ART is a live global opacity on the folk-art alpha (ships at 1.00) — difference a W_ART=1.00 render against W_ART=0, or add an AOV. Either way it is a contained change.

REGENERATE tex/swirl.png / swirl_b.png AT THE REFERENCE'S OWN LINE QUALITY, or accept that the poster is drawn by hand from ref_side.jpg and the tile is not the source. The census gap (196 components vs 66, top-3 66.4% vs 84.4%) is the measurement that decides which.

FIX tex/senor.png's MISSING KEYLINE if the wordmark appears in any layout. Measured: among pixels with alpha>200 the 1st-percentile luma is 168.3 and the fraction below luma 80 is 0.0000 — there is no dark ink in the asset at all, against SPEC §3's 'SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow'. Silver on red with no keyline is mud at 200 dpi. script_gen.py is NOT called by build.py, so regenerate by hand or the render silently keeps the old file.

DECLARE ONE BRAND RED as a design ruling with its own provenance line, reconciling the four authored values, and record that it is NOT taken from a render and NOT averaged from the photographs (probe_rev71_red.py prints its own prohibition: 'the photograph's red G/R is 0.0149 .. 0.0344, a 2.3x span. DO NOT QUOTE A SINGLE FIGURE FOR IT').

OPTIONAL, FOR THE MOTION VERSION ONLY: teach folk_gen.py to write a per-component paint-order rank into an unused channel, so a threshold sweep paints the art on largest-first. It already computes the components. Regenerate by hand — folk_gen is not called by build.py.
NOTHING ELSE. No geometry, no lighting, no render chain, no alpha, no stitch. This concept is the one that ships while every pipeline blocker in the program is still open.

all_concepts.note: Cotán's format literally IS a dark niche with produce hung on strings over a sill, and this vehicle has three of them only because the donor was missing three windows — so the subject already is the format rather than a style applied to it. 'The cheapest fact about the vehicle becomes the most beautiful thing in the picture' is the best line in the batch. Understands F259's constraint well enough to demand a SEPARATE named rig so the photograph-facing gates don't red for the wrong reason. Costs the most new geometry (5-8 SSS produce props) and food-photography has had a bodegón moment, so it is slightly less unclaimed than it believes.

concept.title: BODEGÓN — THE HATCH AS A COTÁN NICHE
concept.one_line: Photograph the serving window as a seventeenth-century Spanish still life: black ground, one raking light, a cabbage hanging on a string over the sill, and no bus visible anywhere.
concept.the_image: Black. In the middle of a tall portrait sheet, one landscape rectangle: the serving aperture, dead square to camera, 515.5 × 403.0 mm with its 55 mm corner radius, floating in a black surround that is most of the page. The bay's white bobble fringe scallops the opening — the only ornament in the picture, catching light as a row of small moons. Inside the opening it is nearly dark. A single hard-ish source enters from upper left at roughly 25° above horizontal, warm, about 3000 K, and everything falls to black within 400 mm of depth. On the sill, arranged on Sánchez Cotán's hyperbolic curve — the swag that runs from the upper left of the niche down to the lower right — a whole cabbage and a bulb of garlic SUSPENDED ON STRINGS from the bulb wire above, then on the stone of the sill itself a stack of tortillas, one lime halved with the cut face turned to the light, one dried chile. Nothing else. Far back and barely resolved: 40 mm of the steel worktop's lit edge (GAL_Z_WORK 1.5010) and one bulb burning as a small orange sun, deliberately out of focus. No wordmark, no folk art, no roundel, no vehicle. Palette by area: 70 % black, then warm cream, one cold green (GAL_GREEN 0.1450,0.3050,0.1750 is already in the tree), one red-orange, brass. Motion version: a 6-second silent loop in which only two things move — the hanging cabbage rotating maybe 15° and back, and the bulb's filament breathing. The camera is locked. Nothing else in the frame moves at all. Three prints, one per bay, hung as a triptych.
concept.emotional_claim: Reverence, and the shock of being taken seriously. This is the emotional opposite of every food-truck image ever made: no sizzle, no crowd, no sun, no smiling person holding a taco. It is quiet, dark and formal, and it says that the ingredients — a cabbage, a lime, a stack of tortillas — deserve the treatment Spain gave to game birds and quinces in 1600. For anyone who knows Cotán it is a jolt of recognition. For everyone else it is simply an unaccountably serious picture of a lime, in a category where nothing is ever serious, and that is why they stop. It also does something no other asset in this program can: it makes the hole in the side of the bus, which exists only because the donor was missing three windows, into a sacred architectural frame. The cheapest fact about the vehicle becomes the most beautiful thing in the picture.
formats: Gallery-format print series of three, 500 × 700 mm portrait, on uncoated rag, with a spot gloss varnish on the bulb only and nothing else.
In-restaurant installation: the same three at 1:1 — 515 mm wide each — hung with their sills at the real 1.307 m, so they read as three more hatches cut into the restaurant wall.
Menu cover and wine-list cover, 210 × 297 mm, the niche small in a large black field.
6-second loop for social, 4:5 and 9:16. It will be the only dark, still, silent thing in the feed.
Packaging: the black niche as the face of a takeaway box or bag, printed on kraft so the black goes matt and warm.
Christmas / seasonal card, 148 × 210 mm — the composition takes a seasonal ingredient swap without any redesign at all.
concept.why_not_derivative: It is not a VW-bus picture. It is a still life that happens to be framed by one, so it does not compete in the ocean at all — no silhouette, no sunset, no palms, no daisies, no blueprint, no line art, none of the seven documented saturation tropes, and no vehicle to be generic about. The lineage is exact rather than borrowed: the bodegón is the Spanish still-life tradition that crossed to New Spain and became the Mexican one; Cotán's signature format is literally a dark rectangular window niche with produce hung on strings and set on the sill; and this vehicle has three of those, 515 × 403 mm, with the glass removed and a dark galley behind. I am not applying a style to a subject — the subject already is the format. It also happens to be the only concept here that is immune to the project's two worst measured defects: gloss_compare's paint-spread failure is irrelevant because there is no paint in frame, and the salmon red is irrelevant because the red body is outside the crop.
concept.production_notes: THIS IS THE RISKY ONE AND I WANT THAT ON THE RECORD. A cautious team rejects it in the first review for four reasons, all fair: it is dark, it does not show the product in the appetising way, it does not show the bus, and it cites a painter nobody in the room has heard of. Propose it anyway — the owner's stated bar is 'emotion evoking' and the record carries, in his own words via F92, 'the emotional bar that sits ABOVE clinical accuracy'. Two hard production constraints. FIRST, build this as a SEPARATE NAMED RIG, never as an edit to the studio. F259 licenses a relight — 'Relight the studio and fix the ground if necessary' — but its constraint travels with it (DO NOT change RED, and flank_compare / gloss_compare / probe_rev70_tyre must not regress), and a low-key single-source rig will make every one of those photograph-facing gates unreadable. If it is a second rig, nothing goes red for the wrong reason. SECOND, read everything in linear and refuse clipped data: photometry.py enforces this and its own rules apply hardest to a picture that is 70 % black — a single blown highlight on the lime destroys the whole conceit. Print: the black must be a rich four-colour black or a spot, never 100K, or the fringe's small moons disappear into it. Ceiling to carry: nothing about how this renders is verified, because F45 leaves the aperture interior unmeasured — though F98's measurement that the render's interior sits at 0.705 of exterior cream value against the photograph's 0.774 says the interior is already darker than reference, which is the direction this concept wants.
model_work_required: THE FOOD DOES NOT EXIST. This is the only concept of my three that needs genuine new geometry: five to eight hero produce props — cabbage, garlic bulb, halved lime, dried chile, a stack of tortillas — with real subsurface scattering. Nothing edible exists among the 229 objects. Budget it honestly as the cost of the idea, not as a detail.

INTERIOR CAMERAS AND A MEASURED APERTURE INTERIOR — same precondition as concept 2. F45's roof-aperture half is OPEN, UNGATED and never measured, and this composition is entirely an interior lit through a hole.
A SINGLE-SOURCE LOW-KEY RIG, built as a named second rig so the existing photograph-facing gates are not disturbed. Do not touch the studio.

SUSPENSION HARDWARE. gal_hook ×6 exist and bulb_string / tb_bulbflex give a flex curve to hang from, but the actual strings, knots and the way a cabbage hangs need building. In Cotán the string is half the picture.

GROUND THE BOBBLE FRINGE OR RETHINK IT. It is the picture's only ornament at 500 mm print size, and t1_detail records 'Ball diameter and pitch are INFERRED (each ball is ~2 px)'. This is the one element that would embarrass us at gallery scale.

Confirm the show-side glass really is absent in the render — t1_shell's OPEN_BAYS = (0, 1, 2) says all three panes are removed on +Y, which is exactly right for a niche and should be verified by looking, not by grep.

F72 sits just outside the crop and will creep in on any wider frame: the counter props read within 2.4 DN of the painted body where the photograph shows 60+ DN, and gal_caddy has no dark frame member at all.

all_concepts.note: The sharpest single image here: at 0.95 m the brass nosing IS the horizon, and the picture divides into the reachable and the unreachable by geometry alone rather than by styling. The growth chart ruled with the bus's actual measured heights is the best product in all ten — it is the only idea that converts 76 revisions of measurement into an object a family uses. Real cost honestly named: no human figure exists in the tree and post.py destroys alpha, so the descending hand is genuinely awkward to composite.

concept.title: COUNTER HEIGHT
concept.one_line: Shoot the whole brand from 0.95 m — a four-year-old's eyeline — where the counter lip is above your head and the taco arrives from the sky.
concept.the_image: Camera at z = 0.95 m, 0.55 m out from the counter's outer edge, 28–35 mm, tilted up about 12°, standing where a child stands at bay 3. FRAMING, bottom to top: the lower 55% of the frame is nothing but cream counter fascia, dull, sharp, filling the eye the way a wall does. At 62% frame height a single hard brass hairline runs edge to edge — the nosing at 1.1890 m — and it is dead level with the horizon of the picture, which is the whole compositional gag: the brand's strongest horizontal is a thing you cannot see over. Above it, a band of undercut shadow, then the aperture sill at 1.307 m, then bay 3's opening with the white bobble fringe scalloped along its edge like a row of small moons, then the bulb string at roughly 1.765 m, then the painted lid leaning out over the entire top of the frame at 76° like a ceiling of flowers. Entering top-right, foreshortened and enormous, a forearm and a paper-wrapped taco coming down. LIGHT: focus locked on the brass line at f/2.8 — everything below it sharp and matte, everything above it soft and warm, so the picture is literally divided into the reachable and the unreachable. Key comes from the bulbs and from the 1.110 × 2.034 m sky hole above the counter; the cream fascia is fill-lit and slightly cool. PALETTE: cream occupies the bottom half, one brass line, red only as a 40 mm sliver of flank at frame left, gold folk art dissolved into bokeh, amber bulbs as the top light. MOTION VERSION (vertical, 15 s): locked camera, nothing moves for 9 seconds except the bulbs breathing — then the hand comes down, sets the food on the brass line, and leaves frame. No cut. No music.
concept.emotional_claim: The exact physical memory of being small at a counter: the wood or the metal at your eye level, the impossibility of seeing what is happening up there, and then the arrival of something wonderful from above. It is awe produced by geometry rather than by styling, and it lands on two audiences at once — children feel it as the present tense, adults feel it as a recovered memory. It is also the only frame in this whole program in which the viewer is not a spectator of a vehicle but a customer standing at a hatch.
formats: Children's picture book, 24pp, 210 × 210 mm — the bus is NEVER shown whole; every spread is at 0.95 m, and the reveal on the final spread is the side elevation at adult height. This is the F18 audience served in a format F18 never named, and it is a different artefact from F18.

Growth chart, 300 × 1600 mm, matte paper, with the REAL heights ruled on it: counter 1.19 m, serving sill 1.31 m, aperture head 1.71 m, bulb string ~1.77 m, roof 1.99 m. A child measures themselves against the actual bus.
Restaurant paper placemat, 420 × 297 mm, one colour + cream, printed so it reads correctly from a seated child's angle.
Kids' tee, 90 mm left-chest: brass line, fringe, one hand. Two inks on natural.
Die-cut sticker sheet, A6 kiss-cut: the fringe run, one bulb, the brass corner, a hand and a taco.
15 s vertical film, 1080 × 1920, silent or with room tone only.
3 m restaurant wall graphic, printed at 1:1, so a real child stands beside a rendered counter at the same height as the real one.
concept.why_not_derivative: Every VW bus in the merchandise category is a three-quarter portrait shot from adult eye height, because that is how you photograph a vehicle you admire. This is not a portrait of a vehicle — it is a point of view from inside a transaction, and it is only available because this bus is a building with a counter on it. Structurally it also cannot be mistaken for VW merchandise: `ROUNDEL_X = 2.1290`, `ROUNDEL_Z_AG = 1.0170` — the roundel is four metres away, behind the camera's shoulder, out of frame in every shot in the series. And the reason it is unclaimed is measurable: `studio.views()` defines fourteen cameras and the lowest z in any of them is 1.52 m. In 76 revisions and 793 commits nobody has once rendered this object from the height of the person the original deliverable was written for.
concept.production_notes: Print the growth chart and the placemat as one-colour-plus-substrate; do not attempt process red, since `flank_compare` on out/r75_side.png reads the render's red at median (196,81,67) against the photograph's (158,16,6), G/R 0.422 vs 0.114 — it images salmon, and this composition happily uses almost no red. The brass nosing is the only element that must hold a hard edge at every size, so specify it in final millimetres per SKU (0.6 mm minimum) and never scale one master. For the book, shoot every spread from the same z = 0.95 and vary only x/y — the constancy of the eyeline is the whole device. This is NOT the delivery render and is not gated by F191/F193; say so in the proposal. F192's 'ask once he names the medium' condition is met by the growth chart, which has a real trim size.
model_work_required: Add a `child` camera to `studio.views()` at z = 0.95 with tgt z ≈ 1.30 — trivial, but nothing at that height exists and the composition cannot be previewed without it.

THE GALLEY INTERIOR IS UNGATED AND THIS FRAMING POINTS STRAIGHT AT IT. F45 (roof-aperture interior, 2.91e5 px²) and F15 (A7 unlit roofed body, 6.92e5 px²) have never been measured against a photograph. Render one child-height frame and LOOK before designing to it — `t1_detail.py` records the photographed truth as 'NOTHING inside any aperture is darker than display luma 73 … The galley is a bright room.'

RESOLVE A STALE SOURCE COMMENT AGAINST THE MACHINE. `t1_detail.py` says 'THE SHELL DOES NOT CUT THAT HOLE … Until it is cut, the opening is stood in for HERE … `gal_ceiling` is an emissive panel at the roof line.' STATE.md says 'roof aperture: open, and solid fore / aft / both sides' and reports no roof above 1.710 m at |y|<0.30. The machine outranks the prose; establish which is live before lighting anything through that hole.

THE BOBBLE FRINGE IS INFERRED AND THIS SHOT MAKES IT A HERO. `t1_detail.py`: 'Ball diameter and pitch are INFERRED (each ball is ~2 px)' in the reference. At this camera each ball is hundreds of pixels. Either measure it from a better frame or add a PHOTOS_WANTED item — one close square-on frame of one aperture edge closes it.

F144 STANDS AND IT IS NOW THE KEY LIGHT: 'THE FESTOON BULBS READ AS PEARLS, NOT LIGHTS.' `BULB_PITCH = 0.0286`, `BULB_R = 0.0110` — 22 mm bulbs on a 28.6 mm pitch. Fix the emission and the bloom threshold or the top of every frame is dead.
No human figures exist anywhere in the tree. The hand is the single most important element and it must be built, photographed and composited, or drawn.

`T1_ALPHA` has not been run since rev 62 and no ledger contains the string; every frame in out/ is colortype 2. The hand composite needs a real alpha, and `post.py` destroys alpha (measured: RGBA in, colortype 2 out), so the optics pass cannot be used on this route.

all_concepts.note: Highest emotional voltage and the only concept that makes the model earn its existence — you cannot separate wear from paint in a JPEG, so this is the first output a good photographer could not have shot. 'A thing gets worn where it is loved' is a real line and the accumulation film is the only honest motion vocabulary for a vehicle that cannot drive. Two things keep it off 9: the whole claim rests on inferred touch points ('where the hands go is an INFERENCE, not a survey' — it says so, which is to its credit, but the emotional payload is exactly the invented part), and the warm-on-black glow map sits one bad palette decision away from reading as a thermogram. Also the largest build: authored wear, a pass kit, and an AOV that grep finds nowhere in the tree.

concept.title: Touched
concept.one_line: The bus rendered as nothing but the marks people left on it — every worn, polished, rubbed and tarnished place glowing on black, and the vehicle legible only from its own damage.
concept.emotional_claim:
This is the one that can make somebody's throat go tight.

Every other object in this category is about escape — the road, the sunset, the going. This one says a thing gets worn where it is loved, and here is the map. It reframes damage as a record of service: twenty years of people being fed, written into brass and paint.

And the mechanism is that every single mark is HUMAN CONTACT rather than weather. The bus's shape is being drawn by its customers. Somebody who ate at that counter, or leaned on that sill, or pushed that door handle, is literally in the picture — not represented, PRESENT, as the place where the metal went bright. That is a thing a photograph cannot say and a slogan cannot say, and it is why this concept exists.

It is also, quietly, an argument about the brand: we are not selling you a vehicle, we are showing you twenty years of hands.
formats: THE HERO: a large print, black ground, A1 (594 x 841 mm) or bigger, landscape. On a soft-black uncoated or a matte-laminated heavyweight. This one WANTS scale and it wants dark — at small sizes the shape does not resolve and the whole trick fails. Below A2 do not make it.
MOTION: 20-30 s, no audio dependency. 16:9 for the screen at the counter, 1:1 and 9:16 for social. It loops natively because the last frame fades to the first.

THE COMMERCIAL DERIVATIVE, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST APPAREL ITEM IN ANY OF THESE THREE CONCEPTS: a tee or a tote carrying ONE mark on black and nothing else — the counter-nosing wear band alone, ~200 mm long, a single warm smear. No bus, no logo, no words. It passes the logo-removal test absolutely, because there was never a logo.

SCREEN PRINT ON BLACK in a warm metallic or a glow ink — one plate, one pull. A metallic on black under a restaurant's warm lighting does physically what the image is about, which no CMYK reproduction can.
Restaurant wall, large, behind the pass. This piece belongs in the building it is about.
concept.why_not_derivative:
Nothing in the VW-bus market looks remotely like this, and — the stronger claim — nothing in that market COULD. Every trope in the category is a silhouette treatment: sunset silhouette, line art, blueprint, pop-art fill. This is the ANTI-silhouette, a shape defined by the absence of shape, assembled in the viewer's eye out of disconnected marks.

More importantly it cannot be made from a photograph at all. You cannot separate wear from paint in a JPEG — the two arrive in the same pixel. It requires a 3D asset with separable material passes and authored, causally-located wear. Which is to say: this is the first idea on the table that MAKES THE MODEL EARN ITS EXISTENCE. Seventy-five revisions have produced an asset whose every output so far is something a good photographer could have shot. This one is not.

And it contains no VW roundel, no VW body colour, and arguably no VW shape — only the marks Tacombi's own customers made on a vehicle Tacombi owns.
concept.production_notes:
THIS IS THE RISKY ONE AND I AM NOT SANDING IT DOWN. A cautious team rejects it in the room: a food brand's hero image with no food, no bus, no colour, no logo and no legible product, made entirely of damage. Propose it anyway.

IT IS A PASS-COMPOSITE, DONE ALMOST ENTIRELY IN NUMPY, so it iterates in seconds rather than 5.5 minutes a look once the passes exist. It needs a wear mask as a renderable channel, an object/material ID pass to isolate brass from chrome from paint, and an AO/curvature pass. NONE of these exist — grep for pass_index / use_pass across the tree returns nothing outside the denoiser config.

COPY matte_tap's COLOUR CONTRACT VERBATIM on every File Output slot: color_management='OVERRIDE', view_transform='Raw', look 'None', gamma 1.0. Otherwise a slot inherits AgX/Punchy and every 'linear' pass comes back S-curved. matte_tap's docstring records exactly that trap, and probe_rev54_aov.py is the working precedent for driving an arbitrary internal shader socket to an output by graph walk.

WATCH THE KILL: render with every wear mask at zero and confirm the frame is IDENTICALLY black. matte_tap already did this class of negative control and got cover 0.0000 % against 0.267 mean alpha. A wear pass that is not watched failing is a glow of unknown origin.

16-BIT OR IT BANDS, AND THIS IS THE CONCEPT WHERE IT ACTUALLY BITES. A soft warm gradient falling into black across a metre of print, at 8 bits, will show contour rings — and studio.setup_render writes 16-bit while stitch.py and post.py both truncate silently through PIL. Nothing in the record names this as a print risk. Fix the read path or dither deliberately; do not discover it at the printer with plates cut.

STATE THE HONEST CEILING, IN THE PIECE IF IT CARRIES A CAPTION AND CERTAINLY TO THE OWNER: WHERE THE HANDS GO IS AN INFERENCE, NOT A SURVEY. I looked at ref_side.jpg at 3x — a customer's forearm is on the cab door sill and a cook in white is working the hatch, so the sill and the door are grounded. The counter nosing, the door handle and the engine-lid handle are common sense about a serving counter, not measurement. Nobody has ever photographed this bus's door handle close up, and PHOTOS_WANTED has never carried a touch-point item. 'It cannot be recovered from what we hold' is the true statement, and the ask that would close it is a set of close frames of the touch points — a ten-minute job for anyone standing next to the vehicle.

AND SAY WHAT IT IS NOT: it is not F18. F18's style is locked to 'cartoon with rendered depth' and its scene to 'nothing but the bus, die-cut tight, plus the sun and the papel picado', and its trigger — 'build it after the model is done' — has not fired. This is a different artefact and must be offered as one. F191 and F193 hold the DELIVERY RENDER; this is look-development and should be labelled that way, which is also honest, because 'get the bus ready' is precisely what authoring real wear would be doing.
model_work_required: AN AUTHORED WEAR SYSTEM, WHICH DOES NOT EXIST, AND THIS IS THE BIG BUILD. Today weathering is ONE shared noise field — MOTTLE_AMP 0.55 plus the dust ramp plus the fade — applied everywhere at once, so the roof and the door handle wear identically. I cropped out/r75_side.png at the rocker and looked: there is no grime tide, no chip, no scuff, no handprint anywhere; the arch lip is as clean as the roof. TOUCHED needs wear with CAUSES: per-material, per-location masks keyed to contact, hand-painted in the same pipeline as swirl.png. This is also the fix the entire ARTIFACT territory needs, so it is not a cost of this concept — it is the reason to do this concept.

THE CHIP GATE IS DEAD ON THE RED AND BOTH PROCEDURAL ROUTES ARE ALREADY REFUTED IN SOURCE (Pointiness is mesh-density-dependent; True Normal 'detects TESSELLATION, not folds' and was withdrawn). Stop trying to derive it. Author it. Same conclusion as Relic, reached from the other end.

A PASS KIT — passes.py, ~80 lines. use_pass_object_index, use_pass_material_index, use_pass_normal, use_pass_position, use_pass_diffuse_color, AO, and cryptomatte. Drive pass_index off build.py's own ASSIGN list, which gives 17 stable material keys (paint, chrome, chrome_d, glass, tyre, rubber, dark, steel, bumpercream, countercream, capred, capwhite, lidmural, lidsign, roundelred, amber, bulb) so the ID islands map to design intent for free. Z and cryptomatte to OPEN_EXR_MULTILAYER.
A WEAR AOV — the authored masks driven out through an Emission AOV so the composite can read them directly, rather than being inferred from the beauty. probe_rev54_aov.py is the precedent.

T1_SENOR_TARNISH=1 for the three tarnish blooms. They are the only marks in the piece that are already measured to six figures, which is worth saying out loud: 'Señor' median (85,46,35) against clean silver (126,123,127), warm oxide at a* +14.0 against +6.9.
THE BRASS NOSING NEEDS A LENGTHWISE WEAR PARAMETER — bright in the middle 1.8 m, dull at the ends. It is the single most important mark in the image and the model has no handle for it.
16-BIT READ/WRITE THROUGH stitch.py AND post.py, or an explicit dither on export. On black-ground work this is not a nicety.

IF THE MOTION VERSION IS MADE: prototype T1_SAVE (build.py's only persistence, and it appears in ZERO handoff documents). A wear accumulation is a mask animation, not a geometry animation, so it does not need keyframed hinges — but it does need one saved scene rather than a rebuild per frame, or the flicker floor eats it. And take the flicker seriously: the render is not run-to-run deterministic, ~2.04 % of pixels move >8 levels on hero34f and 7.90 % on the body, which on a sequence is a visible boil rather than a stills noise floor.

all_concepts.note: The third caption line — printing the object's own uncertainty beside its dimension — is genuinely unseen on merchandise, and it converts 75 revisions of stubbornness into the product's actual content, which is the rarest kind of alignment available here. Plate 1 (a 22 mm bulb life-size on a 320 mm sheet) is a real physical shock. Held below the top because 'museum specimen plate' is an established genre and 'being trusted' is a designer's feeling more than a customer's; the audience for a 6 pt provenance grade is narrow. Honest that the macro camera class does not exist.

concept.title: AS MEASURED
concept.one_line: Six macro specimen plates of parts VW never made — each printed at a stated magnification and captioned with its own dimension AND its own certainty, so the sheet publishes its doubt alongside its beauty.
concept.the_image:
SIX SQUARE PLATES, 320 x 320 mm, subject dead centre on paper-white with a 40 mm margin. Light is a COPY STAND, not a studio: two large sources at plus/minus 45 degrees elevation, no visible key, no glamour, no environment. Everything sharp corner to corner — f/22 — and the caption prints the near/far limits so the sharpness is a stated fact rather than a look. No cast shadow; a 2 mm contact darkening only, so each object floats on the sheet like a pressed specimen.

PLATE 1 — THE BULB, 1:1. A single 22.0 mm festoon bulb reproduced at EXACTLY life size, alone, in the middle of a 320 mm sheet. 298 mm of empty paper around a thumbnail. This is the shock plate and it opens the set: the viewer's hand goes to it before their eye does.
PLATE 2 — THE BADGE, 6.9:1. The hubcap roundel filling the frame: cream V over W, the 8.08 mm ring band, the 6.0 mm plate, on the dome's red, the dome's curvature reading as one slow vertical gradient behind the glyph.
PLATE 3 — THE NOSING, 30:1. 19.9 mm of brass in elevation, a single horizontal band running edge to edge. Tan laminate above, cream below, one specular line along the crown of the roll. A Barnett Newman zip that happens to be a counter lip.
PLATE 4 — THE EDGE, 23:1. The tail board's 26 mm edge stack square-on: near-black band, cream band, red band. Three horizontal stripes and nothing else.
PLATE 5 — THE LUG, 18:1. One transverse tread groove, 6.0 mm deep, the crown falling away either side.
PLATE 6 — THE LOUVRE, 28:1. Two blades and the 7.0 mm aperture between them, the dark box receding behind.

PALETTE: paper white; the object's own colours; ONE caption ink (warm near-black); ONE hairline rule in brass. Nothing else on the sheet.
TYPOGRAPHY: 6 pt condensed caps, bottom-left, THREE LINES ONLY — WHAT IT IS / HOW BIG IT IS / HOW SURE WE ARE. Examples, verbatim from source: "TAIL BOARD EDGE · 26.0 mm · BOARD THICKNESS NOT MEASURED"; "TREAD LUG · 64 PER REVOLUTION · DECLARED — THE MEASUREMENT ADMITS 48 TO 84"; "COUNTER NOSING · 19.9 mm IN ELEVATION · MEASURED, 113 COLUMNS · PROJECTION 7.0 mm INFERRED"; "HUBCAP BADGE · 86.9 mm · PROPORTION NEVER COMPARED TO A PHOTOGRAPH". The third line is the entire idea.
concept.emotional_claim: BEING TRUSTED. The pleasure of a museum label written by someone who declined to bluff. Every other object in a shop tells you it is perfect; this one hands you a beautiful thing and, in six-point type, tells you exactly which part of it nobody has checked. Reading "22.0 mm · NOT MEASURED" under a lovely object produces a specific and rare feeling — you are being addressed as an adult. It also converts seventy-five revisions of stubborn honesty into the product's actual content, so the thing that made this project slow becomes the thing that makes it unbuyable elsewhere.
formats: SET OF SIX PLATES, 320 x 320 mm, matte uncoated 300 gsm, litho or giclée. Uncoated and matte because a specimen sheet must not glare — the object supplies all the gloss in the picture and the paper must supply none.

MASTER SHEET, 700 x 1000 mm, all six in a 3x2 grid with one shared scale bar serving the whole sheet. This is the wall piece; the jump between 1:1 and 30:1 across one sheet is the experience. DO NOT PROMISE THIS UNTIL THE STITCH CHAIN IS PROVEN ABOVE 3840 px (see production notes).

POSTCARD / BOOKMARK SET, 105 x 148 mm, same six plates, same captions at 4.5 pt. The cheap tier, and the one that goes in a pocket at the counter. Caption legibility must be proof-printed, not assumed.
WEB SCROLL — one page, six plates, the magnification ratio counting up as you scroll from 1:1 to 30:1. Free, and it is the argument for the paper.
NOT APPAREL. The caption is the concept and 6 pt type does not survive a screen or a needle. Anything that drops the third line is a different, worse idea.
concept.why_not_derivative: The VW-bus merch ocean sells THE WHOLE VEHICLE — sunset silhouette, surf, palms, minimal line art, blueprint elevation. Every single one of those is a picture of a van. THERE IS NO VAN IN THIS. The nearest trope is the blueprint, which is a standing stock category sold by the sheet, and the difference is exactly the one that matters: a stock VW blueprint annotates the FACTORY object, drawn from a manual anyone can buy, and every dimension on it belongs to Volkswagen. Every subject here belongs to the CONVERSION — a brass counter lip, a tail-board edge, a festoon bulb, a louvre — parts VW never pressed and no catalogue holds. It is also the only merchandise I know of that PRINTS ITS OWN UNCERTAINTY. An advert cannot do that; a stock asset has no uncertainty to print because nobody measured anything.
concept.production_notes:
MAGNIFICATION LADDER, computed from live source constants, at a 600 mm print with the subject filling the frame: bulb 22.0 mm = 27.3:1; counter nosing gold 19.9 mm = 30.2:1; louvre pitch 21.1 mm = 28.4:1; tail-board edge stack 26.0 mm = 23.1:1; hubcap badge 86.9 mm = 6.9:1; hubcap 274.0 mm = 2.2:1.

RESOLUTION IS FINE; THE CAMERA IS NOT. A 320 mm plate at 300 dpi is 3780 px, INSIDE the 3840 x 2640 the MARGIN chain was proven at (rev 57, one view, 106.8 min). The 700 x 1000 mm master sheet needs ~8270 px and is 2.15x above anything ever stitched — that one needs a proving run and stitch.py's exit code READ, not assumed.

EVERY CAPTION FIGURE MUST BE READ FROM SOURCE AT BUILD TIME, NEVER TYPED. A plate whose dimension went stale is worse than no plate, and it would be the exact failure this whole set is about. The grade line likewise: pull it from the constant's own comment or from OPEN_FINDINGS, do not paraphrase.

Substrate: uncoated, matte, warm-white rather than blue-white — the cream and brass both die against a cool white. Caption ink warm near-black, never 100% K.
model_work_required: A MACRO CAMERA CLASS. This is the whole blocker and it is not a resolution problem — it is a camera problem, which is much better news. `studio.views()` has no macro entry; the nearest is `detail_f` at loc (4.90, 2.15, 1.85) to tgt (1.95, 0.05, 1.16), a ~3.5 m standoff. And nothing can be cropped out of what exists: I measured the subject bbox in out/r75_side.png at x 212-1457 (1245 px on a 1600 px frame), which puts a 22.0 mm bulb at 5-7 px and the 86.9 mm badge at 24-27 px. Build a `macro_*` family: 100-200 mm lens, 0.15-0.5 m standoff, one per plate.

USE `aim()`'s EXISTING DOF REPORTING AS THE CAPTION'S OWN HONESTY. It already reads `T1_FSTOP`, sets `aperture_blades = 9` and `aperture_rotation = radians(11)`, and `dof_limits()` returns near/far/hyperfocal. Set f/16-f/22 for the all-sharp specimen look and PRINT the returned limits in the caption. Nothing in this project has ever used this machinery.

FIX THE HUBCAP BADGE'S BLACK RELIEF HALO BEFORE PLATE 2. I cropped out/r75_side.png at the rear hubcap at 6x and looked: every stroke of the render's badge carries a heavy dark self-shadow and the glyph reads as a dark blob, where ref_side.jpg at 6x shows clean cream strokes on red with no dark at all. Cause is almost certainly `CAP_EMBLEM_DEPTH = 0.0060` — a 6.0 mm plate on an 86.9 mm badge — plus the `capwhite` albedo. Ablate the depth and look before tuning anything.

THE MOTTLE / DENOISER SPECKLE IS THE PICTURE AT 6.9:1. I looked at out/r75_hero34r.png at 2x: the body red carries visible dark pepper across the whole panel. `MOTTLE_AMP` defaults to 0.55 via `T1_MOT_AMP`. At specimen magnification that speckle stops being texture and becomes dirt on the plate. Render the ladder and choose deliberately.

PLATE 2 IS THE ONE THAT COULD BE WRONG AND THE RECORD SAYS SO. STATE.md: "hubcap badge is SELF-CONSISTENCY ONLY -- CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC has never been compared to a frame; see PHOTOS_WANTED item 7." Printing a proportion nothing has ever checked at 6.9:1 is the wrong direction. Either close item 7 (ONE HUBCAP, SQUARE ON AND CLOSE — still open) or let the caption's third line carry it, which is the honest and interesting option.

EXPORT `T1_FX=0` BY HAND FOR ANY STITCHED PLATE. `grep -c T1_FX hq_render.py` returns 0, while hero.py — the chain it replaced — forces it off with the docstring "Per-strip optics band at the seams." And pass `--backdrop white` explicitly: post.py's live constant is `BACKDROP = "headroom"` with peak 252, so the default drops a 252-grey field inside a white margin.

all_concepts.note: Strongest single payload in the brief — hungry, late, the lights are on — and that IS a food brand's whole business. The form-following halftone is a genuine technical differentiator with the same normals argument as the loteria. The window-decal derivative (bulb line alone as one continuous stroke, working at 900 mm and at 32 px) is probably the most commercially valuable single item anywhere in this set and doubles as the logo-scale device. Marked down because two-ink night-poster-of-a-lit-place is a known register, and it correctly flags that the lit interior is an unmeasured go/no-go (F45 and F15 both ungated).

concept.title: ABIERTO
concept.one_line: Two inks, a coarse form-following halftone, and the only light in the picture is the bulb line and three lit holes — the bus as the thing you spot across a plaza when you are hungry and it is late.
concept.the_image:
The vehicle three-quarter from the serving side, at DISTANCE, from a standing customer's eye height of 1.55 m — which is the reference photograph's own derived camera height (`REF_MEASUREMENTS.md`: 'a pinhole model with camera height ≈ 1.55 m, horizon y ≈ 340'), not the 3.55 m the shipped hero sits at. The vehicle occupies roughly 45% of the frame width and sits LOW in the composition, with a great deal of dark above it. No landscape. No sky. No ground plane you can name.

TWO INKS: a deep near-black warm (≈ #1A1210) and one warm light (a cream-gold, ≈ #E8C87A), on natural uncoated stock that carries the mid-tone.

The tonal structure is brutal. The body is almost entirely the dark ink. The ONLY light in the picture is:
— the FESTOON BULB LINE, tracing the drip rail nose to tail, wrapping the rear roof dome, and running the free edge of the propped tail board. One continuous stroke of light describing the whole silhouette in a single gesture.
— the THREE SERVING APERTURES, glowing, each 515.5 × 403.0 mm with its 55 mm corner radius, the bobble fringe reading as a scalloped rim of light, and the galley's shapes inside them as dark cut-outs against the glow.
— the COUNTER'S TOP SURFACE catching that glow as one hard horizontal band — the strongest line in the composition.
— the MURAL LID lit from below by the apertures, so its rosettes read as a faint patterned field rather than as a graphic.

EVERYTHING IS HALFTONE. No smooth gradient anywhere. And here is the trick that makes it geometry rather than a filter: THE SCREEN ANGLE FOLLOWS THE SURFACE NORMAL. The dot grid wraps the body's curvature like a mesh stocking — the roof's screen runs one way, the flank's another, the wheel arch's dots curve round it. On the flat counter slab the screen is dead straight, which is what makes the counter read as the only flat thing in the picture. A halftone taken off a photograph cannot do this; it needs a normal pass.

Dot spec: 34 lpi at A1 (a 0.75 mm cell), 55 lpi at A3. Coarse on purpose, so the dot is a visible object at one metre and dissolves into tone at four.
concept.emotional_claim:
You are hungry, it is late, and you see the lights are on. That is the whole payload, and it is the most primitive good feeling a food brand can own. The bus is not being presented to you as a product — it is being presented as a destination you have just spotted, at the distance from which you spot it. Everything about the composition serves that: low in frame, far away, dark above, and the only information is where the light is.

The coarse halftone does the second half of the emotional work in a way a clean render structurally cannot. Big visible dots read as distance, as memory, as a printed thing — as something that already happened to you rather than something being sold to you now.
formats: A1, 594 × 841 mm, two-ink screen print on natural 300 gsm. The flagship, and it wants to be big: at 34 lpi the dot is a texture you walk up to and then lose. This is a wall piece, not a poster.
A3, 297 × 420 mm, at 55 lpi for the shop. Re-screen for the size; do not scale the A1 file.
305 × 305 mm album format, cropped to the aperture band alone — three lit rectangles, a counter line, and dark. Almost abstract, and the strongest thing in the set at small size.

RESTAURANT APPLICATION, and this is where it earns its keep: the same image at 1.2 × 1.7 m as a two-colour wall vinyl or a hand-painted mural behind the counter, halftone scaled to a 3 mm dot so it reads from the street. Two colours is within a signwriter's reach.

Window decal derivative, single ink: the BULB LINE ALONE, gold on clear vinyl, 900 mm wide. One continuous stroke that describes the entire vehicle — it works at 900 mm and it works at 32 px, which makes it the natural logo-scale device and the natural favicon.

Motion derivative, if and when animation is authorised: the same frame with the bulb line igniting nose to tail. It is a single path, so it animates for free. Flagged only — there is NO owner ruling on animation anywhere in the record.
concept.why_not_derivative:
The market's night VW is a campfire silhouette against a starfield — a vehicle parked in wilderness, meaning escape. This has no landscape, no sky, no horizon, no stars, and no vehicle-as-freedom. It is a BUILDING WITH ITS LIGHTS ON, seen across a distance, in two inks. That is a completely different proposition from the same body shape, and it is the proposition Tacombi's own founding account supports: the engine was scrapped and the transmission sold, so this thing does not go anywhere and never will.

The form-following screen is the technical differentiator and it is not decoration: no halftone derived from a photograph can rotate its screen with the surface, because a photograph has no normals. Anyone can see that this was drawn from an object that was modelled, which is the only honest reason for this project to exist in the first place.

Honest flag: a night piece brushes against territory the record parks. F92 holds the Playa hero as 'DEPRIORITISED, NOT CANCELLED' and licenses nothing to do now — but its object is a photoreal environment DELIVERY RENDER via `playa_env.py`, not an illustrated two-ink print, and F57 records that the in-tree playa path renders no vehicle at all. Meanwhile F259 explicitly opens the lighting rig: 'Relight the studio and fix the ground if necessary', with the single constraint 'DO NOT change RED' — which this concept honours by having no red ink in it. State that distinction and put it to him rather than assuming it.
concept.production_notes:
BUILD THE SEPARATION FROM A LINEAR LUMINANCE, NOT FROM THE TONE-MAPPED FRAME. Read the 16-bit master through `photometry.read_png`, never PIL — PIL has no 16-bit RGB path and truncates silently (F263 / rule 58), and the whole downstream chain, `stitch.py` and `post.py` alike, already throws the low byte away at its first line. An 8-bit source will band across the very large dark body areas, and a halftone AMPLIFIES banding rather than hiding it. This is the single most likely way this concept fails at the printer.

SCREEN ANGLES AND MOIRÉ. Run the light ink at 45° base and the dark at 15°, with the normal-driven rotation on top. Then check against the two regular repeats already on the vehicle: the louvre block at `LOUV_PITCH = 0.021111` m (21.1 mm) and the tyre tread at π × 0.6649 / 64 = 32.6 mm. At A1 those land at roughly 3.1 mm and 4.8 mm on the sheet — four to six halftone cells, squarely in the moiré band. PROOF AT FINAL SIZE ON THE ACTUAL STOCK; moiré cannot be judged on screen.
