formats: Digitally printed cups, napkins, sleeves, bags, wrap and tissue — the whole short-run consumable range, where variable data costs nothing per unit
Loyalty and gift cards, each a unique field with its seed printed — the cheapest possible collectible mechanic

In-store screen, 9:16 or 16:9: the field PAINTS ITSELF ON in the signwriter's own measured order — largest mass first, then tendrils, then rosettes, then the dark commas last, which is the real hierarchy (the first three strokes lay 84.4 % of the ink)
Web and app background generated per session, seed shown in the footer
A LOCKED two-ink version (gold + dark on red), fixed and unchanging, for screen-printed apparel, litho, embroidery and vinyl — the system splits deliberately and says so
Brand-book spread showing the GRAMMAR plus twelve example seeds captioned "none of these is the pattern"
concept.why_not_derivative: It is the only idea here that cannot be screenshotted and resold, because there is no file to steal — the asset is a program. The entire VW-merch category is built on reproducing one image at volume; this refuses to have an image. It also converts the single genuinely unusual property of this project into public brand behaviour: the vehicle's artwork is already PROCEDURAL, authored by a generator that exists, that was built against a measured census, and that solves sizes rather than counts. Nobody in the category has a generator, because nobody in the category measured anything. And it is the strongest possible answer to "is this an advert or a thing people want": an advert is identical every time by definition.
concept.production_notes: THIS IS THE RISKY ONE AND HERE IS EXACTLY WHY A CAUTIOUS TEAM KILLS IT: it only works on digital print. Spot-screen, flexo and litho all want one locked plate, so the system must formally SPLIT — a locked two-ink version for screened and stamped goods, a generated version for anything digitally printed — and the guidelines have to say that plainly rather than pretending it is universal. Second refusal, and it is the one that gets argued about in the room: the brand book CANNOT SHOW THE PATTERN. It shows the grammar — mark inventory, area ratios, density gradient, four-ink triad, minimum stroke in final millimetres — and then twelve seeds explicitly labelled as not-the-pattern. That is an unusual document and some people will experience it as the absence of a deliverable. It is not; it is a stricter deliverable, because a grammar can be violated in ways a JPEG cannot. Third: every generated field still obeys the same reduction ladder as concept 1 — stroke widths declared in final millimetres per SKU, 0.5 mm positive minimum, and the smallest components dropped below ~200 mm. A generator that emits sub-0.2 mm hairlines at cup scale will do it a hundred thousand times.
model_work_required: REFACTOR folk_gen.py TO TAKE A SEED AND EMIT SVG. Today it emits a 4096² raster bound to the vehicle's flank. The cheap half is already done: it is NOT called by build.py, so it is already a standalone generator with no render dependency — this is the single highest-leverage piece of work in this brief and it needs no Blender at all.

FIX F16 FIRST, BEFORE GENERATING ANYTHING. The rosettes are drawn at the diameter of their gold CORE and are systematically undersized. Generating a hundred thousand undersized rosettes multiplies one open finding by a hundred thousand, across physical objects that cannot be recalled.

RECONCILE THE COMPONENT CENSUS BEFORE TRUSTING THE GRAMMAR: 30 (folk_gen's own rev-11 row), 66 (ref_side.jpg), 196 (the grounding pass on the shipped tile). A generator tuned to the wrong one produces a family-consistent field that is consistently wrong.

DECLARE ONE BRAND RED AS A DESIGN RULING WITH ITS PROVENANCE, before a single unit prints. Three authored reds disagree in the tree; the render images salmon (G/R 0.422 against the photograph's 0.114); and the photographs cannot supply one either — the probe prints its own prohibition against quoting a single figure. This must be chosen, written down and signed off, not sampled.

NOT F18. This is deliberately a different artefact from the die-cut sticker, whose style and scene the owner locked and whose build trigger has not fired. It also runs against the instinct behind a locked brand asset, and I am proposing it anyway — the refusal to lock is the idea, not a side effect of it.

all_concepts.note: Emotionally direct and beautifully specified, and the 9-sided iris already sitting unused in aim() is lovely craft. But shallow-DOF fairy-light bokeh is close to the most photographed image on earth — this is a stock photo with better provenance, and craft is not originality. Worst buildability in the set by some distance: it is named after a filament the model does not have (the bulb is one opaque 7x4 ball), and F144 already grades the model-side lever EXHAUSTED on the exact element the whole concept rests on.

concept.title: THE FILAMENT
concept.one_line: One festoon bulb at 27:1 after dark — glass, brass crimp and tungsten coil sharp, the rest of the chain dissolving into nine-sided amber bokeh with the flex sagging black across it.
concept.the_image:
LANDSCAPE 3:1. Camera at the drip rail, 200 mm equivalent, 250 mm standoff, WIDE OPEN at f/2.0. Time: the twenty minutes after sunset — the sky gone, the cream body still holding a trace of cool ambient, the bulbs the only warm source in frame.

The rail runs lower-left to upper-right on a shallow diagonal. ONE bulb is sharp, third from the left, sitting on the lower-left thirds intersection — and you can see INTO it: the glass envelope, the brass cap's crimp, and the tungsten coil, a tight helix maybe 4 mm long, the single brightest thing in the picture, blooming just past clipping so it flares rather than clips flat. Everything in front of and behind it dissolves by distance: the next bulb is a soft amber lozenge, the one after a clean 9-SIDED DISC, and by the fifth they are overlapping bokeh the size of oranges, stacking into a warm field at the upper right.

The black flex sags between them in slack catenaries — out of focus, a soft dark line drawn across the amber. It is the only line in the picture and it does all the drawing.

Underneath, the cream body takes the SPILL: a warm wash falling off with distance, so the bottom third is a gradient from lit ivory to cool grey. Above the rail: nothing. Dark.

PALETTE IS TWO COLOURS AND A BLACK LINE. Emission at the material's own authored (1.000, 0.760, 0.442) — saturation 0.558, which the render currently loses entirely; cream lit warm; flex at true black. No third hue anywhere in frame. No red, no gold, no folk art, no bus.

MOTION VERSION — 2.4 s seamless loop. The chain ignites LEFT TO RIGHT, one bulb at a time, on an 8 fps STEPPED cadence: 25 bulbs on the tail board is 25 steps, which is the run length the geometry already computes. Each bulb flares past the bloom threshold and settles back one step later, so the leading edge of the ignition is a travelling overshoot. Ends held lit. Loops by cutting to black for two frames — an inverter dropping out, not a fade.
concept.emotional_claim: ARRIVING SOMEWHERE WARM AFTER DARK. Not nostalgia — APPETITE. A bulb chain at this distance is pre-verbal: it means the place is open, someone is inside, you can sit down and be fed. That is the entire emotional business of a taqueria compressed into one out-of-focus amber node, and it arrives before the viewer identifies a single object. The person who has eaten at Tacombi recognises it instantly; the person who has not simply wants to be wherever this is. It is also the only asset in the whole programme that would go on a wall in a home rather than a shop.
formats: PANORAMIC PRINT, 1200 x 400 mm, on SATIN or GLOSS. This is the one image in the programme that WANTS the glare — a real specular sheen on the paper makes the bokeh read as light rather than as printed orange. Matte would kill it.
PORTRAIT PRINT, 900 x 1200 mm, for the single-bulb-plus-catenary crop. Big enough that the coil is life-size-plus and the viewer leans in.

WALLPAPER SET — phone lock screen (1290 x 2796), desktop (3840 x 2160). Free, and it is the piece that does the marketing for everything else. A lock screen is worn in public more often than a t-shirt.
LOOP, 1080 x 1350, 2.4 s, silent. Social and in-store screens. The ignition is the whole content; no type on the frame.

LIMITED EDITION: same panoramic, screen-printed on deep-black uncoated with SPOT FOIL OR SPOT UV ON THE IN-FOCUS BULB ONLY, so the one sharp light catches the actual light in the actual room. One extra pass, one extra plate, and it makes the print physically responsive to where the buyer hangs it.

APPAREL — the bokeh chain as a PRINTED hem stripe or side-seam tape, 200 x 25 mm. Printed, never embroidered: a needle cannot make bokeh, and a satin-stitched version of this is a row of orange ovals, which is the failure it is trying to avoid.
concept.why_not_derivative: The category's night imagery is bus-at-sunset with a warm gradient behind it — the single most saturated frame on the shelf. THIS HAS NO BUS, NO SUNSET, NO HORIZON AND NO SILHOUETTE. It is a light source photographed at 27:1; the vehicle is present only as a cream surface catching spill in the bottom third, unidentifiable. It sits closer to contemporary photography than to merchandise. And the specific object being photographed — a festoon string clipped to a food truck's drip rail — belongs entirely to the taqueria: zero VW shape content, zero VW mark content, nothing a factory ever made. It passes the logo-removal test completely, because there is no logo in it to remove.
concept.production_notes:
THE ONE-BULB CROP IS 27.3:1 AT A 600 mm PRINT AND 54:1 AT 1200 mm. That is not a crop of anything — it is a dedicated camera, which is good news because it means the resolution ceiling never binds. A 1200 x 400 mm panoramic at 300 dpi is 14173 px on the long edge, far above anything ever stitched, SO SHOOT THE HERO BULB AS ITS OWN FRAME AND COMPOSE THE CHAIN, rather than rendering one enormous stitched plate. The out-of-focus bulbs carry almost no high-frequency detail, so they can be rendered small and upscaled without penalty; only the sharp bulb needs real pixels.

THIS CONCEPT TAKES THE OPTICS CHAIN AND GIVES UP THE CUT-OUT, DELIBERATELY. post.py reads `rgba[..., :3]` and saves three channels, so alpha and optics are mutually exclusive in this tree. A macro bokeh print wants bloom and grain and does not want a silhouette. Say that in the ledger rather than discovering it.

Seed the grain from the frame number for the loop. post.py's `grain(..., seed=7)` is fixed, so identical grain on every frame reads as dirt on the lens — the single most amateur tell available and one line to fix.

DUSK IS A RELIGHT, NOT A REPAINT, AND THE OWNER HAS ALREADY OPENED IT. F259, rev 71: "Relight the studio and fix the ground if necessary." The rig is open; "DO NOT change RED" is the constraint and this concept never touches RED — there is no red in the frame.
model_work_required: THE BULB HAS NO FILAMENT. THIS IS THE HEADLINE ITEM AND THE CONCEPT IS NAMED AFTER IT. `_ball(verts, faces, c, r, nu=7, nv=4)` builds a SOLID 7x4 UV sphere, and `emissive()`'s docstring says exactly what it is: "A lit festoon bulb: warm emission over a pearl-white envelope." There is no glass, no cap, no gas, no coil — the whole bulb is one opaque ball with emission on it. BUILD: a transmissive glass envelope, a brass/bakelite cap with its crimp, and a coiled tungsten filament as the ONLY emitter inside it. Everything this image promises lives in that one addition.

THE EMISSION IS SWAMPED AT STUDIO EXPOSURE, AND THE REGISTER ALREADY MEASURED IT ON A PAINTED WINDOW. t1_mats.py, F134's own comment: "the rendered bead reads sat 0.087 against a photographed 0.561 (ref_side.jpg, painted window), while THIS emission colour's own saturation is 0.558 ... the envelope `base` below has saturation 0.067, which is what the render actually reads, so the null hypothesis is that the emission contributes nothing at studio exposure and we are seeing the base lit by the cyclorama." I CONFIRMED IT BY LOOKING: in out/r75_side.png at 3x the drip-rail chain renders as a row of WHITE PEARLS with no warmth and no spill, while ref_side.jpg at 6x shows an amber line that visibly washes the cream below it. F144 stands. ABLATE `T1_BULB_STR` AND `T1_BULB_BASEV` BEFORE TUNING EITHER (rule 36) — both switches exist, both are measurement-only, and neither changes what ships.

SEVEN SEGMENTS AROUND IS A HEPTAGON AT 27:1. `nu=7, nv=4` is 22 vertices per bulb — invisible at the 5-7 px a bulb occupies in the side render, unmissable at macro. Raise `nu`/`nv` for a macro build behind its own switch. (Note this is exactly the property CONCEPT 3 keeps on purpose; the two concepts want opposite builds and both are legitimate.)

THE FLEX IS A SQUARE WIRE. `T.sweep(wire, [(0.0026, 0.0026), (0.0026, -0.0026), (-0.0026, -0.0026), (-0.0026, 0.0026)], ...)` is a 5.2 x 5.2 mm SQUARE section. Flex is round. And in ref_side.jpg the tail-board run hangs as a SLACK CATENARY drooping well below its anchors, while `bulbflex` follows the rail rigidly. The sag is the drawing in this image — build it.

PUSH THE EMITTER ABOVE THE BLOOM THRESHOLD SO IT ACTUALLY FLARES. `T1_BULB_STR` ships at 9.0 and post.py's `BLOOM_THR` is 0.94. Drop the key, raise the emitter, and check the flare is coming from the compositor rather than from clipping — a clipped white core is not a flare and will print as a flat disc.

EXPLOIT THE IRIS THAT ALREADY EXISTS AND HAS NEVER BEEN USED. `aim()` sets `aperture_blades = 9` and `aperture_rotation = math.radians(11)`, so out-of-focus speculars come back as 9-SIDED amber polygons rather than perfect discs. That single detail is the difference between this reading as a photograph and reading as a Gaussian blur, and it is already in the code.

all_concepts.note: The sharpest single observation in the brief — the faceting is ALREADY in the mesh, so the aesthetic costs nothing — and the enamel pin is exactly the right format for a 7-sided bulb. Fails the test that matters most here: nothing about it is about THIS bus or THIS brand. Hard-shaded low-poly-as-retro-CGI is a whole exhausted design trend, and the same four posters could be made from any object at all. Its self-declared bravery (throw away the photorealism) is also its weakness — being contrarian about the pipeline is not the same as having an idea about the vehicle.

concept.title: MACHINED
concept.one_line: THE RISKY ONE — abandon photorealism at exactly the scale where it breaks: four hard-shaded, visibly faceted macro posters that show the object as it is actually built, twenty-eight flat quadrilaterals and all.
concept.the_image:
FOUR POSTERS, 500 x 700 mm portrait. ONE hard key at 35 degrees upper-left, one weak fill, black shadow, NO bounce, NO environment, NO bloom, NO grain, NO vignette, NO denoiser mush. FLAT SHADING throughout — every facet is a single flat tone with a hard terminator at every edge. Nothing is smoothed and nothing pretends.

POSTER 1 — THE BULB, ~27:1, filling two-thirds of the sheet. A SEVEN-SIDED BARREL with four latitude rings: twenty-eight quadrilateral faces, each one a distinct flat value stepping from near-white on the key side, through four or five warm mid-greys, to a single near-black facet on the shadow side. It reads as a cut gem, a brass nut, a twelve-sided die — anything but a light. The square-section flex enters bottom-left as a hard 5.2 mm cable. KEPT, NOT FIXED: at this scale the square section is honest and it is beautiful.
POSTER 2 — THE DOME, 2.2:1. The hubcap as a faceted hemisphere, the 96-segment cap ring stepping visibly around it, and the badge rendered as a FLAT CRISP GRAPHIC with no relief shadow at all — the black halo that ruins it photoreally simply does not exist under flat shading.
POSTER 3 — THE TIP, 23:1. The tail board's end, where `seg=4` corners read as FOUR VISIBLE CHAMFERS rather than a radius, and the three colour bands — near-black, cream, red — meet each chamfer as hard mitres. Six flat shapes and eight edges.
POSTER 4 — THE CORNER, 4:1. The counter's 150 mm plan radius as a POLYGON, the brass nosing stepping round it in visible flats, the tan slab above and cream fascia below meeting it in two straight lines.

PALETTE: three or four FLAT INKS, DECLARED not sampled — one red, one cream, one brass, one near-black. No gradient anywhere on any sheet except the facet steps themselves, and those are STEPS, not gradients. Riso or screen print, so the ink sits ON the paper and the flats are physically flat.

TYPE ON THE FACE: NONE. One blind-embossed chop bottom-right. The dimension and the part name go on the REVERSE, letterpressed, where only the owner sees them.
concept.emotional_claim: WANTING TO PICK IT UP. Facets make an object feel HELD — cut, turned, machined, finished by a hand on a lathe. At 27:1 a bulb with seven visible flats stops being a light and becomes a jewel, a nut, a die: a well-made small thing. That is a tactile pleasure photorealism can never deliver, because photorealism asks you to BELIEVE and faceting invites you to TOUCH. And there is a second, quieter feeling underneath it: the sheets are honest. This is what we actually built. It rhymes exactly with the vehicle's own origin — a $3,000 bus, missing three windows, cut open with a grinder — because it is a picture of construction rather than a picture of a finish.
formats: POSTER SET OF FOUR, 500 x 700 mm, RISO or screen print on uncoated 250 gsm. Riso IS this aesthetic: three spot inks, no halftone, hard edges, visible mis-registration of half a millimetre that makes the flats sit on the paper rather than in it. Do not offset this; offset would smooth exactly what the concept is about.

ENAMEL PIN of the faceted bulb, 25 mm. Seven facets is a LOW enough count to survive hard enamel at 25 mm — a photoreal bulb at that size is a blob, a seven-sided one is a legible object. This is the format the concept was born for.
EMBROIDERED PATCH, 60 mm, merrowed edge. Satin stitch wants flat panels bounded by hard edges, which is precisely what flat shading produces. Four to five thread colours, one per value step.
CERAMIC COASTER / TILE SET, 100 mm square, four designs. Flat colour and hard edges are what ceramic decals do best; a gradient would band.

MOTION: a slow 6 fps STEPPED orbit around a single faceted bulb, 48 steps, no motion blur, no easing. The facets flip value one at a time as the key crosses each edge — the whole animation is twenty-eight surfaces taking turns. 1080 x 1080, silent, seamless.
NOT a large-format photoreal-substitute hero. This is a graphic system, not a picture of a vehicle, and scaling it to a two-metre wall piece would just be big flat shapes.
concept.why_not_derivative: THIS CONTRADICTS THE ENTIRE PREMISE OF THE PROJECT AND I AM PROPOSING IT ANYWAY. Seventy-five revisions were spent chasing photorealism; this throws it away at the one scale where photorealism is losing, and says so out loud. A cautious team rejects it in the first meeting — 'it looks unfinished', 'it looks like a 1993 render', 'we paid for a photoreal model'. All three are true and none is an objection. The VW-bus category has exactly two poles, photoreal and flat-vector; a hard-shaded faceted CAD object is neither, reads as machined prototype or early-CGI or Memphis-era product render, and there is nothing remotely like it on that shelf. It is also structurally impossible to mistake for a photograph of a VW bus, because there is no bus in frame and no photography in the treatment. AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE OF THE THREE THAT IS IMMUNE TO EVERY OPEN DEFECT AT ONCE: the salmon red becomes a chosen ink; the gloss deficit is irrelevant because there is no specular; the emblem's arrangement becomes a design decision instead of a nine-times-rejected fidelity failure; the mottle and the denoiser boil vanish under flat shading.
concept.production_notes:
THE FACETING IS ALREADY IN THE MESH — THIS COSTS ALMOST NOTHING AND THAT IS THE POINT. `_ball(..., nu=7, nv=4)` gives the bulb twenty-eight quads. `T.rrect(TB_CHORD, TB_WIDTH, 0.012, seg=4)` gives the tail board four-segment corners. The cap ring is `seg=96`. The tail-board edge prisms are `seg=3` and `seg=4`. The tyre is `TREAD_SEG * TREAD_LUGS` = 384. Every one of those numbers is a design asset the moment you stop hiding it.

TURN OFF `shade_smooth` AND TURN OFF THE OPTICS. `T1_FX=0`, and pass post.py `--backdrop white` explicitly — its live constant is `BACKDROP = "headroom"` at peak 252, which would put a grey field inside a white margin. Bloom, CA, vignette and grain all actively fight a hard-edge flat image.

DO NOT USE `clay_all()` OR ANY MATERIAL OVERRIDE. It clears every material slot and throws away the artwork that IS this vehicle's identity, leaving a grey van. The faceting must come from NORMALS, not from materials: flat-shade and keep the diffuse colour.

PALETTE MUST BE DECLARED, NOT EYEDROPPERED. I looked at the render's rear hubcap at 6x: the dome is salmon-pink with a hard plastic crescent highlight, where ref_side.jpg's is oxblood with a soft sweep. This concept does not need the render's red to be right — it chooses its ink — but nobody may sample it off a frame. Reconcile the three authored reds into one and write down which: t1_mats `RED = (0.5520, 0.0294, 0.0176)` = sRGB(196,49,36); lid_gen `RED = (159, 45, 22)`; cal_gen `RED = (214, 46, 30)`.

Riso spot inks: specify by ink name, not by CMYK build. Fluorescent orange under the brass gives the nosing a glow no process build can reach.
model_work_required: THE SAME MACRO CAMERA CLASS AS 'AS MEASURED' — 100-200 mm lens at 0.15-0.5 m — but at f/22 with everything sharp. Nothing here is croppable from existing frames: at the side render's ~272 px/m a 22.0 mm bulb is 6 px. `studio.views()` has no macro entry; `detail_f` stands at ~3.5 m.

FLAT SHADING SWITCH. The shell is `shade_smooth` and the whole concept depends on turning that off without touching topology. One switch, applied at the object level, with a watched kill — render the bulb smooth and flat and put the crops side by side before believing it.

KEEP THE LOW SEGMENT COUNTS. This is the one item that is a DECISION rather than a task, and it is the opposite of what CONCEPT 2 needs: `nu=7, nv=4` on the bulb and `seg=4` on the tail-board corners must be PRESERVED for the macro build. If a future revision raises them for photoreal reasons, this concept quietly dies. Record it, or add a `T1_MACRO_FACET` build that pins them.

NO PASS INFRASTRUCTURE EXISTS, AND THE ENAMEL / RISO / EMBROIDERY TIERS NEED IT. `grep pass_index|use_pass` returns nothing outside studio.py's denoiser config — no ID pass, no normal pass, no AO pass, no cryptomatte. For the POSTER tier this is not required (Blender can render the flats directly). For anything that needs per-facet flat regions as vector — the pin, the patch, the Riso separations — a material/object ID pass is the shortest route and is a contained build.

NOTHING ELSE. NO FIDELITY WORK AT ALL. This concept requires no emblem fix, no red correction, no gloss work, no tread measurement, no bulb filament, and no resolution proving run beyond a 500 x 700 mm sheet at 300 dpi (5906 x 8268 px — above the proven 3840, so ONE stitch run must be exercised and its exit code read). It is the only one of the three that could ship while every open finding in the register stays open, and it is the reason to consider it despite the risk.

concept.title: EL COMBI — La Lotería
concept.one_line: A 24-card lotería deck in which every card is an engraving of one part of this one vehicle — the game of archetypes played with a taco truck's components.
concept.the_image:
Pure black line on warm cream uncoated stock. No tone, no colour, no shading — a 19th-century trade-catalogue engraving crossed with a Mexican broadside. Card face 60 × 100 mm: a single object, centred, floating in cream, inside a 2 mm black rule with a 1 mm inner hairline; a number top-left in a slab face; the Spanish name in caps along the foot in hand-drawn condensed grotesque, English small beneath.

THE LINE SYSTEM, which is the whole idea: silhouette 0.5 mm, creases 0.3 mm, hatching 0.12–0.18 mm. No flat black mass wider than ~3 mm anywhere. Value comes ONLY from hatch density — four densities at roughly 8 / 4 / 2 / 1 lines per mm. And the hatch direction FOLLOWS THE SURFACE: it runs longitudinally along the flank, wraps circumferentially round the tyre, radiates from the pole of the hubcap dome, and cross-hatches only in true occlusion — under the counter, inside the wheel arches, behind the apertures. That is the difference between an engraving and a Photoshop filter, and it requires a normal pass, which is to say it requires the model.

THE DECK, 24 cards: 1 El Combi (the whole vehicle, lid propped, counter out — the full asymmetric 4.580 × 3.132 m propped silhouette, 1.462:1). 2 La Ventana (one serving aperture, 515.5 × 403.0 mm with its 55 mm corner radius, bobble fringe running the whole inner edge). 3 El Mostrador (the counter's radiused tail and brass nosing). 4 La Rueda (the hubcap bullseye: 274.0 mm cap, 86.9 mm badge). 5 El Farol (one festoon bulb on its flex). 6 La Plancha. 7 El Tablero (the mural lid, propped). 8 La Flor (one mural rosette, ten lobes, peace-glyph centre — carry it, don't sanitise it). 9 La Calidad (the sunburst, type at −19.7°). 10 El Sol. 11 El Espejo. 12 La Bocina. 13 El Sesenta y Tres (the empty chrome plate frame). 14 La Rejilla (the louvre block, ten slots at 21.111 mm pitch). 15 La Cinta (the bulb string alone, a single continuous line running edge to edge off both sides of the card). 16 El Toldo (the tail board on its stay, 0.7110 m chord at 38.0°). 17 La Carta (a menu card). 18 La Cortina (the bobble fringe alone, a scalloped run, nothing else). 19 El Faro. 20 El Pico (the nose blade and its two irons — CROPPED BELOW THE ROUNDEL). 21 El Vaso. 22 La Llave. 23 La Sombra (the cast shadow alone: a card that is only the shape the bus makes on the ground). 24 La Combi Cerrada — the same vehicle SHUT, which is a picture this project has never rendered in 76 revisions.
concept.emotional_claim: The absurd dignity of giving a taco truck's parts the treatment normally reserved for the moon, the mermaid and death. A child gets a game and asks what La Cortina is. An adult gets the joke — this is a deck of archetypes with no archetypes in it — and then, a beat later, gets the affection underneath it: somebody decided every one of these things. Somebody chose the fringe. The engraving register does the second half of the work; engraving is how we draw objects we have decided are important, so drawing a bulb holder that way is a small act of love performed with a straight face. And it is unambiguously a thing families keep, without being a sticker.
formats: Deck of 24 cards, 60 × 100 mm, 3 mm die-cut corner radius, 300 gsm uncoated CREAM board (not white — a warm 5–8% ground is what makes a line engraving read as a broadside rather than as clip art). Single black ink, offset or letterpress. Tuck box carrying the folk-art repeat in the same one ink.
Six tablas (playing boards), 210 × 297 mm, 4 × 4 grid of 16 cards each, same stock — the deck only becomes a GAME when the boards exist, and the boards are where a family sits down.

Individual cards blown up as A3 prints, 297 × 420 mm. The line is vector so it survives, but each size needs its own hatch pass — see production notes. La Sombra and La Cinta are the two that become genuinely strange at this scale.
Kiss-cut sticker sheet, all 24 at 25 mm, A5. At 25 mm the hatching is gone and each card reduces to silhouette plus creases — draw that reduction, do not scale to it.
Card backs and the tuck box as a one-ink folk-art repeat, built from the three components that carry 84.4% of the gold.
Restaurant application: the 24 cards printed as a single 700 × 1000 mm uncut sheet, framed. It is a specimen sheet, and it is the cheapest wall piece in this whole programme.
concept.why_not_derivative:
The VW-bus merch ocean is photographic, painterly, or minimal single-weight line art. Nobody engraves a bus, for a concrete reason: you cannot hatch a photograph convincingly, because convincing hatching has to follow the form, and following the form requires having the form. This is the one treatment that is only available to someone who spent 75 revisions building the geometry — it is the strongest possible argument for the model existing at all.

And 'a lotería deck made entirely out of one object's parts' exists nowhere, in any category. It is a deliberate category error: lotería is universal archetypes, and this deck refuses to have any. That is the joke and it is also the brand's actual position — this is not a bus that means freedom, it is a specific parked object with a fringe on it.

Trademark surface is near zero: El Pico crops below the bumper line, no card carries the roundel, and the hubcap card can be drawn as the ring geometry alone (STATE.md notes the badge's width fraction 'has never been compared to a frame', so drawing it from the model at card scale would be publishing an unverified proportion).
concept.production_notes:
DELIVER VECTOR, NOT RASTER. At 0.12 mm a rasterised hatch will stair-step on the plate. Grease Pencil Line Art is the only route in this tree to editable strokes and therefore to SVG.

SET HATCH DENSITY IN FINAL MILLIMETRES PER SIZE AND NEVER SCALE BETWEEN SIZES. A 0.12 mm line scaled from A3 to a 60 mm card becomes 0.024 mm and disappears; scaled the other way it becomes a fat rule. Each of the four output sizes needs its own hatch pass. This is the single most likely way this concept fails silently.

Line floors: 0.12 mm for offset, 0.18 mm for letterpress (the bite closes finer lines). Cream stock, warm not neutral. Black only — a second ink would undo the entire premise.

This is a DIFFERENT ARTEFACT from F18 and must be offered as one. F18's style is locked to 'cartoon with rendered depth' and its scene to 'nothing but the bus, die-cut tight, plus the sun and the papel picado', and its trigger — 'build it after the model is done' — has not fired. This deck is neither that style nor that scene, so it is not gated by that trigger; say so in the proposal rather than letting the hold read as blocking it. Do not raise the papel picado question: he ruled it deferred until the sticker is actually being built.

THIS IS THE RISKY ONE AND I WILL SAY SO. A cautious team rejects it three ways: it is a game rather than a poster, so it does not look like merch; engraving looks nothing like any food brand's identity; and it is 24 finished illustrations before a single unit ships. I am proposing it anyway, because it is the only idea here that turns the project's real asset — 229 individually named, individually measured objects — into content, and because it is the only one a family would still have in a drawer in ten years.
model_work_required: A LINE-EXTRACTION PASS. There is none: `grep -rln "freestyle|grease|gpencil|use_pass_|pass_index|cryptomatte" --include=*.py .` returns one unrelated probe. Build the Grease Pencil Line Art modifier route in preference to Freestyle — it emits EDITABLE VECTOR STROKES and is the only path in this tree to SVG. Crease angle 30–40°, NOT lower: `T1_body` is shade-smooth and a low angle will find the subdivision instead of the form.

A NORMAL PASS and an AO/occlusion pass, to drive hatch DIRECTION and hatch DENSITY respectively. Copy `matte_tap`'s colour contract verbatim — `color_management='OVERRIDE'`, `view_transform='Raw'`, look 'None', gamma 1.0 — or every pass comes back AgX-curved and the density mapping is wrong everywhere. Note `probe_rev55_truenorm.py` already establishes that `Normal` collapses on the smooth-shaded shell and `True Normal` is the fix; use True Normal.

PER-OBJECT ISOLATION RENDERS for 23 of the 24 cards. This is a visibility loop, not modelling — the objects are already separately named in STATE.md's inventory (`fringe | 3`, `menucard | 3`, `plate` + `plate_digits`, `louvres | 2`, `bulb_string`, `mir_head | 2`, `counter_nosing`, `cap`/`capring`/`capvw`, `tail_board` + `tail_board_stay`, `plancha`).

THE SHUT VEHICLE, for card 24, and this is real source work rather than a render. `t1_shell.py` couples the lid's width to its angle: `LID_W = (LID_X0 - LID_X1) / LID_ASPECT / math.sin(math.radians(LID_OPEN_DEG))`. I computed the sweep from the live constants (LID_X0 0.9640, LID_X1 −1.0700, LID_ASPECT 1.7130): 76° → 1.2237 m (shipped), 45° → 1.6792, 30° → 2.3748, 10° → 6.8379, and 0° is a ZeroDivisionError. A naive angle sweep INFLATES the mural board to longer than the bus. Freeze LID_W at its shipped value behind an ablation, guard it, and WATCH THE GUARD FAIL on the coupled build before believing it green. The near-closed case will also trip `assert _top.co.y > LID_Y_HINGE + 0.010`, which is correct for a posed still and wrong for a swept one.

NOT REQUIRED, and this is the concept's biggest practical advantage: no T1_ALPHA, no materials, no lighting rig, no colour management downstream, no large-format stitch, no 16-bit path, no emblem fix, no gloss work, no red decision. It is the only one of the three that ships without unblocking anything else in the pipeline.

verdicts.lens: ORIGINALITY — is this genuinely fresh, or a well-executed version of something already on a thousand products?
verdicts.reasoning:
The concept asserts "'a lotería deck made entirely out of one object's parts' exists nowhere, in any category." The first half of that is false and the second half is broken by its own card list.

WHAT IT RESEMBLES, NAMED.
(1) THE FORMAT. Custom/themed lotería is one of the most re-skinned containers in graphic design and it is saturated in precisely the adjacent market — Mexican food brands. Etsy carries at least five distinct standing market pages for it (etsy.com/market/loteria_cards_custom, /customize_loteria_cards, /loteria_custom_cards, /custom_loteria, /loteria_card_design). Worse for the originality claim: "design your own lotería card on a subject of personal meaning" is a HIGH-SCHOOL ART ASSIGNMENT, with published lesson plans (lundgrenart.weebly.com/loteria-card-project.html) specifying the vertical format, the number, and the Spanish word over English word — which is this concept's card layout, exactly. Substituting your own subjects into lotería is not a transgression of the form; it IS the form's entire commercial and pedagogical life. The concept's central defence — "a deliberate category error… lotería is universal archetypes and this deck refuses to have any" — describes a move the format absorbs a thousand times a year.
(2) THE REGISTER. Engraved/crosshatch vehicle illustration is a mature commercial genre with named practitioners (Steven Noble: line art, scratchboard, woodcut, engraving) and a settled technique literature (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scratchboard). Combined with the "VW bus blueprint/patent print" category the grounded reality already flagged as a standing Dreamstime and Etsy line, the technical-drawing-of-a-VW-bus space is occupied.
(3) THE STRUCTURE. "One object decomposed into its parts as a card set" is itself a genre: exploded-view drawing (a documented category), taxonomy posters sold as a product line (Pop & Pac Studio, behance.net/gallery/82289603), and knolling/flat-lay.

So this sits at the intersection of three worn genres. Combination freshness is real, and I do not want to underrate it — the intersection is genuinely unoccupied and I could not find it. But an intersection of three saturated genres is not the same as a new idea, and this one has a specific structural weakness a critic will find in ten seconds.

THE CONCEIT IS BROKEN BY ITS OWN DECK, AT EXACTLY THE PLACES A CRITIC LOOKS. The thesis is "a deck of archetypes with no archetypes in it." Card 10 is EL SOL — the single most-reproduced lotería card in existence. El Vaso, La Llave and El Espejo are archetype-shaped too. Four of 24 cards (17%) are not measured parts of this vehicle, and the deck's unique claim is precisely that all of them are. Verified against the machine: STATE.md's object inventory has no speaker object at all, and F309 RETIRED the roof loudspeakers as "removable event gear," a POSE, not vehicle geometry — so LA BOCINA (card 12) is a card of a thing the register says is not on the bus, listed in a production note that claims 23 of 24 cards are isolation renders of "objects already separately named in STATE.md's inventory." El Sol also collides head-on with the project's own art direction: AUDIT_rev43.md, sticker sev-4, "THE SUN — it must NOT be a rayed disc. The vehicle already carries ELEVEN radial bursts." Four cards reached for evocative Spanish nouns instead of the object, and every one of them is a slide back toward the generic lotería the concept claims to refuse.

THE FRESHEST THING IN IT IS INVISIBLE. The load-bearing originality argument — hatching must follow the surface, following the surface requires normals, therefore only someone who built the geometry can do this — is TRUE, and I verified the enabling gap (grep for freestyle/grease/gpencil/line_art across all .py returns nothing; there is no line pass in this tree). But it is a derivation story, not a perceptual one. A viewer holding the card cannot tell a normals-driven hatch from a skilled illustrator's, and skilled illustrators have been hatching cars along their form since the 1930s parts catalogues. Originality that lives in the pipeline and not in the artefact is a production anecdote.

WHAT GENUINELY EARNS ITS SCORE. Three cards are inventions I have not seen anywhere: LA CORTINA (a bobble fringe alone, as a subject), LA SOMBRA (only the shape the bus makes on the ground), and LA COMBI CERRADA (an image this project has never made in 76 revisions, and which the concept's own notes show requires real source work because LID_W is coupled to LID_OPEN_DEG and hits ZeroDivisionError at 0°). Those three are each better than most whole concepts. The cultural placement is right — combi+lotería without costume-Mexican. And the trademark reasoning (crop El Pico below the roundel; no card carries the mark; the hubcap badge's width fraction is unverified per STATE.md so do not publish it) is unusually disciplined.

STRONG, NOT EXCEPTIONAL. Three real inventions and a true structural argument, wrapped in the most re-skinned container in Mexican graphic design, defended by an "exists nowhere" claim that is false, and undercut by four of its own cards.
fatal_flaws: THE ORIGINALITY CLAIM IS FALSE AS WRITTEN. 'A loteria deck made entirely out of one object's parts exists nowhere, in any category' — custom/themed loteria is a saturated Etsy category (five standing market pages) AND a published high-school art assignment whose brief specifies this exact layout: vertical card, number, Spanish word, English beneath. Re-skinning loteria with your own subjects is the format's convention, not a violation of it. Any proposal built on this sentence will be embarrassed by a five-minute search.

THE DECK CHEATS ITS OWN CONCEIT AT 4 OF 24 CARDS, AND EVERY CHEAT IS TOWARD THE GENERIC. El Sol (card 10) is the most-reproduced loteria card that exists; El Vaso, La Llave and El Espejo are archetype-shaped. The thesis is 'no archetypes in it.' The single sharpest idea in the concept is contradicted by 17% of its own contents.

LA BOCINA (card 12) IS NOT A PART OF THIS VEHICLE AND THE REGISTER SAYS SO. F309 retired the roof loudspeakers as 'removable event gear… a POSE, not vehicle geometry'; STATE.md's object inventory contains no speaker object. The production note claims 23 of 24 cards are isolation renders of objects 'already separately named in STATE.md's inventory' — that is not true for this card, nor for El Sol or El Vaso. Building it repeats F309's exact named mistake.

EL SOL COLLIDES WITH THE PROJECT'S OWN ART DIRECTION. AUDIT_rev43.md, sticker sev-4: 'THE SUN — it must NOT be a rayed disc. The vehicle already carries ELEVEN radial bursts, and it is the drawing's only light source.' The concept quotes AUDIT_rev43 elsewhere but ships a sun card without addressing it.

THE DIFFERENTIATOR IS INVISIBLE IN THE ARTEFACT. 'Hatching that follows the normal requires normals' is true and verified (no line-extraction pass exists in this tree), but no viewer can perceive the difference between a normals-driven hatch and a good illustrator's. As printed, the deck's originality rests on the loteria conceit — the half that is weakest — while the half that is strongest never reaches the eye.

THE GAME MATH DOES NOT WORK, WHICH IS WHERE THEMED DECKS DIE. Standard loteria is 54 cards against boards of 16. Six 4x4 tablas drawn from 24 cards collide so heavily the game plays badly. 'Not quite a game' is the failure mode of every themed loteria on Etsy, and the concept proposes exactly that.
improvements: PURGE THE FOUR ARCHETYPES AND MAKE THE CONCEIT AIRTIGHT — this is the single highest-value change and it costs nothing but a card list. Cut El Sol, El Vaso and La Bocina outright. KEEP La Llave but redefine it as `gal_warmer_tap` (llave IS a tap in Mexican Spanish) — that one move converts a generic archetype into a specific measured part while keeping the pun, and it is the model of what every card should do. Replace the other three from objects I verified in STATE.md's live inventory: `gutter` (LA CANAL — the drip rail, i.e. the thing the bulb string runs on), `fuel_flap` (LA TAPA), `roof_vent` (EL RESPIRADERO), `englid_handle`, `hinge_barrel` (EL GOZNE), `speedo_face` (EL VELOCIMETRO), `wheelhouse`, `seat_welt`, `pedal_a/b/c`. Then the sentence 'there is not one archetype in this deck' becomes literally true and checkable, which is the only version of the claim worth making.

PUT THE DERIVATION ON THE CARD FACE, WHERE A VIEWER CAN SEE IT. Add a footer line per card carrying a REAL measured dimension out of STATE.md: 'LA VENTANA · 515.5 x 403.0 mm · r 55' or 'LA RUEDA · CAP 274.0 mm · BADGE 86.9 mm'. No VW-bus print on Etsy can write that sentence truthfully, because nobody else measured the object. It converts 76 revisions of measurement from an invisible production fact into the visible thing that separates this deck from a patent print — and it costs one line of type. CEILING: check each figure against STATE.md before setting it, and do NOT print the hubcap badge's width fraction, which STATE.md flags as 'SELF-CONSISTENCY ONLY — never compared to a frame.'

DRAW AT LEAST TWO CARDS A PHOTOGRAPH PHYSICALLY COULD NOT PRODUCE. The normals argument only earns its keep if the artefact proves it. Concretely: (a) make LA VENTANA hatch THROUGH the aperture onto the galley behind it — a photograph has no data in that volume, the model has ~30 named gal_* objects; (b) add one SECTION CUT card, the vehicle sliced at a stated station, hatched on the cut face in the engraving convention. A section is the one image class that is impossible from reference and trivial from geometry. That is the deck's proof of origin, and right now it has none.

SIGN THE CATEGORY ERROR INSTEAD OF LEAVING IT UNSTATED. Card 1 in the Don Clemente deck is El Gallo. Make card 1 EL COMBI and say so on the tuck box in one line — 'this deck has 24 cards and not one of them is an archetype.' Unstated transgressions read as ignorance of the form; stated ones read as authorship. This is the cheapest tier-raising edit available.

RESOLVE THE GAME MATH: either go to 54 cards or stop calling it a game. The inventory supports 54 — STATE.md lists 229 named mesh objects — and at 54 the tablas work, the deck reads as a real loteria rather than a souvenir set, and the 'every part of one object' conceit gets MORE impressive with scale, not less. If 54 is too much illustration, drop the tablas entirely and reposition as a SPECIMEN SET of 24, which is a stronger and more honest object than a game that plays badly. Do not ship the current middle.

PROMOTE LA COMBI CERRADA FROM CARD 24 TO THE BOX. It is the only image in the proposal that does not exist anywhere in the world, including in this repository. It is also, by the concept's own production notes, the riskiest — LID_W is coupled to LID_OPEN_DEG in t1_shell.py and a naive sweep inflates the mural board past the length of the bus, with 0 degrees a ZeroDivisionError. Decide it early: if the shut vehicle ships, it is the deck's cover and its headline; if it does not, the deck loses its best originality claim and the pitch must be rewritten. Do not leave it as the last card in the list.

DIFFERENTIATE FROM SCRATCHBOARD ON PURPOSE, NOT BY ACCIDENT. The nearest register-competitor is scratchboard/woodcut automotive illustration, which is white-on-black and tonal. Commit hard the other way: black-on-cream, no flat mass over ~3mm (already specified — good), and add one rule that scratchboard structurally cannot follow — a strict FOUR-DENSITY quantised hatch with no blending between densities, stated on the colophon card. A visible, nameable, countable rule system is what separates an engraving-STYLE product from an engraved one, and it is the kind of constraint that survives being described in a sentence.

verdicts.lens: Producibility and fidelity: can this be made from THIS asset, given failing gates, unbuilt geometry, an unproven large-format chain, and an emblem rejected nine times — and what unscoped model work does it actually need?
verdicts.reasoning:
I tested the pipeline rather than reasoning about it, and the result cuts both ways.

THE GOOD NEWS IS BIGGER THAN THE CONCEPT CLAIMS, AND I WATCHED IT PRINT. The concept lists the line-extraction route as major unscoped work. It is not. In this container, `python3` reports `blender 4.5.3 LTS`; `LINEART` is a live modifier identifier; `bpy.ops.wm.grease_pencil_export_svg` exists. I built a scene, added `bpy.ops.object.grease_pencil_add(type='LINEART_SCENE')`, and read the evaluated depsgraph: `LINEART POINTS: 518 CURVES: 100`, then exported — `SVG OP: {'FINISHED'}`, `svg: True 112267`, `path elements: 100`. Headless, no window, ~10 lines. The concept's own grep is right that nothing in the tree uses it (`grep -rln "freestyle\|grease\|gpencil\|line_art" --include=*.py .` returns nothing), but the route is a one-liner, not a build. That is a genuine de-risking no document in this project knows about.

THE FATAL GAP IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE CONCEPT FLAGS. Line Art emits contours, creases and silhouettes. It does not hatch. The concept's entire visual premise — "value comes ONLY from hatch density", four densities at 8/4/2/1 lines per mm, direction following the surface, longitudinal on the flank, circumferential on the tyre, radial from the hubcap pole — has **no tool, and is not in the scoped work at all**. The concept lists "a normal pass and an AO pass" as if that were the deliverable. Those are rasters. Turning a raster normal+AO field into *vector* strokes at 0.12 mm, streamlined along surface flow, quantised to four densities, is a bespoke engraving engine, and it is the whole artefact. Line Art gets you the outline; the engine is what makes it an engraving rather than a colouring book. That is the single largest piece of unscoped software here and the proposal does not name it.

THE LID_W ANALYSIS IS EXACTLY RIGHT AND STILL UNDERSTATES THE BREAK. I recomputed from the live constants (`LID_X0, LID_X1 = 0.9640, -1.0700`, `LID_ASPECT = 1.7130`): 76°→1.2237, 45°→1.6792, 30°→2.3748, 10°→6.8379. Every figure matches. But the concept names the wrong failure: it predicts `assert _top.co.y > LID_Y_HINGE + 0.010` in `tail_board`. The *first* failure is `assert LID_W <= _LID_W_MAX + 1e-9` at **module scope** in `t1_shell.py`, so `import t1_shell` raises before anything runs — rule 51's class, taking every probe that imports it down with a traceback. And the source states the admissible range itself: "the roof's own width, 68.9-90 deg." Card 24 can close from 76° to about 69° and no further. "La Combi Cerrada" is a re-derivation of a measured constant, not an ablation.

TEN OF TWENTY-FOUR CARDS HAVE A CONCRETE PRODUCTION PROBLEM. Checked against STATE.md's inventory and the register: **12 La Bocina** has no geometry and F309 *retired* the roof loudspeakers as removable event gear — drawing it re-adds what a live finding removed. **21 El Vaso** has no object (no vaso/cup/taza anywhere in the inventory). **5 El Farol** wants one bulb, but `t1_detail.py:3597` reads `ob = join([ob, flex], "bulb_string")` — it is one merged object. **8 La Flor** and **9 La Calidad** are texture-only (no mesh to extract, so the concept's "engraving needs normals" argument does not apply to them), and both carry open defects — F74(a) `lidmural.png` "cropped at the bottom", F16 the pink star "built BELOW the burst where both red frames put it above". **14 La Rejilla** cites ten slots; `LOUV_N = 10` is live but AUDIT_rev43 reads "louvre block has twelve slots, not ten, and the built block is two slots short" — a card of nothing but louvres is the one place a customer can count. **16 El Toldo** prints "0.7110 m chord", which F245 says is one of three irreconcilable values — "two-height closure 0.710, calibrated chord read 0.790, F165 0.829 ... One of them is wrong and nothing in this tree resolves it. Do not average them." **23 La Sombra** has no Line Art route at all (a shadow is not geometry) and needs the shadow layer, i.e. T1_ALPHA — which flatly contradicts the concept's own "NOT REQUIRED: no T1_ALPHA".

Its angle, at least, is safe: the concept draws 38.0°, and F242 refutes F165's 28.0° — "The shipped 38.0 matches the primary frame to 0.8°".

WHY IT STILL CLEARS "WORKABLE". The dependency argument is correct and it is the strongest producibility case in the programme: one ink, no materials, no lighting rig, no colour management, no 16-bit path, no stitch chain, no emblem, no gloss, no red decision. `El Pico` cropping below the roundel keeps the nine-times-rejected mark off every card. It is the only concept that ships without first unblocking something the owner has held. And its technical claims verify under test, which on this project is rare.
fatal_flaws: THE HATCHING ENGINE DOES NOT EXIST AND IS NOT SCOPED. Line Art emits contours and creases only — I confirmed it produces curves, not fills or hatches. The concept's entire visual identity (four densities at 8/4/2/1 lines per mm, direction following the surface) requires a bespoke raster-normal-to-vector-stroke generator that no document mentions and no line of the proposal budgets. Without it the deck is outline art, which is trope (e) in the grounded market survey — 'minimalist line drawing style' — i.e. the concept collapses into the exact derivative category its own 'why_not_derivative' section claims to escape.

CARD 12 LA BOCINA HAS NO GEOMETRY AND CONTRADICTS A LIVE RETIREMENT. No speaker object exists in STATE.md's 229-object inventory; the only 'loudspeaker' string in any .py is deliver.py's stale README. F309 retired them: 'REMOVABLE EVENT GEAR', with 'two independent scenes show the roof BARE'. Drawing the card re-introduces as a brand archetype the one thing the record deliberately removed.

CARD 24 LA COMBI CERRADA BREAKS AT MODULE IMPORT, NOT AT BUILD. `assert LID_W <= _LID_W_MAX + 1e-9` is at module scope in t1_shell.py, so a reduced T1_LIDDEG raises AssertionError on `import t1_shell` — killing every probe that imports it, with no summary line (rule 51). The source's own admissible range is '68.9-90 deg', so the vehicle cannot be closed past ~69° without re-deriving a measured constant. The 'picture never rendered in 76 revisions' is unrenderable as specified.

CARD 23 LA SOMBRA CONTRADICTS THE CONCEPT'S OWN DEPENDENCY CLAIM. A cast shadow is not geometry, so Line Art cannot trace it. It needs deliver.py's shadow_only layer, which needs T1_ALPHA — thirteen revisions un-run (no LEDGER contains the string), and every frame in out/ is colortype 2 with no alpha. The proposal's headline producibility argument, 'no T1_ALPHA', is false for at least one card.

CARD 21 EL VASO HAS NO OBJECT. Nothing cup-like exists in the inventory — gal_sqbottle, gal_can_u, gal_can_l, gal_bot and gal_tube are bottles, cans and tubes. The card would have to be invented, which is fine for El Sol but not for a deck whose premise is that every card is a measured part of this one vehicle.
improvements: SHIP THE HATCH ENGINE AS CARD ZERO, BEFORE DRAWING ANY OF THE 24. Make one card end-to-end and look at it. Concretely: render True Normal (probe_rev55_truenorm.py already establishes 'Normal collapses on the smooth-shaded shell and True Normal is the fix' — reuse its arm, do not re-derive) plus an AO pass, both through matte_tap's colour contract verbatim (color_management='OVERRIDE', view_transform='Raw', look None, gamma 1.0) or every density maps wrong. Then write hatch_gen.py: project the normal field to screen, streamline it, and quantise spacing to four bands from AO. VALIDATE ON A KNOWN ANSWER FIRST, which is this project's own proven method ('Prove the proxy on a known answer, then use it'): a sphere must hatch concentric at the pole and parallel at the limb, and a flat plane must hatch dead straight. If it cannot do the sphere it cannot do the hubcap. Budget this as the revision, not as a note.

REPLACE THE THREE DEAD CARDS WITH BUILT OBJECTS, ALL OF WHICH ARE BETTER SUBJECTS. La Bocina (no geometry, F309-retired) -> EL VOLANTE, the steering wheel: wheel_rim + wheel_hub + wheel_horn + wheel_spoke|2, fully built, and a wheel is a real loteria form. El Vaso (no object) -> EL RELOJ, the instrument: speedo_bezel + speedo_face + speedo_glass, built, and a dial is the most engravable object on the vehicle. If a third is wanted, LA TAPA (fuel_flap|1) or EL PEDAL (pedal_a/b/c). All four are single named objects already isolable by visibility.

STOP PRINTING DIMENSIONS THE RECORD CANNOT DEFEND. Drop '0.7110 m chord' from El Toldo entirely — F245 leaves three irreconcilable values (0.710 / 0.790 / 0.829, an 11 % spread) with an explicit instruction not to average them. Drop the badge diameter from La Rueda: STATE.md says 'hubcap badge is SELF-CONSISTENCY ONLY -- CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC has never been compared to a frame'. Drop '515.5 mm' from La Ventana: the three bays measure 0.516 / 0.515 / 0.516 and are not one number. And check El Combi's '4.580 x 3.132' — 4.580 is STATE's row flagged '+525.0 mm OUT', which is the propped tail board projecting aft, not the vehicle. A deck is the first artefact in this project's history that publishes measured figures to a customer; every number on a card needs the same grade as a verifier row, or no number at all.

COUNT THE LOUVRES BEFORE DRAWING THEM, OR CROP SO THEY CANNOT BE COUNTED. LOUV_N = 10 is live in t1_detail.py; AUDIT_rev43 reads 'twelve slots, not ten, and the built block is two slots short'. La Rejilla is a card whose entire content is an enumerable rhythm, so it converts an unresolved two-slot discrepancy into a checkable printed claim. Either resolve it off ref_side.jpg (620,440)-(1000,620) with the window painted first, or crop the card to a partial run that reads as texture rather than as a count.

RE-SPECIFY CARD 24 AS A DERIVATION, AND GUARD IT. Do not sweep T1_LIDDEG. Add T1_LIDW_FREEZE that pins LID_W at its shipped 1.2237 and bypasses the module-level bound assert, WATCH THE ASSERT FAIL on the coupled build at 45 degrees before believing the frozen one green (rule 3), and state in the card's own provenance that the shut lid's width is the propped width held constant, not a measurement of a shut lid — because nothing we hold shows this vehicle shut with its roof intact. Alternatively, and more honestly, retitle the card LA COMBI EN REPOSO and draw it at the 69-76 degree range the source admits.

GENERATE LA SOMBRA GEOMETRICALLY, NOT PHOTOMETRICALLY. Project the mesh silhouette along the key light vector onto z=0 and take that outline as a curve — it needs no alpha, no render, and no T1_ALPHA, and it keeps the concept's 'no unblocking required' claim true. If instead you use deliver.py's shadow_only layer, say plainly in the proposal that the deck depends on a switch nobody has run since rev 62, and run it first.

BUILD ONCE, ISOLATE 23 TIMES. build.py already carries an undocumented `if os.environ.get("T1_SAVE"): bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(...)` — the only geometry persistence in the repo, and named in no handoff document. Save one .blend at T1_SUB=2, then run all per-card isolations from that file. This turns 23 builds into 23 visibility passes, keeps the tree frozen (no source edits while a queue runs), and incidentally gives the project the export path the grounded reality says it lacks.

MEASURE LINE ART'S OUTPUT ON THE REAL MESH BEFORE COMMITTING TO VECTOR DELIVERY. Suzanne (~500 faces) gave 100 curves / 518 points / 112 KB of SVG. The combi is 366,490 faces with 5,186 ngons at SUB=2 and a shade-smooth T1_body. Run one Line Art pass at SUB=1 on the whole vehicle, print the curve and point counts, and look at the SVG at card scale — if it emits tens of thousands of paths, El Combi is unprintable as vector and the crease angle, the ngons and the subdivision level all need settling first. The concept's 30-40 degree crease guess is untested; sweep it and look, do not assume it.

SET AND STATE THE PHYSICAL SCALE, WHICH THE ONLY PRIOR SPEC LOST. AUDIT_rev43's sticker millimetres are unusable because the scale they were projected through did not survive truncation — its own ceiling says 'every millimetre figure above is a PROJECTION from a measured metre through a stated scale'. Do not repeat that. Print the scale on each card's spec sheet (60 mm card / 4.065 m vehicle = 1:67.75 for the side elevation), and hold the concept's own rule that each output size gets its own hatch pass. This is the one production note in the proposal that is already correct — make it a guard, not a paragraph.

OFFER IT EXPLICITLY AS NOT-F18, WITH THE HOLD ADDRESSED IN THE SAME SENTENCE. The proposal already does this and should be firmer: F18's style is locked to 'cartoon with rendered depth' and its scene to 'nothing but the bus, die-cut tight, plus the sun and the papel picado', and its trigger 'build it after the model is done' has not fired. This deck is neither that style nor that scene, so F191/F193 do not gate it — but say so in one line rather than leaving the owner to infer it, and do not raise the papel picado (he deferred it explicitly). Note also that the F18 clause dropped between rev 39 and rev 43 — 'vector line and flat colour, shading and occlusion sampled from the 3D asset' — describes this deck's pipeline almost exactly, which is an argument for the engine being reusable for F18 later.

verdicts.lens: Emotional resonance, brand fit and IP exposure
verdicts.reasoning:
On brand fit this is the best-reasoned concept in the set. Lotería is culturally native to a brand whose own name is a portmanteau of taco + combi, founded by a Mexican in Mexico City — it is not costume-Mexican, which is the failure mode every other route walks into. And the engraved-specimen register maps unexpectedly well onto Tacombi's actual merch voice, which the market research shows is deadpan leisure-outfitter catalogue copy ("casual, convenient leisure products since 2006", "purpose-built, all-weather knit", "Monument T") rather than folk maximalism. The 700 × 1000 uncut sheet, framed, is the strongest single restaurant artefact proposed anywhere in this program. IP consciousness is genuine and deliberate rather than decorative: El Pico crops below the roundel, and the concept caught by itself that drawing the hubcap badge would publish CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC, which STATE.md says "has never been compared to a frame."

It is not exceptional because the two things my lens weights hardest each have a real hole.

First, a register collision the concept never defends. Lotería's emotional signature is saturated colour and naive folk painting — Don Clemente is riotous. This invokes the most colour-drenched form in Mexican popular graphics and delivers a Victorian trade catalogue in one black ink. That can be brilliant counterpoint, but the concept justifies monochrome only circularly ("a second ink would undo the entire premise"), and the premise is hatch-follows-normal, not monochrome. It also fights the record's own reading that gold is the connective ink tying the palette together, and that this bus belongs to bright-colours tricked-out combi culture.

Second, the joke is aimed at the wrong person. Lotería's pleasure is recognition — everyone already knows La Sirena, La Muerte, El Diablito, and the caller riffs on that shared knowledge. A deck with no archetypes deletes recognition and substitutes a puzzle legible to a designer. For families and children at a restaurant, 24 unnameable objects is friction before it is delight. The load-bearing sentence of the whole concept — "A child gets a game and asks what La Cortina is" — is asserted and never tested, and there are no dichos, no calling verses, no cantador. Lotería is a form that is SPOKEN; this ships 24 images and zero voice.

On IP the concept is mostly careful but has inverted its own risk ranking. La Combi Cerrada, promoted as the crown jewel and singled out by the screener, is the vehicle with every Tacombi-specific feature hidden: no counter, no open hatches, no propped lid, no deployed bulbs. What remains is precisely the split-screen T1 silhouette the market research identifies as the saturated surf-bus shape and as the thing VW claims as a trademark. It is simultaneously the deck's most generic image, its highest-exposure image, and — per its own verified LID_W arithmetic and the `assert _top.co.y > LID_Y_HINGE + 0.010` — its most expensive card by a wide margin.
fatal_flaws: NO CANTADOR AND NO DICHOS. Lotería is a called game; the affection and the humour live in the rhymed verses, not the pictures. The concept ships 24 images and no voice, which is why it currently reads as an art object rather than something a family plays. This is the single largest emotional gap and the cheapest to close.

THE RECOGNITION MECHANIC IS DELETED, NOT SUBVERTED. 'A lotería deck with no archetypes' is a joke that lands for a designer looking at the deck; it does not land for the family playing it, because lotería's pleasure is knowing the card before it is called. The emotional_claim asserts a child will be charmed by La Cortina; nothing tests it, and the whole concept rests on that sentence.

LA COMBI CERRADA IS THE MOST GENERIC AND MOST LEGALLY EXPOSED IMAGE IN THE PROGRAM, AND IT IS BEING SOLD AS THE HIGHLIGHT. Shut, the vehicle is a split-screen T1 in elevation — every Tacombi-specific feature (counter, open hatches, propped mural lid, bulb string) concealed. The market finding says a frame showing the counter and open hatch 'cannot be mistaken for stock' while one showing mostly the donor silhouette can. It is also the only card needing real source surgery: the verified sweep gives 76°→1.2237, 45°→1.6792, 30°→2.3748, 10°→6.8379, 0°→ZeroDivisionError, plus the near-shut case tripping `assert _top.co.y > LID_Y_HINGE + 0.010`.

LA BOCINA IS NOT PART OF THIS VEHICLE AND THE REGISTER SAYS SO EXPLICITLY. F309 retires the roof loudspeakers as geometry: 'REMOVABLE EVENT GEAR', 'BUILDING IT WOULD PLANT A POSE PERMANENTLY', identification resting on ONE frame after F143's second-frame corroboration was withdrawn. `grep -rn 'speaker' --include=*.py .` returns exactly one hit, deliver.py's stale README line. The card cannot be drawn from the model and breaks the deck's own stated rule.

THE ONE-INK RULE IS DEFENDED CIRCULARLY AND FIGHTS THE FORM IT INVOKES. 'A second ink would undo the entire premise' is false — the premise is that hatch direction follows the surface normal, which is untouched by adding a flat spot colour. Monochrome is a production preference dressed as a conceptual necessity, and it puts the deck in the opposite emotional register from the tradition it is trading on.

THE PREMISE LEAKS AND THE PREMISE IS THE ORIGINALITY CLAIM. 'Every card is an engraving of one part of this one vehicle' — but El Sol is not a part of the vehicle and La Bocina is not the vehicle. Two exceptions in 24 is enough to let a sceptic dismiss the category error as loose rather than rigorous. (El Vaso and La Llave survive: `gal_sqbottle` and `gal_warmer_tap` both exist in the inventory.)

LA RUEDA IS EMOTIONALLY GUTTED BY ITS OWN IP FIX. The hubcap's charm is the four-band bullseye — cream rim, red dome, light VW — that rhymes with the nose emblem at wheel scale. Stripping it to 'the ring geometry alone' to dodge the glyph leaves a plain circle, which is the least memorable card in a deck whose whole pitch is memorability.
improvements: WRITE THE 24 DICHOS. One Spanish couplet per card in Tacombi's deadpan catalogue voice, printed on the tabla foot or inside the tuck box, English small beneath. This converts an art object into a game, restores the cantador the form requires, and is the highest emotional return per unit of effort in the entire concept. It also gives the brand a piece of writing it can reuse in every other channel.

GIVE EVERY CARD A SECOND LINE NAMING THE ARCHETYPE IT DISPLACES — 'LA CORTINA / el adorno', 'LA SOMBRA / la muerte', 'EL FAROL / la luna'. This restores lotería's recognition pleasure without abandoning the category error; the joke becomes legible AT the table instead of only to a designer holding the deck. It is a typographic change, not a redraw.

GO TO TWO INKS: BLACK PLUS THE FOLK-ART GOLD. Use `GOLD = (0.8600, 0.5400, 0.0600)` from t1_mats.py as a flat ground plate or exactly one spot per card — never as tone. Hatch density still carries all value, so the engraving discipline and the normal-pass argument survive intact, while the deck stops reading as a museum specimen and starts reading as a lotería. Cream stock + black + gold is also the vehicle's own three-colour system.

KILL LA COMBI CERRADA. REPLACE IT WITH 'LA COMBI VERDE' — the green donor bus as bought: $3,000, missing three of its windows, only the front bench, no headlamps, bare painted rims with no hubcaps (all documented in SPEC section 0.1, graded S, and in ref_workshop.jpg). This is strictly better on all three of my axes at once: it is a Tacombi-only image no competitor can make, it carries the brand's own origin story, it has near-zero VW trademark surface because the conversion is the subject, and it needs no LID_W surgery, no lid sweep and no assert work. It also gives the deck a narrative bookend against card 1.

KILL LA BOCINA. REPLACE IT WITH 'EL SEÑOR' — the silver-leaf swash capital T alone, the wordmark's ornate ribbon sweeping back. It is built (`script_L`/`script_R`, tex/senor.png at 4096x1738), it is the brand's typographic DNA, and it puts Tacombi's own mark in the deck where the VW roundel deliberately is not. Alternatively 'LA ORILLA', the counter's brass nosing and radiused tail, which the record calls the shape that says mid-century cantina rather than food truck.

REDRAW LA RUEDA AS THE WHEEL IN ITS ARCH, NOT THE ISOLATED CAP. Include the arch lip and its measured 39.7 mm tyre gap, the circumferential tyre hatch, and the cream rim dish — keeping the concentric bullseye rhythm and the drama, while the badge sits small enough to be pure ring geometry. This removes both the VW glyph and the unverified CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC without leaving a boring card.

AUDIT ALL 24 CARDS AGAINST STATE.md's OBJECT INVENTORY BEFORE ANY DRAWING STARTS, AND PUT THE SURVIVING RULE ON THE BOX. If the claim is 'twenty-four things that are on this one bus', make it exactly true — La Bocina fails it, El Sol needs an explicit exemption as the light source. The rigour is the originality; publish the rule and honour it, because the first person who notices a card that isn't on the bus dismantles the whole conceit.

ADD A CARD CARRYING THE SPANISH SIGNAGE — 'GRACIAS POR SU PREFERENCIA', hand-lettered, from ref_nolita_doorshut.jpg. It is the single strongest anti-VW, pro-Tacombi mark available: warmth, language and hospitality in one line, and no trademark surface at all. FLAG THE CEILING IN THE PROPOSAL: that lettering belongs to the Nolita livery state, so under rule 11 it must be offered as a card about the BRAND, not presented as artwork on the target bus.

SAY IN THE PROPOSAL THAT THIS IS NOT F18 AND WHY THAT MATTERS COMMERCIALLY, NOT JUST PROCEDURALLY. The concept already notes the style and scene locks do not apply. Go further: state that a deck plus tablas is a $15-25 retail object a family takes home, where a sticker is a giveaway — so this does not compete with F18, it sits above it, and the sticker can still be built later against its own locked brief when the owner fires that trigger.

PROTOTYPE THREE CARDS BEFORE COMMITTING TO 24, AND MAKE THEM LA CORTINA, LA SOMBRA AND EL MOSTRADOR. The first two are the concept's boldest claims and the ones most likely to read as empty rather than strange; El Mostrador is the safest and proves the hatch-follows-normal pipeline on a compound curve. Print all three at final 60 x 100 mm on the actual cream stock and put them in front of a child before authorising the remaining 21 — the emotional claim is currently untested and three cards is what it costs to test it.

concept.title: No Legible
concept.one_line: A wall of everything on this vehicle that could not be read — printed at exactly the size and blur it was photographed at, with the measurement that failed set beside it — and one line, in the middle, perfectly clear.
concept.the_image: B0, portrait, edge to edge, on the measured menu-strip yellow (172,144,17) — hue 48.0, a deep ochre, not a lemon. The field is a dense justified column of near-type: fifteen or twenty specimens of the vehicle's own lettering, each reproduced at the ACTUAL pixel scale and blur at which the record read it, then enlarged with the blur intact, so what you get is a page of beautiful, hopeless, half-resolved letterforms in dark red ink (72,46,6). Reading down: the mural lid's top strip, with the palm-frond occlusion left as a 695-pixel void between JUICES, and &, and beneath it in 7 pt caps 'THE THREE LEGIBLE WORDS AVERAGE 53.6 PX PER CHARACTER. THE GAP ACCOMMODATES 13.0 +/- 0.6 CHARACTERS. GOURMET TACOS IS 13 CHARACTERS. THAT IS A CONSISTENCY, NOT A READING.' Below that, the side strip's terminal block — three small lines that resolve at 16x to '?ANO M?' / '??O?A?' / 'Torta?', printed as exactly that, question marks and all, captioned 'REPORTED AS UNREAD; DRAWN AS ILLEGIBLE SMALL TYPE.' Below that, La Santa's seven merged downstrokes with the four perpendicular cuts drawn across them as hairlines and the counts 6 / 5 / 5 / 4 set in the margin, captioned 'LA SANTA REMAINS CONSISTENT AND REMAINS UNREAD. DO NOT REPORT IT AS VERIFIED.' Below that, the three pillar menu cards reproduced as what the model actually builds — five flat colour bands and a fine stripe field, no letters at all — captioned 'THE INDIVIDUAL WORDS ARE 1.5 PX TALL AND ARE NOT MEASURABLE.' Below that, '1963' as its seven-segment bars at 5 px, captioned 'FLAGGED.' And then, dead centre of the sheet, occupying a clean rectangle of untouched yellow with 40 mm of air on every side, one line set large, crisp, and completely legible, in silver with its keyline: GRACIAS POR SU PREFERENCIA. No image of the bus. No mark. No logo. Light: none — flat spot inks on paper. The only tonal event on the whole sheet is the sudden clarity in the middle.
concept.emotional_claim: Recognition, then a small ache, then warmth. Anyone who has eaten at a taqueria has stood in front of a hand-painted board they could only half read, and ordered anyway, and been right to. The poster reproduces that exact experience and then rewards it: the one thing you CAN read is the thing the counter fascia actually says to you when you have paid. It reframes illegibility as intimacy rather than as failure — the signs are worn because the place is used. And for anyone inside the company it is quietly devastating, because it is a monument built entirely out of the project's own honest admissions of what it could not measure.
formats: B0 wall poster, 1000 x 1414 mm, two spot inks (strip yellow, dark red ink) plus a silver for the one legible line, on uncoated. It must be BIG: the whole piece depends on the viewer walking up close, failing to read, and then finding the one line that works. At A3 it is just a texture.
B1, 707 x 1000 mm, as the shop edition, numbered in pencil lower-left with a blind-emboss chop rather than a signature — there is no artist's hand to sign a piece assembled from measurements.
Restaurant installation: the same wall, printed direct-to-substrate or wheat-pasted, in the queue line where people are already standing and reading.

A 210 x 297 mm placemat version, with the legible line at the bottom where the plate does not cover it. This is where it earns its keep commercially — it is the cheapest object in the whole programme and the most likely to be photographed.
Postcards, one specimen per card, in a set of twelve. Each card carries its own caption on the reverse verbatim from the record.
NOT apparel. A shirt made of blurred type reads as a mistake at conversational distance and the joke does not survive being worn.
concept.why_not_derivative: It is not merchandise about a vehicle. It has no bus, no wheels, no silhouette, no VW mark, no sunset and no flowers, so it does not enter the category at all — it enters the category of the Mexican street sign, which nobody has mined. And its content is genuinely unavailable to anyone else: every specimen on the sheet exists only because lid_gen.py wrote down what it could not read instead of guessing, at 8-22x magnification, with the failure recorded as a result. A stock illustrator would have invented the missing thirteen characters. The whole poster is a monument to not having done that.
concept.production_notes: THIS IS THE RISKY ONE AND HERE IS EXACTLY WHY A CAUTIOUS TEAM KILLS IT. It contradicts the owner's own stated direction head-on: he ruled at rev 61 'senor Tacombi should be clearer in the render than in that photo. Well defined. I want this 3d model to look like new. Enhanced from the photo.' This poster does the opposite on purpose — it prints his signage as a smear. It also sits at an angle to SPEC section 10.10's 'ABSOLUTE REPLICATION OF ALL ARTWORK' hard bar, though not in breach of it: section 10.10's object is the MODEL's decals, and this is a derived artefact, but somebody will read it as the bar being abandoned and that argument has to be won in advance rather than after printing. It should be put to him as multiple choice with a printed A3 crop attached and the trade stated plainly — 'this piece is deliberately unclear, and here is why that reads as warmth and not as an error.' If he says no, it dies, and that is the correct outcome; do not soften it into legibility, because a half-legible version of this poster is just a badly printed menu. Production: the blur must be REAL and must be reproduced at its own scale — enlarge the actual measured crops, do not simulate a blur filter over clean type, or the whole honesty of the object collapses. Do not mix livery states on one sheet: rule 11 governs, and the Nolita chalkboard specimens (BIENVENIDOS, VENGA A NOLITA, TACOS DE HOY) belong to a different paint state from the Playa menu strips. If both are wanted, print two posters, not one. One factual check before anything goes to press: SPEC says the Nolita fascia reads '251 ELIZABETH STREET' while the rev-50 measurement record reads '267 ELIZABETH STREET' on two frames — those disagree, and a street number printed a metre wide is the worst possible place to inherit a stale figure.
model_work_required: NOTHING ON THE 3D MODEL. This concept is the one that needs no render, no alpha, no export and no geometry — it is built entirely from the reference photographs and from lid_gen.py's and t1_detail.py's own recorded readings. That is a feature: it ships under the F191 and F193 holds without touching anything they gate.

BUT IT EXPOSES ONE REAL MODEL GAP WORTH FIXING SEPARATELY: the three pillar menu cards are BUILT as geometry (CARD_W 0.0948 x CARD_H 0.3383 m at z 1.5667, on pillars measured at X +0.884 / +0.256 / -0.388) and carry NO LETTERING AT ALL — gal_menucard is five flat colour bands plus a fract stripe field, and its own docstring explains why: 'the individual WORDS are 1.5 px tall and are NOT MEASURABLE -- what is built is the band structure and the two measured colour statistics, not invented text.' That is the correct call and it should not be overturned by guessing. What would close it is a photograph, and PHOTOS_WANTED has never carried a menu-card item. Add one: one pillar menu card, square on and close.
RESOLVE THE '251' vs '267' ELIZABETH STREET DISCREPANCY between SPEC and the rev-50 measurement record before any deliverable prints an address.

IF the legible centre line is ever set from the vehicle's own hand rather than redrawn, it needs the same vector export named in concept 2 — there is currently no vector of any lettering in this tree.

verdicts.lens: ORIGINALITY — is this genuinely fresh, or a well-executed version of something already on a thousand VW-bus products (and, more dangerously, already on a thousand gallery walls)?
verdicts.reasoning:
Two separate originality questions, and this concept answers them very differently.

AGAINST THE VW-BUS MERCH CATEGORY IT IS A TOTAL ESCAPE, and that is earned rather than asserted. Every trope named in the market survey — sunset silhouette, surf, hippie/flower-power, 70s wash, minimal line art, boho/watercolour/pop-art — requires the vehicle to be depicted. This has no bus, no wheels, no silhouette, no VW mark. It also dodges the trap the survey singles out as the obvious move for a project holding a photoreal 3D model: BLUEPRINT/exploded-diagram, which Dreamstime sells as a standing category. Nothing here reads as a VW product. That is rarer in this set than it sounds.

AND ITS RAW MATERIAL IS VERIFIABLY UNOBTAINABLE ELSEWHERE. I checked every load-bearing specimen against source rather than trusting the concept. `lid_gen.py` carries `"?ANO M?" / "??O?A?" / "Torta?"` and "Reported as unread; drawn as illegible small type" verbatim; "The occluded span is 695 px. The three legible words average 53.6 px per character, so the gap accommodates 13.0 +/- 0.6 characters"; the La Santa block's "Perpendicular cuts across the word at four heights give 6, 5, 5 and 4 separated dark runs" and "remains CONSISTENT and remains UNREAD. Do not report it as verified"; `STRIP = (172, 144, 17)`, `INK = (72, 46, 6)`. `t1_detail.py` carries "The individual WORDS are 1.5 px tall and are NOT [MEASURABLE] ... not invented text". None of this was composed for the poster. The screener's core claim — that a stock illustrator would have invented the missing thirteen characters — holds up, and the caption register ("DO NOT REPORT IT AS VERIFIED") is a genuinely strange voice no illustrator arrives at.

BUT THE FORM IS BORROWED, AND FROM CANONICAL WORK. The stack is three well-known practices laid on top of each other. Jenny Holzer's REDACTION PAINTINGS (2004–) is the structural match: declassified documents enlarged to wall scale, illegibility as the subject, the withheld as the content. Thomas Ruff's JPEGS (2004) is the methodological match, and the concept's own production note — "the blur must be REAL ... do not simulate a blur filter over clean type" — is Ruff's exact rule restated.
