Trevor Paglen's LIMIT TELEPHOTOGRAPHY and Forensic Architecture's evidence presentation are the caption match: the image at its resolution limit with the measurement that produced the limit set beside it, and an explicit statement of what could not be determined. The specimen-grid-on-a-flat-coloured-ground is the vernacular-signage typology of Louise Fili's GRAFICA DELLA STRADA, SIGN PAINTERS (Levine/Macon 2012), and the Becher/Eijkelboom lineage. So on the axis I was given, the honest reading is: the material is fresh, the form is not. This is a well-executed version of something that exists — just in the gallery rather than on the merch table.

AND THE HERO MOVE IS THE WEAKEST ELEMENT ON THIS AXIS. "One perfectly clear line in a field of noise" is a stock poster device, it carries the entire emotional payload, and the emotional claim written around it (recognition, ache, warmth) pulls the piece back toward the familiar genre it had escaped. The piece's actual fresh asset is the cold machine voice; the centre line is where it flinches into sentiment.

IT ALSO BREAKS ITS OWN STATED RULE ON THAT SAME ELEMENT. `MEASURE_rev50.md`'s classification table lists "267 ELIZABETH STREET / NUEVA YORK | A | A | A | P | ? | ? | P (+ 'Gracias por su Preferencia') | A | A" — the hero line is present in the Nolita frames ONLY and is marked ABSENT in ref_side, ref_rear34 and ref_playa_34. Every other specimen on the sheet (the menu strips, La Santa, the pillar cards) is read off ref_side/ref_rear34, i.e. the Playa folk-art state. So the poster mixes livery states on one sheet — the exact thing its own production note forbids under rule 11, while naming only the chalkboard specimens as the risk. The finish compounds it: the record has that line as red script on cream, while the concept sets it "in silver with its keyline", which is `Senor`'s finish from a third element in a different state (F157). The single most load-bearing mark on the sheet is a two-state hybrid in both provenance and treatment.

Not exceptional, because exceptional on this axis requires the form to be as unprecedented as the corpus, and right now the corpus is doing all the work. Well clear of workable, because the material is real, verified, and genuinely unavailable to a competitor, and because it leaves the saturated category entirely rather than decorating its way out.

CEILINGS. I judged category-saturation against the supplied market survey, which declares itself qualitative with no counts and no share-of-market — so "escapes the tropes" is defensible, "escapes the most saturated tropes" is not something I can rank. The art-historical precedents are from my own knowledge and I could NOT verify them in this container; WebSearch is deferred here and the record notes direct fetches return EGRESS_BLOCKED. Treat the Holzer/Ruff/Paglen/Fili attributions as named leads to check before this is presented as an original form, not as verified citations. I rendered nothing and looked at no photograph; I verified the corpus strings only.
fatal_flaws: THE HERO LINE VIOLATES RULE 11 ON THE SHEET'S MOST LOAD-BEARING ELEMENT. `probe_scratch/rev50/measure/MEASURE_rev50.md`'s classification table reads `| 267 ELIZABETH STREET / NUEVA YORK | A | A | A | P | ? | ? | P (+ "Gracias por su Preferencia") | A | A |` — absent from ref_side, ref_rear34 and ref_playa_34, present only in the Nolita frames. Every other specimen on the poster is read off the Playa folk-art state. The production note forbids exactly this mixing and names only the chalkboard specimens as the hazard, missing that its own centre line is from the same forbidden state.

THE FINISH OF THAT LINE IS A THIRD ELEMENT'S. The record has the Gracias line as red script on the cream counter fascia; the concept sets it "in silver with its keyline", which is the `Senor Tacombi` flank script's ruled finish (F157, state A). So the hero mark is a hybrid of two livery states in provenance AND a third element in treatment — an invention presented as a found artefact, in a piece whose entire originality claim is that nothing on it was invented.

THE FORM IS THREE CANONICAL PRACTICES STACKED: Holzer's REDACTION PAINTINGS (illegibility monumentalised, the withheld as subject), Ruff's JPEGS (enlarge the real degradation, never simulate it — the concept's own production rule, verbatim), and Paglen / Forensic Architecture (resolution-limited evidence captioned with the measurement and an explicit statement of what could not be determined). The corpus is unprecedented; the container it sits in is not.

THE COMPOSITION IS A UNIFORM TYPOLOGY GRID — fifteen specimens all making one point at one treatment. That is one idea at length, and the grid-of-vernacular-signage-on-flat-colour is itself the established form of Fili's GRAFICA DELLA STRADA and the Becher/Eijkelboom typology lineage.

THE 'ONE CLEAR LINE IN A NOISE FIELD' REVEAL IS A STOCK POSTER DEVICE, and it carries the whole emotional payload. The emotional claim built on it (recognition, ache, warmth) is the most conventional writing in the concept and pulls against the cold instrument voice that is the piece's genuinely original register.
improvements: MAKE THE HERO THE HOLE, NOT A SENTENCE — this is the single change that moves the form from borrowed to unprecedented. Replace the legible centre line with an EMPTY rectangle of untouched strip yellow, sized to the measured occlusion, captioned only `695 PX OCCLUDED BY A PALM FROND. 13.0 +/- 0.6 CHARACTERS.` Holzer redacts with black; Ruff fills with artefact; this leaves nothing and gives you the DIMENSION of the absence, which no one in that lineage has done. It also resolves the rule-11 violation outright, because the void is state-A material from `lid_gen.py`'s own line "The occluded span is 695 px". If a legible line is still wanted, it must come from ref_side/ref_rear34, not from a Nolita frame, and it must be set in the finish the record gives it.

DERIVE THE LAYOUT FROM THE MEASUREMENTS INSTEAD OF DESIGNING IT — kills the typology grid. Scale every specimen so one photographed pixel equals one fixed physical size on the sheet (4 mm, say). Then the mural strip is enormous, La Santa is mid-sized, `1963` at 5 px is a thumbnail, and the pillar menu cards at "1.5 px tall" are a hairline you physically cannot resolve at any viewing distance. The page becomes a bar chart of legibility that reads as a column of type, the B0 format stops being a taste decision and becomes forced by the evidence, and the composition is authored by the camera rather than by a designer working in a known idiom.

PROMOTE THE MODEL'S OWN REFUSAL TO SECOND PANEL. `t1_detail.py` builds the three pillar menu cards as five flat colour bands and a stripe field with no letters, because "The individual WORDS are 1.5 px tall and are NOT [MEASURABLE] ... not invented text". Setting that abstract colour-band object directly beside the photograph's blur is the one juxtaposition on the sheet with NO precedent in Holzer, Ruff or Paglen — it is not degraded evidence, it is a machine declining to guess. Currently it is row four of fifteen. Give it a panel and a caption in its own words.

CUT THE RECORD'S QUESTION-MARK NOTATION AS AN ACTUAL DISPLAY GLYPH. `"?ANO M?" / "??O?A?" / "Torta?"` uses `?` as a letterform placeholder — a typographic convention this project invented by accident and that nobody has drawn. Draw it: a question mark cut on the same skeleton, weight and cap-height as the strip lettering, so it sets INLINE as a letter rather than reading as punctuation. That gives the piece a proprietary typographic element and stops the blur being the only visual idea, which is where the Ruff comparison bites hardest.

LET THE INSTRUMENT VOICE CARRY THE WHOLE SHEET AND DELETE THE WARMTH FROM THE BRIEF. `DO NOT REPORT IT AS VERIFIED` / `REPORTED AS UNREAD` / `THAT IS A CONSISTENCY, NOT A READING` is a register no poster uses. Set every caption in that voice with no exceptions and no closing sentiment, and let the viewer supply the ache unprompted. The moment the poster tells you to feel something it rejoins the genre it escaped.

STATE THE ANTI-HOLZER RULE IN THE PRODUCTION NOTES AND HOLD IT: NO BLACK ANYWHERE, NO BAR, NO RULE, NO BOX. Two spot inks only — strip yellow (172,144,17) and ink (72,46,6), both measured in `lid_gen.py`. A single black bar anywhere on this sheet collapses it into a Redaction Painting pastiche, and it is the most likely accident at press.

MAKE THE PAIR THE ARTEFACT INSTEAD OF POLICING THE MIX. The concept already says print two posters rather than one if both states are wanted. Go further: PLAYA and NUEVA YORK as a diptych, same format, same inks, same rules, each built only from its own state's readings — the difference between the two sheets IS the brand's history, and rule 11 stops being a constraint and becomes the subject. That is a structural idea the precedent works do not have, because none of them has two paint states of one object.

FIX THE FRAMING OF THE OWNER ASK — it is currently harder to win than it needs to be. The concept says it contradicts the rev-61 ruling head-on, but that ruling's object is the RENDER ("I want this 3d MODEL to look like new"), and this is a derived 2D artefact with no render in it. Under rule 34 a requirement inherits its object. Put it to him as: the model stays clean and new, and this poster is made from the PHOTOGRAPHS' limits, not from the model's finish. Same for SPEC 10.10, whose object is the model's decals. Also carry the 251-vs-267 flag forward as a PROGRAM note — `SPEC.md` line 344 says 251 while `MEASURE_rev50.md` and `LEDGER_rev49.md` both read 267 — since the address does not appear on this sheet unless the centre line changes.

verdicts.lens: Producibility and fidelity: can this be made from THIS asset, given failing gates, unbuilt geometry, an unproven large-format chain, and an emblem rejected nine times — and does what it prints survive contact with the record?
verdicts.reasoning:
On producibility this is the strongest concept possible from this asset, and I mean that structurally rather than as praise. It needs no render, no Blender, no alpha, no export, no stitch. That means it is the only concept that ships entirely under F191 and F193 without touching anything those holds gate; it is immune to every pipeline defect in the grounded reality (T1_ALPHA unrun for thirteen revisions, post.py destroying alpha, stitch/post being 8-bit on a 16-bit render, nothing above 1600x1100 existing on disk, hq_render missing T1_FX=0, no OBJ/glTF/USD path at all) because none of them is in its way. Its source being low-resolution is the POINT, so the unproven large-format chain is irrelevant rather than merely avoided. And it carries no bus and no VW mark, which sidesteps the live, uncarried trademark exposure the market lane flags.

I checked the specimens rather than trusting the concept. They are verbatim and they are real. lid_gen.py section D carries "The occluded span is 695 px. The three legible words average 53.6 px per character, so the gap accommodates 13.0 +/- 0.6 characters. 'GOURMET TACOS' is 13 characters. That is a CONSISTENCY, not a reading." Section D also carries the terminal block: "they resolve to about '?ANO M?' / '??O?A?' / 'Torta?' ... Reported as unread; drawn as illegible small type." Section E carries "Perpendicular cuts across the word at four heights give 6, 5, 5 and 4 separated dark runs" and "'La Santa' remains CONSISTENT and remains UNREAD. Do not report it as verified." t1_detail.py's gal_menucard carries "The individual WORDS are 1.5 px tall and are NOT MEASURABLE -- what is built is the band structure and the two measured colour statistics, not invented text." plate_1963 carries "(seven-segment bars); at the hero scale a digit is ~5 px. FLAGGED." STRIP = (172, 144, 17) is in source with "menu-strip yellow, ink excluded". Nothing in the body of this poster is invented.

I also tested the thing most likely to kill it, by looking. My worry was that enlarging a 7-px cap height out of a 1024x768 JPEG yields DCT blocking and chroma smear — digital degradation, which reads as a bad screenshot, not as a hand-painted board seen across a plaza. It does not. probe_scratch/rev50_fidelity-bar_ref_lidtop_x6.png at 6x is soft, warm and grainy, with "1963" dissolving into segments. ref_side.jpg cropped (290,80)-(760,330) at 3x already shows FRESH / JUICES / CEVICHE TOSTADAS / SHRIMP & FISH half-legible on both side strips, with the left strip's copy behind the man's cap exactly as the docstring says. ref_rear34.jpg cropped (600,20)-(760,180) at 7x gives the La Santa specimen intact: "La" lower left, the red star point-up, the spiral-eyed S with its descender swinging down-left, the merged downstrokes climbing right and running off the top edge of the cream, the light keyline against the dark outline. The aesthetic is verified, not asserted.

What holds it back from exceptional is that all four of its problems land on the same element — the one line the whole piece cannot do without. GRACIAS POR SU PREFERENCIA occurs exactly once in this repository: probe_scratch/rev50/measure/MEASURE_rev50.md line 318, as a parenthetical inside a P/A/? presence table cell. No crop, no px/m, no cap height, no ink median, no grade. Every other specimen on the sheet arrives with a measured caption; the payoff line is the only one with nothing under it, which inverts the poster's own logic. It is also state B (Nolita), while the field colour, the mural strips and La Santa are state C (Playa) — the concept's own production notes say "If both are wanted, print two posters, not one," and then it puts both on one. Its material is wrong too: the fascia line is red hand-lettered script, not "silver with its keyline," and that keyline is measured absent from tex/senor.png. And it lives on ref_nolita_doorshut.jpg, 480x320, the smallest frame held, so "large, crisp, completely legible" means a hand-lettering commission the concept lists only as conditional ("IF the legible centre line is ever set...") when it is in fact the largest undeclared piece of work in the proposal.

Separately, La Santa is owner-ruled not on the vehicle at all — F164, RULED-rev62, "The forward one is separate from the Bus," restaurant furniture — which contradicts the poster's own framing line. Every one of these is cheap to fix, and none touches the body of the sheet, which is why this is strong rather than workable.
fatal_flaws: LIVERY-STATE MIXING — the concept names the trap and walks into it. GRACIAS POR SU PREFERENCIA is present only in ref_nolita_doorshut.jpg = state B (Nolita, New York; plain red flank, chalkboard lid). The field colour STRIP (172,144,17), the mural top strip, the side strips and La Santa are all state C (Playa, current folk-art). MEASURE_rev50.md's classification table puts them in different states and CLAUDE.md rule 11 governs. The concept's own production notes say 'Do not mix livery states on one sheet ... If both are wanted, print two posters, not one' — and then the sheet does exactly that. These are also two different restaurants in two different countries, so no reframing rescues it.

THE CENTREPIECE HAS NO MEASUREMENT UNDER IT. 'Gracias por su Preferencia' appears exactly once in the whole repository — probe_scratch/rev50/measure/MEASURE_rev50.md line 318, as a parenthetical in a '267 ELIZABETH STREET / NUEVA YORK' row of a P/A/? presence table. No crop, no cap height, no px/m, no ink colour, no clipping fraction, no grade. On a poster whose every other caption is a real measurement quoted verbatim from a docstring, the one line carrying the entire emotional payoff is the only unmeasured object on the sheet.

THE CENTRE LINE'S MATERIAL IS WRONG TWICE. The concept sets it 'in silver with its keyline.' The fascia line is RED hand-lettered script on cream. Silver-with-keyline is the Señor Tacombi wordmark's treatment — a different element in a different livery state — and the grounded reality measures that keyline ABSENT from the shipped asset: of tex/senor.png pixels with alpha>200, the 1st-percentile luma is 168.3 and the fraction below luma 80 is 0.0000. So the poster borrows a treatment from the wrong element, and the borrowed treatment does not exist in the asset it is borrowed from.

THE CRISP LINE IS AN UNSCOPED HAND-LETTERING COMMISSION. Its only source is a 480x320 frame — the smallest held — where the line occupies roughly 150x20 native px inside the (280,140)-(470,230) fascia crop. It cannot be enlarged to a legible B0 centrepiece; it must be redrawn. There is no vector of any lettering anywhere in this tree (the only SVG ever committed is vw_canonical_2019.svg, a different object). The concept lists this as conditional — 'IF the legible centre line is ever set from the vehicle's own hand' — when it is unconditional and is the single largest piece of undeclared work in the proposal.

LA SANTA IS NOT ON THIS VEHICLE, AND THE OWNER HAS RULED SO. t1_shell.py's signboard(): 'So it is not a roof lid, and it is not on the vehicle at all. It is a detached sign that happens to fall behind the combi in ref_rear34.jpg.' F164, RULED-rev62, owner: 'The forward one is separate from the Bus' — restaurant furniture, and it 'must not be modelled as attached to it, nor used as evidence about the bus's own lids.' The poster's premise line is 'everything on this vehicle that could not be read.' Its best specimen is not on the vehicle.

AN UNDECLARED CONSTRUCTION PRINTED AS A MEASUREMENT. The concept prints the specimens 'in dark red ink (72,46,6).' lid_gen.py's own comment: 'INK = (72, 46, 6) # strip lettering; measured median (91,59,7) is blur-limited, so the core is set darker.' So (72,46,6) is an authored value chosen for a texture generator, not the photograph's ink — and it is ochre-brown, not dark red. On this poster of all posters, quoting a construction as a measurement is the one error the piece cannot absorb. (STRIP (172,144,17) is honestly measured, 'ink excluded', and is fine.)
improvements: SPLIT IT INTO TWO POSTERS AND LET THE NOLITA ONE CARRY THE PAYOFF — this single move fixes flaws 1, 2 and 3 at once, and it is what the concept's own production notes already demand. Poster A (NOLITA): field in a Nolita-state colour, specimens all state B — the chalkboard's 'TACOMBI' tricolour, 'TACOS DE HOY', 'BIENVENIDOS' down both jambs, '...DA NOLITA ★', '267 ELIZABETH STREET / NUEVA YORK' — and GRACIAS POR SU PREFERENCIA as the legible centre, native to its own state, in red script. Poster B (PLAYA): the strip-yellow field with the top strip's 695-px void, the '?ANO M?' terminal block, the menu cards and '1963'. Poster B then needs its own state-C payoff line; the honest candidate is the top strip's fully-legible fragment, since lid_gen.py measures 'FRESH' at x 276-570 and 'JUICES,' at 589-926 as READ rather than reconstructed. Weaker emotionally than Gracias, so consider making Poster A the hero and Poster B the companion.

MEASURE THE CENTRE LINE BEFORE PRINTING IT, AND PUT THE MEASUREMENT IN THE RECORD, NOT ONLY ON THE POSTER. Give it exactly what lid_gen.py gave the strips: crop ref_nolita_doorshut.jpg at the counter fascia, rectify it, read at 8-16x, and record cap height in px, the px/m at that station, the ink median WITH its clipping fraction, the letterform description, and a provenance grade — then write it into a generator docstring the way section D records the menu strips. This is roughly an afternoon of pure-python work, needs no Blender, and it converts the poster's weakest element into its best-documented one. Until it exists, the piece is asking a viewer to trust the one caption that has nothing behind it.

NAME THE THREE REGISTERS OF FAILURE — the largest artistic upgrade available, and it costs only layout. The sheet currently presents three genuinely different admissions as one texture. (a) THE PHOTOGRAPH COULD NOT RESOLVE IT: the 695-px palm void, '?ANO M?' / '??O?A?' / 'Torta?', La Santa's 6/5/5/4 cuts. (b) THE MODEL DREW A SCHEMATIC BECAUSE OF (a): '1963', where t1_detail.py says '(seven-segment bars); at the hero scale a digit is ~5 px. FLAGGED.' (c) THE MODEL DREW NOTHING BECAUSE OF (a): the menu cards, where the docstring says 'what is built is the band structure and the two measured colour statistics, not invented text.' Set these as three labelled bands or columns. This turns a wall of blur into an argument, and (c) — a machine that declined to invent — is the most moving panel on the sheet. As it stands, (b) and (c) are silently presented as photographic blur, which is a category error the poster's own thesis cannot afford.

ENLARGE FROM THE NATIVE FRAME, NEVER THE RECTIFIED ONE, AND PRINT BOTH SCALES IN THE CAPTION. Every figure the concept quotes — 695 px, 53.6 px per character, cap height 64 px — is in lid_gen.py's 2400x1500 RECTIFIED frame, which is roughly a 9x upsample of ref_side.jpg's native pixels (the whole propped board spans only about cols 300-760 of a 1024x768 frame). Enlarging the rectified frame prints resampling artefacts, not photography, and breaks the concept's own central promise that 'the blur must be REAL.' Enlarge from the native JPEG and caption each specimen with both numbers — the native px and the rectified px the record read it at. I confirmed the native material carries it: ref_side at 3x already gives half-legible strips, ref_rear34 at 7x gives La Santa intact, and probe_scratch/rev50_fidelity-bar_ref_lidtop_x6.png shows the 6x look is warm and soft rather than blocky.

REFRAME THE PREMISE LINE FROM 'THIS VEHICLE' TO 'THIS TAQUERIA' — it is truer, it costs nothing, and it legitimises the best specimen. F164 (RULED-rev62) puts La Santa on a detached sign standing behind the combi, not on the bus. Under a vehicle framing the specimen has to be cut; under a place framing it belongs, and so do the fascia lettering and the menu cards. Make the change deliberately and say in the ledger that F164 is why, rather than leaving a poster that asserts something the owner has ruled against.

FIX THE INK, OR CAPTION IT AS CONSTRUCTED. Either print the honestly measured (91,59,7) and note it is blur-limited, or keep (72,46,6) and caption it 'CORE SET DARKER THAN THE BLUR-LIMITED MEDIAN (91,59,7)' — which is itself a good caption and entirely on-message. Also stop calling it 'dark red'; it is an ochre-brown. Keep STRIP (172,144,17) exactly as is: lid_gen.py records it 'ink excluded' and it is one of the cleanest measurements on the sheet.

DECIDE THE SEPARATION BEFORE QUOTING THE PRINT. 'Two spot inks plus a silver on uncoated' will not survive the printer: the specimens are continuous-tone JPEG enlargements, not line art, and cannot be spot-separated cleanly. Pick one and specify it — (a) CMYK plus one spot silver for the legible line, (b) each specimen halftoned to a single spot at a deliberately coarse line count, where the coarseness is on-message and reinforces the thesis, or (c) duotone. Option (b) is the most beautiful and the most in keeping, and it also makes the enlargement artefacts intentional rather than apologised for.

MAKE THE '251' vs '267' CORRECTION A DELIVERABLE, NOT A PRE-PRESS CHECK. SPEC.md line 344 reads '251 ELIZABETH STREET / NUEVA YORK'; MEASURE_rev50.md, LEDGER_rev49.md and NEXT_CONTEXT_PROMPT_rev50.md all read 267, and SURVEY_rev49_photoreal.md records it verified left-to-right on a contact sheet of all nine distinct frames. The weight is with 267 and SPEC is the outlier — but SPEC is the document this project calls authoritative on livery, so the fix belongs IN SPEC in the same edit (rule 13), not only on the artwork. A street number printed a metre wide is the worst possible place to inherit a stale figure, and the concept is right to flag it; it should go one step further and close it.

ADD THE ONE PHOTOS_WANTED ITEM THIS CONCEPT EARNS. The menu-card panel is the sheet's most moving specimen and it is 20.4 x 65.7 px native in ref_side.jpg (t1_detail.py, x 432-453, y 328-394, at the local 211.5 px/m). PHOTOS_WANTED has never carried a menu-card item. Add 'one pillar menu card, square on and close' — it is the only model-side work this concept implies, it is a photograph request rather than geometry, and if he supplies it the poster gains a panel AND gal_menucard gains the lettering it currently and correctly refuses to invent.

KEEP THE THING THAT MAKES THIS WORK, AND SAY SO IN THE PROPOSAL. The rarest property here is that the concept carries the docstrings' own CEILINGS into the artwork as captions — 'That is a CONSISTENCY, not a reading', 'Do not report it as verified', 'Reported as unread; drawn as illegible small type.' Most concepts strip ceilings; this one makes them the subject. When this is put to the owner against his rev-61 'I want this 3d model to look like new. Enhanced from the photo,' lead with that: the poster is not disobeying the ruling, it is a different artefact about a different thing — the ruling's object is the MODEL, and applying it to a derived print is precisely the rule-34 error that F92/F188 cost this project twelve revisions of misattribution. Say that explicitly in the ask, with an A3 proof attached, or the objection will be raised for you and framed as disobedience.

verdicts.lens: Emotional resonance, brand fit and IP exposure
verdicts.reasoning:
I checked the specimens rather than trusting the pitch, and they are real. `lid_gen.py` carries verbatim: "The occluded span is 695 px. The three legible words average 53.6 px per character, so the gap accommodates 13.0 +/- 0.6 characters. \"GOURMET TACOS\" is 13 characters. That is a CONSISTENCY, not a reading."; "they resolve to about \"?ANO M?\" / \"??O?A?\" / \"Torta?\" ... Reported as unread; drawn as illegible small type."; "\"La Santa\" remains CONSISTENT and remains UNREAD. Do not report it as verified." with "Perpendicular cuts across the word at four heights give 6, 5, 5 and 4 separated dark runs"; "strip yellow (172,144,17), hue 48.0". `t1_detail.py` carries "The individual WORDS are 1.5 px tall and are NOT" measurable, and "at the hero scale a digit is ~5 px. FLAGGED." Nothing is invented. That grounding is genuinely rare and it is why this ranks above the rest of the set.

On IP it is the cleanest concept possible against the axis that actually threatens this programme: no VW roundel, no bus silhouette, no split-screen profile, nothing VW enforces. It reaches for a Tacombi-specific route (the vehicle's own hand-lettering) where every competitor reaches for the van. Correct call, correctly executed.

But three defects sit at precisely the one point the whole piece depends on — the legible line — and they compound.

FIRST, IT BREAKS ITS OWN LIVERY RULE AT ITS CENTRE. I read the classification table in `probe_scratch/rev50/measure/MEASURE_rev50.md`: the row "267 ELIZABETH STREET / NUEVA YORK" is **A** (absent) on ref_side, ref_rear34 and ref_playa_34, and **P** only on nolita_flank and nolita_doorshut — "**P** (+ \"Gracias por su Preferencia\")". That file's own §2.2 classes the four Nolita frames as state **B** and ref_side/ref_rear34/ref_playa_34 as state **C**, and says states "must never be pooled". Every specimen in the field is state C. The hero line is state B. The concept's production notes forbid exactly this — "Do not mix livery states on one sheet: rule 11 governs" — and then name only BIENVENIDOS / VENGA A NOLITA as the specimens to keep out, missing that its own centrepiece is from the same state. A poster whose moral authority is method discipline cannot break the project's most-enforced rule in its own focal rectangle.

SECOND, THE ONE LEGIBLE ELEMENT IS THE ONE INVENTED ELEMENT. The record reads the fascia line as red script on cream. The concept sets it "in silver with its keyline". Silver is F157's ruling and F157's object is the flank word `Senor` only — HANDOFF_CARRIERS §4: "OVERRIDES SPEC §3's WEATHERED LOCK FOR THAT WORD ONLY". Applying it to a different piece of lettering on a different panel in a different livery state is rule 34's exact shape. In a sheet built entirely from refusals to guess, the single guessed thing is the payoff.

THIRD, THE PAYOFF PHRASE IS THE MOST GENERIC SENTENCE IN MEXICAN COMMERCE. "Gracias por su preferencia" is on millions of receipts, shop windows and till rolls. The field is unforgeable; the punchline is a stock phrase. So the emotional yield rests on the least Tacombi-specific text on the sheet, and a viewer who does not know it came off this bus reads it as a generic courtesy — which is the same failure mode as reaching for a sunset.

A fourth, quieter IP flag nobody raised: "La Santa" is not Tacombi's. `LEDGER_rev49.md` — "on the **GROUND, BEHIND** the bus", retired for that reason; SURVEY_rev49 lists it under retired identifications. It is very plausibly a neighbouring business's trade name, and the record simultaneously says the word is "a RECONSTRUCTION, not a reading". Printing it a metre wide, captioned, on Tacombi promotional material publishes a reconstruction of a third party's name.

Two smaller things. The category claim is measured against the wrong market — blurred type plus forensic caption is a populated editorial/gallery genre, so the novelty is in the DATA, not the LOOK, and a stranger reads the captions as affectation unless provenance is on the sheet. And the format logic self-contradicts: "At A3 it is just a texture" sits beside a 210×297 placemat (smaller than A3) named as the commercial workhorse, and a twelve-card set of single specimens, when the mechanism IS accumulation-then-relief and one specimen alone has no mechanism at all.

Brand fit is split. The wall installation in the queue line and the placemat are exactly right for a brand whose own voice is deadpan and environmental ("casual, convenient leisure products", "Monument T", "purpose-built"). The numbered B1 with a pencil number and a blind-emboss chop is gallery register and reads as the studio enjoying itself; it is the one format that would look wrong beside the beanie.

The owner conflict is handled honestly, which I credit — but the framing offered will probably lose the ask, and it does not have to. Fix the state, fix the finish, fix the payoff, and this is the best thing in the set.
fatal_flaws: THE HERO LINE IS FROM A DIFFERENT LIVERY STATE THAN THE FIELD, breaking the concept's own stated rule. MEASURE_rev50.md's classification table puts "267 ELIZABETH STREET / NUEVA YORK ... (+ \"Gracias por su Preferencia\")" as PRESENT only on the Nolita frames and ABSENT on ref_side, ref_rear34 and ref_playa_34; its §2.2 calls the Nolita frames state B and the folk-art frames state C and says the states "must never be pooled". The whole field is C. The centrepiece is B. The production notes forbid this and name only the chalkboard specimens as the risk, missing their own.

THE ONLY LEGIBLE ELEMENT IS THE ONLY INVENTED ELEMENT. The fascia line is recorded as red script on cream; the concept sets it in silver with a keyline. Silver is F157, whose object is the flank word `Senor` alone — "OVERRIDES SPEC §3's WEATHERED LOCK FOR THAT WORD ONLY". Carrying that finish to different lettering, on a different panel, in a different livery state is rule 34 firing inside a poster whose entire premise is that nothing was guessed.

THE EMOTIONAL PAYOFF RESTS ON A STOCK PHRASE. "Gracias por su preferencia" is standard Mexican commercial courtesy printed on receipts and shop windows nationwide. The blurred field is unforgeable; the one thing the viewer takes away is not brand-specific, not from the target livery, and not attributable to Tacombi without the restaurant around it.

THIRD-PARTY MARK EXPOSURE, UNFLAGGED. LEDGER_rev49.md places the "La Santa" board "on the GROUND, BEHIND the bus" and it was retired from the model precisely because it is not this vehicle; the record also calls the word "a RECONSTRUCTION, not a reading". Reproducing it a metre wide, captioned, on Tacombi promotional material publishes a reconstruction of what is probably another business's trade name. The concept scrupulously avoids VW and walks into this instead.

THE SHEET HAS NO ATTRIBUTION AT ALL — "No image of the bus. No mark. No logo." In the queue line the room supplies the attribution; anywhere else (social, shop, press, print) it advertises nothing and cannot be traced to Tacombi. For a programme whose stated purpose is promotional material, that is a live cost, not a purity gain.
improvements: SWAP THE PAYOFF LINE TO ONE THAT IS BOTH IN-STATE AND UNMISTAKABLY THIS BUS. The strongest candidate is already in the same source as the field: lid_gen.py reads the mural header's legible words at 53.6 px per character, and t1_mats.py/cal_gen.py carry '100% Calidad' on the cream with its measured -19.7° set. Either '★ FRESH JUICES ... & TORTAS ★' (same board, same state, same ink, the words that ARE legible where the rest is not) or '100% CALIDAD' (state C, on the target bus, and quietly funny beside a sheet of illegible signage) keeps the sheet inside one livery state and makes the punchline unforgeable. '100% CALIDAD' is the better joke and the better brand line.

IF 'GRACIAS POR SU PREFERENCIA' IS KEPT, MAKE THE STATE CHANGE THE SUBJECT INSTEAD OF HIDING IT. Print it in its recorded red script on its recorded cream, in a cream rectangle set into the yellow — a physical inset, clearly a different panel — captioned in the same 7pt caps as everything else: 'READ ON ref_nolita_doorshut.jpg. A DIFFERENT PAINT STATE OF THE SAME VEHICLE. NEW YORK, NOT PLAYA.' That converts the violation into the sheet's most honest gesture and preserves the rule the poster claims to live by.

KILL THE SILVER. Set the legible line in its measured colours or set it in the sheet's existing dark red ink (72,46,6). Do not carry F157's silver to a word F157 does not cover. If a metallic is wanted for production reasons, put the silver on the blind-emboss chop or the edition mark, never on a specimen.

REPLACE THE 'LA SANTA' SPECIMEN, OR STRIP THE NAME OFF IT. Print the seven merged downstrokes with the 6/5/5/4 cuts and caption it 'A LETTERED PANEL STANDING BEHIND THE BUS. SEVEN DOWNSTROKES. FOUR CUTS GIVE 6, 5, 5, 4. NOT ON THE VEHICLE. NOT READ.' — no proposed name at all. That is both more faithful to the record (the word is a reconstruction) and removes a third party's trade name from Tacombi merchandise. Confirm with the owner whether La Santa is a neighbouring business before it appears in any form.

PUT PROVENANCE ON THE SHEET SO THE CAPTIONS READ AS FACT, NOT AFFECT. One line of 6pt at the foot: 'EVERY SPECIMEN ABOVE IS REPRODUCED AT THE SCALE AND BLUR AT WHICH IT WAS PHOTOGRAPHED. NO MISSING CHARACTER HAS BEEN SUPPLIED. READINGS TAKEN AT 8-22x FROM SIX PHOTOGRAPHS OF ONE VEHICLE.' Without it the poster is competing in the crowded annotated-editorial genre; with it, it is a document and the genre comparison stops applying.

ADD ONE SMALL, UNMISTAKABLE ATTRIBUTION. Not a logo lockup — the tail plate's '1963' seven-segment bars at their measured ~5 px, blind-embossed rather than printed, bottom right. It attributes without breaking the no-mark rule, it is on the target vehicle, and it is the one specimen on the sheet that IS a date-stamp.

RE-FRAME THE OWNER ASK SO IT CAN SURVIVE. His rev-61 ruling is 'I want this 3d model to look like new. Enhanced from the photo' — its object is the MODEL. This poster is about the PHOTOGRAPHS' limits, not the model's. Put it to him as: 'This is a monument to what the CAMERA could not resolve, not to the bus being unclear. The model gets clearer; the photographs stay honest.' Attach a printed B1 crop, not A3 — the concept's own argument says A3 is a texture, so a small ask proof will produce a false no.

DROP THE TWELVE-CARD SET AND THE NUMBERED GALLERY EDITION. One specimen alone has no mechanism — the mechanism is accumulation then relief. And the pencil-numbered, blind-chopped B1 is gallery register against a merch voice that sells 'purpose-built, all-weather' beanies. Keep the B0 wall piece, the in-restaurant installation, and one large-format takeaway. If a small object is wanted, make it a single card carrying the WHOLE sheet reduced, with the legible line still legible — that preserves the mechanism at 105x148 mm.

FIX THE PLACEMAT'S OWN CONTRADICTION. At A4 the sheet is a texture by the concept's own argument. Redesign the placemat as a THREE-specimen sheet at print-legible size with the payoff line at the foot, not a reduction of the B0. Different object, same idea, and it is the item most likely to be photographed and posted.

CUT OR RE-CAPTION THE PILLAR MENU CARD SPECIMEN. It is the only specimen with no photographic provenance — what is shown is the model's five flat colour bands, i.e. a BUILD decision, while the caption ('THE INDIVIDUAL WORDS ARE 1.5 PX TALL AND ARE NOT MEASURABLE') is about the photograph. Two different kinds of failure inside one taxonomy weakens the sheet. Either show the photographed card at its own blur, or caption it explicitly: 'THE MODEL DECLINES TO DRAW THESE WORDS. WHAT IS BUILT IS THE BAND STRUCTURE.'

SETTLE 251 vs 267 ELIZABETH STREET BEFORE ANY ADDRESS PRINTS. I confirmed the split: SPEC.md line 344 reads '251 ELIZABETH STREET / NUEVA YORK' while SURVEY_rev49_photoreal.md, MEASURE_rev50.md, LEDGER_rev49.md and NEXT_CONTEXT_PROMPT_rev50.md all read 267 on two frames. Four measured records against one prose line. The concept flags this correctly — act on it, and if the address is dropped along with the Nolita state, the discrepancy stops being this poster's problem at all.

CHECK AUTHORSHIP OF THE HAND-LETTERING BEFORE PRINTING IT ISOLATED. Nothing in the repository records who painted the mural board or the strips. Depicting them ON the vehicle is depicting Tacombi's own property; enlarging the lettering to a metre wide as the artwork itself is closer to reproducing a signwriter's work. A one-line question to the owner ('do we know who painted the board?') costs nothing and is worth asking before a B0 run.

concept.title: THE UNCERTAINTY PLATE
concept.one_line: A factory elevation drawing where every dimension line confesses how it was obtained — and the ones that cannot be obtained are drawn anyway, in the signwriter's hand, as sentences.
concept.the_image:
Landscape sheet, warm uncoated paper stock (not white, not cyanotype blue — the blue is the cliché). The vehicle is a TRUE orthographic side elevation, drawn as line only: a black-brown keyline at three declared weights (0.55 mm outer silhouette / 0.35 mm panel edges and shut lines / 0.20 mm hatch reveals, louvre blades, bulb sockets), with FOUR flat fills and no shading at all — body red, cream, folk-art gold reduced to its three largest masses only, and a warm near-black for tyres and glazing. The propped tail board runs off the top-right of the sheet on its measured 38.0-degree diagonal and is deliberately allowed to cross into the title block. Below and around it: full drafting furniture — extension lines, arrowed dimension rules, section flags, a scale bar, a north-style datum arrow at the front axle.

The subversion is entirely in the annotation, and it runs on TWO INKS AND TWO TYPE VOICES that mean two different things.

MEASURED dimensions are set in tight mono numerals, solid ink, hard filled arrowheads, exactly as a factory plate would: `2400 WHEELBASE` · `1369 / 1359 TRACK` · `664.9 TYRE` · `515.5 × 403.0 SERVING APERTURE ×3` · `17.75 mm/m RAKE` · `39.7 ARCH TO TYRE` · `109.5 | 129.5 PILLARS` (and that last one is the whole thesis in one figure — the three holes are equal but the two pillars between them are NOT, and no stylised bus drawing on earth gets that right).

UNMEASURED dimensions are drawn in a 40% tint, the arrowheads replaced by open square brackets, and the number replaced by hand-lettered script in the vehicle's own silver-leaf letterform — the same hand that painted 'Gracias por su Preferencia' on the counter fascia. These are the poems, and they are all true:
  · across the propped tail board — `[ 550 ] chosen, not measured. The board's plane contains the width, so it projects only through parallax. Upper bound 590. Lower bound: none.`
  · at the rear hatch's swing — `[ 64° ] a pose. No photograph we hold shows it open.`
  · at the roof — `[ ] height retired as a target, rev 22. What this vehicle stands at is open and unmeasured.`
  · at the tread — `[ 64 lugs ] declared. Two methods disagree; the honest answer is somewhere between 48 and 84.`
  · at the engine bay — `ENGINE: NONE. TRANSMISSION: SOLD.`
  · at the three apertures — `Arrived missing three windows. We left them that way.`
  · at the empty plate frame — `1963. The only date on the vehicle, and it is stamped on an empty plate.`

One further wrongness, small and deadly: the lid's own dimension line carries `WIDTH = f(ANGLE)` with a tiny inset graph, because in this model the mural board's width is genuinely a function of how far it is open (1.2237 m at 76°, 3.47 m at 20°). A blueprint annotating its own impossibility.

Title block bottom-right, six-point mono, unfakeable: `UNIT 01 · TYPE 2 · 1963 · PLAYA DEL CARMEN · 229 MESH OBJECTS · 376,383 VERTICES · 0 NON-MANIFOLD BODY EDGES · REV 76`.
concept.emotional_claim: Recognition, then a small shock, then affection. You approach it as a spec sheet — the most emotionally cold object in graphic design — and at reading distance you discover it is being honest with you about what it does not know. The feeling is INTIMACY WITH A MACHINE'S HUMILITY. Every other technical poster asserts; this one admits, and admission is disarming in a way assertion never is. And the specific admissions are all about care: somebody measured the pillars between three holes to a tenth of a millimetre AND was unwilling to guess at the width of a board. That combination — obsessive where it can be, silent where it can't — is exactly what a person means when they say a thing was made with love. The '[ 550 ] chosen, not measured' line is the one people photograph and send to each other.
formats: A2 landscape (594 × 420 mm) — THE PRIMARY, and it is chosen to fit the proven chain, not the ambition. 3840 px on the long edge is 488 mm at 200 dpi, so A2 sits inside what has actually been rendered once (3840×2640, rev 57). Ship A2 first.
A1 (841 × 594 mm) as the LIMITED tier, and only after a proving run: A1 at 200 dpi wants 4677 px, 22 % above anything this chain has ever produced. Do not promise A1 before that run.
A4 (297 × 210 mm) as a free insert at the restaurant, on the same uncoated stock, unnumbered. Same drawing, annotations reduced to five lines. This is the version people actually keep.
A 1080 × 1350 crop set for social: five separate posts, each one a single dimension line and its confession, cropped tight. The 'ENGINE: NONE' one is the launch post.
210 × 99 mm bookmark / bill-drop from a vertical slice through the rear quarter: louvre block, Calidad burst, rear wheel, and the '1963' annotation.
concept.why_not_derivative: The category already sells 'VW van blueprint' by the sheet — Dreamstime carries it as a standing stock shelf — and every one of those is a GENERIC bus, traced, annotated with plausible-looking numbers nobody measured. This sheet is unforgeable in three separate ways at once. (1) It dimensions the CONVERSION, not the vehicle: apertures, counter, tail board, louvre block. Anything you could draw from a factory manual is deliberately absent. (2) Its numbers come off a mesh that has been measured for seventy-six revisions and can be regenerated on demand — the wheelbase reads +0.0 mm to spec, the track +0.0 mm, the tyre −0.1 mm — so it is a document about a real object rather than a decoration in the shape of one. (3) Nobody else would ever print the uncertainties, because a stock seller does not HAVE uncertainties; they have a traced outline and a font. The confessions are the moat. It also escapes the trope structurally: a blueprint is the most SHAPE-forward treatment available and therefore the worst posture on the VW trade-dress question — this one solves that by dimensioning only the parts Volkswagen never made, and by using the side elevation, in which the VW roundel does not appear at all.
concept.production_notes:
Four spot inks on uncoated: one declared red, one cream, one gold, one warm near-black. Five if the wordmark appears — silver, and specify it as a FINISH (foil or metallic ink), never as grey. DO NOT sample the red off a render: flank_compare on out/r75_side.png reads the render's flank at median (196,81,67) against the photograph's (158,16,6) — it images salmon, roughly ten just-noticeable differences off. And do not average the photographs either; probe_rev71_red.py prints its own prohibition, 'the photograph's red G/R is 0.0149 .. 0.0344, a 2.3x span. DO NOT QUOTE A SINGLE FIGURE FOR IT.' Choose one red as a design ruling, record its provenance, and reconcile it against the three authored reds that currently disagree (t1_mats sRGB(196,49,36), lid_gen (159,45,22), cal_gen (214,46,30)). A flat-ink artefact can be more chromatically correct than the render currently is, and should say so out loud.

Every figure on the sheet must be generated by a script that IMPORTS the constants (t1_shell.BAY_W, BAY_CX, Z_SILL, Z_HEAD, TB_TILT_DEG, TB_WIDTH, REAR_OPEN_DEG; t1_detail.LOUV_PITCH, LOUV_N, CAP_R; build.ROUNDEL_D) and reads STATE.md — never transcribed into the artwork file. A transcribed figure goes stale silently and this project has lost revisions to exactly that. Print the generator's own commit hash in the title block.

BRAND RISK, NAMED: a cautious team will ask to delete the confessions and keep the numbers. That kills it. The confessions ARE the concept, and they are also the reason this is the one artefact in the program that a customer reads for two minutes instead of two seconds. If the owner wants only the certainties, that is a different, weaker poster and should be labelled as one.

EDITION: open edition unnumbered on A4; A1 hand-numbered in pencil, authenticated by a BLIND EMBOSS chop rather than a signature — there is no artist's hand on a render and a forged signature on CGI is embarrassing. Archive the stitched master file as the edition master: Cycles sets no seed here and the run-to-run floor is ~2.04 % of pixels moving >8 levels, so a re-render is NOT a re-print.
model_work_required: FIX THE ORTHOGRAPHIC CLIPPING — I measured it today and it blocks any elevation series. studio.views()['front'] and ['rear'] are ortho=3.55 with horizontal sensor fit, so at 1600×1100 the vertical extent is 3.55 × 1100/1600 = 2.4406 m, covering z 0.2997 to 2.7403, while the vehicle spans z 0 at the tyres to STATE.md's 'bbox top 3.132' with the lids up. out/r75_front.png proves it: 42 ink pixels on the top row and 738 on the bottom row, subject bbox y 0..1099 of 1100. Derive ortho_scale from build.py's own printed bbox with a stated margin instead of the typed 3.55, and add a verify_clone row asserting zero ink on all four borders of any ortho frame — WATCH IT GO RED at 3.55 before believing it green.

out/r75_side.png is CLEAN — I measured 0 ink on all four borders, subject bbox x 212..1457, y 111..963 of 1600×1100, so the side elevation needs no reframing. It is the only camera in the tree that is already correctly composed. (For contrast: out/r75_hero34r.png carries 492 ink pixels on its right column — the counter runs off the edge — so the rear three-quarter needs reframing before it is used anywhere.)

A LINE PASS. Nothing in this tree has ever extracted a line. Try the Grease Pencil Line Art modifier on the `side` ortho first, because it produces EDITABLE VECTOR STROKES that export to SVG, which is what a drafting sheet actually needs; Freestyle is the fallback for stroke quality; a Sobel on normal+Z passes is the cheap 2D prototype. Crease angle 30–40°, not lower — T1_body is shade-smooth and a low angle finds the subdivision. The mesh is clean enough to trust: 229,489 quad against 1,040 tri and 5,186 ngon, 0 non-manifold body edges, cutters rolled back none.

RENDER WITH T1_ALPHA=1 for the flat-fill masks, and DO NOT route it through post.py — measured, post.py takes RGBA in (colortype 6) and writes colortype 2, so optics and cut-out are mutually exclusive and the silhouette is silently destroyed. T1_ALPHA appears in zero ledgers; it has not been exercised since rev 62. Run it once and watch deliver.py's C1 go from FAILED to PASS.

FIX tex/senor.png's MISSING KEYLINE if the wordmark appears at size. SPEC §3 requires 'SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow' and the shipped asset has no dark ink at all — among pixels with alpha>200 the 1st-percentile luma is 168.3 and the fraction below luma 80 is 0.0000. lid_gen.py already authors the convention as DARKLINE = (72,26,16). script_gen.py is NOT called by build.py, so regenerate tex/senor.png by hand or the render silently keeps the old file. Cheapest visible improvement in the inventory.

NOTHING ELSE. No new geometry, no emblem work, no gloss work. This sheet ships while F191's hold stands, because the side elevation does not contain the nose roundel — only the four hubcap badges, at 1.62 mm on an A2 sheet, below any scale at which their arrangement is judgeable. Ship the elevation FIRST and say why.

verdicts.lens: ORIGINALITY — is this genuinely fresh, or a well-executed instance of something already on a thousand VW-bus products and a thousand design-nerd print shelves?
verdicts.reasoning:
I verified the two figures the concept stakes its uniqueness on, because if they were invented the whole originality case collapses. Both hold. From live `t1_shell.py` constants (`BAY_W = 0.5155`, `BAY_CX = (0.6720, 0.0470, -0.5980)`) the bays run +0.41425..+0.92975 / -0.21075..+0.30475 / -0.85575..-0.34025, so the two pillars measure exactly 109.5 mm and 129.5 mm — equal holes, unequal pillars, derivable by anyone who has the mesh and by nobody who has a traced outline. And `LEDGER_rev50.md`'s own derivation `W·sin a = (LID_X0 − LID_X1) / 1.713 → 1.2237 m` does reproduce 3.472 m at 20°, so `WIDTH = f(ANGLE)` is arithmetically true and not a rhetorical flourish. The content is real and unforgeable. That is what lifts this above workable.

What keeps it off "exceptional" is that the FORM is not fresh, and the concept's own escape argument is weaker than it thinks.

The core device — technical elevation drawing whose annotations abandon engineering nomenclature for a plain human voice, and whose whole emotional effect is the mismatch between drafting furniture and confessional language — is xkcd 1133, "Up Goer Five" (2012). That is a blueprint of a Saturn V annotated in a deliberately humble register, it is one of the most reproduced posters on the internet, and it is sold as a print. The concept does not name it. Adjacent and equally close: Giorgia Lupi and Stefanie Posavec's "Dear Data" and Lupi's "Data Humanism" manifesto, whose entire argument is that a chart should show its own imperfection and method — a decade-old, named movement; and Kate Crawford & Vladan Joler's "Anatomy of an AI System," a large-format annotated technical diagram where the prose annotations carry the argument, hanging in MoMA and the V&A. "Annotated drafting sheet with an essayistic voice" is a genre, not an invention.

Worse for the pitch: uncertainty annotation is already a DRAFTING CONVENTION. Measured-survey practice writes "VIF" (verify in field), "assumed", "NTS", "approx.", and draws unverified geometry dashed. HABS measured drawings do exactly this. So the sheet's headline subversion is a re-discovery of professional convention presented as a poetic invention — which is fine as craft and fatal as a novelty claim, because any draftsperson will recognise it in three seconds.

The visual language is also the category default. "Warm uncoated, not cyanotype blue" dodges one cliché by adopting the other: mono numerals, four spot inks, drafting furniture, six-point title block, scale bar, blind-emboss chop, pencil-numbered edition — that is the house style of Draplin-adjacent small-batch print, Field Notes, Herb Lester and roughly four hundred Etsy shops. And the grounded reality already records Dreamstime carrying "Vw Van Blueprint" as a standing stock shelf.

And the moat is misidentified. The concept says a stock seller "does not HAVE uncertainties." True, and irrelevant — a stock seller can WRITE them. Fake humility costs nothing; nobody in a restaurant checks whether 129.5 mm is real. The differentiator is therefore copywriting, which is the most forgeable layer in the stack. The genuinely unforgeable thing (the numbers) is invisible; the visible thing (the confessions) is trivially cloned. That asymmetry is the concept's central originality flaw and it is stated backwards in the pitch.

What IS original and should be protected: assigning the vehicle's own silver-leaf signwriter hand to the epistemic category of "unknowable" is a specific, non-transferable idea — the letterform on the counter fascia becomes the typeface of doubt. `WIDTH = f(ANGLE)` with an inset graph is a real beat: a dimension that is a function of a pose is a genuinely strange thing to put on a plate. "ENGINE: NONE. TRANSMISSION: SOLD." is unrepeatable because it is true of exactly one vehicle. Three good ideas inside a saturated container.

One structural problem the pitch waves at and then walks past: it claims the side elevation escapes the VW trade-dress question because the roundel is absent. On originality grounds the side elevation is the WORST choice — the split-screen T1 profile is the single most-drawn image in the entire category, and a blueprint is the most shape-forward treatment available. The conversion (counter, three apertures, propped board, louvre block) occupies a minority of the sheet while the trademarked silhouette occupies the rest. At thumbnail, on social, in a feed, this reads as "VW bus blueprint" and nothing else.
fatal_flaws: The core device has a famous, unnamed precedent: xkcd 1133 'Up Goer Five' (2012) is a technical elevation annotated in a plain, humble voice, sold as a poster, and structurally the same joke. Adjacent: Lupi & Posavec's 'Dear Data' / 'Data Humanism' (uncertainty-as-aesthetic, a named decade-old movement) and Crawford & Joler's 'Anatomy of an AI System' (large annotated technical diagram carrying an essay). Pitching this without naming them looks naive.

The 'subversion' is an existing drafting convention. Measured-survey practice already annotates uncertainty — VIF (verify in field), 'assumed', 'approx.', NTS, dashed lines for unverified geometry, HABS survey notes. The sheet re-invents professional notation and presents it as invention.

The moat is copywriting, not data. A stock seller cannot HAVE the uncertainties but can trivially WRITE them; nobody verifies 109.5 mm in a restaurant. The unforgeable layer (the numbers) is invisible; the visible layer (the confessions) is free to clone. The pitch states this backwards.

The visual language is the saturated default of the small-batch print category — warm uncoated stock, mono numerals, four spot inks, six-point title block, scale bar, blind emboss, pencil-numbered edition. It escapes cyanotype blue by landing on the Draplin/Field Notes cliché instead.

All the uncertainty is VERBAL. Nothing about the drawing LOOKS uncertain — no range bars, no dashed assumed geometry, no visual disagreement. So the originality lives entirely in text that vanishes at thumbnail, feed and A4 scale, exactly where the artefact competes.

The side elevation is the most-drawn image in the category and the most shape-forward posture on the VW trade-dress question. The conversion — the only unforgeable content — occupies a minority of the sheet area while the trademarked T1 profile occupies the rest.

The title block's '229 MESH OBJECTS · 376,383 VERTICES' imports the 3D-artist-portfolio genre. It tells the reader the subject is a render, which is the least interesting fact about the object and is the one credential every CG poster on ArtStation already claims.
improvements: MAKE THE UNCERTAINTY GRAPHIC, NOT VERBAL — this is the single biggest lift and the one move that clears Up Goer Five, whose annotations are also purely verbal. The record already holds ranges: the tail board is 38.0° ±2.3 and chord 0.7110 ±0.028 (STATE.md / F165), the lug count is a measured 48..84 bracket that probe_rev74_tread.py REFUSES to collapse. Draw those as RANGE DIMENSIONS: a dimension line with two arrowheads and a tinted band spanning the whole admissible interval, so a reader sees a 36-unit-wide grey bar where a stock plate would print '64'. A drawing where some dimensions are BANDS and some are LINES is a visual idea; a drawing where some numbers have sentences under them is a copy idea.

PRINT THE DISAGREEMENT INSTEAD OF DESCRIBING IT. The tail board is built at 38.0° and photographed at 28.0° (HANDOFF_CARRIERS §0.05, two rulers, F165 unresolved for seven revisions). Draw it TWICE — the built board solid, the photographed board ghosted at 40% — overprinted from the same hinge, with the 10° wedge between them left open and unlabelled. The reader sees two boards and understands before reading a word. A copywriter can fake a confession; they cannot fake a drawing that contradicts itself.

ADOPT REAL SURVEY NOTATION, THEN BREAK IT — three epistemic tiers, not two. Solid line + filled arrowhead = MEASURED. Dashed line + 'VIF' flag = ASSUMED BUT VERIFIABLE (the 64° hatch swing, the 12-vs-10 louvre count). Reserve the silver-leaf hand ONLY for the third class, which no convention covers: NOT RECOVERABLE FROM WHAT WE HOLD — the tail-board width with an upper bound of 590 and NO LOWER BOUND, the retired roof height. Then the hand-script means something specific rather than 'the poetic ink', and it appears perhaps four times on the sheet instead of seven, which is what makes it land.

PRINT IT ON TRANSLUCENT STOCK AS A TWO-SHEET REGISTERED PAIR. Real dyeline/diazo prints were sepia on translucent — that is the historically honest stock and it is not the kraft cliché. Ship an opaque base sheet carrying ONLY the measured layer (solid ink, hard arrowheads, no prose) and a translucent vellum overlay carrying ONLY the unmeasured layer (the brackets and the hand-script). Registered, it is the full plate; lifted, the reader physically holds the project's doubt in one hand and its knowledge in the other. Nobody in this category sells that, it is cheap, and it converts the concept's central idea from text into an object. This is the exceptional-tier move.

CUT THE CAB OFF. Crop the sheet at the B-pillar so the drawing begins at the first serving aperture and runs aft. What remains is a counter, three holes, a louvre block, a propped board and a wheel — a drawing of a taqueria, not of a Volkswagen. It removes the trademarked silhouette entirely, it makes the unforgeable content 100% of the sheet instead of 35%, and at thumbnail it stops reading as 'VW bus blueprint', which is currently its fatal social-scale failure. The 109.5 / 129.5 pillar pair survives the crop and becomes the sheet's hero figure rather than a detail.

SHIP IT AS AN INCOMPLETE SHEET SET, NOT A POSTER. Number it 'SHEET 1 OF 4' and print SHEET 3 — REAR ELEVATION as an almost entirely blank sheet carrying its border, its title block, and one line: 'NOT ISSUED. NO PHOTOGRAPH OF THIS FACE EXISTS.' A blank survey sheet that explains its own blankness has no precedent I can name in this category, costs one ink, and is the piece people will actually photograph. It also converts the program's real constraint — three usable frames of the folk-art livery, five byte-identical duplicate pairs — into the artefact's content.

REPLACE THE TITLE-BLOCK VANITY STATS WITH A SURVEY TALLY. Delete '229 MESH OBJECTS · 376,383 VERTICES'. Put in their place: 'DIMENSIONS TAKEN: 34 · DIMENSIONS REFUSED: 9 · SOURCE FRAMES: 3 · SURVEY REV 76'. That last pair of numbers IS the poster, compressed into six point, and it is the only line on the sheet a stock seller could not write without doing the work first.

NAME THE PRECEDENT IN THE PITCH DOCUMENT. Say out loud: 'this is Up Goer Five's device applied to a real measured survey, and the difference is that our uncertainties are checkable and drawn rather than written.' Stating it pre-empts the obvious objection and forces the team to defend the delta — which, after the improvements above, is defensible.

verdicts.lens: PRODUCIBILITY AND FIDELITY — can this be made from THIS asset, given failing gates, an unproven large-format chain, and an emblem rejected nine times?
verdicts.reasoning:
I checked this concept against the machine rather than the prose, and it survives better than anything I expected.

WHAT EARNS IT. Every dimension it prints reproduces exactly, in ~1s, importing t1_shell/t1_detail without bpy: `pillar1 109.5 mm` / `pillar2 129.5 mm` (from BAY_CX (0.672, 0.047, -0.598), BAY_W 0.5155) — the concept's own thesis figure, exact; aperture 0.5155 x (1.7750-1.3720) = 515.5 x 403.0; TB 38.0 / 0.711 / 0.550; REAR_OPEN_DEG 64.0; LOUV_N 10, LOUV_PITCH 0.021111. And `LID_W = (LID_X0 - LID_X1) / LID_ASPECT / math.sin(math.radians(LID_OPEN_DEG))` really is a function of the angle: I evaluated it at 20/40/76/90 deg -> 3.4717 / 1.8473 / 1.2237 / 1.1874. The "WIDTH = f(ANGLE)" inset graph is not a conceit; it is the live source line.

THE CAMERA CHOICE IS MEASURED-CORRECT AND I CONFIRMED IT INDEPENDENTLY. Border-ink on the four r75 frames: `r75_side.png 1600x1100 bbox x 212..1458 y 111..963 | border ink T0 B0 L0 R0`; `r75_front.png ... y 0..1099 | T42 B738`; `r75_hero34f.png | B265 L563`; `r75_hero34r.png | R493`. The side camera is ortho 5.90 (vertical extent 5.90*1100/1600 = 4.056 m about z=1.52, i.e. z -0.51..3.55, which contains STATE.md's `bbox top 3.132`), and it is the ONLY correctly-framed camera in the tree. The concept picked it for the right reason.

IT ALSO SOLVES THE PROJECT'S BLOCKING PROBLEM STRUCTURALLY. The side elevation does not contain the nose roundel, so this ships while F191 ("Keep holding - fix the emblem first") stands, and while F314 keeps the weight closed. It needs zero new geometry. That is rare and it is the strongest producibility argument in the concept.

WHY NOT EXCEPTIONAL. Three things break, and one of them is at the centre of the image.

(1) THE HERO GRAPHIC CANNOT BE DRAWN IN THE VIEW IT CHOSE. The concept's best line is `[ 550 ] chosen, not measured ... Upper bound 590. Lower bound: none` annotated across the propped tail board. But TB_WIDTH is the Y extent, and HANDOFF_CARRIERS §0.05's own refutation of build item 1 says it in terms: "the side elevation looks exactly along the board's plane, so the face is invisible by construction, not by omission." In true side ortho the board is an edge-on blade of thickness TB_T (~22 mm) at 38 deg. The dimension the sheet's best confession attaches to has nothing to attach to. The concept does not mention this.

(2) THE TWO-INK TAXONOMY IS WRONG, AND ITS OWN FIRST THREE NUMBERS PROVE IT. It has MEASURED (solid mono) and POSED (bracketed script). The tree has more classes than that, and STATE.md disagrees with itself on two of the concept's headline figures. RAKE: `rake 17.75 mm/m (locked 17.75)` and `rake coefficient applied | 17.8 mm/m` and `roof line slope (measured off the mesh) | -18.1 mm/m` — the concept prints 17.75 in the MEASURED ink, but 17.75 is a locked INPUT and the measurement is -18.1, differing in magnitude and in sign convention. TRACK: the concept prints `1369 / 1359`, which is the table row `track front | 1.3690 | 1.3690 | +0.0 mm ok`, while the same file's verify block reads `measured TRACK_F=1.3713 TRACK_R=1.3613` — 2.3 mm apart, two rulers in one machine-written file. A plate whose entire authority is provenance cannot misfile provenance on its opening line.

(3) GENERATING FROM THE CONSTANTS REPRODUCES A MEASURED 76-83 mm ARTWORK ERROR. The concept mandates a generator that imports the constants. The wordmark's placement constant is `SCR = dict(x0=0.784, x1=-0.494, z0=0.4453, z1=0.9896)`. flank_compare on out/r75_side.png prints live: "best integer shift (-16, -10) cells = (+76.2 mm in x, -47.6 mm in z)" and, by a route sharing no step with it, "SCR's own x extents are +83 / +80 mm aft of flank_X(LOCKUP), and the cream/red differential puts the ink top +61.1 mm high." On A2 at roughly 1:7.8 that is ~10 mm of visible misplacement on 31% of the vehicle's length — and a drafting plate INVITES measurement in a way a photoreal render does not, so the format makes this defect worse than it currently is.

AND THE TECHNIQUE HAS NO PRIOR ART HERE. `grep -rn "line_art|LineArt|freestyle|Freestyle|grease|GPENCIL" --include=*.py .` returns nothing. Zero. The deliverable is line-only, and no line has ever been extracted from this asset. svgraster.py's own header records "This machine has no cairosvg / svglib / skia". The concept lists this as one bullet; it is a whole-revision item with a real chance of returning nothing.

The wordmark asset is also unshippable as flat art as it stands: I measured tex/senor.png (4096x1738 RGBA) — among alpha>200 pixels, min luma 146, 1st percentile 165.7, `frac<80 = 0.0000`. There is no dark ink in it at all, against SPEC §3's "SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow". Silver flat-fill on flat red in a four-ink print with no keyline will nearly vanish.

CEILING ON MY OWN READING: I ran no Blender, no build, no render. Everything above is off the five frames already in out/, pure-python probes, and source constants. I did not measure the `rear` camera's framing (only front, side, hero34f, hero34r), and I could not verify whether the pip bpy wheel exposes Grease Pencil SVG export at all — that is the single largest unknown in the whole proposal and it is unresolved.
fatal_flaws: THE HERO GRAPHIC IS UNDRAWABLE IN THE CHOSEN VIEW. The sheet's best confession — '[ 550 ] chosen, not measured' — is annotated across the propped tail board in a TRUE SIDE ORTHOGRAPHIC elevation, where TB_WIDTH is the Y extent and the board is edge-on by construction. HANDOFF_CARRIERS §0.05 states it verbatim as the refutation of its own build item 1: 'the side elevation looks exactly along the board's plane, so the face is invisible by construction, not by omission.' The dimension has no extension lines to attach to. Unaddressed in the concept.

THE PROVENANCE TAXONOMY IS WRONG ON ITS OPENING NUMBERS. Two inks (measured / posed) cannot express this tree. '17.75 mm/m RAKE' is printed as MEASURED; STATE.md carries 'rake 17.75 mm/m (locked 17.75)', 'rake coefficient applied | 17.8 mm/m' AND 'roof line slope (measured off the mesh) | -18.1 mm/m' — a locked input, an applied coefficient, and a measurement that disagrees in magnitude and sign convention. '1369 / 1359 TRACK' is likewise the SPEC row, while the same file's verify block reads 'measured TRACK_F=1.3713 TRACK_R=1.3613'. The sheet's entire moral authority is provenance.

THE MANDATED GENERATOR REPRODUCES A MEASURED 76-83 mm ARTWORK MISPLACEMENT. build.SCR = dict(x0=0.784, x1=-0.494, ...) is the wordmark's placement, and flank_compare on out/r75_side.png prints 'best integer shift (-16, -10) cells = (+76.2 mm in x, -47.6 mm in z)' plus an independent cross-check 'SCR's own x extents are +83 / +80 mm aft of flank_X(LOCKUP) ... ink top +61.1 mm high'. ~10 mm on A2, on the largest graphic on the flank, on a document format that invites measurement.

THE RENDERING TECHNIQUE HAS ZERO PRIOR ART IN THIS TREE AND IS SCOPED AS ONE BULLET. grep for line_art|LineArt|freestyle|Freestyle|grease|GPENCIL across all .py returns NOTHING. No line has ever been extracted from this asset; the only vector ever committed is vw_canonical_2019.svg, and svgraster.py's header records 'This machine has no cairosvg / svglib / skia'. Whether the pip bpy wheel even exposes Grease Pencil SVG export is unverified. The deliverable is line-only, so this is not a bullet — it is the artefact, and it can return nothing.

THE WORDMARK ASSET HAS NO DARK INK AND CANNOT SURVIVE FLAT-INK PRINTING. Measured on tex/senor.png (4096x1738 RGBA): among alpha>200 pixels, min luma 146, 1st-percentile 165.7, frac below luma 80 = 0.0000. SPEC §3 requires 'SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow'. Silver flat-fill on flat red with no keyline nearly disappears. script_gen.py is not called by build.py, so this is a hand-regeneration step with no guard on it.
improvements: TURN FLAW 1 INTO THE SHEET'S BEST LINE. Keep the board edge-on in the main elevation and run a leader to a small inset (a plan or rear ortho), and rewrite the annotation so it is true of the drawing the reader is holding: '[ 550 ] chosen, not measured. THIS ELEVATION CANNOT SEE IT — the board's plane contains the width, so it projects only through parallax. Upper bound 590. Lower bound: none.' A confession about the drawing in front of you is far stronger than one about a photograph you cannot check. CAVEAT: the inset needs a second camera and I did not measure `rear`'s framing; front is ortho 3.55 and clips (T42/B738), so re-derive the inset's ortho_scale from build.py's printed bbox, do not inherit 3.55.

REPLACE TWO INKS WITH FOUR, AND MAKE THE FOURTH THE PUNCHLINE. (1) MEASURED off the mesh; (2) DECLARED-then-VERIFIED (wheelbase, tyre, aperture — the input was locked and the mesh agrees); (3) POSED (TB_WIDTH, REAR_OPEN_DEG 64.0, TREAD_LUGS 64); (4) DISAGREES WITH ITSELF. Put RAKE in class 4 and print it in full: '17.75 locked · 17.8 applied · -18.1 measured off the mesh · sign convention unreconciled'. Put TRACK there too: '1369 nominal / 1371.3 measured'. Class 4 is funnier, more honest, unforgeable, and costs nothing — and it fixes the taxonomy error rather than hiding it.

DO NOT TRACE THE ARTWORK OFF THE RENDER OR PLACE IT FROM build.SCR. Composite it from the masters, which are already 3-4K: swirl.png and swirl_b.png 4096², lidmural/lidsign 4096x2476, senor 4096x1738, calidad 3072x2267. Position them where the photograph-calibrated map puts them, not where the build does, and then PRINT THE DISCREPANCY as a dimension in class 4: 'WORDMARK: as built, +83 mm aft and +61 mm high of the calibrated position. Drawn where the photograph puts it.' That converts flaw 3 into the sheet's second-best line and applies the concept's thesis to itself.

SCOPE THE LINE PASS AS A ~1s GO/NO-GO BEFORE ANY OTHER WORK, WITH A NAMED FALLBACK. Step 1: check whether the pip bpy wheel exposes the GP_LINEART modifier and bpy.ops.wm.gpencil_export_svg at all. If yes, editable vector is live. If no, the vector route is DEAD on this machine and the honest fallback — which needs no new render path — is a raster line pass: Sobel/Laplacian over normal + Z + object-index AOVs from the existing side camera, thresholded to a 1-bit key. State in the proposal WHICH of the two the sheet ships on. Do not promise editable vector before that check returns.

SHIP THE ORTHO-BORDER GUARD FIRST, AND NAME THE FRAMES IT ALREADY REDS. It is a watched kill for free: I measured, live, r75_front T42/B738, r75_hero34f L563/B265, r75_hero34r R493, r75_side 0/0/0/0. So a verify_clone row asserting zero ink on all four borders of an ortho frame goes RED on three of four existing frames on day one (rule 3 satisfied without inventing a defect), and it then protects the one camera this concept entirely depends on from being silently reframed by a later revision. Derive ortho_scale from build.py's own printed bbox plus a stated margin instead of the typed 3.55.

ADD THE KEYLINE AND GUARD IT IN THE SAME EDIT. lid_gen.py already authors the convention as DARKLINE = (72,26,16). Regenerate tex/senor.png by hand — script_gen.py is NOT called by build.py, so the render silently keeps the old file otherwise — and add one verify_clone row asserting a non-zero fraction of ink below luma 80 among alpha>200 pixels. Watch it go red on the shipped asset first: it will, at exactly 0.0000. This is the cheapest visible improvement in the whole inventory and this concept is the artefact that most needs it.

PRINT THE GENERATOR'S PROVENANCE AS A DIMENSION, NOT A FOOTNOTE, AND GUARD THE AGREEMENT. The title block already carries '229 MESH OBJECTS · 376,383 VERTICES · 0 NON-MANIFOLD BODY EDGES'. Add 'FIGURES GENERATED <commit> · STATE.md <commit> · FRAME out/rNN_side.png' and add a row asserting the three agree. At rev 75 STATE.md was written at commit 8bbe354 while HEAD was elsewhere — a sheet printed from a stale STATE.md is precisely the failure this sheet is about, and it would be invisible without the row.

DROP A1 FROM THE PROPOSAL UNTIL A PROVING RUN EXISTS, AND NAME THE UNNAMED RISK. A1 at 200 dpi wants 4677 px; the only >3840 render in the record is HANDOFF_rev15's 4320x2880 through hero.py's PAD chain, not hq_render.py's MARGIN chain, and no frame from either survives because out/ is untracked. Separately: hq_render.py contains zero occurrences of T1_FX, while hero.py forces T1_FX=0 with the docstring 'Per-strip optics band at the seams'. For THIS sheet the fix is trivial and should be stated as a positive: render the master with T1_FX=0 and skip post.py entirely — a line-and-flat-fill plate wants no bloom, no CA, no vignette and no grain, and post.py would destroy the alpha anyway (measured: RGBA in, colortype 2 out).

IF T1_ALPHA IS USED FOR THE FLAT-FILL MASKS, TREAT IT AS UNEXERCISED, NOT AS WORKING. grep across every LEDGER_rev*.md returns no occurrence of T1_ALPHA — it has not been run since F159 closed it at rev 62. Budget one render to exercise it and watch deliver.py's C1 go from FAILED to PASS before the mask pipeline is assumed. Do not route that frame through post.py.

verdicts.lens: Emotional resonance, brand fit and IP exposure
verdicts.reasoning:
I checked the two claims the concept's credibility rests on and both hold. `t1_shell.py` gives `BAY_W = 0.5155  # equal, measured` and `BAY_CX = (0.6720, 0.0470, -0.5980)`; computed, the pillars are 109.5 mm and 129.5 mm — the asymmetry is real and is exactly the kind of fact no traced stock drawing has. And `LEDGER_rev50.md` carries `W·sin a = (LID_X0 − LID_X1) / 1.713 ... 1.2237 m`, from which the 20° figure recomputes as 3.472 m. So `WIDTH = f(ANGLE)` is a true, verifiable absurdity and it is the single best idea in the concept.

But on MY axis the concept misallocates its emotion. It has THREE registers wearing two inks:
(1) measured facts about the object — cold, credible, fine;
(2) BIOGRAPHY of the object — `ENGINE: NONE. TRANSMISSION: SOLD.` / `1963, stamped on an empty plate` / arrived missing three windows. This is Tacombi's own origin myth, it is warm, it is unfakeable, and it is where every ounce of the feeling lives;
(3) EPISTEMIC LIMITS OF A BLENDER PROJECT — `[550] chosen, not measured`, `[64°] a pose. No photograph we hold shows it open`, the 48–84 lug bracket. The screener calls these "the moat". They are not. They are inside baseball about a modelling exercise the buyer does not know exists, and the "we hold" is the render team's voice, not the vehicle's.

The register-3 problem is worse than dilution, it is a brand-fit hazard: TACOMBI OWNS THIS BUS. A poster in which the company confesses it could not establish the width of a board on its own van invites one reply — "it's parked in Playa, go and measure it." Humility only reads as humility when measurement was genuinely impossible. Here it was impossible only for a team working from seven photographs, and the poster never says so. So the emotional promise ("intimacy with a machine's humility") is delivered to the maker and withheld from the customer.

IP: the concept's defence — "it dimensions only the parts Volkswagen never made" — is contradicted by its own headline dimension list four paragraphs earlier: `2400 WHEELBASE`, `1369/1359 TRACK`, `664.9 TYRE`, `17.75 mm/m RAKE` are all factory VW figures, and the title block reads `TYPE 2`, which is VW's own model designation. Worse than depiction: a dimensioned elevation in a ruled title block is the one form that reads as a FACTORY DOCUMENT, i.e. it flirts with implied VW authorship rather than mere reference. The side-elevation choice (no nose roundel) is a genuinely smart structural dodge and I credit it, but the sheet then reintroduces VW at the two places that matter most for endorsement confusion — the naming and the specs — and leaves two hubcap roundels in the drawing besides.

Brand fit is otherwise better than I expected. Tacombi's shop voice is deadpan leisure-outfitter catalogue — "purpose-built, all-weather knit beanie", "Monument T", "Seaside Expo Tote" — and a spec plate sits inside that register comfortably. But that voice is deadpan-WARM; a 0.20 mm-keyline drafting sheet with epistemology in the margins is deadpan-CLINICAL, and it is a poster for design-literate adults, not for the family that just ate at the counter. That narrows the audience considerably for a restaurant brand.

Two production points that bear on feeling rather than craft: setting the confessions as hand-lettered silver-leaf script at a 40 % tint is both a metallic-ink impossibility (metallics do not tint or screen) and a legibility failure at annotation size — and it spends the silver, which the sheet has already correctly reserved as the wordmark's FINISH. And the line people will actually photograph is not `[550] chosen, not measured`; it is `ENGINE: NONE. TRANSMISSION: SOLD.` — four words that contain the whole company — which the concept buries seventh in a list.

Strong, not exceptional: the device is fresh, one line in it is a real brand asset, and it escapes the saturated blueprint shelf structurally. It is one re-allocation away from being the best thing in the program.
fatal_flaws: THE EMOTIONAL PAYLOAD IS IN THE WRONG REGISTER. The lines that move a stranger are biographical (ENGINE: NONE / TRANSMISSION: SOLD; 1963 on an empty plate; arrived missing three windows) and they are outnumbered and outranked by lines about a 3D modelling project's uncertainty (parallax bounds, a 48–84 lug bracket, 'no photograph we hold'). The concept's own hero example — '[ 550 ] chosen, not measured' — is the least legible of the seven to anyone outside this repository.

'WE HOLD' IS THE RENDER TEAM'S VOICE, NOT TACOMBI'S, AND THE POSTER NEVER ESTABLISHES WHY MEASUREMENT WAS IMPOSSIBLE. Tacombi owns the vehicle. Unless the sheet declares itself a survey FROM PHOTOGRAPHS of a specific configuration on a specific day, every uncertainty reads as an admission that nobody walked out with a tape measure. Charm inverts into carelessness.

THE IP DEFENCE CONTRADICTS THE ARTWORK. 'It dimensions only the parts Volkswagen never made' is stated in why_not_derivative while the_image leads with WHEELBASE 2400, TRACK 1369/1359, TYRE 664.9 and RAKE 17.75 mm/m — all factory VW dimensions — and stamps TYPE 2 in the title block. A ruled, dimensioned elevation of a VW carrying VW's own model designation is the single form most likely to be read as a factory-issued document, which is an endorsement-confusion risk, not merely a depiction one.

THE SECOND INK CARRIES TWO INCOMPATIBLE MEANINGS. The bracket/tint/script register is defined as 'unmeasured', but 'Arrived missing three windows' is not an uncertainty — it is a source-grade historical fact (and SPEC grades the window-to-hatch link E, an inference, not S). A sheet whose entire thesis is provenance discipline breaks its own notation on its warmest line.

SILVER-LEAF SCRIPT AT A 40 % TINT IS NOT PRINTABLE AND NOT READABLE. Metallic inks do not tint or screen usefully; the concept has also already reserved silver as the wordmark's FINISH, so the annotation voice cannibalises the one material moment on the sheet.
