THE AUDIENCE IS NARROWER THAN THE BRAND. This is an object for design-literate adults; nothing in it reaches the family at the counter. That is legitimate for one tier but should be stated, and the program should not treat this as the flagship emotional artefact.
improvements: INVERT THE HIERARCHY: make BIOGRAPHY the hero register and epistemology the footnote. Set 'ENGINE: NONE. TRANSMISSION: SOLD.' as the largest annotation on the sheet, on its own leader line into the empty engine bay, at display size. It is Tacombi's origin in four words, it is source-graded from the company's own telling ('The engine was scrapped, transmission sold, seats swapped for cooking equipment, and the roof was reeled back'), it is unfakeable by any stock seller, and it contains zero VW property. That single line is the poster; the drafting furniture is its setting.

ADD ONE SENTENCE THAT LICENCES EVERY CONFESSION, in the title block, and the whole brand-fit objection dissolves: 'Surveyed from seven photographs. Playa del Carmen livery, as it stood. Nothing measured on the vehicle.' Now '[64°] a pose — no photograph we hold shows it open' is archaeology of a configuration that no longer exists (the Nolita bus carries no folk art, no script), not an admission of laziness. This is the cheapest and highest-leverage change in the list.

STRIP EVERY FACTORY VW DIMENSION AND THE VW NAMING, and let the sheet dimension the CONVERSION only — the three apertures, the 109.5 | 129.5 pillars, the counter cantilever and its radiused tail, the tail board's 38.0°, the louvre block, the drip-rail bulb pitch, the bobble-fringe pitch. Delete WHEELBASE, TRACK, TYRE and RAKE; delete 'TYPE 2'. Retitle: 'UNIT 01 · TACOMBI · PLAYA DEL CARMEN · 2006 —'. The drawing then describes a taco stand that happens to be built on a van, which is simultaneously better IP posture, better brand ownership, and a stronger anti-derivative claim than the current version can make.

KEEP 109.5 | 129.5 AS THE TECHNICAL HERO and annotate WHY it is there: 'Three equal holes. Two unequal pillars. Nobody who traces this gets that right.' I recomputed it off t1_shell.py's own BAY_W and BAY_CX and it lands exactly. It is the one figure that proves the sheet was measured rather than styled, and it currently sits unremarked in a list of eight.

SPLIT THE SECOND INK INTO TWO CLEAN NOTATIONS instead of one overloaded one. Bracketed script = 'this is a pose we chose' (the 550, the 64°, the 64 lugs). A different, unbracketed mark — a small dagger, or a rule with an open circle terminal — = 'this is what happened to the bus' (engine, windows, 1963). Three registers, three notations, and print the key. The key itself becomes a piece of the design.

KILL THE SILVER FOR ANNOTATION. Set all confessions in the warm near-black at a lighter weight and a slightly larger size than the mono; keep the signwriter's hand as the LETTERFORM, not as a metallic. Spend the silver on exactly one thing: the 'Señor Tacombi' wordmark if it appears at all. And if it does, regenerate tex/senor.png first — I confirmed the shipped asset has no dark ink whatever among pixels with alpha>200 (1st-percentile luma 168.3, fraction below luma 80 = 0.0000), against SPEC §3's requirement of 'SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow'. Silver on cream with no keyline will vanish.

PROMOTE 'WIDTH = f(ANGLE)' FROM DETAIL TO SECOND HERO. I verified it: 1.2237 m at 76° recomputes to 3.472 m at 20°, exactly as claimed. A dimension that is a function of a pose is the funniest and most human thing on the sheet — the drawing catching itself. Give the inset graph real estate, put the two endpoints on it as labelled points, and caption it in one line: 'How wide the board is depends on how open it is. That is a fact about photographs, not about the board.'

CHANGE THE SOCIAL LAUNCH POST. Lead with ENGINE: NONE, not with a bracketed width. Five posts, in this order: engine/transmission; 1963 on an empty plate; three missing windows; 109.5 | 129.5; WIDTH = f(ANGLE). The first three need no explanation and belong to Tacombi; the last two reward the people who lean in.

GIVE THE A4 INSERT ITS OWN JOB rather than being a reduced A2. Five biographical lines only, no epistemology, no drafting furniture beyond a scale bar — this is the version that goes home with a family, and it should be readable in eight seconds. Reserve all register-3 material for the A2/A1, where a reader has two minutes.

IF THE OWNER ASKS TO DELETE THE CONFESSIONS, DO NOT DEFEND ALL OF THEM — defend register 2 and concede register 3. The production note currently treats every confession as load-bearing and threatens that removal 'kills it'. That is the wrong hill: the biography must survive, the parallax bounds are negotiable, and offering that trade voluntarily is what will get the biography kept.

audited_finalists.title: PAPEL DE GRASA — The sheet that lights up while you eat

concept.title: PAPEL DE GRASA — The sheet that lights up while you eat
concept.one_line: Deli paper printed on both faces in perfect back-to-front register: the bus dark and shut on top, the bus lit and open underneath — and the oil from your taco turns the paper translucent so the lights come on in the shape of where you ate.
concept.the_image:
A 305 × 305 mm square of natural-kraft greaseproof. 

TOP FACE, ONE INK, dark maroon (the folk art's own dark ink, ~#501010), coarse flexo line work, no halftones, no fills over ~15% coverage. A true orthographic side elevation of the bus at 1:14 — 290 mm long, so it runs almost the full sheet, floating with 8 mm of air top and bottom. The bus is SHUT and DARK: roof lid down, counter drawn as a single closed horizontal, the three serving apertures as empty outlined rectangles, the bulb string drawn as an unlit bead chain — small open circles on a hairline. Only the three largest folk-art masses are drawn, in outline, nothing shaded. Tiny type along the bottom edge, 5 pt, one line, no logo: *Playa del Carmen · 1963 · 4,065 mm*. It looks like a closed shop. On dry paper that is the entire design and it is deliberately a bit austere, a bit dull.

REVERSE FACE, ONE INK, warm amber-gold, printed in mirror so it registers back-to-front within ±1.5 mm. It carries ONLY the light: every bulb as a filled disc with a soft halo; the three apertures filled solid amber; the mural lid's eleven flowers as solid amber shapes standing UP where the top face shows the lid down; a spill of amber under the counter line. Nothing structural — no outline, no body, no wheels. On a dry sheet this face is invisible from the top.

THEN THE FOOD ARRIVES. Grease wicks outward from wherever the taco sits. Where the paper saturates it goes translucent and the amber blooms through the maroon line work — bulbs igniting one at a time along the roof, the hatches opening into light, the flowers rising out of the closed lid. The reveal spreads for the length of the meal and stops wherever you stopped eating. Every sheet is a different photograph of a different lunch. You cannot make two the same and you cannot make it happen on purpose.
concept.emotional_claim: Delight first — an actual gasp from a seven-year-old, and a slower one from the adult opposite who works out what is happening. Then a small, good ache: to see it you had to ruin it. It is a magic trick that costs less than a cent and cannot be replicated at home, and it makes the customer a collaborator — the image is finished by the meal. It also lands the brand's real proposition without a word of copy: the bus opens and lights up when there is food. That is what the object DOES, expressed as a physical property of the paper rather than as a claim.
formats: 305 × 305 mm DELI SHEET on 40–45 gsm natural greaseproof/glassine, food-contact, low-migration inks both faces. Grammage matters: heavier than ~50 gsm and the oil does not carry the reverse image through fast enough; lighter than ~35 gsm and it tears under a wet taco. This is the primary unit and it is given away, never sold.
400 × 400 mm TRAY LINER, same artwork scaled, for sit-down locations — bigger sheet, more real estate for the bloom to travel across, and it survives a whole plate rather than one taco.

#10 GREASE-RESISTANT BAG, the same two-face trick on the front panel only, so the reveal happens in the customer's hand on the walk home. Lower reveal reliability (less contact area) — treat as a bonus, not the promise.

VELLUM EDITION, 305 × 305 mm on 110 gsm translucent vellum, screen-printed both faces, sold flat in a glassine envelope with a small brass clip so it can be hung in a window. Backlit by a window it shows the lit state permanently. This is the version for people who want the image without destroying it — and it quietly sells the trick to anyone who has not eaten with it.
NAPKIN, 1-colour top face only, no reverse — do NOT run the trick on napkins. Napkins get used on faces. The trick belongs on the surface the food sits on.
concept.why_not_derivative: There is no VW-bus merchandise anywhere that is designed to be destroyed. Every sticker, tee, poster and print in the category is engineered for permanence; this one only completes when it is soiled, and its final composition is authored by an act of eating. It is also the only piece in this whole program that is native to the actual business — a taqueria's highest-volume printed object is greaseproof, and it is the one substrate a poster studio never touches. Trade-dress and trademark posture is the best available: one-ink line art at 1:14 on a side elevation, so the VW roundel is not in frame at all, the nose is edge-on, and the artefact is given away rather than sold. It contradicts nothing in F18 and IS NOT OFFERED AS F18 — F18 is a die-cut vinyl keepsake, locked to 'cartoon with rendered depth', for children to keep. This is the opposite artefact: paper, ephemeral, and it does not survive the meal. Ship them as a pair and they argue with each other productively.
concept.production_notes: THE PHYSICS IS THE RISK AND IT MUST BE TESTED BEFORE ANY DESIGN IS APPROVED. Greaseproof and glassine both go translucent under oil — that part is ordinary — but three things are unverified and only a physical test settles them: (1) whether amber ink on the reverse reads through a PARTIALLY saturated sheet or only a fully soaked one; (2) whether the top-face dark ink migrates or smears once wetted; (3) back-to-front registration tolerance on a web press, which is the whole trick — at 1:14 a bulb is roughly 1.5 mm and a 3 mm misregister puts every light off the roofline. Buy the paper, hand-screen ten test sheets, and put real food on them in week one. If registration cannot hold ±1.5 mm, the fallback that still works: abandon fine registration entirely and print the reverse as LOOSE AMBER FIELDS (a band along the roofline, three rectangles behind the apertures) that only need to land within ±6 mm. The trick survives; the precision does not. Reduction is measured, not guessed: folk_gen.py's own component census gives `COMP_TOP = {1: 47.8, 2: 73.7, 3: 84.4, 5: 87.8, 10: 93.5}` and a histogram in which 48 of the 66 gold components carry 2.29% of the ink — so drawing only the largest three masses reproduces 84.4% of the read at a fraction of the line count, which is exactly what a coarse one-ink flexo job needs. Inks must be food-contact compliant and low-migration; this is a regulated substrate, not a poster. Do NOT put the wordmark on the top face — the sheet is more interesting anonymous, and the reveal is the signature.
model_work_required: A LINE PASS. Nothing in this tree produces vector or line art — the only .svg ever committed is `vw_canonical_2019.svg`, which the register grades a DIFFERENT OBJECT. Try the Grease Pencil Line Art modifier on the orthographic `side` view first: it produces EDITABLE VECTOR STROKES that export to SVG, which is exactly what flexo plates and screen positives want. The mesh is clean enough to trust it — STATE.md reads `non-manifold edges (body) | 0` and 229,489 quads against 1,040 tris. Fallback: Freestyle at a 30–40° crease angle, or a Sobel on the normal/Z passes.

THE BULB STRING MUST BE SEPARABLE FROM THE VEHICLE. It is currently collapsed into one object — t1_detail.py does `ob = join([ob, flex], "bulb_string")` — and the reverse-face artwork is nothing BUT the bulbs. Keep the per-bulb objects addressable behind an ablation so nothing regresses, or trace the path by hand off the render.

THE SHUT STATE HAS NEVER BEEN BUILT OR LOOKED AT IN 76 REVISIONS, and the top face is the shut bus. Worse, it is BLOCKED BY A REAL DEFECT: t1_shell.py computes `LID_W = (LID_X0 - LID_X1) / LID_ASPECT / math.sin(math.radians(LID_OPEN_DEG))`, so the lid's WIDTH is coupled to its angle as 1/sin — a naive angle sweep inflates the mural board past the length of the bus and divides by zero at 0°. Freeze LID_W at its shipped value behind `T1_LID_WCOUPLE`, add a guard that the panel's width does not move when the angle does, and WATCH IT FAIL on the coupled build first.

THE MURAL LID ASSET IS CROPPED. F74(a) is open and correct: `tex/lidmural.png` is cut off at the bottom, flowers sliced mid-bloom, yellow side columns truncated, where ref_side.jpg shows a board framed on all four sides. The reverse face draws the flowers rising out of the lid, so this must be repaired in lid_gen.py and REGENERATED BY HAND — lid_gen.py is not called by build.py, so a stale texture ships silently.

NOT MODEL WORK BUT ADJACENT AND FREE: F144 records that the render's bulbs "READ AS PEARLS, NOT LIGHTS". On this artefact the paper does the glow, so the 2D piece is correct before the 3D is — which is a reason to ship it early rather than a reason to wait.

verdicts.lens: ORIGINALITY — is this genuinely fresh, or a well-executed instance of an existing genre? Judged only on novelty of the idea and the visible artefact, not on feasibility, brand fit or execution quality.
verdicts.reasoning:
The axis inversion is real and I cannot name a competitor doing it: every VW-bus artefact in the surveyed market is engineered for permanence, and this one only completes when destroyed. The substrate nativity is the strongest originality claim in the piece — greaseproof is the taqueria's own highest-volume printed object, and no poster studio touches it. And the semantic lock is the good kind: grease means food, food means the bus is trading, so the physics IS the message rather than a gimmick bolted to it. That is above competent.

But the SCREENER OVERSTATES IT, and the overstatement is in the comparison set. "No VW-bus merchandise is designed to be destroyed" is true and irrelevant — the real prior art is not VW merch, it is REVEAL-MECHANIC ADVERTISING, which is a crowded, awarded genre, and the brief names none of it. Closest siblings, in descending order of proximity: (a) BEER COASTERS that reveal a printed message as condensation from the glass makes the board translucent — same substrate class, same absorbency physics, same hospitality setting, same "the product you ordered develops the image" logic; (b) GREASE-REVEAL FAST-FOOD WRAPPERS, which are an established burger/fried-chicken campaign device using exactly this oil-translucency effect; (c) RAIN-ACTIVATED STREET WORK (Rainworks and the Seoul rain murals) and wet-reveal umbrellas, which established liquid-as-developer as a mass idiom a decade ago; (d) THERMOCHROMIC drinks packaging, the same reveal grammar on a different trigger; and (e) — closest emotionally, and the brief's own audience makes it dangerous — CHILDREN'S DINNERWARE WITH A HIDDEN PICTURE UNDER THE FOOD, a mass-market product built on precisely "eat and the image appears." A seven-year-old at the table may have met that mechanic before breakfast.

Worse for the lens: the part of this artefact that MOST people will actually see is the most derivative part. Over ninety percent of sheets get stacked, handed over, or eaten off lightly — so the dry state is the design, and the dry state is a one-ink orthographic side elevation in line work. The grounded market survey names exactly that as two saturated stock categories, MINIMAL LINE ART ("a vintage minimalist line drawing style", "trace monotone and black lines") and BLUEPRINT/TECHNICAL (Dreamstime carries a standing "Vw Van Blueprint" category). The brief concedes it is "deliberately a bit austere, a bit dull" without noticing that austere-technical-line-bus is the trope. And the reveal state is warm amber glow, which is the category's dominant nostalgic register — the sunset-and-bulbs read the same survey documents at length. So the concept's originality is concentrated entirely in the TRANSITION, and both endpoints sit on trope.

The single most original-sounding claim is also the least supported: "every sheet is a different photograph of a different lunch." One taco on a sheet makes one roughly circular blob. A blob is not a composition, and twenty blobs are not twenty different artworks. If the reveal is in practice a wet patch with some bulbs inside it, the piece collapses from participatory generative object down to the known grease-reveal wrapper, which is where the prior art already is. Nothing in the concept directs, structures or authors the spread — it merely hopes the spread is interesting.

Strong, not exceptional: fresh for this brand, genuinely fresh in this category, conceptually locked — but the mechanic has multiple nameable precedents the brief does not engage, and both the dry and revealed images land on documented tropes.
fatal_flaws: THE REVEAL MECHANIC IS A KNOWN ADVERTISING GENRE AND THE BRIEF NAMES NO PRIOR ART. Condensation-reveal beer coasters, grease-reveal fast-food wrappers, rain-activated street work, thermochromic packaging and hidden-picture children's plates are all the same idea — an absorbent or reactive substrate developed by the thing the customer consumed. The 'why_not_derivative' section defends against VW-bus merch, which is the wrong comparison set, so the concept has never actually been tested against its real competitors.

THE DRY STATE — WHICH IS WHAT MOST PEOPLE WILL SEE — IS THE MOST SATURATED TROPE IN THE CATEGORY. A one-ink orthographic side elevation in line work is simultaneously the 'MINIMAL LINE ART' and 'BLUEPRINT/TECHNICAL' stock categories the market survey documents (Dreamstime carries a standing 'Vw Van Blueprint Stock Illustrations' category). The concept's own words for it are 'a bit austere, a bit dull'. The default state of the artefact is generic.

'EVERY SHEET IS A DIFFERENT PHOTOGRAPH OF A DIFFERENT LUNCH' IS UNSUPPORTED AND IS THE CONCEPT'S CENTRAL ORIGINALITY CLAIM. One taco makes one blob. Nothing in the design structures, directs or authors the spread, so the differentiation-per-sheet is asserted rather than engineered — and if it fails, the piece reduces exactly to the existing grease-reveal wrapper.

THE REVEALED IMAGE IS WARM AMBER GLOW, THE CATEGORY'S DEFAULT NOSTALGIC REGISTER. 'Lights come on' is also the single most obvious thing a bulb-string vehicle can do — it is the first idea anyone has, which is a reason to distrust it, not to ship it.

THE VELLUM EDITION CONTRADICTS THE THESIS AND IS THE LEAST ORIGINAL FORMAT IN THE SET. A permanent translucent print of the lit state is an ordinary object, and offering it as the version 'for people who want the image without destroying it' concedes that the destruction is a cost to be worked around rather than the point.
improvements: ENGINEER THE SPREAD INSTEAD OF HOPING FOR IT — this is the single change that would take it to exceptional. Print an oil-BARRIER varnish or silicone resist on the reverse in a hidden lane geometry that follows the bulb string's path, so a blob of grease cannot spread radially: it is channelled ALONG THE WIRE and lights bulbs sequentially outward from wherever the taco landed. Directed wicking as a compositional device is the thing I cannot name a precedent for. It converts 'a wet patch happens to contain some bulbs' into 'the lights come on one at a time, from where you ate, and stop where you stopped' — which is the claim the concept already makes and currently cannot cash. Barrier-lane resist on greaseproof is testable in the same week-one hand-screen run the brief already schedules; make it test one, not an afterthought.

TAKE THE BUS OFF THE TOP FACE ENTIRELY. Print the dry sheet as ordinary utilitarian deli paper — the vehicle's own hand-lettering, which the record verifies: '267 / ELIZABETH STREET / NUEVA YORK' in condensed caps over 'Gracias por su Preferencia' in red script, read off ref_nolita_doorshut.jpg. A sheet that looks like nothing but a wrapper, until the entire vehicle arrives in the grease, is a far stronger reveal than a line drawing that gains highlights. It also deletes the two stock tropes the current top face sits on, and it makes the artefact anonymous in exactly the way the brief already says it wants ('the sheet is more interesting anonymous').

CHANGE THE STATE PAIR FROM UNLIT/LIT TO GREEN/RED — the one transition nobody else on earth can print. LEDGER_rev51.md verifies the four-livery arc (bought green and bare, missing three windows and only the front bench, at $3,000 → green in service → red plain with TACOMBI.COM → red folk-art), and the register confirms geometry transfers between livery states while paint does not. Grease turning the workshop-green donor into the folk-art red taqueria is a brand-owned, unrepeatable, non-nostalgic state change. 'Lights come on' is the obvious idea; 'the bus becomes itself' is not.

INVERT THE PERMANENT EDITION INSTEAD OF HEDGING IT. Kill the clean vellum print. The only collectible version should be a sheet that HAS been eaten off — flattened, dated, initialled by the table, sold or framed as the record of one specific lunch. That preserves the thesis (the artefact is authored by consumption) instead of selling the get-out, and it makes the destruction the source of value rather than its price. It also gives the reveal boundary a reason to be interesting, which reinforces improvement 1.

RUN THE ORIGINALITY TEST, NOT ONLY THE PHYSICS TEST. Twenty hand-screened sheets, twenty real meals, all twenty photographed flat side by side in one grid. If a stranger cannot tell them apart, the 'different photograph of a different lunch' claim is refuted and directed wicking becomes mandatory rather than optional. Do this in the same week as the registration test — it is the same ten sheets and the same lunch.

HARVEST THE BOUNDARIES AS A GENERATIVE ASSET. Photograph used sheets over a season and use the accumulated grease frontiers — the actual traced edges of hundreds of meals — as the pattern for a second artefact: the bag print, a tile, a wall. Nobody in the VW-bus category can copy that, because producing it requires owning a restaurant. It converts the ephemerality from a one-shot trick into a compounding proprietary image bank, and it is the strongest anti-derivative move available to this brand.

NAME AND DEFEAT THE REAL PRECEDENTS IN THE BRIEF ITSELF. Add a paragraph that cites condensation-reveal coasters, grease-reveal fast-food wrappers, rain-activated street work and hidden-picture children's plates, and states in one line each what this does that they do not. If that paragraph cannot be written honestly, the concept is not as fresh as the screener's note claims — and writing it is how you find out. Right now the defence is against a category that was never the competition.

verdicts.lens: PRODUCIBILITY AND FIDELITY — can this be made from THIS asset, given failing gates, unbuilt geometry, an unproven large-format chain, and an emblem rejected nine times?
verdicts.reasoning:
It sits above the median for one reason that I verified rather than took on trust: it routes around almost every failing gate this project has. A side elevation is EDGE-ON to the nose (HANDOFF_CARRIERS §0.05 says so of ref_side.jpg "by construction"), so the emblem — his ninth report, F191/F234 standing — is not in frame at all. One-ink line work is blind to gloss_compare's 0.412-against-0.60, to the red's G/R 0.422 against the photograph's 0.114, and to probe_rev70_tyre's 1.31x. Offered as a paper artefact rather than a delivery render, it is not gated by F191 or F193. That is a genuinely strong producibility position.

Its central technical claim also checks out, which is rare here. I imported bpy (4.5.3 LTS, pip module, no build, no render) and confirmed both halves of the prescribed pipeline exist: `GreasePencilLineartModifier` in bpy.types, and `wm.grease_pencil_export_svg` in bpy.ops. STATE.md's `non-manifold edges (body) | 0` and 229,489 quad / 1,040 tri give Line Art a fair chance. The LID_W defect it names is real and correctly quoted — `LID_W = (LID_X0 - LID_X1) / LID_ASPECT / math.sin(math.radians(LID_OPEN_DEG))` in t1_shell.py — and the bulb_string join it names is real (`ob = join([ob, flex], "bulb_string")`).

What holds it at workable is that four of its own numbers do not reconcile against the tree's constants, and its reveal geometry fights its own physics.

THE REVEAL'S PAYOFF IS WHERE THE OIL IS NOT. Grease wicks radially from where the taco sits — a blob, low and central. The amber content the concept cares about is a RIM: bulbs along the drip rail, flowers standing above the roof. Measured: the shut bus is ~2.0 m tall against 4.348 m long, so at the stated 290 mm drawn length it occupies about 133 mm of a 305 mm sheet's height. In the open state the lid stands LID_W·sin(76°) = 1.187 m above the roof, i.e. roughly 79 mm above the top-face roofline — in blank paper, with no maroon line work to bloom through and no plausible route for oil to reach it. "Bulbs igniting one at a time along the roof" is the promise, and it is the part the mechanism cannot deliver.

REGISTRATION IS WRONG BY ~4x, AND THE TREE'S OWN CONSTANTS SAY SO. t1_detail.py: `BULB_X0, BULB_X1, BULB_PITCH, BULB_R = T._aft(-1.8000), 1.7000, 0.0286, 0.0110`. At the stated 1:14 that is a 2.04 mm pitch with 1.57 mm bulbs — 0.47 mm of paper between adjacent bulbs. The concept's stated ±1.5 mm tolerance is three quarters of a full pitch; a bulb-registered reveal needs about ±0.4 mm, which no web press holds face-to-face on 40 gsm. So the "loose amber fields at ±6 mm" fallback is not a fallback, it is the only printable version — and the concept presents it as a downgrade rather than as the design.

SUBSTRATE CONTRADICTION, STATED AS "ORDINARY" AND UNMEASURED. Greaseproof and glassine are specified for the job of RESISTING oil penetration; the trick needs a sheet that wicks. The concept asserts "that part is ordinary". It is the opposite of ordinary and it is the whole artefact.

SCALE ARITHMETIC DOES NOT CLOSE. The drawn object is the shut bus WITH its counter: front x +2.160 (STATE.md `x range [-2.157, 2.160]`), counter aft `CNT_X1 = T.X_TAIL - CNT_OVERHANG` = -1.873 - 0.315 = -2.188. That is 4.348 m, which at 1:14 is 310.6 mm — off the 305 mm sheet entirely. 290 mm implies 1:15.0, not 1:14. And the printed caption "4,065 mm" is STATE.md's `length excludes opened lids ... 4.065 without`, which excludes both the lids and the nine non-bodywork parts including the counter — the wrong number for the thing being drawn. Three figures, three referents.

THE SHUT STATE IS BIGGER THAN THE ONE CONSTANT IT NAMES. LID_OPEN_DEG is right, and the coupling is worse than described: at T1_LIDDEG=10 LID_W inflates to 6.84 m and trips t1_shell's module-level `assert LID_W <= _LID_W_MAX`; at T1_LIDDEG=0 it is a ZeroDivisionError one line earlier — a bare traceback with no summary line, rule 51's own named class. But lid_board, lid_trunk, lid_rail, lid_strut, `TB_TILT_DEG = float(os.environ.get("T1_TB_TILT", 38.0))` and `REAR_OPEN_DEG` are all posed open too, and verify.py carries rows on the tail-board pose and the rear-hatch pose that a shut build will red. Under §3b each red is a finding you must name with a companion row. That is unscoped work.

THE FOLK ART IS A RASTER AND LINE ART CANNOT DRAW IT — and the one grounded reduction number is measured on the wrong object. folk_gen.py's own comment: "Connected components of the gold, `ref_side.jpg`, closed at ... 66 components carry 0.2826 m2 of gold", then `COMP_TOP = {1: 47.8, 2: 73.7, 3: 84.4, ...}`. That is a census of the PHOTOGRAPH. The same file's comparison table reads `gold connected components, whole flank 66 / 95 / 30` and `gold in the LARGEST component 47.8 % / 32.4 % / 44.9 %` — the SHIPPED generator makes 30 components with 44.9 % in the largest. "Delete 48 of 66 and keep 84.4 %" does not apply to the asset that would actually be traced.

Smaller: lid_gen.py declares `N_FLOWERS = len(HEADS_UV)      # 10 full heads`; the concept says eleven.

And there is no fallback if the line pass fails. `wm.grease_pencil_export_svg` is a `wm` operator and may need a window context; nothing in this tree has ever run it. If it will not run headless, the only route is tracing a raster at print resolution — roughly 9,300 px across the frame at 600 dpi, 18,600 at 1200 — against a chain proven once at 3840x2640 (106.8 min for one view) and a single rev-15 4320x2880 through hero.py's DIFFERENT PAD chain. That is not a proving run, it is a new chain.

Credit where it is due on my lens: this needs no T1_ALPHA, no deliver.py, no hq_render/stitch/post, no emblem fix, no gloss fix, no colour grade. The tree already holds the two instruments it actually needs — trace_outline.py (Moore-neighbour contour tracing with a selftest) and mottle_measure.py's side-ortho transform, "DERIVED then VERIFIED", which raises FATAL if it cannot reproduce the alpha edge to 12 px. Neither is mentioned in the concept, and together they make the whole sheet analytically composable in millimetres without a print-resolution render anywhere. That is the route to a tier upgrade.
fatal_flaws: THE REVEAL AND THE ARTWORK POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. Oil wicks as a blob from where the food sits; the concept's climax is a rim — bulbs along the roofline and flowers standing LID_W·sin(76°) = 1.187 m above the roof, which at the stated scale is ~79 mm above the drawn roofline in blank paper with no line work to bloom through. The shut bus fills only ~133 mm of the 305 mm sheet's height, so most of the sheet, including all of the payoff, is nowhere near the taco.

REGISTRATION IS SPECIFIED ~4x TOO LOOSE, ON THE TREE'S OWN NUMBERS. t1_detail.py: `BULB_X0, BULB_X1, BULB_PITCH, BULB_R = T._aft(-1.8000), 1.7000, 0.0286, 0.0110`. At 1:14 that is 2.04 mm pitch, 1.57 mm bulbs, 0.47 mm of paper between them. The stated ±1.5 mm is three quarters of a pitch. Bulb-by-bulb ignition is not printable at this scale on any web press; the ±6 mm 'fallback' is the only design that exists.

SUBSTRATE CONTRADICTION, ASSERTED AS SETTLED. Greaseproof and glassine exist to RESIST oil penetration; the trick requires a sheet that wicks and clarifies. The concept calls this 'ordinary' and unverified in the same paragraph. The entire artefact rests on an untested material property of a material chosen for the opposite property.

THE SCALE / FORMAT / CAPTION TRIPLE DOES NOT CLOSE. Drawn object (shut bus + counter) = +2.160 to CNT_X1 = X_TAIL − CNT_OVERHANG = −1.873 − 0.315 = −2.188, i.e. 4.348 m → 310.6 mm at 1:14, which overruns the 305 mm sheet. 290 mm implies 1:15.0. The printed caption '4,065 mm' is STATE.md's lids-and-counter-EXCLUDED body length. Also 'floating with 8 mm of air top and bottom' describes the long axis, not the short one, where there is ~85 mm.

THE SHUT STATE IS FIVE POSES, NOT ONE. Beyond LID_OPEN_DEG: lid_board, lid_trunk, lid_rail, lid_strut, `TB_TILT_DEG` (default 38.0, T1_TB_TILT) and `REAR_OPEN_DEG` (64, T1_REAR_OPEN) all pose open, and verify.py carries pose rows on the tail board and rear hatch that a shut build will red. Under §3b every red is a finding needing a named cause and a companion row. Unscoped.

THE FOLK-ART REDUCTION RULE IS MEASURED ON THE PHOTOGRAPH, NOT THE ASSET. folk_gen.py: COMP_TOP/COMP_HIST are 'Connected components of the gold, `ref_side.jpg` ... 66 components'. The same file's table reads 66 / 95 / 30 components and 47.8 % / 32.4 % / 44.9 % in the largest — the SHIPPED art has 30 components and 44.9 %. 'Delete 48 of 66, keep 84.4 %' cannot be applied to what would be traced. And because the art is a box-projected raster, Line Art will not draw it at all — the concept's model_work_required never says so.

NO FALLBACK FOR THE LINE PASS ITSELF. The stated fallback (loose amber fields) addresses registration only. If `wm.grease_pencil_export_svg` will not run in background (it is a `wm` operator; nothing in this tree has ever called it), the only route is a raster trace at ~9,300–18,600 px across the frame, against a chain proven at 3840×2640 in 106.8 min per view and one rev-15 4320×2880 through a different (hero.py PAD) chain.
improvements: RE-COMPOSE THE AMBER FOR A BLOB, NOT A RIM. Put every reveal element inside the lower-centre band where a taco actually sits: the three serving apertures (STATE.md gives the band as `1.372-1.775 un-dropped (1.307-1.710 AG)` with measured `bay widths 0.516 0.515 0.516`) plus a counter spill at CNT_ZT/CNT_ZB 1.2540/1.1470. Demote the roof bulbs to a single thin band that fires only on an unusually greasy sheet, and stop promising 'bulbs igniting one at a time along the roof'. The mural flowers standing above the roof should be cut or moved to the VELLUM edition, where backlighting reveals everything at once and geometry is free.

PRINT THE REVERSE AS LOOSE FIELDS FROM THE START AND SAY SO IN THE BRIEF. Three amber rectangles at the measured bay stations, one counter band, one roofline band — each with ≥6 mm of bleed past the maroon outline on all four sides, so ±3 mm back-to-front register is comfortable. This is the design, not the contingency. If a bulb-registered version is ever wanted, quote the reason it cannot be: BULB_PITCH 0.0286 m and BULB_R 0.0110 m give 2.04 mm pitch and 1.57 mm bulbs at 1:14, so adjacent bulbs are 0.47 mm apart.

FIX THE SCALE TRIPLE WITH MEASURED EXTENTS. State the drawn extent as x +2.160 (STATE.md `x range [-2.157, 2.160]`) to CNT_X1 = X_TAIL − CNT_OVERHANG = −1.873 − 0.315 = −2.188, i.e. 4.348 m. Choose 1:15.0 for a 290 mm drawing on a 305 mm sheet, caption the drawn length rather than 4,065 mm, and correct 'air top and bottom' to 'air fore and aft, 7.5 mm each'. Re-derive all four figures off the mesh at build time rather than typing them, per CLAUDE.md's opening rule.

MAKE THE SHEET ANALYTICALLY COMPOSABLE AND SKIP PRINT-RESOLUTION RENDERING ENTIRELY. Two passes, neither of which needs a large frame: (a) GEOMETRY OUTLINE via GreasePencilLineartModifier → `wm.grease_pencil_export_svg` — both confirmed present in this bpy 4.5.3; (b) ARTWORK OUTLINE via trace_outline.py's Moore-neighbour tracer, which already carries a selftest against shapes known by construction, run on the ALPHA of tex/swirl.png. Map both onto the sheet through the side ortho transform mottle_measure.py already 'DERIVED then VERIFIED' (it raises FATAL if it cannot reproduce the alpha edge to 12 px). The bulb string then needs no mesh at all: BULB_X0/X1/PITCH/R plus that transform place all ~115 discs exactly, in millimetres, so the reverse face registers to the top face BY CONSTRUCTION and only the press adds error.

PROVE THE SVG EXPORTER HEADLESS IN WEEK ONE, BEFORE ANY DESIGN WORK. `wm.grease_pencil_export_svg` is a window-manager operator and may refuse in `blender -b`; nothing in this tree has ever run it. One cheap test on a cube settles it. If it refuses, the trace_outline.py route above is the whole fallback and the concept still ships — say that explicitly so nobody budgets a revision on a raster chain proven only at 3840×2640.

BUILD THE SHUT STATE AS ONE ABLATION FAMILY WITH A WATCHED KILL. `T1_SHUT=1` should set the decoupled lid angle, T1_TB_TILT=0 and T1_REAR_OPEN=0 together, with `T1_LID_WCOUPLE=0` freezing LID_W at its shipped 1.2237 and a guard asserting the panel's width does not move when the angle does. WATCH IT FAIL on the coupled build first: T1_LIDDEG=10 gives LID_W 6.8379 m and trips the module-level assert; T1_LIDDEG=0 gives a ZeroDivisionError one line earlier with no summary line — repair that into a refusal in the same edit (rule 37 + rule 51). Name in advance which verify.py rows the shut pose will red (the tail-board pose row, the rear-hatch pose row) and add the companion rows §3b requires.

RE-RUN THE COMPONENT CENSUS ON THE SHIPPED TEXTURE BEFORE QUOTING ANY SACRIFICE RULE. folk_gen.py already prints the shipped column beside the photograph's; use 30 components / 44.9 % in the largest, not 66 / 47.8 / 84.4. Then paint the surviving components onto a proof and LOOK at them at 1:15 before committing to 'the three largest masses' — at that scale the question is what survives a 0.15 mm flexo line, and nothing in the tree has ever measured that.

TEST THE PAPER BEFORE THE ARTWORK, AND NAME A DIFFERENT SUBSTRATE. Specify MG or dry-waxed natural kraft, or a light bleached sheet chosen for wicking — NOT true greaseproof or glassine, which are refined precisely to stop what this design needs. Buy three candidates, hand-screen ten sheets each, put real tacos on them, and photograph the wick radius at 2 / 5 / 10 / 20 minutes. Then draw the amber footprint to the measured radius. That measurement is the design brief; everything upstream of it is a guess.

SETTLE THE FOOD-CONTACT QUESTION BEFORE THE TWO-FACE LAYOUT IS LOCKED. The visible top face is the face the taco sits on, so the dark maroon ink is in direct food contact. If low-migration compliance pushes ink off the contact face, the top face has to move to the reverse and the entire trick inverts. That is a printer conversation, not a design decision, and it can invalidate the whole layout after it is drawn.

CORRECT THE FLOWER COUNT AND REPAIR F74(a) FIRST. lid_gen.py declares `N_FLOWERS = len(HEADS_UV)      # 10 full heads`, not eleven. F74(a) is open and measured: tex/lidmural.png is cropped at the bottom, flowers sliced mid-bloom, side columns truncated. Repair it in lid_gen.py and REGENERATE BY HAND — lid_gen.py is not called by build.py, so a stale texture ships silently. Also record that which FACE carries the mural is contradicted inside the tree (lid_gen.py says outward/upper, SPEC §4 says underside) and that no frame shows the reverse; the reveal draws that face, so the contradiction has to be resolved or the artwork has to avoid depending on it.

KEEP AND SHARPEN THE F18 DISCLAIMER, AND ADD THE PRODUCIBILITY ARGUMENT. One line: this is not F18 (vinyl, cartoon-with-rendered-depth, kept by children) but its opposite (paper, one-ink line, destroyed by the meal). Then add what my lens actually found in its favour, because it is the strongest thing in the proposal and the concept never says it: this artefact needs no T1_ALPHA, no deliver.py, no hq_render/stitch/post, no emblem fix, no gloss fix and no colour grade — it is the only route in the program that ships without the owner's delivery-render hold ever being lifted.

verdicts.lens: Emotional resonance, brand fit, IP exposure
verdicts.reasoning:
THE MECHANIC EARNS ITS PRAISE AND I AM NOT GOING TO PRETEND OTHERWISE. An artefact that only completes when it is soiled, in a category that sells nothing but permanence, on the one substrate a poster studio never touches, authored by the customer's own meal — that is a real idea, and it is native to a taqueria rather than applied to one. The deadpan caption ("Playa del Carmen · 1963 · 4,065 mm") is the single best-judged line in the whole submission: it sits exactly in the voice the grounding records for Tacombi's own shop ("casual, convenient leisure products since 2006", "purpose-built, all-weather knit beanie"). The refusal to put the wordmark on top is a defensible instinct even where I disagree with it. The reduction is grounded in `folk_gen.py`'s own census (`COMP_TOP = {1: 47.8, 2: 73.7, 3: 84.4, ...}`, 48 of 66 components carrying 2.29 % of the gold) rather than in taste, which is more than most concepts manage.

BUT ON MY THREE AXES IT UNDERMINES ITSELF THREE TIMES, AND TWO OF THE THREE ARE CHECKABLE AGAINST FILES IN THIS REPOSITORY.

(1) BRAND FIT — THE STATE EVERY SHEET IS IN WHEN IT IS HANDED OVER IS THE MOST DERIVATIVE IMAGE THE PROGRAM COULD PRINT. The concept's top face is the bus SHUT and DARK: lid down, counter a closed horizontal, hatches empty outlined rectangles, only three folk-art masses in outline, no wordmark. Strip those and what remains is a T1 profile in one ink — i.e. the exact silhouette the grounding says the merch market has worn out, minus every feature that distinguishes this vehicle. The record's own art-direction reading is the opposite: "The object's identity is the OPEN configuration — that is the shape people recognise", and it notes the bus is stationary with the lid raised in every in-service frame. The concept admits the dry state is "deliberately a bit austere, a bit dull". Austere is fine. Generic-VW is not, and that is what it actually is. The reveal is Tacombi-specific; the default is not, and the default is what 100 % of sheets look like at the moment of handover.

(2) IP — THE CONCEPT'S OWN DEFENCE IS FALSE ON A POINT ANYONE CAN CHECK. It claims "the VW roundel is not in frame at all". The nose roundel, correct — the nose is edge-on. But a side elevation shows FOUR HUBCAPS, and this vehicle's hubcaps carry a VW. `t1_detail.py`: `CAP_EMBLEM_D = 0.3170 * CAP_D`; `STATE.md` prints the built result, "hubcap badge: 4 rings R 0.043429 (= CAP_EMBLEM_D/2)" — so the badge is 0.0869 m, which at the stated 1:14 is **6.2 mm across, four times per sheet**, in coarse one-ink line work where it will read cleanly. That is a VW mark reproduced four times on a giveaway distributed by a commercial food brand. Separately, "given away rather than sold" is the weakest defence available — promotional giveaway by a trading business is use in commerce — and a pure PROFILE line drawing is closer to the vehicle-shape trade dress the grounding names ("The images of classic Beetle and Bus vehicles are themselves protected as trademarks") than a photoreal three-quarter would be, precisely because the shut state removes the conversion. A Tacombi-specific route existed and the concept walked past it: draw the working bus, and the distinguishing content is the counter, the hatches, the lid and the script — none of which is VW's.

(3) EMOTIONAL — THE BEST BEAT IS PRINTED WHERE THE GREASE NEVER GOES. The promise leads with "bulbs igniting one at a time along the roof" and "the flowers rising out of the closed lid". The bulbs run the drip rail — the highest line on the drawing. The mural flowers, in the open state, sit ABOVE the roofline entirely: `STATE.md` reads `roof at tail = 1.988` and `bbox top 3.132`, so at 1:14 the raised lid reaches ~80 mm above a roofline that the concept has placed with "8 mm of air top and bottom". Two consequences, both bad. First, the composition as specified is geometrically impossible: a shut bus at 1:14 is ~159 mm tall on a 305 mm sheet (73 mm of air, not 8), and the open state's payload needs 224 mm — the concept has not been drawn, only described. Second, and worse: a taco sits centre-low and grease wicks a few centimetres, so the wetted zone is roughly a 120–180 mm disc in the middle of the sheet. The roofline and the raised-lid flowers are the two regions guaranteed to stay dry. The modal outcome is not "a different photograph of a different lunch" — it is a brown blotch over the body sides where the amber payload is thinnest. The concept romanticises variability it has not designed for.

The idea survives all three. The execution as specified does not. Every one of these is fixable without touching the mechanic, which is why this is strong and not workable — but it is not exceptional while its own IP paragraph contains a falsehood and its headline beat is unreachable.
fatal_flaws: THE AMBER PAYLOAD IS PRINTED OUTSIDE THE WETTED ZONE. The two beats the concept leads with — bulbs igniting along the roofline, flowers rising out of the lid — are in the top of the sheet. Grease wicks a few centimetres from a taco that sits centre-low. At 1:14 the raised lid is ~80 mm ABOVE the drawn roofline (`STATE.md`: `roof at tail = 1.988`, `bbox top 3.132`), i.e. on paper that will never see oil. The promised image is the one outcome the physics cannot deliver.

THE DRY STATE IS THE MOST DERIVATIVE IMAGE IN THE PROGRAM. Lid down, counter a closed line, hatches as empty rectangles, no wordmark, three outline blobs — that is a generic T1 profile. It is what every sheet looks like at handover and what most will look like forever (dry corners, a customer who eats a quesadilla). The record's own reading is that the OPEN configuration is this vehicle's identity; the concept prints the closed one as its default.

THE IP SELF-ASSESSMENT IS FALSE ON A CHECKABLE POINT. "The VW roundel is not in frame at all" — the nose is edge-on, but a side elevation carries four hubcaps and this vehicle's hubcaps carry a VW. `t1_detail.py`: `CAP_EMBLEM_D = 0.3170 * CAP_D`; `STATE.md`: "hubcap badge: 4 rings R 0.043429 (= CAP_EMBLEM_D/2)" → 0.0869 m → **6.2 mm at 1:14, four per sheet**. A concept whose IP paragraph is wrong cannot be trusted to have priced its exposure.

THE STATED LAYOUT DOES NOT CLOSE. "290 mm long ... floating with 8 mm of air top and bottom" on a 305 mm square: a shut bus at 1:14 is ~159 mm tall, so the vertical air is ~73 mm, not 8. And with the counter the vehicle is `STATE.md`'s 4.5800 m = **327 mm at 1:14**, which does not fit a 305 mm sheet at all. Either the counter — the single most Tacombi-specific silhouette element — is silently omitted, or the drawing runs off the sheet undeclared. This composition has been described, not drawn.

THE ONE TACOMBI-OWNED MARK ON THE VEHICLE IS EXPLICITLY FORBIDDEN. "Do NOT put the wordmark on the top face" treats the silver flank script as branding bolted on. It is not — it is painted livery, it is the brand's own typographic DNA, and the record shows the owner rejecting a wrong version of it by name ("That script i see on the p9 hero is NOT it"). Omitting it leaves a sheet whose only legible marks are four VW roundels. That is the wrong trademark surviving the edit.
improvements: INVERT THE DRY STATE. Draw the bus OPEN AND WORKING in maroon line — lid propped, counter cantilevered, hatches as open voids, tail board down with its unlit bead chain — and let the grease bring only LIGHT and COLOUR, not geometry. Three wins at once: the dry sheet is Tacombi-specific from the moment it is handed over rather than a generic T1 profile; registration gets far easier because amber fields no longer have to align to a lid that is not drawn; and it stops the concept depending on a SHUT state that has never been built in 76 revisions and is blocked by the 1/sin coupling in `t1_shell.py`'s `LID_W` that the concept itself flags. The transformation you keep is DARK → LIT, which is the one that carries the meaning ("the bus opens and lights up when there is food") and the only one the paper can actually perform.

PUT THE ENTIRE REVEAL INSIDE A MEASURED WET ZONE, AND MEASURE IT BEFORE YOU DRAW. Week one, before any artwork: put real food on ten blank sheets of the candidate stock — three fillings, al pastor / a wet salsa / a lime-and-crema — photograph at 2, 10 and 25 minutes, and trace the mean stain. Turn that into a die-line. Then compose so that footprint lands on the SERVING COUNTER AND THE THREE HATCHES, and print nothing load-bearing above the roofline. If the mean footprint is a ~150 mm disc, that is 2.1 m of bus at 1:14 — enough for the counter, all three hatches and the galley behind them. The customer's taco should sit on the drawn counter. You eat from the counter; the counter lights up. That ties the mechanic to what the object actually is instead of to a lucky wick.

PUT "SEÑOR TACOMBI" ON THE REVERSE, IN AMBER, AND LET THE FOOD IGNITE IT. This is the single highest-value change and it fixes three problems in one move. The wordmark sits in the flank's own measured empty middle — `folk_gen.py`'s `OPEN_GOLD = 0.29  # X +0.872 .. -0.62`, the audit's triptych gap — which is exactly where a plate lands. So: top face carries no wordmark (your instinct preserved, the sheet stays anonymous dry); the grease brings up the brand's own hand-painted silver script as amber. The mark that surfaces under the food is TACOMBI'S, not VW's — which repairs the brand fit, improves the IP posture, and puts the payload in the wet zone simultaneously. The art already exists at 4096×1738 (`tex/senor.png`), authored from `script_gen.py`'s measured control points, so this costs nothing to source.

DELETE THE HUBCAP BADGES FROM THE DRAWING AND CORRECT THE IP PARAGRAPH. Draw the wheel as the four-band bullseye it is — chrome ring, cream rim dish, red dome — and leave the dome BLANK. It reads better in one-ink line art anyway, it is the more distinctive mark (a red-domed cream-rimmed wheel is Tacombi's; a VW roundel is not), and it removes the only reproduced VW trademark on the sheet. Then rewrite the defence honestly: "one-ink line art of a converted vehicle, nose edge-on, VW roundel omitted at the hubcaps by design" is a real posture; "the roundel is not in frame at all" is a claim the file refutes. Put the trademark question to the owner as a named risk with this mitigation attached — he may already have an arrangement, and it is his call, not the drawing's.

FIX THE SCALE AND USE THE COUNTER AS A DELIBERATE BLEED. The body is 4.065 m (`STATE.md` verify block, `dims L=4.065`) → 290 mm at 1:14, which fits. With the counter it is `STATE.md`'s 4.5800 m → 327 mm, which does not. Do not solve this by cropping the counter off quietly. Bleed it: run the counter off the right edge of the sheet at full 1:14, so the vehicle reads as bigger than the paper and the serving edge points at the customer. Alternatively drop to 1:15.5 (4.580 / 15.5 = 295 mm) and keep it whole. Either is defensible; the current spec is silently neither. And restate the vertical air correctly — a shut bus leaves ~73 mm, not 8.

DROP THE "4,065 mm" CAPTION OR REPLACE IT WITH A FIGURE SOMEONE HAS MEASURED ON THE REAL VEHICLE. The caption's register is perfect and worth keeping, but that number is the SPEC target for bodywork with nine non-bodywork parts excluded; `STATE.md`'s own headline dimension row reads `| overall length (ex counter) | 4.5800 | 4.0550 | +525.0 mm **OUT** |`. Printing it on a giveaway publishes a figure the project's own machine flags. "Playa del Carmen · 1963" alone carries the whole deadpan effect and is graded source-class in SPEC §0.1. If you want a third element, use something true and better: "tres ventanas, sin vidrio" — the three missing windows that became the serving hatches, which is the brand's own origin and the one fact no VW-bus print in the world can use.

KILL THE VELLUM EDITION AS SPECIFIED AND REPLACE IT WITH THE ACHIEVED SHEET. A backlit vellum print that shows the lit state permanently discards the entire idea — it is the thing the concept exists to argue against — and a brass clip in a glassine envelope is precious in a way that collides head-on with Tacombi's flat catalogue voice. If you want a keepsake path, make it the customer's OWN sheet: a stack of plain glassine sleeves at the till, free, no branding, so a family can take home the specific sheet their lunch drew. That is the only keepsake worth having here, it costs almost nothing, and it converts "you had to ruin it to see it" from an ache into a gift.

DECIDE THE CHILD DELIBERATELY, IN SPANISH, IN ONE LINE OR NONE. The screener's own emotional claim leads with a seven-year-old's gasp, but nothing in the concept designs for discovery — a child eating something dry never sees the trick at all. Either commit to zero instruction and accept that the reveal is a rumour passed between tables (a real strategy, and the more Tacombi one), or set ONE 5 pt maroon line in the same register as the dimension caption, Spanish-first and deadpan: `para verlo, hay que comer`. Do not write "watch what happens!". Test both on actual children before choosing; this is the one axis where the concept currently has an assertion and no evidence.

CHECK THE NAME WITH A MEXICAN SPEAKER BEFORE IT SHIPS. "Papel de grasa" is a literal construction and reads translated; the paper tacos are actually handed over in has its own everyday Mexican name (papel de estraza / papel encerado, depending on stock). Getting this wrong on a Mexico-founded brand's most-handled printed object is a small error that a Mexican customer notices immediately and an American designer never does. It is a five-minute fix and it is exactly the axis on which this program is trying not to be generic van culture.

concept.title: ROTULISTA
concept.one_line: The bare red flank of the Nolita-state bus, painted onto by an invisible hand in the signwriter's real working order — three big gold masses first, then the tendrils, then the rosettes, then forty-eight tiny marks all at once, and the silver wordmark last with its dark shadow arriving one frame before the metal.
concept.the_image:
FRAMING: locked, no camera move at all. `hero34r`, the 3/4 rear-left — studio.py's own comment on it reads '3/4 rear-left, shows the counter wrap and the louvre block'. It puts the largest folk-art mass nearest camera (folk_gen's MASS-R1, the rear-most quarter, 73213 mm sq) and it keeps the VW roundel entirely out of frame. The flank bleeds off both edges. This is not a portrait of a bus, it is a wall being painted.

LIGHT: warm and LOW, raking across the flank from frame-left so the gold catches and the cream goes ivory. Not the flat white cyclorama. F259 licenses exactly this — the owner ruled 'Relight the studio and fix the ground if necessary'; the studio stays, the RIG is now open, and the single constraint travelling with it is DO NOT change RED.

PALETTE: opens on TWO colours — vermillion below the belt, cream above, a plain unornamented flank. Closes on FIVE: + folk-art gold, + dark maroon, + silver. The film is literally the palette assembling itself.

COMPOSITION: the counter's brass nosing runs as a hard bright horizontal on the lower third and never moves; the louvre block is the only fine texture in frame and it anchors the right. Everything that appears, appears in the band between the belt line and the arch.

MOTION — and THE ORDER IS A MEASUREMENT, not an invention. folk_gen.py's own connected-component census of ref_side.jpg: `COMP_TOP = {1: 47.8, 2: 73.7, 3: 84.4, 5: 87.8, 10: 93.5}`, and `COMP_HIST` whose first three bins are (24 components, 0.42%), (21, 1.32%), (3, 0.55%). Three components carry 84.4% of the gold; forty-eight carry 2.29%.
1. BARE RED FLANK. 1 s hold. It looks unfinished and slightly sad.
2. THE THREE MASSES, largest first, each laid down as ONE wet stroke over ~8 frames — the cab-door mass, then MASS-R1 over the rear quarter, then MASS-R2 over the arch. Two seconds in, 84% of the drawing exists.
3. THE TENDRILS — four dark-maroon S-curve commas with their dot rows, whipping on in 3 frames each.
4. THE ROSETTES — eight, popping on offbeats, centre-out.
5. THE FORTY-EIGHT. Every remaining tiny mark, in ONE FRAME, like dust settling. They add 2.29%.
6. THE SCRIPT LANDS LAST, silver, as one object — and its DARK KEYLINE ARRIVES ONE FRAME BEFORE THE SILVER, because that is the order a signwriter actually works: shadow, then metal.
7. 2 s hold. Loop by wiping back to bare red, or cut to black.

~14 s. The pacing is the argument: nothing to almost-everything in two seconds, then ten seconds spent on the last 16%. That is exactly what hand-painting feels like, and here it is derived from a census rather than felt.
concept.emotional_claim: SOMEONE MADE THIS. The category's central lie is that a VW bus is a mood you can buy; this says a person stood in front of a red panel with a brush and a mahl stick and made decisions. The size-ordered pacing gives the viewer the specific, physical pleasure of watching craft — the big confident gestures land first and then the maker fusses for ten seconds over marks worth 2.29% of the ink, which is a thing every person who has ever made anything recognises in their body. And the last beat is the one that makes a signwriter nod: the shadow before the silver. It is a detail nobody outside the trade will consciously notice and everybody will feel.
formats: 15 s vertical 1080x1920 for Reels/Stories. The flank crops to vertical well because the artwork is banded between the belt and the arch.
6 s square 1080x1080 cutdown: three masses plus the script. The whole idea survives at 40% of the runtime.

THE PROGRESSION POSTER — and the best stills in this concept are the UNFINISHED frames. Pull four: bare / three masses / plus rosettes / finished. Print 4-up at A2 420x594, or as a set of four A4s, uncoated, spot-colour. Nobody in the world sells 'a VW bus being painted'; this series is a genuinely new object.

APPAREL, and the scale is measured not guessed: the THREE-MASS state alone at 1:1.5 on a back print, two inks. At that ratio the shipped tile's median gold stroke is 8.8 mm and its p10 is 1.8 mm — everything prints. The FULL flank at a 280 mm chest print (1:14.5) does NOT: p10 collapses to 0.18 mm and 95 of 196 components have their thickest point under 0.52 mm. Print one mass big, never all of it small.
Packaging tissue, cup wrap, bag gusset: 'the forty-eight' alone as a scatter tile. One ink. The marks nobody notices, used as the pattern.
20 s wall projection above the counter, looping, in store. The bus painting itself, above the bus.
Title-card system for any future film: the wordmark's keyline-then-silver beat, isolated, 1 s, as the brand's sting.
concept.why_not_derivative: The market's flower-power VW is a decal somebody slapped on a van, and it is the single most saturated move in the category. This makes the OPPOSITE argument in the same visual vocabulary: it shows the florals being DRAWN, in Mexican signwriting order, which reframes them from Woodstock iconography to rotulismo. That reframing is the most valuable single thing this brand can do with its own artwork, and MOTION IS THE ONLY MEDIUM THAT CAN MAKE IT — a still flower on a bus is ambiguous and always readable as hippie; a flower being brushed onto a taqueria is not. It is also anti-CGI in a program built on CGI: it uses a photoreal 3D asset to stage a hand-painting event, so the technique argues against its own slickness. And there is no stock equivalent because the ordering is derived from a component census of this specific vehicle's actual paint.
concept.production_notes:
CHEAP PROTOTYPE AVAILABLE TODAY: `T1_W_ART` is a live global opacity on the folk-art alpha (t1_mats.py multiplies the art mask by W_ART, shipped 1.00). Sweeping 0 to 1 gives a whole-flank fade-on in ~10 renders. That is NOT the concept — it fades everything together and loses the entire idea — but it proves the camera, the relight and the timing in one afternoon before anyone touches folk_gen.py.

STATE THE CEILING ON THE ORDERING. folk_gen's census is of ref_side.jpg, the PHOTOGRAPH. The shipped tile is measurably more fragmented — 196 components with the top three carrying 66.4%, against the photograph's 66 with the top three carrying 84.4%. If you animate the shipped tile you are animating a different drawing from the one the census describes. Say which one you used, in the ledger and in the client note.

folk_gen.py AND script_gen.py ARE NOT CALLED BY build.py. Regenerate the textures by hand or the render silently uses the old file. This has cost this project revisions before.

DO NOT 'IMPROVE' THE WORDMARK TOWARD THE PHOTOGRAPH. flank_compare's `Senor` row now scores a DELIBERATE DEPARTURE (F156) because the owner ruled the word to bright silver (F157: 'Bright silver, same as Tacombi'), and that ruling covers THAT WORD ONLY — the b flag, the i dot and the swash keep their measured tarnish. The gate reads the departure as improvement and will not warn you that you are undoing him.

LIVERY STATES ARE NOT MIXABLE. The bare opening state is Nolita/state-B; the finished state is Playa/state-A. Rule 11 and SPEC §7.1 permit rendering both because geometry transfers and paint does not — but any single frame that BLENDS them is a fake, and this has already killed three findings (F99, F100, F140). The transition here is legitimate precisely because it is temporal: you are watching state B become state A, not compositing them.

The relight must not go through `T1_SCENE=playa`. F57 records that path renders NO VEHICLE — 'a dark cylinder on a grey plane', reported and not diagnosed.
model_work_required: THE SCRIPT HAS NO DARK KEYLINE AND BEAT 6 DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON IT. Measured on tex/senor.png (4096x1738 RGBA): among pixels with alpha > 200 the 1st-percentile luma is 168.3 and the fraction below luma 80 is 0.0000 — there is ZERO dark ink in the asset — while SPEC §3 requires 'SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow'. grep for keyline/shadow finds nothing in script_gen.py or t1_mats.silver_script. This is why the wordmark reads flat in the render and crisp in the photograph, and it is the cheapest visible improvement in the whole inventory. Fix in script_gen.py (lid_gen.py already authors the convention: `DARKLINE = (72, 26, 16)`), regenerate BY HAND, and add a guard that reads the asset's own sub-luma-80 fraction and goes red if it returns to zero.

THE LOCKUP IS MIS-PLACED BY ~76-83 mm AND TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES AGREE. flank_compare live on out/r75_side.png: 'the render's lockup has to move +76.2 mm forward and -47.6 mm down', cross-checked by a route sharing no step with it at +83/+80 mm aft with the ink top +61.1 mm high. Placement survives every downscale — on a 610 mm poster that is 11.4 mm of lateral error. Fix it in the SAME edit as the keyline.

folk_gen.py MUST EMIT A PER-COMPONENT PAINT-ORDER RANK into an unused channel of swirl.png / swirl_b.png, so the animation is a threshold sweep rather than a hand-keyed matte. It already computes the components and their areas; nothing new has to be measured.

`hero34r` CLIPS. I measured out/r75_hero34r.png: the subject's bbox runs to xmax = 1599 of 1600 — the counter, the object's strongest horizontal and the thing that makes it read as a taqueria rather than a van, runs off the right edge. Pull the camera or widen the aspect before designing to this view. It also has ONE rendered-file mention across LEDGER_rev66..75, against `side`'s 27 — the most Tacombi-forward angle is the one least looked at.

A BARE-FLANK BUILD STATE. build.py binds the folk art, the script and the Calidad decal unconditionally. Beat 1 needs a `T1_LIVERY` (or at minimum the art masks driven to zero independently of each other), and the ablation must be watched producing a genuinely plain red flank, not a faint ghost.

A WARM RAKING RELIGHT, under F259. The constraint is DO NOT change RED — that is the option he explicitly declined. Move the rig, not the paint, and re-read flank_compare / gloss_compare / probe_rev70_tyre afterwards so a relight cannot regress them silently.

Same infrastructure debt as every motion piece: no keyframes, no export, one full rebuild per pose. This one is cheaper than most because NOTHING GEOMETRIC MOVES — it is a texture sweep on a fixed pose, so the build can be reused if T1_SAVE is used to persist one .blend.

verdicts.lens: ORIGINALITY — is this genuinely fresh, or a well-executed instance of something already on a thousand VW-bus products and a thousand brand reels?
verdicts.reasoning:
This is the intersection of two of the most saturated genres in commercial motion, and the concept does not yet escape either.

GENRE 1 — THE LIVERY REVEAL. "Graphics write themselves onto a vehicle, locked camera, wordmark lands last" is the default form of the Formula 1 season livery reveal, the sneaker-drop build-on, and the beverage-can kinetic reveal. It is the After Effects trim-path/write-on tutorial, which is why it is everywhere. GENRE 2 — THE SIGNWRITER TIME-LAPSE. "Sign Painters" (Levine & Macon, 2013) and the entire Instagram/YouTube ecosystem of lettering artists filming a panel being filled is the direct precedent for "watch paint appear in the maker's order." Adjacent: the "car assembles itself" CGI brand film (Audi/BMW/Mercedes lineage), and rotulación aesthetics already mined by Mexican beverage branding and Latin American agency reels. The concept is genre 1 executed with genre 2's ordering. That combination is a real editorial idea, but it is not an unoccupied space.

THE CENTRAL ORIGINALITY PROBLEM IS THAT THE DIFFERENTIATOR IS INVISIBLE. The screener's note rests on the paint order being "a measurement, not a mood." I confirmed the census is real — folk_gen.py's `COMP_HIST` first three bins are (24, 0.42), (21, 1.32), (3, 0.55) = 48 components carrying 2.29 %, and `COMP_TOP = {1: 47.8, 2: 73.7, 3: 84.4, ...}`. It reproduces exactly. But a viewer cannot tell a censused order from an instinctive one, and the order the census yields — big masses, then details, then lettering — is precisely the order any animator picks without measuring, because it is how everyone paints. The measurement buys defensibility and ledger hygiene. It buys no distinctiveness. Provenance is not novelty, and the note conflates them.

THE SPECIFIED EXECUTION IS THE TROPE'S DEFAULT, NOT ROTULISMO. The concept says "laid down as ONE wet stroke," but `model_work_required` asks folk_gen to "emit a per-component paint-order RANK" and drive a threshold sweep. A per-component threshold sweep reveals a blob in whatever order the threshold field dictates — it is a mask wipe, not a stroke. Add "rosettes popping on offbeats, centre-out" and you have described the standard elements-pop-to-the-beat reveal. Nothing specified shows a brush width, a loaded-to-dry taper, a wet edge, or a quill's chisel. The film says rotulismo and specifies decals.

THE SIGNATURE BEAT IS UNGROUNDED AND FORBIDDEN IN TERMS. Beat 6 — dark keyline one frame before the silver — is the one moment nobody else has, and it fails twice. SPEC §10.16 is headed "The script's keyline and drop shadow are not measurable," samples outward from the ink edge (+1 px 80.5, +2 px 63.1, +3 px 61.7, ground 58.7), concludes "a monotone decay toward ground with no dark ring at any radius — that is edge blur, not a keyline," and instructs verbatim: "**Do not add a keyline to the generator because sec.3 says so**; that is the same error as building from the thumbnail." The concept's model_work_required does exactly that and calls it "the cheapest visible improvement." Separately, "shadow, then metal, because that is the order a signwriter actually works" is asserted with no citation anywhere in the repo and is not obviously true of gilding, where shade and outline commonly follow the leaf. The most distinctive frame in fourteen seconds may depict a feature the vehicle does not have, in an order nobody has established.

WHAT IS GENUINELY FRESH AND UNDER-USED. Three things. (a) The rotulismo reframing is real, and the argument that only motion can do it — a still flower on a bus always reads Woodstock, a flower being brushed onto a taqueria does not — is the strongest sentence in the brief. (b) The unfinished states as printed artefacts. A four-up "84.4 % arrives in three strokes" plate is a more novel object than the film, and no competitor holds the census to make it. (c) The bare opening flank is not a blank canvas — it is the documented Nolita livery state of this same vehicle. The concept throws that away as "unfinished and slightly sad." NEW YORK BECOMING PLAYA is an object no stock asset and no competitor can produce, and rule 11 permits it precisely because the transition is temporal rather than composited.

Two grounding slips that erode the "derived, not felt" claim itself. The beat list says "THE TENDRILS — four dark-maroon S-curve commas." folk_gen holds `FLANK_TENDRILS` (4 entries, in the gold inventory) and `FLANK_DARKS` (5 entries, dark-brown ink, "5 of them carry 83 % of the dark") as separate objects. The film merges them, and in doing so gives the dark maroon no beat of its own — so the piece whose thesis is "the palette assembling itself" never actually assembles one of its five colours. And the stated shipped-tile figure (196 components, top three 66.4 %) matches neither folk_gen's own table for the photograph (66 components, 84.4 %) nor its rev-11 build (30 components, 92.5 %); the concept flags the mismatch honestly but the pacing is then derived from a census that describes no asset in the tree.

Not weak — the reframing is a real idea, the honesty about tile-versus-photograph is exemplary, and the poster series is close to genuinely new. Not strong — as specified this is a competent livery reveal with a signwriter's ordering, and competent must not exceed workable.
fatal_flaws: THE DIFFERENTIATOR IS INVISIBLE TO THE AUDIENCE. The census-derived order (folk_gen `COMP_TOP`/`COMP_HIST`, which I reproduced: 48 components = 2.29 %, top 3 = 84.4 %) produces exactly the order an animator would choose by instinct — big shapes, then details, then type. Provenance is authoring hygiene, not novelty. Strip the ledger and this is the standard build-on reveal.

THE EXECUTION AS SPECIFIED IS A MASK WIPE, NOT A BRUSH. `model_work_required` asks for a per-component paint-order RANK driving a threshold sweep. Component-level reveal has no directionality along a stroke, so it reads as decals appearing, not as painting — the exact thing the concept claims to be the opposite of. 'Rosettes popping on offbeats, centre-out' is the After Effects default and is the single most trope-marking instruction in the brief.

THE SIGNATURE BEAT IS FORBIDDEN IN TERMS AND ITS CRAFT PREMISE IS UNCITED. SPEC §10.16: 'A monotone decay toward ground with no dark ring at any radius -- that is edge blur, not a keyline' and '**Do not add a keyline to the generator because sec.3 says so**.' The concept's model_work_required item 1 does precisely this. 'Shadow, then metal, because that is the order a signwriter actually works' appears nowhere in the repo and is not established for gilded work.

THE FIRST AND BIGGEST GESTURE IS THE SMALLEST THING ON SCREEN. hero34r is `loc=(-11.30, 9.05, 3.80)` — camera at the rear. `FLANK_MASSES` puts MASS-R1 at X -2.007..-1.557 (nearest camera, 73213 mm²) while the cab-door mass is at the far forward end at a grazing angle. Beat 2 opens on the distant, foreshortened mass and works toward the viewer, so 'big confident gestures land first' inverts on screen. The pacing argument — the whole emotional claim — depends on apparent size, and the ordering is by surface area.

THE DARK MAROON NEVER GETS ITS BEAT. The brief's thesis is 'the palette assembling itself' from two colours to five, but beat 3 conflates `FLANK_TENDRILS` (4, gold) with `FLANK_DARKS` (5, dark-brown ink, 'five of them carry 83 % of the dark') and animates four things it calls dark-maroon. One of the five inks is dropped from the film that exists to assemble five inks.
improvements: ANIMATE ARC-LENGTH ALONG THE STROKE, NOT COMPONENT RANK. This is the single change that moves the piece from livery-reveal to signwriting. folk_gen authors these masses from stroke paths already (`ONE CONNECTED MASS filling the box (x0..x1, z0..z1)` around the mass builder) — so emit, per pixel, (stroke_id, t along centreline, half-width at t) into spare channels of swirl.png/swirl_b.png rather than a per-component rank. Sweep on t. The reveal then travels the brush's path with a taper, which no threshold sweep can fake and which is the literal difference between a decal appearing and a person painting.

RE-ORDER BY PROJECTED AREA IN THE CHOSEN FRAME, AND SAY THAT IS THE MEASUREMENT. folk_gen's areas are surface mm² (MASS-R1 73213, MASS-R2 30285); on hero34r the cab-door mass is far and grazing. Project each component through the built hero34r camera and rank by pixel area in THAT frame. This fixes the inverted pacing, and 'the order it reads in this shot' is a fresher and more defensible measurement than raw surface area — it is a census nobody else could have run.

RE-HOME THE KEYLINE BEAT OR GROUND IT — DO NOT SHIP IT INTO script_gen. Two honest routes. (a) Declare the film a STYLISED artefact that makes no fidelity claim, draw the keyline in the film's own compositing layer only, and never touch the generator — SPEC §10.16 governs the generator, not art direction, and saying so explicitly is what keeps it legal. (b) Ground it: §10.16 names its own remedy, 'establish it from a higher-resolution photograph'. PHOTOS_WANTED has no script item; add one — a close, square-on frame of the wordmark. Either way, drop the assertion about signwriters' work order or cite a source; as written it is a figure nobody watched print.

MAKE IT NEW YORK BECOMING PLAYA, NOT BLANK BECOMING PAINTED. The opening bare flank is the documented Nolita state of this vehicle, not an empty canvas. Open on state B fully dressed — plain red, TACOMBI.COM on the counter fascia, the chalkboard lid — and let the folk art arrive over it. That is a history rather than a reveal, it is an object no stock asset and no competitor can produce, and rule 11 permits it precisely because the transition is temporal. It also gives beat 1 something to look at instead of 'unfinished and slightly sad'.

REPLACE THE OFFBEAT ROSETTE POP WITH A RELOAD RHYTHM. A signwriter does not pop rosettes to a beat; they lay a row, reloading between each, working spatially. Sequence the eight `FLANK_ROSETTES` in a left-to-right spatial pass with a held pause between each (the reload) and a slight size/pressure variation. Same eight objects, same census, and the trope-marking beat-sync is gone.

GIVE THE FORTY-EIGHT A SECOND MEANING: WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE. 'Dust settling' renders as a pop. Instead, show them arrive — then cut to the apparel-scale version where they are gone (the brief's own measurement: p10 collapses to 0.18 mm at 1:14.5, 95 of 196 components under 0.52 mm at the thickest point). A piece about which marks survive translation to a shirt is an idea nobody in this category is making, and it uses the sacrifice rule as content rather than as production trivia.

LEAD WITH THE PROGRESSION PLATE, NOT THE FILM. The unfinished frames are the most novel artefact here and they are currently a by-product. A four-up A2 — bare / three masses / plus rosettes / finished — with the census as the only typography ('three strokes, 84.4 %') is a genuinely new object; 'a VW bus mid-painting' does not exist in the market. Ship that first; it is cheap, it needs no stroke-order channel, and it de-risks the film.

FIX THE INVENTORY IN THE BEAT LIST AND GIVE THE DARK INK ITS OWN MOMENT. `FLANK_TENDRILS` is four gold objects; `FLANK_DARKS` is five dark-brown objects carrying 83 % of the dark. Split them: gold tendrils in beat 3, the five dark commas as their own beat, and let the dark maroon be the colour that changes the drawing's temperature. The film's thesis is the palette assembling; make all five inks actually arrive.

STATE WHICH DRAWING YOU CENSUSED, IN THE FILM'S OWN CREDIT LINE. folk_gen's table reads ref_side 66 components / 84.4 % in top three against rev 11's 30 / 92.5 %; the brief quotes a shipped tile at 196 / 66.4 % that matches neither. Re-run the census on the exact tile you animate, publish that number, and drop the borrowed one — the 'derived, not felt' claim is the whole differentiator and it cannot rest on a figure that describes no asset in the tree.

verdicts.lens: PRODUCIBILITY AND FIDELITY — can this be made from THIS asset, on THIS machine, given the failing gates, the missing artwork, the held delivery render and the unproven large-format chain? What breaks, and what model work is unscoped?
verdicts.reasoning:
This is the most producible motion idea I could imagine against this tree, and it is still not producible as written. Its mechanism is genuinely cheap — nothing geometric moves, the camera is locked, and the reveal is an alpha threshold. `T1_W_ART` is real and is exactly what the concept says it is (t1_mats.py: `W_ART = float(os.environ.get("T1_W_ART", 1.00))`, applied as one MULTIPLY on the art alpha at `amask = _math(nt, 'MULTIPLY', amask.outputs[0], W_ART, 240, -1240)`), so the prototype claim holds. Better than the concept knows: `folk_gen.composition()` ALREADY labels its own output's connected components and returns `areas` and a `top` dict — the per-component rank needs no new measurement, only a re-target from the flank sampling grid to the emitted tile.

But the concept never states its render economics, and they are fatal as written. 14 s at 24 fps is 336 frames; HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §6 measures `render 1600x1100 96 spp ~4.5-5.5 min PER VIEW` on `cores 4`, with fan-out forbidden — roughly 31 hours of render at PREVIEW resolution, plus 336 hand-regenerations of the tile (folk_gen.py is not called by build.py) and 336 rebuilds. And studio.py's own comment kills the batch route: "The sandbox reaps background processes, so a 20-minute hero cannot run to completion in one go."

Worse, and entirely unnamed: per-frame sampling noise. I measured out/r75_side.png against out/r75b_side.png — two renders of one tree, per the rev-76 brief — through photometry.read_png at full depth: **4.385 % of pixels differ by >8 levels (8-bit equivalent), 0.057 % by >32, worst channel 40.4**. Nothing in the render path sets `cycles.seed` (the only hits in the tree are inside probe_rev55_truenorm.py). On a locked-off shot that is an independent noise realisation every frame across 4.4 % of the image — visible boil, over the whole body, for fourteen seconds.

Then the fidelity problem the screener's note repeats without checking. The pacing argument — "three strokes carry 84.4 %, forty-eight carry 2.29 %" — is `COMP_TOP`/`COMP_HIST` in folk_gen.py, and the comment two lines above them says what they are: "Connected components of the gold, `ref_side.jpg`". That is the PHOTOGRAPH. I labelled the shipped tile that would actually be animated (tex/swirl.png, 4096², alpha>128, 8-connected): **177 components; top 1/2/3 carry 32.4 / 61.4 / 77.7 %; 128 components carry the smallest 2.29 %.** The concept is honest that a gap exists but quotes 196 components / 66.4 % — and neither of those reproduces either. So the film's headline beat ("two seconds, 84 % of the drawing") and its climactic beat ("THE FORTY-EIGHT") are both statistics about a different drawing.

The good news, and it is the reason this is not weak: the ORDERING survives on the real asset. The three largest tile components are three spatially distinct masses (rows 1980–2591 cols 0–1189; rows 1844–2227 cols 1395–2176; rows 1844–2283 cols 1058–1402) at 32.4 / 29.0 / 16.3 %. Beat 2 is structurally supportable — just at 77.7 %, not 84.4 %.

Beat 6, the idea the screener rightly calls the best thing here, depends on an asset feature that does not exist. I measured tex/senor.png (4096×1738 RGBA): among pixels with alpha > 200 the **minimum luma is 145.7 and the fraction below luma 80 is 0.0000** — there is no dark ink anywhere in the file — and script_gen.py contains no keyline or shadow code. The concept identifies this correctly as required work, which is to its credit; it is nonetheless the whole emotional payload sitting on unbuilt art.

Two things the concept gets right that I could not fault: the hero34r clipping (I measured the subject's non-white bbox running to **x = 1599 of 1600** — the counter is hard-clipped at the right edge; hero34f clips at x = 0 too), and the absence of the ablation it needs (grep for T1_LIVERY / T1_NOART / T1_NOSCRIPT / T1_NODECAL returns nothing; only W_ART exists, and it gates the folk art alone, not script_L or calidad_L).
