One thing it gets wrong on its own terms. It invokes rule 11 to defend the transition — "you are watching state B become state A, not compositing them." What beat 1 actually renders is state A with the flank decals switched off: the flower-mural lid, the counter, the bobble fringe and the menu cards are all still state-A dressing. State B has a chalkboard/awning lid, gold lettering on the serving glass and TACOMBI.COM on the fascia, none of which exists as an asset in tex/. So beat 1 is a third livery that never existed — precisely the composite that killed F99, F100 and F140.

Finally, a self-inflicted exposure. The concept chooses a warm LOW raking key so the gold catches. That is the exact condition under which gloss_compare's failure is loudest — the render's paint spreads 0.412 of the photograph's against a 0.60 bar, across 787k px² of red and 2.03M px² of cream in the delivery frame per visibility_budget on this very view. Raking light on a lobe that broad reads as vinyl, and the film's subject is the flank.

Workable, not weak: every one of these has a concrete fix, and the biggest one (improvement 2) collapses the cost by three orders of magnitude and removes the flicker entirely.
fatal_flaws: RENDER ECONOMICS ARE UNSTATED AND PROHIBITIVE AS WRITTEN. 14 s x 24 fps = 336 frames; HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §6 measures '~4.5-5.5 min PER VIEW' at 1600x1100/96 spp on 'cores 4' with fan-out forbidden -> ~31 h of render at PREVIEW resolution, before the 336 hand-regenerations of the tile (folk_gen.py is not called by build.py) and 336 rebuilds. studio.py closes the batch escape: 'The sandbox reaps background processes, so a 20-minute hero cannot run to completion in one go.' The concept's production_notes say 'one full rebuild per pose' and never multiply it out.

PER-FRAME CYCLES NOISE WILL BOIL THE WHOLE FRAME, AND IT IS UNNAMED. Measured by me on the two side frames the rev-76 brief calls renders of ONE tree, read through photometry.read_png at full depth: 4.385 % of pixels differ by >8 levels (8-bit equivalent), 0.057 % by >32, worst channel 40.4. No cycles.seed is set anywhere in the render path (the only hits are inside probe_rev55_truenorm.py). On a locked-off camera that is an independent noise realisation every frame over 4.4 % of the image, for 14 seconds. This is the defect a static shot is least able to hide.

THE CENSUS THE ENTIRE PACING RESTS ON IS OF THE PHOTOGRAPH, NOT OF THE TILE BEING ANIMATED — AND THE CONCEPT'S OWN CORRECTION FIGURES DO NOT REPRODUCE EITHER. folk_gen.py's comment directly above the constants reads 'Connected components of the gold, `ref_side.jpg`'. I labelled tex/swirl.png (4096^2, alpha>128, 8-connected): 177 components; top 1/2/3 = 32.4/29.0/16.3 %, cumulative 77.7 %; 128 components carry the smallest 2.29 %. Against the concept's headline 84.4 % / forty-eight, and against its stated correction of 196 components / 66.4 %. The screener's 'the paint ORDER is a measurement, not a mood' is true of ref_side.jpg and not yet true of the asset.

BEAT 1 IS A LIVERY STATE THAT NEVER EXISTED, AND THE CONCEPT INVOKES RULE 11 TO DEFEND IT. Switching the flank art off leaves the state-A flower-mural lid, counter, bobble fringe and menu cards in frame. Real state B has a chalkboard/awning lid, gold lettering on the serving glass and TACOMBI.COM on the fascia — none of which exists as an asset (tex/ holds calidad, emblem, lidmural, lidsign, nose, senor, swirl, swirl_b, and nothing else). 'State B becoming state A' is not what is on screen; a third, invented state is. That is the composite that killed F99, F100 and F140.

BEAT 6 — THE BEST IDEA IN THE CONCEPT — HAS NO ASSET. Measured on tex/senor.png (4096x1738 RGBA): among pixels with alpha > 200 the minimum luma is 145.7 and the fraction below luma 80 is exactly 0.0000. There is no dark ink in the file, and script_gen.py has no keyline or shadow code, against SPEC §3's 'SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow'. The film's closing beat is 'the shadow arrives one frame before the metal' and the shadow does not exist.
improvements: STOP RENDERING FRAMES. RENDER TWO, AND DO THE REVEAL IN 2D. Nothing geometric moves and the light is fixed, so the difference between 'mass 1 present' and 'mass 1 absent' is very nearly a matte composite. Render the BARE state and the FINISHED state once each with T1_ALPHA=1 (studio.py's `_alpha_delivery()` branch; F159 measured the proof frame at 57.9 % transparent / 25.5 % opaque / 16.6 % partial, with the contact shadow surviving in partial alpha), take deliver.py's `layers/*_no_shadow.png` and `*_shadow_only.png`, and drive the reveal at 2D with the per-component rank map. That takes the budget from ~31 hours to ~11 minutes, removes the inter-frame Cycles noise ENTIRELY (two realisations, not 336), and makes the piece editable at compositor speed. GUARD IT, do not assume it: render ONE intermediate state in 3D and A/B it against the 2D composite of the same state, against the measured 4.385 %/>8-levels floor. If the 2D composite sits inside that floor, the shortcut is proven; if it does not, you have measured the folk art's own light contribution for the first time. Watch that A/B fail on a deliberately wrong composite before you believe it passing.

RE-DERIVE THE CENSUS ON THE TILE AND REBUILD THE PACING ON IT — THE FUNCTION ALREADY EXISTS. `folk_gen.composition()` labels its own output's gold components (`M = ndimage.binary_closing(gold, ...)`, `L, n = ndimage.label(M, ...)`) and returns `areas`, `n` and a `top` dict for k in (1,2,3,5,10); `report_composition()` already prints 'ref_side' beside 'achieved'. Two changes: (a) run it and quote the ACHIEVED column, never COMP_TOP; (b) re-target the labelling from the flank sampling grid and the separate 1 mm/px door plane onto the emitted 4096^2 tile in tile-UV space, which is where the animation needs the ranks. My reading of the tile gives 177 / 77.7 % / 128 — treat that as an indication and let the script print its own. Then rewrite the beats: 'THREE STROKES, 78 % OF THE DRAWING' and 'THE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-EIGHT'. Both are still remarkable; both are then true of the thing on screen. Publish the ref_side figures beside them as the photograph's, explicitly labelled, so the difference between the drawing and its source is part of the story rather than a hidden defect.

CUT THE FRAME RATE ARGUMENT INTO THE IDEA. Even after improvement 1, do not smooth-fade. Signwriting is discrete: a stroke is laid or it is not. Cut the reveal on TWOS or THREES with hard state changes and no cross-dissolve — 12–16 distinct states, held. That is truer to the subject, it is immune to whatever inter-frame residue survives the 2D route, and it removes the one thing that would read as CGI in a film whose whole argument is anti-CGI. It also makes the 'forty-eight/one-hundred-and-twenty-eight in ONE FRAME' beat land harder, because every other beat has also been a hard cut.

AUTHOR THE KEYLINE, REGENERATE BY HAND, AND GUARD IT SO IT CANNOT VANISH. lid_gen.py already carries the convention (`DARKLINE = (72, 26, 16)`); add the keyline and drop shadow in script_gen.py, regenerate tex/senor.png BY HAND (script_gen.py is not called by build.py — CLAUDE.md and §6 both say so, and this has cost revisions), and add a verify_clone.sh row that reads the ASSET's own fraction of alpha>200 pixels below luma 80 and goes RED at zero. Watch it fail on the current file first — it will, at 0.0000, which I measured. Without that row the film's closing beat can silently disappear on any regeneration.

FIX THE LOCKUP'S PLACEMENT IN THE SAME EDIT, OR DO NOT HERO THE WORDMARK. flank_compare on out/r75_side.png reports 'the render's lockup has to move +76.2 mm forward and -47.6 mm down', corroborated by an independent route at +83/+80 mm aft with the ink top +61.1 mm high. Beat 6 is a close-up of that lockup at the film's climax. AND THE TRAP, which the concept names and which must stay named in the ledger: do NOT let the fix drift into 'improving' the Senor row toward the photograph — F156 records that row as scoring a DELIBERATE DEPARTURE since F157 ('Bright silver, same as Tacombi'), that ruling covers THAT WORD ONLY, and the gate reads the departure as improvement and will not warn you.

RESOLVE THE LIVERY-STATE CLAIM BEFORE ANYONE WRITES IT DOWN. Drop 'state B becomes state A' from every note. Either (a) frame beat 1 honestly as 'the panel before the painter' — a sanctioned fiction, named as one, with the precedent stated: SPEC measures the papel picado ABSENT from the reference ('Bunting in that render would be an invention') and the owner locked it into the sticker scene anyway, so he accepts invention when it is declared; or (b) confine the reveal to the flank artwork and never claim a city. Option (a) is stronger and costs nothing but a sentence.

BUILD THREE INDEPENDENT ABLATIONS AND WATCH EACH ONE PRODUCE A GENUINELY BARE PANEL. There is no switch for the script or the Calidad decal — grep for T1_LIVERY / T1_NOART / T1_NOSCRIPT / T1_NODECAL returns nothing across the tree. W_ART is a single global MULTIPLY on the folk-art alpha only. Beat 1 needs the folk art, script_L/script_R and calidad_L gated separately, and rule 47 applies: ablate each and check the output ACTUALLY MOVED, because a ghost at low alpha will read as a smudge rather than as bare paint and no gate will tell you.

RE-AIM THE CAMERA BEFORE DESIGNING TO IT, AND RE-MEASURE. I measured out/r75_hero34r.png: the subject's non-white bbox runs to x = 1599 of 1600 — the counter, the single element that makes this read as a taqueria rather than a van, is hard-clipped at the right edge (out/r75_hero34f.png clips at x = 0 likewise). The concept's own composition note puts 'the counter's brass nosing as a hard bright horizontal on the lower third'; it currently runs off. Either pull the camera and re-measure the bbox, or lead with the 1080x1920 vertical — which is the format that actually wants this crop, since the artwork is banded between the belt and the arch. Note also that hero34r has ONE rendered-file mention across LEDGER_rev66..75 against side's 27: the most Tacombi-forward angle is the least exercised, so budget for surprises.

RECONSIDER THE RAKING KEY, OR BUDGET THE RELIGHT AS A REAL F259 JOB. The warm low key is chosen to make gold catch; it is also the condition under which the render's specular deficit is loudest — gloss_compare reads the render's paint spreading 0.412 of the photograph's against a 0.60 bar, across 787k px^2 of red and 2.03M px^2 of cream on this very view per visibility_budget. Either soften and raise the key and lose a little glint, or take F259's licence properly ('Relight the studio and fix the ground if necessary'), re-read gloss_compare / flank_compare / probe_rev70_tyre afterwards, and put the before/after in the ledger. DO NOT change RED — that is the option he declined. And do not reach for T1_SCENE=playa: F57 records it renders no vehicle at all, 'a dark cylinder on a grey plane'.

SAY WHICH ARTEFACT THIS IS, IN THE FIRST LINE OF THE PROPOSAL. This is NOT F18 — F18's style is locked to 'cartoon with rendered depth' and this is photoreal, and its trigger ('build it after the model is done') has not fired. Naming that removes the hold as an objection. Separately, the delivery render is held (F191, reaffirmed F193) and 3840 is explicitly not the target (F192) — but a 1080x1920 social piece is under all three ceilings, and naming a medium is precisely the precondition F192 says unlocks the resolution ask. A one-line scoping sentence converts three apparent blockers into none.

PERSIST ONE BUILD. `build.py` supports `T1_SAVE` (`bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile`) and it appears in NO handoff document — grep returns 0 in the brief, the carriers, CLAUDE.md, README.md, START_HERE.md and OPEN_FINDINGS.md. Since this piece is a texture sweep on ONE fixed pose, saving the .blend once removes the rebuild from every subsequent state and is the only lever in the tree that reduces the per-state cost. Record it in the ledger — it is unscoped infrastructure that every future motion or multi-state piece would inherit.

verdicts.lens: Emotional resonance, brand fit and IP exposure
verdicts.reasoning:
This is the least VW-dependent and most Tacombi-owned idea a program built on this asset can make: every element that appears on screen — the gold masses, the tendrils, the rosettes, the silver wordmark — is Tacombi's own commissioned paint, not Volkswagen's. It also does the one reframe the market brief says is worth more than anything else (florals from Woodstock to Mexican hand-painting) in the only medium that can do it. The pacing is derived, not felt: I verified folk_gen.py's census live — `COMP_TOP = {1: 47.8, 2: 73.7, 3: 84.4, 5: 87.8, 10: 93.5}` and COMP_HIST's first three bins (24, 21, 3 components at 0.42/1.32/0.55 %) do sum to 48 components carrying 2.29 %. The two-seconds-then-ten-seconds shape is a real property of this vehicle's paint. And the unfinished-state poster series is the single freshest artefact in the whole program: nobody sells "a VW bus being painted", and the states are printable straight off the reveal.

It is not exceptional for three reasons, and the first two are load-bearing on the lens.

IP: "it keeps the VW roundel entirely out of frame" is false as written. `t1_detail.py` builds a VW glyph on every hubcap — `glyph = T.vw_bars(1.0, CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC, ... tag=f"capvw{side}")`, and build.py's `_WHEEL_PREFIX = ("tyre", "rim", "cap", "capvw")` — so a 3/4 rear flank view carries four VW roundels, plus the closed T1 silhouette that the market brief records as itself claimed as a mark ("The images of classic Beetle and Bus vehicles are themselves protected as trademarks"). Worse for a piece that intends to be scrutinised: STATE.md says of exactly that mark "hubcap badge is SELF-CONSISTENCY ONLY -- CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC has never been compared to a frame". The only VW mark in frame is the one nothing has ever checked against a photograph.

EMOTION: the whole payload rides on one unsourced sentence — "that is the order a signwriter actually works: shadow, then metal", and behind it the claim that ornament-before-lettering is the trade's order at all. There is no citation anywhere in the concept, and the project's own rules forbid publishing a figure or a claim you have not watched print. The audience most likely to amplify a sign-painting film is sign painters, and they will name it if it is wrong. The screener's praise ("trade knowledge nobody will name and everybody will feel") is precisely the failure mode: it is being graded on plausibility.

BUILDABILITY OF THE FEELING: the copy promises "ONE wet stroke over ~8 frames" and a mahl stick; the prescribed mechanism is "a per-component paint-order rank into an unused channel ... so the animation is a threshold sweep". A rank channel gives pop-on, not stroke-on. Pop-on reads as motion graphics — a texture appearing on a 3D object — which is the exact opposite of "SOMEONE MADE THIS", and it is anti-CGI-ness is the concept's stated differentiator. There is no hand, no brush and no wet edge anywhere in the deliverable.

Credit where earned: the state transition is chronologically true, not invented — LEDGER_rev51 grades the plain Nolita flank "RED, EARLIER" and the folk-art flank "RED, CURRENT" — so this is the bus's own history, and the concept is right that a temporal transition is legitimate where a blended frame would be a fake. The F259 relight is correctly scoped (rig open, RED untouched), the F156/F157 trap is correctly flagged, and the keyline defect is real: I measured tex/senor.png myself — among alpha>200 pixels the 1st-percentile luma is 167.0 and the fraction below luma 80 is exactly 0.0000. There is no dark ink in the asset at all, so beat 6 currently animates something that does not exist.
fatal_flaws: THE IP CLAIM IS WRONG IN THE ONE PLACE IT MATTERS. 'It keeps the VW roundel entirely out of frame' holds only for the nose. t1_detail.py builds `glyph = T.vw_bars(1.0, CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC, ... tag=f"capvw{side}")` on every hubcap and build.py lists `capvw` in `_WHEEL_PREFIX`, so a 3/4 rear flank frame carries four VW marks — and STATE.md says of that exact mark 'hubcap badge is SELF-CONSISTENCY ONLY -- CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC has never been compared to a frame'. The only VW glyph on screen is the only one never checked against a photograph. Add the closed T1 silhouette, which the market brief records as itself trademarked, and the concept's central IP advantage is asserted rather than achieved.

THE EMOTIONAL KEYSTONE IS UNSOURCED TRADE LORE. 'The dark keyline arrives one frame before the silver, because that is the order a signwriter actually works: shadow, then metal' has no citation in the concept, in the repo, or anywhere it points. Nor does the larger premise that a rotulista lays ornament before lettering — a signwriter more usually sets the lettering layout first because it is the element that must land, and ornament fills around it. The concept's own inherited AUDIT row ('THE FLANK IS A TRIPTYCH AND THE WORDMARK SITS IN A 1.51 m GAP') is consistent with either order. The film's entire claim to authenticity is one unverified sentence, and it is the sentence the screener liked most.

THE PROMISED FEELING IS NOT PRODUCIBLE BY THE PRESCRIBED MECHANISM. 'Laid down as ONE wet stroke over ~8 frames' requires directional growth along each stroke's path with a soft leading edge. model_work_required asks only for 'a per-component paint-order RANK into an unused channel ... so the animation is a threshold sweep' — which yields components popping on in size order. Pop-on is motion graphics. There is no hand, no brush, no mahl stick and no wet edge in the deliverable, so 'SOMEONE MADE THIS' is carried entirely by the copy and not by anything on screen.

IT IS A FOURTEEN-SECOND TACOMBI FILM WITH NO FOOD, NO PEOPLE, NO PLACE AND NOTHING SERVED. The vehicle's identity, on this project's own reading, is the CONVERSION — three serving hatches born of missing windows, the cantilevered counter, the bulb string, the propped tail board. This piece uses the flank as a wall and the counter's brass line as a static compositional rail. It is a beautiful craft film about paint that could, with a different subject in frame, be about any hand-painted object anywhere.

THE TITLE OVERSELLS THE CATEGORY. 'ROTULISTA' names a sign painter; rótulos are hand-painted commercial signage, which describes the SILVER WORDMARK. The gold acanthus, rosettes and comma tendrils belong to the decorative vehicle-painting tradition, not to rotulismo. The title claims a lineage for the florals that the florals do not have, in a concept whose whole argument is that the florals have been misfiled once already.
improvements: REFRAME TO THE BAND, NOT THE BUS — this single change fixes the IP hole, the vertical cutdown and the hero34r clipping at once. The concept already states the artwork lives 'in the band between the belt line and the arch'. Crop to that band, bleeding off all four edges: no hubcaps (kills all four `capvw` VW glyphs), no closed T1 silhouette (kills the shape mark), no clipped counter. The 1080x1920 vertical stops being a derived cutdown and becomes the native frame. Then say plainly in the client note what remains: the vehicle is a VW and the film is a Tacombi paint film, and no VW mark appears in it — a claim you can then actually defend.

GET THE PAINT ORDER FROM A PERSON, NOT FROM A CENSUS. The census proves what is BIG, not what came FIRST — those are different claims and the concept conflates them. Two routes nobody has tried: (a) ask the owner who painted the bus, whether Tacombi commissioned the rotulista, and whether any photograph or footage of the painting exists — this is a Tacombi-owned fact one message away; (b) if it cannot be recovered, restate the claim honestly on screen and in the deck as 'largest first, by measured area' and DELETE 'that is the order a signwriter actually works'. The honest version is still a strong idea; the unsourced version is the kind of detail that gets the piece dunked on by the exact community it courts.

MAKE THE STROKE A STROKE. folk_gen.py draws the acanthus from parametric curves — it knows each stroke's PATH, not merely its area. Have it emit an arc-length parameter per component (0..1 along the stroke) alongside the order rank, so the reveal grows along the brush direction with a 2-3 px soft leading edge and a faint darker wet margin that dries off over ~4 frames. That is the difference between a texture appearing and a stroke being made, and it is the difference between this piece and a Lottie file. Prototype it on ONE component — the cab-door mass — before committing the whole tile.

END ON THE SHOP OPENING, NOT ON THE PAINT DRYING. Add a beat 8: the bulb string ignites along the drip rail and the nearest serving hatch's shutter goes up. Two seconds. It converts a craft film into a Tacombi film, it picks up the one motif the market research says is uniquely this brand's ('missing three of its windows' is why the serving hatches exist), and it gives the loop a reason to loop — paint, open, serve, wipe to bare red. Without it the piece's last frame is indistinguishable from a still.

BUILD THE KEYLINE PROPERLY AND GIVE THE BEAT TIME TO READ. I re-measured tex/senor.png: among alpha>200 pixels the 1st-percentile luma is 167.0 and the fraction below luma 80 is 0.0000 — there is no dark ink in the asset whatsoever, so the film's closing beat currently has nothing to animate. Author it in script_gen.py using lid_gen.py's own existing convention (`DARKLINE = (72, 26, 16)`), regenerate by hand (script_gen is not called by build.py), and add a guard that reads the asset's sub-luma-80 fraction and goes red at zero. Then stage the beat at 3 frames (125 ms), not 1 (42 ms) — one frame at 24 fps is below the threshold at which a viewer registers order rather than simultaneity, and the whole point is that they feel the order.

MAKE THE POSTER SERIES ITSELF THE MEASUREMENT — this is the strongest artefact in the concept and it is currently under-specified. Pull the four states at the census's own inflection points rather than at arbitrary beats: 1 component (47.8 % of the gold), 3 (84.4 %), 10 (93.5 %), all 66. Set the percentage as the only caption, small, in the house Bookman/Cooper family the market brief identifies. Four prints that are simultaneously a drawing and a proof, and nobody else on earth can make them because nobody else has counted this bus's paint.

RENAME IT, OR EARN THE NAME. 'ROTULISTA' describes the wordmark's tradition, not the florals'. Either retitle to something that covers both ('A MANO', or the painter's name if the owner can supply it), or keep ROTULISTA and restructure so the film's climax is explicitly the LETTERING — which would also resolve the ordering problem, because lettering-last is defensible when the piece is about the letterer.

STATE WHICH DRAWING YOU ANIMATED, ON THE FRAME. The concept is admirably honest in its production notes that the shipped tile (196 components, top three carrying 66.4 %) is a different drawing from the photograph the census describes (66 components, top three 84.4 %). But the ordering is the film's ENTIRE claim to being derived. If you animate the shipped tile with the photograph's census, the pacing is a fiction dressed as a measurement. Either re-census the shipped tile and pace to ITS numbers, or fix the tile's fragmentation first — and say which in the ledger, the client note and the caption of the poster series.

audited_finalists.title: The Same Camera, Twenty Years Later

concept.title: The Same Camera, Twenty Years Later
concept.one_line: Render the 2006 photograph from the 2006 photograph's own recovered camera, in its own measured light, with its own plants at their measured depths — and hang the two side by side.
concept.the_image: A PAIR, or a dissolve between them, and the entire effect is that NOTHING SLIDES. LEFT / 2006: ref_rear34.jpg exactly as it is, 1200 × 824, warm and soft — the woman resting her cheek on her hand at a chrome-legged formica table, orange vinyl chairs, a green-checked cloth, the napkin dispenser, the palm trunk dead centre, the hand-lettered yellow sign FAVOR DE ORDENAR Y PAGAR AQUÍ, the mural lid up and blazing orange in the top right, the tail with its '1963' plate. RIGHT / 2026: the identical frame rebuilt. Same camera position, same lens, same light, same vegetation — and the bus rendered at full fidelity, sharp to the rivet. THE PEOPLE, THE CHAIRS AND THE TABLES ARE NOT THERE, and that absence is the content, not a cheat: what this project holds, measured, is the vehicle and the planting. LIGHT SPEC, EVERY NUMBER MEASURED AND QUOTABLE, all from studio.playa()'s own docstring and playa_env.py's header: NO sun, NO sky, NO haze, NO dapple gobo — all four are measured ABSENCES, not omissions. One large low LATERAL source (the palapa's single opening) under an absorbing ceiling. The signatures that identify it: the same red reads 3.95 : 1 between the flank facing the opening and the tail face 72° away; the palm trunk runs 12.5 : 1 across its own diameter; an up-facing cream surface is DARKER than a vertical one facing the opening (0.93 : 1) and brighter than one turned away (1.87 : 1). Shadows are WARMER, not bluer — the bright/dark ground split measures db* +2.4, which is the opposite sign to a sun/skylight pair. Foliage sits 52.1 L* below the cream (foliage L* 32.7, cream L* 84.8), and the band across the top of frame is a continuous polychrome FLOWERING mass — 55.1 % foliage, 13.4 % crimson heads, 5.5 % cream florets, jagged interpenetrating lower edge. Palette is therefore: one soft lateral wash, no specular highlight anywhere in frame, cream at the top of the range, a 52-unit drop into green, and warm shadow. Set beneath the pair in a hairline: the lens, the camera coordinates, and the two years. MOTION ARM: 4 s cross-dissolve, 3 s hold each end, looping. Because the camera is IDENTICAL the palm trunk lands on the palm trunk and the roof line lands on the roof line — that perfect registration is the whole trick, and it exists only because someone solved the pose.
concept.emotional_claim: Vertigo, then reverence. You know this photograph — it is the founding image — and now you are standing inside it, and it is sharp, and everyone has gone home. It is the feeling of a measured survey drawing of a building you have eaten in: not nostalgia (nostalgia is soft and this is the sharpest thing in the room), but the quiet astonishment that somebody went and measured the afternoon. And it makes an argument no copy line could: the lunch ended, the people left, the bus is still there.
formats: GALLERY PAIR, TWO PRINTS AT ~200 × 137 mm, hung 60 mm apart in matched frames. THE SIZE IS SET BY THE PHOTOGRAPH, NOT BY THE RENDER, and this is the honest constraint: ref_rear34.jpg is 1200 × 824 native, so 200 mm wide is ~152 dpi and 297 mm would be ~103 dpi. Print it INTIMATE. Match the render's apparent sharpness to the photograph's rather than letting the render out-resolve its partner — the pair only works if they are the same object seen twice, not a snapshot next to a CGI flex.

THE FOUNDING-STORY WALL, one pair per location, by the till or the queue — the 'how we know' panel. This is where a brand puts provenance instead of an advert, and it satisfies the insider test: it rewards the person who has stood in that yard and says nothing embarrassing to anyone else.
4-SECOND DISSOLVE LOOP at 1200 × 824 native — do not upscale. In-store screens, social, and the About page. The dissolve is the only motion this asset needs and it moves nothing in the frame.
PRINTED SPREAD: photograph verso, render recto, gutter down the middle, in any book, menu insert or anniversary piece. The gutter does the dissolve's job in print.
NOT A T-SHIRT AND NOT A STICKER. This artefact dies at small scale — its whole content is fine registration between two images. Do not let it be reduced.
concept.why_not_derivative: It is structurally impossible for anyone else to make. It requires all four of: the original photograph, a photorealistic measured reconstruction of that exact vehicle, a SOLVED camera for that exact frame, and a measured reconstruction of that exact environment. The camera is not estimated — studio.py records it as recovered from the rear rim flange conic fit (139.1 px = 0.440 m → 316 px/m), the horizon row and the wheel-ellipse axis ratio, and then CONFIRMED by a feature the solve never saw: it predicts the bus's far top corner at image column 554.6 and the cream lid panel is read at 555. Every VW-bus print in the market is a drawing of a generic bus. This is a photograph and its own forensic double, and the seventy-five revisions of measurement everyone treats as overhead become the product.
concept.production_notes: TWO THINGS GATE THIS AND BOTH ARE OWNER-SHAPED, NOT TECHNICAL. (1) F57 is OPEN and undiagnosed: 'T1_SCENE=playa RENDERS NO VEHICLE. Asked for a hero through build.py's own playa path, the frame comes back as a dark cylinder on a grey plane — the ground disc and nothing else … Found by LOOKING; every exit code was clean.' It has never been diagnosed because nobody has had a reason to. This concept is the reason. (2) F92 rules the Playa hero 'DEPRIORITISED, NOT CANCELLED' and HANDOFF_CARRIERS §4 is explicit that it licenses NOTHING TO DO NOW — 'Do not re-ask it; do not act on it either.' So this concept must be PUT TO HIM, as multiple choice with the pair mocked up, not started. It is also the strongest possible occasion to put it: F92 is the carrier of 'the emotional bar that sits ABOVE clinical accuracy', which is exactly what this asset is for. TECHNICAL NOTE THAT WILL BITE: studio._cull_foreground hides pl_* geometry standing between camera and vehicle, and its own docstring explains why — plants placed for the reference camera are correctly behind the bus from that bearing and wrongly in front of it from a hero bearing. For playa_ref specifically the culling must be OFF, because that camera is the one every mass was placed for. Verify it, watch it, and say which you ran. DO NOT publish a latitude/longitude in the caption: no coordinate for that yard exists anywhere in this repository and inventing one would be exactly the class of unverified figure this project has spent seventy revisions removing. Caption with what is measured — lens, camera vector, the two years — and let the owner supply the place line.
model_work_required: DIAGNOSE F57. T1_SCENE=playa currently renders no vehicle at all. Reported at rev 57b, never diagnosed, and every other item here is downstream of it.

RUN playa_env AND LOOK AT IT. It is 74 KB of measured, self-contained procedural planting with eleven masses placed by inverting the reference camera, and grounding shows ZERO rendered-file mentions for playa, playa_ref or playa_w across LEDGER_rev66..rev75. It has never been looked at in ten revisions. Render playa_ref once, crop it, and compare it against ref_rear34.jpg — that comparison IS the deliverable and it has never been made.
CONFIRM _cull_foreground IS DISABLED FOR playa_ref, and add a row that says so in its own label. Culling on this one camera would remove the exact plants the frame exists to show.

F74(a), OPEN AND DIRECTLY IN FRAME: 'tex/lidmural.png is cropped at the bottom — the bottom row of flowers is sliced mid-bloom and the yellow side columns are truncated, where ref_side.jpg shows a board framed on all four sides. The render is faithful to the asset, so the defect is in lid_gen.py's output.' The mural lid is the largest, loudest, most saturated object in the upper right of this exact frame. Regenerate BY HAND — lid_gen.py is NOT called by build.py, so a stale texture ships silently.

RESOLVE WHICH FACE OF THE LID CARRIES THE MURAL. lid_gen.py says the OUTWARD/upper face; SPEC §4 says the underside; t1_shell.py's own comment says the mural faces the counter and calls that the one arrangement reproducing all three photographs. Unresolved in live source, and in this frame it decides what the biggest object in the picture is.

THE TAIL BOARD'S DARK ANGLED RECESS IS n = 1 AND SHOULD STAY UNBUILT (F325: 30 × 12 px, 58 pixels below lum 90, in a 480 × 320 frame that is byte-identical to another reference — so it is one sighting, not two). It is visible in this composition. Leave it out and say why; that is a real result, not a to-do.

COLOUR CEILING TO CARRY, NOT TO FIX: flank_compare on out/r75_side.png reads the render's red at median (196,81,67), G/R 0.422, against the photograph's (158,16,6), G/R 0.114 — it images salmon. In THIS concept the error is maximally exposed because the photograph is hanging beside it. The remedy is a print GRADE on the output file, which is outside F259's 'DO NOT change RED' (that governs the model's paint). Say which you did, in the ledger, in the same edit.

verdicts.lens: ORIGINALITY — is this genuinely fresh, or a well-executed version of something already on a thousand VW-bus products (and, separately, on a thousand non-VW products)?
verdicts.reasoning:
WHERE IT EARNS THE SCORE. Against the category, it is clean. The grounding's own trope census for VW-bus merch is sunset silhouette, surf, hippie flower-power, 70s/80s wash, minimal line art, blueprint diagram, boho/watercolour/pop-art. This resembles none of them, and it is the only concept I have seen that makes the project's seventy-five revisions of measurement into the subject rather than the overhead. The single most original artefact in the whole document is one sentence in studio.py that the concept buries in `why_not_derivative`: the camera "predicts the bus's far top corner at image column 554.6 and the cream lid panel is read at 555." A held-out feature confirming a pose solve is not something any competitor can fake, borrow, or buy.

WHERE IT IS BORROWED, AND THE CONCEPT NEVER SAYS SO. The container is one of the most worn forms in photography. Rephotography is a named, populated genre — Klett's Rephotographic Survey Project and Third Views, Douglas Levere's New York Changing, Larenkov's WWII ghost blends, the entire then-and-now dissolve idiom. Depopulation is equally worn — Matt Logue's Empty LA, Lucie & Simon's Silent World, the whole 2020 empty-city wave. Photograph-beside-CG-reconstruction is the house style of heritage and forensic viz (Rome Reborn class work) and is the single most common portfolio piece in CG generally: "I rebuilt this photo in 3D" is an ArtStation genre. So the concept sits inside three well-populated genres from outside its category and claims it is "structurally impossible for anyone else to make." That claim is false at the idea level and it is the weakest sentence in the document.

THE DEEPER PROBLEM: IT WEARS REPHOTOGRAPHY'S COSTUME WITHOUT ITS ENGINE. Then-and-now works because something CHANGED. Here nothing changes. Both panels show the same vehicle in the same livery — LEDGER_rev51 grades the folk-art red state "RED, CURRENT" — at the same instant, from the same camera. What differs between the panels is sharpness and population, which is not time passing, it is a clean-up. The artefact is actually a forensic survey plate and would be more original if it stopped pretending to be a rephotograph.

AND THE DATE IS INVENTED. I checked: `_getexif()` returns empty on ref_rear34.jpg, ref_side.jpg and ref_playa_34.png. Nothing in the tree dates that photograph. SPEC records the bus bought green and the taqueria opened 6 February 2006 — the frame shows the folk-art livery with the Señor Tacombi script and the mural lid, i.e. the current state, so "2006" is probably wrong as well as ungrounded. The concept explicitly and correctly refuses to invent a lat/long, then invents a year and puts it in the title.

AND THE CENTRAL CONCEIT CONTRADICTS ITS OWN ASSET. "THE PEOPLE, THE CHAIRS AND THE TABLES ARE NOT THERE, and that absence is the content, not a cheat: what this project holds, measured, is the vehicle and the planting." That is not what the project holds. playa_env.build() calls `_furniture(m_lam, m_alu, m_vinyl, m_chrome, m_steel, m_ging)`; the module authors C_LAMINATE "table top", C_VINYL "chair vinyl, C* 43.8", C_CHROME "chair frame", a `_gingham_mat()` for the green-checked cloth, `_sign_on_trunk()` for the ochre FAVOR DE ORDENAR sign, plus `_fence()` and `_palapa_corner()`. Only the two women are unbuilt. So the absence the concept sells as a discovered constraint is an unforced authorial choice — and it chose the MORE generic of the two available images. An empty terrace is Empty LA. A terrace with the gingham cloth still on the table, the orange vinyl chairs still pushed in, the sign still telling nobody where to pay, and the diners gone, is stranger, more specific, and already built.

NET: genuinely fresh subject and genuinely rare provenance, wrapped in a borrowed container, sold with an overreaching claim, dated with an invented figure, and centred on a conceit its own source code refutes. The core survives all four. Strong, one honest pass from exceptional.
fatal_flaws: THE DATE PAIR IS INVENTED, AND IT IS THE TITLE. No EXIF on ref_rear34.jpg (I checked all three playa frames — `_getexif()` empty), nothing in the tree dates it, and the folk-art livery it shows is LEDGER_rev51's "RED, CURRENT" state, not the 2006 conversion (SPEC: bought green, opened 6 Feb 2006). The concept forbids inventing a lat/long in the caption and then invents a year in its own title and in every panel label.

THE CENTRAL CONCEIT IS FACTUALLY WRONG ABOUT ITS OWN TREE. "what this project holds, measured, is the vehicle and the planting" — playa_env.build() also calls `_furniture(...)`, `_fence(...)`, `_palapa_corner(...)` and `_sign_on_trunk(...)`, with authored constants for laminate table tops, orange chair vinyl, chrome chair frames and a `_gingham_mat()`. The chairs, tables, cloth and sign ARE built. The absence sold as content is a choice, and it is the more generic of the two available images.

IT BORROWS REPHOTOGRAPHY'S FORM WITHOUT ITS ENGINE. Then-and-now pays off on CHANGE; both panels here show the same object in the same livery at the same instant from the same camera. Nothing changes but sharpness and population, so the diptych/dissolve is decoration rather than structure — and it is the most conventional container available for the idea.

"STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE FOR ANYONE ELSE TO MAKE" IS FALSE AT THE IDEA LEVEL. Forensic and heritage reconstruction do exactly this pairing as routine practice; Klett's Rephotographic Survey Project, Levere's New York Changing and Larenkov's blends do the photographic half; "I rebuilt this photo in 3D" is a standing CG-portfolio genre. The true claim is narrower and better and the concept does not make it.

THE MOST ORIGINAL THING IN THE CONCEPT IS NOT IN THE ARTEFACT. The held-out confirmation — predicted column 554.6 against a read 555 — lives in `why_not_derivative`, a rationale field, not in the image or the caption. As specified, the viewer sees a sharp render next to a soft photograph and has no way to know a solve happened.
improvements: RETITLE AWAY FROM TIME, TOWARD KNOWLEDGE, AND DELETE EVERY DATE. Kill "The Same Camera, Twenty Years Later", "LEFT / 2006", "RIGHT / 2026" and "the two years" from the hairline caption. The artefact is not about a decade passing; it is about someone having measured an afternoon. Name it for the act — a survey plate, a solve, a reading — and caption it with the only three things that are actually established: the recovered camera (-4.829, +2.222, 1.900), the 36 mm lens / 53.1 deg horizontal field, and the held-out check. This removes the concept's one unverified figure and simultaneously fixes the genre mismatch, because a survey plate does not owe you a before and after.

PUT THE FURNITURE BACK — IT IS ALREADY BUILT AND IT IS THE STRANGER IMAGE. Render playa_ref with `_furniture`, `_gingham_mat`, `_sign_on_trunk`, `_fence` and `_palapa_corner` live, so the green-checked cloth, the orange vinyl chairs, the chrome frames and the ochre FAVOR DE ORDENAR Y PAGAR AQUI sign are all present and only the two women are gone. Then the absence is precise instead of total: a sign addressed to nobody, a laid table, no diners. That is a specific image nobody else can make; an empty terrace is Empty LA with a bus in it. Restate the honesty line accordingly: the people are absent because people were never in scope, and say that in one clause rather than mis-describing the asset.

MAKE THE SOLVE VISIBLE — THIS IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST TIER LIFT. Add a third state, or overprint the render, with the solve's own working drawn on it in a hairline: the rear rim flange conic (139.1 px = 0.440 m -> 316 px/m), the horizon row 230, the wheel-ellipse minor/major 0.348, and a single tick at image column 555 labelled "predicted 554.6 / read 555 — a feature the solve never saw". One mark and one line of type carries the entire idea, and it is the only element in the concept that no photographer, no illustrator and no rival brand can reproduce. Right now that sentence is in a rationale field where no viewer will ever meet it.

REPLACE THE DISSOLVE WITH REGISTRATION. A 4 s cross-dissolve is the default gesture of a genre this artefact should stop quoting, and it hides the very thing it claims as content (that nothing slides). Ship instead a hard cut or a flip at 1200 x 824 native with four corner registration marks visible on both frames, so the viewer's eye does the checking. If motion is wanted, animate the OVERLAY appearing over the photograph and then the photograph being replaced beneath a static overlay — the marks stay, the picture changes underneath them. That is a form the category does not have.

CLAIM THE NARROW TRUTH AND NAME THE GENRE YOU ARE IN. Delete "structurally impossible for anyone else to make". Write instead: this is a forensic reconstruction plate, a form heritage and accident work has used for decades — what is uncommon is that the subject is one working object the brand owns, and that the pose is validated against a feature withheld from the solve. Naming the lineage makes the increment credible; claiming novelty over a populated genre makes the whole document sound like it has not looked.

MAKE THE ENVIRONMENT CHOICE LOAD-BEARING WITH A MEASUREMENT YOU ALREADY HOLD. playa_env's header lists four MEASURED ABSENCES — no sun, no sky, no haze, no dapple gobo — and the concept's own palette says there is no specular highlight anywhere in frame. That is precisely the one environment in which gloss_compare's standing failure (0.412 of the photograph's spread against a 0.60 bar on out/r75_hero34f) is not the defect it is in the studio. Say so explicitly in the proposal and in the ledger, with both figures. Then the scene is not a mood preference, it is the only scene where the model's worst open gate does not apply — an argument, not a taste.

GIVE THE PRINT FORMAT A HONEST RESOLUTION STORY OR DROP THE PRINT ARM. The concept correctly refuses to out-resolve its 1200 x 824 partner, then proposes a 200 mm pair at ~152 dpi — and the artefact's whole content is fine registration, which is exactly what dies at 152 dpi. Either print small and dense (about 100 mm wide, ~305 dpi, a plate you lean in to read) or make the screen loop the primary and treat print as a book spread at native pixels with the gutter doing the work. Do not ship a wall pair whose defining property is unresolvable at the size proposed.

verdicts.lens: Producibility and fidelity — can this be made from THIS asset, given the grounded reality (failing gates, unbuilt geometry, unproven large-format chain, an emblem rejected nine times)? What breaks, and what unscoped model work does it need?
verdicts.reasoning:
The concept is unusually well-grounded for a first draft, and three of its producibility instincts are genuinely correct and checkable. (1) Its camera is real, not aspirational: `studio.py` carries `"playa_ref": dict(loc=(-4.829, 2.222, 1.900), tgt=(-0.55, -0.10, 1.28), lens=36, focus=(-1.20, 0.55, 1.20), fstop=4.5)` with the solve and the 554.6/555 confirmation in its own comment. (2) Its light spec is transcribed accurately from `playa_env.py`'s header and `studio.playa()`'s docstring — the four measured absences, the 3.95:1 flank/fascia signature, db* +2.4, foliage L* 32.7 against cream 84.8. (3) Most importantly for this lens, it is the only delivery-shaped concept I have seen here that does NOT touch the unproven large-format chain: at 1200x824 native it needs `render_set` and nothing else — no `hq_render.py`, no `stitch.py` seam check, no `post.py` alpha destruction, no F49 exit-code trap. And the emblem — his ninth report, F191's gate — is out of frame by construction: the camera sits at x -4.83, tail-side, so the nose roundel is not in the picture. That is a real, structural reason this concept survives the project's worst open defect where a `hero34f` concept would not.

But on this axis the concept cannot be made today, and its central promise is refuted by things already in the record.

THE PROMISE IS "NOTHING SLIDES." That is the entire content — the concept says so ("that perfect registration is the whole trick"). Registration is exactly what this asset cannot currently deliver, for three independent reasons the concept does not name.

First, the poses in the upper-right quadrant the concept calls its hero are invented, not measured, and one is measured WRONG. `HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md` §0.05, on the propped tail board that `ref_rear34.jpg` (820,0)-(1200,300) shows: photographed angle above horizontal 28.0 deg against F165's built 38.4 deg — "~10 deg TOO STEEP" — and F165 "is seven revisions old and was NOT re-measured at rev 69." `STATE.md` prints the live pose as `principal-axis chord 0.7110 m, angle 38.0 deg`. `t1_shell.py` carries `TB_WIDTH = 0.5500      # POSE CHOICE, NOT MEASURED`. And `STATE.md` on the hatch: `rear hatch: glass_rear swung +64.00 deg SIGNED about its hinge (declared 64.0, NOT MEASURED -- a POSE)`. Hang the pair on a wall and the board will visibly slide by ten degrees against its own photograph, in the brightest object in frame. The concept's emotional claim dies at that moment and no grade fixes it.

Second, the environment's scale datum disagrees with the machine. `playa_env.py` declares `ROOF = 1.923                   # bus roof height, the scale datum (report S0.1)`. `STATE.md` reads `roof at tail = 1.988` and `roof@rear-axle=1.9833`. That is 60-65 mm, ~3.4 %, on the datum the whole placement report was solved through. I checked and `ROOF` is referenced nowhere else in `playa_env.py`, so it is a documentation constant and the eleven mass positions are baked literals rather than live-recomputed — which means the error is frozen into the numbers rather than propagating, but it also means nothing will ever correct it. Every plant depth, and the 554.6 confirmation, is a rev-10 result about a rev-10 mesh. `H_ROOF 1.960 is RETIRED as an accuracy target (rev 22)` — the roof line has moved since that solve and the record says so.

Third, none of it is guarded. `grep -c "playa_ref\|REF_CAM\|554" verify_clone.sh` returns 0 on a 437-row verifier. There is no row anywhere that says the render registers with `ref_rear34.jpg`, and the project's own standard (CLAUDE.md's opening: a figure in a paragraph goes stale silently) forbids shipping the claim without one.

THE PATH IS ALSO COLD AND BROKEN. F57 is `MEASURED-rev57b`, `OPEN — reported, not diagnosed`: "T1_SCENE=playa RENDERS NO VEHICLE ... a dark cylinder on a grey plane — the ground disc and nothing else ... Found by LOOKING; every exit code was clean." Eighteen revisions cold with no diagnosis, and I could not shortcut it: I checked the obvious candidate and it is not the answer — `_cull_foreground` has existed since `87148dc rev 10` and only touches `pl_*`, and `studio.playa()`'s canopy plates are already `ob.visible_camera = False`. So the cause is genuinely unknown and the concept's item-1 estimate is unbounded. Grounding separately reports zero rendered-file mentions of `playa`, `playa_ref` or `playa_w` across LEDGER_rev66..rev75 — 74 KB of environment code that has not been executed, let alone looked at, in roughly sixty-five revisions, against a mesh that has changed underneath it the whole time.

The concept's `_cull_foreground` note is right and understated. `render_set` calls `_cull_foreground(v["loc"], v["tgt"], log=log)` unconditionally, for every view, and `grep -c "T1_CULL\|cull.*os.environ" studio.py` returns 0 — there is no switch. So "confirm it is disabled for playa_ref" is not a confirmation, it is a source change to `studio.py` plus an ablation plus a verifier row, in a project where rule 47 says a switch that stops ablating fails silently. That is unscoped work the concept lists as a check.

Two things the concept gets right that I want on the record because they are rare here. It refuses to invent a lat/long, naming that as "exactly the class of unverified figure this project has spent seventy revisions removing" — correct, and it is the discipline most concepts drop. And it refuses to let the render out-resolve its 1200x824 partner, which is the right call for a different reason than it gives: `flank_compare` reads the render's red at median (196,81,67) G/R 0.422 against the photograph's (158,16,6) G/R 0.114, so hanging a sharper render beside its own reference maximises the exposure of the project's largest colour error. The concept admits this and proposes an output-file grade, correctly distinguishing it from F259's "DO NOT change RED" (which governs the model's paint). But that grade does not exist, has no specification, no instrument, and no floor, and `post.py` — the only optics tool in the tree — is documented as discarding alpha and reading through PIL's 8-bit path. So the one remedy offered for the one defect the format most exposes is itself unbuilt.

Net: strong idea, real and unique leverage, correctly scoped away from the chains that are broken — but on producibility it is gated on an undiagnosed bug, a 65-revision-cold code path, an unguarded stale camera solve, and two in-frame poses that falsify its only promise. That is "workable," not "strong," and the gap is closable — see the improvements, which convert the first deliverable from a finished pair into the measurement that would either earn the pair or kill it cheaply.
fatal_flaws: THE REGISTRATION PROMISE IS ALREADY REFUTED IN-FRAME, AND THE CONCEPT DOES NOT NAME IT. The propped tail board is in ref_rear34.jpg (HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §0.05 cites (820,0)-(1200,300)) and F165 measures it photographed at 28.0 deg against built 38.4 deg -- '~10 deg TOO STEEP', and 'was NOT re-measured at rev 69'. STATE.md prints the live pose as 'angle 38.0 deg'. Beside it, STATE.md reads 'rear hatch: glass_rear swung +64.00 deg SIGNED about its hinge (declared 64.0, NOT MEASURED -- a POSE)', and t1_shell.py carries 'TB_WIDTH = 0.5500      # POSE CHOICE, NOT MEASURED'. A ten-degree slide on the brightest object in the frame destroys 'nothing slides', which is the concept's entire content, and no colour grade or camera fix touches it.

THE ENVIRONMENT'S SCALE DATUM DISAGREES WITH THE MACHINE BY 60-65 mm. playa_env.py: 'ROOF = 1.923                   # bus roof height, the scale datum (report S0.1)'. STATE.md: 'roof at tail = 1.988' and 'roof@rear-axle=1.9833'. ~3.4 % on the datum the mass-placement report and the camera solve were built through. I verified ROOF is referenced nowhere else in playa_env.py, so the placements are baked literals and the error is frozen rather than propagating -- but it also means nothing will ever correct it, and STATE.md records that 'H_ROOF 1.960 is RETIRED as an accuracy target (rev 22)', i.e. the roof line has moved since the rev-10 solve.

THE 554.6/555 CONFIRMATION IS QUOTED AS A LIVE PROPERTY AND IT IS A REV-10 RESULT ABOUT A REV-10 MESH. The concept's 'why_not_derivative' rests on it entirely ('CONFIRMED by a feature the solve never saw'). It is a comment in studio.py from commit 87148dc (rev 10). Between then and now the roof target was retired, the rake locked, the nose bulge moved, the bumper drapd and the tread shipped. Nothing in the tree re-checks it: grep -c 'playa_ref\|REF_CAM\|554' verify_clone.sh returns 0 on a 437-row verifier.

F57 IS UNDIAGNOSED AND ITS COST IS UNBOUNDED, AND THE OBVIOUS DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG. OPEN_FINDINGS.md F57: 'T1_SCENE=playa RENDERS NO VEHICLE ... a dark cylinder on a grey plane -- the ground disc and nothing else', MEASURED-rev57b, 'OPEN -- reported, not diagnosed'. I checked the two natural culprits and eliminated both: _cull_foreground has existed since rev 10 (commit 87148dc) and only touches objects named pl_*, and studio.playa()'s palapa_roof / canopy / backwall plates are already built with 'ob.visible_camera = False'. So the cause is genuinely unknown, and every other item in the concept is downstream of it.

playa_env.py HAS NOT BEEN EXECUTED OR LOOKED AT IN ~65 REVISIONS, AGAINST A MESH THAT MOVED THE WHOLE TIME. 74 KB, authored at rev 10, zero rendered-file mentions of playa / playa_ref / playa_w across LEDGER_rev66..rev75. It imports bpy and mathutils and builds eleven masses from baked coordinates. Nothing establishes it still imports, still builds, or still places anything sensible. 'RUN IT AND LOOK AT IT' is listed as one line of model work; it is an unbounded first-contact debug on dead code.

_cull_foreground HAS NO OFF SWITCH, SO THE CONCEPT'S 'CONFIRM IT IS DISABLED' IS A SOURCE CHANGE, NOT A CHECK. studio.render_set calls '_cull_foreground(v["loc"], v["tgt"], log=log)' unconditionally for every view in the loop, and grep -c 'T1_CULL\|cull.*os.environ' studio.py returns 0. Exempting playa_ref means editing studio.py, adding an ablation that is watched firing (rule 3), and adding a verifier row -- in a file whose own docstring says the hero cameras are why the cull exists.

THE ONE REMEDY OFFERED FOR THE DEFECT THE FORMAT MOST EXPOSES IS UNBUILT. flank_compare on out/r75_side.png reads the render's red at median (196,81,67) G/R 0.422 against ref_side.jpg's (158,16,6) G/R 0.114 -- it images salmon, and this format hangs it beside its own photograph. The concept proposes 'a print GRADE on the output file' and is right that this sits outside F259's 'DO NOT change RED'. But no such grade exists in the tree, it has no instrument, no floor and no guard, and post.py -- the only optics tool -- reads through PIL's 8-bit path and discards alpha.
improvements: SHIP THE REGISTRATION DIFF FIRST, NOT THE PAIR. Make the rev-76 deliverable a single 1200x824 overlay: render playa_ref at exactly 1200x824 (T1_RX=1200 T1_RY=824, matching ref_rear34.jpg's native aspect 1.4563 -- do NOT use 1600x1100, which is 1.4545 and drifts the edges), then publish a difference image plus five named landmark residuals in pixels: the palm trunk centreline, the roof line at the tail, the '1963' plate centre, the counter's rear corner radius, and the tail board's tip. PAINT EACH LANDMARK WINDOW AND LOOK AT IT BEFORE PUBLISHING ANY NUMBER (rule 8). This is cheap, it is a measurement rather than a Playa hero so F92's 'do not act on it' does not bite, and it converts the concept's unfalsifiable emotional claim into one number. If the residuals are small the pair is earned and you have the owner ask; if they are large you have killed the concept for the price of one render, which is a real result.

RE-MEASURE THE TAIL BOARD ON ONE RULER BEFORE ANY PAIR IS MOCKED UP, AND STATE F165'S CEILING IN THE ROW. HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §0.05 already prescribes this and it has sat since rev 62: the photographed 28.0 deg is read along the panel's TOP edge, F165's 'built' 38.4 is the bbox diagonal, and the live constant is TB_TILT_DEG = 38.0 -- three rulers. §0.05's own warning binds: 'the frame is 480x320 and the hatch spans ~90 px -- TWO SIGNIFICANT FIGURES. Do not fit to 28.0 as though it were 28.00.' Measure the photographed angle on ref_rear34.jpg (1200x824, ~2.5x the pixels of the frame F165 used) rather than IMG_3840, since ref_rear34 is the frame the concept registers against. This is the single highest-value model work the concept unlocks and it closes a seven-revision-old carrier as a side effect.

MAKE THE REAR HATCH'S 64 deg A MEASURED ANGLE FROM ref_rear34.jpg, OR STATE IN THE CAPTION THAT THE HATCH IS A DECLARED POSE. STATE.md is explicit: 'declared 64.0, NOT MEASURED -- a POSE'. This is the one frame in the reference set that could constrain it, because playa_ref looks at the tail from a solved camera -- so the concept is also the occasion to close F242. Either measure it here or say plainly in the hairline caption which elements are measured and which are posed. A piece whose subject is forensic honesty cannot silently carry two invented angles.

ADD T1_CULL=0 AS A REAL ABLATION SWITCH IN THE SAME EDIT, AND WATCH IT FAIL. Change studio.render_set's unconditional '_cull_foreground(v["loc"], v["tgt"], log=log)' to read an environment switch written out literally as os.environ.get("T1_CULL") -- verify_clone.sh asserts every T1_ switch appears as a literal os.environ.get("NAME") in source, so a helper taking the name as a variable hides it from that row (studio.rig_from_env's own comment says so). Then WATCH IT: render playa_ref both ways and report the culled-object count from _cull_foreground's own 'culled %d pl_* objects' log line. A switch that culls zero either way is rule 47's silent failure and proves nothing.

RE-DERIVE THE 554.6 PREDICTION ON THE CURRENT MESH AND PUT IT IN verify_clone.sh AS A ROW. It is the concept's whole differentiation claim and it is currently a rev-10 comment with zero guard rows. Project the built body's far top corner through the playa_ref camera in a pure-python probe (bpy is a pip module here, so this runs in ~1 s) and print the column. If it still lands near 555 the concept's premise survives 65 revisions of drift and that is a genuinely publishable result; if it has moved, you have found a real finding and the concept needs the camera re-solved. Either way the row makes the claim testable instead of transcribed, which is CLAUDE.md's opening rule.

RECONCILE playa_env.py's ROOF = 1.923 AGAINST STATE.md's 1.9833 / 1.988 IN SOURCE, WITH THE CONSEQUENCE STATED. Since ROOF is referenced nowhere else in the file, the honest fix is not to change the number but to annotate it -- 'declared as the scale datum of report S0.1; the live mesh reads 1.9833 at the rear axle and 1.988 at the tail (STATE.md), so every baked mass coordinate in this file carries a ~3.4 % datum error that has never been re-derived' -- and add a verifier row comparing the two so the divergence cannot widen unnoticed. Rule 16: annotate, do not delete.

DESCOPE THE OWNER ASK TO WHAT F92 ACTUALLY PERMITS, AND ATTACH THE DIFF. The concept correctly says this must be put to him, but HANDOFF_CARRIERS.md §4 is blunt: 'Do not re-ask it; do not act on it either.' The way through is not to ask about the Playa hero at all -- it is to show him the REGISTRATION DIFF as a measurement result, one crop and one sentence, with the choice framed as multiple choice about whether a photograph-and-double pair is worth opening F92 for. That respects the ruling's object (the Playa hero as a deliverable) while using the one thing the ruling names as its own value -- 'the emotional bar that sits ABOVE clinical accuracy'. Ask it with the question tool; a revision has been lost to sending figures and forgetting to ask.

SPECIFY THE PRINT GRADE AS A NAMED, MEASURED, REVERSIBLE OUTPUT STEP OR DROP IT FROM THE CONCEPT. If the pair ships, the grade needs: a named window on both images, medians read through photometry.read_png (not PIL -- F263/rule 58: every frame is 16-bit on disk and PIL truncates silently), the before and after G/R printed, and an explicit statement that it touches the OUTPUT FILE and not the model's RED (F259). Without that it is a hand-wave attached to the largest measured colour error in the project, in the one format that puts the error next to its own ground truth.

NAME THE PEOPLE-ABSENCE AS A CAPTION LINE, NOT AS AN UNSPOKEN EFFECT. The concept argues the empty chairs are content, and it is a good argument, but a viewer who does not know the project reads it as an incomplete render. One hairline sentence -- what was measured and what therefore could be rebuilt -- turns the absence from a gap into the thesis. This costs nothing and it is the difference between the piece reading as forensic and reading as unfinished.

IF F57 RESISTS DIAGNOSIS IN ONE SESSION, RENDER playa_ref VIA T1_PREVIEW WITH T1_SCENE=playa AND REPORT WHAT YOU SEE RATHER THAN CHASING IT. build.py's path is readable: _scene = os.environ.get("T1_SCENE", "studio") gates both rig_from_env and render_set's transparent=(_scene != "playa"), and the vehicle is built well before either. So the vehicle IS in the scene; F57's frame lost it for some other reason. Time-box the hunt, and if it holds, publish 'F57 reproduces / does not reproduce on playa_ref at rev 76' as the finding. 'It cannot be recovered from what we hold' is a real result and so is 'the bug is still there and here is the frame'.

verdicts.lens: Emotional resonance, brand fit and IP exposure
verdicts.reasoning:
I opened the plate. ref_rear34.jpg is a hot, crowded, joyful photograph: a woman resting her cheek on her hand at a chrome-legged formica table, a second woman with a bag mid-ground, orange vinyl chairs, a green-checked cloth, the yellow FAVOR DE ORDENAR Y PAGAR AQUÍ sign nailed to a palm trunk (which sits at roughly image x 310 of 1200 — NOT "dead centre" as the concept writes; the concept describes a frame it appears not to have looked at carefully). The core is real and the differentiation claim survives inspection: playa_env.py's own header records the camera recovered from the rear-wheel ellipse ("minor/major 0.348 ... f = 1200 px") and confirmed by a feature the solve never saw — "it predicts the bus's far (nose) top corner at image x = 554.6, and the report reads the cream lid panel as beginning at x = 555." studio.py repeats it. That is a genuinely uncopyable asset and the strongest sentence in the concept, and it is buried in why_not_derivative instead of being the caption.

On BRAND FIT and IP the concept scores better than it knows and never says so. This frame is the anti-derivative frame: counter wrap, brass nosing, folk-art scrollwork, the Señor Tacombi script, the 100% Calidad burst, the mural lid, the empty chrome "1963" plate — and the VW nose roundel is not in shot at all. Against grounded reality's own warning that "the images of classic Beetle and Bus vehicles are themselves protected as trademarks," this is the lowest-VW-exposure route in the whole program, and it simultaneously dodges the emblem defect the owner has reported nine times. The concept leaves that entire argument on the floor.

Now the failures, all on my axis.

FIRST, the title is a claim about time that the artefact cannot make and the repository cannot support. I checked the plate: `exif keys: NONE`. Nothing in SPEC.md, REF_MEASUREMENTS.md or any carrier dates ref_rear34.jpg — the only dates in SPEC are the purchase and the 6 February 2006 opening, neither of which is this photograph. So "2006", "Twenty Years Later" and "the two years" in the caption are invented figures, in a concept that piously refuses to invent a lat/long two paragraphs later. Worse, the claim is false even if the year were right: the right-hand image is not 2026, it is a reconstruction of the same instant with the humans deleted. Rephotography ("Second View") moves people because time actually passed in the world. Here nothing passed. "The lunch ended, the people left, the bus is still there" is a sentence the artefact cannot earn — and the one viewer who was actually standing there will feel the wrongness even if he cannot name it.

SECOND, IP exposure sits in the LEFT plate, not the render, and the concept never raises it. Two identifiable people, one face fully legible front-on, printed at ~200 mm in matched frames at every location and looped for 4 s on social. No release is mentioned anywhere. This is the single clearest legal-adjacent exposure in the concept and it goes unnamed.

THIRD — and this is the one that kills the emotional claim mechanically — THE ABSENCE IS NOT CURATED. The pitch is "NOTHING SLIDES." Things will slide, at the roofline. F309 records the roof box at "image x 592-635" in this exact frame; it is retired as geometry, so the photograph has a loudspeaker and the render does not. t1_shell.py gates the "La Santa" board behind T1_SIGNBOARD=1 and says "no hero should be rendered with it on" — that board is a large pale mass top-centre of this frame and it will simply be gone. Add the yellow palm sign, the bamboo fence, the blender and bottles. So the right half is not "everyone went home"; it is a patchy ~40% subtraction. The difference between elegiac and unfinished is exactly whether the viewer can infer a rule, and there is no rule.

FOURTH, the format is the one that maximally exposes every unresolved fidelity gap. Hung 60 mm apart in matched frames, the only act available to the viewer is A/B. flank_compare reads the render's red at median (196,81,67) G/R 0.422 against the photograph's (158,16,6) G/R 0.114 — it images salmon, at roughly ten JNDs. The concept disposes of this in one clause ("the remedy is a print GRADE on the output file") without noticing that grading the render to match the photograph converts the asset into a forgery of a photograph and directly contradicts the owner's "I want this 3d model to look like new. Enhanced from the photo."

FIFTH, brand register. Tacombi's own merch voice is deadpan leisure-outfitter — "casual, convenient leisure products since 2006", "Horizon Beanie", "Monument T". A hairline caption of lens and camera coordinates under matched frames is museum register. That is a legitimate stretch for a founding-story wall, but the concept asserts fit rather than earning it, and it puts the piece "by the till" — a two-second glance — for an artefact whose payload requires knowing the source photograph, noticing sub-pixel registration and caring about measurement. It is a founder-facing artefact dressed as a customer-facing one. And by its own honest admission it dies at small scale and is not a t-shirt or a sticker, so against "give me everything I might need" it produces one wall piece and a dissolve.

The idea is genuinely good and genuinely uncopyable. It is one honest reframe — drop the time claim, curate the absence into a stated principle, handle the faces — from being strong.
fatal_flaws: THE DATE IS INVENTED, AND IT IS THE TITLE. I read the plate: `exif keys: NONE`. No file in this repository dates ref_rear34.jpg — SPEC.md's only dates are the purchase 'in 2006' and 'Opened 6 February 2006', neither of which is this photograph. 'LEFT / 2006', 'Twenty Years Later' and 'the two years' in the caption are all unverified figures, in a concept whose own production_notes correctly refuse to invent a latitude on exactly this principle.

THE TEMPORAL ARGUMENT IS FALSE REGARDLESS OF THE DATE. The right-hand image is not 'now' — it is a reconstruction of the same instant with the people removed, built from measurements taken off these very photographs. 'The lunch ended, the people left, the bus is still there' requires the render to depict the present, and it depicts the past minus the humans. Rephotography moves people because time passed in the world; here nothing passed.

IDENTIFIABLE PEOPLE IN THE LEFT PLATE, UNADDRESSED. The photograph carries two recognisable women, one face fully legible front-on. The concept proposes printing it at ~200 mm in matched frames at every location and looping it on social, and never mentions a release. The IP exposure in this concept is in the PHOTOGRAPH half, not the render half, and it is the one exposure the concept does not name.

THE ABSENCE IS UNCURATED, WHICH BREAKS THE ONE PROMISE THE ARTEFACT MAKES ('NOTHING SLIDES'). F309 puts the roof loudspeaker at 'image x 592-635' in this exact frame and retires it as geometry, so the photograph has a box on the roofline and the render will not. t1_shell.py gates the 'La Santa' board behind T1_SIGNBOARD=1 with 'no hero should be rendered with it on' — a large pale mass in the top centre of this frame that will vanish. Plus the yellow palm sign, the bamboo fence, the counter blender and bottles. The concept names only people, chairs and tables. What the viewer will actually see is a patchy subtraction, which reads as unfinished render, not as departed lunch.

THE FORMAT MAXIMALLY EXPOSES THE PROJECT'S LARGEST UNRESOLVED DEFECT AND THE CONCEPT WAVES IT THROUGH. flank_compare on out/r75_side.png reads render red (196,81,67) G/R 0.422 against photograph (158,16,6) G/R 0.114 — salmon against vermillion, at roughly ten JNDs — and a 60 mm-apart matched pair makes A/B the only available act. 'The remedy is a print GRADE on the output file' is one clause for the whole risk, and a grade that matches the photograph contradicts the owner's rev-61 standard, 'I want this 3d model to look like new. Enhanced from the photo.'

IT DESCRIBES A FRAME IT DID NOT LOOK AT CLOSELY. 'The palm trunk dead centre' — the trunk sits at roughly image x 310 of 1200. It names one woman where there are two. In a project whose first rule is RENDER IT, CROP IT AND LOOK AT IT, a concept that mis-describes its own hero plate has not passed rule 1.
improvements: KILL THE YEAR AND PUT THE CONFIRMATION IN THE CAPTION INSTEAD. Retitle to something that makes no time claim ('The Afternoon, Measured' / 'One Camera, Solved'), and set the wall label to exactly what is measured and quotable: lens 36 mm, camera (-4.829, +2.222, +1.900) m, 53.1 deg horizontal field, and then the line that IS the emotional payload — 'the solve predicts the bus's far top corner at image column 554.6; the photograph reads 555.' That sentence is currently buried in why_not_derivative. Make it the headline; it is the only sentence in the concept that produces awe rather than asserts it.

CURATE THE ABSENCE INTO A STATED PRINCIPLE, AND LET THE PRINCIPLE BE THE THESIS. Decide the rule BEFORE rendering and print it on the label: 'everything that was measured; nothing that was carried in.' That keeps the bus, the palm and the planting; it removes people, chairs, tables, the La Santa board (F164 — restaurant furniture, the owner ruled it separate from the bus), the roof loudspeaker (F309 — a pose, not vehicle geometry) and the yellow sign. Add one measured line underneath: 'N objects stand in the photograph; M of them are ours and are drawn.' This converts the concept's biggest technical liability — the patchy subtraction — into its argument, and it is the brand's own voice: we only draw what we measured.

HANDLE THE FACES BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE, AND SAY SO IN THE PROPOSAL. Three options, pick one explicitly: (a) the owner knows who they are — get releases; (b) crop the plate to bus + palm + sign and exclude both figures, which costs the concept nothing since the registration is what matters; (c) if the presence/absence of people is the content, keep them and say in one caption line that the render draws only what was measured. Do not print a legible face at 200 mm in every location by default.

PROVE THE REGISTRATION WITHOUT NEEDING THE FULL RENDER — THAT IS THE OWNER ASK. You cannot pitch 'nothing slides' with a comp where things slide. Render playa_ref once as a clay/silhouette pass and overlay it on ref_rear34.jpg at 50%, and show the roofline landing on the roofline and the wheel ellipse landing on the wheel ellipse. One frame, no fidelity required, no colour decision required. Note this is also diagnostic for F57: 'T1_SCENE=playa RENDERS NO VEHICLE' — a silhouette pass tells you immediately whether the vehicle is absent from the scene or absent from the shot (studio._cull_foreground hides pl_* between camera and vehicle, and playa_ref is the ONE camera every mass was placed for, so culling must be off here). Put THAT overlay to him under F92, not a mocked-up pair.

MAKE THE IP ARGUMENT OUT LOUD — IT IS THE STRONGEST BRAND-FIT POINT AVAILABLE AND THE CONCEPT LEAVES IT UNSAID. This frame contains no VW nose roundel; the nose is out of shot behind the raised lid, and the hubcap glyphs are sub-legible at 200 mm. What it does contain is entirely Tacombi's: the counter wrap and brass nosing, the folk-art scrollwork, the Señor Tacombi script, the 100% Calidad burst, the mural lid, the empty '1963' plate. Against 'the images of classic Beetle and Bus vehicles are themselves protected as trademarks', this is the lowest-exposure route in the program AND it sidesteps the emblem the owner has rejected nine times. State it in the proposal as a reason to pick this frame over any three-quarter front.

SETTLE THE RED AS ITS OWN STEP, AND SHOW HIM BOTH. Produce the ungraded pair (salmon, honest) and the graded pair (matched), hand him both, and label whichever ships: 'the colour is graded on the output file; the paint is not touched.' That keeps F259's 'DO NOT change RED' intact and surfaces rather than hides the rev-61 / SPEC-§3 collision the record forbids you to resolve silently. Do not let a single clause in a concept doc make that decision.

MOVE IT OFF THE TILL AND GIVE THE DATA A SECOND LIFE AT SMALL SCALE. The payload needs dwell time — put it where people wait or sit, not where they pay. And ship the caption block alone as the small-format asset: lens, camera vector, the 554.6/555 confirmation, set as type. That is a coaster, a menu footer, a bag print, and it is precisely the deadpan leisure-catalogue register Tacombi already writes in ('purpose-built', 'Monument T', 'Horizon Beanie'). The pair is the wall piece; the survey line is the merch. Right now the concept produces exactly one artefact against an owner who asked for 'everything I might need'.

FIX THE MURAL LID BEFORE THIS FRAME OF ALL FRAMES. F74(a) is open: 'tex/lidmural.png is cropped at the bottom — the bottom row of flowers is sliced mid-bloom and the yellow side columns are truncated.' In the photograph that lid is the blazing orange mass across the entire top right and it is the single loudest object in the composition. Regenerate BY HAND — lid_gen.py is not called by build.py, so a stale texture ships silently — and resolve which face carries the mural (lid_gen.py says outward, SPEC §4 says underside, t1_shell.py says it faces the counter) before rendering, because in this frame that disagreement decides what the biggest object in the picture is.

audited_finalists.title: AQUÍ ME QUEDO — The Still Point

concept.title: AQUÍ ME QUEDO — The Still Point
concept.one_line: THE RISKY ONE: the bus drawn as the only motionless, fully-coloured, hard-edged thing in a picture where everything else is moving — with a plant growing up through the front wheel arch.
concept.the_image:
FRAMING: wide, low, AT A CHILD'S EYE — camera around 0.95–1.00 m, which puts the horizon under the belt line and makes the bus loom kindly rather than sit like a product on a shelf. Shot from the FLANK or a rear three-quarter, never the nose (see model work). The bus dead centre, absolutely planted, filling the middle third.

THE CORE MOVE: the bus is drawn with a hard, clean, unbroken line and no motion cues of any kind. Everything else in the frame is moving and drawn accordingly — children running past with two or three ghosted repeats of their own outline, a dog mid-leap drawn three times, a scooter, a kite, a paper bag lifting off the ground, a ball in the air, blown leaves, birds, steam — all in soft edges and multiples. The bus alone is sharp. It has no speed lines because it does not move and never will again.

TWO DETAILS A CAUTIOUS TEAM WILL CUT: (1) each front tyre sits very slightly INTO the paving — a shallow settled dish under it, the object having been in one spot long enough to make its own hollow. (2) A small green plant grows up through the front wheel arch: four or five leaves and one flower, drawn with exactly the same care as the mural. Not a weed. A volunteer.

LIGHT: late-afternoon warm from behind and to the left. Long, soft, moving shadows on everything that moves; one hard, clean, still shadow under the bus that anchors it like a plinth. THE BULBS ARE ALREADY ON although the sky is still bright — the small true detail of a place that opened before it needed to.

PALETTE: the moving world is drawn in three washed-back tints. The bus carries all five inks at full strength and is the only fully-coloured object in the picture. Then the plant is THE ONLY GREEN IN THE FRAME — no other green anywhere — so a child's eye goes bus, then plant, then everything else, in that order, every time.

COPY, hand-lettered, small, low: *«Aquí me quedo.»* and beneath it at half size, 'This is where I stay.'

MOTION VERSION: a slow six-second loop in which ONLY the moving world moves. The bus never does — not a bob, not a settle, not a breath. The joke lands around second four, when a child realises the big thing in the middle is the one thing that is never going to do anything.
concept.emotional_claim: The specific warmth of the fixed point — the shop that is always there, the grandparent's chair, the tree in the yard that was already old. For a child it is a promise rather than an adventure: *I will be here when you come back.* It inverts the entire emotional stock of the category, which is escape, and replaces it with the thing children actually need from the world, which is permanence. The plant is the tenderest possible way to say 'arrived and never left' — it says this has been here long enough for something to grow, and it says it without a word of copy.
formats: Single large poster, A1 (594 × 841 mm), the wall piece

DIE-CUT STICKER of the bus alone from this drawing — plant included, and the CAST SHADOW as the die-cut base rather than a contour cut around the tyres. That is AUDIT_rev43.md's own rule arriving from a different direction: 'DIE-CUT OUTLINE — bridge the underbody with the cast shadow, and let no feature narrower than 0.159 m touch the cut line.'
Wraparound on a paper takeaway bag: the moving crowd runs round the sides, the bus sits still on the front face
Child's tee, 240 mm chest, four inks — bus + plant + shadow only, no scene
Slow six-second loop for social and the menu screen
Postcard set: the same scene at four times of day, only the light and the crowd changing
concept.why_not_derivative: It is the category's exact inverse. Every sunset-silhouette, surf-rack, road-trip VW print on the market sells motion and escape — and this vehicle cannot move: SPEC.md §0.1 grades it S, in Tacombi's own published words, 'The engine was scrapped, transmission sold, seats swapped for cooking equipment.' No competitor can honestly draw a VW bus that cannot leave, because no other seller owns one that had its engine taken out. It is also the correct MEXICAN reading rather than the American one: 'combi' is a pesero, a working microbus that hauls people to work, and Tacombi's own name is taco + combi. Every trope in the market — peace signs, daisies, tie-dye, sunset, surfboard — belongs to the Woodstock reading of the same body shell. And the composition removes the nose entirely, so the roundel that is simultaneously the most generic and the most enforced element on the object is simply not in the picture.
concept.production_notes:
