**WHY THIS IS THE RISKY ONE, SAID PLAINLY RATHER THAN SANDED OFF:** (a) it makes the hero product the least dynamic object in its own picture, which a cautious reviewer reads as 'boring hero'; (b) the plant and the settled hollow read as NEGLECT to anyone scanning quickly — they are the emotional core and they are the first two things a nervous reviewer deletes; (c) it contradicts the owner's own standard in the record. He ruled at rev 61: 'I want this 3d model to look like new. Enhanced from the photo.' A plant growing through the wheel arch is not new. It is not WEATHERED either — SPEC §3's lock is 'chalky, sun-faded, uneven, chipped edges, dusty lower body', which is decay. This is a third thing the record has no word for: TIME. F230 already names the collision between that rev-61 ruling and SPEC §3's WEATHERED lock as one of two owner questions that gate the render and CANNOT BE ANSWERED BY CODE. This concept forces that question instead of dodging it — so put it to him AS A PICTURE, as multiple choice with the crop attached, not as a paragraph. That is also the legitimate occasion to close F192, whose own condition is 'ask it once he names the medium'; (d) formally it refuses the category's only move, so if it fails it will fail as INERTNESS rather than as calm. That is a real risk and I am not going to pretend otherwise.

**IT CONTRADICTS F18 AND I PROPOSE IT ANYWAY.** F18's scene is locked to 'nothing but the bus, die-cut tight, plus the sun and the papel picado'. The die-cut here adds a plant, adds a shadow base and has NO SUN. It is therefore explicitly a DIFFERENT ARTEFACT from F18 and is not offered as the F18 deliverable — which also means it is not gated by F18's trigger, 'build it after the model is done'. Do not raise the papel picado: the owner ruled 'Leave it open, I'll decide when the sticker is actually being built. DO NOT RE-PUT IT UNTIL THEN.'

**NO SUN AS A RAYED DISC ANYWHERE IN THIS PROGRAMME.** AUDIT_rev43.md's reasoning is right and independently checkable: 'The vehicle already carries ELEVEN radial bursts, and it is the drawing's only light source.' The Calidad starburst, the mural rosettes, the hubcap rings, the headlamps and the wheel spokes all compete for it.

**HOLD THE GREEN.** One green in the whole picture and it belongs to the plant. If a second green appears, the idea is gone.
model_work_required: **SHOOT THE FLANK, NOT THE NOSE — and the reason is measured.** At a 0.95–1.00 m camera the roundel lands dead centre of a child's eyeline: build.py carries `ROUNDEL_Z_AG = 1.0170`, and `ROUNDEL_D = 0.2800`. A five-year-old stands nose to nose with it. And it is wrong: probe_rev69_fitpose's P2 reads 0.8528 against P1b's ceiling of 0.9465, and probe_rev46_vw's C8 reads 'photo 3.39, built 2.84 -- the built cells are 1.19x TOO ROUND.' It is the owner's ninth report, F191 and F234 both stand, and it is also the most trademark-exposed element on the object. Composing it out is the same correct decision twice over.

**NO CHILD'S-EYE CAMERA EXISTS.** studio.views() defines 14 cameras and the standing preview list is four (`front,side,hero34f,hero34r`). The closest is `low34` at eye 1.55 m, which no preview list has ever rendered. A ~0.95 m camera is a new dict entry and a frame nobody in 76 revisions has seen. Render it and LOOK before designing to it.

**The cast shadow is both the composition's anchor and the sticker's cut path, and it is separable — but only on paper.** deliver.py writes `combi_%s_shadow_only.png` and `combi_%s_no_shadow.png`, with the split measured at rev 62: shadow-catcher pixels near-black (max channel < 12/255) against a vehicle mean of 143, the vehicle side 97.1 % fully opaque and 99.99 % ONE connected component. But **T1_ALPHA has not been run since rev 62** — no LEDGER contains the string, every frame in out/ is PNG colortype 2, and deliver.py currently prints 'CONTROLS: 4 checked, 1 FAILED -- C1' and 'PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY'. One render closes it and every format here depends on it.

**post.py DESTROYS ALPHA** — measured RGBA in, colortype 2 out, and its docstring nowhere says so. Optics (bloom / CA / vignette / grain) and a cut-out are mutually exclusive from this repo. Decide the order before anything is graded, and note post.py's live default is `BACKDROP = "headroom"` (peak 252) while its own docstring still claims white — a 252 field inside a #FFFFFF margin is a visible rectangle on the sheet.
The settled hollow under each tyre, the plant, the crowd, the ghosting, the steam and the birds are ALL DRAWN. Nothing in the tree does people, volumetrics or ground deformation.
The bulbs-on-in-daylight beat needs F144 addressed or drawn around: 'THE FESTOON BULBS READ AS PEARLS, NOT LIGHTS.' For a flat illustration, draw them right; do not wait on the render.

If the Calidad decal appears anywhere in the crop, draw its pink star from the PHOTOGRAPH, not the model: F16 is OPEN — 'the isolated star is built BELOW the burst where both red frames put it above; every flank rosette is drawn at the diameter of its gold core.' The same row means every shipped rosette is systematically undersized.

**No close tyre crop in any large format.** t1_detail.py carries `TREAD_LUGS = 64  # DECLARED, inside the MEASURED bracket 48..84 (F308)` and `TREAD_CUT = 0.0060  # DECLARED groove depth, m.  NOT measured`, and probe_rev74_tread's T2 refuses to publish a count at all. At poster scale the lugs become countable and we would be publishing a specific checkable claim the project explicitly cannot defend. PHOTOS_WANTED has never carried a tyre item; one close square-on frame would close it.

verdicts.lens: ORIGINALITY — is this genuinely fresh, or a well-executed version of something already on a thousand VW-bus products?
verdicts.reasoning:
The STRATEGIC inversion is real and the concept earns credit for it: the category sells escape, this sells permanence, and the substrate fact underneath it is proprietary and S-graded in the repo — SPEC.md §0.1 quotes Tacombi's own words, "The engine was scrapped, transmission sold, seats swapped for cooking equipment." Nobody else selling VW-bus merch owns a bus that had its engine taken out. That is a genuine anti-derivative foundation.

But the EXECUTION reaches for three off-the-shelf devices to express it, and the concept has checked none of them.

(1) Sharp-hero-against-ghosted-crowd is the single most reproduced device in long-exposure street photography. It has a name in the how-to literature — 500px calls it "the spectral effect"; Digital Photography School's beginner guide teaches it as "one person standing still in a crowd of moving people," and Brent Mail's tutorial page is literally titled "Lost in the Crowd." It is a beginner exercise, not a proprietary idea.

(2) Plant-growing-through-the-machine is a merch category, not a fresh detail — and it is a merch category attached to THIS EXACT VEHICLE TYPE. Redbubble sells "Abandoned Bus Overgrown with Plants"; Etsy sells "Abandoned and Overgrown School Bus"; Etsy's "Bus Stop Poster, Abandoned Overgrown Forest Landscape ... Post-apocalypse Decay" is the same image sold as decay. The concept's own risk note fears the plant "reads as NEGLECT" — that is not a misreading risk, that is the established genre reading of exactly that mark on exactly that object. The claim "no competitor can honestly draw a VW bus that cannot leave" is refuted by a category of prints that draw nothing else.

(3) One saturated colour in a washed-back frame is the red-coat / selective-colour cliché, banned from most photo competitions and the default filter of amateur work. Using it to steer the eye bus→plant→world is a filter move dressed as a compositional device.

Add a fourth borrowing the concept does not flag: the title. "The Still Point" is T. S. Eliot, Burnt Norton — "At the still point of the turning world." It is one of the most-quoted phrases in English modernism, used as the name of hundreds of books, albums and yoga studios. It is also tonally foreign to the argument the concept itself makes — that the correct reading of this object is Mexican (pesero, taco + combi), not Anglophone.

And the motion version negates its own device. Blur-versus-sharpness only carries meaning in a still frame, where blur is the ONLY available signifier of movement. In a six-second loop, an object being motionless is the default state of every object in every video — it carries zero information. "The joke lands around second four, when a child realises the big thing in the middle is the one thing that is never going to do anything" is asserted, not designed; there is nothing in the loop to notice.

What IS original, and it is not nothing: the bulbs already on while the sky is still bright ("a place that opened before it needed to") is a precise, tender, category-free observation nobody else has. The settled dish under the tyre is honest to the object rather than borrowed. The 0.95 m child's-eye camera is a genuinely under-used framing — the repo confirms no such view exists (studio.views() defines 14, the standing preview list is four; the closest, low34, is 1.55 m and has never been rendered). Composing the nose out is a correct double decision, and the repo backs the fidelity half of it: probe_rev69_fitpose's P2 reads 0.8528 against P1b's ceiling of 0.9465, and probe_rev46_vw's C8 reads "photo 3.39, built 2.84 -- the built cells are 1.19x TOO ROUND."

So: one proprietary emotional foundation, two or three genuinely fresh details, and a signature stack built from three clichés and a borrowed title. That is a well-executed version of things that already exist, with good original material buried inside it. Workable. The good news is that the fresh material is strong enough that this could reach strong on a rewrite, because the fixes are subtractions.
fatal_flaws: THE CORE DEVICE IS A BEGINNER PHOTOGRAPHY EXERCISE. Sharp-static-subject against ghosted-moving-crowd is taught as an introductory technique — 500px's guide, Digital Photography School's 'A Beginner's Guide to Long Exposure Street Photography' ('one person standing still in a crowd of moving people'), Brent Mail's tutorial 'Lost in the Crowd'. The concept treats it as the idea rather than as the most obvious available way to say the idea.

THE PLANT LANDS INSIDE AN EXISTING MERCH CATEGORY FOR THE SAME VEHICLE. Searched and confirmed: Redbubble 'Abandoned Bus Overgrown with Plants', Etsy 'Abandoned and Overgrown School Bus', Etsy 'Bus Stop Poster, Abandoned Overgrown ... Post-apocalypse Decay'. Overgrown-vehicle art is a genre and its meaning is DECAY. The concept calls the plant 'not a weed, a volunteer' — but the audience does not read the artist's intent, it reads the genre, and the genre says derelict. On a FOOD brand that is not a soft risk, it is a food-safety adjacency.

'NO COMPETITOR CAN HONESTLY DRAW A BUS THAT CANNOT LEAVE' IS FALSE AS WRITTEN. An entire print category draws buses that cannot leave. What is proprietary is not immobility — it is the REASON for it (engine scrapped and sold, deliberately, to make a kitchen) and the fact that it is still open and trading. The concept has the right fact and states its uniqueness claim one step too wide.

THE TITLE IS A T. S. ELIOT QUOTATION. 'The Still Point' is Burnt Norton — 'At the still point of the turning world.' Heavily used as a title across books, albums and businesses. It also imports an English high-modernist register into a concept whose own argument is that the correct reading of this object is Mexican, not Anglo.

SELECTIVE COLOUR IS THE RED-COAT CLICHÉ. 'The moving world in three washed-back tints, the bus at full strength, one green in the frame' is desaturate-everything-but-one — the most recognisable amateur-photography filter there is, and disallowed in most photo competitions. It is doing the eye-routing job that composition, scale and light should be doing.

THE MOTION VERSION DESTROYS THE STILL VERSION'S DEVICE. Blur signifies motion only in a still frame. In video, stillness is the default state of every object and communicates nothing; the 'second-four realisation' has no mechanism to occur. The loop is not a translation of the idea, it is the idea's absence.

THE EMOTIONAL TERRITORY, ONCE YOU LEAVE VW-BUS MERCH, IS THE MOST CROWDED CLAIM IN BRAND ADVERTISING. 'We have always been here / I'll be here when you come back' is the default heritage-brand position for every bank, pub, hotel and family business. The inversion is fresh WITHIN the category and utterly conventional outside it — so the freshness depends entirely on the execution, which is where the borrowings are.
improvements: REPLACE GHOSTING WITH A MEDIUM COLLISION, NOT A BLUR. Draw the moving world in a visibly different medium from the bus — loose gouache/brush with wet edges and visible stroke ends for everything that moves, flat hard-edged vector fill for the bus. Same claim (one thing is fixed, everything else is provisional), zero long-exposure baggage, and it separates by MARK-MAKING rather than by focus. Cheaper to screen-print too, since brush marks can be one spot colour.

OR, BETTER AND STRANGER: SHOW THE MOVING WORLD ONLY BY ITS TRACES. No ghosted bodies at all. A dropped napkin caught mid-fall, one shoe leaving the frame edge, a dog's tail exiting stage right, a still-swinging bead curtain, a bike on its side with the wheel drawn as if still spinning, chalk marks on the paving, a hand entering frame at the counter. Absence-of-people rather than ghosts-of-people is a device the category does not use, it is far more child-legible, and it makes the bus the only complete thing in the picture without a single blur.

MOVE THE PLANT INTO A POT AND OUT OF THE ARCH. A herb the kitchen actually uses — cilantro, epazote — in a chipped tin can, wedged on the counter shelf or under the front wing, with a watering mark on the paving beside it. Same green, same 'been here long enough', but the reading flips from RECLAIMED BY NATURE to TENDED BY SOMEONE. It kills the overgrown-bus genre collision, it kills the neglect risk the concept already fears, and it strengthens the emotional claim rather than weakening it, because a tended plant proves a person, and a volunteer weed proves only time. If the team refuses to let go of the volunteer, keep BOTH — a weed one person pulled and a pot they planted — but the pot must be the dominant green.

SEPARATE THE BUS BY TEMPERATURE, NOT SATURATION. Give the moving world a full-strength palette shifted a half-step cool (blue-grey shadows, cooler skin, cooler paving) and keep the bus in its warm inks. Warm-against-cool is a painter's separation that has never read as a filter; desaturate-except-one always will. This also lets the plant be one green among a full-colour world rather than the only chroma in a grey one, which is a subtler and more confident eye-route.

RENAME OFF THE PROPRIETARY FACT, NOT OFF ELIOT. Drop 'The Still Point' entirely. «Aquí me quedo» can carry the piece alone. If a second line is wanted, take it from the S-graded source rather than English poetry — the engine was scrapped and the transmission sold, and 'Sin motor desde 2006' / 'No engine since 2006' is a sentence no competitor can print. That is the anti-derivative title, and it is sitting in SPEC.md §0.1 unused.

RE-CONCEIVE THE LOOP FOR TIME OR CUT IT. Two options that actually work in motion. (a) SPEED COLLISION: one locked frame in which the crowd runs at 4x time-lapse and the bus stays at real time — the difference is then a RATE difference, which video can express, instead of a motion/no-motion difference, which it cannot. (b) FAR BETTER, AND IT USES THE CONCEPT'S BEST ORIGINAL DETAIL: the loop is nothing but the bulb string coming on while the sky is still bright. Six seconds, no people, no ghosting, no plant. The whole idea — a place that opened before it needed to, and will be lit when you get here — in one gesture the category has never made.

PROMOTE THE BULBS-ON-IN-DAYLIGHT BEAT TO THE CONCEPT AND DEMOTE EVERYTHING ELSE. It is currently one sentence inside a paragraph about light, and it is the most original thing in the entire submission: it is true, it is specific to a working food business, it is emotionally exact, and it belongs to no existing trope. A version of this concept in which that is THE idea — bulbs lit against a bright sky, nobody in frame yet, the counter wiped and waiting — would be more original than the present stack of three borrowed devices, and it needs neither ghosting nor selective colour to land.

EXPLOIT THE 0.95 m CAMERA INSTEAD OF JUST SPECIFYING IT. At a child's eye height the counter lip is ABOVE the viewer's eyeline — a child cannot see the food, only the underside of the counter, the brass nosing edge, and hands coming down over it. Draw THAT frame: the view where you cannot quite see over. It is an image nobody in this category has, it is literally true to the audience F18 names ('for children at the restaurant'), and it says 'this is a place for you and you are small here' with no motion device at all. Render it first — the repo confirms no camera below 1.55 m has ever been rendered in 76 revisions, so nobody has seen this frame.

DO THE COMPETITIVE IMAGE SWEEP BEFORE DRAWING, AND BRING BACK THE THREE NEAREST NEIGHBOURS. Twenty minutes on 'overgrown VW bus', 'abandoned combi flowers', 'long exposure crowd still subject', 'still point turning world poster'. Pin the closest three on the wall and design AWAY from them. The concept currently asserts its own uniqueness without having looked; that assertion is the weakest sentence in it and the sweep would have caught two of the three collisions above.

WHEN THIS GOES TO THE OWNER, SHOW THE PLANT AS A CROP, NOT A PARAGRAPH — AND SHOW IT THREE WAYS. The concept is right that this forces F230's unanswerable question (rev 61's 'I want this 3d model to look like new' against SPEC §3's WEATHERED lock), and right that it must be asked as a picture. Make it genuinely multiple choice: (A) volunteer weed through the arch, (B) potted herb in a tin, (C) no plant at all, bulbs-on-in-daylight carrying the whole claim. One crop each, one sentence each. He can then rule on TIME as a third state without having to invent the vocabulary himself — which is the concept's best intellectual contribution and deserves to survive the redraft.

verdicts.lens: Producibility and fidelity — can this be made from THIS asset, and what breaks
verdicts.reasoning:
This concept has a real and unusual producibility ADVANTAGE that it under-claims for itself, and one contradiction at its centre that it does not name at all.

THE ADVANTAGE, VERIFIED. The composition removes the project's three worst-defended surfaces by construction, not by luck. (a) No nose means no roundel: `build.py` carries `ROUNDEL_D = 0.2800` and `ROUNDEL_Z_AG = 1.0170` (read live), so at the concept's own ~0.95 m camera the emblem would sit dead on a child's eyeline — and it reads 0.8528 against P1b's 0.9465 ceiling, is the owner's ninth report, and F191/F234 both stand. (b) A camera BELOW the sill puts the three serving apertures and the roof aperture above the eyeline, which composes out F45 (roof-aperture interior, "OPEN — item B at rev 58. UNGATED and never measured", 7.4e5 px² of a 3840 frame) and F72 (the counter props within 2.4 DN of the body cream where the photograph shows a 60+ DN spread). Those are two ungated defects that no gate would have caught and no revision can currently fix. (c) The die-cut-via-cast-shadow is the repo's own rule arriving from the right direction, and `deliver.py` genuinely emits `combi_%s_shadow_only.png` / `combi_%s_no_shadow.png` with a measured split.

THE CONTRADICTION. The concept never decides whether the deliverable is a RENDER or a DRAWING, and the answer changes every other line. "Hard, clean, unbroken line", "five inks at full strength", "washed-back tints", "four inks" is flat vector illustration. But `model_work_required` asks for a new camera render, a T1_ALPHA run, `deliver.py` layers, and cites tread-count and rosette-diameter fidelity rules that only bind a render. If it is a drawing, the four failing photograph gates stop being blockers — gloss_compare 0.412 against a 0.60 bar, flank_compare worst region `i` 0.686, probe_rev70_tyre 0.2556 against 0.1953, F240's red at G/R 0.42–0.52 against 0.114 — because not one of them measures a drawing. If it is a render, F191's hold applies and every one of those gates is live. The concept gets the benefit of both readings and pays the cost of neither.

AND THE PIPELINE IT ASSUMES DOES NOT EXIST. I grepped the whole tree for a non-photoreal path: `grep -rn "freestyle|Freestyle|line_art|LineArt|toon"` across all .py returns ZERO hits. There is no line pass, no flat-fill pass, no NPR switch, no ablation, no guard. The recovered rev-39 clause this whole track leans on — "vector line and flat colour, shading and occlusion sampled from the 3D asset" — is an UNBUILT PIPELINE, and the concept lists `deliver.py`'s layers as though they supplied it. They do not: that split is VEHICLE versus SHADOW, not LINE versus FILL. This is the largest unscoped item in the concept and it appears nowhere in its own model-work list.

IT ALSO FIGHTS ITS OWN CAMERA. `cyclorama()` is a FLAT shadow-catching ground — its own comment says "Deliberately NOT a curved cyc wall". At 0.95–1.00 m the ground goes near edge-on, so the contact shadow foreshortens to a sliver and is largely occluded by the vehicle. The concept simultaneously requires a child's-eye camera AND "one hard, clean, still shadow under the bus that anchors it like a plinth" AND that same shadow as the die-cut base. Those cannot all be true. Note that AUDIT_rev43's own viewpoint finding is 18° at eye height 1.55 m — HIGHER than this concept — and the extra height is precisely what makes a shadow readable as a bridge.

The camera itself is unbuilt and mis-specified. `side` is ORTHOGRAPHIC (`ortho=5.90`), so "wide, low, at a child's eye, from the flank" cannot be `side` — ortho has no eye height and cannot loom. `low34` is eye 1.55 m and is a FRONT three-quarter (`loc=(11.60, 7.90, 1.55)`), i.e. it shows the nose the concept forbids, and it has never appeared in any preview list. `hero34r` sits at z 3.80. So this needs a new dict entry AND a wider lens — at 0.95 m close enough to loom you are at the `playa` 42 mm or the recovered 36 mm, not the 78 mm SPEC 10.8 measures the heroes at. And `deliver.py`'s VIEWS table has exactly six entries; a new view not added there is silently dropped from every package.

Finally the plumbing: T1_ALPHA is a rev-62 result carried forward with no LEDGER mention since, every frame in `out/` is PNG colortype 2, `deliver.py` on today's frames prints "PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY" while writing the package and its transparency README anyway, and `post.py` destroys alpha (RGBA in, colortype 2 out) so optics and cut-out are mutually exclusive. A1 at 300 dpi is ~9933 px; nothing above 3840 has ever been stitched through hq_render's MARGIN chain, and `grep -c T1_FX hq_render.py` is 0 where hero.py forces it off to stop per-strip optics banding at the seams.

Workable, not weak: the emotional idea is sound and the composition is doing real defensive work. It is two decisions and one measurement away from strong.
fatal_flaws: RENDER OR DRAWING IS NEVER DECIDED, AND IT IS THE ONLY QUESTION THAT MATTERS HERE. The image description ('hard, clean, unbroken line', 'five inks at full strength', 'four inks') is flat vector illustration; the model-work list asks for a new camera render, T1_ALPHA, deliver.py layers and cites tread/rosette fidelity rules that bind only a render. As a drawing, gloss_compare (0.412 vs 0.60), flank_compare (worst region i 0.686), probe_rev70_tyre (0.2556 vs 0.1953) and F240's red (G/R 0.42-0.52 vs 0.114) are all irrelevant. As a render, F191's hold is live and all four are blockers. The concept takes both readings.

THE LINE-AND-FLAT-COLOUR PIPELINE DOES NOT EXIST AND IS NOT IN THE MODEL-WORK LIST. `grep -rn "freestyle|Freestyle|line_art|LineArt|toon"` across every .py in the tree returns ZERO hits. There is no NPR pass, no ablation switch, no guard. The rev-39 clause the track depends on — 'vector line and flat colour, shading and occlusion sampled from the 3D asset' — is unbuilt, and the concept cites deliver.py's layers as if they were it. deliver.py splits VEHICLE from SHADOW, not LINE from FILL.

THE CAMERA DESTROYS THE SHADOW THE CONCEPT IS ANCHORED ON. `cyclorama()`'s own comment: 'Deliberately NOT a curved cyc wall' — it is a flat shadow-catching ground. At 0.95-1.00 m that plane is near edge-on, so the cast shadow foreshortens and is largely self-occluded. The concept needs that same shadow to be a 'hard, clean, still shadow... like a plinth' AND to serve as the die-cut base per 'bridge the underbody with the cast shadow'. AUDIT_rev43's own viewpoint finding is 1.55 m, and the extra height is what makes the bridge readable.

THE COMPOSITION CONTRADICTS ITS OWN TREAD CONSTRAINT. model_work_required says 'No close tyre crop in any large format' — correctly, since `TREAD_LUGS = 64  # DECLARED, inside the MEASURED bracket 48..84` and probe_rev74_tread's T2 refuses to publish a count (48..84, a 1.73x span). But the image puts the plant through the FRONT WHEEL ARCH and a settled dish under the front tyre, making it the eye's second stop. On A1 with the bus at ~600 mm the 32.6 mm lug pitch lands ~4.8 mm on the sheet — individually countable, publishing a specific checkable claim the project explicitly cannot defend. The same tyre also reads 1.31x too light (F318 open, its prescribed band fix undone).

THE CAMERA IS UNBUILT AND MIS-SPECIFIED THREE WAYS. `side` is ORTHOGRAPHIC (ortho=5.90) so it cannot be a low child's-eye flank at all; `low34` is 1.55 m and is a FRONT three-quarter (loc x +11.60) showing the forbidden nose, never rendered by any preview list; `hero34r` is z 3.80. A ~0.95 m looming camera also needs a 36-42 mm lens rather than the heroes' 78 mm (SPEC 10.8 LOCKED). And deliver.py's VIEWS has six entries — a new view not added there is dropped from every package it feeds.

EVERY FORMAT DEPENDS ON A TRANSPARENCY PATH THAT IS 13 REVISIONS UN-RUN AND CURRENTLY REFUSING. All frames in out/ are PNG colortype 2; deliver.py on them prints 'CONTROLS: 4 checked, 1 FAILED -- C1' / 'PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY' and writes the 22-file package plus its 'TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND' README anyway. post.py destroys alpha (RGBA in, colortype 2 out) and its docstring does not say so, so optics and cut-out are mutually exclusive — which the poster and the sticker both need, in opposite directions.

A1 IS OUTSIDE THE PROVEN CHAIN AND THE CHAIN HAS A KNOWN SEAM DEFECT. A1 at 300 dpi is ~9933 px. Nothing above 3840x2640 has been stitched through hq_render's MARGIN chain, `grep -c T1_FX hq_render.py` returns 0 where hero.py forces T1_FX=0 to stop per-strip optics banding at seams, and stitch.py's seam refusal is exit 2 (F49, 'a guard whose exit code nobody reads is not a guard').
improvements: DECLARE IT A DRAWING IN ONE SENTENCE AT THE TOP, AND DEMOTE THE RENDER TO AN UNDERLAY. Write: 'The deliverable is drawn. The render supplies exactly two things — a geometrically correct perspective underlay and an occlusion pass. No pixel of the render ships.' That single sentence voids gloss_compare (0.412/0.60), flank_compare (i 0.686), probe_rev70_tyre (1.31x) and F240's red (G/R 0.42-0.52 vs 0.114) as blockers, because not one of them measures a drawing — and it removes F191's hold, which gates the DELIVERY RENDER and nothing else. This is the highest-value edit in the list and it costs nothing.

SPLIT THE CAMERA FROM THE LOOK. Render the underlay at AUDIT_rev43's own 1.55 m — author `low34r` as `low34`'s rear-three-quarter mirror on the show side (+Y), roughly `dict(loc=(-11.30, 9.05, 1.55), tgt=(0.10, 0.00, 1.30), lens=78, fstop=8.0)` — and draw the child's-eye loom by lowering the HORIZON in the artwork, not the camera. You keep the 78 mm every hero measurement was taken through (SPEC 10.8), you keep a readable cast shadow, and you keep the nose out of frame. Add `"low34r"` to deliver.py's VIEWS in the same edit or the package silently drops it.

PICK ONE OF TWO LINE ROUTES AND NAME IT. Either (a) trace by hand over the underlay — zero new code, honest, and what 'cartoon with rendered depth' has always meant here; or (b) build a real `T1_LINE=1` pass (Blender Freestyle or a Grease Pencil Line Art modifier) as a separate PNG, WITH a watched kill: render it with the modifier disabled and confirm the pass comes back empty, then confirm it moves when the camera moves. Do not cite deliver.py's shadow split as the occlusion pass again. If you want a real occlusion pass, the mechanism already exists and is in no live document: `T1_MATTE` and matte_tap's File Output tap, with its validation in `matte_tap.__doc__`.

MOVE THE PLANT OFF THE TYRE AND STATE A TREAD RULE. Put the volunteer between the paving and the shadow's edge just AFT of the front tyre, or at the rear arch. Same reading — 'here long enough for something to grow' — same only-green device, and it takes the eye off the one object the project refuses to characterise. Then write the rule into the concept: 'the tread reads as one continuous dark band; no lug is individually drawn at any reproduction size.' That is the honest drawing of a 48..84 bracket and it is defensible in front of the register. Add a tyre item to PHOTOS_WANTED while you are there — it has never carried one, and one close square-on frame would close F308b.

PRICE THE SHADOW BEFORE ANYONE DRAWS ANYTHING. One render at the chosen camera with T1_ALPHA=1, then read deliver.py's own printed partition: it already reports the footprint split, opacity and connectivity (rev-62 proof frame: 37.8/62.2 %, vehicle side 97.1 % fully opaque, 99.99 % ONE connected component). Set the acceptance in advance: the shadow must be a single connected region that BRIDGES the underbody, and if it is under roughly 15 % of the footprint or the bridge breaks, the die-cut format is not producible at that angle. That is one render against a whole artwork commission.

RUN T1_ALPHA ONCE AND MAKE IT A REV-76 MEASUREMENT. No LEDGER contains the string; F159 is a rev-62 reading carried forward for thirteen revisions. One `T1_ALPHA=1` render of the chosen view converts it from a record into a measurement and unblocks every format here. In the same note, fix the ordering explicitly, because post.py will otherwise eat the silhouette: POSTER = optics on the white-backdrop master; STICKER / TEE / BAG = a separate T1_ALPHA render with NO post.py. Also flag that post.py's live default is `BACKDROP = \"headroom\"` while its docstring still claims white — a 252 field inside a #FFFFFF margin is a visible rectangle on the sheet.

DROP THE POSTER TO A2, OR BUDGET THE PROVING RUN EXPLICITLY. A2 (594 mm long side) is inside what 3840 has actually done once; A1 is not, and the chain above 3840 is unproven. If A1 stays, scope it as work: one hq_render at the target size with `T1_FX=0` exported BY HAND (hq_render has no T1_FX and hero.py's docstring says per-strip optics band at the seams), then stitch.py and READ ITS EXIT CODE — 2 on a seam. And use the medium as the legitimate occasion to close F192, whose own unlock condition is 'ask it once he names the medium'.

DRAW THE BULBS; DO NOT WAIT ON F144. The concept's best small beat — bulbs already lit in daylight — cannot come from the render: F144 measured the string at a saturation ratio of 1.38 against the photograph's 4.96/3.82, and BOTH levers are refuted by ablation, T1_BULB_STR=60 making it WORSE (1.40 -> 0.88) because the bead clips and clipped pixels are neutral by definition. Say in the concept that the bulbs are an illustration decision, so no one budgets a revision chasing a lever the register already closed.

PUT THE TIME-VERSUS-NEW COLLISION TO THE OWNER AS A CROP, NOT A PARAGRAPH — AND SAY WHICH ARTEFACT IT IS. The concept is right that a plant through the arch is neither 'look like new' (rev 61) nor SPEC section 3's WEATHERED, and right that F230 names that collision as one of two owner questions that gate the render and cannot be answered by code. Make it actionable: two crops of the same drawn frame, one with the plant and hollow and one without, as multiple choice with the question tool. And state plainly in the same message that this is NOT the F18 deliverable (no sun, adds a plant, adds a shadow base), so it is not gated by F18's 'build it after the model is done' trigger — and do not mention the papel picado, which he ruled closed until he opens it.

verdicts.lens: Emotional resonance, brand fit and IP exposure
verdicts.reasoning:
The core emotional claim is the best in the set and it is TRUE OF THIS OBJECT, which almost nothing in this category can say. SPEC.md line 37 carries Tacombi's own published words, graded S: "The engine was scrapped, transmission sold, seats swapped for cooking equipment." A bus that cannot leave is not a mood the illustrator asserts — it is a fact the client published about itself. "I will be here when you come back" therefore lands as testimony rather than sentiment, and it inverts the entire stock of VW-bus merch (escape, sunset, surf rack) without needing to be clever about it. The plant as the only green in the frame is a real compositional device with a real reading order, not a mood board word. That is exceptional-tier thinking.

It is NOT exceptional as executed, for three reasons that all sit squarely on my axis.

FIRST, THE COPY UNDOES THE PICTURE. The stated strength is that the plant "says this has been here long enough for something to grow, and it says it without a word of copy." The concept then adds «Aquí me quedo» AND an English gloss beneath it at half size, saying exactly that. Two lines explaining the one thing the drawing already does silently. The gloss is also the specific tell of appropriated-Spanish design: the vehicle itself never translates itself — it carries "Gracias por su Preferencia", "BIENVENIDOS", "VENGA A NOLITA ★" and translates none of them (the artdirection lane read all three off ref_nolita_doorshut.jpg at 5x). A bilingual subtitle is a thing done TO a Spanish phrase by an English-speaking design team.

SECOND, IT GHOSTS THE CUSTOMERS AT A HOSPITALITY BRAND. Everything that moves is drawn in "three washed-back tints" with ghosted repeats; the bus alone carries "all five inks at full strength and is the only fully-coloured object in the picture." At a taqueria that means the children, the staff and the food are all smears, and the vehicle is the only fully realised thing. The emotional claim is warmth toward a person returning; the rendering de-saturates and multiplies that person into motion blur. For a piece whose stated audience is children hanging it on a wall, the child in the picture is the blur. That is a genuine inversion of the claim, not a stylistic quibble, and the concept does not price it.

THIRD, THE IP CLAIM IS OVERSTATED AND THE MISS IS AT CHILD EYE HEIGHT. "the composition removes the nose entirely, so the roundel ... is simply not in the picture" is only half true. STATE.md's inventory carries `capvw | 8` and SPEC.md line 287 locks "red domed hubcaps with a light VW in the centre" — four wheels, each with a VW roundel, at exactly the height a 0.95 m camera puts in the middle of frame. A flank or rear-three-quarter view composes OUT one VW mark and composes IN two to four, larger relative to a child's eyeline than the nose badge would have been. Worse for the sticker: the market lane found "The images of classic Beetle and Bus vehicles are themselves protected as trademarks", and a die-cut whose whole product IS an outline is the single form on which a shape claim bites hardest. The mitigation the concept needs is available and it did not reach for it — the converted silhouette (counter cantilever, three open hatches, propped tail board, raised lid) is not a T1 outline and is not VW's.

Brand fit is otherwise strong and correctly grounded: the pesero reading over the Woodstock reading, the deliberate refusal of the rayed-disc sun on AUDIT_rev43.md's own independently-checkable reasoning, the flank over the nose. Where it wobbles is register. Tacombi's live merch voice is deadpan leisure-outfitter — "Monument T", "Horizon Beanie", "purpose-built, all-weather knit", "an original leisure-filled T for relaxed coastal living". «Aquí me quedo» in hand-lettering is warmer and more folkloric than anything currently on that store. That is not disqualifying — the vehicle's own signwriting IS folkloric — but the concept should know it is proposing a register shift for the brand, not matching one.

On the risk it names itself: "inertness" is the right worry and it is honestly stated. My read is that the plant, the settled hollow and the bulbs-already-on are what save it — three signs of TIME PASSING on a still object — so the stillness reads as duration rather than deadness. That defence works. What does not work is the food-adjacency the concept never names: a plant growing up through the wheel arch plus a settled dish in the paving, on a working food vehicle, sits one association away from "not maintained". Charming on a bookshop; a different conversation on a taqueria. The owner should see that pairing as a picture before it is committed, which is exactly the mechanism the concept already proposes for F230.

Strong, not exceptional. The idea is exceptional; the execution gives away three of its own advantages.
fatal_flaws: THE COPY REPEATS THE PICTURE AND THEN TRANSLATES ITSELF. The concept's own case is that the plant says 'arrived and never left' without a word of copy; it then adds «Aquí me quedo» plus 'This is where I stay' at half size beneath. The second line is the failure — the vehicle carries 'Gracias por su Preferencia', 'BIENVENIDOS' and 'VENGA A NOLITA ★' and glosses none of them. Self-translating Spanish is the signature of a non-Spanish-speaking design team handling a Spanish phrase.

IT DE-SATURATES THE CUSTOMER AT A HOSPITALITY BRAND. 'The bus carries all five inks at full strength and is the only fully-coloured object in the picture' means the children, the staff and the food are washed tints and motion smears. The emotional promise is made TO a returning person; the rendering makes that person the least real thing in the frame. For a children's piece, the child in it is a blur.

THE IP CLAIM IS WRONG ON THE MEASUREMENT. 'the roundel ... is simply not in the picture' — STATE.md carries `capvw | 8` and SPEC.md line 287 locks 'red domed hubcaps with a light VW in the centre'. A 0.95 m child's-eye flank view removes one VW mark and centres two to four hubcap roundels in the child's eyeline. The composition trades a small nose badge for four wheel badges.

THE DIE-CUT IS THE MOST TRADEMARK-EXPOSED ARTEFACT IN THE PROGRAMME AND IS SPECIFIED AS 'the bus alone'. The market lane established that the bus SHAPE is claimed ('The images of classic Beetle and Bus vehicles are themselves protected as trademarks'), and a die-cut sells nothing but an outline. Cutting the split-screen T1 profile is the one form where the shape claim has the most purchase, and the conversion — counter, three hatches, propped tail board, raised lid — is what makes the outline Tacombi's rather than VW's.

THE PLANT + SETTLED HOLLOW PAIRING HAS A FOOD-SPECIFIC READ THE CONCEPT DOES NOT PRICE. It names the generic 'neglect' risk. At a taqueria the sharper adjacency is hygiene: vegetation growing through the bodywork and a standing-water dish under the tyre, on a vehicle that serves food. One volunteer plant is charming; the hollow doubles it into a different sentence.
improvements: CUT THE ENGLISH GLOSS ENTIRELY. Keep «Aquí me quedo» alone, hand-lettered, small and low, and let the untranslated Spanish be part of the object's dignity — the way the real bus carries 'Gracias por su Preferencia' with no subtitle. If a non-Spanish-speaking buyer needs the meaning, put it on the sticker backing card or the product page, never in the artwork.

GO FURTHER AND TEST THE NO-COPY CUT AS THE PRIMARY. Render two comps: (A) with «Aquí me quedo», (B) with no lettering at all, the plant and the stillness carrying it. The concept's own argument says B should win. Put both to the owner as multiple choice with the crops attached — that is the same ask that closes F230 and F192, and it costs one extra drawing.

GIVE THE MOVING WORLD ITS COLOUR BACK, AND MAKE THE DEVICE EDGE-SHARPNESS INSTEAD OF SATURATION. Keep the bus as the only HARD-EDGED, unghosted object — that device is intact and it is the good one — but let the children, the food and the dog stay fully coloured. What the picture must not do is make the vehicle more real than its customers. The green rule survives untouched: the plant is still the only green.

OR, BETTER: LET ONE PERSON BE STILL WITH THE BUS. A single figure at the counter, drawn as sharply as the vehicle, no ghost repeats — everyone else moving. That converts 'the only motionless thing' from a formal trick into a relationship, kills the inertness risk outright, and makes the promise 'I will be here when you come back' land on a served person rather than on a parked object. It is also the single cheapest fix for the ghosted-customer flaw.

SPECIFY THE HUBCAP CENTRE. In every drawn artefact, render the hubcap as the four-band bullseye the photographs show — chrome ring / cream dish / red dome / light centre disc — with the centre a PLAIN light disc, no glyph. SPEC §10.10's absolute-replication bar governs the 3D model's decals, not a derived illustration (the priorart lane establishes this), so this is a free change. It removes two to four VW marks from the frame and costs nothing a child will notice.

REWRITE THE DIE-CUT SPEC AS 'THE CONVERTED SILHOUETTE, NOT THE VEHICLE SILHOUETTE'. The cut path must include the cantilevered counter, the three open hatches, the raised lid and the propped tail board — the outline should be unrecognisable as a stock T1 profile. Keep the cast-shadow base as proposed; that already satisfies AUDIT_rev43.md's 'bridge the underbody with the cast shadow, and let no feature narrower than 0.159 m touch the cut line'. State in the brief that the shape claim is why, so nobody 'simplifies' the counter back off later.

DROP THE SETTLED HOLLOW; KEEP THE PLANT. The hollow adds nothing the plant does not already say and it carries the standing-water read on a food vehicle. If some ground evidence of duration is wanted, use a faint sun-bleached rectangle of paler paving around the bus's footprint — the shadow it has cast for years — which says the same thing, is unambiguously about time rather than about maintenance, and reinforces the plinth-shadow that already anchors the composition.

PUT THE PLANT TO THE OWNER AS A PICTURE, NOT A PARAGRAPH, AND SAY WHICH RULING IT COLLIDES WITH. Three crops: bus with plant, bus without, bus with a small potted plant set BESIDE the wheel (grown-nearby rather than grown-through). That third option keeps the whole emotional payload — something has been here long enough to grow — while removing the hygiene adjacency and the collision with his own rev-61 'I want this 3d model to look like new'. Frame it exactly as F230 says such questions must be framed: it cannot be answered by code.

DRAW THE LETTERING IN THE STATE-A HAND, NOT THE NOLITA ONE. The vehicle's Spanish cursive that everyone will reach for — 'Gracias por su Preferencia' — is on the CHALKBOARD livery (ref_nolita_doorshut.jpg ≡ IMG_3840.jpeg, md5 f1b6f98c6a12b6e9ea0ec3edc68e945a), a different livery state. Mixing states is this project's own named error (rule 11 killed F99/F100/F140 on exactly that). Draw «Aquí me quedo» fresh in the Señor Tacombi swash family — the fat late-60s display hand with the rolled spiral counters, the state-A signwriter — so the phrase looks painted by the person who painted the flank.

STATE THE REGISTER SHIFT IN THE PROPOSAL RATHER THAN LETTING IT BE DISCOVERED. Tacombi's current merch voice is deadpan outfitter-catalogue ('Monument T', 'Horizon Beanie', 'purpose-built, all-weather knit'). This piece is warmer and more folkloric than anything in that shop. Say so in one line and argue it: the store voice is the PRODUCT voice, the vehicle is the ORIGIN, and the origin is allowed to speak in its own register. Naming it pre-empts the exact note a brand reviewer will otherwise deliver as a rejection.

CHECK THE BULBS-ON-IN-DAYLIGHT BEAT SURVIVES ILLUSTRATION. It is the best small true detail in the concept and F144 is the reason the render cannot supply it — measured, the render's bulbs read saturation ratio 1.38 against ref_side.jpg's 4.96 and ref_rear34.jpg's 3.82, 2.8–3.6x short, and the row records BOTH model-side levers refuted by ablation. Draw them as warm amber against a still-bright sky; do not wait on the render and do not colour-pick them off it.

NAME THE ONE ASSET THIS CONCEPT NEEDS THAT DOES NOT EXIST. No camera below 1.55 m has ever been rendered (studio.views() defines 14, the standing preview list is four; `low34` at 1.55 m has never appeared in a preview list). Before any drawing is committed to the 0.95 m eyeline, add the camera, render one frame and LOOK at it — the concept's whole 'looms kindly rather than sits like a product' claim is untested, and this project's first rule is that every shipped defect passed VERIFY and was found by looking at a crop.

audited_finalists.title: AZULEJO 1963 — the bus fired into Puebla tin-glaze

concept.title: AZULEJO 1963 — the bus fired into Puebla tin-glaze
concept.one_line: The orthographic side elevation hand-painted in cobalt on tin-glazed talavera tile, grout lines running straight through the vehicle, and the three serving hatches left as bare unpainted glaze.
concept.the_image:
SOURCE VIEW: the true orthographic side elevation. `studio.views()['side']` is `ortho=5.90, lens=None` — a genuine parallel projection, and talavera does not do perspective, so the craft and the camera already agree. I measured out/r75_side.png at 77.8% x 77.5% frame fill with clean margin on all four sides and no clipping; it is the one existing frame that can be traced as-is.

PANEL: 6 tiles wide x 4 high, each 105 mm, = 630 x 420 mm. Vehicle at 1:8 — the propped silhouette (4.580 x 3.132 m, from STATE.md's `x range [-2.157, 2.160]` plus the tail board reaching x -2.420, and `bbox top 3.132`) lands at 572 x 391 mm inside it, lid up, tail board propped, counter cantilevered.

PALETTE, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE IDEA: Puebla talavera's historic six are cobalt blue, tin-white ground, copper green, manganese black-brown, antimony yellow, and one rare orange. THERE IS NO VERMILLION IN THIS CRAFT. The vehicle's dominant colour does not exist in the material. So: body in COBALT, the cream upper body and roof as raw tin-white glaze (warm off-white, never paper white), the folk art in antimony yellow with manganese outline, the counter's brass nosing in antimony, tyres in manganese. The single orange is spent on exactly one thing — the four hubcap domes. Four small warm discs in an otherwise blue-and-white panel, landing on the wheels, which is where the eye goes anyway.

LINE: everything outlined in manganese at ~1.5 mm on the panel, brush-loaded so each stroke starts fat and tapers to a hairline — which is already the flank art's own signature (I looked at ref_side.jpg cropped to the rear quarter: every gold acanthus stroke is thick-to-hairline, terminating in a tight rolled volute).

THE GROUT IS THE POINT. Tile joints run straight through the vehicle — do NOT compose to avoid them. One joint crosses the Senor Tacombi lockup; one crosses a wheel. Joints are 3 mm of unglazed warm-grey bisque. Each tile is a fraction of a degree off square, so the grid wanders. If the grid is perfect and the edges are crisp, it reads as a printed tile and the whole idea dies.

GLAZE BEHAVIOUR THE DIGITAL VERSION MUST FAKE: talavera glaze is convex and pools. Cobalt goes markedly darker where a stroke terminates and where two strokes cross, and it bleeds ~0.5 mm into the white so no edge is clean.

THE HATCHES: the three serving apertures are left as bare tin-white glaze, undrawn — the only three areas of the panel carrying no ink at all. STATE.md: `open serving apertures on +Y: 3`, `bay widths 0.516 0.515 0.516` — they are EQUAL, so the rhythm is measured, not eyeballed. Three empty rectangles in a blue drawing is the founding story stated in negative.

BORDER: one tile-wide, the flank's own acanthus in cobalt, running all four sides. Talavera panels are always bordered; ours borrows the vehicle's own ornament to do it.

LIGHT: photograph it, never render it. Single raking source from the left so the convex glaze catches, the grout falls into shadow, and it reads as a wall you could put your hand on.
concept.emotional_claim: Permanence and civic weight. Tile is what a country puts on the front of a building it means to keep — it is the material of churches, market halls and fountains, not of trucks. Rendered in it, the taqueria stops being a vehicle that turned up and becomes a place that has always been there. And the palette does something nobody expects: stripped of its red, the bus stops reading as fun and starts reading as a monument. A person feels the same thing they feel in front of a tiled shopfront in a Mexican town square — that somebody built this on purpose, out of expensive materials, expecting it to outlast them.
formats: 24-tile wall panel, 630 x 420 mm, bus at 1:8 — one per restaurant, hand-painted in Puebla, signed and dated on the reverse of the corner tile. This is the anchor object; everything else is derived from it.

Compact retail panel, 4 x 3 tiles, 420 x 315 mm, bus SHUT at 1:11 (4.065 x 2.227 m per STATE.md's `overall height (vehicle max, lids excluded) 2.2268`). Framed and boxed. The shut state has never been rendered in 76 revisions, so this SKU doubles as the first sighting of the closed silhouette.

Single-tile coasters, 105 mm, set of six, one motif each: an 8-lobed rosette, a dark comma-with-dots tendril, one acanthus volute, the wheel bullseye, the three hatches, and '1963'. Each motif drawn at ITS OWN scale rather than shrunk off the bus — the largest flank rosette is a 68 mm equivalent circle (folk_gen.FLANK_ROSETTES, 3632 mm2), so at 105 mm it is drawn UP, not down, and nothing collapses.

Trivet, 2 x 2 tiles, 210 mm square: the wheel bullseye alone. Four concentric bands of the brand palette; STATE.md gives the badge at `4 rings R 0.043429` = 31.7% of the 274 mm cap, so it scales as a ratio.

Printed derivative: the panel photographed square-on under raking light. A2 poster, tote, tissue wrap, cup sleeve. The photograph of a ceramic object is a fundamentally different image from a render of a bus, and it inherits none of the render's colour problems.
concept.why_not_derivative: Every VW-bus artefact on the market is a photograph, an illustration, or a line drawing, and essentially all of them are red or rainbow. This one is a fired ceramic object with NO RED IN IT, with grout running through the vehicle's face. The tile grid is a reduction rule the category has never used: it forces the drawing into flat, bounded, brush-loaded strokes and refuses gradients, gloss and photorealism outright — which is the exact opposite of the saturated 'sunset silhouette' and 'blueprint' shelves. It also sidesteps the project's largest measured defect rather than inheriting it: flank_compare on out/r75_side.png reads the render's red at median (196,81,67), G/R 0.422, against the photograph's (158,16,6), G/R 0.114 — it images salmon. A craft with no vermillion in its palette cannot get the red wrong. And there is a real, quotable geographic rhyme: talavera poblana is made in Puebla, and Puebla is where VW de Mexico built the Combi from 1970. One line of copy, no invention.
concept.production_notes:
VENDOR: a certified talavera taller in Puebla (the craft carries a denominacion de origen; use a certified maker or do not call it talavera). Hand-painted maiolica on tin glaze, single firing after decoration. Lead times are long and per-panel variation is high — that is a feature for the restaurant anchors and a problem for retail, so cap the retail SKU at one panel size and accept that no two are identical.

COLOUR: do NOT hand the taller a hex value sampled off a render. Give them cobalt, antimony, manganese, copper green and the one orange as PIGMENT names and let the kiln decide. Every hex in this brief is an 8-bit display-space reading through PIL off warm, uncorrected frames — a mood reference, never an albedo. Separately, probe_rev71_red.py prints its own prohibition on the photograph side: 'the photograph's red G/R is 0.0149 .. 0.0344, a 2.3x span. DO NOT QUOTE A SINGLE FIGURE FOR IT.'

DRAWING SOURCE FOR THE ORNAMENT: draw the border acanthus from ref_side.jpg at 4-6x magnification, NOT from tex/swirl.png. The shipped tile is measurably more fragmented than the photograph — 196 gold connected components against the photograph's 66, with the top three carrying 66.4% against the photograph's 84.4% (folk_gen.COMP_TOP = {1: 47.8, 2: 73.7, 3: 84.4, ...}). The generator matches the coverage and misses the hand.

SIMPLIFICATION, WITH A MEASUREMENT UNDER IT: folk_gen.COMP_HIST's first three bins are (24, 0.42%), (21, 1.32%), (3, 0.55%) — 48 of 66 gold components carry 2.29% of all the gold. Delete all 48. That is a measured licence to reduce, not a taste call, and it is what makes the border cuttable in a brush.

DIGITAL PROOF BEFORE FIRING: build the panel as flat art with the bleed and the pooling faked, print it at size on matte, and pin it up at 2 m. Then fire one test tile and compare. Do not go to a 24-tile panel off a screen.

CEILING: nobody in this session has seen any current Tacombi merchandise, brand guideline, official colour or logo lockup — tacombi.com, shop.tacombi.com and fontsinuse.com all returned EGRESS_BLOCKED. Do not state a Tacombi brand colour anywhere in this programme until the owner supplies one.
model_work_required: NOTHING BLOCKING — this concept can start today off out/r75_side.png, which already exists at 1600x1100 with clean margins. That makes it the fastest of the three to a physical proof.

If any other elevation is used, FIX THE ORTHOGRAPHIC CLIPPING FIRST. studio.views()['front'] and ['rear'] are ortho=3.55 with horizontal sensor fit, so at 1600x1100 the vertical extent is 3.55*1100/1600 = 2.4406 m, covering z 0.2997 to 2.7403 — against a vehicle that reaches z=0 at the tyres and 3.132 at the top. out/r75_front.png has ink running off both borders. Derive ortho_scale from build.py's printed bbox with a stated margin instead of the typed 3.55, and add a verify row asserting zero ink on all four border rows/columns. Watch it go red on 3.55 before believing it green.

DO NOT PAINT THE EMBLEM FROM THE MODEL. At 1:8 the nose roundel would be 35 mm and plainly judgeable (ROUNDEL_D = 0.2800 in build.py). It is the owner's ninth report: probe_rev69_fitpose's P2 reads 0.8528 against P1b's 0.9465 ceiling, and probe_rev46_vw's C8 reads 'photo 3.39, built 2.84 -- the built cells are 1.19x TOO ROUND'. The side elevation does not contain the roundel at all, which is the main reason this concept is unblocked by F191 — but the four hubcap badges do appear, at 34 mm each, and STATE.md warns 'hubcap badge is SELF-CONSISTENCY ONLY -- CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC has never been compared to a frame'. Draw both from ref_playa_34.png, not from the render.

F74(a) is open and would propagate into any lid artwork: tex/lidmural.png is cropped at the bottom — the bottom flower row sliced mid-bloom and the olive-yellow side columns truncated, where ref_side.jpg shows a board framed on all four sides. I opened the master and confirmed it. lid_gen.py is NOT called by build.py, so regeneration is a hand step or the render silently keeps the old file. Fix before the lid appears at 1:8.
NOT GATED by F191/F193 — this is a hand-painted ceramic object, not the delivery render. Say so explicitly in the proposal so the hold does not read as blocking it.

verdicts.lens: ORIGINALITY — is this genuinely fresh, or a well-executed version of something already on the shelf?
verdicts.reasoning:
The concept has one genuinely original engine and it is buried under a conventional execution.

WHAT IS REAL. "The material physically cannot hold the brand's dominant colour" is a non-obvious constraint that does creative work rather than decorating it. I verified the premise: the Talavera de Puebla denominación de origen permits six colours — blue, yellow, black, green, orange and mauve — and red is not among them. So the vermillion genuinely cannot exist in the object, and the claim that a de-redded bus stops reading as fun and starts reading as civic is a real perceptual consequence, not a mood assertion. The second real move is the grout run deliberately THROUGH the vehicle's face. Commissioned tile murals overwhelmingly compose to keep the joint off the subject; refusing that is counter-conventional and is the freshest single decision in the brief.

WHAT KILLS THE TIER. Three pieces of prior art sit directly on this, and the concept knows about none of them.

(1) THE IMAGE ALREADY SHIPS. "Lisbon Tram Ceramic Tile, Portuguese Azulejo Blue White Home Decor" is a live Etsy product: a beloved vintage vehicle, hand-painted, cobalt on tin-white, sold as decor. Same image, same product logic, same tin-glaze maiolica family — different country. This concept is a transposition of an existing souvenir category from Portugal to Puebla, and at thumbnail the two are the same object.

(2) THE HEADLINE COPY LINE IS SPENT. The brief's stated differentiator is "a real, quotable geographic rhyme: talavera poblana is made in Puebla, and Puebla is where VW de Mexico built the Combi. One line of copy, no invention." That rhyme has already been executed as a physical object and is on public display in that city — a VW New Beetle decorated in talavera by Talavera Salazar, at the Museo del Automóvil de Puebla. The concept's own novelty argument is pre-empted by a museum piece.

(3) THE CATEGORY HAS A CANONICAL OBJECT. El Vochol — a VW Beetle in 2,277,000 Huichol beads, internationally toured, resident at the Museo de Arte Popular — is what anyone in Mexico thinks of first on hearing "VW rendered in Mexican folk craft." It is the reference this will be measured against.

The Vochol and the Talavera Beetle put craft ON a vehicle; this puts a vehicle IN craft, which is a real distinction — but the brief never makes it, so it reads as coincidence rather than position.

Beyond the prior art, the execution is respectful rather than inventive, and respectful rendition is exactly what a thousand craft-transposition products are. Cobalt outline, brush-loaded taper, glaze pooling and bleed, a one-tile acanthus border, a bordered panel, coasters and a trivet: that is the standard talavera vocabulary applied faithfully. Custom talavera tile murals of an arbitrary subject are an existing commercial service, not an invention.

The composition is the biggest leak. The orthographic side elevation is the single most-reproduced VW-bus image in existence — every line-art, blueprint and decal product on the saturated shelf uses it. The brief picks it for a pipeline reason it states outright: it is "the one existing frame that can be traced as-is." Production convenience is driving the picture, and it lands the concept on the most generic framing available.

Two smaller originality-relevant errors. The palette list — "cobalt blue, tin-white ground, copper green, manganese black-brown, antimony yellow, and one rare orange" — drops MAUVE, which is one of the six permitted colours, and invents scarcity for ORANGE, which is standard. So the sharpest-sounding move in the brief, "the single rare orange is spent on exactly one thing," rests on a false premise about the craft. And the bare-white hatches are weaker than claimed: the apertures really are openings onto a bright galley, so unpainted white is the literal reading, not a conceptual one — and three empty rectangles in a blue drawing risk reading as unfinished.

Net: one strong original idea (no red available), one strong original move (grout through the face), inside an execution and a framing that are adjacent to products currently for sale. That is the honest definition of workable.
fatal_flaws: The core image is already a commercial product in another craft tradition: 'Lisbon Tram Ceramic Tile, Portuguese Azulejo Blue White' — a beloved vintage vehicle hand-painted cobalt-on-white tin glaze, sold as decor. This concept is that product relocated from Portugal to Puebla, and the brief does not know it exists.

The stated differentiator — the Puebla/VW geographic rhyme, offered as 'one line of copy, no invention' — is already executed as a physical object on public display in Puebla: a VW New Beetle in talavera by Talavera Salazar at the Museo del Automóvil. The copy line is spent before it is written.

El Vochol (VW Beetle in 2.27 million Huichol beads, international museum tour, Museo de Arte Popular) is the canonical 'VW in Mexican craft' object and the inevitable comparison. The brief never names it, so it cannot position against it.

The palette premise is wrong on the craft's own rules. The denominación de origen permits six colours: blue, yellow, black, green, ORANGE and MAUVE. The brief drops mauve entirely and calls orange 'rare'. The concept's sharpest move — 'the single rare orange spent on four hubcaps' — is built on invented scarcity a Puebla taller will correct on the first call.

The composition is chosen for pipeline convenience, not for the image. The orthographic side elevation is the most-reproduced VW-bus framing in existence and is the exact silhouette the blueprint and line-art shelves already own; the brief selects it because out/r75_side.png can be traced as-is.

The SKU ladder is generic and contradicts the concept's own claim. Talavera coasters and trivets are a saturated Etsy/Amazon category; a bus motif on one is indistinguishable at thumbnail from every other talavera coaster, and six tidy motifs are the opposite of the 'monument' register the emotional claim asks for.
improvements: TRANSPOSE THE RED INTO MAUVE INSTEAD OF DELETING IT. Mauve is one of the six permitted colours and the brief never uses it. Assign the body mauve, not cobalt, and state the house rule on the reverse tile: the craft has no vermillion, so the vehicle's identity colour was moved to the nearest permitted pigment. A mauve-and-white bus is far stranger and more memorable than a blue-and-white one, and it makes the concept's whole argument VISIBLE IN THE OBJECT rather than only in the brief. Cobalt then falls back to line and shadow, where tin-glaze uses it best.

ABANDON THE ORTHOGRAPHIC SIDE ELEVATION AND DRAW IT THE WAY A TILE PAINTER WOULD. Colonial tile panels and Mexican retablo painting flatten and splay: a façade and its interior shown simultaneously, no foreshortening, hierarchy by importance not by distance. Draw the flank, the cantilevered counter, the propped lid's mural face and the galley interior all splayed into one plane at once. That is a picture neither the Lisbon tram tile nor the blueprint shelf can make, it is native to the craft rather than borrowed from a render, and it frees the concept from tracing an existing frame.

ALIGN EXACTLY ONE JOINT TO A MEASURED DATUM AND LET THE OTHER TWENTY-THREE FALL WHEREVER. Land a tile joint precisely on the two-tone belt line — STATE.md gives it live at 1.2070 m, with 'V_APEX + V_RISE == Z_BELT | 1.2070 == 1.2070 — held' — so the vehicle's own strongest horizontal IS a grout line. One aligned joint among twenty-three arbitrary ones makes the grid look quarried from the vehicle rather than laid over it, and it upgrades the grout from a texture note to the composition's spine.

REPLACE THE COASTER SET WITH FRAGMENTS, NOT MOTIFS. Ship single tiles as numbered pieces OF THE PANEL — 'tile 14 of 24' — cut through mid-drawing, so each one is a broken piece of a larger thing and the set only resolves if you collect it. That is a format the talavera-coaster shelf is not running, it makes the object collectible rather than decorative, and it is the only version of a small SKU that supports the 'monument' claim instead of contradicting it.

OWN THE PRIOR ART AS THE POSITION. Write the reverse-tile line against the Vochol and the Talavera Beetle rather than around them: those objects put the craft ON a vehicle; this one fires the vehicle INTO the craft — a taquería turned into the material of the buildings it parks in front of. Naming the precedents converts the concept's biggest liability into its clearest statement of what it is.

DELETE 'ONE RARE ORANGE' BEFORE IT REACHES A VENDOR. Orange is standard. If scarcity is wanted it must be manufactured and declared as a house constraint — 'this panel uses four of the six permitted colours, and the fourth appears only on the wheels' — which is a stronger, checkable rule than a false claim about the craft.

PROOF IT AGAINST THE SHELF BEFORE FIRING. Print the panel at size and pin the three closest existing objects beside it: the Lisbon tram azulejo, a stock talavera flower mural, and a photograph of the Talavera Beetle. If a stranger reads the proof as 'the Mexican version of the Lisbon tram tile', the drawing is not finished. Make that comparison a gate on the fired test tile, not an afterthought.

MAKE THE BARE HATCHES UNMISTAKABLY DELIBERATE. Three unpainted rectangles on a white ground read as unfinished, and they are also the literal truth (the apertures really are openings onto a bright galley), so the concept gets no credit for them as they stand. Ring each one with the panel's heaviest manganese line and drive the ink density up in the surrounding body so the voids are the only quiet in a loud drawing — then the founding fact that the donor bus was bought 'missing three of its windows' reads as a decision rather than an omission.

verdicts.lens: Producibility and fidelity: can this panel actually be made from THIS asset, given failing gates, unbuilt geometry, an unproven large-format chain and a nine-times-rejected emblem — and what unscoped model work does it hide?
verdicts.reasoning:
I verified the concept's load-bearing claims against the machine rather than the prose, and looked at the frame it proposes to trace.

WHAT CHECKS OUT, AND IT IS THE BEST PRODUCIBILITY ARGUMENT IN THE PROGRAM. `studio.views()["side"]` really is `lens=None, ortho=5.90` — a true parallel projection, and `probe_rev73_tailboard.py`'s own calibration (F296, the half that survives F300) says so independently: "an XZ angle projects TRUE in the orthographic `side` view". I measured `out/r75_side.png` myself: ink bbox x 212..1457, y 111..963, fill 77.9% x 77.5%, and border ink top/bottom/left/right = 0/0/0/0. Clean margins, nothing clipped. The concept's front/rear clipping warning also reproduces: `out/r75_front.png` has 40 px of ink on the top border row and 738 on the bottom. The palette argument is sound in the way it claims — a craft with no vermillion cannot inherit the render's largest measured defect (flank_compare live on this tree: reference median (158,16,6) G/R 0.114 against render (196,81,67) G/R 0.422), and a flat glaze cannot inherit gloss_compare's 0.412-of-photograph spread. The side elevation genuinely does not contain the nose roundel, so F191's gate object is out of frame. And the retail asset is a photograph of a fired object, which means this track is immune to the entire unproven delivery chain — hq_render's missing T1_FX=0, stitch.py's untested seam above 3840, post.py destroying alpha and truncating to 8 bits, F192's open dimension. That is the concept's strongest producibility property and it does not state it.

WHAT DOES NOT. Three things break.

(1) THE HERO SILHOUETTE IT NAMES CANNOT BE TRACED FROM THE FRAME IT NAMES. I cropped the tail of `out/r75_side.png` and looked. The "tail board propped" is a white bulb-studded rod at ~38° with two thin dark stay wires, floating clear of the roof dome. No cream face, no red edge stripe, no dark lower stripe, no board. The record already gives the mechanism — F276: "the side elevation looks exactly along the board's plane, so the face is invisible by construction, not by omission", and F295 repeats it: "it shows the board almost exactly EDGE-ON ... the board's FACE is invisible in it". In cobalt on tile that element becomes an inexplicable dotted diagonal. The concept asserts it as part of the panel's composition.

(2) THE LARGEST ELEMENT IN THE FRAME HAS NO PALETTE ALLOCATION. Looking at the whole frame, the mural lid occupies roughly the top 40% of the ink bbox and is the loudest thing in the drawing — a dark brown ground, orange/yellow flowers, olive-yellow menu strips lettered in dark red. The concept allocates cobalt/tin-white/antimony/manganese/copper-green plus one orange spent on hubcaps, and never says what the mural becomes. On a 6x4 panel that is two full tile rows undesigned. Its master is also defective and I confirmed it on disk: `tex/lidmural.png` is 4096x2476 and F74(a) is open — "cropped at the bottom — the bottom row of flowers is sliced mid-bloom and the yellow side columns are truncated" — and `lid_gen.py` is not called by `build.py`, so regenerating it is a hand step.

(3) THE RESOLUTION CLAIM IS WRONG BY ~3x AND "NOTHING BLOCKING" IS FALSE. `ortho=5.90` over 1600 px is 271.2 px/m. At the concept's own 1:8 that is 2.17 px/mm — 55 dpi. That is not a cartoon a painter can pounce a 630 mm panel from; the Señor Tacombi lockup (flank_compare live: 1275.9 x 541.1 mm) is only ~346 px wide in that frame and lands at 159 mm on the panel. And `out/` is untracked and starts empty on a clone, while Cycles here sets no seed — so the named frame is a record, not a durable asset.

Two more traced-in defects the concept does not mention, both in this exact view. `tex/senor.png` contains NO dark ink at all — I measured it: 2,071,536 px at alpha>200, 1st-percentile luma 165.7, fraction below luma 80 = 0.0000 — while SPEC §3 requires the script "SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow". A craft whose entire language is manganese outline would trace a keyline-less wordmark. And the lockup is measurably misplaced: flank_compare live says "the render's lockup has to move +76.2 mm forward and −47.6 mm down", i.e. 9.5 mm and 6.0 mm on a 630 mm panel — made MORE legible, not less, by the concept's deliberate choice to run a grout joint through it, because the joint supplies a datum. Also visible in the frame: a torn white artifact across the cab-door glass.

The idea survives all of this. Every one of the three breaks is a revision, not a refutation, and the underlying material logic — design to the craft's limits, spend the one rare pigment where the eye already goes, let the grid cut the vehicle — is the strongest reason in the program to prefer this over a render-derived print. Strong, not exceptional, because it promises "nothing blocking" while naming a compositional element that does not exist in its own source view.
fatal_flaws: THE PROPPED TAIL BOARD, NAMED IN THE PANEL'S HERO SILHOUETTE, DOES NOT EXIST IN THE SIDE ELEVATION. I cropped out/r75_side.png at the tail and looked: it renders as a white bulb-studded rod at ~38 degrees on two thin stay wires, floating clear of the roof dome — no cream face, no red edge stripe, no dark lower stripe, no board. The record states the mechanism twice: F276 ("the side elevation looks exactly along the board's plane, so the face is invisible by construction, not by omission") and F295 ("it shows the board almost exactly EDGE-ON ... the board's FACE is invisible in it"). In cobalt on tile it reads as a scratch or an aerial.

THE MURAL LID HAS NO PALETTE ALLOCATION, AND IT IS THE LARGEST ELEMENT IN THE FRAME. It occupies roughly the top 40% of the ink bbox — a dark brown ground, orange/yellow flowers, olive-yellow menu strips lettered in dark red. The concept's five pigments cover body, cream, folk art, brass, tyres and hubcaps and stop. Two of six tile rows are undesigned. Its master is also defective on disk (F74(a), tex/lidmural.png 4096x2476, bottom flower row sliced and side columns truncated) and lid_gen.py is not called by build.py.

THE 'NOTHING BLOCKING / TRACE AS-IS' CLAIM IS FALSE ON TWO COUNTS. Resolution: ortho=5.90 over 1600 px is 271.2 px/m = 2.17 px/mm = 55 dpi at the concept's own 1:8. That will not carry the script letterforms, the menu cards or the louvre block into a 630 mm hand-painted cartoon. Durability: out/ is untracked, does not exist on a clone, and the render sets no Cycles seed — the named frame is a record of a reading, not an asset.

tex/senor.png CARRIES NO DARK INK AT ALL — measured: 2,071,536 px at alpha>200, 1st-percentile luma 165.7, fraction below luma 80 = 0.0000 — against SPEC section 3's requirement that the script be 'SILVER with a dark keyline and drop shadow'. Tracing that asset into a manganese-outlined craft yields a keyline-less wordmark on the panel's second-most-important element.

THE THREE BARE HATCHES — the concept's central poetic move — DELETE THREE OF THE OWNER'S NAMED ARTWORK PARTS WITHOUT SAYING SO. The apertures in the frame are full of galley, and the bobble fringe and the pillar menu cards live on and between them. F94 records 'ABSOLUTE REPLICATION OF ALL ARTWORK' as 'a hard bar' and names the menu cards among the seven. The deletion may well be right, but it is an owner-bar departure and the concept passes over it in silence.
improvements: RE-RENDER THE SIDE AT 4800x3300 IN ONE PASS AND COMMIT IT AS A TRACKED CARTOON MASTER. The aspect is identical to 1600x1100 (1.4545) and studio.aim sets sensor_fit='HORIZONTAL' with ortho_scale fixed, so the framing is bit-for-bit the same composition — no re-framing, no re-verification of margins. It gives 813.6 px/m = 6.51 px/mm = 165 dpi at 1:8. Pixel count is 9.0x, so budget ~50 min against the brief's own '~5.5 min a frame' and WATCH it: the largest single-pass in the record is 3200x2200 (F233); 4320x2880 (HANDOFF_rev15) went through hero.py's PAD chain, i.e. stitched. This deliberately avoids hq_render.py + stitch.py + post.py entirely — say so, because it means F49's seam exit code, F192's open dimension and post.py's 8-bit/alpha-destroying path are all out of scope for this track.

ADD A BORDER-INK ASSERTION TO THE CARTOON RENDER AND WATCH IT FAIL FIRST. Measured today on out/r75_side.png: top 0, bottom 0, left 0, right 0 non-white border pixels; on out/r75_front.png: top 40, bottom 738. Assert zero on all four edges of the side cartoon and watch it go red on the front frame before believing it green (rule 3). That is the whole framing risk, tested in one line, and it protects the panel from a silent ortho_scale drift between now and firing.

CUT THE TAIL BOARD FROM THE ORTHOGRAPHIC TRACE AND DRAW IT INSTEAD, OR DROP IT. Two clean options, both cheap. (a) Draw the board's FACE from ref_side.jpg rows 180-320 cols 855-1010, which HANDOFF_CARRIERS section 0.05 records as showing 'a CREAM face, a RED edge stripe, a dark navy/black stripe on the lower edge, and a lit bulb string along it' — and say plainly that this one element departs from the parallel projection, which is a drawing decision a tile painter makes routinely. (b) Omit the board and show the vehicle with the lid up only. Do NOT trace the render's stick. And if (a): carry F245's unresolved chord conflict as a stated ceiling — two-height closure 0.710, calibrated read 0.790, F165 0.829, 11% apart, 'One of them is wrong and nothing in this tree resolves it. Do not average them' — which at 1:8 is 10 mm of panel.

ALLOCATE THE MURAL EXPLICITLY, BEFORE ANY TILE IS FIRED. A concrete proposal that keeps the no-red rule and fixes the panel's tonal balance: mural ground in MANGANESE (the panel's darkest mass, at the top, over the cobalt body), flowers in ANTIMONY YELLOW with cobalt centres, menu strips in raw TIN-WHITE with manganese lettering. That also lets the strips carry the real copy, which I read off the frame: 'FRESH JUICES, GOURMET TACOS & TORTAS' across the head rail and 'GOURMET / TACOS & TORTAS / FRESH / JUICES / CEVICHE TOSTADAS / SHRIMP & FISH / TACOS' down the side columns. Regenerate tex/lidmural.png first (F74(a)) and remember lid_gen.py is NOT called by build.py, so it is a hand step or the render silently keeps the cropped file.

DRAW THE WORDMARK FROM ref_side.jpg, NOT FROM THE RENDER, AND MOVE THE GROUT JOINT OFF IT UNTIL THE PLACEMENT IS RESOLVED. Two independent routes disagree on where it belongs: flank_compare's registration search says the render's lockup must move +76.2 mm forward and -47.6 mm down; the cross-check reads +83/+80 mm aft with the ink top +61.1 mm high. Do not average them. At 1:8 that is 9.5-10.4 mm, and the concept's own joint-through-the-lockup gives the viewer a straightedge to measure it against. Draw the keyline the model does not have — SPEC section 3 already requires it, so this is replication, not invention — and note flank_compare's 'i' region at 0.686 of its own ceiling is a shape defect, not a weight one (ink 657 ref vs 662 render, +0.8%), so a hand redraw fixes it for free.

SPEND THE ONE RARE ORANGE SOMEWHERE VALIDATED, OR VALIDATE THE HUBCAP FIRST. The concept directs the eye to four hubcap domes, which is the one element STATE.md flags as unvalidated: 'hubcap badge is SELF-CONSISTENCY ONLY -- CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC has never been compared to a frame; see PHOTOS_WANTED item 7'. And the stated source, ref_playa_34.png, is a 500x400 three-quarter frame. Use ref_side.jpg (680,540)-(820,680) at 1024x768 instead — square-on to the wheels, the frame the artdirection lane already read the four-band bullseye from. If it cannot be validated, spend the orange on the counter's brass nosing, which is measured (t1_mats: 'brass nosing on the OUTER EDGE, body cream below').

DEFUSE THE LOUVRE COUNT THE WAY THE CONCEPT ALREADY DEFUSES THE TREAD COUNT. The side elevation dodges the tread's 48..84 bracket for free because the transverse lugs sit on the crown and project edge-on — say that, it is a real advantage. But it walks straight into the louvres: t1_detail.py carries LOUV_N = 10 with LOUV_PITCH 0.021111, while AUDIT_rev43.md's tail lane reads 'The rear-quarter louvre block has twelve slots, not ten, and the built block is two slots short' with 'a FLOOR of twelve'. At 1:8 the block is ~24 mm tall at 2.6 mm pitch — countable on the panel. Either draw it as an unresolved dark band with no countable slot count, or resolve the count before firing.

NAME THE SACRIFICE, WITH THE MEASUREMENT THAT LICENSES IT. The bare hatches delete the galley, the bobble fringe and the pillar menu cards — the last of which F94 names among the seven parts under 'ABSOLUTE REPLICATION OF ALL ARTWORK ... A hard bar'. State it as a deliberate reduction and cite the precedent already measured on this vehicle: folk_gen.COMP_HIST's first three bins are (24, 0.42%), (21, 1.32%), (3, 0.55%) — 48 of 66 gold components carry 2.29% of all the gold, and COMP_TOP shows the top three carry 84.4%. That is a measured licence to reduce rather than a taste call, and it is the argument that keeps this from reading as an unaudited departure from an owner bar.

FIX OR MASK THE CAB-DOOR GLASS ARTIFACT BEFORE TRACING. Looking at the frame at the cab, the door glass carries a torn white shape and a dark scribble across it. Whatever it is, a tracer will faithfully reproduce it in cobalt. Crop it and look before the cartoon goes to Puebla — this is rule 1 applied to the one frame the whole artefact depends on.
