STATE THE F191/F193 POSITION IN ONE SENTENCE AT THE TOP OF THE PROPOSAL, AND STATE THE IMMUNITY ARGUMENT WITH IT. 'This is a hand-painted ceramic object photographed under raking light; it is not the delivery render, so F191 ("Keep holding — fix the emblem first") and F193 do not gate it — and because the retail image is a photograph of a fired panel, it inherits none of the render chain's open problems: not the salmon red, not gloss_compare's 0.412, not the 8-bit stitch path, not the unresolved delivery dimension.' That is the single most persuasive producibility paragraph available to this concept and it is currently missing.

verdicts.lens: Emotional resonance, brand fit, and IP exposure
verdicts.reasoning:
The central move is genuinely strong and I will not pretend otherwise: designing to a material's limits rather than skinning it, and the three serving hatches left as bare unpainted glaze — the founding story told in negative, grounded in STATE.md's measured `bay widths 0.516 0.515 0.516` — is the one detail here that would make a person stop. Nobody would mistake this for hippie-bus merch, which is the whole point of the anti-derivative axis.

But on my lens it has three unaddressed problems and one it actively creates.

WRONG REGION, AND THE ONLY JUSTIFICATION GIVEN CREDITS THE WRONG BRAND. SPEC.md §0.1: "bought in Mexico City in 2006, driven through the Yucatán", "parked it comfortably in … Playa del Carmen." Talavera poblana is Puebla — central highlands, ~1,000 km from the vehicle's home and from the brand's founding. The concept's own stated geographic rhyme is "talavera poblana is made in Puebla, and Puebla is where VW de Mexico built the Combi from 1970." That is a VOLKSWAGEN rhyme dressed as a Tacombi one. The single line of copy the concept offers to justify its material credits the German manufacturer, not the restaurant. A brand whose entire claim is Yucatán/Playa authenticity would be commissioning the wrong state's craft and explaining it with the wrong company's factory.

IT REMOVES THE BRAND'S COLOUR AND SPENDS ITS ONE WARM ACCENT ON A VOLKSWAGEN MARK. "There is no vermillion in this craft" is presented as the idea's engine, and it does neatly dodge the render's measured salmon defect. But red-and-cream IS the recognition. The concept's one rare orange — its only warm note, deliberately placed "where the eye goes anyway" — lands on the four hubcap domes, and `t1_detail.py` builds `capvw` glyphs on those caps (STATE.md: `capvw | 8`). So the piece's focal accent is four Volkswagen roundels, on a sold physical object, made in Puebla, whose entire subject is a trademarked vehicle silhouette in true profile. The grounded market read is explicit: "The images of classic Beetle and Bus vehicles are themselves protected as trademarks", and licensed VW bus tees exist on eBay. Of every format in this programme, a permanent hand-painted ceramic panel of the whole vehicle in elevation is the highest exposure — and the concept's production notes carry a ceiling on Tacombi brand colours and say nothing at all about VW.

THE WORDMARK — THE ONLY TACOMBI-SPECIFIC MARK IN THE SIDE ELEVATION — IS UNASSIGNED, AND THE MATERIAL CANNOT RENDER IT. `build.py` puts `script_L` on the flank at `SCR = dict(x0=0.784, x1=-0.494, ...)`, squarely in view. The palette paragraph assigns cobalt, tin-white, antimony, manganese and one orange to body, cream, folk art, line, tyres and hubcaps — and never names the script. Worse, the owner has ruled on its finish: F157, "Bright silver, same as Tacombi", overriding SPEC §3's weathered lock for that word. Traditional maiolica has no metallic in the six. So the brand's single ruled-on artwork finish is unrenderable in the chosen material, and the concept has not noticed. Meanwhile the brief deliberately runs a grout joint through that lockup — good instinct on the grid, but it is being run through the one element that says "Tacombi."

BRAND VOICE. Grounded reality on shop.tacombi.com: "casual, convenient leisure products since 2006", "Seaside Expo Tote", "Horizon Beanie", "Monument T", "purpose-built, all-weather knit." That is deadpan leisure-outfitter catalogue. A heavy heritage ceramic panel with civic weight is a different company's voice. Not fatal — "Monument T" suggests they have some appetite for the register — but the concept asserts fit rather than testing it.

EMOTIONAL CLAIM, AUDITED. "Permanence and civic weight… somebody built this on purpose, expecting it to outlast them" is real and well-argued for ONE object: the panel on the restaurant wall. It flatters the founder and the press. It does not yet describe a person who buys something. And the format ladder quietly dissolves the idea: talavera coasters with a rosette on them are the most generic object in any Mexican restaurant gift shop, and "the panel photographed square-on… A2 poster, tote, tissue wrap" is tile-texture merch — a printed picture of a craft object, which is precisely the derivative move the concept was built to escape. The anchor is excellent; the ladder beneath it is where the idea leaks out.

Not a kill: every one of these is fixable without touching the core insight, and the hatches-in-negative idea is worth keeping through the fixes. But as briefed it is a beautiful object with the wrong state's craft, no brand red, no wordmark colour, four VW roundels as its focal accent, and a retail tail that lands in the souvenir aisle.
fatal_flaws: THE GEOGRAPHIC JUSTIFICATION CREDITS VOLKSWAGEN, NOT TACOMBI. Talavera poblana is Puebla; SPEC.md §0.1 puts the vehicle 'bought in Mexico City in 2006, driven through the Yucatán' and 'parked… in Playa del Carmen'. The concept's only stated rhyme is that Puebla is 'where VW de Mexico built the Combi from 1970'. The material has no link to the brand's own place — the link runs through the German manufacturer.

THE ONE WARM ACCENT IS SPENT ON FOUR VOLKSWAGEN ROUNDELS. The concept places its single rare orange on the hubcap domes 'where the eye goes anyway', and t1_detail.py builds `capvw` glyphs there (STATE.md: `capvw | 8`). A Tacombi-specific route existed at that exact spot — the '1963' plate motif, or a plain dome — and was not taken.

HIGHEST IP EXPOSURE OF ANY FORMAT IN THE PROGRAMME, UNMENTIONED. A sold, permanent, hand-painted ceramic object whose whole subject is a trademarked vehicle in true side elevation, carrying VW marks four times. Grounded market read: 'The images of classic Beetle and Bus vehicles are themselves protected as trademarks.' The production notes carry a ceiling on Tacombi's brand colour and say nothing about VW at all.

THE WORDMARK HAS NO COLOUR AND THE MATERIAL CANNOT GIVE IT ONE. `script_L` sits on the flank (build.py `SCR = dict(x0=0.784, x1=-0.494, …)`), so it is in the view; the palette paragraph never assigns it. Owner ruling F157 — 'Bright silver, same as Tacombi' — specifies a metallic that traditional maiolica's six-colour palette cannot fire. The brand's only ruled-on artwork finish is unrenderable here and the brief has not noticed.

REMOVING RED IS ASSERTED AS A GAIN, NEVER TESTED. 'Stripped of its red the bus stops reading as fun and becomes a monument' is a strong claim about a person's reaction, offered with no proof, on a brand whose recognition is red-and-cream. It also conveniently sidesteps the project's largest measured defect — which is a reason to suspect the argument, not to trust it.

THE FORMAT LADDER DISSOLVES THE IDEA. Talavera coasters with a rosette are indistinguishable from any Mexican gift-shop stock; 'the panel photographed square-on… A2 poster, tote, tissue wrap' is a printed picture of a craft object, i.e. tile-texture merch. The anchor is distinctive; every SKU under it drifts toward the generic.

BRAND VOICE MISMATCH, UNADDRESSED. Tacombi's live retail voice is 'casual, convenient leisure products since 2006' — 'Seaside Expo Tote', 'Horizon Beanie', 'purpose-built, all-weather knit'. Heritage ceramic with civic weight is a different register. The concept asserts fit and never argues it.

NO BUYER IS NAMED. The emotional case is built for the restaurant wall and the founder's sense of permanence. Who pays for the framed retail panel, and why, is unstated — which is the difference between a press object and a product.
improvements: MOVE THE CRAFT TO THE VEHICLE'S OWN REGION: pasta tile / mosaico hidráulico, the unglazed pressed-cement floor tile that is the domestic vernacular of Mérida and the Yucatán coast — i.e. the place SPEC.md says the bus was parked. Three wins at once: the geography becomes Tacombi's own rather than Volkswagen's; the palette is mineral oxide, which INCLUDES a terracotta/oxide red, so the brand's colour survives; and it is matte, cheaper, faster and lower-variance than a certified talavera taller. VERIFY the oxide-red claim with a sample before committing — I have not measured it. If talavera is kept anyway, DELETE the Puebla/VW-plant line from the copy entirely: it credits the wrong company.

KILL THE VW GLYPH FROM THE HUBCAPS AND PUT THE ORANGE ON A TACOMBI MARK. The concept's own logic — one rare accent, placed where the eye already goes — is right; the target is wrong. Paint the four cap domes plain oxide, or carry the '1963' from the engine-lid plate (SPEC §4: 'chrome number-plate surround on the engine lid reading "1963", empty') as the single warm motif. Removes four reproductions of a trademarked mark from a sold physical object and moves the focal accent onto something only this bus has. This one change is the largest single upgrade available.

RESOLVE THE WORDMARK BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE IS FIRED, AND SHOW HIM FIRED TILES. F157 rules it bright silver and the material has no metallic. Three real options, and they are cheap to test as three single tiles: (a) RESERVE — leave the script as bare unpainted ground with a manganese outline, the traditional maiolica reserve technique, which puts it in the same visual family as the three empty hatches and makes the negative-space idea a system rather than a one-off; (b) a second lustre firing on the wordmark ALONE — genuinely expensive, genuinely permanent, and it is literally the concept's own emotional claim ('expensive materials, expecting it to outlast them'); (c) cobalt, and accept the loss. Put the three fired tiles to the owner as multiple choice with the crop attached — this is exactly the project's own asking protocol and it is a question about a photograph of a tile, which he can answer.

CONTROL WHICH JOINT CROSSES THE LOCKUP. Running grout through the vehicle is the right instinct and should stay. Running it through a LETTER of the only Tacombi-specific mark in the frame is not. Offset the 105 mm grid so the joint that crosses the script falls in the word gap between 'Señor' and 'Tacombi', or below the baseline. Keep the joint through the wheel — that one earns its keep.

PUT THE 'NO RED' CLAIM ON TRIAL, AT SIZE, BEFORE COMMISSIONING. Two flat proofs printed at 630 × 420 mm on matte, pinned at 2 m: cobalt body vs oxide-red body, everything else identical. Show him both as multiple choice with the reference photograph attached. He has never seen this bus in any colour but red; 'stripped of red it becomes a monument' is a prediction about his own reaction and he is the only instrument for it. Half a day, and it decides the whole programme's palette.

NAME THE MAKER, ON THE OBJECT AND IN THE COPY, AND SHARE THE REVENUE. A US-headquartered taqueria commissioning a protected Mexican craft to render a German vehicle is a story that goes either way depending entirely on whether the taller is a credited partner or an anonymous vendor. Signed-and-dated on the reverse is not enough — put the workshop's name on the front-facing copy, on the retail card and in the press line, with a share. This converts the largest cultural exposure in the concept into the strongest authenticity asset Tacombi could hold, and it is on-brand in a way a tote is not.

REBUILD THE FORMAT LADDER AROUND THE NEGATIVE SPACE, AND DROP THE COASTERS. The idea's best asset is three empty rectangles that mean something. Anchor: the 24-tile panel, installed at each location on OPENING DAY, with that location's city and date fired into the corner tile — a ritual object staff and regulars can point at, not a lobby decoration. Retail: a SINGLE tile, 105 mm, boxed — the three hatches alone, or '1963' — priced to be bought on impulse and to sit on a shelf as an object rather than under a glass as a coaster. Cut the six-coaster set and the trivet from launch entirely; they are the SKUs that make it look like everyone else's tile.

IF PRINTED DERIVATIVES SHIP, PHOTOGRAPH THE OBJECT, NEVER THE PATTERN. A tote carrying a flattened square-on scan is tile-texture merch and inherits none of the concept's meaning. Shoot it raking, with the panel's edge, its shadow, the wall behind and a hand or a sleeve in frame — so the printed piece reads as evidence that a heavy physical thing exists somewhere. Deadpan product-catalogue framing, which is also the one register that matches the live shop voice ('purpose-built', 'Monument T').

GET A ONE-LINE ANSWER FROM THE OWNER ON VW BEFORE ANY CLAY IS CUT. He is the brand; he may already hold an arrangement, in which case this is a non-issue and should be recorded as such. If he does not, a permanent physical object of a trademarked vehicle in full profile is the wrong place in the programme to find out. Ask it as one sentence alongside the palette question — not as a legal opinion, as a fact only he has.

concept.title: TRES HUECOS — The Aperture Wall
concept.one_line: Take the bus out entirely and repeat only the hole it has instead of windows: three hatches at life size, at the exact height they sit on the real vehicle, so standing at the wall is standing at the counter.
concept.the_image:
NO VEHICLE. The repeat unit is the serving side's architecture, drawn flat, at 1:1, from the constants rather than from any render.

THE UNIT, measured off t1_shell.py and STATE.md: three apertures, each 515.5 × 403.0 mm (`BAY_W = 0.5155  # equal, measured` and `Z_SILL, Z_HEAD, BAY_R = 1.3720, 1.7750, 0.0550`), corner radius 55.0 mm, on centres `BAY_CX = (0.6720, 0.0470, -0.5980)`. That gives pitches of 625.0 and 645.0 mm and therefore pillars of 109.5 and 129.5 mm — THE TWO PILLARS ARE NOT EQUAL, and the 20 mm difference is the single most important instruction in this concept. Every designer's hand will want to regularise it. Do not. It is measured, it is the hand of the man who cut the holes, and it is what stops the wall reading as a template. Total repeat span 1785.5 mm.

THE COURSES, every height machine-written and rendered at 1:1 ABOVE THE ACTUAL FLOOR: the aperture band sits 1.307–1.710 m (STATE.md: `band 1.372-1.775 un-dropped (1.307-1.710 AG)`). Below it, the belt line at 1.2070 m (`belt line @ x=0.962 (live) | 1.2070`) is the red/cream break — cream above, red below. Lower still, a fine horizontal stripe of ten slots at 21.111 mm pitch across 0.1900 m, running 0.895–1.085 m AG (t1_detail.py `LOUV_N = 10`, `LOUV_Z_TOP, LOUV_Z_BOT = 1.0850, 0.8950`, `LOUV_PITCH = 0.021111`) — the louvre band, which is the only regular repeat the real vehicle owns. The whole wall is therefore raked: the roof line falls at 17.75 mm/m (`rake 17.75 mm/m (locked 17.75)`), so every course is drawn on a 1.02° descent, front to back. It is imperceptible and it is why the wall breathes.

INK, three flats plus a scallop: field CREAM sRGB(206,208,200); the band below the belt in RED sRGB(196,49,36); the apertures themselves NEAR-BLACK, flat, no rendering, no interior — holes, not windows. Round the inside edge of every aperture runs a scalloped row of cream balls: the white bobble fringe, which t1_detail.py records as "CONFIRMED present in ref_side.jpg — a scalloped row of white balls runs round the inside edge of all three apertures". Optional fourth ink: brass `COUNTERTAN = (0.5870, 0.4930, 0.3060)     # = sRGB (201,186,150)` as a 20 mm rule at the sill, standing for the counter's nosing.

At small scales the same unit becomes a pure geometric repeat — three soft-cornered rectangles, two unequal gaps, a fine stripe below — and reads as mid-century modernist grid work until someone tells you what it is.
concept.emotional_claim:
BEING SERVED. This is the only pattern in the programme with a body position built into it: printed at 1:1 with the apertures at 1.307–1.710 m above the actual floor, an adult stands at the wall exactly as they stand at the hatch — the sill at the wrist, the head rail above the eye. You cannot walk past it neutrally; the wall puts you in a queue. The emotion is the anticipation of the moment before food arrives, which is the single strongest feeling this brand actually sells, and it is delivered by dimension rather than by picture.

Underneath that sits the origin story, told without a word. The $3,000 bus was "missing three of its windows" (SPEC §0.1, graded S — the founder's own account); the signature feature of this company is an ABSENCE. A pattern made only of that absence says it better than any image of the vehicle could. And the 20 mm pillar asymmetry is the tenderness in it: somebody cut these by eye and got them nearly, humanly, not-quite even.
formats: 1:1 digital wall mural, non-woven wallcovering, 1.3 m drops, wall height 2.6–3.0 m. Horizontal repeat 1785.5 mm, so the repeat crosses drops — panel-print it per wall rather than sell it as a roll. THE PRIMARY USE: restaurant interiors, the Nolita/Playa dining rooms, event walls.
1:4 — repeat 446.4 mm, apertures 128.9 × 100.8 mm, pillars 27.4 / 32.4 mm. Packaging wrap, shipper boxes, menu covers, tissue.
1:12 — repeat 148.8 mm, apertures 43.0 × 33.6 mm, pillars 9.1 / 10.8 mm. Textile: shirting, jacket lining, bandana, scarf border, apron.

Encaustic / cement floor tile, 200 mm: one bay per tile, three tiles plus grout = one repeat, the unequal pillars expressed as two different grout widths. The most Mexican object in the whole programme, and it needs no render at all.
Perforated metal or laser-cut screen at 1:1 — the pattern as an actual architectural element, back-lit, in a doorway or a service pass.
Tile-and-stripe combination for tabletop laminate and paper placemats, 1:6.
concept.why_not_derivative:
There is no bus in it. That single decision puts it outside the entire VW-bus merchandise category — you cannot compare it to a sunset silhouette, a line drawing, a blueprint or a doodle tile, because it does not depict a vehicle at all. It also passes the logo-removal test completely: strip every word off it and it is still unmistakably one specific object's architecture.

The stock alternative — "repeat the windows of a VW bus" — would give you a row of EQUAL rectangles, because a factory bus has equal glass. Ours has three equal holes at UNEQUAL centres, which only exists because somebody cut them into a bus that was already missing its glass. The 625/645 mm pitch against the 515.5 mm bay is a fingerprint no stock asset can carry and no one can copy without the measurement.

And it carries zero trademark exposure on either claim: no VW roundel appears anywhere, and the trade-dress content — three cut apertures, a bobble fringe, a counter nosing, a louvre band — is entirely the conversion, none of which Volkswagen made.
concept.production_notes:
THIS IS THE CHEAPEST AND LEAST GATED CONCEPT IN THE PROGRAMME. It needs no render, no Blender, no alpha, no stitch chain and no delivery-render permission — every figure above is read off t1_shell.py, t1_detail.py and STATE.md and can be drawn in Illustrator this week. That is not a compromise; the pattern is BETTER drawn than rendered, because a photoreal aperture would carry the render's salmon red (flank_compare: render (196,81,67) against the photograph's (158,16,6)) and the paint's measured gloss deficit (gloss_compare on out/r75_hero34f.png: render spread 0.495 against the photograph's 1.202 — 0.412 of it, FAIL against a 0.60 bar). A flat drawing has neither problem, and the real bus is hand-painted flat colour anyway.

THE ONE THING THAT IS NOT MEASURED, STATED PLAINLY: the bobble fringe's ball diameter and pitch. t1_detail.py says so itself — "Ball diameter and pitch are INFERRED (each ball is ~2 px)." So the scallop is a DRAWN DECISION, not a measurement. Draw it, declare it as a design choice, and do not let it acquire a false provenance line. Everything else on the sheet is machine-written.

IF YOU WANT DEPTH IN THE APERTURES — don't, for v1. Flat black is stronger and it is honest. If a later version wants the galley visible through the holes, note that F45 (roof-aperture interior) and F15 (unlit roofed body, 6.92e5 px², item 4 of 16 in visibility_budget) are BOTH ungated: nothing in the tree has ever measured whether the inside of this vehicle renders lit. Render one side frame and look through the bays before committing a wall to it.

THE FRINGE IS UNDER-BUILT BY ONE APERTURE. The model puts the bobble fringe round the three serving bays only (`for i, (xr, xf) in enumerate(S.BAYS)`, STATE.md `fringe | 3`), but the photographs put it round the WINDSCREEN too. Irrelevant to this pattern, which uses only the serving side — but it is a found element with no register row, and it should be recorded rather than lost.

PRINT: 3–4 spot flats, no process build. The near-black aperture wants a solid, not a rich black build, or the 55 mm corner radii will show registration fringing at 1:1. On the tile version, fire the aperture as a single glaze — the whole appeal is one uninterrupted dark field against cream.

SCALE DISCIPLINE: line weights must be specified in FINAL MILLIMETRES per product, never scaled from a master. The louvre stripe at 1:1 is 21.111 mm pitch and reads as ten strokes; at 1:12 it is 1.76 mm and reads as ten strokes; at 1:50 it is 0.42 mm and becomes a grey band. Decide at which product it stops being slots and becomes a rule, and draw that separately.
model_work_required: NONE FOR v1. This is the concept's chief virtue and it should be stated as such in any proposal: every dimension is already machine-written and no capability in the tree needs to be exercised, fixed or unblocked to ship it.

IF a later version wants real depth in the apertures: F45 (roof-aperture interior) and F15 (A7, unlit roofed body, 6.92e5 px²) are both UNGATED — never measured against a photograph. Render one `side` frame, crop it at the bays, and look through them before designing to what is behind the holes.

THE BOBBLE FRINGE'S BALL DIAMETER AND PITCH ARE INFERRED, NOT MEASURED (t1_detail.py: "each ball is ~2 px"). If the scallop is going to carry a 1:1 wall, one close square-on frame of an aperture edge would close it. PHOTOS_WANTED has an existing carrier structure for exactly this kind of ask, and it has never had a fringe item.

OPTIONAL AND CHEAP: nothing here reads the mesh, so add a small script that IMPORTS `t1_shell.BAY_W`, `BAY_CX`, `Z_SILL`, `Z_HEAD`, `BAY_R` and `t1_detail.LOUV_PITCH`, `LOUV_N`, `LOUV_Z_TOP`, `LOUV_Z_BOT` and prints the pattern's final millimetres per named scale. Re-derive; do not transcribe. A transcribed table goes stale silently and this repository has a rule about that.

verdicts.lens: ORIGINALITY — is this genuinely fresh, or a well-executed version of something already on a thousand products? Judged only on that axis; I verified the load-bearing dimensional claims against live source because in this concept the *dimensions are the originality argument*.
verdicts.reasoning:
The editorial move is genuinely good and I want to say so before attacking it: deleting the vehicle and patterning only the hole is the one decision in this set that steps outside the VW-bus merch category entirely, and it is defensible from the founder's own account (the bus was "missing three of its windows"). That is a real idea.

But the FORM it takes is a populated genre, and the concept names none of its neighbours. Three soft-cornered apertures in a row, cream field, red band below, fine slot-stripe under, optionally in cement tile — that is celosía / breeze-block screen work (an entire Mexican and mid-century architectural pattern category), it is mosaico hidráulico (Mexican pasta tile, where cream/red geometric repeats are the saturated default), and it is the mid-century curtain-wall / Case Study facade repeat that has been a wallcovering staple for twenty years. The concept's own text concedes this — "reads as mid-century modernist grid work until someone tells you what it is." The "our brand is the absence" conceit is separately one of the most-taught tropes in graphic design (FedEx arrow, WWF panda). None of that is disqualifying; it means the concept must earn its freshness on the specific payload, and the payload is where it fails verification.

THE ORIGINALITY HOOK IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The concept says the 20 mm pillar asymmetry is "measured, it is the hand of the man who cut the holes... an uncopyable human fingerprint," and the screener's note leans on it hardest. The arithmetic is right — `BAY_CX = (0.6720, 0.0470, -0.5980)` and `BAY_W = 0.5155` give pitches 625.0/645.0 and pillars 109.5/129.5 mm. But the same comment block that supplies those centres states their uncertainty in the same sentence: "Measured bay centres, from six sub-pixel cut edges anchored by ratio to the two hubs... +0.672 / +0.047 / -0.598 **+/- 0.015**." Propagated, each pitch carries ±21.2 mm and their difference ±30.0 mm. The 20 mm asymmetry is **0.67σ** — indistinguishable from equal on the source's own stated error. And SPEC.md, summarising the same geometry two lines after publishing those centres, writes: "Corner radius 0.055, **pillars 0.11**" — one number, not two. So the project's own record does not hold the asymmetry the concept is built on. This is precisely the class of defect this repo has rules about (rule 5: never put a figure in a test you have not watched print; rule 12: report the measurement with its ceiling). The concept publishes a differentiator at 0.67σ with no ceiling attached.

THE ORIGINALITY LIVES AT ONE FORMAT OF SIX. The fresh part — 1:1, sill at a real body height, "the wall puts you in a queue" — exists only on the 1:1 wall. At 1:4 packaging, 1:12 textile, 200 mm tile, placemat and screen, the body-position device is gone and what remains is the generic grid the concept itself named. Five of the six listed formats are competent mid-century geometry.

AND THE BODY-POSITION CLAIM, WHICH IS THE EMOTIONAL CORE, IS WRONG BY ABOUT HALF A METRE. "the sill at the wrist" — the sill is at 1.307 m AG (STATE.md: `band 1.372-1.775 un-dropped (1.307-1.710 AG)`). An adult's wrist is around 0.8 m. 1.307 m is sternum-to-shoulder. The real geometry is more interesting than the claim: `CNT_ZT, CNT_ZB = 1.2540, 1.1470` puts the counter top ~1.189 m AG (my arithmetic, using the 65 mm drop the band itself carries at that station — the ride drop varies with x, so this is approximate), i.e. a 118 mm step from counter top to aperture sill and a head rail at 1.710 m. That is a chest-high counter under a brow-high window — a ticket-window posture, not a bar. Nobody has drawn that, and it is a better story than the one in the brief.

TWO "MEASURED" ELEMENTS ARE TRANSPLANTS, which matters because the authenticity of the dimensions IS the originality argument. (a) The louvre stripe: `LOUV_X0, LOUV_X1 = T._aft(-1.2850), T._aft(-1.6700)` — the block sits aft of x −1.285, while the repeat spans −0.856…+0.930. It is nowhere near the apertures; running it under all three bays is invention wearing a machine-written figure. (b) The brass "20 mm rule at the sill": the counter nosing is on the counter's outer edge at ~1.08–1.19 m AG, ~120 mm below the sill and outboard of the body plane. Both are drawings decisions dressed as measurements.

FINALLY, THE LOGO-REMOVAL TEST IS ASSERTED, NOT PASSED. "strip every word off it and it is still unmistakably one specific object's architecture" — only to someone who has stood at this bus. To everyone else, three rounded rectangles are a mid-century grid. The two elements that could actually make it attributable — the bobble fringe and the brass nosing — are exactly the ones the concept marks as a "drawn decision" and "optional fourth ink." The identity-carrying marks are demoted and the generic ones promoted.

Net: a strong editorial instinct, honest about its own production reality, executed as a form that already exists in three adjacent categories, with its single claimed fingerprint failing at 0.67σ. That is workable, not strong.
fatal_flaws: THE UNCOPYABLE FINGERPRINT IS NOT ESTABLISHED. t1_shell.py states the bay centres as '+0.672 / +0.047 / -0.598 +/- 0.015'. Propagated, the difference between the two pillars carries +/-30.0 mm; the claimed 20 mm asymmetry is 0.67 sigma. SPEC.md, describing the same geometry, publishes 'Corner radius 0.055, pillars 0.11' — ONE pillar figure. The concept's central originality claim is contradicted by the record it cites.

THE FRESH IDEA EXISTS AT ONLY ONE OF SIX FORMATS. The 1:1 body-position device is the whole originality. At 1:4, 1:12, 200 mm tile, placemat and screen it is absent, and what remains is — in the concept's own words — 'mid-century modernist grid work.'

IT DOES NOT NAME ITS NEIGHBOURS, AND THEY ARE CROWDED: celosia / breeze-block screen patterns, Mexican mosaico hidraulico (the concept's own tile format is the saturated centre of that category), mid-century curtain-wall facade wallcoverings, and the 'brand-as-negative-space' trope (FedEx, WWF). A concept claiming category escape must show the escape.

THE EMOTIONAL CLAIM IS DIMENSIONALLY WRONG. 'the sill at the wrist' — the sill is 1.307 m AG (STATE.md), roughly sternum height. The counter top is a separate, lower line (CNT_ZT 1.2540 un-dropped, ~1.19 m AG), and the 118 mm step between them is the actual serving posture. The one thing the concept says only IT can do, it has mis-specified.

TWO ELEMENTS ARE TRANSPLANTED FROM ELSEWHERE ON THE VEHICLE WHILE CARRYING MEASURED FIGURES. The louvre band lives at x -1.285..-1.670 (t1_detail.LOUV_X0/X1), entirely aft of the -0.856..+0.930 repeat; the brass nosing sits ~120 mm below the sill on the counter's outer edge. Presenting them as courses of the aperture wall breaks the 'every figure is machine-written' claim that the originality rests on.

THE LOGO-REMOVAL TEST FAILS AS DRAWN. The only two marks that make three rectangles attributable to THIS bus — the bobble fringe and the brass nosing — are marked 'a DRAWN DECISION' and 'Optional fourth ink'. Without them the pattern is not identifiable as Tacombi by anyone who has not been served at the vehicle.
improvements: REPLACE THE FINGERPRINT. Drop the 20 mm inter-bay asymmetry (0.67 sigma, and SPEC says 'pillars 0.11'). Use the DOOR-TO-BAY-0 pillar instead: REF_MEASUREMENTS.md item 6 — 'The pillar between the door and aperture 1 is only 0.128 m — the conversion cut the openings hard up against the cab.' That is an asymmetry with a stated CAUSE, and it puts the fingerprint at the repeat's EDGE where it is visible, not in a 20 mm interior wobble. CEILING YOU MUST CARRY: REF's 0.128 m does not reconcile with the constants — its own shutline at model X = +0.948 against BAYS[0][1] = 0.92975 gives 18 mm, and REF_MEASUREMENTS is the file carrying the documented 100 mm origin error (SPEC 10.29). So this needs ONE re-measurement before it can be printed: six sub-pixel edges anchored by ratio to the two hubs, the same method that produced the bay centres. That single measurement is the only work this concept owes and it converts an unfounded claim into a founded one.

MAKE THE REPEAT TWO-STATE, AND LET THE CONVERSION BE THE PATTERN. The show side has three holes; the off side still has GLASS (t1_shell: 'OPEN_BAYS = (0, 1, 2)  # +Y show side: all three glass removed'). Alternate an unglazed run against a glazed run across the wall. That encodes 'somebody cut one side of this bus open' as a compositional device rather than as a dimension, it is a fact no stock asset can carry, and — critically — it survives every scale down to 1:12, which the 1:1 body-position device does not.

CUT THE LOUVRE STRIPE OR MOVE IT WHERE THE MESH PUTS IT. It is at x -1.285..-1.670, aft of the whole repeat. If a lower band is wanted, use the two things that are actually there: the belt line at 1.2070 and the solid cream panel aft of bay 3 that carries the Calidad decal (SPEC: 'Aft of bay 3 is solid sheet metal'). That gives the repeat a genuine TERMINUS — the wall stops being an infinite grid and becomes a vehicle-length unit with an end, which is both truer and less generic than an endless repeat.

PROMOTE THE FRINGE AND THE BRASS FROM OPTIONAL TO MANDATORY, AND GO GET THE PHOTOGRAPH. They are the only two elements that make the pattern attributable. t1_detail.py says 'Ball diameter and pitch are INFERRED (each ball is ~2 px)' — so commission ONE close square-on frame of an aperture edge; PHOTOS_WANTED has the carrier structure and has never had a fringe item. Draw the brass at its true station (counter nosing, ~1.08-1.19 m AG, outboard) rather than as a rule at the sill, and the wall gains a second horizontal at a different depth — which is also what stops it reading flat.

DESIGN A SECOND UNIT FOR SMALL SCALE INSTEAD OF SCALING THIS ONE. At 1:12 the apertures are 43 x 33.6 mm and the queue is gone. Concrete rule: below 1:6, stop drawing the aperture and draw the SILL LINE + fringe scallop as a border rule — the serving edge, not the hole. One mark for the wall, a different mark for cloth and packaging. That converts the 'originality lives at one format' flaw into a deliberate two-mark system.

FIX THE BODY-POSITION SPEC AND MAKE IT THE HEADLINE. Draw THREE courses at their true AG heights: counter top ~1.19 m, aperture sill 1.307 m, head rail 1.710 m (CNT_ZT 1.2540 un-dropped plus the 65 mm drop the band carries at that station — state that the drop varies with x and that this is arithmetic, not a printed figure). The 118 mm step from counter to sill is the posture nobody else has drawn: you are served at chest height through a window whose head is at your brow. Rewrite the emotional claim around that and it stops being a wrong assertion and becomes the concept's strongest and most specific asset.

PUT THE PRIOR ART IN THE DECK AND BEAT IT ON THE PAGE. One spread, four thumbnails: a celosia screen, a mosaico hidraulico floor, a mid-century curtain-wall wallcovering, and a negative-space logo. Under each, the one sentence saying what this does that it does not — chiefly: those are INVENTED grids, this is a MEASURED one, and its irregularities have causes. A concept whose whole pitch is 'not derivative' currently asserts that without evidence; naming the neighbours and out-specifying them is what would move it from workable to strong.

STATE THE PROVENANCE OF EVERY LINE ON THE ARTWORK ITSELF. Print a key: MEASURED (bay width, band heights, corner radius, belt line), MEASURED-WITH-STATED-ERROR (bay centres, +/-15 mm), INFERRED (fringe ball pitch), DRAWN (everything else). On a 1:1 restaurant wall that key can literally be a small plate at the corner — and it converts the project's obsessive methodology into the artefact's own content, which is a piece of originality nobody in the VW-bus category can copy because nobody else has 75 revisions of measurement to cite.

verdicts.lens: PRODUCIBILITY AND FIDELITY — can this be made from this asset, given failing gates, unbuilt geometry, an unproven large-format chain and a held delivery render; and are the numbers it publishes actually measurements?
verdicts.reasoning:
On pure producibility this is the strongest concept I could be handed. It is the only one that clears every gate the grounded reality names, and it clears them by not touching them: no render, so it never inherits the salmon red (flank_compare live: render median (196,81,67) against the photograph's (158,16,6), G/R 0.422 vs 0.114) or the gloss deficit (gloss_compare on r75_hero34f: spread 0.495 against the photograph's 1.202, FAIL at a 0.60 bar); no T1_ALPHA, thirteen revisions un-run; no hq_render/stitch/post chain, which carries zero verify_clone rows and has never been proven above 3840; no emblem, so F191's hold and the ninth report are simply not in scope; no VW roundel, so the trademark exposure the market lane names is genuinely absent. "NONE FOR v1" under model_work_required is true, and that is rare and valuable.

But the lens is producibility AND FIDELITY, and the concept's own thesis is that the emotion is delivered by dimension rather than by picture. That converts every published figure into a load-bearing part. Three of them fail against the source, and one fails fatally.

The 20 mm pillar asymmetry — which the concept calls "the single most important instruction in this concept," which the screener calls "an uncopyable human fingerprint," and which is the entire why_not_derivative argument — is below its own measurement floor. t1_shell.py states the uncertainty in the same comment block the concept quotes its centres from: "+0.672 / +0.047 / -0.598 +/- 0.015". A pitch is a difference of two centres (sigma 21.2 mm); the asymmetry is a difference of two pitches (sigma 30.0 mm). 20.0 +/- 30.0 is 0.67 sigma. Three equal 119.5 mm pillars sit comfortably inside the measurement. Worse, the concept is re-committing a defect this repository already retired: the same comment block kills SPEC 10.5's bay taper with "Held equal: a 2 mm taper is below the measurement floor and inventing one is how 10.5's version got here." The taper was sub-floor variation in bay WIDTH; this is sub-floor variation in bay SPACING. Same error, one level up, and the source refutes it twenty lines above the constants the concept cites.

The 1.307 m body anchor is read at the wrong station. rake_drop(x) = 0.047925 + 0.017750x is applied per-vertex at build.py step 8b, so the AG sill is x-dependent: 1.3121 at bay 0, 1.3232 at bay 1, 1.3347 at bay 2. STATE.md's "1.307-1.710 AG" is the value at X_DROP_REF = 0.96197 — forward of the leading edge of bay 0, i.e. at a station that is not on any aperture. t1_shell.py's own comment ("ends up at z - 0.065 above ground") is the same simplification and is true only at that station. The concept transcribed a prose line instead of asking the geometry, which is the specific failure mode CLAUDE.md's rule 10 exists for. The error is 5 to 28 mm — small, but this is a concept that asks to be judged on millimetres.

The rake sign is inverted. Drop grows forward, so AG courses rise toward the tail: STATE.md reads roof 1.9399 at the front axle against 1.9833 at the rear, and slope "-18.1 mm/m" in x. "Every course is drawn on a 1.02 deg descent, front to back" is backwards, and it is the sentence the concept is proudest of.

Then a geometric contradiction that is purely a production problem: a raked motif cannot tile horizontally. Over one 1785.5 mm repeat the courses climb 31.7 mm, so any true horizontal repeat must jog by 31.7 mm at every boundary. For the 1:1 panel-printed wall this is fine — it is a mural, and the concept says so. For the 1:4 packaging wrap, the 1:12 textile, the 1:6 placemat and above all the cement tile ("one bay per tile, three tiles plus grout = one repeat"), it breaks: with a rake, the three tiles are three different artworks at three different aperture heights, not one SKU repeated. Four of six named formats need the rake dropped, and the concept never says which of its two mutually exclusive properties wins.

Finally the louvre band is spatially fabricated and numerically contested. LOUV_X0/X1 = _aft(-1.2850), _aft(-1.6700) — both aft of the rear axle at -1.100, so the block sits several hundred millimetres behind bay 2's rear edge at -0.856, entirely outside the 1785.5 mm repeat. It is a discrete ~385 mm patch on the rear quarter, not a course running under the apertures. And the concept calls it "the only regular repeat the real vehicle owns" while AUDIT_rev43.md line 158 carries a fidelity finding against it: "The rear-quarter louvre block has twelve slots, not ten, and the built block is two slots short," with the ceiling adding that "the louvre count is capped at a FLOOR of twelve." Ten is the built defect, not the measurement, and the concept proposes to print it at 1:1.

The body-position claim is also wrong in a way that matters, because it is the emotional payload. A sill at 1.31-1.33 m is at the sternum of a 1.75 m adult, not "at the wrist" — standing wrist height is roughly half of stature. The head rail claim survives (1.715-1.738 m is above a ~1.63 m eye height). The real reading is that you reach UP to a serving hatch, which is a better and truer observation than the one written, and it connects to the children's audience F18 already names.

None of this is unfixable, and none of the fixes needs Blender, a render or an owner decision — which is why this lands at workable rather than weak. But as written it publishes four wrong numbers in a concept whose whole argument is that its numbers are the art, and its differentiation rests on a difference that is 0.67 sigma. It is not yet the thing the screener thinks it is.
fatal_flaws: THE 20 mm PILLAR ASYMMETRY IS BELOW ITS OWN MEASUREMENT FLOOR AND THE SOURCE SAYS SO TWENTY LINES ABOVE THE CONSTANT. t1_shell.py: 'Measured bay centres, from six sub-pixel cut edges anchored by ratio to the two hubs ... +0.672 / +0.047 / -0.598 +/- 0.015.' Each pitch is a difference of two centres (sigma 21.2 mm); the asymmetry is a difference of two pitches (sigma 30.0 mm). 109.5 vs 129.5 is 20.0 +/- 30.0 = 0.67 sigma. Equal pillars at 119.5 mm are fully inside the measurement. This is the concept's stated 'single most important instruction' and the whole of its why_not_derivative argument.

IT REPEATS A DEFECT THIS REPOSITORY ALREADY RETIRED, IN THE SAME COMMENT BLOCK IT QUOTES FROM. t1_shell.py on the bay widths: 'Held equal: a 2 mm taper is below the measurement floor and inventing one is how 10.5's version got here.' SPEC 10.5's taper was sub-floor variation in bay WIDTH, refuted as perspective. The concept does the identical thing with bay SPACING and calls the result a human fingerprint.

THE HEIGHT ANCHOR IS QUOTED AT A STATION THAT IS NOT ON ANY APERTURE. rake_drop(x) = 0.047925 + 0.017750x is applied per-vertex at build.py step 8b (SPEC: 'applied at build.py:537 step 8b'), so the AG sill is 1.3121 / 1.3232 / 1.3347 at bays 0/1/2. STATE.md's '1.307-1.710 AG' is the value at X_DROP_REF = 0.96197, forward of bay 0's leading edge (0.930). The published band is 5-28 mm low, and it was transcribed from a prose line rather than computed at the bays.

THE RAKE RUNS THE WRONG WAY. Drop grows forward, so above-ground courses RISE toward the tail: STATE.md roof z 1.9399 at the front axle against 1.9833 at the rear, 'roof line slope (measured off the mesh) -18.1 mm/m'. The concept's 'every course is drawn on a 1.02 deg descent, front to back' is inverted.

A RAKED MOTIF CANNOT TILE HORIZONTALLY, AND THE CONCEPT SELLS BOTH PROPERTIES. Over one 1785.5 mm repeat the courses climb 31.7 mm, so a true horizontal repeat jogs 31.7 mm at every boundary. The 1:1 panel-printed wall survives as a mural; the 1:4 wrap, 1:12 textile, 1:6 placemat and especially the cement tile do not. The tile format as written ('one bay per tile, three tiles plus grout = one repeat') becomes three distinct tile artworks, not one SKU.

THE LOUVRE BAND IS NOT ADJACENT TO THE APERTURES AND ITS SLOT COUNT IS A CONTESTED BUILT DEFECT. LOUV_X0/X1 = _aft(-1.2850), _aft(-1.6700) sit well aft of bay 2's rear edge at -0.856 -- a discrete ~385 mm patch on the rear quarter, outside the 1785.5 mm repeat, not a course beneath it. And AUDIT_rev43.md line 158: 'The rear-quarter louvre block has twelve slots, not ten, and the built block is two slots short,' with the ceiling stating 'the louvre count is capped at a FLOOR of twelve.' The concept would print the model's own two-slot deficit at 1:1 and call it the vehicle's only regular repeat.

THE BODY-POSITION CLAIM, WHICH IS THE ENTIRE EMOTIONAL PAYLOAD, IS WRONG BY ABOUT 400 mm. A sill at 1.312-1.335 m AG is at the sternum of a ~1.75 m adult; standing wrist height is roughly half of stature, around 0.85-0.95 m. 'The sill at the wrist' is false. (The head-rail half survives: 1.715-1.738 m is above a ~1.63 m eye height.)

THE 1:1 INSTALLATION DATUM IS UNSPECIFIED, AND WITHOUT IT THE WHOLE THESIS EVAPORATES ON SITE. Non-woven murals are routinely hung top-aligned or centred. If an installer aligns to the ceiling on a 2.6 m wall rather than to the floor, the apertures land at an arbitrary height and the concept becomes an ordinary pattern. Nothing in the production notes states a floor datum, a hang tolerance, or what to do on a non-level floor.
improvements: RETIRE THE ASYMMETRY CLAIM OR RE-MEASURE IT PROPERLY -- and prefer re-measuring, because it is cheap and it would be a genuine finding. Do NOT derive the pillars by differencing four centres, which is what inflates sigma to 30 mm. Measure the two pillars DIRECTLY as edge-to-edge gaps between adjacent sub-pixel cut edges on one frame, where the homography error is largely common-mode and cancels. At ref_side.jpg's 220 px/m a 20 mm difference is 4.4 px, which sub-pixel edges can resolve; cross-check on ref_nolita_doorshut.jpg (107 px/m, cab door SHUT, admissible for geometry under rule 11). Publish the result as 'pillar A vs pillar B = X +/- sigma', paint the two windows first, and look at them. If sigma lands under ~7 mm the fingerprint is real and this concept jumps a tier on that one number alone. If it does not, draw three equal 119.5 mm pillars and delete the fingerprint paragraph -- the concept still works, it just has to argue from the apertures rather than from the gaps.

REDRAW EVERY HEIGHT AT THE BAYS, NOT AT X_DROP_REF, AND FLIP THE RAKE. Compute AG z per bay as z_authored - (0.047925 + 0.017750 * x). The sheet becomes: sill 1.3121 / 1.3232 / 1.3347, head 1.7151 / 1.7262 / 1.7377, courses RISING 17.75 mm/m toward the tail, 31.7 mm across the 1785.5 mm span. Then rewrite the poetic line, which gets better rather than worse: the wall does not descend, it lifts as it runs aft -- the tail of the bus sits high because the nose is raked down, and the courses climb away from you toward the counter's far end.

CUT THE LOUVRE BAND FROM v1 ENTIRELY. It is spatially outside the repeat (LOUV_X0/X1 are aft of the rear axle at -1.100, versus bay 2's rear edge at -0.856), and its count is a contested built defect with a measured FLOOR of twelve against the model's ten (AUDIT_rev43.md line 158). Printing it at 1:1 publishes a two-slot error as a measurement. If a lower course is wanted, use something that IS under the apertures and IS measured: the belt line as the red/cream break, drawn as a line rather than a scalar -- STATE.md gives it at three stations (1.2010 front axle, 1.2223 mid, 1.2436 rear axle), so it rakes parallel to the aperture band and needs no new figure.

RESOLVE THE RAKE-VERSUS-REPEAT CONTRADICTION EXPLICITLY, PER FORMAT, IN THE PRODUCTION NOTES. Two clean products, not one: (a) RAKED MURAL -- 1:1 only, panel-printed per wall, non-repeating, courses climbing 17.75 mm/m, the rake is the whole point; (b) LEVEL REPEAT -- rake set to zero, one flat course height, for the 1:4 wrap, 1:12 textile, 1:6 placemat and the tile. State that the rake is deliberately dropped in (b) and why, so it reads as a decision rather than a loss. This single split also rescues the tile: with zero rake, one bay per tile is genuinely one SKU.

REWRITE THE EMOTIONAL CLAIM TO THE HEIGHT THE VEHICLE ACTUALLY HAS, WHICH IS BETTER THAN THE ONE WRITTEN. At 1.312-1.335 m the sill is at an adult's sternum and above a child's head -- you REACH UP to be served, and a child is served over their own eyeline. That is a truer observation, it is the physical reason a serving hatch on a van feels different from a counter, and it lands directly on the audience F18 already names ('for children at the restaurant'). Drop 'the sill at the wrist' and keep 'the head rail above the eye', which is correct at a ~1.63 m eye height.

SPECIFY THE INSTALLATION DATUM AS PART OF THE ARTWORK, NOT AS a note. Print a trim line and a legend on the drop margin: 'ALIGN THIS LINE TO FINISHED FLOOR LEVEL. Sill lands 1312 mm AFF at the leading bay.' Give the fitter a hang tolerance (+/- 10 mm reads; +/- 50 mm does not), state that the pattern is bottom-aligned and any excess is trimmed at the CEILING, and specify behaviour on a non-level floor (follow the floor, not a spirit level -- the pattern is raked anyway). Without this the 1:1 thesis is at the mercy of whoever holds the paste brush.

WRITE THE DERIVE SCRIPT AND MAKE IT THE DELIVERABLE'S SOURCE OF TRUTH -- the concept already proposes this and it should be promoted from 'optional and cheap' to mandatory, because four of the six numbers on the current sheet are transcription errors of exactly the kind it prevents. It must IMPORT t1_shell.BAY_W, BAY_CX, Z_SILL, Z_HEAD, BAY_R and t1_core.rake_drop, apply rake_drop per bay, and print final millimetres per named scale plus the propagated sigma on every derived gap. Nothing in it needs bpy, so it runs in about a second. Have it refuse to print a pillar asymmetry whose value is under 1 sigma -- that one guard would have caught this concept's central claim.

STATE THE BOBBLE FRINGE'S PROVENANCE ON THE ARTWORK SHEET, NOT ONLY IN THE NOTES. t1_detail.py: 'Ball diameter and pitch are INFERRED (each ball is ~2 px)', and the same file records the scallop as 65 balls per aperture. On a 1:1 wall each ball is a real drawn object at a real size, so mark the scallop layer 'DRAWN, NOT MEASURED' in the file and in any caption. Then add the missing ask: PHOTOS_WANTED has carriers for this kind of request and has never had a fringe item -- one close square-on frame of an aperture edge would close it, and it is the only photograph this entire concept needs.

ADD THE ONE THING THAT WOULD MAKE THE CONCEPT UNARGUABLE AT ZERO COST: put the aperture band's three AG sill heights on the drawing as a visible measure line with its provenance, the way an architectural elevation carries dimensions. The concept's claim is that dimension IS the content; then show the dimension. It also makes the piece self-auditing -- anyone can check the wall against t1_shell.py -- which is the only defence a 1:1 print has against the class of error this concept currently contains.

verdicts.lens: Emotional resonance, brand fit and IP exposure — would a real person feel something and want to own this, does it read as Tacombi rather than generic van culture, and does it lean on VW marks where a Tacombi-specific route existed.
verdicts.reasoning:
The IP position is the best in anything I have seen from this program and it earns real praise: no roundel, no silhouette, no bus. Strip every word off it and there is nothing for Volkswagen to point at — which matters, because the program's stated purpose is commercial merchandise imagery of a trademarked vehicle. And the brand root is genuine and sourced, not invented: SPEC §0.1 grades as S the founder's own account that the $3,000 bus was "missing three of its windows." Making the product out of the absence is an idea only this company can have. It also needs no render, no alpha, no stitch chain and no delivery-render permission, which under three standing owner holds is a strategic asset, not a compromise.

But the concept does not work as pitched, on my axis, for four reasons.

First, its own IP argument is false for one of its four elements. It claims the trade-dress content is "entirely the conversion, none of which Volkswagen made." The louvre band is not the conversion — t1_detail.py calls it "the rear-quarter air-intake louvre block," a T1 factory pressing. It is the single VW-owned thing on the wall, and it is there by choice.

Second, that same course is the concept's only dimensional failure, and dimension is the ONLY carrier of feeling here. The brief's whole thesis is "the emotion is delivered by dimension instead of picture," so a frame error is an emotional-claim error in a way it would not be on a poster. The louvres are 429.2 mm aft of the last bay and 385 mm wide — a discrete block outside the repeat, not a course beneath it — and 0.895–1.085 is the authored frame, so the stated AG band is 65 mm high. In a concept whose chief boast is that every figure is machine-written, the one course invented for rhythm is transcribed wrong and placed wrong.

Third, brand fit. The brief confesses the problem and files it as a feature: "reads as mid-century modernist grid work until someone tells you what it is." A pattern that needs narration to be brand-specific has failed. It escapes VW-bus merch and lands squarely in a second, equally saturated category — Palm Springs, breeze-block, Eames-era grid — which the brief never acknowledges and which the screener's "the whole category can't be compared to it" misses entirely. It will be compared, constantly, just not to vans. Relatedly, the cement-tile format is sold as the most culturally correct object in the set and is closer to the opposite: Mexican encaustic pattern vocabulary is dense, polychrome and curvilinear — the vocabulary the flank folk art already uses — so a rectilinear grid on pasta tile is a Northern European pattern in a Mexican medium.

Fourth, the emotional mechanism is mismatched to its own primary format, and the wall is cold. The 1:1 body-position effect is a three-second doorway moment; the named primary use is dining rooms, where the wall is seen at distance, obliquely, for an hour — the one context where the conceit is least available. And the concept strips out every warm thing the brand actually owns (bulbs, brass, gold, hand-lettering, lit interior) and keeps only geometry, while the one warm element it retains, the bobble fringe, is the sole INFERRED number on the sheet ("each ball is ~2 px"). It is most confident about its coldest parts and least grounded on its only warm one. The 20 mm asymmetry does almost no emotional work either: the two pillars are never adjacent, separated by a 515 mm aperture, so nobody reads it as tenderness. It is provenance, and it should be argued as provenance.

Top of workable, not strong. The idea is sound and the corrections are cheap and specific.
fatal_flaws: THE CONCEPT'S OWN IP CLAIM IS FALSE FOR ONE ELEMENT. It asserts the trade-dress content is 'entirely the conversion, none of which Volkswagen made.' t1_detail.py names the louvres 'the rear-quarter air-intake louvre block' — a T1 factory pressing, i.e. the one VW-owned feature on the wall. On the lens's own IP question ('does it lean on VW marks where a Tacombi-specific route existed'), a Tacombi-specific route existed and was not taken.

THE LOUVRE COURSE IS DIMENSIONALLY WRONG THREE WAYS, IN THE PROPERTY THE CONCEPT BOASTS MOST. Location: LOUV_X0/X1 = _aft(-1.2850)/_aft(-1.6700) puts it 429.2 mm aft of the last bay's edge, 385 mm wide, entirely outside the 1785.5 mm repeat — it is a discrete rear-quarter block, not a continuous course under the apertures. Frame: 0.895–1.085 is the AUTHORED un-dropped band; AG is 0.830–1.020, so the stated AG figure is 65 mm high, and the concept mixes frames on one sheet (it used AG correctly for the apertures). Dimension: '10 slots ... across 0.1900 m' reuses the 0.190 vertical band height as a horizontal extent; the horizontal extent is 0.385 m.

IT CONFESSES ITS OWN BRAND-FIT FAILURE AND FILES IT AS A FEATURE: 'reads as mid-century modernist grid work until someone tells you what it is.' A brand pattern that requires narration to be brand-specific has not achieved brand fit. It escapes the VW-bus category and lands in an equally commodified one — mid-century grid, breeze-block, Palm Springs — that the brief never names and cannot claim immunity from.

THE 1:1 EMOTIONAL MECHANISM IS MISMATCHED TO ITS OWN NAMED PRIMARY FORMAT. 'Standing at the wall is standing at the counter' is a doorway/pass moment measured in seconds. The stated primary use is 'restaurant interiors, the Nolita/Playa dining rooms' — seen from a table, at distance, obliquely, for an hour, which is precisely where the body-position conceit is unavailable.

IT IS EMOTIONALLY COLD, AND CONFIDENT IN INVERSE PROPORTION TO GROUNDING. Every warm element the brand actually owns — bulb string, brass, gold folk art, hand-lettering, lit interior with people in it — is stripped out; three flat near-black voids at eye level remain. The single warm element retained, the bobble fringe, is the ONLY inferred number on the sheet (t1_detail.py: 'Ball diameter and pitch are INFERRED (each ball is ~2 px)').

THE 20 mm ASYMMETRY DOES NO EMOTIONAL WORK AND IS OVERSOLD AS 'the tenderness in it.' The two pillars are 109.5 and 129.5 mm and are never adjacent — separated by a 515.5 mm aperture — so viewers read them as even. Its real value is provenance and anti-counterfeit, which is a different and weaker argument than the one being made.

NO VERTICAL COMPOSITION IS SPECIFIED. On the stated 2.6–3.0 m wall the brief defines red below 1.207 m and a 403 mm aperture band at 1.307–1.710 m, leaving roughly half the wall as unresolved cream field above the head rail. A mural is a vertical composition; only the horizontal repeat has been designed.

THE LOUVRE COUNT IT PUBLISHES AS FACT IS CONTESTED AND DIRECTIONALLY UNSAFE. LOUV_N = 10, while AUDIT_rev43.md reads 'twelve slots, not ten' and t1_detail.py's own header says 'under-counting is possible, over-counting is not' — so 10 is a floor. The concept calls this 'the only regular repeat the real vehicle owns' while its aperture (0.0070) is flagged in source as 'INFERRED, not measured -- 1.5 px'.
improvements: CUT THE LOUVRE COURSE ENTIRELY. One deletion fixes four defects at once: it removes the only VW-owned feature on the wall (restoring the concept's 'entirely the conversion' claim to true), and it removes the location error, the 65 mm frame error and the contested/inferred count. Nothing else on the sheet is affected — the apertures, belt line, rake and fringe stand untouched.

REPLACE IT WITH THE DRIP RAIL AND BULB STRING AS THE TOP TERMINATING COURSE — this is the highest-value single change available. t1_detail.py places it 'OUTSIDE the skin, ~55 mm above the aperture heads', i.e. ~1.765 m AG, directly above the 1.710 head rail. It is horizontal, so it works as a course; it is 100 % conversion with zero VW content, so it strengthens the IP argument the louvres weakened; it is the vehicle's only self-luminous element, so it answers the coldness; and it caps the composition, so it answers the unresolved upper field. Specify it three ways by product: printed cream dots on a brass rule at 1:1 wallcovering; spot-gloss or foil at 1:4 packaging; a real low-voltage festoon channel in the hospitality build, where the pattern stops being wallpaper and becomes a lit architectural element.

MAKE THE COUNTER A PHYSICAL COURSE, NOT AN OPTIONAL 20 mm BRASS RULE. The body-position claim is not carried by the aperture height alone — it is carried by the thing your wrists rest on. In the 1:1 build, run an actual shelf or rail at the 1.307 m sill in COUNTERTAN sRGB(201,186,150). That converts the concept's best idea from a printed assertion into a physical fact, and it is the difference between a mural people photograph and a mural people lean on.

WARM THE APERTURE INK AND BE GENEROUS WITH THE SCALLOP — this is the fix for the mid-century collision. Three flat-black rounded rectangles on cream is Palm Springs. A warm near-black (or a two-value dark, deeper at the head, warmer at the sill) with a full, confident cream bobble scallop round every edge is Mexican. The scallop is the concept's only piece of hand-drawn language and it is currently a footnote; make it the second-loudest thing on the wall after the holes.

PUT THE MENU CARDS ON THE PILLARS. Three are built and measured (STATE.md `menucard | 3`; t1_detail.py '96 x 311 mm card'), one per pillar, and they solve three problems simultaneously: they introduce Tacombi's own type into a pattern that currently has no voice; they turn each pillar from a gap into a place; and by giving the eye a constant-width object on both pillars they make the 109.5/129.5 asymmetry actually perceptible for the first time. This is the cheapest route from 'geometrically interesting' to 'unmistakably this restaurant'.

RE-ARGUE THE 20 mm ASYMMETRY AS PROVENANCE, NOT AS FEELING. Drop 'the tenderness in it'. State it as what it is: an uncopyable dimensional fingerprint that authenticates the goods, defensible because it comes from a measured constant no competitor holds. Then, if you want it FELT, make it visible — the pillar menu cards above, or a deliberate 1:1 wall break that puts the two pillars adjacent at a corner return.

REASSIGN THE PRIMARY FORMAT TO WHERE THE 1:1 CLAIM IS TRUE. Move dining-room wallcovering to secondary and lead with the contexts that reproduce the queue: the order pass, the service window surround, a doorway or entry vestibule, the queue-rail wall, a takeaway hatch. The dimension only does emotional work where a body actually stands and waits, and the brief should name those rooms.

REDRAW THE CEMENT TILE OR DROP IT. Rectilinear grid on encaustic pasta tile is a Northern European pattern in a Mexican medium, not cultural correctness. If tile stays, let the aperture sit in a field drawn from the vehicle's OWN Mexican vocabulary — the flank's gold scroll, the rosette, the comma-with-dots — so the tile carries the folk art and the grid carries the architecture. That also gives the programme a tile that could not be mistaken for anyone else's.

STATE THE FRAME ON EVERY NUMBER ON THE SHEET — AG or authored, per line. The concept already mixed them once (apertures AG, louvres authored-but-labelled-AG). Since the entire emotional claim is that the heights are right against a real floor, a frame label is not pedantry here, it is the load-bearing part.

WRITE THE CONSTANTS SCRIPT THE CONCEPT ALREADY PROPOSES, AND MAKE IT PRINT THE FRAME. Import t1_shell.BAY_W, BAY_CX, Z_SILL, Z_HEAD, BAY_R and have it emit final millimetres per named scale WITH the AG conversion applied and labelled. The louvre error is exactly the class of defect that script exists to prevent, and it occurred because the table was transcribed instead of derived.

ADD ONE FORMAT THE BRIEF IS MISSING AND THE PATTERN IS PERFECT FOR: the takeaway bag and the shipper. At 1:4 the repeat is 446.4 mm — almost exactly a bag face — and a bag is held at arm's length by a person who has just been served, which is the only portable context that reproduces the concept's own emotional moment. It also puts the pattern in the customer's hand at zero incremental cost against the existing packaging line.

concept.title: Twelve Shadows
concept.one_line: The bus is never shown. Only its shadow — the deployed silhouette, lid up, counter out, tail board propped — cast by the real sun at Playa del Carmen, once an hour, across one serving day. A vehicle that tells the time by not moving.
concept.the_image: Single flat ink on bare paper. No object, no ground texture, no horizon — just a shape and a lot of nothing. THE SET, twelve panels, 11:00 to 22:00, one hour apart, from real computed sun positions at 20.6N 87.1W: at 11:00 the shadow is a compressed, dense, near-square mass with the counter's cantilever reading as one hard bar across it. At 14:00 it is short, heavy, pooled tight under the object, almost illegible — and that panel earns its place by being the one that gives nothing. By 17:00 it lengthens and the lid's shadow SEPARATES into a distinct wing riding above the body mass. By 19:00 it is a long raked lozenge running off the sheet edge, with the propped tail board a thin spear 515 mm past the tail (STATE.md: 'length excludes opened lids: 4.317 with them, 4.065 without'). The 21:00 panel has no sun shadow at all — and it is NOT blank: it is the festoon's own light, a scatter of small warm ovals pooled on the ground beneath the drip rail. The set ends with the bus lighting itself. THE ROSETTE, an alternative single sheet: all twelve overlaid from a common origin at low opacity in brand red. What comes out is a radiating burst — which IS the vehicle's own dominant ornament (the Calidad sunburst, the mural rosettes, the hubcap rings) arrived at by pure fact instead of by drawing a flower. The bus, by not moving, draws its own folk art. PALETTE: one ink, red on cream or black on natural; a second warm gold ink for 21:00 only. TYPE: one line, bottom left, hairline — the hour, the date, 20.6N 87.1W. Enormous white space. Nothing else.
concept.emotional_claim: Patience, and then permanence. This is the only idea in the program that makes the brand's central fact — it stopped — into something you can WATCH HAPPEN. A shadow is physical proof of stillness; twelve of them are proof of a day's work. It is also quietly ruthless toward a merchandise category built entirely on motion: our vehicle's only movement is the sun's. And by panel three the viewer recognises the shape without ever having been shown the object, which is the most flattering thing a picture can do to a person.
formats: TWELVE-PANEL SET, each 300 x 400 mm, one-colour screen print on uncoated 250 gsm, boxed — or issued one per month, which turns a print into a subscription and a subscription into a reason to come back.

SINGLE ROSETTE PRINT, 700 x 700 mm, two-colour on heavy uncoated. Solid flat ink at this size is the ONE case where the chain's undeclared 8-bit truncation cannot hurt you (studio.py sets `color_depth = '16'`; stitch.py and post.py both read through PIL and truncate silently) — a hard-edged mask has no gradient to band. Trap 0.2 mm; consider a double hit against pinholing on uncoated.

A PAINTED SUNDIAL ON THE TERRACE at a Playa site — hour marks laid where the actual bus's shadow actually falls. The graphic becomes a piece of ground the customer stands on, and the real object validates it every day at no cost. This is the version I would fight for.

12-SECOND SCREEN LOOP, one frame per hour, static camera, no cut, no camera move: the shadow sweeps and stretches while nothing else in frame ever changes. The most anti-advert motion piece imaginable — it is a clock.
ALL-OVER of the rosette for tissue, cup wrap, wrapping paper, endpapers, tote gusset. One tile, free across the whole range.
FAVICON / APP MARK: the 14:00 shadow alone, solid, at 32 px. It survives because it is a single closed silhouette with no interior detail.
concept.why_not_derivative: There is no shadow-only VW-bus artwork anywhere, because a shadow is only interesting if the object is stationary — and the entire category's emotional stock is motion and escape. Every trope in it (sunset, surf, road, blueprint, line art) requires the vehicle drawn. This refuses to draw it and is still unmistakable, because the DEPLOYED silhouette — lid wing, counter bar, tail spear — is unlike any vehicle shadow anyone has ever seen. It is also the perfect anti-photoreal move for this specific asset: not one of the model's four failing photograph-comparison gates can touch a shadow. No salmon red, no matte paint, no emblem, no tread count, no gloss deficit. The piece is immune to every open defect in the register by construction.
concept.production_notes: The sun positions must be REAL or the whole piece is a lie: compute altitude and azimuth for 20.6N 87.1W on a named date, hourly, and PRINT THE EPHEMERIS IN THE COLOPHON so anyone can recompute it. That is the piece's own guard. Set `T1_SHADOW` (ships 9.0, with `T1_SHADOW_FLOOR` 0.030) by looking at the crop, not by inheriting it — studio.py's own comment says the shipped value is a presentation device for a bus sitting on white and that `T1_SHADOW=1.0` restores the floating arm exactly, while C3 fires at 20. Record that choice in the ledger as a GRADE FOR A DERIVED ARTEFACT, not a change to the delivery rig; rule 34 exists because a ruling about the studio RIG was once wrongly applied to a second deliverable for twelve revisions, and F259 ('Relight the studio and fix the ground if necessary') opens the rig anyway with 'DO NOT change RED' as its only constraint.
model_work_required: THE ASSET IS ALREADY EMITTED BUT CURRENTLY UNREACHABLE. deliver.py writes `combi_%s_shadow_only.png` per view and the split is measured — shadow-catcher pixels near-black (max channel < 12/255) against a vehicle mean of 143, partitioning the footprint 37.8 / 62.2 %. It is blocked because every frame in out/ is colortype 2 with no alpha, `T1_ALPHA` appears in NO LEDGER since rev 62, and deliver.py correctly refuses: 'CONTROLS: 4 checked, 1 FAILED -- C1 ... PACKAGE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY'. One env var and one render unblocks it.

THERE IS NO SUN. studio.rig() takes a scalar `key` and builds a fixed cyclorama; no azimuth or elevation parameter exists anywhere in the tree. Build a small dedicated rig: one SUN lamp at a computed altitude/azimuth, one shadow-catcher plane (studio.py already carries `ob.is_shadow_catcher = bool(int(os.environ.get("T1_CATCH", "1")))`), alpha on, optics off.
DO NOT ROUTE IT THROUGH `T1_SCENE=playa`. F57 records that path renders NO VEHICLE — 'a dark cylinder on a grey plane', reported and never diagnosed. Build the minimal sun rig instead.

THE SHIPPED POSE IS ENOUGH AND THAT IS LUCKY. `t1_shell.py` computes `LID_W = (LID_X0 - LID_X1) / LID_ASPECT / math.sin(math.radians(LID_OPEN_DEG))` — the lid's WIDTH is coupled to its angle as 1/sin, so any variant that opens or closes the lid inflates the mural board past the length of the bus (and divides by zero at 0 deg). At the shipped `LID_OPEN_DEG = 76.0` it is correct, so this concept ships WITHOUT that fix — but freeze LID_W behind an ablation before anyone tries an animated lid.

THE 21:00 PANEL NEEDS REAL WORK AND IT IS THE BEST PANEL. F144 stands: 'THE FESTOON BULBS READ AS PEARLS, NOT LIGHTS.' The bulbs must actually cast onto the ground plane. They are one joined object (t1_detail: `join([ob, flex], "bulb_string")`, STATE.md `bulb_string | 1`, `tb_bulbs | 1`, `tb_bulbflex | 1`) with an emissive material and live switches T1_BULB_STR / T1_BULB_BASEV — so it is a lookdev job, not a modelling one.

Render each of the twelve at the SAME camera and the SAME ortho scale or the set is worthless. Use a top-down or fixed elevated camera on the ground plane; `topdown` exists (loc 2.60, 4.60, 6.40, lens 62) and has never been rendered by any preview list — look at one frame before committing.

verdicts.lens: ORIGINALITY — is this genuinely fresh, or a well-executed version of something already on a thousand products? Judged by naming the existing work it resembles.
verdicts.reasoning:
The category read is correct and sharp: VW-bus merch runs entirely on motion (sunset, surf, road, escape), and a brand whose founding fact is "the engine was scrapped, transmission sold" (SPEC.md §0.1, graded S) is genuinely mis-served by every trope in it. Refusing to draw the vehicle at all is a real strategic move, and the deployed silhouette — lid wing, counter bar, tail spear — is a shape no stock asset has.

But the ORIGINALITY axis judges the image, not the argument, and on the image this is a well-executed version of two mature devices with canonical owners.

The rosette — the screener's named best moment, and the concept's own proudest claim ("the bus draws its own folk art") — is Charles Ross's SUNLIGHT CONVERGENCE / SOLAR BURN (1971–72) with the sun's authorship removed. Ross put a wood panel under a Fresnel lens on his roof every day for a year, 366 panels; laid end to end the burns form an analemma, a double spiral. It won an AIGA award and became a University of Utah Press book in 1976. Ross's entire point is that the SUN makes the mark and the weather signs it ("passing clouds cause unburned interruptions... rainy or overcast days produce blank boards"). Our rosette is a computed overlay that we draw. It is the same radiating figure reached by the weaker of the two available routes, and the stronger route has been occupied for fifty-four years.

The twelve-panel hourly shadow overlay is not an invention either — it is a standard architectural deliverable. Hourly sun-path diagrams and cumulative shadow overlays are routine practice, and "sunlight shadow art print" is already a live Etsy market category. A design director will read this as "someone made a shadow study of a food truck." That is a competent recontextualisation, not a new idea.

Shadow-as-subject is separately the most-worked device in the adjacent art field: Kumi Yamashita (object concealed, shadow is the picture), Vincent Bal's SHADOWOLOGY (a daily serial shadow practice since 2016 — the same serial move), Tim Noble & Sue Webster, Shigeo Fukuda, Larry Kagan. The "twelve of one subject under changing light" form is Monet's Rouen Cathedral, Hokusai's Fuji, the Bechers, Ruscha. None is a VW bus, so no collision is literal — the concept's "there is no shadow-only VW-bus artwork anywhere" is true only because of the two words "VW bus."

Two repo findings damage it further, and one of them is decisive. First, the documentary premise is refuted by the project's own photometry: studio.playa()'s docstring, written against ref_rear34.jpg, reads "NO SUN. The brightest ground patches sit only +5 L* over their surround with 7.4 px edges... the bright/dark ground split measures db* +2.4: the SHADOWS ARE WARMER. A sun/skylight pair has the opposite sign by construction, so there is no sun/skylight pair," plus "NO SKY... the set is under a closed canopy with one lateral opening" and "limestone in deep open shade, not a lit apron." The bus at Playa stands under a palapa and casts no sun shadow — measured, not assumed. The production note then says "the sun positions must be REAL or the whole piece is a lie" and instructs printing the ephemeris "so anyone can recompute it." The piece advertises an audit it fails at the first question. And the ephemeris IS the differentiator from a generic long-shadow print; strip it and this is the Etsy category.

Second, the model earns almost nothing. A shadow needs a silhouette, which a designer can pen-tool off ref_side.jpg in an afternoon. The exception is the high-sun panels, where the cast shape is a true 3D projection no tracer can fake — and those are precisely the panels the concept describes as "compressed," "pooled tight," "almost illegible," the ones that "give nothing." The 75 revisions of measured geometry are required only where the picture is blank.

It clears "weak" because there is a real idea here and a specific, cheap path to a genuinely novel one (improvements A and B below, both already measured in this repository). It cannot clear "workable" as written, because its best moment is owned and its truth claim is refuted.
fatal_flaws: THE ROSETTE IS CHARLES ROSS'S 'SUNLIGHT CONVERGENCE / SOLAR BURN' (1971-72) WITH THE SUN'S AUTHORSHIP REMOVED. 366 panels, one per day, marks burnt by the sun itself through a Fresnel lens, forming an analemma / double spiral when laid end to end; AIGA award, University of Utah Press book 1976. The concept's proudest claim — a radiating burst 'arrived at by pure fact instead of by drawing a flower' — is exactly Ross's thesis, executed by him with the sun as the mark-maker rather than as a coordinate we look up.

THE DOCUMENTARY PREMISE IS REFUTED BY THE PROJECT'S OWN PHOTOMETRY, AND THE COLOPHON INVITES THE AUDIT THAT EXPOSES IT. studio.playa(), measured against ref_rear34.jpg: 'NO SUN... the bright/dark ground split measures db* +2.4: the SHADOWS ARE WARMER. A sun/skylight pair has the opposite sign by construction, so there is no sun/skylight pair'; 'NO SKY... under a closed canopy with one lateral opening'; 'limestone in deep open shade.' The bus does not stand in the sun at its own site. 'PRINT THE EPHEMERIS IN THE COLOPHON so anyone can recompute it' publishes a verifiable claim about the one fact that is fiction.

THE 'HOURLY SHADOW OVERLAY OF ONE OBJECT' IS A STANDARD ARCHITECTURAL DELIVERABLE, NOT AN INVENTION. Hourly sun-path diagrams and cumulative shadow overlays are routine shadow-study practice, and 'sunlight shadow art print' is an existing commercial market category. The visual language is simultaneously professionally standard and already in market.

LEGIBILITY AND ORIGINALITY RUN INVERSE ACROSS THE SET, AND THE CONCEPT SAYS SO ITSELF. The 14:00 panel is 'almost illegible' and 'earns its place by being the one that gives nothing' — the most original mark, communicating nothing. The 19:00 panel is 'a long raked lozenge,' which is a stretched bus silhouette: the single most generic mark in the entire category. Every small format inherits the generic end — and the proposed 32 px favicon is explicitly 'a single closed silhouette with no interior detail,' i.e. a silhouette icon. On a tote nobody can tell shadow from silhouette. The originality lives in the caption.

ONE OF THE THREE DIFFERENTIATING SHAPE-SIGNATURES IS ~2x OVERSTATED AND ITS CITATION DOES NOT SUPPORT IT. The concept calls the propped tail board 'a thin spear 515 mm past the tail' and cites STATE.md's 'length excludes opened lids: 4.317 with them, 4.065 without' — a 252 mm delta that contains no 515 mm. The 515 comes from 4.580 - 4.065, the whole non-bodywork overhang budget, whose 4.580 row is named 'overall length (ex counter)' and spans x 2.160 to the board's tip. The board's own aft projection is body rear x -2.157 against tip x -2.4131 (F243, post-retraction) = ~256 mm, ~6% of a 4.065 m body — about 19 mm at 300 mm print width, and less once a raking sun foreshortens it. CEILING: STATE.md's own line 28 is internally ambiguous about which parts the 252 mm covers, so re-measure off the mesh rather than trusting either reading.

THE 3D ASSET IS LOAD-BEARING ONLY WHERE THE PICTURE IS BLANK. A raking shadow is recoverable by pen-tooling ref_side.jpg; only the high-sun panels are genuine 3D projections a tracer cannot fake, and those are the panels the concept describes as compressed, pooled and illegible.

THE FORMAT THE CONCEPT SAYS IT 'WOULD FIGHT FOR' IS THE LEAST ORIGINAL ITEM IN THE SET. Painted analemmatic / human sundials on plazas and schoolyards are a standing public-art product category with commercial suppliers. Laying hour marks where a shadow falls is what a sundial IS.

SHADOW-AS-SUBJECT IS THE MOST-WORKED DEVICE IN THE ADJACENT FIELD AND THE CONCEPT NAMES NO ANCESTOR. Kumi Yamashita (object concealed, shadow is the picture), Vincent Bal's SHADOWOLOGY (a daily serial shadow practice since 2016), Tim Noble & Sue Webster, Shigeo Fukuda, Larry Kagan; and for serial-light-study, Monet's Rouen Cathedral, Hokusai, the Bechers, Ruscha. 'There is no shadow-only VW-bus artwork anywhere' is true only because of the words 'VW bus.'
improvements: A. KILL THE SUN AND USE THE ONE LIGHT THE RECORD PROVES IS REAL — THIS IS THE SINGLE HIGHEST-VALUE CHANGE. studio.playa() already characterises the actual illumination at the site: 'one large, low, LATERAL source -- a palapa opening -- and an absorbing ceiling,' shadows measurably WARMER than the lit ground (db* +2.4), edges 7.4 px soft, zero aerial perspective, no sky. A shadow series lit by THAT is unprecedented and unfakeable, because the shadows go sideways, they are soft, and they are warmer than the light — an inversion that cannot occur under a sun/sky pair 'by construction,' which is why no shadow print in existence has it. Print db* +2.4 and the 7.4 px edge figure in the colophon instead of an ephemeris. This converts the colophon from a liability into the strongest text on the sheet and removes Ross's shadow entirely, because the light is no longer the sky's.

B. MAKE THE 21:00 PANEL THE WHOLE PIECE, NOT THE ENDING — THIS IS WHAT RAISES IT A TIER.
