The festoon-lit ground scatter is the only image in the set with no precedent I can name, and it is the only one whose shadows are MULTIPLE and RADIAL: dozens of small sources on a string throw overlapping soft penumbrae, a mark no sun can make. Run the twelve panels across ONE bulb-string hour — the string lit bulb by bulb, or swinging — instead of twelve hours of sun. This also repairs the rosette's authorship problem at a stroke: the radiating figure now comes from the vehicle's OWN lamps, so the brand's ornament is made by the brand's own object rather than looked up from an almanac. That is the claim the concept wanted and did not earn. COST, STATED: F144 stands — 'THE FESTOON BULBS READ AS PEARLS, NOT LIGHTS' — so this promotes the concept's optional lookdev job to load-bearing. It is tractable: bulb_string is one joined object (t1_detail join([ob, flex], 'bulb_string'); STATE.md bulb_string | 1, tb_bulbs | 1, tb_bulbflex | 1) with live switches T1_BULB_STR / T1_BULB_BASEV.

C. REPLACE THE EPHEMERIS COLOPHON WITH ONE THE PIECE CAN PASS. Print what the repo actually owns and its uncertainties: the lateral-source geometry, db* +2.4, 'no sky,' the site, and the deployed pose WITH its ceilings — TB_WIDTH 0.5500 'POSE CHOICE, NOT MEASURED. Inside the 0.59 bound'; the hatch 'swung +64.00 deg... declared 64.0, NOT MEASURED -- a POSE'. A colophon that prints its own error bars is far rarer on merchandise than one that prints coordinates, and it is the only version of this piece that survives a reader with the repository open.

D. RE-MEASURE THE THREE SHAPE-SIGNATURES OFF THE MESH BEFORE DESIGNING TO THEM, THEN CHOOSE THE HOUR BY WHICH OVERHANG SEPARATES rather than by the clock. The board's aft projection is ~256 mm, not 515 mm — ~19 mm at 300 mm print width, and the concept's own line discipline ('a 0.15 mm floor', 'let no feature narrower than 0.159 m touch the cut line') will erase it if the sun rakes ACROSS the board rather than along it. Pick the sun azimuth that throws the lid wing, the counter bar and the tail spear as three separated masses; that separation, not the hour, is the entire anti-derivative content.

E. BREAK THE EQUAL-PANEL GRID, BECAUSE THE GRID IS WHAT MAKES IT READ AS AN ARCHITECTURAL SHADOW STUDY. Two cheap options: (i) print all twelve at TRUE relative area on one sheet — the 14:00 shadow is genuinely tiny and the 19:00 one runs off the edge, so equal panels already misrepresent the thing the piece is about; or (ii) one sheet, one hour, twelve editions, and the customer who comes at 14:00 gets the 14:00 print. Option (ii) turns a print series into a record of a visit, which is much closer to what 'something families keep' is actually asking for, and no VW-bus product does it.

F. RUN THE 'READS AS SILHOUETTE' TEST BEFORE ANY SMALL FORMAT IS DESIGNED. Print one high-sun and one raking panel at 76 mm and show them beside a plain flat bus silhouette. If a viewer cannot say which is the shadow, then the tote, cup wrap, all-over and 32 px favicon are carrying the generic end of the idea and should be cut or re-derived from the 21:00 scatter instead. This is an afternoon and nobody has done it; the concept currently proposes the favicon as its most compressed expression while describing it in terms that define a silhouette icon.

G. REFRAME THE TERRACE PIECE OR DROP IT FROM THE PITCH. Leading with 'the version I would fight for' on a painted sundial invites the one comparison the concept least wants. If it stays: say plainly that the sundial form is borrowed, and make the borrowed thing the deployed shape — hour marks in the outline of a bus with its lid up and its counter out is a figure no sundial has ever used, and that sentence is the only defensible originality claim the format has.

H. NAME THE ANCESTORS IN THE BRIEF — Ross, Yamashita, Bal, and the architectural shadow study — and state in one line what this does differently. A concept that names its lineage and departs from it deliberately reads as authored; 'there is no shadow-only VW-bus artwork anywhere' reads as under-researched and will be the first thing a design director tests.

verdicts.lens: Producibility and fidelity — can "Twelve Shadows" actually be made from THIS asset, given four failing photograph gates, an emblem rejected nine times, an unproven large-format chain, and a delivery render under a standing owner hold?
verdicts.reasoning:
The central producibility claim is TRUE and it is the strongest one in the program. A one-bit shadow mask consumes no material, no texture and no paint, so every failing gate is genuinely out of reach of it: flank_compare's red (render G/R 0.422 against the photograph's 0.114), gloss_compare (0.412 against a 0.60 bar), probe_rev70_tyre (0.2556 against 0.1953), probe_rev69_fitpose (0.8528 against P1b's 0.9465). All four read colour or tone. None can touch a silhouette. And the geometry it needs is built and clean — STATE.md reads `non-manifold edges (body) | 0`, `cutters rolled back | none`, 229 mesh objects — and already posed deployed, with the counter and tail board projecting exactly as the piece wants.

The infrastructure is also closer than the record advertises. `cyclorama()` is a flat 90 m ground plane at z=0 with `ob.is_shadow_catcher = bool(int(os.environ.get("T1_CATCH", "1")))`; `aim()` already does `d.type = 'ORTHO'`; and `ob.visible_camera = False` is an established in-tree idiom (studio.py's `_plate` uses it for the palapa). Every primitive the piece needs exists.

But the concept's own account of its dependencies is wrong in four places, and one of them may make the piece impossible as written.

FIRST, IT FABRICATES A FIGURE AND ATTRIBUTES IT TO A LINE THAT SAYS OTHERWISE. It writes "the propped tail board a thin spear 515 mm past the tail (STATE.md: 'length excludes opened lids: 4.317 with them, 4.065 without')". That line's own difference is 252 mm, and STATE.md attributes the projection to NINE parts jointly: counter, counter_nosing, counter_top, tail_board, tail_board_stay, tb_bulbflex, tb_bulbs, tb_edge_dark, tb_edge_red. The 515 comes from 4.580 − 4.065, a different row entirely. Neither number is the tail board's own projection and the citation does not support the claim. In a piece whose entire pitch is "the sun positions must be REAL or the whole piece is a lie", the first provenance claim in the document is wrong.

SECOND, THE CAMERA GEOMETRY IS UNSOLVED. At 20.6°N solar-noon altitude runs roughly 46° in December to near-zenith in June. At high sun the shadow lies under the vehicle, and from the concept's own prescribed top-down camera the bus occludes its own shadow. The fix is one line and is already an idiom in this tree — set the vehicle camera-invisible and keep it casting — but the concept never names it, so as written a majority of the panels render as pictures of a bus roof.

THIRD, "THE ASSET IS ALREADY EMITTED" IS FALSE FOR THIS PIECE. deliver.py's `combi_%s_shadow_only.png` is the STUDIO shadow from a multi-source area rig, which studio.py's own matte tap measures as "a large soft pool under and to the left of the vehicle reaching alpha 0.4980" and, on the side ortho, "mean alpha 0.0038 in the 4-30 px band directly below the silhouette". That is a formless smudge. Reused, it gives twelve identical blobs. "One env var and one render unblocks it" is not true; a new rig is needed either way.

FOURTH, THE BEST PANEL IS ON A DIFFERENT RIG FROM THE OTHER ELEVEN, WHICH THE CONCEPT'S OWN CONSISTENCY RULE FORBIDS. A shadow catcher writes occlusion into alpha; it does not render illumination. Warm pools on the ground need a lit ground (T1_CATCH=0), which studio.py records as returning defect D3 — "the sweep falls off to a 166 grey with a hard horizon line across the frame". And the emitter is unmeasured: `M["bulb"] = emissive("bulb", (1.000, 0.760, 0.442), strength=_bs)` at T1_BULB_STR 9.0 on ~11 mm envelopes, with F144 ("THE FESTOON BULBS READ AS PEARLS, NOT LIGHTS") standing. Nothing establishes those bulbs throw a readable pool ~1.9 m down, and small bright emitters at range in a renderer that sets no seed are the classic fireflies case.

One correction in the concept's favour: its LID_W catch is right and understated. `LID_W = (LID_X0 - LID_X1) / LID_ASPECT / math.sin(math.radians(LID_OPEN_DEG))` is followed by `assert LID_W <= _LID_W_MAX + 1e-9` with a named message, so a variant lid fails loudly at import rather than shipping an inflated board. And its "topdown exists" citation is a mis-read — that view is `lens=62, fstop=11.0` at (2.60, 4.60, 6.40), a three-quarter elevated perspective camera with depth of field, not an overhead ortho.

Net: the idea is unusually light on this asset and the immunity argument survives scrutiny, which puts it at the top of its band. But four of its stated dependencies are wrong, one wrong figure is cited to a line that contradicts it, and the geometry that decides whether the piece is possible at all has not been tested. That is workable, not strong — and two of the improvements below move it.
fatal_flaws: FABRICATED FIGURE, CITED TO A CONTRADICTING LINE. The concept states 'the propped tail board a thin spear 515 mm past the tail' and cites STATE.md's 'length excludes opened lids: 4.317 with them, 4.065 without'. That line's difference is 252 mm and it names NINE projecting parts jointly (counter, counter_nosing, counter_top, tail_board, tail_board_stay, tb_bulbflex, tb_bulbs, tb_edge_dark, tb_edge_red). The 515 is 4.580 - 4.065 from a different row. Neither is the tail board alone. Rule 5 and rule 18, in the concept whose own guard is provenance.

THE SHADOW IS OCCLUDED BY THE OBJECT AND THE CONCEPT DOES NOT SAY SO. At 20.6N the sun runs from ~46 deg (Dec) to near-zenith (Jun) at solar noon; at high sun the shadow lies under the vehicle and the prescribed top-down camera sees the roof, not the shadow. The fix exists in-tree (`ob.visible_camera = False`, used by studio.py's `_plate` for the palapa) but is never named, so the piece as specified does not render its own subject on a majority of panels.

'THE ASSET IS ALREADY EMITTED BUT UNREACHABLE' IS FALSE. deliver.py's `combi_%s_shadow_only.png` carries the STUDIO area-rig shadow, which studio.py's matte tap measures as 'a large soft pool under and to the left of the vehicle reaching alpha 0.4980' and, on a side ortho, 'mean alpha 0.0038 in the 4-30 px band directly below the silhouette'. It is a formless smudge, not a directional silhouette. The claim that one env var and one render unblocks the piece is wrong; a new rig is required regardless of T1_ALPHA.

THE 21:00 PANEL RUNS ON A DIFFERENT RIG FROM THE OTHER ELEVEN, VIOLATING THE CONCEPT'S OWN 'SAME CAMERA, SAME ORTHO SCALE OR THE SET IS WORTHLESS'. A shadow catcher writes occlusion into alpha and renders no illumination, so light pools need T1_CATCH=0 - which studio.py records as reinstating defect D3, 'the sweep falls off to a 166 grey with a hard horizon line across the frame'. The emitter is also unmeasured: T1_BULB_STR ships 9.0 on ~11 mm envelopes with F144 standing, and nothing establishes a readable pool ~1.9 m below.

THE CORE CREATIVE BET IS UNTESTED AND IS A ONE-FRAME QUESTION. Everything rests on 'the deployed silhouette - lid wing, counter bar, tail spear - is unmistakable'. No frame in this repository has ever shown it. CLAUDE.md's rule 1 exists for exactly this, and the concept proposes twelve renders, a print spec, a terrace installation and a favicon on top of an assumption that costs one crop to check.

IT CLAIMS DOCUMENTARY AUTHORITY THE RECORD CONTRADICTS. The piece's guard is 'PRINT THE EPHEMERIS IN THE COLOPHON'. But studio.py's own measured finding on the Playa reference reads 'NO SUN. The brightest ground patches sit only +5 L* over their surround ... the bright/dark ground split measures db* +2.4: the SHADOWS ARE WARMER. A sun/skylight pair has the opposite sign by construction, so there is no sun/skylight pair.' The one frame of the real vehicle at Playa is open shade. A hypothetical sundial is fine; one that advertises computed fact while depicting a lighting condition measured absent from its own location is not.
improvements: RUN THE ONE-FRAME KILL BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE, AND MAKE IT THE FIRST LINE OF THE PRODUCTION NOTES. One render: sun lamp at 30 deg altitude, every vehicle mesh set `ob.visible_camera = False`, T1_CATCH=1, overhead ortho, T1_ALPHA=1, T1_FX=0. Read the alpha, threshold it, CROP IT AND LOOK AT IT. The entire concept is the claim that the deployed silhouette reads as this bus and nothing else; that is a rule-1 question and it costs ~5 minutes of one core. If the wing, the bar and the spear do not read, no other note in the document matters.

NAME THE OCCLUSION FIX EXPLICITLY - IT IS THE MISSING LINE THAT TURNS THIS FROM UNSOLVED TO BUILDABLE. Set `ob.visible_camera = False` on every vehicle mesh while leaving shadow visibility on, exactly as studio.py's `_plate()` already does for `palapa_roof` and `canopy`. Then the render alpha IS the shadow, with no object in frame, at ANY sun altitude and from ANY camera - which also removes the need to threshold a subject silhouette back out of the mask, and makes the near-vertical-sun panels legible instead of impossible.

FIX OR DELETE THE 515 mm, AND STATE WHAT IT IS THE PROJECTION OF. Either quote 252 mm and name all nine parts STATE.md attributes it to, or measure the tail board alone off the mesh and say which ruler. Better still, delete the on-vehicle figure entirely: the piece's actual content is the SHADOW's projection, which is a different length at every hour, so quoting a body dimension here is measuring the wrong object anyway (rule 34's shape).

RENDER A 24-FRAME HALF-HOURLY SWEEP FIRST AND CHOOSE TWELVE FROM THE CONTACT SHEET - DO NOT COMMIT TO 'ONE PER HOUR' IN ADVANCE. At 20.6N a run of the midday panels will collapse into near-identical rectangles because the shadow is roughly the vehicle's plan; the concept already suspects this (it pre-defends 14:00 as 'the one that gives nothing') but does not know how many panels are lost. Pick the twelve that are DIFFERENT, then let the hour labels be irregular and say so in the colophon. An honest irregular set is a better object than twelve slots half of which repeat.

DEMOTE THE 21:00 PANEL TO A SEPARATE COMPANION SHEET IN THE SECOND INK - PANEL ZERO, OR THE REVERSE OF THE SET. It needs T1_CATCH=0 (a lit ground, with studio.py's D3 falloff), a different camera exposure, and an unmeasured emitter behind F144. As panel 12 it breaks the set's own consistency rule and puts the whole piece's release on a lookdev job. As a companion it can fail, or ship late, without taking the eleven with it - and it reads better as a coda than as a twelfth of a series.

SHIP THE ARTEFACT AS VECTOR PATHS, NOT AS RENDERED PIXELS, AND SAY SO. The masks are hard-edged and closed by construction; trace each once and hold the piece as paths. That removes `hq_render.py`, `stitch.py`'s seam exit code (F49), post.py's alpha destruction, the undeclared 8-bit truncation and F192's open delivery dimension from the critical path in one move - and it makes the 700 mm rosette, the terrace sundial and the 32 px favicon literally the same asset at three scales. This is the single change that most improves the producibility case, and the concept half-argues it without committing.

REPLACE THE 'ALREADY EMITTED' FRAMING WITH THE TRUE AND STRONGER ONE. Say: the geometry is built, clean and already in the deployed pose - `non-manifold edges (body) | 0`, `cutters rolled back | none`, lid at LID_OPEN_DEG 76.0, counter and tail board projecting per STATE.md's own 'what projects' list - and NOTHING ELSE IS NEEDED. No material, no texture, no paint, no emblem. That claim is both correct and a better argument than the false reuse claim it replaces.

PUT THE 'NO SUN' MEASUREMENT IN THE COLOPHON AND LET THE PIECE BE AN AVOWED HYPOTHETICAL. Quote studio.py verbatim - 'there is no sun/skylight pair' - beside the ephemeris. The piece becomes 'here is where this bus's shadow WOULD fall, computed, at a place we only ever photographed in shade', which is more interesting than a false documentary claim and is unfalsifiable in the honest direction. It also pre-empts the one audit finding that would otherwise embarrass the set.

ADD ONE GUARD IN THE SAME EDIT AND WATCH IT FAIL (rule 13 + rule 3). A probe that reads a mask and refuses if the shadow is not a single connected component above a stated area - watched failing on a high-sun panel where the tail board's spear detaches from the main mass. Without it nobody notices the day the spear separates, and a detached fragment is exactly the defect that survives every visual check at contact-sheet scale and ruins the 700 mm print.

CORRECT THE TWO SOURCE MIS-CITATIONS SO THE NEXT CONTEXT DOES NOT INHERIT THEM. `topdown` is `lens=62, fstop=11.0` at (2.60, 4.60, 6.40) - a three-quarter elevated PERSPECTIVE camera with depth of field, not an overhead ortho, so 'look at one frame before committing' will teach you nothing about this piece; a new ortho view is needed and `aim()` already supports it via `d.type = 'ORTHO'`. And state the LID_W guard accurately in the concept's favour: the `assert LID_W <= _LID_W_MAX + 1e-9` means a variant lid fails LOUDLY at import with a named message, so the animated-lid risk is a hard stop, not a silent inflation.

verdicts.lens: EMOTIONAL RESONANCE, BRAND FIT AND IP EXPOSURE
verdicts.reasoning:
THE IP POSITION IS THE BEST IN THE PROGRAM AND THE CONCEPT'S OWN REASONING FOR IT IS BACKWARDS. It ships no roundel, no chrome badge, no VW wordmark — good. But the market lane's finding is that VW claims the vehicle SHAPE ("The images of classic Beetle and Bus vehicles are themselves protected as trademarks"), and a silhouette is trade dress in its most naked form, stripped of exactly the painted conversion that would let you argue "this is our modified vehicle, not your product." The concept is safe only where the DEPLOYED shape is legible — lid wing, counter bar, tail spear. It is then most exposed precisely where it plans to ship most widely: the proposed 32 px favicon is "the 14:00 shadow alone", which the concept itself describes as "short, heavy, pooled tight under the object, almost illegible" — i.e. the app mark is the one panel of twelve with the least conversion detail and the most VW-shaped blob. The IP argument and the legibility argument point at the same fix and neither has been made.

THE CENTRAL EMOTIONAL CLAIM IS CONTRADICTED BY THE PROJECT'S OWN MEASUREMENT OF PLAYA. The piece's production note sets its own bar: "The sun positions must be REAL or the whole piece is a lie." But `studio.playa()`'s docstring, rebuilt against measurement at rev 10, says of the only Playa frames we hold: "**NO SUN.** The brightest ground patches sit only +5 L* over their surround with 7.4 px edges … the bright/dark ground split measures db* +2.4: the SHADOWS ARE WARMER. A sun/skylight pair has the opposite sign by construction, so there is no sun/skylight pair", and "the set is under a closed canopy with one lateral opening" — a palapa. So an artefact whose whole emotional stock is "physical proof of stillness, documentary fact" is founded on hard direct sun that the record measures as ABSENT at the site. The ephemeris in the colophon would be true and the picture would still be a fiction. By its own stated standard it fails.

THE DATE IS THE PIECE'S MOST CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION AND NOBODY HAS MADE IT. "A named date" is left blank, and at 20.6°N the date decides whether the set exists. Local sunset there runs roughly 18:15 in winter to about 19:20 in summer, so on the brand's own S-graded founding date — SPEC.md: "Opened 6 February 2006" — the 19:00 and 20:00 panels have no sun at all, and four of twelve panels are empty. Pick a summer date and you get the panels but lose the only date the brand owns; near the zenith crossings you also get a degenerate noon shadow and an azimuth flip. Related: the ROSETTE, which the screener rightly calls the best moment, is very probably a FAN, not a burst. Shadow azimuth sweeps roughly 120–180° across a serving day at that latitude, not 360°, so the overlay is one-sided — and the ornament it claims to rhyme with (the Calidad sunburst, "many narrow sharp points of uneven length", cal_gen.py) is fully radial. "The bus draws its own folk art" is the concept's best sentence and it rests on an unrun computation.

BRAND FIT IS THE WEAKEST AXIS AND THE CONCEPT MISTAKES SUBTRACTION FOR DIFFERENTIATION. It boasts of being "immune to every open defect in the register" — no red, no gloss, no emblem, no tread. That immunity is bought by discarding every asset that makes this bus Tacombi's rather than Volkswagen's: the gold folk art, the silver-leaf script, the flower mural, the Calidad burst, the bobble fringe, the brass counter band, the Spanish signwriting, the food, the people. What is left is a shape and a coordinate line — and "20.6N 87.1W" as a graphic device is itself a saturated leisure/outfitter trope, a derivative element hiding inside an anti-derivative concept. A promotional artefact for a FOOD brand with no food, no colour, no warmth and no name in it. It also requires prior knowledge to work: "by panel three the viewer recognises the shape without ever having been shown the object" is only true of someone who already holds the object in memory. It flatters people who already know and says nothing to anyone else — the inverse of what promotional material is for. It is closer to a design-annual gesture (shadow-only series are a well-worn art-direction move, however unworked in van culture) than to the deadpan catalogue register the shop actually speaks in ("purpose-built, all-weather knit beanie").

THE 21:00 PANEL IS THE BEST IDEA HERE AND ITS STATED ROUTE IS REFUTED — BUT IT SURVIVES ON BETTER GROUNDS THAN THE CONCEPT GIVES. The concept calls it "a lookdev job, not a modelling one" via T1_BULB_STR / T1_BULB_BASEV. F144 (MEASURED-rev61) kills both by ablation, before anything was tuned: "T1_BULB_STR=60 — 6.7× the shipped emission — moves the ratio 1.40 → 0.88, i.e. WORSE, because the bead is already near the top of the range and more emission drives it toward CLIPPING"; "T1_BULB_BASEV=0.30 … moves it 1.38 → 1.50 — nothing"; "the model-side lever is exhausted." What neither the concept nor the screener spotted is that F144's actual diagnosis rescues the panel: "A saturated amber bead requires the SURROUND to be dimmer relative to the bulb, which is F62's ceiling and the owner's standing studio ruling." The 21:00 panel is NIGHT. The surround is dark by construction. This is the one frame in the whole project where F144's blocker dissolves — but it dissolves for a reason the concept does not know, and if it is built on the two refuted switches it will fail.

THE TERRACE SUNDIAL IS THE ONLY COMPLETE VERSION OF THIS IDEA AND IT IS BURIED FOURTH. It repairs every flaw above at once: the real bus stands there supplying the context the prints require the viewer to already have; the shadow falls where it actually falls, canopy or no, so the authenticity problem evaporates and no ephemeris has to be defended; and IP exposure goes to zero because it is documentation of the company's own property on the company's own ground. It is also the one format nobody can copy. The concept says "This is the version I would fight for" and then ranks it third of six.
fatal_flaws: THE PIECE'S DOCUMENTARY PREMISE IS REFUTED BY THE PROJECT'S OWN MEASUREMENT. It claims shadows 'cast by the real sun at Playa del Carmen' and sets its own bar as 'The sun positions must be REAL or the whole piece is a lie.' studio.playa(), rebuilt against measurement at rev 10, reads: 'NO SUN. The brightest ground patches sit only +5 L* over their surround with 7.4 px edges … the SHADOWS ARE WARMER. A sun/skylight pair has the opposite sign by construction, so there is no sun/skylight pair' and 'the set is under a closed canopy with one lateral opening' — a palapa. A true ephemeris over a light that was never on the vehicle is still a fiction, and this is the ONE concept whose entire emotional value is that it is factual.

THE DATE IS UNNAMED AND IT DECIDES WHETHER THE SET EXISTS. At 20.6°N local sunset runs roughly 18:15 (winter) to about 19:20 (summer), so on the brand's own S-graded founding date — SPEC.md 'Opened 6 February 2006' — the 19:00, 20:00 and 21:00-sun panels do not exist and four of twelve are blank. A summer date gets the panels and abandons the only date the brand owns. Nobody has computed a single sun position.

THE ROSETTE — the concept's and the screener's best moment — IS ALMOST CERTAINLY A FAN, NOT A BURST. Shadow azimuth sweeps on the order of 120–180° across a serving day at that latitude, one-sided, while the ornament it claims to rhyme with is fully radial (cal_gen.py: 'a SPIKY sunburst -- many narrow sharp points of uneven length'). 'The bus draws its own folk art' is the whole poetic payload and it rests on an unrun computation.

IT ACHIEVES ANTI-DERIVATIVE STATUS BY DELETING THE BRAND. Every Tacombi-specific asset — gold folk art, silver-leaf script, flower mural, Calidad burst, bobble fringe, brass counter band, Spanish signwriting, food, people — is discarded, and the 'immune to every open defect' boast is a description of that deletion. What remains is a VW-shaped silhouette plus a coordinates line, and coordinates-as-graphic is itself a saturated leisure/outfitter trope. A food brand's promotional artefact with no food, no colour, no warmth and no name.

IT REQUIRES PRIOR KNOWLEDGE TO WORK AT ALL. 'By panel three the viewer recognises the shape without ever having been shown the object' is only true of someone who already knows the object. It flatters existing fans and recruits nobody — the inverse of promotional material — and the print formats (boxed set, subscription) are the deployments where that failure is most expensive.

THE 21:00 PANEL'S STATED ROUTE IS REFUTED BY ABLATION. F144, MEASURED-rev61: 'T1_BULB_STR=60 — 6.7× the shipped emission — moves the ratio 1.40 → 0.88, i.e. WORSE … T1_BULB_BASEV=0.30 … 1.38 → 1.50 — nothing … the model-side lever is exhausted.' The concept names exactly those two switches and calls it 'a lookdev job, not a modelling one.'

THE PROPOSED APP MARK IS THE MOST TRADEMARK-EXPOSED AND LEAST LEGIBLE OF THE TWELVE. 'FAVICON / APP MARK: the 14:00 shadow alone, solid, at 32 px' — the same panel the concept describes as 'short, heavy, pooled tight under the object, almost illegible.' A pooled midday shadow loses the lid wing, the counter bar and the tail spear, which are the only features distinguishing it from a stock VW bus outline that VW claims as trade dress.

A DELIBERATE DUD IN A PAID SET. '14:00 … almost illegible — and that panel earns its place by being the one that gives nothing.' That is a gallery argument, not a merchandise one; in a boxed twelve or a twelve-month subscription it is the month the customer feels cheated.
improvements: LEAD WITH THE SUNDIAL. Reorder the whole concept so the painted terrace sundial at a Playa site is the primary artefact and the prints are its documentation. It fixes the authenticity flaw (you paint where the shadow ACTUALLY falls, palapa or no — no ephemeris to defend), the prior-knowledge flaw (the real bus stands there supplying context), and the IP flaw (documentation of the company's own vehicle on the company's own ground, zero marks reproduced) in one move. Bring hour marks in the brand's gold, hand-painted by the same signwriting hand as the flank, and the piece stops being cold.

MEASURE THE SITE BEFORE COMPUTING THE SKY. The record says the reference set is under a palapa with one lateral opening and no direct sun. Ask the owner ONE multiple-choice question with a crop attached: does the Playa bus stand in open sun at any hour, in a palapa, or has it moved? If it is canopied, the honest piece is not twelve sun shadows — it is the palapa's own lateral light, which the record has already characterised, and the set becomes ONE opening's light crossing a stationary object. That is a stranger and more truthful picture than a generic sundial and it is unique to this site.

NAME THE DATE AND MAKE IT 6 FEBRUARY, THEN LET THE ASTRONOMY DICTATE THE PANEL COUNT. Compute the actual sunrise/sunset for 20.6N 87.1W on 6 February and ship however many hours have sun — probably seven or eight, not twelve. A set of EIGHT panels titled '6 February, Playa del Carmen' carries the brand's own founding fact (SPEC.md, graded S) and gains a real ending: the last sunlit hour, then the bulbs. Print the computed ephemeris in the colophon as promised, and print the sunset time as the reason the set ends where it does.

REPLACE THE ROSETTE WITH THE ANALEMMA, OR CALL THE FAN A FAN. Overlay ONE hour — say 13:00 — across twelve months instead of twelve hours across one day. That yields the true solar figure-eight: a genuinely strange closed curve that only a stationary object can draw, and the emotional claim upgrades from 'a day's work' to 'a year of standing still,' which is exactly the brand's founding fact (engine scrapped, transmission sold). If you keep the one-day overlay, compute it first and title it honestly as a fan; do not promise a burst you have not seen.

CHANGE THE APP MARK TO THE LONGEST SHADOW, NOT THE SHORTEST. Use the last sunlit hour — the raked lozenge where the lid wing separates and the tail board reads as a spear 515 mm past the tail (STATE.md: 'length excludes opened lids: 4.317 with them, 4.065 without'). It is more legible at 32 px because it has interior structure, and it is far better trademark ground because the conversion is what carries the shape. Test it: render the candidate silhouette, paste it beside a stock VW T1 side silhouette at 32 px, and if a stranger cannot tell them apart, do not ship it.

PUT THE VEHICLE'S OWN WORDS IN, NOT COORDINATES. Drop '20.6N 87.1W' — it is the leisure-brand cliché this program exists to avoid. Use what is actually painted on the bus: '1963' from the chrome plate frame on the engine lid, or 'Gracias por su Preferencia' from the counter fascia, set in the brand's own house family (Cooper Black / Davida per the identity record) rather than a hairline sans. One line of Spanish converts the piece from austere gallery object to something with a voice, at zero cost to the composition.

BUILD THE 21:00 PANEL ON F144's ACTUAL DIAGNOSIS, NOT ITS REFUTED LEVERS. Do NOT touch T1_BULB_STR or T1_BULB_BASEV — both are ablated and both fail (60× emission makes the ratio WORSE by clipping; darkening the envelope does nothing). F144's live diagnosis is 'A saturated amber bead requires the SURROUND to be dimmer relative to the bulb.' A night frame supplies that for free. So the panel is a RIG job: kill the cyclorama, drop exposure, let the bulbs be the only source, and re-read F144's saturation ratio on the result — it should move for the first time in fifteen revisions. That makes this concept the piece that finally moves a stuck finding, which is worth saying out loud in the proposal.

DELETE THE DUD PANEL OR GIVE IT A JOB. If the near-zenith hour gives nothing, either drop it and ship an odd count, or make it the ONE panel that is not a shadow — the overhead view of the counter's own cast bar, or the pooled shadow shown at 4× scale as a detail plate. A merchandise set may not contain a month the buyer resents.

STATE THE IP POSITION EXPLICITLY IN THE PROPOSAL RATHER THAN CLAIMING IMMUNITY. Write one line: 'no VW mark is reproduced; the recognisable form is the CONVERSION — raised lid, cantilevered counter, propped tail board — which is Tacombi's, not Volkswagen's.' Then make that line true by rejecting any panel or crop where the conversion is not legible. That converts a vague safety claim into a shipping rule, and it is the same rule that makes the piece good.

OFFER THE WARM COMPANION SO THE PROGRAM IS NOT ALL SUBTRACTION. Pair the shadow set with ONE full-colour piece from the same day — the 21:00 bulbs in gold on black, or the flank's three gold masses (folk_gen.py measures the largest three components at 84.4% of all gold, so it simplifies almost losslessly). The shadow set then reads as the restrained half of a system rather than as a brand that removed its own colour.

concept.title: THE FILAMENT
concept.one_line: Delete the bus. What is left — one continuous warm line of ~115 lamps tracing a shape you already know — is the identity.
concept.the_image: There is no vehicle. On black, a single drawn path of light: ~115 discrete beads on a hairline wire, running 3.5 m of drip rail as a long gentle horizontal, turning down and around the rear roof dome, then breaking away up the propped tail board's 38° diagonal on its own string. The wire SAGS in small catenaries between the beads — that sag is the whole difference between a festoon and a dotted rule, and it must be drawn, not scaled. One hard clean horizontal beneath, shorter, no beads: the counter's brass nosing. If the aperture surrounds resolve as beaded (see model work), three tall rounded rectangles of the same beads hang under the main line, on the measured equal pitch — STATE.md: 'bay widths 0.516 0.515 0.516'. Nothing else. SCALE BEHAVIOUR IS THE DESIGN: at 32 px the beads fuse into one continuous glowing stroke; at 300 mm they separate into individual lamps with visible wire between them; at 3 m they are objects. One graphic, three readings, all correct. TWO RENDERINGS, both shipped as masters: (a) LINE — one warm ink (the authored 1.000/0.760/0.442 flattened to a single amber) on pure black, no glow, no gradient, hard-edged, for embroidery, foil, vinyl and small sizes; (b) GLOW — the same path with real bloom, halation blooming into the black, for screen and for the animated bug. MOTION, and this is the logo animation: 1.4 s. Beads catch left-to-right but NOT in order — two or three fire early, one lags. At ~1.1 s a single flicker across the whole string, one frame dark. Then steady, and hold indefinitely. It loops by simply never resolving into stillness.
concept.emotional_claim: Recognition without a name on it. Somebody who has eaten at Tacombi sees the bus instantly; somebody who hasn't sees a beautiful line and wants to know what it is. That asymmetry — rewards the insider, never punishes the stranger — is precisely what makes a mark get worn rather than displayed, and it is the difference between a badge and an advert. Emotionally the line is also the correct promise: it is the shape of the moment the place opens.
formats: NEON OR LED SIGN, 1.2–2.4 m, for the restaurants themselves. This is the one that goes back into the physical world: the graphic is a fabrication drawing for a real light, and the bead pitch is not invented — 28.6 ± 1.0 mm, measured twice by FFT in ref_side.jpg. A brand whose logo is a real lamp on its own wall is a brand that is telling the truth.
ANIMATED LOGO BUG 512 × 512 and 1080 × 1080; FAVICON at 32 px. The line survives the favicon; a bus silhouette does not — test this first, it is the strongest single argument for the idea.

EMBROIDERY, 55 mm on a black cap front, single thread, CHAIN OR BEAN STITCH — a running stitch, so the ~1.2 mm satin-column floor does not apply and a hairline wire with bead knots is actually producible. One needle, low stitch count, cheap enough to run on everything.

HOT FOIL, amber on black: matchbook, coaster, hang-tag, business card, 25–90 mm. Foil is the correct material because it is the only ink that changes with the light in the room, which is what the subject does.
KISS-CUT VINYL STRIP, 200 × 12 mm, for a laptop edge or a shelf lip. The one sticker format the line is actually suited to — long, thin, and it does not want to be a bus-shaped die-cut.
concept.why_not_derivative: Every competitor mark in this category is a bus outline. This is not the bus and not an outline — it is the light the bus makes, which is a thing only an owner who lit one would ever think to draw. It passes the logo-removal test outright (remove the word 'Tacombi' and it is still unmistakably one specific vehicle) and it is the lowest-exposure mark available in the whole programme: no VW roundel, no factory pressing, no filled bus silhouette (the shape claimed as trade dress), no folk art, no red, no sunset, no wheels. It is an identity built entirely out of a feature Volkswagen never made and a hardware-shop festoon a founder screwed to a drip rail. It also cannot be mistaken for CGI, which matters: a photoreal render is a saturated technique and this is a drawing.
concept.production_notes: EXTRACT THE PATH FROM THE MESH, NOT FROM A RENDER. bulb_string() already computes every bead centre in closed form — x stepping from BULB_X0 = T._aft(-1.8000) to BULB_X1 = 1.7000 at BULB_PITCH = 0.0286, z = (T.ZT_ALL(x) - T.RT_ALL(x)) + 0.01512 off the drip-rail roll start, y = side*(T.WX(x)*T.G(z) + 0.0180). Write a ~30-line exporter that projects those centres through the orthographic `side` camera (studio.views()['side'] is `lens=None, ortho=5.90`, a true parallel projection) and dumps SVG. That gives a mathematically exact path with no tracing, no resolution ceiling and no render dependency — and it is the only vector asset this repository would then contain, because today the sole committed .svg is vw_canonical_2019.svg, which F168 records as a DIFFERENT OBJECT from the 1955–67 pressing. EMBRACE THE ASYMMETRY: the string is built show-side only, so the mark is inherently one-sided. Do not mirror it to make it 'balanced' — the vehicle is asymmetric when it is working (lid up one side, counter out the other) and that is the point. FOR THE GLOW MASTER, render at low key with `--bloom 1.0` (post.py defaults it to 0.0) and note that BLOOM_THR = 0.94 only behaves on a dark field. THE COLOUR IS AVAILABLE AND IS NOT THE PROJECT'S CONTESTED ONE: the amber comes from the authored emission (1.000, 0.760, 0.442), whose saturation F144 measured at 0.558 against the photographed bulb's 0.561 — 'the hue is right to 0.003'. That is the single best-grounded colour in the entire vehicle, unlike the red, which exists as four unreconciled numbers (t1_mats sRGB(196,49,36), lid_gen (159,45,22), cal_gen (214,46,30)) and images salmon in the render.
model_work_required: RESOLVE THE APERTURE-SURROUND CONTRADICTION FIRST — THE SHAPE OF THE MARK DEPENDS ON IT, AND THE RECORD DISAGREES WITH THE BUILD. F144 states 'The bulb string runs the whole length of the drip rail AND forms the serving-aperture surrounds (F112)', and F112 (REFUTED-rev60b) says 'the aperture surround is a BEADED BULB STRING, which is what the render already builds'. But t1_detail.py's own measured note says the opposite and the build follows the note: 'The aperture surround is a matte white bobble fringe, not lamps, and the only lit string is on the drip rail OUTSIDE the skin, ~55 mm above the aperture heads' — and it is built by bobble_fringe() with material 'capwhite', unlit, at FRINGE_PITCH 0.0260 against the festoon's 0.0286. So the record says three rings of light and the machine builds three rings of matte white plastic. That is decidable by looking at ref_side.jpg at magnification and it decides whether the mark has three hanging rectangles or none.
WRITE THE BEAD-CENTRE SVG EXPORTER. Small, no Blender needed at render time if the centres are dumped once, and it is the tree's only route to a vector asset.

VERIFY THE STRING'S EXTENT BEFORE DRAWING IT LONG. The source's own comparison: 'the string runs model x +1.69 -> -1.64 photographed against -1.80 -> +1.70 built, +5 %.' The built string is 5 % longer than the photographed one. For a mark, decide deliberately which extent is authored and say which.

ADD THE TAIL-BOARD RUN AND THE REAR DOME TURN AS PART OF ONE PATH. tb_bulbs and tb_bulbflex exist as separate objects on the board; the drip rail and the board string are currently unrelated geometry. For the mark they must be one continuous drawn stroke, which is an authoring decision in the exporter, not a model change.

OPTIONAL BUT VALUABLE: FIX F144 IN THE MODEL SO THE GLOW MASTER CAN COME FROM A RENDER RATHER THAN BEING DRAWN. F144's two levers are both ablated and refuted (T1_BULB_STR=60 made the ratio WORSE, 1.40 → 0.88, by driving the bead toward clipping; T1_BULB_BASEV=0.30 moved it 1.38 → 1.50, nothing). Its own diagnosis is that the surround must be dimmer — i.e. the nocturne. Until that is measured, the LINE master is drawn and is not blocked by anything.

verdicts.lens: ORIGINALITY — is this genuinely fresh, or a well-executed version of something already on a thousand VW-bus and hospitality products?
verdicts.reasoning:
The subtraction instinct is the best thing here and it is real: delete the vehicle, keep one retrofit feature. The provenance is unusually honest for a concept doc — `t1_detail.py` genuinely carries "pitch 28.6 +/- 1.0 mm, ~115 bulbs" measured by FFT at 211 px/m, so the "~115 lamps" and the pitch are quoted correctly, not invented. The trademark reasoning is genuinely smart (no roundel, no filled silhouette, no factory pressing), and the neon-sign-as-fabrication-drawing loop is the single freshest move in the package.

But on the originality axis the concept's load-bearing claim does not survive contact with the geometry it cites, and I could not make it survive.

WHAT THE PATH ACTUALLY IS. `BULB_X0, BULB_X1 = T._aft(-1.8000), 1.7000` — the string spans ~3.5 m, and `z = (T.ZT_ALL(x) - T.RT_ALL(x)) + 0.01512` puts it on the drip rail, whose slope `STATE.md` measures at "roof line slope (measured off the mesh) | -18.1 mm/m". My arithmetic on those two figures: the "long gentle horizontal" drops about 63 mm over 3.5 m — a 56:1 line. Graphically, it is straight. Add the tail-board diagonal (F163's bbox z 1.754…2.209) and the whole mark is roughly 7:1; add the three bays hanging to 1.307 AG and it is roughly 4:1.

And the mark contains no VW. `BULB_X1 = 1.7000` against `STATE.md`'s "x range [-2.157, 2.160]" — the string stops 0.46 m short of the nose. The V-swage, the split screen, the round arches, the belt break: none of them is in the path. So "remove the word 'Tacombi' and it is still unmistakably one specific vehicle" is an assertion with nothing under it, and the geometry argues against it. What a stranger sees is a horizontal wire of beads with a spur. That is a festoon — the single most worn motif in hospitality graphics, sitting on patio bars, beer gardens, wedding venues and taqueria menus. With the bays it reads as a tram or a diner car, not a T1.

The favicon claim inverts. A 7:1 mark in a 32 px square is 32 × 4.6 px — a dash. A bus silhouette at 4.065 × 2.23 m is 1.8:1 and fits a square far better. The concept names favicon survival as "the strongest single argument for the idea"; on aspect ratio it is the weakest.

PRIOR ART IT RESEMBLES. (1) Automotive lighting signatures — Volvo's Thor's hammer, Audi's DRL graphics, Porsche's rear light bar. "The light the vehicle makes is the identity" is not a private insight; it is mainstream OEM brand practice, and it directly refutes "only an owner who lit one would ever think to draw." (2) Festoon/string-light marks and dividers across hospitality. (3) Marquee and carnival bulb lettering — the whole bead-on-wire vocabulary. (4) Connect-the-dots / constellation marks, which is structurally what beads-on-a-path forming a silhouette is. (5) Neon vehicle-outline signs, an established Etsy/Amazon category that includes VW buses. (6) The light-traces-the-object reveal, standard in car commercials.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY FRESH, and it is narrower than claimed: this is the light of a *retrofit*, not of a factory fitting — a hardware-shop festoon screwed to a drip rail by a founder — and the deliberate one-sidedness (`side=1`, show side only) is an uncommon identity constraint. That is a real differentiator and the concept buries it in production notes.

The formats are also arithmetically unbuilt at the stated pitch. 115 beads across a 55 mm cap front is 0.48 mm per bead; chain and bean stitch have a stitch-length floor well above that, so the embroidery format is not producible as specified. The 200 mm vinyl strip gives 1.74 mm per bead, at or below practical weeding detail. The pitch the concept treats as its precision credential is sub-perceptual everywhere except the neon sign and the 3 m case.

One thing the concept gets right and should be credited for: it found a live contradiction the project has not resolved — F112 says "the aperture surround is a BEADED BULB STRING", while `t1_detail.py` builds `bobble_fringe()` at `FRINGE_PITCH = 0.0260` in `capwhite`, unlit, and its own note says "not lamps". It is correct that this decides the mark's shape. It is wrong to leave it conditional, because it is the difference between a vehicle and a wire.

Competent, well-sourced, cheap to build, and the cheapest in the programme — but the differentiating content is precisely what it deletes. Workable.
fatal_flaws: THE RECOGNITION CLAIM IS UNEVIDENCED AND THE GEOMETRY ARGUES AGAINST IT. The path carries no VW-identifying feature: `BULB_X1 = 1.7000` stops 0.46 m short of the nose (`STATE.md` x range [-2.157, 2.160]), so no V-swage, no split screen, no arches, no belt break. On `STATE.md`'s measured -18.1 mm/m roof slope the 3.5 m rail drops ~63 mm — graphically a straight line. 'Still unmistakably one specific vehicle' is asserted, never tested, and what remains is a festoon.

THE FAVICON ARGUMENT INVERTS. My arithmetic on the quoted extents: rail + tail board is roughly 7:1, with bays roughly 4:1. A 7:1 mark in a 32 px square is a 4.6 px-tall dash. A bus silhouette (4.065 × 2.23 m per STATE.md) is 1.8:1 and fits a square far better. The concept names favicon survival as its strongest single argument; it is its weakest.

'ONLY AN OWNER WHO LIT ONE WOULD EVER THINK TO DRAW' IS FALSE AND INVITES A COMPARISON IT LOSES. Light-signature-as-brand-identity is mainstream automotive practice — Volvo's Thor's hammer, Audi's DRL graphics, Porsche's light bar. The claim as written points a reader straight at an entire industry doing this already.

TWO OF THE FIVE FORMATS ARE NOT PRODUCIBLE AT THE STATED PITCH. 115 beads across 55 mm is 0.48 mm per bead — below any running-stitch floor, so the embroidery format fails arithmetically. 200 mm vinyl gives 1.74 mm per bead, at or below practical weeding detail. The measured 28.6 mm pitch is sub-perceptual at every size except the neon sign.

THE SHAPE IS LEFT CONDITIONAL ON AN UNRESOLVED CONTRADICTION. F112 says the aperture surrounds are a beaded bulb string; `t1_detail.py` builds `bobble_fringe()` at `FRINGE_PITCH = 0.0260` in `capwhite`, unlit, and its own comment says 'not lamps'. The concept correctly identifies that this decides whether the mark has three bays, then designs as if either outcome were acceptable. Without the bays there is no vehicle; with them it reads as a tram.

THE MOTION BEAT IS THE GENRE'S MOST-USED GESTURE. 'One flicker, one frame dark at ~1.1 s' is fairy-light flicker — the default animation for every string-light graphic in existence. It is the one place the concept reaches for the cliché rather than the object.

THE SAG IS PRESENTED AS THE LOAD-BEARING DIFFERENTIATOR AND IS AN INVENTION. `bulb_string()` computes z per-x straight off the drip rail; there is no catenary in the mesh. 'That sag is the whole difference between a festoon and a dotted rule' therefore rests on drawn, not measured, geometry — which is fine, but it must be declared, and it cannot also carry the concept's fidelity argument.
improvements: TEST THE RECOGNITION CLAIM FIRST, AND LET IT KILL OR RESHAPE THE IDEA. Export the bead centres, render the path unlabelled at 32 / 128 / 512 px and at 55 mm, and show it to people who have eaten at Tacombi. The concept's entire emotional claim is the insider/stranger asymmetry; nothing in the package establishes the insider half. Budget this before the exporter, not after.

ADD THE ONE FEATURE THAT MAKES IT A T1 AND NOT A FESTOON: A SECOND LIGHT RUN DOWN THE V-SWAGE. The nose break is the T1's most identifying line and it is already in the machine — `STATE.md`'s 'V_APEX + V_RISE == Z_BELT | 1.2070 == 1.2070 — held', and SPEC §3's 'Break | belt line, sweeping down across the nose into the T1 V-swage'. No festoon graphic anywhere has a V. Author it as a declared INVENTION, which the record already licenses for derived artefacts: the owner sanctioned exactly this when he locked papel picado into the sticker scene knowing SPEC measures it absent ('Bunting in that render would be an invention'). This single addition converts a horizontal wire into an unmistakable nose-on-and-flank read.

SHIP TWO LOCKED LOCKUPS AND STOP CLAIMING ONE GEOMETRY DOES EVERYTHING. (a) HORIZONTAL, roughly 7:1 — rail plus tail board — for banners, strips, the vinyl edge and the neon. (b) SQUARE — the V-swage descent plus the forward rail turn, roughly 1:1 — for the favicon, the bug and the cap front. Publish both as masters. Do not carry the favicon claim on the 7:1.

DEFINE AN EXPLICIT BEAD LADDER WITH A STATED FLOOR AND MAKE THE REDUCTION DESIGNED. Something like: 115 beads above 400 mm; 48 from 100–400 mm; 18 below 100 mm; 9 at 32 px. State that below 400 mm the mark abandons true pitch deliberately. This fixes the embroidery (48 beads over 55 mm = 1.15 mm, still tight — at 18 it is 3.1 mm and comfortably stitchable) and turns an arithmetic failure into a documented scale system.

PROMOTE THE ASYMMETRY FROM A PRODUCTION NOTE TO THE MARK'S GOVERNING RULE. `bulb_string(side=1)` builds show-side only. Make it law: the mark has ONE legal orientation and the brand never mirrors it, because the vehicle is asymmetric when it is working. Most marks are orientation-agnostic; a mark that refuses to flip is genuinely uncommon and it encodes a true fact about the object. This is currently the concept's most original property and it is in the footnotes.

REPLACE THE FLICKER WITH A BEAT ONLY THIS OBJECT HAS. The model already carries the answer: `tb_bulbs` / `tb_bulbflex` are separate objects from `bulb_string` — the tail-board run is a different string. So light the rail, hold, and bring the tail-board diagonal up LATE and separately, because it is a second circuit. 'The other string comes on a beat later because it is another string' is true of the vehicle and is nobody else's animation.

REWRITE THE ANTI-DERIVATIVE ARGUMENT AROUND THE RETROFIT, NOT AROUND 'THE LIGHT IT MAKES'. Drop the light-signature framing entirely — it loses to Volvo and Audi. Lead instead with what is defensible and better: this is the light of a $3,000 donor bus that was 'missing three of its windows', lit by a hardware-shop festoon a founder screwed to a rail. SPEC §0.1 carries that as source-grade. The mark is a retrofit, not a fitting — that is the claim no OEM light signature can make.

DECIDE THE APERTURE QUESTION BEFORE DRAWING, AND MAKE IT A DESIGN DECISION. Look at `ref_side.jpg` at magnification, settle F112 against `t1_detail.py`'s 'not lamps' note, and then design ONE mark. If the bays are beaded, they are the mark's rhythm section and `STATE.md`'s 'bay widths 0.516 0.515 0.516' is the pitch. If they are matte bobbles, the mark needs the V-swage run even more urgently.

GIVE THE MARK A SECOND COLOUR FROM THE VEHICLE'S OWN MEASURED SYSTEM. One amber on black is the exact palette of every string-light graphic printed. The amber is well-grounded (F144: emission saturation 0.558 against the photographed 0.561, 'the hue is right to 0.003') so keep the beads — but put the WIRE in the counter's brass tone (`t1_mats.COUNTERTAN`, sRGB (201,186,150)), or run the tail-board string a step cooler. Two of the brand's own colours instead of the genre's one.

CORRECT THE EXTENT AND SAY WHICH RULER YOU AUTHORED. `t1_detail.py`: 'the string runs model x +1.69 -> -1.64 photographed against -1.80 -> +1.70 built, +5 %.' The built string is 5 % longer than the photographed one. For a mark that will be cut in vinyl and bent in glass, pick one and state it in the spec — and declare the catenary sag as drawn, since `bulb_string()` has none.

verdicts.lens: Producibility and fidelity — can THE FILAMENT be made from this asset as it stands, what breaks, and what unscoped model work it needs
verdicts.reasoning:
This is the only concept in reach of the asset TODAY, and that part survives audit. I re-ran `bulb_string()`'s formulas in plain python with no Blender: `import t1_core as T` works, and `z = (T.ZT_ALL(x) - T.RT_ALL(x)) + 0.01512`, `y = T.WX(x)*T.G(z) + 0.0180` evaluate directly. `BULB_X0 = T._aft(-1.8000) = -1.6368`, `BULB_X1 = 1.7000`, `BULB_PITCH = 0.0286` → span 3.3368 m, n = 117 intervals, **118 beads** (not "~115"; 115 is the photograph's FFT estimate, not the build). `studio.py` confirms `"side": dict(loc=(0.0, 26.0, 1.52), tgt=(0.0, 0.0, 1.52), lens=None, ortho=5.90)` — a true parallel projection. So the rail path is exact, cheap, Blender-free, and it needs no relight, no emblem, no red, no alpha, no large-format chain. It routes around every failing gate in the grounded reality. That is real and it is the concept's best argument.

But three load-bearing claims do not survive.

**The colour is measured in the wrong space.** `emissive()` writes `b.inputs["Emission Color"].default_value` — Blender colour inputs are scene-linear. F144 computed the saturation of the LINEAR triple (1.000, 0.760, 0.442) as though it were display values and got 0.558, then compared it to the photographed bulb's 8-bit sRGB 186/121/81 (sat 0.564) and concluded "the hue is right to 0.003". Converted properly, (1.000, 0.760, 0.442) linear is sRGB (255, 226, 177): **saturation 0.304 against the photograph's 0.564, and hue 37.5° against 22.9°**. Two rulers (rule 38), and the quoted statistic is a saturation being called a hue. The concept's "the single best-grounded colour in the entire vehicle" is founded on that. It is a pale cream-amber, not the deep amber the concept describes.

**The mark's defining gesture is invented, not extracted.** The rail z reads 1.8112 / 1.8133 / 1.8143 / 1.8145 / 1.8139 / 1.8148 across the span — **3.6 mm of deviation over 3.34 m**. It is a dead-straight horizontal, and the wire is a straight `T.sweep` between bead centres. There is no catenary anywhere in the mesh. The concept says the sag "must be drawn, not scaled" and then says the exporter yields "a mathematically exact path with no tracing" — those are in direct conflict: the exact path is a dotted rule. Worse, the concept's model_work #4 calls the dome turn "an authoring decision in the exporter, not a model change". It is not: the rail string ends at x −1.637 and `tail_board_bulbs` starts at the board base near x −1.85, z ~1.75 (chord 0.711 at 38°, tip x ≈ −2.41, z 2.209), so the exporter yields **two disjoint polylines separated by ~0.21 m in X with the board base ~0.06 m below the rail**. The connector — the one gesture that makes it read as a bus rather than a bar chart — is neither built nor exportable.

**The scale story fails in most of its own formats.** Mark width ≈ 4.11 m (rail forward end +1.700 to board tip −2.41). Pitch 28.6 mm, bead 22 mm, air 6.6 mm — a 77 % duty cycle, already a nicked line rather than pearls. Scaled: 55 mm cap → pitch 0.383 mm, bead 0.294 mm; 25 mm foil → 0.174 / 0.134 mm; 200 mm kiss-cut vinyl → bead 1.07 mm with **0.321 mm weeding gaps**; 90 mm foil → 0.626 / 0.482 mm. Beads survive only at ≥ ~300 mm (pitch 2.09, bead 1.61, gap 0.48) and on the sign. So in four of the five named formats the mark degenerates to two straight horizontals plus a diagonal, and the vinyl strip is not weedable at all. The "one graphic, three readings" claim holds for print above 300 mm and for screen — not for the craft formats it leads with.

Producible, cheap, and route-around-the-blockers correct. Ships an ungrounded ink and a degenerate drawing at most of its stated sizes.
fatal_flaws: THE COLOUR IS A CROSS-RULER ARTEFACT. `t1_mats.emissive()` writes `b.inputs["Emission Color"].default_value = (*colour, 1)` — scene-linear. F144 read (1.000, 0.760, 0.442) as display values to get saturation 0.558 and compared it to an 8-bit sRGB photograph value. In display space that emission is sRGB (255, 226, 177): saturation 0.304 vs the photographed 0.564 (1.86x short) and hue 37.5° vs 22.9° (14.6° off). The concept inherits 'the hue is right to 0.003' verbatim. Its one colour is not grounded, and the statistic quoted is a saturation, not a hue.

THE SAG AND THE DOME TURN ARE INVENTIONS PRESENTED AS EXTRACTIONS. Measured off `t1_core`: rail z = 1.8112 / 1.8133 / 1.8143 / 1.8145 / 1.8139 / 1.8148 at x −1.637 → +1.700 — straight to 3.6 mm over 3.34 m. `bulb_string()` sweeps a straight wire between bead centres; there is no catenary in the mesh and nothing in the record measures one on a rail-stapled festoon. The concept's own production note ('mathematically exact path with no tracing') contradicts its own image note ('the sag must be drawn'). What the exporter actually yields is 118 collinear dots.

THE 'ONE CONTINUOUS PATH' DOES NOT EXIST AS GEOMETRY. `bulb_string` ends at x −1.6368; `t1_shell.tail_board_bulbs(base, tip)` runs the board's own chord (TB_CHORD 0.7110 at TB_TILT_DEG 38.0, tip z 2.2087 per STATE.md, board bbox x −2.420…−1.846). Two disjoint runs, ~0.21 m apart in X and offset in Z, with nothing between them. Calling the join 'an authoring decision in the exporter, not a model change' is wrong — you cannot export a segment that is not built.

BEAD PITCH — THE MARK'S ENTIRE IDENTITY — IS DESTROYED IN FOUR OF FIVE NAMED FORMATS. At a 4.11 m mark width: 55 mm cap → pitch 0.383 mm / bead 0.294 mm (no embroidery stitch resolves that; the cap ships a plain line, so 'a hairline wire with bead knots is actually producible' is false); 25 mm foil → 0.174 / 0.134 mm; 90 mm foil → 0.626 / 0.482 mm with 0.145 mm gaps that will bridge; 200 mm kiss-cut vinyl → 1.071 mm beads with 0.321 mm weeding gaps, which is not cuttable. Only the sign and print ≥300 mm articulate.

THE DIAGONAL IS DRAWN AT A CONTESTED ANGLE. TB_TILT_DEG = 38.0 while F165 photographed 28.0° ('~10 deg TOO STEEP'), on two different rulers, never re-measured since rev 62 — HANDOFF_CARRIERS §0.05 item 3 is still unpaid. TB_WIDTH 0.5500 and TB_Y_CENTRE 0.0000 are both labelled 'POSE CHOICE, NOT MEASURED' in `t1_shell.py`. The board diagonal is the mark's only non-generic stroke and it is authored from a figure the record disputes by ten degrees.

THE GLOW MASTER IS BLOCKED AND MIS-ROUTED. F144 is OPEN with BOTH levers refuted by ablation ('T1_BULB_STR=60 ... moves the ratio 1.40 → 0.88, i.e. WORSE'; 'T1_BULB_BASEV=0.30 ... 1.38 → 1.50 — nothing'), so a render gives pearls, not lamps. And the named route destroys the output anyway: `post.py` carries `BACKDROP = "headroom"` (not black) and, per the grounded pipeline audit, discards alpha entirely — output colortype 2. A glow master cannot come off that path.

NO GUARD, AND THE MARK WOULD SILENTLY DRIFT FROM THE VEHICLE. Nothing in `verify_clone.sh` touches an exported path, and `t1_detail.py`'s own warning is that BULB_PITCH 'must NOT be re-spaced'. CLAUDE.md rule 13 requires the guard in the same edit. A shipped mark with no row is a second unversioned copy of a measured constant.
improvements: FIX THE INK BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE, AND FILE THE FINDING. Take the mark's amber from the PHOTOGRAPH in display space — F144's own painted window, sRGB 186/121/81, saturation 0.564, hue 22.9° — not from the linear emission constant. State its ceiling in the same sentence: ref_side.jpg is globally WARM per HANDOFF_CARRIERS §0.1, and ref_playa_34.png is the only frame with a neutral white reference (paving 116,119,120), so cross-check there before locking the hex. Separately, raise F144's saturation figure as a rule-38/rule-57(a) defect: 0.558 is the linear triple read as display; in display space it is 0.304 against 0.564, and the row calls a saturation a hue.

SPLIT THE ASSET IN TWO AND STOP CALLING IT ONE EXTRACTION. (a) MEASURED SPINE — bead centres from `BULB_X0/BULB_X1/BULB_PITCH` and `T.ZT_ALL/RT_ALL/WX/G`, plus `tail_board_bulbs`' chord, plus `bobble_fringe`'s `_resample_closed(bay_outline, FRINGE_PITCH)` rings, plus `counter_nosing`'s constant-z path at CNT_ZT 1.2540. (b) AUTHORED OVERLAY — the catenary sag and the rear-dome connector, each behind a named parameter (SAG_MM, DOME_R) and each labelled INVENTED in the exporter's own header. Print both in the exporter's summary line so nobody downstream mistakes the drawn half for the measured half.

GROUND THE DOME TURN OR DROP IT. The grounded art-direction pass reports ref_rear34.jpg cropped (950,60)–(1200,420) showing 'the same bead curving over the rear roof corner on a gold rail'. Paint that window, look at it, and read the turn's radius and bead count there BEFORE drawing it (rule 8) — it is the only frame that can answer it, and if it cannot, 'it cannot be recovered from what we hold' is a real result and the mark ships as two runs with a deliberate break.

SHIP TWO DRAWINGS, NOT ONE SCALED ONE, AND PUBLISH THE CROSSOVER. ARTICULATED master for ≥300 mm print and ≥600 px screen (pitch 2.09 mm, bead 1.61 mm, gap 0.48 mm — the arithmetic at a 4.11 m mark width). REDUCED master for ≤200 mm that CHANGES the drawing: crop to rail + one aperture ring + the board diagonal, hold bead pitch at a fixed ≥1.5 mm regardless of scale, and sacrifice count rather than resolution. State the crossover in mm on the master sheet so a production house cannot scale across it by accident.

RE-CUT THE FORMAT LIST ON THE ARITHMETIC. Kill kiss-cut vinyl (0.321 mm weeding gaps at 200 mm) and replace it with PRINTED vinyl. Set the foil floor at ~90 mm, not 25 mm, and even there expect gap bridging at 0.145 mm — proof one before committing the matchbook. Accept that the 55 mm cap is a LINE and design it as one (one continuous bean-stitch run plus the diagonal), or move to a three-bead reduced motif at ≥1.5 mm pitch. Say plainly which formats carry beads and which do not.

RE-SPEC THE SIGN AT 1:1 OR WITHDRAW THE 'FABRICATION DRAWING' CLAIM. At 2.4 m the pitch is 16.70 mm and the bead 12.85 mm — that is an LED rope, not the 22 mm festoon globes at 28.6 mm the photograph shows. A 1:1 sign is 4.11 m and reproduces the real lamp exactly; anything shorter is an abstraction and should be labelled one. This is the format that carries the whole 'it is a real light on their own wall' argument, so it is worth the extra 1.7 m.

RESOLVE F112/F144 vs `t1_detail` BY LOOKING, AND NARROW THE QUESTION CORRECTLY. The GEOMETRY is beads either way — `bobble_fringe()` builds `_ball(...)` at FRINGE_PITCH 0.0260 on `poly_offset(bay_outline, −FRINGE_INSET)`, so the three rounded rectangles are exportable today. What is unresolved is only the MATERIAL: F112 (MEASURED-rev60b) and F144 (MEASURED-rev61) both say lamps; `t1_detail` builds 'capwhite' matte bobbles and its comment says 'the only lit string is on the drip rail'. Paint the ref_side.jpg window first, then read it. This decides the mark's LICENCE to draw them glowing, not its shape — correct the concept's framing accordingly.

AUTHOR THE DIAGONAL FROM A DECIDED ANGLE AND SAY WHICH. Either pay HANDOFF_CARRIERS §0.05 item 3 first (re-measure the board's angle and chord on ONE ruler, with F165's two-significant-figure ceiling stated), or draw the mark at the PHOTOGRAPHED 28.0° and record in the master sheet that the mark and the model deliberately disagree pending that measurement. What must not happen is the mark inheriting 38.0° silently and then outliving a model correction.

ADD THE GUARD IN THE SAME EDIT AND WATCH IT FAIL. A pure-python probe that re-derives bead count and pitch from `BULB_X0/BULB_X1/BULB_PITCH` and `TB_CHORD/D.BULB_PITCH`, compares them to the shipped SVG's own path data, and prints a summary line (rule 9). Watch it go red by perturbing BULB_PITCH before you believe it green (rule 3). Then one `verify_clone.sh` row on it. Without this the mark is an unversioned copy of a constant the source explicitly forbids re-spacing.

AUTHOR THE GLOW IN 2D, NOT THROUGH THE RENDER. Drop `post.py` from the production note entirely — F144's two levers are refuted, so the render cannot supply the glow, and `post.py` defaults to a headroom backdrop and discards alpha. Build the GLOW master from the vector LINE master with a 2D bloom. That removes the concept's only dependency on an open finding and on the unproven optics chain.

CORRECT TWO FIGURES AND STRIKE ONE MODEL_WORK ITEM. The build carries 118 beads (n = 117 intervals over 3.3368 m at 0.0286), not ~115 — 115 is the FFT estimate off the photograph. And model_work #3 is chasing a stale source comment: the '+5 %' extent note predates the rev-16 `_aft` re-spacing, and on the shipped tree the built span is 3.3368 m against the photographed 1.69 → −1.64 = 3.33 m — agreement to 0.2 %. Delete that item and note the comment as stale.

RUN THE FAVICON TEST FIRST, WITH THE REAL ASPECT, AND BE READY FOR IT TO FAIL. The mark's bbox is ~4.11 m wide by ~0.975 m tall (counter nosing CNT_ZT 1.2540 to board tip z 2.2087), i.e. 4.2:1. At 32 px wide that is 7.6 px tall, with the aperture rings — the only feature that says 'serving hatches' — spanning the 1.307–1.710 m band, about 3.1 px. Predict a grey smear. If it fails, the REDUCED master above is not an option, it is the mark.

verdicts.lens: Emotional resonance, brand fit, and IP exposure
verdicts.reasoning:
IP is where this concept genuinely earns its keep, and it is the best position in the programme: no roundel, no pressing, no filled silhouette, no folk art. It is built from a hardware-shop festoon a founder screwed to a drip rail, which is exactly the kind of thing VW has no claim on. The motion beat is the best single line in the whole submission — "it is the shape of the moment the place opens" — and it is emotionally exact: the flicker-on with two beads early and one lagging, then never quite resolving, is a real feeling, not a styling flourish. The production route is honest and cheap; I confirmed `BULB_PITCH = 0.0286` with the source's own two-blind-specialist derivation ("FFT ... pitch 28.6 +/- 1.0 mm, ~115 bulbs") and the closed-form bead centres in `bulb_string()`.

But on my axis it fails twice, and both failures are structural rather than executional.

FIRST, THE RECOGNITION CLAIM IS NOT SUPPORTED BY THE GEOMETRY, AND THE CONCEPT KNOWS IT. The whole emotional proposition is "somebody who has eaten at Tacombi sees the bus instantly." What is actually drawn is a long horizontal, a curve at one end, a short diagonal, and one plain rule beneath. That is a festoon string, not a vehicle. The features that make this bus identifiable to a customer — the three serving hatches they were handed food through, the counter they stood at, the two-tone break, the folk art — are absent or reduced to a single line. The concept's own hedge gives it away: "IF the aperture surrounds resolve as beaded." Those three hanging rectangles are the only element that could read as "three serving windows," i.e. the only Tacombi-specific silhouette cue in the mark, and the concept makes its central claim contingent on a question it has not resolved. I resolved it, and it goes against them: `t1_detail.py` builds `bobble_fringe()` at `FRINGE_PITCH 0.0260` with material `capwhite`, unlit, and SPEC.md agrees in terms — "bobble fringe, not lamps; the only lit string is on the drip rail OUTSIDE the skin." F112 asserts the opposite and is itself demonstrably wrong about the build (it claims beaded "is what the render already builds," which it is not). Two of three records say pom-poms. So the most likely outcome is a mark with no apertures at all — a horizontal and a diagonal — and no insider recognition to reward.

SECOND, AND WORSE FOR BRAND FIT: IT ESCAPES ONE CLICHÉ BY RUNNING INTO ANOTHER. Warm amber bulbs on black is the most-used signifier in hospitality identity of the last fifteen years. The concept's anti-derivative argument is scoped entirely to the VW-merch category, where it wins; in the category the artefact will actually be seen in — restaurant branding — it is arguably more generic than a bus outline. The screener discounted this; I do not. And the palette cost is real: Tacombi's system is five parts (vermillion red, cream, folk gold, brick, brass), and THE FILAMENT discards four of them. It also inverts the brand's time of day. Every reference frame of the working vehicle is daylight — Playa open shade under palms, Nolita's cool grey-blue market fluorescent. Nothing in the reference set is a nocturne. The existing merch voice is deadpan leisure-outfitter ("purpose-built, all-weather knit beanie," "casual, convenient leisure products since 2006"), and the brand's own emotional centre, per the owner's own words elsewhere, is families and children. Amber-on-black is a natural-wine bar. It is beautiful and it is not this brand.

The IP claim is also mildly oversold. The path traced is the drip rail and rear roof dome — that is the T1 roofline, i.e. a dotted contour of the shape VW claims as trade dress. Far weaker exposure than a filled silhouette, and the tail-board diagonal is genuinely Tacombi's, but "no filled bus silhouette" is not the same as "no bus shape," and the proposal should say so rather than claim a clean zero. One smaller correction: the source records that show-side-only is INFERRED, not measured ("Pitch, bulb size and the fact that it is show side only are INFERRED"), so the asymmetry argument is standing on an inference.
fatal_flaws: The core emotional claim — instant insider recognition of a specific vehicle — is unsupported by what is actually drawn. A horizontal, a curve and a diagonal do not read as a bus; they read as a festoon. No test of this is proposed, and the concept's own conditional ('if the aperture surrounds resolve as beaded') concedes that its recognition cue is unverified.

The one element that could carry recognition — three beaded rectangles reading as serving hatches — is very likely not there. `t1_detail.py` builds `bobble_fringe()` at FRINGE_PITCH 0.0260 in unlit `capwhite`, and SPEC.md says 'bobble fringe, not lamps; the only lit string is on the drip rail OUTSIDE the skin.' F112 claims otherwise but is wrong about the build it cites. The mark's shape therefore probably collapses to two strokes.

Amber-string-lights-on-black is the dominant cliché of hospitality identity. The concept's originality argument is measured only against VW-van merch; in the category where the mark will actually live it is highly derivative, and no part of the proposal addresses this.

It abandons four of Tacombi's five palette components and inverts the brand's time of day. Every working reference frame is daylight; the merch voice is deadpan leisure-outfitter; the brand's emotional centre includes families and children. A nocturne in a single amber is a different brand's warmth.
improvements: RESOLVE THE FRINGE QUESTION FIRST, AND IF IT IS POM-POMS, BUILD ON THAT INSTEAD — it is a better idea than the one proposed. White ball-fringe round three openings is Mexican market and fiesta vernacular; Edison festoon is Brooklyn. A mark made of three rounded rectangles of white bobbles hanging under one warm line is both more Tacombi-specific and more joyful, gives you a second ink and a second material, and reads to children in a way an amber filament never will. Decide it by looking at ref_side.jpg at magnification before any drawing is made — one hour, and it changes which concept you are building.

PUT THE THREE APERTURES IN THE MARK UNCONDITIONALLY, in whichever material the frame settles. They are the recognition cue and the whole insider-reward proposition rests on them. Use the measured equal pitch already in STATE.md ('bay widths 0.516 0.515 0.516'). Two strokes is a festoon; two strokes plus three hanging openings on a measured rhythm is a serving counter.

TEST THE RECOGNITION CLAIM BEFORE COMMITTING, and it costs nothing: draw the bare path, show it to ten people who have eaten at a Tacombi with no wordmark and no context, and ask what it is. If fewer than half say 'the bus' or 'Tacombi,' the emotional thesis is refuted and the mark needs the apertures, the counter tail, or the tail board's angle exaggerated. This is the same discipline the project applies to everything else — do not publish the claim without watching it print.

SHIP A DAYLIGHT COLOURWAY AS A CO-EQUAL MASTER, not a variant: the same path in vermillion or brass on cream. That single addition brings the mark back into Tacombi's actual palette, makes it usable on packaging, paper, apparel and signage where black grounds are wrong, and rescues it from the bar-identity register. Amber-on-black then becomes the night state, which is what it is genuinely excellent at.

STOP CALLING IT THE LOGO AND POSITION IT AS THE 'OPEN' MARK — the night signal, the animated bug, the sign on the wall, the thing that lights when service starts. That is precisely what the 1.4s flicker-on is emotionally about, and it is far more defensible as a system component than as a primary identity that must also work on a menu, a bag and a child's sticker. Scoped that way, its weaknesses stop being weaknesses.

STATE THE IP POSITION HONESTLY RATHER THAN CLAIMING ZERO EXPOSURE. The path traced is the T1 roofline, i.e. a dotted contour of the shape claimed as trade dress. Say so, then note the mitigations that are real: it is a contour not a fill, it carries no roundel or pressing, and the tail-board run is the converted vehicle's own. An overclaim here is the kind of thing that gets caught by a lawyer rather than by a designer.

DROP THE ASYMMETRY ARGUMENT OR RE-GROUND IT. The source says show-side-only is INFERRED ('Pitch, bulb size and the fact that it is show side only are INFERRED'), not measured, so 'do not mirror it, the vehicle is asymmetric when working' is a design preference dressed as a fact. Keep the preference — it is a good one — and say it is a choice.

KEEP THE MOTION EXACTLY AS SPECIFIED. The two-early-one-lagging catch, the single dark frame at ~1.1s, and the refusal to resolve into stillness are the best-observed things in the submission and they are the reason this concept deserves a second pass rather than a kill.

concept.title: TWENTY-FOUR SECTIONS
concept.one_line: The bus sliced transversely every 150 mm and every slice drawn as a filled cross-section on one sheet — a CT scan of a taco stand, in which the three sections through the serving bays are dense with machinery and the sections through the engine bay are empty.
concept.the_image:
THE RISKY ONE. A cautious team rejects it because at thumbnail size it does not look like a bus.

The vehicle is cut transversely at a regular station interval and every slice is drawn as a filled closed shape, arranged in a grid and read left-to-right, nose to tail, like a contact sheet. Across the 4.065 m body (STATE.md: `dims L=4.065`), 150 mm gives 27 sections, 200 mm gives 21. Every section is printed at the same scale, on the same ground line, so the object's anatomy evolves as your eye travels the grid.

Each section is FILLED COLOUR, not line: the outer body a solid warm red band, the cream upper a solid band, glass a thin dark line, and everything the plane passes through drawn solid in the galley's own seven colours.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY REVEALS — this is the entire idea and it is three distinct acts:

ACT ONE, the cab. Sections forward of about x = +1.04 pass through a fully built interior: `seat_back`, `seat_base`, `seat_welt` and their passenger pairs, `wheel_rim` / `wheel_hub` / `wheel_horn` / two `wheel_spoke`, `dash`, `dash_grille`, `dash_glovebox`, three pedals, `gear_lever`, `mirror_int`. Dense, small, mechanical.

ACT TWO, the galley — and the body wall OPENS. The three sections at the measured bay centres (`BAY_CX = (0.6720, 0.0470, -0.5980)`) cut straight through the serving apertures. Each of those three shows: a break in the flank 515.5 mm wide; the counter slab in section, 107 mm thick (`CNT_ZT, CNT_ZB = 1.2540, 1.1470`) projecting 321 mm in plan (`CNT_Y_IN, CNT_Y_OUT = 0.8450, 1.1660`); the plancha or the worktop; a rack; the strip light near the roof line at z 1.788–1.802; and the back wall at y = −0.480. Three sections in the run are full of the machinery of feeding people. That is the cutaway, and it arrives as a rhythm rather than as a single reveal.

ACT THREE, the tail, and it is the punchline. The sections aft of about x = −1.30 pass through the engine bay of a 1963 Type 2 — and there is NOTHING IN THEM. An empty ring of sheet metal where on any other split-screen bus on earth there would be a dense air-cooled flat-four. That is Tacombi's own founding sentence rendered as a drawing rather than written as copy: "The engine was scrapped, transmission sold" (SPEC.md §0.1, graded S).

COMPOSITION: a 4 × 6 or 3 × 7 grid on warm paper. Each cell holds one section, labelled only with its station in millimetres from the front axle. Consistent ground line across every cell. No leader lines, no callouts, no perspective anywhere. Gold hairlines for the station labels and the cell rules only. One line of type at the foot in the brand's deadpan register — something at the exact temperature of "1963 Type 2 · transverse sections at 150 mm · station −1900: empty."

MOTION VERSION, and it is nearly free once the sections exist: the slices play in sequence nose to tail as a 3-second loop — the shape breathing open at the three bays and hollowing out at the tail. That is a title card, a social loop and a menu-screen ident from one asset. And it obeys the only motion law this vehicle has: it never drives. The SECTION PLANE moves; the bus does not.
concept.emotional_claim:
Awe first, then a small joke, and the gap between them is where the artefact lives.

The awe is the sheer measured-ness. You cannot fake this image. Twenty-seven consistent cross-sections of a specific vehicle is visibly the output of someone who knows the object to the millimetre, and it lands as evidence of care before it lands as information. That is the emotional payload of every good technical illustration and it is unusually strong here.

Then, six or seven seconds later, you notice the tail sections are empty — and if you know what a Type 2's tail contains, or you read the one line of type, the whole poster reorganises itself around an absence. It is the brand's origin story delivered as a punchline you find yourself, which is the strongest form.

And it is warm despite being a scan, because the palette is warm and the sections are hand-weighted: the reds and creams and ambers of a kitchen, arranged with the patience of a boat-lofting drawing.
formats: B1 707 × 1000 mm, edition print, hand-numbered in pencil, authenticated with a blind emboss chop rather than a signature (there is no artist's hand on a render and a forged signature on CGI is embarrassing). Colophon at the foot in 6 pt naming revision, resolution, sample count and date — unfakeable provenance and completely anti-advert

ALL-OVER APPAREL REPEAT. The sections tile beautifully: pattern at three metres, anatomy at thirty centimetres. This is the format that solves the walking-advert problem structurally — it reads as texture first and as a bus second, so only someone who knows sees the bus
Wrapping paper, cup sleeves, and a menu's endpapers, from the same repeat
3-SECOND LOOP, 1:1 and 9:16, for social and for the in-store menu screen — sections playing nose to tail
SINGLE-SECTION MICRO-GOODS: station +0.047, the middle bay, the one with the griddle in it, as a 40 mm enamel pin, a woven label, or a 25 mm sticker. This is the entry point that teaches the poster
Postcard set: three cards, one per bay section, at 148 × 105
concept.why_not_derivative:
