Nothing in the VW-bus merchandise market is remotely like this, and the two nearest tropes are both refused on purpose.

It is NOT A BLUEPRINT. Dreamstime sells "Vw Van Blueprint Stock Illustrations" by the sheet, and the blueprint move is the obvious way to dramatise a 3D model — white lines on cyan, orthographic elevation, dimension arrows. This is filled colour shapes on warm paper with no elevation and no dimension arrows anywhere. And critically, a stock blueprint annotates a generic VW; every section here is of the CONVERSION.

It is NOT AN EXPLODED DIAGRAM. Nothing floats, nothing hovers, nothing is pulled apart on an axis. The vehicle is intact; the plane moves.

Its actual relatives are medical imaging and boat lofting, neither of which has ever been pointed at a food truck. And it can only exist because someone measured this exact object for seventy-five revisions — it converts the program's most exotic and least-used asset (a clean, manifold, 229-object mesh with `non-manifold edges (body) | 0`) directly into content, which nothing else in the program does.

And the punchline is proprietary. "The engine bay is empty" is a fact about ONE bus in the world. No competitor can print it, because every other bus in the category still drives — which is precisely the thing the category is selling.
concept.production_notes:
WHY A CAUTIOUS TEAM REJECTS IT, said plainly so it is not discovered late: at thumbnail it reads as abstract pattern, and someone will say customers will not understand it. Ship it anyway. The pattern-at-distance / anatomy-up-close split is the feature, not the bug, and the single-section pin is the cheap entry point that teaches the poster. Do not sand this into a friendlier cutaway; the friendlier cutaway is Concept 1 and it already exists.

FILLED SHAPES, NOT LINE. The temptation will be to outline every section for legibility. Resist it — filled colour is what separates this from the blueprint category, and the sections have enough internal contrast (red band, cream band, steel, amber, green) to read without a keyline.

STATION LABELS FROM THE DATUM, GENERATED. Label from the front axle, and generate every figure from the constants at layout time.

THE ENGINE-BAY CAPTION MUST BE HONEST AND IT IS A TWO-PART FACT. The MODEL has no engine object — STATE.md's inventory contains none. The REAL VEHICLE has no engine, by the brand's own S-graded account. Those are two different facts that happen to agree, and the caption must not claim the model measured an absence it simply never modelled. Say it the true way: "no engine is modelled, because there is none in the vehicle." That sentence is better copy than the dishonest version anyway.

SPOT INKS AGAIN — five, per AUDIT_rev43's "seven inks printed; five if cut." The sections are large flat areas of a small number of colours, which is the ideal screen-print case and terrible CMYK material (large flat process fields band and mottle).

RENDER EACH SECTION AS ITS OWN TILE at high resolution. This entirely sidesteps the large-format stitch problem: no single frame needs to be 4677 px, because the sheet is assembled from 27 small ones. That is a real production advantage over both other concepts and it is worth saying out loud.

MOTION: 27 frames at ~5.5 min each is roughly 2.5 hours of render for the whole loop, and it never needs re-rendering because the sequence is the same asset as the poster. Do not fan out Blender — it is CPU-bound on four cores and two instances make both slower.

SEED THE GRAIN PER FRAME IF POST IS EVER APPLIED. post.py's grain is `seed=7`, fixed — identical grain on every frame reads as dirt on the lens and instantly betrays a still-image pipeline. For this concept the right answer is simply no grain at all.
model_work_required: A SECTION CUTTER — and there is nothing like it in the tree. build.py step 3 issues windscreen, side, rear and gap cutters and nothing else; there is no clip plane, no slice, no section path anywhere. Needs a `T1_SECTION_X` boolean intersect against a thin slab, run N times. ⚠ AND THIS IS EXACTLY THE OPERATION THIS TREE HAS BEEN BURNED BY: STATE.md's own warning reads "The cab-door gap booleans passed at SUB=1 and collapsed the shell at SUB=2 for six revisions. Run both." Watch the slice fail before believing it.

CAPPING, AND IT IS THE REAL ENGINEERING. A boolean slice leaves open boundary edges. The body shell is a thin skin — 2.8 mm per the source's own description of the galley as "a sealed 2.8 mm steel box" — so an UNCAPPED section renders as two hairlines rather than a solid band, and the entire visual idea collapses. Every cut surface must be capped and given the section's own fill material. Prototype this on ONE station before committing to twenty-seven.

THE OFF-SIDE PROBLEM IS AT ITS ABSOLUTE WORST HERE, AND IT IS THE LARGEST PIECE OF NEW GEOMETRY ANY OF THESE THREE CONCEPTS NEEDS. Every transverse section crosses the backdrop plane at `GAL_Y_BACK = -0.4800` and continues to the off-side flank — and beyond that 24 mm slab there is NOTHING. The source is explicit that `gal_end_f` and `gal_end_a` exist "to stop a camera seeing past the backdrop into unlit body cavity." Sections aft of the galley will be honest; the three money sections THROUGH the galley will show a 24 mm slab floating in a void unless a real off-side liner and floor are built. Build them. They are worth having regardless, and both other concepts benefit.

VERIFY THE SECTIONS AGAINST THE MESH, NOT AGAINST THE PICTURE. Each cut's cross-sectional area and its component count should be printed and checked, so a section that silently loses a capped face is caught by a number rather than by someone squinting at cell 14 of 27.

NO ALPHA STRICTLY REQUIRED (each section renders on its own tile), NO EMBLEM WORK, NO NOSE WORK, and no dependency on the stitch chain at delivery size. The cab and galley objects benefit from Concept 2's form work but do not require it — at section scale a box reads as a box legitimately, because in section it IS a rectangle.

ONE HONEST CHECK BEFORE ANY OF IT: render three trial sections — one cab, one bay centre at x = +0.047, one tail at x ≈ −1.90 — crop them and LOOK. If the tail section is not legibly, satisfyingly empty, the punchline does not land and the concept should be reconsidered rather than rescued.

verdicts.lens: ORIGINALITY — is the form genuinely fresh, or a well-executed instance of an existing idiom? Judged by naming the nearest prior art and testing whether the concept's distinctiveness survives contact with it.
verdicts.reasoning:
The FORM is borrowed and the pitch does not admit it. Serial transverse sections of one object, same scale, same ground line, read left-to-right in a grid, is a mature idiom with at least six close ancestors, none of which the "why_not_derivative" section names: the naval-architecture BODY PLAN / station lines (which the pitch does cite, as a relative, without noticing it is the direct parent); Damien Hirst's serially-sectioned animals (Mother and Child Divided, 1993), which is the fine-art canon for exactly "a familiar body sliced and displayed in sequence"; the Bechers' typological grid, which is where "same scale, same ground line, read as a set" comes from; Ed Ruscha's Every Building on the Sunset Strip for the contact-sheet serialism; Nick Veasey's X-ray photography, which has been pointed at VW campers and sells as art print; and — most damagingly — the laser-cut / stacked-plywood "sliced vehicle" wall-art and model category, which is a live consumer merchandise genre that includes VW buses. That last one directly refutes the pitch's central sentence, "Nothing in the VW-bus merchandise market is remotely like this." The pitch refutes the two tropes it is NOT (blueprint, exploded diagram) and never names the ones it IS.

The pitch also narrows the reference class until it wins: "medical imaging and boat lofting, neither of which has ever been pointed at a food truck." That is the shape of a weak originality argument. Sections have been pointed at food (Beth Galton's cut-food cross-sections are a whole genre), at buildings, at animals and at vehicles. "Food truck" is the qualifier doing all the work.

The CONTENT is genuinely fresh, and the screener identified the right thing. "A 1963 Type 2 whose tail sections are empty" is proprietary, unfakeable from a stock shell, and it is a punchline the viewer finds unaided. That is a real idea and it is why this is not "weak". But it is ONE fact, and the concept's originality rests entirely on it — which means the fact had better be true, and against this tree it is not. build.py builds `trunk_bay` explicitly so "the opening reads as a compartment and not a hole"; STATE.md's inventory carries `trunk_bay | 1`, `underpan | 1`, `chassis_rail | 2`, `van_floor | 1`, `under_close_a | 1`. And `t1_detail.py`'s `CNT_X_IN = CNT_X1 + (CNT_Y_OUT - CNT_Y_IN)  # -2.002  tail leg inner face` puts the counter's tail leg inside the aft-most stations. So a transverse cut aft of x = −1.30 does not give "an empty ring of sheet metal"; it gives a lined compartment with a floor, an underpan, two chassis rails and, at the extreme stations, counter legs. The one original element in the concept is asserted, not measured, in a project whose first rule is that a claim in prose is not a measurement.

Third originality problem, unexamined: a body plan is beautiful because a hull's stations all differ — the pleasure of the idiom IS the evolving silhouette. A T1 is a slab-sided box. STATE.md prints `bay widths 0.516 0.515 0.516`, so the three hero sections are near-identical BY CONSTRUCTION, and the outline between the axles barely moves. The concept's promise that "the object's anatomy evolves as your eye travels the grid" is probably false for this specific vehicle, and would be true of almost any other subject. An idea that would be more original applied to something else is not yet original here.

Fourth: the motion version — slices playing nose to tail in a 3-second loop — is the most-seen single instance of this entire idiom on the internet (the CT-scroll GIF). It is the least original thing in the concept and it is offered as "nearly free", which is exactly why it will ship unexamined.

What lifts it above "weak": the empty-tail insight is real content, the non-uniform-information structure (dense galley / hollow tail) is an unexploited seam inside the idiom, and rendering 27 small tiles instead of one large frame is a genuinely smart production dodge. What holds it at "workable": the form is inherited, the nearest neighbours are unnamed and one of them is a live VW-bus product category, the pitch's differentiation argument is a narrowing trick rather than a difference, and the single proprietary element is factually wrong against the mesh it claims to be reading.
fatal_flaws: THE PUNCHLINE'S PREMISE IS FALSE AGAINST THE TREE, and it is the concept's only original element. `build.py` states in terms that a lining exists behind the engine lid: "The bay behind the engine lid, so the opening reads as a compartment and not a hole." STATE.md's inventory carries `trunk_bay | 1`, `underpan | 1`, `chassis_rail | 2`, `van_floor | 1`, `under_close_a | 1`; `t1_detail.py` has `CNT_X_IN = CNT_X1 + (CNT_Y_OUT - CNT_Y_IN)  # -2.002  tail leg inner face`. A transverse cut aft of x = −1.30 therefore passes through a closed lined compartment, a floor, an underpan, two chassis rails and — at the extreme stations — the counter's tail leg. It is not "an empty ring of sheet metal" and it is not "NOTHING IN THEM". Unchecked, in a project whose CLAUDE.md says a claim in prose is not a measurement.

THE 'why_not_derivative' SECTION REFUTES THE TWO TROPES THE CONCEPT IS NOT AND NAMES NONE OF THE ONES IT IS. Unnamed nearest neighbours: naval body plan / station lines (the direct parent, cited as a cousin), Damien Hirst's serially-sectioned animals, Bernd & Hilla Becher's typological grids, Ed Ruscha's Every Building on the Sunset Strip, Nick Veasey's X-ray photography (pointed at VW campers, sold as prints), Beth Galton's cut-food cross-sections, and the laser-cut / stacked-plywood 'sliced vehicle' wall-art category. The last of these is a live consumer merchandise genre that includes VW buses, which directly refutes the pitch's sentence "Nothing in the VW-bus merchandise market is remotely like this."

THE DIFFERENTIATION IS A NARROWING TRICK, NOT A DIFFERENCE. "Medical imaging and boat lofting, neither of which has ever been pointed at a food truck" wins by shrinking the reference class until the set is empty. Sections have been pointed at food, buildings, animals, engines and vehicles. Strip the qualifier and the claim does not survive.

THE IDIOM'S CORE PLEASURE IS UNAVAILABLE ON THIS SUBJECT AND THE PITCH NEVER CHECKS IT. A body plan works because a hull's stations all differ. A T1 is a slab-sided box; STATE.md prints `bay widths 0.516 0.515 0.516`, so the three money sections are near-identical by construction and the outline barely evolves between the axles. The promised "anatomy evolves as your eye travels the grid" is likely to be 27 near-identical rounded rectangles varying only internally.

THE MOTION VERSION IS THE MOST DERIVATIVE ELEMENT IN THE PROGRAM. Slices playing nose to tail is the CT-scroll GIF, the single most-seen instance of this idiom, and it is offered as "nearly free" — which guarantees it ships without an originality pass.

THE PITCH FILES ITSELF UNDER THE SATURATED GENRE VOLUNTARILY. "A CT scan of a taco stand" is the one-liner. That sentence tells the audience which existing thing to compare it to, and the comparison is unflattering.

ABSENCE IS NOT A DRAWING. Even if the tail sections were empty, an empty cell on a poster reads as a printing error or as the drawing running out. The joke needs a foil and the concept supplies none — only a caption, which arrives after the reader has already decided the cells are blank.
improvements: VERIFY THE PUNCHLINE BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE, AND MAKE IT THE GO/NO-GO. Render exactly one section at x ≈ −1.90, cap it, crop it and look. If it shows `trunk_bay`'s lining plus `underpan` plus two `chassis_rail` — which build.py and STATE.md say it will — the void does not exist and the concept is a competent body plan with no idea in it. Do this before the three-section test the pitch proposes, and before any capping engineering.

IF THE VOID IS FURNISHED, RE-AIM THE PUNCHLINE AT WHAT IS ACTUALLY THERE, WHICH IS BETTER ANYWAY: a lining with nothing behind it. 'The bay is lined and the lining is the whole of it' is a stranger and truer sentence than 'the engine is gone', it is visible in section, and build.py's own comment — "Nothing is invented to fill the bay: PHOTOS_WANTED_rev44 records that 'the engine was scrapped and the transmission sold', so its contents are unknown" — is the caption, already written, already graded.

GIVE THE ABSENCE A PHYSICAL FOIL: DIE-CUT THE ENGINE-BAY CELLS OUT OF THE SHEET. Where the flat-four should be, the poster has holes and the wall shows through. That converts an absence into an object, it is a printing decision no stock-shell competitor can copy, it is cheap, and it makes the joke land before the caption is read. Second-best: one single ghost cell in the palest gold hairline showing the outline of the engine that left, dated. Worst: caption only — which is what the concept currently has.

MAKE THE STATION SPACING THE CONTENT. Uniform 150 mm is what body plans and CT scans do BY DEFINITION, so uniform spacing is the idiom's signature and you inherit it wholesale. Instead: 75 mm through the three galley bays (dense, mechanical), 150 mm through the cab, then widening through the tail until the sections stop. The grid thins out because there is nothing left to cut. That is an original move INSIDE the idiom rather than a use of it, and it makes the sheet's rhythm carry the story without a word.

BREAK THE MONOTONY WITH A SECOND AXIS IN THE SAME GRID. One longitudinal section along the serving side, at the same scale, running full width as a band above or below the transverse cells: it shows the cab, the three apertures, the counter slab and the hollow tail as ONE continuous shape. That silhouette exists nowhere else and cannot be mistaken for either a body plan or a CT set. It also rescues the sheet if the 27 transverse outlines prove near-identical.

INVERT THE MOTION OR DROP IT. Do not scroll the plane nose to tail. Either hold the section plane still and pull the vehicle through it — the plane becomes a doorway and the bus passes, which is the only motion this vehicle is allowed and reads as service rather than driving — or run the slices ASSEMBLING into the solid bus and stopping short at the tail. Both are unfamiliar; the scroll is the most familiar image in the genre.

REPLACE THE MARKET ASSERTION WITH EVIDENCE, IN THE PITCH ITSELF. Every other claim in this program is measured; "nothing in the VW-bus merchandise market is remotely like this" is not, and I believe it is false for at least the stacked-slice / laser-cut sectioned-vehicle category. Search it, name the five nearest neighbours by title in the pitch, and differentiate on the axis that actually holds: every one of them sections a COMPLETE vehicle. This sections a CONVERTED one. THE DIFFERENTIATOR IS THE CONVERSION, NOT THE SLICING — and the pitch currently sells the slicing.

STOP CALLING IT A CT SCAN, IN THE PITCH AND IN THE COPY. Adopt the naval body plan / station-line lineage instead: it is warmer, it is period-correct for a 1963 object, it justifies the warm paper and the gold hairlines, and it points at an ancestor nobody expects on a taqueria poster. One word changed in the one-liner; a different genre for the whole artefact.

PUT THE CONVERSION IN THE LABELS. 'station −1900' is a coordinate. 'station −1900 · engine bay · empty since 2006' is content, and the year is S-graded in SPEC.md §0.1 from Tacombi's own account. Same ink, and it moves the sheet from a technical exercise to a document about a specific object's history.

RE-PICK THE MICRO-GOOD. A lone rounded-rectangle section at x = +0.047 on a 40 mm pin is unreadable as anything — it is a shape, not a bus, not a joke. The entry good must be the cell that carries the idea: a tail section, empty, with its station label. That teaches the poster in one object; the busy galley section does not.

RUN THE SUBSTITUTION TEST AND REPORT IT. Would this sheet be equally good of a Citroën HY, a Bedford CA or a Grumman Olson? Everything that survives that swap is inherited form. On my reading only two things fail it: the three aperture breaks in the flank and the hollow tail. Concentrate every design decision on those two — bigger cells for the bay sections, the tail cells die-cut — and let the other twenty-one be quiet and small. A sheet where 21 of 27 cells are generic and 6 are proprietary should not give the 21 equal weight.

IF ALL OF THE ABOVE FAILS, THERE IS A GENUINELY UNPRECEDENTED VERSION AND IT IS ONE PARAMETER AWAY: rotate the cut plane progressively across the set — a helical section series, nose-vertical through tail-horizontal. Body plans and CT sets are orthogonal by definition, so a rotating section set has no ancestor I can name in any of the seven genres above. It is also the version most likely to fail the capping engineering, so cost it before promising it.

verdicts.lens: Producibility and fidelity — can this sheet actually be made from THIS mesh, this render chain and these gates, and does the resulting image say what the concept promises?
verdicts.reasoning:
The mechanics are more tractable than the screener's note implies, and the content is far weaker. Taking those in order.

MECHANICALLY IT IS EASIER THAN BILLED. The concept and the screener both frame capping as "the whole picture" and reach for a boolean intersect against a slab — which is exactly the operation STATE.md warns about ("The cab-door gap booleans passed at SUB=1 and collapsed the shell at SUB=2 for six revisions"). But a planar section does not need a boolean. Blender's `mesh.bisect` with `use_fill=True` caps a planar cut with an n-gon directly, on a joined duplicate, and the body is the one asset in this tree that guarantees it will work: STATE.md reads `non-manifold edges (body) | 0` and `cutters rolled back | none`. Ortho cameras already exist (`studio.views()`: `"front": ... ortho=3.55`). And the 27-tiles-instead-of-one-big-frame argument is real and is the concept's strongest producibility claim: it genuinely sidesteps `hq_render.py`/`stitch.py`, which F192 records has never been proven above 3840 and whose seam check exits 2 (F49).

THE CONTENT IS THE PROBLEM, AND IT IS MEASURABLE. The concept's Act Two — "three sections in the run are full of the machinery of feeding people" — is false against the built model, and I read the constants rather than the prose. `t1_detail.galley()` builds `X0, X1 = -1.3000, 1.0400` and every fitting inside it sits between roughly y −0.48 and y −0.05 and between z 1.26 and 1.85 (`gal_worktop` y −0.4400..−0.1800; `gal_tube` z 1.7880..1.8020; the backdrop `GAL_Y_BACK = -0.4800` spanning z 1.2000..1.8950). Below z 1.20 the interior is void all the way down to `van_floor`, a 40 mm slab at z 0.5400 — a 660 mm empty band across the full width. And `FLOOR_W = 1.200` (half-width 0.600, marked "AUTHORED, rev 38") against a body half-width near 0.875, so even the floor stops 275 mm short of each flank. Outboard of the backdrop at y −0.480 to the off-side skin is another ~395 mm of nothing, which the source names twice as "unlit body cavity".

So the money sections are a thin ribbon of equipment at head height floating over a hollow rectangle. The tail sections are also hollow. The contrast the whole poster turns on — dense galley, empty tail — does not exist in the asset. The punchline has no straight man.

WORSE, A SECTION PLANE HAS NO CAMERA, AND THIS MODEL IS BUILT FOR CAMERAS. `gal_end_f` spans y −0.5000..+0.2600, z 1.2000..1.8600, and its own comment says what it is: "end returns: without them a 3/4 camera looks along the flank past the ends of the backdrop into unlit body cavity". `gal_end_a`'s half-width is derived from the rear aperture that looks at it. These are sight-line occluders, not bulkheads. In a transverse section at x ≈ +1.05 the forward one renders as a stub of wall floating in mid-air, stopping at y +0.260 with nothing beyond it. That generalises: every camera-driven simplification in a model tuned against four views (`T1_PREVIEW=front,side,hero34f,hero34r`) becomes visible in the one view that cannot be dressed. F14 — `gal_end_f`'s sight lines — is the oldest INHERITED row in the register and the concept walks straight into it.

AND THE SKIN CANNOT BE A BAND. `build.py` sets `sol.thickness = 0.0028`. Lay 24 sections on B1 707×1000 with 40 mm margins at STATE.md's own lids-open bbox (`bbox top 3.132`, W 1.7497): the aspect forces six columns, cells ~104 mm wide, scale ≈ 1:16.7. The 2.8 mm shell prints at 0.167 mm — sitting on AUDIT_rev43 §5's own "0.15 mm floor". Capping converts two hairlines into one hairline; it does not produce "a solid warm red band". The band is a drawing decision, which means this sheet is an illustration derived from the mesh, not a render of it — and the concept's production route (render each section as a photoreal tile) is the wrong route for the picture it describes.

WHAT IT DOES DODGE, honestly: the emblem (F191's hold is on the delivery render, and no section publishes the roundel), the gloss gate, the tread's 48..84 bracket, and the stitch chain. If it also went to a material-ID pass it would dodge the salmon red (F240: G/R 0.42–0.52 against the photograph's 0.114) as well — but it doesn't propose that.

Net: producible as an image, not producible as the image described, and the gap is closed only by inventing interior geometry that no frame we hold shows. That is a bigger unscoped build than either sibling concept and it is the kind of invention this project's method exists to refuse. Weak — but with a real salvage, because the void is a better story than the one the concept is telling.
fatal_flaws: THE CENTRAL CONTRAST DOES NOT EXIST IN THE ASSET. Act Two promises galley sections 'dense with machinery'. Measured from the source: `galley()` spans `X0, X1 = -1.3000, 1.0400`, its fittings occupy roughly y -0.48..-0.05 and z 1.26..1.85, the backdrop `GAL_Y_BACK = -0.4800` runs only z 1.2000..1.8950, and below that the interior is void to `van_floor` at z 0.5400. `FLOOR_W = 1.200` (AUTHORED) against a body half-width ~0.875 leaves 275 mm of void either side even at floor level. The bay sections are a thin ribbon over a hollow box. With the galley hollow too, the empty tail is not a punchline — it is the whole drawing.

THE MODEL'S INTERIOR IS CAMERA-DRIVEN AND A SECTION HAS NO CAMERA. `gal_end_f` is built y -0.5000..+0.2600, z 1.2000..1.8600 under a comment that states its purpose verbatim: 'without them a 3/4 camera looks along the flank past the ends of the backdrop into unlit body cavity'. In section it is a wall stub floating in air. `gal_end_a`'s half-width is derived from the aperture that looks at it. This is the general failure — 75 revisions of optimisation against four views, exposed by the one view that cannot be dressed — and F14 (gal_end_f's sight lines) is the register's oldest INHERITED row.

THE 2.8 mm SHELL CANNOT RENDER AS A 'SOLID WARM RED BAND'. `build.py`: `sol.thickness = 0.0028`. Fitting 24 sections on B1 707x1000 at STATE.md's lids-open bbox (top 3.132, W 1.7497) forces ~104 mm cells, scale ~1:16.7, so the skin prints at 0.167 mm — on AUDIT_rev43 §5's own 0.15 mm floor. Capping turns two hairlines into one hairline. The picture the concept describes is an illustration with chosen stroke weights, not a render of the mesh, and the proposed production route is the wrong one for it.

THE UNSCOPED WORK IS INVENTION, NOT MODELLING. To make the galley sections read, someone must build the under-counter volume (cabinets, bottles, drawers) and the off-side liner — the majority of every bay section's area. No frame we hold shows either; the reference set is closed (§0.1, owner ruled rev 54), and the source itself calls that region 'unlit body cavity'. Publishing invented interior on a sheet whose entire emotional claim is 'you cannot fake this image / measured to the millimetre' inverts the project's method.

THE GRID ARITHMETIC IS WRONG THREE WAYS IN ONE DOCUMENT. Title says twenty-four; 150 mm across `dims L=4.065` gives 27; the proposed grids are 4x6=24 and 3x7=21. And 4x6 does not fit B1 at the section's aspect: at 40 mm margins, 24 cells of aspect 1.7497:2.2268 need five columns, and at the lids-open 3.132 they need six.

ALPHA IS WAIVED AND IT IS NOT WAIVABLE. 'NO ALPHA STRICTLY REQUIRED (each section renders on its own tile)' — 27 tiles composited on warm paper need a cut-out or they are 27 white rectangles. Grounded reality: every frame in `out/` is colortype 2 (no alpha), `T1_ALPHA` appears in no LEDGER since F159 at rev 62, and `deliver.py`'s C1 currently reads '[FAIL] C1 ... FAILING ON: hero34f, hero34r, side, front'. `post.py` measurably discards alpha, so the optics chain is closed to this artefact anyway.
improvements: DROP THE BOOLEAN. Use `bpy.ops.mesh.bisect(plane_co=(s,0,0), plane_no=(1,0,0), use_fill=True)` on a joined duplicate — it caps the cut with an n-gon by construction and never touches the shipped shell, so STATE.md's 'cab-door gap booleans ... collapsed the shell at SUB=2 for six revisions' does not apply. Bisect twice, at s and s+0.001, keep the slab, render from the existing ortho `front` camera. Then watch it fail per rule 3: run it at SUB=2 as well as SUB=1, and run it at a station with no geometry to confirm it refuses rather than emitting an empty tile.

RUN THE THREE-SECTION CHECK AS A NUMBER BEFORE IT IS A PICTURE. Print, per station, the CAPPED cross-sectional area and the connected-component count at x = +1.300 (`t1_core.X_AXLE_F`, cab), x = +0.0470 (`t1_shell.BAY_CX[1]`, bay 2) and x = -1.900 (tail). The concept's premise is that bay-2 area is much greater than tail area. On the constants I read it will not be. If bay-2 does not clear the tail by a wide margin, the poster's contrast is dead and no amount of drawing rescues it — kill or re-aim it there, at ~10 minutes of cost.

RE-AIM THE STORY ONTO WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: THE BUS IS EMPTY THROUGHOUT. The measured reading is not 'dense galley, hollow tail' — it is a hollow shell with a 600 mm ribbon of equipment at head height: `CNT_ZT, CNT_ZB = 1.2540, 1.1470` (107 mm counter slab), the backdrop at y -0.480, the strip light at z 1.788-1.802, and void everywhere else. That is a better and more proprietary story than the engine gag: the conversion is a SHELF, not a kitchen; a taqueria is one plane at the right height and nothing else. It needs no new geometry, and it turns finding-1 from a fatal flaw into the subject.

RENDER A MATERIAL-INDEX / FLAT-EMISSION PASS, NOT A PHOTOREAL TILE. `probe_rev54_aov.py` already writes EXR AOVs into `probe_scratch/`, so the route is half-built. Flood-fill the ID pass to flat inks in 2D. This makes the five-spot-ink claim actually deliverable, and it removes at a stroke: the salmon red (F240, render G/R 0.42-0.52 against the photograph's 0.114), the failing gloss gate (0.412 against a 0.60 bar), AgX tone-mapping, `post.py` entirely, and the 2.044 % two-render noise floor. It also collapses the render budget — the quoted '27 frames at ~5.5 min' is a 96-spp photoreal figure and does not survive the change; re-derive it, do not inherit it.

STATE THE SHEET'S SCALE IN THE COLOPHON AND DECOUPLE STROKE WEIGHT FROM WALL THICKNESS. AUDIT_rev43 §5's own ceiling — 'every millimetre figure above is a PROJECTION from a measured metre through a stated scale' — is the model to copy. Print '1:16.7' (or whatever the final grid gives), then declare that the shell is drawn at a chosen weight because 2.8 mm at that scale is 0.167 mm. Honest, and it converts the flaw into the drawing's own footnote.

FIX THE GRID FROM THE MESH. Pick 24 stations at 4.065/24 = 169.4 mm and say so, or 27 at 150 mm and draw 27 cells. Size the cell from STATE.md, not from taste: lids open the bbox top is 3.132 (aspect 1:1.79, needs 6 columns on B1); lids closed it is 2.2268 (aspect 1:1.27, fits 5x5 at ~125 mm). Rendering with the lids DOWN is the cheaper and denser sheet and costs nothing but an env var.

HATCH EVERY UNMEASURED SURFACE AND NAME IT IN THE COLOPHON. The sections will publish, as if measured: `REAR_OPEN_DEG = 64.0` (STATE.md: 'declared 64.0, NOT MEASURED -- a POSE'), `TB_WIDTH = 0.5500` ('POSE CHOICE, NOT MEASURED'), `TREAD_LUGS = 64` ('DECLARED, inside the MEASURED bracket 48..84'), `TREAD_CUT = 0.0060` ('DECLARED groove depth, m. NOT measured'), `FLOOR_W = 1.200` ('AUTHORED, rev 38'), and `gal_end_f`/`gal_end_a` as sight-line occluders. A second tint for these makes the sheet a measurement WITH ITS CEILING — which is the only version of this idea that this project is allowed to print, and it is more interesting than a clean lie.

DO NOT BUILD THE OFF-SIDE LINER OR THE UNDER-COUNTER CABINETS TO MAKE THE PICTURE WORK. Nothing we hold shows either. Either draw the void and caption it, or put ONE multiple-choice question to the owner with a crop of `ref_side.jpg` bay interior — 'what is under the counter: (a) open, (b) cupboards, (c) gas bottles and crates' — using the question tool, per CLAUDE.md. Replace the two bulkhead stubs with full-width planes only if the answer requires it, and add the guard in the same edit.

SHARPEN THE ENGINE CAPTION OR IT OVER-REACHES. The model has no engine — and no gearbox, fuel tank, battery, wiring or heater channels either. So 'empty' is indistinguishable from 'unmodelled', and the drawing gives the viewer no way to tell which absence is the meaningful one. Either name the full list in the caption, or drop the claim and let the shelf story carry the sheet.

BUDGET AND PROVE THE ALPHA PATH EXPLICITLY. Render ONE tile with `T1_ALPHA=1`, read the PNG IHDR and confirm colortype 6, and route it nowhere near `post.py`. F159's 184-distinct-alpha-values reading is a rev-62 result on one proof frame and has not been re-run in thirteen revisions; treat it as unproven until this tile exists.

ADD ONE GUARD, DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY. Per station, compare the capped section's outer width against the body's own lofted half-width at that x, taken from `t1_core` rather than from the bisect — a silently lost cap face then reads as a number, not as someone squinting at cell 14 of 27. Deriving the check from the bisect itself would be rule 6's tautology.

KEEP THE TWO PROPERTIES THAT ARE GENUINELY BEST-IN-PROGRAM AND SAY THEM OUT LOUD IN THE PITCH: 27 small tiles need no `stitch.py` and no proven large-format chain (F192/F49 both sidestepped), and the sheet publishes no emblem, so F191's hold does not reach it. Those are real and neither sibling concept has them.

verdicts.lens: Emotional resonance, brand fit and IP exposure
verdicts.reasoning:
On IP this is the best-positioned concept I can imagine for this program, and that is not a small thing. The trademark exposure the research names is the vehicle's IMAGE — "the images of classic Beetle and Bus vehicles are themselves protected as trademarks" — and the roundel. A transverse section reproduces neither: the silhouette that carries VW's meaning is the profile and the face, and a cut perpendicular to the long axis destroys both. It also structurally sidesteps the emblem: the roundel is a shallow relief on a near-normal nose face (`ROUNDEL_D = 0.2800`), so no section cell contains a readable VW mark. That means this is the only concept on the table that can ship without touching the defect the owner has reported nine times and that F191 gates the delivery render on. Genuine, checkable strength.

Brand fit is where it breaks, and the concept has not noticed the mechanism. Every element of Tacombi's own graphic identity is SURFACE — the folk art on the red (`swirl.png`/`swirl_b.png`, box-projected), the Calidad burst on the cream, the mural lid, and the wordmark, which `build.py` places as a flank decal at `SCR = dict(x0=0.784, x1=-0.494, ...)`. This concept cuts perpendicular to every one of those planes. The script, the burst, the paisley and the mural all reduce to an edge-on sliver or vanish. So the artefact achieves its excellent VW-avoidance by also avoiding Tacombi: twenty-seven cells of a Tacombi poster in which Tacombi appears nowhere. That is the inverse of the IP win and it is the same cut that produces it.

The register is the second brand miss. The concept reaches for CT scan, boat lofting, blind emboss, pencil numbering, and a colophon "naming revision, resolution, sample count and date." Tacombi's actual voice in the grounded research is outfitter-catalogue deadpan — "casual, convenient leisure products," "a convenient coastal super sac," "Your Flavor Has Arrived." Those are two different deadpans. A colophon quoting sample count is the render pipeline congratulating itself inside a customer artefact; the concept says so itself when it claims the payload is "evidence of care" — care by the modeller, legible only to modellers.

The emotional claim is over-sold on its own terms. It promises "a punchline you find yourself" and then specifies a caption that explains the punchline; the "or you read the one line of type" is doing all the work, because a family eating tacos does not know what a Type 2's tail contains. And the joke's delivery has a rhythm problem the concept has not seen: at 150 mm the tail is roughly ten near-identical near-empty cells, close to 40 % of the sheet. A joke told once lands; told ten times in a row it reads as the printer running dry. I checked what a tail section would actually contain — `trunk_bay` is a 0.42 m lining at the tail skin ("A plain lining behind the engine lid, so the bay is not a void"), plus `underpan`, two `chassis_rail` and `under_close_a` — so the mid-tail cells are a thin red ring with two small dark bars. That may well be satisfying once. It is not ten cells of content.

Ownership test, honestly: a designer buys the B1. A diner buys the pin. The single-section enamel pin of the middle bay — the one with the plancha in it — is the most wantable object in the whole list and it is buried at format six. That inversion is the concept's own misreading of who it is for.
fatal_flaws: THE CUT DESTROYS TACOMBI'S IDENTITY WHILE IT DESTROYS VW'S. Every piece of the brand's artwork is a surface decal on a longitudinal plane — the wordmark at `SCR = dict(x0=0.784, x1=-0.494, z0=0.4453, z1=0.9896)`, the folk art box-projected on the flanks, the Calidad burst on the rear-corner cream, the mural on the lid. A transverse plane meets all of them edge-on. The sheet contains no wordmark, no script, no burst, no paisley and no mural. It is a Tacombi artefact with no Tacombi in it, and that is the same property that makes its IP position good.

THE PUNCHLINE REQUIRES PRIOR KNOWLEDGE THE AUDIENCE DOES NOT HAVE, AND THE FALLBACK KILLS IT. 'The engine bay is empty' only lands on someone who knows a 1963 Type 2's tail is dense. For everyone else an empty cell is indistinguishable from an unmodelled cell — and it literally is one: build.py records 'Nothing is invented to fill the bay: ... "the engine was scrapped and the transmission sold", so its contents are unknown.' The concept's remedy is a caption, which converts 'a punchline you find yourself' — its own stated emotional mechanism, and the strongest form — into a joke explained in the margin.

THE PROPOSED CAPTION IS THE ONE PLACE THE CONCEPT REINTRODUCES VW IP IT HAD OTHERWISE ELIMINATED. '1963 Type 2 · transverse sections at 150 mm' puts a Volkswagen model designation on merchandise, against research that reads 'You cannot refer to the brand name Volkswagen, or VW on products without a license.' The image is clean; the copy is not.

THE THIRD ACT IS 40 % OF THE SHEET AND HAS ONE BEAT. At 150 mm across 4.065 m the tail contributes roughly ten cells that all read as the same thin red ring plus `underpan` and two `chassis_rail` bars. Repetition is what the grid's rhythm is FOR, and here it repeats the least interesting cell the most times.

THE REGISTER IS GALLERY, NOT TAQUERIA. Hand-numbered edition, blind emboss chop, colophon naming render revision and sample count. This is a CGI studio's self-promotion dressed as brand merch, and it is at odds with the owner's only stated brief for a customer-facing artefact — 'should spark joy and be something families keep', 'for children at the restaurant'. Numbering an edition of an infinitely reproducible file also invites a question about authenticity the brand gains nothing by answering.
improvements: RE-CENTRE THE ARTEFACT ON ACT TWO AND DEMOTE ACT THREE TO A CODA. The brand is feeding people, not scrapping engines. Make the three bay sections at the measured centres `BAY_CX = (0.6720, 0.0470, -0.5980)` the hero — printed larger, or given the top row alone — with the cab and tail as the supporting run. The griddle section is the emotional content; the empty engine is the footnote that rewards a second look. That single re-weighting fixes the ownership problem, the rhythm problem and the brand-fit problem at once.

PROMOTE THE SINGLE-SECTION PIN TO THE LEAD FORMAT. Station +0.047, the middle bay with the plancha in it, at 40 mm enamel. It is the only object in the list a family would actually take home, it is the entry point that teaches the poster, and it is cheap. Ship it first and let the B1 follow it, not the reverse.

VARY THE STATION INTERVAL INSTEAD OF HOLDING IT CONSTANT. Sample densely through the cab and the galley where the anatomy changes fast, sparsely through the tail. Or collapse the tail run into ONE wide cell captioned as such. A constant interval is a fidelity instinct, not a design one, and it is what produces ten dead cells. State the varying interval on the sheet so the honesty survives.

## What I changed, and what I refused

**Grafted in and pushed further**

- **Purged the archetypes, and verified the replacements against `STATE.md`.** El Sol is gone (it is the most-reproduced lotería card, and `AUDIT_rev43.md` already rules "THE SUN — it must NOT be a rayed disc"). **La Bocina is gone** — F309 retires the roof loudspeakers as "REMOVABLE EVENT GEAR… a POSE, not vehicle geometry," and no speaker object exists in the inventory. **El Vaso is gone**, not renamed to `gal_sqbottle`: loose galley dressing is F309's own failure class. Replacements are all in the live inventory — **El Volante** (`wheel_rim`/`wheel_hub`/`wheel_horn`/`wheel_spoke|2`), **El Reloj** (`speedo_bezel`/`speedo_face`/`speedo_glass`), **El Gozne** (`hinge_barrel|4`/`hinge_leaf|4`). **La Llave stays as `gal_warmer_tap`** — verified at `A(_gcyl("gal_warmer_tap", ...))`.
- **The measured-figure footer, transformed.** Printing dimensions is right; printing *these* dimensions was not. I refused every figure the record cannot defend with one ruler: the chord (F245 leaves 0.710 / 0.790 / 0.829 and says "Do not average them"), the badge Ø (`STATE.md`: "hubcap badge is SELF-CONSISTENCY ONLY — CAP_EMBLEM_WFRAC has never been compared to a frame"), the bay width (0.516 / 0.515 / 0.516), and 4.580 m (flagged "+525.0 mm OUT", while the same file's verify line reads 4.317 with lids / 4.065 without). What replaced it is **the four-stamp provenance system** — MEDIDO / DICTADO / POSTURA / NO CONSTA. Four cards now *print a refusal*. That is the deck's best idea and it came out of the constraint, not around it.
- **Game math fixed without either auditor's remedy.** 3 × 3 tablas of nine, eight of them: mean shared cards between boards is k²/N = 81/24 = 3.4 of 9, against 256/24 = 10.7 of 16 for the proposed 4 × 4.
- **A visible proof of origin.** Card 1 is a partial cutaway, card 2 hatches through the aperture onto the galley. The normals argument is true but imperceptible; the cutaway is perceptible.
- **The hatch engine promoted to the headline of the work**, with the sphere/plane known-answer validation, and **two corrections that would each have cost a revision**: `probe_rev55_truenorm.py`'s own message says *"THE TRUE NORMAL IS NOT THE FIX… fires on every FACET boundary — tessellation, not folds"* (both the concept and an auditor cited it for the opposite), and `matte_tap`'s `color_depth='8'` is a PIL workaround that must not be copied to a density pass.
- **Card 24 re-argued rather than re-specified.** The `LID_W`/angle coupling isn't an obstacle to route around — it is wrong physics. A panel's width is a property of the panel; the aspect 1.7130 is a *projected* reading at one propped angle. Freezing `LID_W` is the correct derivation, and it has grounding: F309 records that in `ref_playa_34.png` "the board is down and the bus is closed."
- Also taken: `T1_SAVE` build-once/isolate-23, Line Art measured on the real mesh first, geometric La Sombra, the cropped louvre run, the dichos and the displaced-archetype line, the box stating the category error, the stated scale, the not-the-sticker framing, the three-card prototype, the four-density no-blend rule as the anti-scratchboard signature.
- **Corrections to the concept's own facts:** La Flor is **eight** lobes and eight petal-dots (`lid_gen.py`: "LOBE COUNT — rev 10's TWELVE IS REFUTED… N_LOBE = 8"); ten is the number of *heads*. The 84.4 % gold figure is the **photograph's**; the built figure is 81.0 %.

**Refused, with reasons**

1. **La Combi Verde.** The *facts* are grade S in SPEC §0.1 (green, $3,000, "missing three of its windows", "only had the front bench"). The *identification* is not: §0.1 says "This is the Playa bus, NOT the Nolita one", the carriers list `ref_workshop.jpg` under "NOT the target, geometry only", and SPEC records the green-vs-red attribution as still contested. There is no frame of the Playa bus as bought and no geometry for it. Drawing it would publish a position on an open identity question and invent an unbuilt vehicle — "it cannot be recovered from what we hold."
2. **Going to 54 cards.** It triples the illustration cost to solve a problem a 3 × 3 tabla solves for free, and the conceit does not improve with dilution.
3. **Dropping the tablas for a specimen set.** That removes the thing the emotional claim rests on — a family at a table.
4. **Gold on the card faces.** Gold is real (`t1_mats.GOLD = (0.8600, 0.5400, 0.0600)`) and the register-collision argument is fair, so gold got the backs, the tabla grid, the box and the colophon. It does not touch an image. Two inks in the object, one ink in every picture.
5. **The Spanish-signage card.** "GRACIAS POR SU PREFERENCIA" returns **zero hits** across every `.md` and `.py` in the tree; it is in no model object and no cited crop. The one Spanish sign the record *does* document — the yellow *"FAVOR DE ORDENAR Y PAGAR AQUÍ"* in `ref_rear34.jpg` (F309) — is a café-patio sign, not on the bus. Both fail the deck's own rule.
6. **Softening the risk paragraph.** It stays, and it got longer: the hatch engine is now inside the honest cost.

I grounded every load-bearing figure against source before rewriting. Some of what I found changes the concept materially.

**What I changed, and why**

Grafted, with grounding done against source rather than the pitch:

- **The 1:1 rule replaces the auditor's "1 px = 4 mm".** It is the same instinct — let the measurements author the layout — but stronger, because it turns the sheet into a document instead of a bar chart. I derived it: 2400 rectified px across `LID_X0 - LID_X1 = 0.9640, -1.0700` gives **0.8475 mm/px horizontally and 0.8200 mm/px vertically** (the rectified frame is 1.600 against `BOARD_ASPECT = 1.654`, a 3.4 % anisotropy nobody has flagged). It then produced two facts I could not have designed: the `JUICES,`→`&` specimen is **1002.6 mm at 1:1 against B0's 1000**, so the format is forced and the specimen is clipped by the paper as it was already clipped by a frond and a vehicle; and the `100% Calidad` decal is **513 × 380 mm of real paint**, which is why it can be the legible payoff without being a smear.
- **The hero is the hole** (auditor 1), as untouched stock in a flooded sheet — but I refused to end the sheet cold there.
- **Five registers, labelled** (auditors 1 and 3), and I added a fifth they did not have: *read, and still reconstructed*. `cal_gen.py` says the photograph is blown at the burst and "the paint is reconstructed saturated". That is what makes the payoff earn its place.
- **Livery states split into three sheets**, the hero swapped to an in-state, on-target, measured element, and the silver killed outright — F157's object is the word `Senor` only.
- **La Santa given its own sheet with no name on it**, titled with the counts. Fixes the third-party trade-mark exposure and F164's "separate from the Bus" in one move instead of two compromises.
- **Ink corrected to the measured (91,59,7)**, halftone declared on the sheet, no black, enlarge from native with both scales captioned, `?` drawn as a letterform, provenance line, rule-34 framing of the ask, 251/267 fixed in SPEC.

Refused:

- **Ending on the hole with nothing legible.** That is auditor 1's own "one idea at length" flaw. The escalation to a legible line whose colour is admitted invented is colder *and* warmer than either alternative.
- **`★ FRESH JUICES … & TORTAS ★` as the payoff** (auditor 3). Those words are the void's shoulders; using them as the hero makes the hero its own caption.
- **The `1963` plate blind-embossed as an attribution mark** (auditor 3). It is already a specimen; repeating it as a signature weakens both. Attribution is the foot provenance line.
- **Twelve postcards** (concept) — replaced by one die-cut card, since the hole is the only element that survives reduction. **Abandoning small formats entirely** (auditor 3) — refused; the placemat as *one 420 mm slice of a 589 mm absence* is the cheapest and best object in the programme.
- **Any suggestion that the specimen-column form should go** because Holzer/Ruff/Paglen/Fili exist. The 1:1 rule is unavailable to all of them, and I flagged those attributions as unverified leads — WebSearch is deferred here.

Corrections to the audit itself: the rectified frame is a **~5.6–6.2×** upsample, not "roughly 9×" (computed from `lid_gen`'s own quad); and I found a discrepancy no auditor raised — **`BOARD_ASPECT = 1.654` (CI [1.591, 1.703]) against `LID_ASPECT = 1.7130`**, two figures for one board, both labelled measured off `ref_side.jpg`, with no document noting the pair.

I verified every load-bearing figure against source before rewriting. Findings that changed the concept are in the note at the end.

**What I changed, and what I refused to.**

**Grafted, with verification.** The uncertainty is now **drawn** — range bands at scale for the 48..84 lug bracket (confirmed in `probe_rev74_tread.py`: *"REFUSES to publish a lug count… THE BRACKET IS THE RESULT"*) and an open-ended band for `TB_WIDTH` (`t1_shell.py`: *"UPPER BOUND, admissible: W <= 19.9/33.5 = 0.59 m. LOWER BOUND: NONE."*). The tail board is drawn twice from one hinge, 38.0° built against 28.0° photographed. The taxonomy became five tiers, and rather than invent them I adopted **`SPEC.md` §0's own M/S/R/E/U grade table** as the legend. Biography is now the hero register; the licensing sentence ("Surveyed from seven photographs. Nothing measured on the vehicle.") is in the title block; factory dimensions are demoted to a disclaimed datum strip and "TYPE 2" is deleted; silver is off the annotations; the vanity stats become a survey tally; the precedent (Up Goer Five, Dear Data, Anatomy of an AI System) is named. `WIDTH = f(ANGLE)` is promoted and its four points verified live off `t1_shell.py`.

**Pushed past what the auditors asked.** Three finds are mine. **(1)** `STATE.md` reports the vehicle **`+525.0 mm OUT`** on overall length — I closed the arithmetic (4.580 all-bodywork / 4.317 excluding the 9 non-bodywork parts / 4.065 without lids / 4.055 spec; the 0.263 m step is the tail board's tip at x −2.420), so the sheet dimensions its own length four times and stamps one OUT. A better class-4 hero than rake. **(2)** SPEC.md line 138 grades the off side **E, "(never photographed)"**, and a photograph search run at the owner's instruction found nothing — so *SHEET 3 — NOT ISSUED* is grounded verbatim rather than invented, and it is the strongest object in the set. **(3)** The **body colour is a ruling, not a measurement** — SPEC.md carries *"Unresolved and material: every colour reference for the PLAYA vehicle says GREEN"* — so the sheet's largest area of ink gets a RULED mark, and I flagged it as a must-ask before print. Also new: the hubcap badges keep the disc and ring but **decline the glyph**, printed in the key.

**Corrections to the concept and to the audit.** The resolution arithmetic was wrong in both: **4677 px is A2 at 200 dpi, not A1** (A1 wants 6622); 3840 px on A2 is **164 dpi**. That inverts the production logic — the raster route cannot reach the primary format, so the line pass is the gate for the whole piece, not a bullet. The auditor's "hubcaps below judgeable scale" is wrong (9.5 mm at A2). **"Gracias por su Preferencia" is not in this repo** — invented; removed, and the hand re-sourced to `sign_gen.py`'s actual brush primitives. The chord 0.7110 is *derived from two measured heights*, not a pixel read, and the photographed 0.829 m carries a flagged flat px/m — so the ghost-overlay annotation names the ruler flaw instead of implying a clean disagreement.

**Refused.** *Crop the cab off the primary.* It deletes the front-axle datum, the wheelbase scale reference and half the drafting furniture that makes the sheet read as a survey rather than as pastiche — and a fragment is more likely to read as decoration, not less. I took the thumbnail and trade-dress problem seriously and solved it structurally: **Sheet 2 is the cropped taqueria elevation, and it is what ships to every feed, the bookmark and all five social posts.** *Delete the machine stats entirely* — I kept `0 NON-MANIFOLD BODY EDGES` (a claim that the survey closes) and dropped the vertex/object boast. *"The moat is copywriting, so the numbers are worthless"* — I reject the conclusion; the fix is to make the numbers visible as geometry, which is now done. *Delete register 3* — demoted to the A2/A1 tier and pre-conceded in negotiation, not removed.

## What I changed, and what I refused

**The single structural change: the bus is now drawn OPEN and DARK, not shut and dark.** This was auditor 3's lead improvement and it pays four ways at once — it deletes the shut-state build entirely (and with it the `LID_W` 1/sin blocker, the pose rows a shut build would red, and the whole unscoped ablation family), it removes the dry sheet from the two stock tropes the market survey documents, it makes the dry state carry the brand at the 90 %+ of handovers that never get wet, and it keeps the only transition that means anything: DARK → LIT.

**The single creative escalation: the resist is now the idea, not an afterthought.** Auditor 1 proposed barrier lanes to structure the wick; I made them the vehicle's own service path so the lights come on in the order a taqueria wakes up — counter, hatches, galley, rail — and made the sequence-vs-blob control test the gate the concept is judged on. That converts "every sheet is a different lunch" from an assertion into something week one either proves or kills. It also solves auditor 2's rim-vs-blob geometry problem without demoting the rail: the rail is last and never promised.

**Grafted in full:** scale fixed to 1:15 with the extent measured from `x range`/`CNT_OVERHANG`/`X_TAIL` (290 mm, 7.5 mm fore/aft, and the open bus fits vertically at 208.8 mm); amber as loose fields with ≥6 mm bleed stated as the design and the 0.44 mm bulb gap quoted as the reason; hubcap badges deleted and the false IP sentence rewritten; `4,065 mm` dropped for a caption that is grade-S throughout; vellum killed; `N_FLOWERS` corrected to 10; folk census re-pointed at the shipped 30/44.9 % rather than the photograph's 66/47.8 %; substrate re-specified away from greaseproof; food-contact question raised before layout lock; SVG-exporter headless proof scheduled week one; `trace_outline.py` + `mottle_measure.py` named as the no-render composition route (I ran the tracer's selftest — `SELFTEST PASS`); the 20-sheet grid; the prior-art paragraph written honestly.

**Refused, with reasons:**

- **Auditor 1's "take the bus off entirely; print the Nolita door lettering instead."** Rejected on the record: `probe_scratch/rev50/measure/MEASURE_rev50.md` scores "267 ELIZABETH STREET / NUEVA YORK (+ Gracias por su Preferencia)" **P on `nolita_flank` and `nolita_doorshut`, A on `ref_side`, `ref_rear34` and `ref_playa_34`** — it is the Nolita livery state, and `LEDGER_rev49.md` §8 calls a Nolita reading a wrong-artwork measurement, while SPEC §0.1 says *"This is the Playa bus, NOT the Nolita one"*. Also: a blank sheet that becomes a bus is a weaker object than a working bus that lights up, because it gives the 90 % of dry sheets nothing at all.
- **Auditor 1's GREEN → RED livery reveal.** Genuinely clever, and rejected: it needs two chromatic inks in register across the whole body rather than fields, the green state's paint belongs to a *different vehicle* in the reference set (rule 11), and it breaks the semantic lock that makes this concept work — grease means food means the bus is trading. Grease does not mean "eight years passed."
- **Auditor 3's "put SEÑOR TACOMBI on the reverse in amber as the payload."** Half-taken. The instinct — Tacombi's mark surfacing under the food, not VW's — is right and I kept it. But the script is this project's most contested artwork (F01/F39: `Senor` is the only region with an area outlier at −28.5 %; F156 makes its gate row a deliberate departure; the owner rejected a version of it twice by name). Making it the reveal's climax invites report ten. So: **outline on top, amber field behind** — the grease fills the brand's own name in, which is a better image than the name appearing, and it does not rest the payload on disputed ink.
- **Auditor 1's "sell the eaten sheets as the only edition."** Kept the thesis, refused the transaction: selling used food paper is a hygiene problem and it turns the ache into a price. The free glassine sleeve at the till does the same work as a gift, and the frontier archive carries the compounding value instead.
- **The bag's two-face version.** Cut, not downgraded. Its own note conceded low reveal reliability, and a giveaway that teaches customers the trick sometimes doesn't work is worse than no bag. The bag now prints the harvested frontiers instead.

**Stated ceilings.** The 1:15 arithmetic is mine off the tree's constants and must be recomputed by the plate script, not typed — the record carries four length figures with four referents (`4.065`, `4.317`, `4.580`, and this drawing's `4.348`) and I did not pick one by hand. The resist's behaviour on kraft is **untested and unverifiable from anything in this repo**; if lanes do not hold oil, this concept is a known grease-reveal wrapper and should be re-judged as one. `wm.grease_pencil_export_svg` has never been run in this tree. And I cannot check *"se prende"* for idiom from files — that needs a Mexican speaker, and I have said so rather than asserting it.

**What I changed, and what I refused**

**The three moves that did the most work — none of them was on an auditor's list:**

1. **Master frame moved from `hero34r` to the orthographic `side`.** `studio.py` reads `"side": dict(..., lens=None, ortho=5.90)`. In an orthographic elevation *surface area is pixel area*, so folk_gen's mm² inventory becomes the on-screen ordering with no reprojection — which dissolves the originality auditor's "inverted pacing" flaw and makes his "re-rank by projected area" fix unnecessary rather than merely done. It is also the painter's own square-on view, and the only uncleaned frame I could find: I measured non-white bboxes of `out/r75_side.png` (x 212..1458, y 111..963 — margin on all four edges) against `r75_hero34r` (x→1599 of 1600) and `r75_hero34f` (x→0, y→1099), both hard-clipped.

2. **The crop to the band is now an IP instrument with a probe, not a composition note.** Specified in body-frame metres (z ∈ [0.706, 1.500], from STATE.md's `front arch lip above hub 0.3732` on a hub at TYRE_D/2, and belt 1.2070). It clears the hubcap badge top (0.3759 m AG) by 330 mm. This kills the four `capvw` glyphs (`visibility_budget` ranks them at 12438 px²), the T1 shape mark, and the right-edge clip, and makes 1080×1920 native. I added a probe that projects `capvw*`/`vw_disc`/`vw_ring`/`vwbar` and asserts zero in-crop pixels, watched failing first.

3. **The signature beat is grounded instead of re-homed or dropped.** Both auditors were right that "shadow, then metal, because that is how a signwriter works" is uncited and that SPEC §10.16 forbids adding a keyline to `script_gen.py`. But `lid_gen._draw_word`'s docstring already reads *"Three passes: dark outline, light keyline, red core"*, and the board's own measurement is in the file: *"the keyline is faint but real: pixels adjacent to the ink reach luma 233 against a cream ground of luma 221."* So the order is a **measured property of hand-painted lettering on this bus** — it just lives on the lid, not the flank. Beat 8 runs it where it is measured; beat 6 runs it on the wordmark as a declared compositing stylisation; and PHOTOS_WANTED gets §10.16's own named remedy.

**Grafted from the auditors:** base-plate 2D compositing with a watched guard (5 renders ≈ 28 min vs ≈ 34 h, and it removes the render noise *by construction* — I measured the floor myself at 4.043 % >8 levels / 0.046 % >32 / worst 40 on the r75 side pair through `photometry.read_png`); arc-length stroke reveal instead of component rank; `FLANK_DARKS` gets its own beat; rosettes on a reload rhythm with a reach-cluster constraint; hard cuts, no dissolves; beat 6 at 3 frames not 1; beat 8 as a shop-opening; the progression plate promoted to lead artefact; `T1_SAVE`; the scoping sentence that clears F18/F191/F192/F193; ask the owner who painted it.

**Refused, with reasons:**
- **The warm low raking key** — the concept's own light. `gloss_compare` reads 0.412 against a 0.60 bar over 787194 px² of red and 2029124 px² of cream in this very view; raking light on a lobe that broad reads as vinyl, on a film about a painted surface. Flat frontal light is also the *better* choice, not just the safer one: it is a panel in a workshop rather than a car commercial. F259's relight licence stays unspent.
- **"New York becoming Playa."** The producibility auditor is right and I verified it: `tex/` holds only calidad, emblem, lidmural, lidsign, nose, senor, swirl, swirl_b. State B's chalkboard lid, glass lettering and TACOMBI.COM fascia do not exist. Beat 0 is a **declared fiction** with the owner's own papel-picado precedent cited.
- **Retitling.** ROTULISTA is earned rather than renamed, by making the *lettering* the climax — which the three-pass beat now does.
- **All three circulating tile censuses, including my own.** The concept's 196/66.4 %, an auditor's 177/77.7 % and my 169/78.2 % (162–194 across alpha>64..200) differ by threshold *and* by ruler — mine is at texel resolution, folk_gen's 66 is at the photograph's 4.735 mm/px in body coordinates. That is rule 38, so I refused to publish 169-vs-66 as a comparison and instead prescribed `folk_gen.report_composition()`'s existing, unrun `achieved` column.
- **The claim that the audience can feel a censused order.** Deleted. The census's value moved to the print, where it is genuinely unrepeatable.

**Measured in this pass, with ceilings:** `tex/senor.png` among alpha>200 — min luma 145.7, p1 165.7, fraction below luma 80 **exactly 0.0000** (no dark ink at all); and SPEC §10.16's *"currently emits a constant (214, 216, 218)"* is **stale** — per-channel std is now 14.15/15.95/17.45 against the photograph's 16–19, so the flatness complaint is discharged and the keyline one is not. Gold stroke width on the shipped tile at 1:1 (0.939 mm/texel from MAP_SCALE 0.26 over 4096): p10 2.66 / p50 13.15 / p90 45.07 mm; at a 280 mm chest print of the whole flank, **30.0 % of the gold falls under 0.5 mm** while a 380 mm one-mass back print puts 0.0 % under it. The original's 8.8/1.8 mm figures *do* reproduce — they are a 1:1.5 reduction of a 4.065 m flank, i.e. a 2.7 m wall graphic, so the figures were right and the format inference was wrong.

I ran `folk_gen.py` for the achieved census, saw that its `main()` writes `tex/swirl.png` and `tex/swirl_b.png`, killed it, and confirmed `git status --porcelain` is clean. The achieved column remains unrun and is the largest owed number in this concept.
